2. MMEL 27-04-02 (DDPG) Preparation - Leading Edge Flap/Slat Position Light Systems - Forward
Panel Lights Inoperative
(Figure 901)
A. General
(1) This task gives the maintenance steps which prepare the airplane for flight with the forward
panel lights inoperative.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
B. References
Reference Title
29-11-00-860-801 Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization (P/B 201)
C. Location Zones
Zone Area
211 Flight Compartment - Left
212 Flight Compartment - Right
D. Procedure
SUBTASK 27-00-00-860-045
WARNING
MAKE SURE ALL PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT
CONTROLS SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING
GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY
HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(1) Pressurize the hydraulic system B to 3000 ±100 psi (211 ±7 kg/cm2
). To pressurize hydraulic
system B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
SUBTASK 27-00-00-710-004
(2) Cycle the flaps.
SUBTASK 27-00-00-700-001
(3) Make sure that the LE DEVICES annunciator on panel, P5-12 operates normally during flap
extension and retraction.
NOTE: If an annunciator panel TRANSIT light fails to illuminate while the corresponding
device is in motion, then this light must be considered inoperative.
SUBTASK 27-00-00-020-001
(4) Remove the bulbs from the applicable lights on the center instrument panel, P2-2.
SUBTASK 27-00-00-930-001
(5) Attach an INOP placard to the applicable lights.

132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304,
306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-465
SUBTASK 27-00-00-930-002

(a) Flap positions 1 through 5:
1) All slats in EXT position.
2) LE flaps extended.
(b) Flap positions 10 through 40:
1) All slats in FULL EXT position.
2) LE flaps extended.
 466-999

(7) Make a placard which shows the LE flap and slat positions:
(a) Flap positions 1 through 25:

 ALL

1) All slats in EXT position.
2) LE flaps extended.

27-00-00-440-801MMEL 27-04-02 (DDPG) Restoration - Leading Edge Flap/Slat Position Light Systems - Forward Panel Lights InoperativePDF p. 113
3. MMEL 27-04-02 (DDPG) Restoration - Leading Edge Flap/Slat Position Light Systems - Forward
Panel Lights Inoperative
(Figure 901)
A. General
(1) This task puts the airplane back to its usual condition after operation with the forward panel
lights inoperative.
B. References
Reference Title
27-32-00-710-801 Stall Warning System - Operational Test (P/B 501)
29-11-00-860-805 Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal (P/B 201)
C. Location Zones
Zone Area
211 Flight Compartment - Left
212 Flight Compartment - Right
D. Procedure
SUBTASK 27-00-00-960-001
(1) Replace the bulbs from the applicable lights.
SUBTASK 27-00-00-810-001
(2) If the LE flap/slat position light was not the problem, then do these steps to correct the fault:
(a) Find the fault code or description of the fault that occurred.
(b) If you find a fault code, then do these steps:
1) Go to the Fault Code Index in the applicable chapter of the FIM and find the fault
code.
NOTE: The first two digits of the fault code is the FIM chapter.
2) Find the task number on the same line as the fault code.
3) Go to the task in the FIM and do the steps in the task.
(c) If you find a description of the fault, then do these steps:
1) Go to the Observed Fault List at the beginning of the FIM and find the best
description for the fault.
2) Find the task number on the same line as the fault description.
3) Go to the task in the FIM and do the steps in the task.
SUBTASK 27-00-00-930-004
(3) Remove the INOP placard from the applicable lights.
SUBTASK 27-00-00-930-005
(4) Remove the placard that has the LE flap and slat positions.
SUBTASK 27-00-00-710-017
(5) Do this Task: Stall Warning System - Operational Test, TASK 27-32-00-710-801.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
E. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 27-00-00-860-044
(1) Remove power from hydraulic system B. To remove power from hydraulic system B, do this
task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805.

EFFECTIVITY

SUBTASK 27-00-00-210-008
(3) Make sure that the remaining lights on the overhead annunciator panel, P5-12, operate
normally during flap extension and retraction.
NOTE: If an annunciator panel TRANSIT light fails to illuminate while the corresponding
device is in motion or an annunciator panel TRANSIT light stays illuminated while the
corresponding device is not in motion, then this light must be considered inoperative.
NOTE: If an annunciator panel EXT or FULL EXT light fails to illuminate while the
corresponding device is not in motion, then this light must be considered inoperative.
NOTE: It is not easy to see the positions of the LE slats 3, 4, 5, and 6 from the flight deck.
Thus, the indications for the LE slats 3, 4, 5, and 6 are not permitted to be inoperative.
For this same reason, indication for LE Flaps 1, 2, 3 & 4 is not permitted to be
inoperative.
SUBTASK 27-00-00-740-012

a) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag:
CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2
Row Col Number Name
E 7 C01208 STALL WARN ASYM MODE

applicable slat can be confirmed to be stationary in the position where the
intermittent indication was observed, then do the following:
NOTE: The FSEU will inhibit the Takeoff Warning (TOW) alert to the PSEU when 7
of 8 LE slats are extended during a takeoff attempt only if circuit breaker
C01208 Stall Warning Asymmetry Mode is open. If the circuit breaker is
closed, the TOW will occur when the crew advances the throttles for takeoff.
a) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag:
CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2

(a) Make sure that hydraulic system B pressure is 3000 ±100 psi (211 ±7 kg/cm2

(b) While monitoring the control column for stick shaker operation, push and hold the STALL

fault.

SUBTASK 27-00-00-860-005
WARNING
MAKE SURE ALL PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT
CONTROLS SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING
GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY
HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(1) Pressurize the elevator hydraulic systems A and B, do this task: Elevator Hydraulic System A
and B - Pressurization, TASK 27-31-00-800-801.
SUBTASK 27-00-00-860-007
(2) Use the STAB TRIM switches to set the stabilizer to 4 units of trim.
SUBTASK 27-00-00-860-048
(3) Set the FLT CONTROL A and B switches to the OFF position.
SUBTASK 27-00-00-860-049
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU ARE CAREFUL WITH THE WIRE BUNDLES WHEN
YOU USE THE TRAMMEL BAR, SPL-1677. THE SHARP EDGES ON THE
TRAMMEL BAR, SPL-1677 CAN CAUSE CHAFING OR DAMAGE TO THE
WIRES.
(4) Use the trammel bar, SPL-1677, to make sure that the horizontal stabilizer "B" dimension is
39.89 ±0.03 in. (1013.21 ±0.76 mm) (Figure 903).
SUBTASK 27-00-00-860-006
(5) Do this task: Null Procedure - Mach Trim Actuator, TASK 27-31-00-700-801.
SUBTASK 27-00-00-010-002
(6) Open this access panel:
Number Name/Location
311BL Stabilizer Trim Access Door
SUBTASK 27-00-00-390-001
(7) Apply a seal to the drain hole in each pitot probe on the vertical fin.
(a) Use vinyl adhesive Scotch Brand No.471 tape, G02219, and black polyethylene sheet
polyethylene film, G00252, to cover and seal the drain holes.
SUBTASK 27-00-00-950-001
CAUTION
WHENEVER AN OPENING IS COVERED, MAKE SURE THAT CONDITION IS
VISIBLE FROM THE GROUND. ENGINES SHOULD NOT BE OPERATED
WITH COVERS IN PLACE BECAUSE THE COVERS CAN COME OFF AND
DAMAGE THE ENGINES.
(8) Attach a "PITOT PROBES COVERED" tag, G02447, that has "PITOT PROBES COVERED"
printed on it in black letters, to the top of the left control wheel in the flight deck with wire.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
WARNING
WHEN THE DRAIN HOLES ARE COVERED, MAKE SURE THAT
CONDITION IS VISIBLE FROM THE GROUND. IN ADDITION, ATTACH A
TAG TO THE LEFT CONTROL WHEEL IN THE FLIGHT DECK AS A
REMINDER THAT THE STATIC PORTS ARE COVERED. FAILURE TO
OBSERVE AND REMOVE COVERINGS OVER STATIC PORTS BEFORE
FLIGHT CAN CAUSE LARGE ERRORS IN AIRSPEED-SENSING AND
ALTITUDE-SENSING SIGNALS. THIS CAN LEAD TO LOSS OF SAFE
FLIGHT.
(a) Put one end of a 4 ft (1.22 m) or longer piece of the orange barricade tape, G02443, over
the black polyethylene sheet covering the drain holes of the pitot probes and secure the
upper edge with a 5 in. (12.70 cm) strip of the adhesive Scotch Brand No.471 tape,
G02219.
1) Smooth Scotch Brand No.471 tape, G02219, on the airplane surface to make sure
that the bond is satisfactory.
SUBTASK 27-00-00-020-002
(9) Remove the restrictor valves from the systems A and B pitot lines.
NOTE: The systems A and B pitot lines are below the elevator feel computer.

CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-3
Row Col Number Name
C 4 C00236 HEATERS ELEV PITOT LEFT

SUBTASK 27-00-00-480-001
(11) Install the regulator, SPL-1742, or equivalent air data model test set, COM-1914, with the pitot
test adapter, COM-1916.
(a) If the regulator, SPL-1742, for the leak test is used, do the following:
NOTE: The DPS 400 Test Set can be used as an alternate tool to the DPS 500.
1) Connect the pressure gage lines from the regulator, SPL-1742, to the drain holes of
the pitot lines.
(b) If the air data model test set, COM-1914, for the leak test is used, do the following:
1) Install the pitot plugs, COM-16577, over the ends of the pitot lines.
2) Install a highly visible streamer on the opening of the aft unpressurized
compartment.
a) Make sure that you can easily see the streamer from the ground.
NOTE: This is to remind you to remove the plugs and install the restrictor
valves again when the test is completed.
SUBTASK 27-00-00-790-001
(12) Do a check for pressure leakage in the feel pitot system.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE PITOT PROBE HAS NO ADDED WEIGHT ON IT
FROM THE TEST HOSE. THE WEIGHT OF THE TEST HOSE CAN BEND
OR TWIST THE PITOT PROBE OUT OF TOLERANCE.
(a) Connect the regulator, SPL-1742, or equivalent air data model test set, COM-1914, to the
two vertical fin pitot probes.
1) Do this step for the regulator, SPL-1742:
a) Connect the pressure lines from the regulator, SPL-1742, with the pitot test
adapter, COM-1916, to the two vertical fin pitot probes.
2) Do this step for the air data model test set, COM-1914:
a) Use the air data accessory kit, COM-25177, to connect the air data model test
set, COM-1914, to the pitot test adapter, COM-1916.
NOTE: The air data accessory kit, COM-25177, contains the hoses to connect
to the air data model test set, COM-1914, and the pitot test adapter,
COM-1916.
CAUTION
DO NOT INCREASE THE PRESSURE TO MORE THAN 5 PSIG (34.5 KPA)
(437 KNOTS OF COMPUTED AIRSPEED (KCAS)), DURING THE TEST. IF
THE PRESSURE IS MORE THAN 5 PSIG (34.5 KPA) (437 KCAS), IT CAN
CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ELEVATOR FEEL COMPUTER.
(b) Operate the air data model test set, COM-1914, or regulator, SPL-1742, to apply
pressure between 0.90 +0.07 / -0.00 psig (6.21 +0.48 / -0.00 kPa) to simulate 194 to 201
kcas.
(c) Set the shutoff valve in the air data model test set, COM-1914, or regulator, SPL-1742, to
the OFF position.
(d) Make sure that the pressure does not decrease more than 0.2 psig (1.4 kPa) (8 kcas)
during a 2-minute time.
NOTE: The low pressure pressurization steps above ensure that there is no significant
system leak before you apply full pressure in the following steps. If there is a leak
in the pitot system or the pressurization equipment, you can exceed the full
pressure of 5 psig (34.5 kPa) (437 kcas) and cause damage to the feel computer
bellows.
(e) Fix any pitot system or pressurization equipment leaks, as necessary.
(f) Operate the regulator, SPL-1742, or equivalent air data model test set, COM-1914, to
pressurize the pitot system to 4.7 psig (32.4 kPa) - 4.9 psig (33.8 kPa) to simulate 425 to
433 kcas.
(g) Set the shutoff valve in the regulator, SPL-1742, or equivalent air data model test set,
COM-1914, to the OFF position.
(h) Make sure that the pressure does not decrease more than 0.3 psig (2.1 kPa) (12 kcas)
during a 2 minute time.
(i) Operate the regulator, SPL-1742, or equivalent air data model test set, COM-1914, to put
the system back to ambient pressure (0 psig (0.0 kPa)).
SUBTASK 27-00-00-730-001
(13) Do a test of control column force.
(a) Make sure that the FLT CONTROL A and B switches are in the ON position.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
CAUTION
DO NOT INCREASE THE PRESSURE TO MORE THAN 5 PSIG (34.5 KPA)
(437 KNOTS OF COMPUTED AIRSPEED (KCAS)), DURING THE TEST. IF
THE PRESSURE IS MORE THAN 5 PSIG (34.5 KPA) (437 KCAS), IT CAN
CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ELEVATOR FEEL COMPUTER.
(b) Operate the regulator, SPL-1742, or equivalent air data model test set, COM-1914, to
pressurize the pitot systems to 2.47 ±0.05 psi (17.03 ±0.34 kPa) (315 ±3 knots).
(c) Install a piece of the Scotch Flatback Masking Tape 250, G00270, on the tail cone along
the direction of the right elevator trailing edge travel.
(d) Attach the adapter, SPL-1674, to the captain's control column.
(e) Move the captain's control column lightly to put the elevator system in the neutral
position.
1) Attach the DO NOT OPERATE tags, STD-858, on the control columns.
(f) Make a mark of the neutral position of the elevator trailing edge on the Scotch Flatback
Masking Tape 250, G00270 (Figure 902).
1) Use this mark of the neutral position as reference.
(g) Remove the DO NOT OPERATE tags , from the control columns.
(h) Measure and mark 1.20 in. (30.48 mm) above the neutral mark.
NOTE: This mark will be the trailing edge up test target position.
(i) Measure and mark 1.20 in. (30.48 mm) below the neutral mark.
NOTE: This mark will be used as the trailing edge down test target position.
(j) Set FLT CONTROL B switch to the OFF position and leave FLT CONTROL A switch in
the ON position.
(k) Move the captain's control column aft with a push/pull gauge (0-50 lbs), STD-1100, to set
the elevator trailing edge to 1.20 ±0.05 in. (30.48 ±1.27 mm) up from the neutral position.
1) Make sure that the force to hold the control column at this position is 32.0 lbf
(142.3 N) - 52.0 lbf (231.3 N).
(l) Move the captain's control column forward with a push/pull gauge (0-50 lbs), STD-1100,
to set the elevator trailing edge to 1.20 ±0.05 in. (30.48 ±1.27 mm) down from the neutral
position.
1) Make sure that the force to hold the control column at this position is 33.0 lbf
(146.8 N) - 56.0 lbf (249.1 N).
(m) Set the FLT CONTROL A switch to the OFF position and FLT CONTROL B switch to the
ON position.
(n) Move the captain's control column aft with a push/pull gauge (0-50 lbs), STD-1100, to set
the elevator trailing edge to 1.20 ±0.05 in. (30.48 ±1.27 mm) up from the neutral position.
1) Make sure that the force to hold the control column at this position is 32.0 lbf
(142.3 N) - 52.0 lbf (231.3 N).
(o) Move the captain's control column forward with a push/pull gauge (0-50 lbs), STD-1100,
to set the elevator trailing edge to 1.20 ±0.05 in. (30.48 ±1.27 mm) down from the neutral
position.
1) Make sure that the force to hold the control column at this position is 33.0 lbf
(146.8 N) - 56.0 lbf (249.1 N).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

9. MMEL 27-10 (DDPG) Restoration - FEEL DIFF PRESS Light Inoperative
A. General
(1) This task puts the airplane back to its usual condition after operation with the FEEL DIFF
PRESS light on the flight controls panel inoperative.
B. Location Zones
Zone Area
211 Flight Compartment - Left
212 Flight Compartment - Right
C. Procedure
SUBTASK 27-00-00-960-002
(1) Replace the FEEL DIFF PRESS light.
SUBTASK 27-00-00-810-003
(2) If the FEEL DIFF PRESS light was not the problem, then do these steps to correct the fault:
(a) Find the fault code or description of the fault that occurred.
(b) If you find a fault code, then do these steps:
1) Go to the Fault Code Index in the applicable chapter of the FIM and find the fault
code.
NOTE: The first two digits of the fault code is the FIM chapter.
2) Find the task number on the same line as the fault code.
3) Go to the task in the FIM and do the steps in the task.
(c) If you find a description of the fault, then do these steps:
1) Go to the Observed Fault List at the beginning of the FIM and find the best
description for the fault.
2) Find the task number on the same line as the fault description.
3) Go to the task in the FIM and do the steps in the task.
SUBTASK 27-00-00-930-009
(3) Remove the LIGHT INOP placard from the FEEL DIFF PRESS light.

CONTROL SURFACES BEFORE YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER.
AILERONS, RUDDERS, ELEVATORS, FLAPS, SLATS, SPOILERS, LANDING
GEAR, AND THRUST REVERSERS CAN MOVE QUICKLY WHEN YOU
SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.

Systems A and B Pressurization, TASK 27-62-00-800-801.

EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) Put the Speedbrake handle in the DOWN position.
NOTE: The spoilers will move down during this step.
(c) Make sure that the flight and ground spoilers are all down.
(d) Put the Speedbrake handle in the FLIGHT DETENT.
NOTE: The spoilers will move up during this step.
(e) Make sure that the flight and ground spoilers deploy.
(f) Put the Speedbrake handle in the DOWN position.
NOTE: The spoilers will move down during this step.
(g) Make sure that the flight and ground spoilers are all down.
(h) Make sure that the stabilizer trim is in the green band.
(i) Put the flaps to a takeoff position.
(j) Release the parking brake.
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT YOU OPEN THE CIRCUIT BREAKER FOR THE
WEATHER RADAR SYSTEM. THE FORWARD MOVEMENT OF A
THRUST LEVER CAN CAUSE THE AUTOMATIC OPERATION OF THE
SYSTEM. THE OPERATION OF THIS SYSTEM CAN CAUSE SERIOUS
INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT IN THE AREA OF
THE NOSE RADOME.

F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1
Row Col Number Name
D 13 C00120 WEATHER RADAR RT
(p) Set the parking brake.
(q) Put the flaps to the retract position.
(r) If the SPEEDBRAKES EXTENDED light remains illuminated while on the ground, remove

(j) Make sure that the STBY RUD ON light is illuminated.
(k) Set the FLT CONTROL B switch on the P5-3 panel to the OFF position.
(l) Make sure that the STBY RUD ON light is not illuminated.
(m) Set the FLT CONTROL A and B switches on the P5-3 panel to the ON positions.
(n) Make sure that the STBY RUD ON light is not illuminated.
(o) Move the flap control lever to the UP detent position.

27-09-14-820-801Control Cables - RiggingPDF p. 196
3. Control Cables - Rigging
A. General
(1) Before you do cable adjustment, permit a minimum of one hour at a constant ambient
temperature of ± 5 degrees F (± 2.8 degrees C) for the airframe temperature to become stable.
(a) It is recommended to do the cable adjustments in a controlled environment such as a
hangar.
NOTE: Direct sunlight on the airframe will cause the cable readings to be inaccurate.
(b) All temperature readings will be taken as ambient outside but adjacent to the applicable
area of the airframe.
(c) The cable tension values will not be correct when there are temperature differences along
the cable run.
(2) Before you do cable adjustment, allow the tensiometer to stabilize to the same ambient
temperature as the airplane.
(3) For cables retensioning, it is recommended to adjust the cables to the upper limit values, to
account for tension loss in service.

SUBTASK 27-09-21-020-001
(1) Remove the hydraulic module [1]:
(a) Disconnect the electrical connector [18], electrical connector [14], and electrical
connector [13] from the spoiler shutoff valve [16], flight controls shutoff valve [17], and low
pressure warning switch [15].

to the unions [3], unions [5], reducer [11] and new packings [2], new packings [4], and
new packing [12].

module [1].

E. Flight Controls Hydraulic Module Test
SUBTASK 27-09-21-720-001
(1) Do the test of the flight controls hydraulic module [3]:
(a) Make sure that the two FLT CONTROL switches, on the P5-3 Flight Controls panel, are in
the ON position (Figure 501).
(b) Make sure that the two SPOILER switches, on the P5-3 Flight Controls panel, are in the
ON position.
(c) Make sure that the manual override lever [4] of the spoiler shutoff valve [1] and flight
controls shutoff valve [2] on the flight controls hydraulic modules [3] are in position 1
(Figure 502).
(d) Operate the aileron control wheel, control column, and rudder pedal sets to bleed the
hydraulic system.
(e) Make sure that there is no leakage of hydraulic fluid at the flight controls hydraulic
modules [3].
(f) Set the two SPOILER switches to the OFF position.
(g) Make sure that the manual override lever [4] of the spoiler shutoff valve [1] on the flight
controls hydraulic modules [3] is in position 2.
(h) Turn the aileron control wheel.
(i) Make sure that the spoilers do not operate.
(j) Set the two FLT CONTROL switches to the OFF position.
(k) Make sure that the manual override lever [4] of the flight controls shutoff valve [2] on the
flight controls hydraulic modules [3] is in position 2.
(l) Make sure that the two LOW PRESSURE warning lights, on the P5-3 Flight Controls
panel, come on.
(m) Set the two FLT CONTROL switches to the ON position.
(n) Make sure that the two LOW PRESSURE warning lights go off.
(o) Set the two SPOILER switches to the ON position.
SUBTASK 27-09-21-860-004
(2) To remove power from hydraulic systems A and B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power
Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805.
SUBTASK 27-09-21-210-001
(3) Make sure that the LOW PRESSURE lights come on.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-09-21-210-002
(4) Make sure that the master warning and caution lights and the flight controls warning light come
on.

(1) Remove the flight controls shutoff valve motor [6].

or before the installation step of the electrical connector(s). This is an operator
option.
WARNING
DO THE STEPS BELOW IF THE AIRPLANE OPERATES WHERE

AIRPLANES THAT YOU FOUND CORROSION IN THE ELECTRICAL
CONNECTORS IN THE MAIN WHEEL WELL. THE ELECTRICAL
CONNECTORS ARE IN A SYSTEM THAT IS NECESSARY FOR SAFE
FLIGHT.
(c) If there was corrosion, correct the problem (SWPM 20-60-03).
(d) Set the manual override lever on the flight controls shutoff valve motor [6] to position 2.
(e) Remove the lockwire from the screws [7].
(f) Remove the screws [7] that attach the flight controls shutoff valve motor [6] to the flight
controls shutoff valve [8].
(g) Remove the flight controls shutoff valve motor [6] from the flight controls shutoff valve [8].

2. Flight Controls Shutoff Valve Test
A. General
(1) The flight controls shutoff valve is part of the flight controls hydraulic module. The hydraulic
module for the hydraulic system A is found in the left main wheel well. The hydraulic module for
the hydraulic system B is found in the right main wheel well.

WARNING
KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL
SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE
COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC
POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(2) Pressurize hydraulic systems A and B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization,
TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
SUBTASK 27-09-31-480-003
(3) Install the NLG towing lever pin, SPL-1499, in the nose wheel steering mechanism
(TASK 32-00-01-480-801).
NOTE: Nose landing gear will move when the rudder pedals are moved. To prevent NLG
movement, install a lockout pin in the nose wheel steering mechanism.
F. Flight Controls Shutoff Valve Test
SUBTASK 27-09-31-710-001
(1) Do a test of flight controls shutoff valve.
(a) Make sure that the FLT CONTROL switches, on the P5 flight controls panel, are in the
ON position.
(b) Make sure that the manual override lever on the flight controls shutoff valve motor is in
position 1 for hydraulic systems A and B.
(c) Operate the aileron control wheel to bleed air from the hydraulic system lines and
components.
1) Make sure that there is no leakage of hydraulic fluid at the flight control hydraulic
modules.
(d) Operate the aileron control wheel, control column, and rudder pedals.
1) Make sure that the ailerons, elevators, and rudder operate satisfactory.
(e) Set the FLT CONTROL switches to the OFF position.
1) Make sure that the manual override lever on the flight controls shutoff valve motor is
in position 2 for hydraulic systems A and B.
(f) Operate the rudder pedals.
NOTE: The rudder must not operate hydraulically, but the rudder pedals will operate
manually. Some rudder surface movement can occur if the pedal input is large
enough to mechanically displace the PCU actuating piston. Full rudder authority
may be available.
1) Make sure that the force to operate the rudder pedals is higher now than when you
set the FLT CONTROLS switches to the ON position.
G. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 27-09-31-860-011
(1) Set the FLT CONTROL switches to the ON position.
(a) Make sure that the manual override lever on the flight controls shutoff valve motor is in
position 1 for hydraulic systems A and B.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-09-31-860-012
(2) Remove power from hydraulic systems A and B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power
Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805.
SUBTASK 27-09-31-080-001
(3) Remove the NLG towing lever pin, SPL-1499, from the nose wheel steering mechanism
(TASK 32-00-01-080-801).

EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Make sure that the flap control lever is in the FLAP UP detent.

2) Make sure the STBY RUD ON light on the P5-3 panel is illuminated.
(c) Set the ALTERNATE FLAPS arm switch to ARM.
1) Make sure that the leading edge flaps and slats and the trailing edge flaps do not
extend.
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT STAY AWAY FROM
THE LEADING EDGE SLATS, TRAILING EDGE FLAPS, AND DRIVE
MECHANISMS. THE FLAPS, SLATS, AND DRIVE MECHANISMS MOVE
QUICKLY. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE
TO EQUIPMENT.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE INBOARD FAN COWL PANEL AND THE
INBOARD AND OUTBOARD THRUST REVERSERS ARE CLOSED AND IN

THRUST REVERSERS ARE IN THE OPEN POSITION. THIS CAN CAUSE
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
CAUTION
DO NOT OPERATE THE TRAILING EDGE FLAPS WITH ELECTRICAL
POWER MORE THAN ONE FULL EXTEND/RETRACT CYCLE IN 25
MINUTES. YOU CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE FLAP ELECTRIC
MOTORS IF YOU OPERATE THEM TOO FREQUENTLY.

1) Make sure that the trailing edge flaps retract.
NOTE: It is not necessary to fully retract the trailing edge flaps with alternate
control.

(i) Move the ALTERNATE FLAPS ARM switch to the ARM position.
1) Make sure that the STANDBY HYD - LOW PRESSURE light is off.

 ALL

SUBTASK 27-09-51-020-001
(1) Remove the compensator cartridge [1]:
(a) Put a 5 gallon (19 liter) container, STD-1154 below the compensator cartridge [1] to catch
hydraulic fluid that drains from the compensator cartridge [1].

the removed packings.
(c) Put a cover on the hydraulic module housing [4] to keep contamination out of the open
port.

E. Low Pressure Warning Switch Installation
SUBTASK 27-09-61-420-001
(1) If they are not installed, install the backup rings [1] and packing [2] on the low pressure
warning switch [3].
(a) Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054 (recommended), or hydraulic fluid, D00153 (alternative),
to the backup rings [1] and new packing [2].
(b) Put the new backup rings [1] and packing [2] in their position on the low pressure warning
switch [3].
SUBTASK 27-09-61-420-002
(2) Install the low pressure warning switch [3]:
(a) Install the low pressure warning switch [3] on the flight controls hydraulic module [5].
(b) Tighten the low pressure warning switch [3] to 362.5 ±12.5 in-lb (41.0 ±1.4 N·m).
(c) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G01912, on the low pressure warning switch [3] and
nearest bolt.
SUBTASK 27-09-61-420-003
(3) Do the following steps to connect the electrical connector [4]:
(a) If the electrical connector(s) was not examined at the removal step, do these steps:
NOTE: The inspection of the electrical connector(s) can be done after the removal step
or before the installation step of the electrical connector(s). This is an operator
option.
1) Before connection of the electrical connector(s), examine the connector(s) for
corrosion.
WARNING
DO THE STEPS BELOW IF THE AIRPLANE OPERATES WHERE
DEICING FLUID THAT CONTAINS POTASSIUM FORMATE OR
POTASSIUM ACETATE IS USED. ALSO, DO THE STEPS FOR ALL
AIRPLANES THAT YOU FOUND CORROSION IN THE ELECTRICAL
CONNECTORS IN THE MAIN WHEEL WELL. THE ELECTRICAL
CONNECTORS ARE IN A SYSTEM THAT IS NECESSARY FOR SAFE
FLIGHT.
2) If there was corrosion, correct the problem (SWPM 20-60-03).
(b) Apply D5026NS or ZC-026 compound, G50171, to the electrical connector [4] (SWPM
20-60-03).
(c) Connect the electrical connector [4] to the low pressure warning switch [3].

27-09-71-820-801Trailing Edge Flap Adjustment for Lateral Trim and TestPDF p. 291
2. Trailing Edge Flap Adjustment for Lateral Trim and Test
A. General
(1) This task supplies the data necessary to adjust the trailing edge flaps to decrease the aileron
trim necessary for straight and level flight during cruise, and with the trailing edge flaps
extended.
(2) It is necessary to adjust the lateral trim if the aileron and rudder trim necessary to keep level
flight are not in the limits shown in (Table 501).
NOTE: There are no specific limits or requirements for lateral trim outside of the flight test
profile below. It is acceptable at other flight conditions to observe different trim settings
from those specified.
Table 501/27-09-71-993-811 Lateral Trim Limits
Flight Condition Aileron Trim Rudder Trim Airspeed Altitude (feet)
Cruise (Flaps UP/Gear Up) 0.75 unit 0.5 unit left /
1.0 unit right
.78 mach 37,000 or higher
Low Speed (Flaps UP/Gear
Up)
0.75 unit 0.75 unit 250 kias 10,000 to 17,000
Flaps Extended to 1 unit
(Gear Up)
1.0 unit *[1] 1.0 unit Flaps 1
Maneuver Speed
10,000 to 17,000
Flaps Extended to 15 units,
Landing Gear Extended
1.0 unit *[1] *[2] 1.0 unit Flaps 15
Maneuver Speed
10,000 to 17,000

*[1] The aileron trim change between flap positions 1 and 15 must be less than 1.0 unit.
*[2] The aileron trim change between flap positions 15 and 40 must be less than 1.4 units. An aileron trim requirement
shift from side to side is acceptable, provided it is within the limit of 1.4 units.
(3) There are the methods to adjust the lateral trim:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) You can change the shims at the aft end of the carriages on the outboard flap to correct
lateral trim during cruise.
NOTE: This method will have an effect on the lateral trim with the flaps extended.
(b) You can change length of the bellcranks on the aft flap drive for the outboard flap to
correct lateral trim with the flaps extended.
NOTE: This method has the most effect with the flaps extended to the 40 unit position.
There is no effect on the lateral trim with the flaps retracted, and a small effect
with the flaps extended to 1 and 15 unit positions.
 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-091
(c) You can change the position of the carriage roller cartridges on the inboard flap to correct
lateral trim for all flight conditions.
NOTE: This method will have a significant effect on the lateral trim with the flaps
extended and retracted.
 ALL
(d) You can change the compression of the bullnose seal on the inboard main flap. If the
bullnose seals are not symmetric between the left and right wings, the airflow past the
seals can cause lateral trim errors with the flaps extended to 40-units. This airflow can
cause the aft flap bellcrank adjustment to be not effective.
NOTE: This method will have an effect on the lateral trim with the flaps fully extended
and with the change in the lateral trim between the 15-unit and 40-unit positions.
 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020
(e) You can install asymmetric seals on the inboard main flap upper and lower surfaces.
Asymmetric seals between the flap and the wing to body fairing will permit some airflow
with the flaps extended. A change to the seal can be used when the change in the trim
requirement between flaps 15 and flaps 40 units is large, and the other methods have not
been effective.
NOTE: This method will have an effect on the lateral trim with the flaps fully extended
and with the change in the lateral trim between the 15-unit and 40-unit positions.
 ALL
(4) You can do more than one of the adjustments to correct for lateral trim problems. The charts
shown in this task are for single adjustments. The results shown in the charts can be added
together if you do multiple adjustments.

SUBTASK 27-09-71-820-001
(1) Do a check of these other systems to make sure that they are not the cause of the lateral trim
error:
(a) Make sure that the ailerons are adjusted correctly, do this task: Do A Check of the Aileron
System Adjustment, TASK 27-11-00-820-805.
NOTE: Make sure that the aileron downrig is symmetric between the left and right aileron
in the limit of 0.10 inch (2.54 mm).
(b) Make sure that the rudder is adjusted correctly, do this task: Rudder Centering Test,
TASK 27-21-00-700-815-002.
(c) Make sure that the outboard trailing edge flaps and aft flaps are adjusted correctly:
1) Do this task: Outboard Trailing Edge Flap Adjustment, TASK 27-51-21-820-801.
2) Do this task: Outboard Aft Flap Installation, TASK 27-51-22-400-801.
NOTE: Make sure that the main flap to aft flap mismatch trailing edge dimensions
are in the limits.
(d) Make sure that the inboard trailing edge flaps are adjusted correctly, do this task: Inboard
Trailing Edge Flap Adjustment, TASK 27-51-11-820-801.
NOTE: If the torque tube door is not sealed near the flap leading edge when the flaps
are extended to flaps 40 units, lateral trim problems can occur.
 006, 007, 013, 014
(e) Make sure the fairing assembly on the inboard side of the inboard upper fixed trailing
edge panel is sealed correctly against the side of body panel.
 ALL
(f) Make sure the spoilers are adjusted correctly. To check the spoilers, do this task: Flight
Spoiler Adjustment, TASK 27-61-00-820-803.
NOTE: Make sure the spoilers on the left and right wings are adjusted symmetrically.
SUBTASK 27-09-71-750-001
(2) Do a test flight to find the lateral trim necessary for straight and level flight for all flight
conditions:
NOTE: One unit of aileron trim is equal to six degrees of control wheel rotation.
NOTE: There are no specific limits or requirements for lateral trim outside of this flight test
profile. It is acceptable at other flight conditions to observe different trim settings from
those specified.
(a) To find the aileron trim necessary during cruise, fly with these conditions:
1) Flight speed: Approximately 0.78 mach.
2) Altitude: 37,000 feet or higher.
3) Fuel load: Balanced in the limit of 150 pounds (68 kilograms).
4) Throttles: Balanced thrust in the limit of 1 percent N1 difference, with autothrottles
OFF.
5) Autopilot engaged with in HDG SEL, with the wings level.
(b) Apply rudder trim to get zero heading change.
(c) Disengage the autopilot.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(d) Apply aileron trim to keep the wings level and maintain zero heading change.
(e) Write down the amount and direction of aileron trim necessary to maintain straight and
level flight.
NOTE: This is the trim for the Cruise condition.
(f) To find the aileron trim necessary for low speed cruise, and with the flaps extended, fly
with these conditions:
1) Altitude: Between 10,000 to 17,000 feet.
2) Fuel load: Balanced in the limit of 150 pounds (68 kilograms).
3) Throttles: Balanced thrust in the limit of 1 percent N1 difference, with autothrottles
OFF.
4) Autopilot OFF.
(g) Fly at 250 kias, with the flaps retracted.
(h) Apply rudder trim to get zero heading change.
(i) Apply aileron trim to keep the wings level and maintain zero heading change.
(j) Write down the amount and direction of aileron trim necessary to maintain straight and
level flight.
NOTE: This is the trim for the Low Speed Flaps UP.
(k) Change the airspeed to flaps 1 maneuvering speed, and extend the flaps to the 1-unit
position.
(l) Apply rudder trim to get zero heading change.
(m) Apply aileron trim to keep the wings level and maintain zero heading change.
(n) Write down the amount and direction of aileron trim necessary to maintain straight and
level flight.
NOTE: This is the trim for the flaps 1 unit.
(o) Change the airspeed to flaps 15 maneuvering speed, and extend the flaps to the 15-unit
position, and extend the landing gear.
(p) Apply rudder trim to get zero heading change.
(q) Apply aileron trim to keep the wings level and maintain zero heading change.
(r) Write down the amount and direction of aileron trim necessary to maintain straight and
level flight.
NOTE: This is the trim for the flaps 15 units.
(s) Change the airspeed to Vref +5 knots, and extend the flaps to the 40-unit position.
(t) Apply rudder trim to get zero heading change.
(u) Apply aileron trim to keep the wings level and maintain zero heading change.
(v) Write down the amount and direction of aileron trim necessary to maintain straight and
level flight.
NOTE: This is the trim for the flaps 40 units.

H. Lateral Trim Correction for the Cruise Condition
NOTE: Use these steps if the aileron trim necessary to keep level flight is not in the limits for the
cruise condition. This change will also have some effect on the other flight conditions. This
procedure changes the thickness of the shims on the carriages for the outboard flap.
SUBTASK 27-09-71-970-001
(1) Use the graphs to find the total shim thickness change necessary to correct the lateral trim
error (Figure 501).
SUBTASK 27-09-71-970-002
(2) Find the thickness and the location of the shims that you will change:
NOTE: The thickness of the shims added on one wing added to the thickness of the shims
removed from the other wing must be equal to the total shim thickness change. If it is
possible, the total shim thickness change should be divided equally between the left
and right wings. If the total shim change is 0.064 inch (1.625 mm) or less, you can
change the shims in only one wing. The maximum permitted thickness of the shims on
a carriage is 0.50 inch (12.7 mm). The minimum permitted thickness of the shims on a
carriage is 0.0 inch.
(a) Flight test condition; Right Trim:
NOTE: Right aileron trim indicates a left wing heavy condition.
1) Add approximately 1/2 of the total shim thickness change to the carriages on the
right outboard flap.
2) Remove approximately 1/2 of the total shim thickness change from the carriages on
the left outboard flap.
(b) Flight test condition; Left Trim:
NOTE: Left aileron trim indicates a right wing heavy condition.
1) Add approximately 1/2 of the total shim thickness change to the carriages on the left
outboard flap.
2) Remove approximately 1/2 of the total shim thickness change from the carriages on
the right outboard flap.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-09-71-040-001
(3) Prepare to change the thickness of the shims on the carriages for the outboard flaps:
(a) Extend the trailing edge flaps to the 40-unit position, do this task: Extend the Trailing
Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-803.
(b) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Deactivation, TASK 27-51-00-040-801.
SUBTASK 27-09-71-820-002
(4) Change the thickness of the shims [5] at the aft link fitting on the inboard and outboard
carriages (Figure 502):
NOTE: The change in the thickness of the shims [5] must be the same for the inboard
carriage [11] and the outboard carriage [6] on a flap.
(a) At the outboard carriage [6], change the thickness of the shims [5]:
1) Remove the nuts [4], washers [3] and bolts [2] that attach the aft link fitting [1] to the
outboard carriage [6].
2) Add or remove shims [5] between the aft link fitting [1] and the outboard carriage [6]
to get the correct shim thickness.
3) Apply sealant, A00247 to the mating surfaces of the shims [5].
4) Put the shims [5] in their location between the aft link fitting [1] and the outboard
carriage [6].
NOTE: The maximum total thickness of the shims [5] is 0.50 inch (12.7 mm). The
minimum total thickness of the shims [5] is 0.00 inch.

I. Lateral Trim Correction for the Flaps Extended Conditions
NOTE: Use these steps if the aileron trim necessary to keep level flight is not in the limits with the
flaps extended. This change will primarily effect the trim at the flaps 40 position, with less
effect at the other flap positions. This change will not have an affect on the lateral trim with
the flaps retracted. This procedure uses the adjustment fitting to change the length of the
bellcranks on the carriages for the outboard flap.
SUBTASK 27-09-71-970-003
(1) Use the graphs to find the total length change of the bellcrank [34] necessary to correct the
lateral trim error with the flaps extended (Figure 503).
NOTE: You will use the nuts [32] on the adjustment fitting [31] at the end of the bellcrank [34]
to change the length of the bellcrank [34].
SUBTASK 27-09-71-970-004
(2) Find the dimension and direction to adjust the nuts [32] for the adjustment fittings [31] on the
bellcranks [34]:
NOTE: The number of turns of the nuts [32] for the adjustment fittings [31] on one wing should
be the same, but in the opposite direction of the nuts [32] on the other wing.
(a) Flight test condition; Right Trim:
NOTE: Right aileron trim indicates a left wing heavy condition.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Decrease the length of the bellcranks on the right wing by the 1/2 the dimension
shown in the graph.
2) Increase the length of the bellcranks on the left wing by the 1/2 the dimension
shown in the graph.
(b) Flight test condition; Left Trim:
NOTE: Left aileron trim indicates a right wing heavy condition.
1) Decrease the length of the bellcranks on the left wing by the 1/2 the dimension
shown in the graph.
2) Increase the length of the bellcranks on the right wing by the 1/2 the dimension
shown in the graph.
SUBTASK 27-09-71-860-001
(3) Extend the trailing edge flaps to the 40-unit position, do this task: Extend the Trailing Edge
Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-803.
SUBTASK 27-09-71-040-002
(4) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Deactivation, TASK 27-51-00-040-801.
SUBTASK 27-09-71-820-003
(5) Change the length of the bellcranks [34] on the inboard and outboard carriages (Figure 504):
NOTE: The change in the length of the bellcranks [34] must be the same for the inboard
carriage and the outboard carriage on a flap in the limit of 0.05 inch (1.27 mm). It is
important to adjust the aft pushrods [53] after you adjust the length of the
bellcranks [34].
(a) Turn the applicable nut [32] on the bellcrank [34] to change the position of the adjustment
fitting [31].
NOTE: To increase the length of the bellcrank [34], loosen the lower nut [32] the distance
shown in the graph. To decrease the length of the bellcrank [34], loosen the
upper nut [32] the distance shown. One full turn of a nut [32] will change the
length of the bellcrank [34] by 0.05 inch (1.27 mm). You can use the distance
from the top of the bellcrank [34] to the bottom flange of the adjustment
fitting [31] as a reference dimension.
(b) Move the adjustment fitting [31] in the bellcrank [34].
(c) Engage the locking washer [33] with the bellcrank [34].
(d) Tighten the other nut [32] to hold the adjustment fitting [31].
(e) Install lockwire on the nuts [32].
SUBTASK 27-09-71-820-004
(6) Adjust the aft pushrods [53] for the aft flap [51] (Figure 505):
(a) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Reactivation, TASK 27-51-00-440-801.
(b) Do this task: Retract the Trailing Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-804.
(c) Measure the mismatch between the aft flap [51] and the main flap at the inboard and
outboard ends of the aft flap [51].
(d) If the mismatch at the inboard and outboard ends of the aft flap [51] is not in the limit of
0.00 ±0.030 inches (1.524 mm), then adjust the length of the applicable aft pushrod [53]:
NOTE: The tolerance on the mismatch is smaller than the normal adjustment tolerance.
This increases the effect of the lateral trim adjustment.
1) Loosen the nuts [52] on the aft pushrod [53].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
2) Turn the applicable aft pushrod [53] until the mismatch is in the limit at the inboard
and outboard ends of the aft flap [51].
NOTE: For each 1/4 turn of the aft pushrod [53], the trailing edge of the aft flap [51]
will move approximately 0.04 inch (1.02 mm).

J. Lateral Trim Correction for Multiple Flight Conditions
NOTE: Use these steps if the aileron trim necessary to keep level flight is not in the limit for the
cruise condition, and with the flaps extended. This adjustment is appropriate if all of the trim
values are either left or right. This procedure changes the adjustment of the carriage roller
cartridges on the inboard flap.
SUBTASK 27-09-71-970-009
(1) Find the total height change of the inboard flap necessary to correct the lateral trim error
(Figure 506):
(a) Use Graph A to find the total trailing edge height change necessary to correct the lateral
trim error for the cruise condition.
(b) Use Graph B to make sure the height change from the previous step is appropriate to
correct the lateral trim for the different airplane configurations.
NOTE: If it is appropriate, you can select a different height change.
SUBTASK 27-09-71-970-010
(2) Find the change to the position of the carriage roller cartridges necessary to correct the lateral
trim error (Figure 506):
NOTE: The change to the carriage roller cartridges will change the height of the trailing edge
of the inboard flap.
(a) Flight test condition; Right Trim:
NOTE: Right aileron trim indicates a left wing heavy condition.
1) Increase the height of the right trailing edge approximately 1/2 the total height
change. This is a positive change to the eccentric.
2) Decrease the height of the left trailing edge approximately 1/2 the total height
change. This is a negative change to the eccentric.
(b) Flight test condition; Left Trim:
NOTE: Left aileron trim indicates a right wing heavy condition.
1) Increase the height of the left trailing edge approximately 1/2 the total height
change. This is a positive change to the eccentric.
2) Decrease the height of the right trailing edge approximately 1/2 the total height
change. This is a negative change to the eccentric.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

wing rollers and the right wing rollers:

27-09-71-820-802Aileron Balance Tab Adjustment to Equalize Lateral Manual Reversion ForcesPDF p. 334
3. Aileron Balance Tab Adjustment to Equalize Lateral Manual Reversion Forces
A. General
(1) Use this procedure to adjust the aileron balance tab if the difference in the lateral manual
reversion forces is more than the permitted 2 to 1 ratio.
(2) In this task the aileron tab control rods are referred to as the "control rods".
B. References
Reference Title
27-11-00-700-803 Manual Reversion Control Friction Test (P/B 501)
27-11-00-820-802 Pogo and Power Control Unit (PCU) Adjustment (P/B 501)
27-11-00-820-803 Aileron Balance Tab Adjustment (P/B 501)
27-11-00-860-801 Pressure from the Aileron Hydraulic Systems A and B -
Deactivation (P/B 201)
27-11-00-860-802 Pressure to the Aileron Hydraulic Systems A and B - Activation
(P/B 201)
C. Location Zones
Zone Area
211 Flight Compartment - Left
212 Flight Compartment - Right
572 Left Wing - Aileron
672 Right Wing - Aileron
D. Prepare for the Adjustment
SUBTASK 27-09-71-860-002
(1) Make sure the aileron balance tab is correctly adjusted. To do a check of the adjustment of the
aileron balance tab, do this task: Aileron Balance Tab Adjustment, TASK 27-11-00-820-803.
SUBTASK 27-09-71-860-003
(2) Make sure the aileron control wheel forces, with power off, are not more than the specified
limits. To do a check of the aileron control wheel forces, do this task: Manual Reversion Control
Friction Test, TASK 27-11-00-700-803.
SUBTASK 27-09-71-860-004
(3) Make sure the stop clearances at the quadrants of the power control unit are not out of
tolerance. To do a check of the stop clearances, do this task: Pogo and Power Control Unit
(PCU) Adjustment, TASK 27-11-00-820-802.
SUBTASK 27-09-71-860-005
(4) If the Flaps Up trim is more than 0.75 unit, make the trim correction first before you do the
manual reversion correction. To adjust the trailing edge flap for lateral trim, do this task: Trailing
Edge Flap Adjustment for Lateral Trim and Test, TASK 27-09-71-820-801.
SUBTASK 27-09-71-860-006
(5) Do this task: Pressure from the Aileron Hydraulic Systems A and B - Deactivation,
TASK 27-11-00-860-801.
E. Aileron Balance Tab Adjustment To Equalize Lateral Manual Reversion Forces
SUBTASK 27-09-71-970-005
(1) Make a record of the force necessary to turn the control wheel approximately 30 degrees
clockwise.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-09-71-970-006
(2) Make a record of the force necessary to turn the control wheel approximately 30 degrees
counterclockwise.
SUBTASK 27-09-71-970-007
(3) Divide the counterclockwise force by the clockwise force to get the force ratio, or divide the
clockwise force by the counterclockwise force to get a force ratio value greater than 1.0.
SUBTASK 27-09-71-970-008
(4) Use the force ratio to find the correct length change for the control rod (Figure 510).
NOTE: For the left or right aileron balance tab, you must change the length of the control rods
in sets. The adjustment of the two control rods must be the same amount. It is
recommended that you split the adjustment equally between the left and right control
rod sets.
(a) To correct high left forces (control wheel counterclockwise), do one of these steps:
1) Make the left control rod set shorter.
2) Make the right control rod set longer.
3) Make the left control rod set shorter and make the right control rod set longer.
(b) To correct high right forces (control wheel clockwise), do one of these steps:
1) Make the right control rod set shorter.
2) Make the left control rod set longer.
3) Make the right control rod set shorter and make the left control rod set longer.
SUBTASK 27-09-71-820-005
(5) Adjust the aileron balance tab [111] (Figure 511):
(a) Do these steps to gain access to the control rods [113]:
1) Move the aileron trailing edge to the down position.
2) Remove the bolts [122] that attach the forward removable fairing [123] to the aileron
[112].
3) Remove the bolts [120] that attach the aft removable fairing [121] to the aileron
balance tab [111].
(b) Loosen the jamnuts [124] and [126] on the control rods [113].
(c) Do these steps if coarse adjustment is necessary;
1) Remove the pins [119], nuts [118], washers [117], bushings [116], washers [115] and
bolts [114] to disconnect the control rods [113] from the aileron balance tab [111].
2) Turn the rod ends on the control rods [113] for adjustment.
NOTE: One-half turn of the rod end lengthens the control rod 0.021 inch (0.53
millimeter). One-half turn of the rod end and the barrel [85] together
changes the position of the tab trailing edge 0.025 inch (0.64 millimeter).
a) To raise the trailing edge of the aileron balance tab [111], lengthen the control
rods [113].
b) To lower the trailing edge of the aileron balance tab [111], shorten the control
rods [113].
3) Connect the control rods [113] to the aileron balance tab [111];
a) Install the bushings [116], washers [115] and [117], bolts [114] and nuts [118].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
b) If there is binding between the control rod [113] and the bolt [114] or deflection
of the control rods [113], adjust the control rod length.
c) Make sure there is a minimum of 0.0150 inch (0.38 millimeter) gap between
the bushing [116] and the washer [115].
d) Tighten the nuts [118] to 50-80 pound-inches (5.6-9.0 newton-meters).
e) Install the pins [119].
(d) Do these steps if fine adjustment is necessary:
1) Turn the barrel [125] on the control rods [113].
NOTE: One turn of the barrel lengthens the control rod 0.008 inch (0.20 millimeter).
a) To raise the trailing edge of the aileron balance tab [111], lengthen the control
rods [113].
b) To lower the trailing edge of the aileron balance tab [111], shorten the control
rods [113].
2) Make sure the threads cover the inspection holes in the barrel [125].
(e) Tighten the jamnuts [124] to 100-140 pound-inches (11.3-15.8 newton-meters).
(f) Tighten the jamnuts [126] to 80-100 pound-inches (9.0-11.3 newton-meters).
(g) Install the bolts [120] that attach the aft removable fairing [121] to the aileron balance tab
[111].
(h) Install the bolts [122] that attach the forward removable fairing [123] to the aileron [112].
F. Put the Airplane Back To Its Usual Condition

(1) Do a freeplay check of one aileron balance tab with no movement of the aileron:

tab, directly under the plunger of the dial indicator, STD-1238.
1) Make a record of the travel shown on the dial indicator, STD-1238.
2) Slowly remove the force.
(e) Do not adjust the dial indicator, STD-1238.
CAUTION
PUT SUFFICIENT PADDING BETWEEN THE FORCE SCALE, AND THE
CONTROL SURFACE TO PREVENT DAMAGE TO THE CONTROL
SURFACE. THE FORCE SCALE CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE
CONTROL SURFACE.
(f) With the push/pull scale 0-25 pound (0-11 kilogram), STD-753, push down with a force of
approximately 5 lbf (22.24 N).
NOTE: Apply the force 0.25 in. (6.35 mm) from the trailing edge of the aileron balance
tab, 0.5 in. (12.70 mm) or less from the plunger of the dial indicator, STD-1238.
1) Make a record of the travel shown on the dial indicator, STD-1238.
2) Slowly remove the force.
(g) Add the up and down freeplay of the aileron balance tab to get the total up and down
freeplay of the aileron balance tab.
1) Make sure that the total up and down freeplay of the aileron balance tab is not more

(h) Remove the dial indicator, STD-1238.
(i) Remove the mount, STD-1279.
(j) Do these steps to make sure that the axial play (inboard-outboard direction) of the aileron
balance tab is not more than 0.04 in. (1.02 mm).
1) Hold the aileron balance tab around the trailing edge and with hand pressure, move
it outboard.
2) Use a 0.0 - 0.5 Inch feeler gauge, STD-1107, or a dial caliper, STD-1303, to
measure the clearance between the aileron and the outboard end of the aileron
balance tab.
a) Make a record of this clearance.
3) Hold the aileron balance tab around the trailing edge and with hand pressure, move
it inboard.
4) Measure the clearance between the aileron and the outboard end of the aileron
balance tab.
a) Make a record of the clearance dimension.
5) Make sure that the difference between the two measured clearances, or the axial
play, is not more than 0.04 in. (1.02 mm).

27-09-91-200-804Horizontal Stabilizer - InspectionPDF p. 359
5. Horizontal Stabilizer - Inspection
A. General
(1) This task is to calculate the freeplay of the horizontal stabilizer (Figure 604). The freeplay is
measured individually at three support locations that support the weight of the horizontal
stabilizer: the jackscrew, the Left Hand Side (LHS) pivot hinge, and the Right Hand Side (RHS)
pivot hinge. A total freeplay value will then be calculated using the freeplay values of the three
locations.
(2) All three supports are under load due to the horizontal stabilizer static weight. To measure the
freeplay at a support, an adequate amount of reverse load is needed. Weights are placed on
top of the front spar area to create the required reverse load at the support where the freeplay
is to be measured. Weights such as shotbags and persons are used as examples in this
procedure.
NOTE: The user has the option to use other types of weights in the procedure.
(3) The freeplay is measured using a displacement gauge, such as a dial indicator, STD-1238, to
check the movement (or slack) at the support mechanism when the load at the support is
reversed.
NOTE: The user has the option to use other types of displacement gauges to replace the
following tools in the procedure:
• dial indicator, STD-1238
• mount, STD-1279
(4) For the LHS pivot hinge or the RHS pivot hinge freeplay measurement, a table is provided to
calculate each individual weight’s contribution to the total reverse load. A total of 2500 ± 200
lbs of reverse load is required. This table is intended to facilitate the user in the placement of
weights to meet the required reverse load at the pivot hinge support where the freeplay is to be
measured (Table 601).
(5) For the jackscrew freeplay measurement, two sets of weights of a total of 1000 ± 40 lbs (500 ±
20 lbs per set) are required. The weights are applied in the area of the front spar of the
horizontal stabilizer.
(6) For this task, only these dimensions will be used:
(a) Linear dimensions are in inches (in.)
(b) Weights are in pounds (lbs.)
NOTE: The tolerances of the pivot hinge total reverse load and the total jackscrew weights are
provided. The variation of individual weights and distance measurements must meet
those tolerances given.

G. Horizontal Stabilizer Freeplay Inspection
SUBTASK 27-09-91-220-023
(1) Do a check of the freeplay for the pivot hinges (LHS and RHS) of the stabilizer center section
(Figure 605).
(a) Measure the freeplay of the LHS pivot hinge (D1):
1) Attach a dial indicator, STD-1238, with a mount, STD-1279, to the LHS of the
fuselage at the Body Station 1156 pivot bulkhead (Figure 605 (Sheet 1), View A).
a) Make sure that the plunger of the dial indicator, STD-1238, is approximately
perpendicular to the stabilizer lower surface where it contacts the LHS
retainer.
b) Position the dial indicator, STD-1238, to allow for subsequent plunger
extension and dial travel of 0.13 inches minimum.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
2) Set the dial indicator, STD-1238, to zero.
NOTE: Movement of equipment or personnel inside the fuselage can cause
inaccuracy with the dial indicator readings. The dial indicator, STD-1238,
should be stable at zero before weight application.
3) Gently place weights on top of the RHS stabilizer front spar in the area shown
(Figure 605 (Sheet 3)).
a) Protect the upper surface of the horizontal stabilizer as necessary to make
sure that the weights do not cause damage.
b) Apply weights per the "Weight Application Requirements and Calculation of
Total Reverse Load (For Pivot Hinge Freeplay Measurements Only)" section of
this task.
4) Record the measurement of the extension of the plunger of the dial indicator,
STD-1238 as "D1".
NOTE: Movement of equipment or personnel inside the fuselage can cause
inaccuracy with the dial indicator readings. The dial indicator, STD-1238,
should show a stable reading when recording the freeplay measurement.
5) Gently remove the weights from the RHS stabilizer.
6) Make sure that the dial indicator value returns to 0 ± 0.003 inch.
a) If this is not met, check the plunger contact, mount, and function of the dial
indicator, STD-1238, to troubleshoot.
b) If this is not met, redo the freeplay check of the LHS pivot hinge.
7) Remove the dial indicator, STD-1238, and mount, STD-1279, from the LHS of the
fuselage.
(b) Measure the freeplay of the RHS pivot hinge (D2):
1) Attach a dial indicator, STD-1238, with a mount, STD-1279, to the RHS of the
fuselage at the Body Station 1156 pivot bulkhead (Figure 605 (Sheet 1), View A).
a) Make sure that the plunger of the dial indicator, STD-1238, is approximately
perpendicular to the stabilizer lower surface where it contacts the RHS
retainer.
b) Position the dial indicator, STD-1238, to allow for subsequent plunger
extension and dial travel of 0.13 inches minimum.
2) Set the dial indicator, STD-1238, to zero.
NOTE: Movement of equipment or personnel inside the fuselage can cause
inaccuracy with the dial indicator readings. The dial indicator, STD-1238,
should be stable at zero before weight application.
3) Gently place weights on top of the LHS stabilizer front spar in the area shown
(Figure 605 (Sheet 3)).
a) Protect the upper surface of the horizontal stabilizer as necessary to make
sure that the weights do not cause damage.
b) Apply weights per the "Weight Application Requirements and Calculation of
Total Reverse Load (For Pivot Hinge Freeplay Measurements Only)" section of
this task.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
4) Record the measurement of the extension of the plunger of the dial indicator,
STD-1238 as "D2".
NOTE: Movement of equipment or personnel inside the fuselage can cause
inaccuracy with the dial indicator readings. The dial indicator, STD-1238,
should show a stable reading when recording the freeplay measurement.
5) Gently remove the weights from the LHS stabilizer.
6) Make sure that the dial indicator value returns to 0 ± 0.003 inch.
a) If this is not met, check the plunger contact, mount, and function of the dial
indicator, STD-1238, to troubleshoot.
b) If this is not met, redo the freeplay check of the RHS pivot hinge.
7) Remove the dial indicator, STD-1238, and mount, STD-1279, from the RHS of the
fuselage.
SUBTASK 27-09-91-220-024
(2) Do a check of the freeplay for the stabilizer jackscrew (Figure 607).
(a) Measure the freeplay of the stabilizer jackscrew (D3):
1) Make sure that the stabilizer is at 4 units of trim.
2) Attach a dial indicator, STD-1238, with a mount, STD-1279, to the Body Station
1088 bulkhead structure (Figure 607, View B).
a) Make sure that the plunger of the dial indicator, STD-1238, is approximately
perpendicular to the surface where it contacts the stabilizer center section
(Texas Star structure).
b) Position the dial indicator, STD-1238, to allow for subsequent plunger
contraction and dial travel of 0.13 inches minimum.
3) Set the dial indicator, STD-1238, to zero.
NOTE: Movement of equipment or personnel inside the fuselage can cause
inaccuracy with the dial indicator readings. The dial indicator, STD-1238,
should be stable at zero before weight application.
4) Gently place weights on top of the LHS and RHS stabilizer front spars (Figure 607,
View C).
a) Protect the upper surface of the horizontal stabilizer as necessary to make
sure that the weights do not cause damage.
b) Place weights within the weight application area shown. Distribute the weights
to avoid localized high pressure at contact.
5) Record the measurement of the contraction of the plunger of the dial indicator,
STD-1238, as "D3".
NOTE: Movement of equipment or personnel inside the fuselage can cause
inaccuracy with the dial indicator readings. The dial indicator, STD-1238,
should show a stable reading when recording the freeplay measurement.
6) Gently remove the weights from the LHS and RHS stabilizers.
7) Make sure that the dial indicator value returns to 0 ± 0.003 inch.
a) If this is not met, check the plunger contact, mount, and function of the dial
indicator, STD-1238, to troubleshoot.
b) If this is not met, redo the freeplay check of the stabilizer jackscrew.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
8) Remove the dial indicator, STD-1238, and mount, STD-1279, from the Body Station
1088 bulkhead structure.
SUBTASK 27-09-91-220-025
(3) Calculate the total freeplay, referred as “H”, of the horizontal stabilizer:
(a) Use the values D1, D2, and D3 to calculate H:
H = 1.25 × D3 + [(D1 + D2)/2]
SUBTASK 27-09-91-220-026
(4) Do a check of the D1, D2, D3, and H values:
(a) If the "D1" value is more than 0.066 inch, then replace the LHS bearing.
1) Remove the hinge fitting. Do this task: Horizontal Stabilizer Center Section Hinge
Fitting Removal, TASK 27-41-31-000-802.
2) Make sure that the bearing is replaced and that other related parts are serviceable.
3) Install a new or serviceable hinge fitting. Do this task: Horizontal Stabilizer Center
Section Hinge Fitting Installation, TASK 27-41-31-400-802.
(b) If the "D2" value is more than 0.066 inch, then replace the RHS bearing.
1) Remove the hinge fitting. Do this task: Horizontal Stabilizer Center Section Hinge
Fitting Removal, TASK 27-41-31-000-802.
2) Make sure that the bearing is replaced and that other related parts are serviceable.
3) Install a new or serviceable hinge fitting. Do this task: Horizontal Stabilizer Center
Section Hinge Fitting Installation, TASK 27-41-31-400-802.
(c) If the "D3" value is more than 0.056 inch, then replace the stabilizer ball nut, ballscrew,
and jackscrew gearbox.
1) Remove the stabilizer ball nut, ballscrew, and jackscrew gearbox. Do this task:
Stabilizer Ball Nut and Jackscrew Gearbox Removal, TASK 27-41-81-000-801.
2) Install the new or serviceable stabilizer ball nut, ballscrew, and jackscrew gearbox.
Do this task: Stabilizer Ball Nut and Jackscrew Gearbox Installation,
TASK 27-41-81-400-801.
(d) If the "H" value is more than 0.078 inch, then do one or both of the following replacement
options as necessary:
1) Replace the bearings at both the LHS and RHS pivot hinge support (Horizontal
Stabilizer Center Section Hinge Fitting Removal, TASK 27-41-31-000-802 and
Horizontal Stabilizer Center Section Hinge Fitting Installation,
TASK 27-41-31-400-802) and other related parts that are not serviceable.
2) Replace the stabilizer ball nut, ballscrew, and jackscrew gearbox (Stabilizer Ball Nut
and Jackscrew Gearbox Removal, TASK 27-41-81-000-801 and Stabilizer Ball Nut
and Jackscrew Gearbox Installation, TASK 27-41-81-400-801).
NOTE: Fleet history shows that the hinge bearings wear significantly more than the
jackscrew does, and this should be considered when making repairs to
restore “H” to within limits.
(5) If any replacement(s) are done to restore D1, D2, D3, and H values to be within their
respective limits, then perform the horizontal stabilizer freeplay inspection procedure again for
verification.
(6) Record the inspection date and the following data of the freeplay check in a history log:
(a) D1, D2, D3, and H values.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) Any replaced parts when restoring D1, D2, D3, and H values to be within their respective
limits.
H. Weight Application Requirements and Calculation of Total Reverse Load (For Pivot Hinge
Freeplay Measurements Only)
(Figure 606)
NOTE: This section is for providing additional information on how to apply weights and calculate the
total reverse load.
SUBTASK 27-09-91-220-027
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT THE WEIGHTS ARE STABLE AND SAFELY SET. DO NOT
LET PERSONNEL IN THE AREA BELOW THE STABILIZER. IF YOU DO NOT
OBEY, THE WEIGHTS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE
TO THE AIRCRAFT.
(1) Apply enough weights during Pivot Hinge Freeplay Inspections so that a Total Reverse Load of
2500 ± 200 lbs is achieved (Figure 605 (Sheet 3)).
NOTE: Make sure that proper fall protection is in place when personnel are used as weights.
The weight per person should not exceed 220 lbs.
(a) Make sure that any weights used have a base area to contact the stabilizer with in order
to avoid localized loading point. Soft padding, if needed, can be used to distribute the
load and protect the surface of the horizontal stabilizer.
(b) For any type of weights applied, make sure that the pressure at the contact area is less
than 4 psi average.
SUBTASK 27-09-91-940-001
(2) Locate Point 0 on the horizontal stabilizer upper surface.
(a) Point 0 is the upper aft and inboard corner of the leading edge (LE) skin common to LE
Station 198.23.
SUBTASK 27-09-91-970-001
(3) For each weight (or stack of weights) applied, do the following:
(a) Record the weight (or total of the stacked weights) in pounds.
(b) Record the distance in inches.
NOTE: This is the distance between Point 0 and the Center of Gravity (CG) of the
applied weight (or stack of weights), along the direction of the front spar
centerline.
(c) If the CG of the individual weight (or individual stack of weights) cannot be placed along
the front spar, it is acceptable to shift the weight(s) in the AFT direction, so long as the
CG of the weight(s) is approximately positioned atop an inspar rib.
SUBTASK 27-09-91-970-002
(4) Calculate the Total Reverse Load using the table below:
NOTE: In the Total Reverse Load table, weight and distance must be recorded in pounds and
inches. Using metric values will cause the calculated Total Reverse Load to be in error.

E. Spoiler Inspection
SUBTASK 27-09-91-220-012
(1) Do a check of the freeplay for spoilers No. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 12 (Figure 609):
CAUTION
PUT SUFFICIENT PADDING BETWEEN THE FORCE SCALE, AND THE
CONTROL SURFACE TO PREVENT DAMAGE TO THE CONTROL
SURFACE. THE FORCE SCALE CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE
CONTROL SURFACE.
(a) Use a force gauge, COM-1557, and apply approximately 21 lbf (93.41 N), 0.5 in.
(12.70 mm) forward of the spoiler trailing edge and directly opposite of the power control
actuator.
NOTE: The up force of approximately 21 lbf (93.41 N) consists of the spoiler panel
weight of 16 lb (7.26 kg) plus 5 lbf (22.24 N) push force.
(b) Measure the freeplay on the inboard edge of the spoiler not more than 0.5 in. (12.70 mm)
from the trailing edge.
(c) Make sure that the spoiler freeplay is not more than 0.1 in. (2.54 mm).
SUBTASK 27-09-91-220-013
(2) Do a check of the freeplay for spoilers No. 6 and 7 (graphite/composite):
CAUTION
PUT SUFFICIENT PADDING BETWEEN THE FORCE SCALE, AND THE
CONTROL SURFACE TO PREVENT DAMAGE TO THE CONTROL
SURFACE. THE FORCE SCALE CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE
CONTROL SURFACE.
(a) Use a force gauge, COM-1557, and apply an up force of approximately 32 lbf (142.34 N),
0.5 in. (12.70 mm) forward of the spoiler trailing edge and at the middle between the two
spoiler power control actuators.
NOTE: The up force of approximately 32 lbf (142.34 N) consists of the spoiler panel
weight of 27 lb (12.25 kg) plus 5 lbf (22.24 N) push force.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) Measure the freeplay on the inboard edge of the spoiler not more than 0.5 in. (12.70 mm)
from the trailing edge.
(c) Make sure that the spoiler freeplay is not more than 0.2 in. (5.08 mm).

E. Pressure from the Aileron Hydraulic Systems A and B - Deactivation
WARNING
YOU MUST REMOVE PRESSURE FROM THE AILERON HYDRAULIC
SYSTEMS A AND B BEFORE YOU DO MAINTENANCE ON THE AILERON
CONTROL SYSTEM. THIS IS TO PREVENT INJURY TO PERSONS, AND
DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT BECAUSE OF ACCIDENTAL OPERATION OF
THE AILERONS.
SUBTASK 27-11-00-860-001
(1) Remove pressure from the aileron hydraulic systems A and B.
(a) Set the FLT CONTROL A and B switches on the forward overhead panel, P5, to the OFF
position.
(b) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2
Row Col Number Name
B 13 C00363 FLIGHT CONT SHUTOFF VALVES FLT CONT
C 13 C01074 FLIGHT CONT SHUTOFF VALVES FLT CONT
(c) Set the ELEC 2, HYD PUMPS A and ELEC 1, HYD PUMPS B switches on the forward
overhead panel, P5, to the OFF position.
(d) Operate the rudder pedals to decrease the remaining hydraulic system pressure.
SUBTASK 27-11-00-860-119
(2) If it is necessary to open a hydraulic line, release pressure from the reservoir for the applicable
hydraulic system (TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or TASK 29-09-00-860-808).
SUBTASK 27-11-00-480-001
(3) Install the lock, SPL-1675, on the flight controls shutoff valves for systems A and B.
(a) Disconnect the electrical connectors from the shutoff valves.
NOTE: For hydraulic system A, the flight control shutoff valve is mounted on inboard side
of hydraulic module A in left main wheel well. For hydraulic system B, the flight
control shutoff valve is mounted on outboard side of hydraulic module B in right
main wheel well.
(b) After you disconnect the electrical connector(s), examine the connector(s) for corrosion.
NOTE: The inspection of the electrical connector(s) can be done after the removal step
or before the installation step of the electrical connector(s). This is an operator
option.
WARNING
DO THE STEPS BELOW IF THE AIRPLANE OPERATES WHERE
DEICING FLUID THAT CONTAINS POTASSIUM FORMATE OR
POTASSIUM ACETATE IS USED. ALSO, DO THE STEPS FOR ALL
AIRPLANES THAT YOU FOUND CORROSION IN THE ELECTRICAL
CONNECTORS IN THE MAIN WHEEL WELL. THE ELECTRICAL
CONNECTORS ARE IN A SYSTEM THAT IS NECESSARY FOR SAFE
FLIGHT.
(c) If there was corrosion, refer to (SWPM 20-60-03) to correct the problem.
(d) Make sure that the manual override levers on the shutoff valves moved to position 2.
(e) Install the lock, SPL-1675, on each shutoff valve.
1) Make sure to install the detent pins.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

Row Col Number Name

27-11-00-820-801Aileron Cables AdjustmentPDF p. 393
2. Aileron Cables Adjustment
(Figure 501, Figure 502)
NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. General
(1) Before you do cable adjustment, permit a minimum of one hour at a constant ambient
temperature of ±5°F (±2.8°C) for the airframe temperature to become stable.
(a) The cable tension values will not be correct when there are temperature differences along
the cable run.
(2) It is recommended that airplanes supplied with the cables that contain higher zinc coating
(Grade D or Grade K) be re-tensioned 3 to 4 months into service. This will bring the tension of
the control cables within the desired range. After the cables are re-tensioned the high zinc
cables (Grade D or Grade K) will continue to relax at a rate that is equivalent to the Grade B
cables. To identify the grade of the cable, refer to the table below:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

*[2] Code 3E is specified only where there is a specific requirement for REDUCED TOLERANCE (RT) percent elongation

*[4] It is not necessary to adjust the Grade D 0.188 (3/16) cables (6J) 3 to 4 months after installation.
(3) It is recommended that cable assemblies on each side of a cable loop be replaced at the same
time using the same cable grade material in order to minimize asymmetric relaxation.
(4) Make sure that you only adjust the applicable aileron cable or cables. The hydraulic brake
cables can be incorrectly identified as the aileron cables.

SUBTASK 27-11-00-820-007
(1) If the rig pin A/S-4 cannot be easily installed and removed or if Power Control Unit (PCU)
movement is observed during hydraulic system cycling, adjust all pogos [1] in the specified
sequence:
NOTE: When adjustment of the four pogos is necessary, make sure you follow these
instructions in the specified sequence. Incorrect adjustment of the upper and lower
pogos on system A or B PCU when adjusted in the opposite directions will cause the
incorrect condition of 'free fit' of rig pin A/S 4.
(a) Disconnect the upper and lower pogos from system B PCU and the upper pogo from
system A PCU.
1) Remove the pins [8], nuts [7], washers [6], bushings [5], washers [4], and bolts [3] to
disconnect the pogos [1] from the power control units.
(b) Adjust the lower (primary) pogo [1] on system A PCU:
NOTE: The initial length of the pogo (rod-end to rod-end) is approximately 13.78 in.
(350.01 mm) and the drain holes are down.
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF
ALL FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS
AND THE LANDING GEAR. THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES,
THE THRUST REVERSERS AND THE LANDING GEAR CAN MOVE
QUICKLY. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE
TO EQUIPMENT.
1) Pressurize hydraulic system A, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization,
TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
2) Loosen the locknut [2] on the pogo [1].
3) Turn the shaft in the barrel and left clevis to adjust the length of the pogo [1] until the
rig pin A/S-4 can be freely installed and removed from the aileron bus drum.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
4) Tighten the locknut [2] to 62.5 ±12.5 in-lb (7.1 ±1.4 N·m).
5) Make sure that the rig pin A/S-4 can be freely installed and removed.
a) If it is necessary, adjust the lower pogo [1] on system A PCU again.
6) Remove power from hydraulic system A, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B
Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805.
7) Make sure that the bushing flanges on the left hand clevis are pointed up, and the
drain hole in the clevis barrel is pointed down, when the clevis is re-connected.
8) Install MS20995NC40 lockwire, G02436, on the locknut [2].
(c) Adjust the lower (primary) pogo on system B PCU;
NOTE: You must adjust the lower pogo on system A PCU first before you adjust the
lower pogo on system B PCU.
1) Install the bolt [3], washer [4], bushing [5], washer [6], nut [7], and pin [8] to connect
the lower pogo to the system B PCU.
NOTE: The initial length of the pogo (rod-end to rod-end) is approximately 13.78 in.
(350.01 mm).
a) Make sure that the drain holes on the pogo [1] are down.
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF
ALL FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS
AND THE LANDING GEAR. THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES,
THE THRUST REVERSERS AND THE LANDING GEAR CAN MOVE
QUICKLY. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE
TO EQUIPMENT.

(d) Adjust the upper (secondary) pogo [1] on system A PCU:
