E. Aileron Balance Tab Adjustment
NOTE: You can adjust the aileron balance tab with the aileron in the faired position or with the
aileron at the downrig position.
NOTE: Measurements can also be taken with protractor, SPL-1682, if needed.
SUBTASK 27-11-00-820-017
(1) Do these steps to check the aileron balance tab [31] with the aileron [32] in the faired position:
(a) Align the lower surface of the aileron trailing edge flush with the lower trailing edge
surface of the adjacent fixed wing structure to ±0.03 inch (±0.8 millimeter) at the outboard
end of the aileron [32].
(b) Make sure that the outboard lower trailing edge surface of the aileron balance tab [31]
aligns with the lower trailing edge surface of the aileron [32] to ±0.03 inch (±0.8
millimeter).
1) If this condition is not met, adjust the aileron balance tab [31].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-11-00-220-002
(2) Do these steps to check the aileron balance tab [31] with the aileron [32] in the downrig
position (Figure 506):
NOTE: The aileron rig position is measured 3.0 ±0.1 in. (76.2 ±2.5 mm) forward of the aft,
inboard corner of the fixed lower panel, and 3.0 ±0.1 in. (76.2 ±2.5 mm) forward of the
aft, outboard corner of the aileron. At this location, the distance between the lower
surface of the fixed lower panel and lower surface of the aileron should be
0.19 ±0.03 in. (4.83 ±0.76 mm).
(a) Measure the vertical distance between the lower surface of the aileron balance tab [31] to
the lower surface of the aileron [32] at the outboard end of the aileron balance tab [31]
(dimension A) (Figure 504):
NOTE: You must measure the distance from the lower aft most points of the aileron
balance tab and aileron.
1) Make sure that the dimension A is 0.060 ±0.070 in. (1.52 ±1.78 mm).
(b) If the dimension A is out of tolerance, adjust the aileron balance tab [31].
SUBTASK 27-11-00-820-011
(3) Do these steps to adjust the aileron balance tab [31]:
(a) Move the aileron trailing edge to the down position.
(b) Remove the bolts [45] that attach the forward removable fairing [46] to the aileron [32].
(c) Remove the bolts [43] that attach the aft removable fairing [44] to the aileron balance
tab [31].
(d) Loosen the jam nuts [47] and jam nuts [49] on the aileron tab control rods [33].
NOTE: You must adjust the two aileron tab control rods the same amount.
(e) Do these steps if coarse adjustment is necessary:
1) Remove the pins [42], nuts [41], washers [40], bushings [39], washers [38], and
bolts [37] to disconnect the aileron tab control rods [33] from the aileron balance
tab [31].
2) Turn the rod ends on the tab control rods [33] for adjustment.
NOTE: One-half turn of the rod end changes the position of the tab trailing edge
0.067 in. (1.7 mm). One-half turn of the rod end and barrel together
changes the position of the tab trailing edge 0.080 in. (2.0 mm).
a) To raise the trailing edge of the aileron balance tab [31], lengthen the aileron
tab control rods [33].
b) To lower the trailing edge of the aileron balance tab [31], shorten the aileron
tab control rods [33].
3) Connect the aileron tab control rods [33] to the aileron balance tab [31].
a) Install the bushings [39], washers [38], washers [40], bolts [37], and nuts [41].
b) If there is binding between the aileron tab control rods [33] and bolt [37], adjust
the length of the aileron tab control rods [33].
c) Make sure that there is a minimum of 0.0150 in. (0.38 mm) gap between the
bushing [39] and washer [38].
d) Tighten the nuts [41] to 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m) - 80 in-lb (9.0 N·m).
e) Install the pins [42].
(f) Do these steps if fine adjustment is necessary:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Turn the barrels [48] on the aileron tab control rods [33].
NOTE: One turn of the barrel, with the rod end fixed, changes the position of the
tab trailing edge 0.027 in. (0.69 mm).
a) To raise the trailing edge of the aileron balance tab [31], lengthen the aileron
tab control rods [33].
b) To lower the trailing edge of the aileron balance tab [31], shorten the aileron
tab control rod [33].
2) Make sure that the threads are visible in the inspection holes in the barrel [48].
(g) Tighten the jam nuts [47] to 100 in-lb (11.3 N·m) - 140 in-lb (15.8 N·m).
(h) Tighten the jam nuts [49] to 80 in-lb (9.0 N·m) - 100 in-lb (11.3 N·m).
(i) Install the bolts [43] that attach the aft removable fairing [44] to the aileron balance
tab [31].
(j) Install the bolts [45] that attach the forward removable fairing [46] to the aileron [32].

(3) Measure the control wheel breakout force in the clockwise and counterclockwise directions:
(a) Install the adapter, SPL-1674 to the captain's control wheel.

(c) Install the mount, SPL-1670 and the protractor, SPL-1680 to the first officer's control

(e) Turn the control wheel clockwise until the aileron starts to move.
1) Using a push/pull scale 0-25 pound (0-11 kilogram), STD-753. Make sure the force

4.5 pounds (20.0 newtons).
(f) Release the control wheel.

EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Using a push/pull scale 0-25 pound (0-11 kilogram), STD-753. Make sure the force
to turn the control wheel is not more than 29.0 pound-inches (3.2 newton-meters) or
4.5 pounds (20.0 newtons).
SUBTASK 27-11-00-820-021
(4) If the control wheels center properly, and breakout forces are within the limits above, then no
adjustment is necessary.
SUBTASK 27-11-00-820-013
(5) If the control wheels are not in the center or the breakout forces are out of tolerance, adjust the
tension of the springs [63] on the centering unit [61]:
(a) Hold the eyebolt [66] while you tighten or loosen the nut [65] in 1/2 turn increments.
NOTE: You must tighten the two eyebolts [66] equally. Tighten the eyebolts [66] to
increase the spring forces. Loosen the eyebolts [66] to decrease the spring
forces.
(b) Adjust the nut [65] until the force to turn the control wheel is not more than 29.0
pound-inches (3.3 newton-meters) or 4.5 pounds (20.0 newtons).
(c) Tighten the checknuts [64].
(d) Make sure the shaft [70] can turn freely.
SUBTASK 27-11-00-750-001
(6) After adjustment of breakout forces above, do the following steps to do a check of the breakout
forces and make sure the control wheel is centered properly:
(a) Turn the control wheel clockwise until the aileron starts to move.
1) Make sure the force to turn the control wheel is not more than 29.0 pound-inches
(3.3 newton-meters) or 4.5 pounds (20.0 newtons).
(b) Release the control wheel.
1) Make sure the control wheel goes back to the neutral position in 0.0 ±0.4 units of
trim (2.4 degrees).
(c) Turn the control wheel counterclockwise until the aileron starts to move.
1) Make sure the force to turn the control wheel is not more than 29.0 pound-inches
(3.3 newton-meters) or 4.5 pounds (20.0 newtons).
(d) Release the control wheel.
1) Make sure the control wheel goes back to the neutral position in 0.0 ±0.4 units of
trim (2.4 degrees).

F. Check of the Aileron System Adjustment
SUBTASK 27-11-00-820-014
(1) Do a check of the aileron system adjustment.
(a) Attach the straight edge, SPL-1671, on the captain's and first officer's control wheels.
(b) Make sure that a rig pin A/S-4, from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, can be freely installed
in the aileron bus drum (Figure 501).
1) If a rig pin A/S-4 cannot be freely installed, do this task: Pogo and Power Control
Unit (PCU) Adjustment, TASK 27-11-00-820-802.
(c) Remove rig pin A/S-4 from the aileron bus drum.
(d) Remove the straight edge, SPL-1671, from the captain's and first officer's control wheels.
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE
FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE
LANDING GEAR. THE CONTROL SURFACES, THE THRUST
REVERSERS AND THE LANDING GEAR CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WITH
THE PRESSURIZATION OF A HYDRAULIC SYSTEM. THIS CAN CAUSE
INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(e) Pressurize hydraulic systems A and B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B
Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
(f) Operate the aileron trim switches, on the P8 control stand panel, until the rig pin A/S-15
from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, can be freely installed and removed (Figure 501).
(g) Make sure that the captain's control wheel is the center of the neutral position.
1) Gently move the control wheel in the backlash band.
2) Make sure that the center of the backlash band aligns with the protractor zero
position.
(h) Make sure that the index mark on the captain's control wheel aligns with the zero mark on
the control column.
(i) Attach the straight edge, SPL-1671, on the captain's and first officer's control wheels.
(j) Make sure that the top ends of the control wheels touch the straight edge, SPL-1671.
(k) Make sure that one end of the first officer's control wheel is no more than 0.20 in.
(5.1 mm) from the straight edge, SPL-1671.
1) If the control wheels do not align, adjust the cables ACBA/ACBB, do this task:
Aileron Cables Adjustment, TASK 27-11-00-820-801.
(l) Make sure that these rig pins from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, can be freely installed
and removed (Figure 501):
NOTE: Install these rig pins at the same time.
1) Rig pins A/S-1 and A/S-1A at the forward drum
2) Rig pin A/S-3 in the aileron input crank
3) Rig pin A/S-4 in the aileron bus drum
4) Rig pin A/S-15 in the aileron trim actuator.
(m) If the above rig pins cannot be freely installed and removed, adjust the cables AA and AB,
do this task: Aileron Cables Adjustment, TASK 27-11-00-820-801.
(n) Remove the straight edge, SPL-1671, from the captain's and first officer's control wheels.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(o) Make sure that the aileron is in the rig position (Figure 506).
NOTE: The aileron rig position is measured 3.0 ±0.1 in. (76.2 ±2.5 mm) forward of the
aft, inboard corner of the fixed lower panel, and 3.0 ±0.1 in. (76.2 ±2.5 mm)
forward of the aft, outboard corner of the aileron. At this location, the distance
between the lower surface of the fixed lower panel and the lower surface of the
aileron should be 0.19 ±0.03 in. (4.83 ±0.76 mm).
1) If the aileron is not in the rig position, adjust the cables ABSA and ABSB, do this
task: Aileron Cables Adjustment, TASK 27-11-00-820-801.
(p) Make sure that the aileron balance tab aligns with the aileron.
1) Measure the distance between the rig position of the aileron balance tab [31] to the
aileron lower surface (dimension A) at these three positions (Figure 504):
NOTE: You must measure from the lower aft most point of the aileron balance tab.
a) At the outboard end of the aileron balance tab, make sure that the dimension
A is 0.06 ±0.07 in. (1.5 ±1.8 mm) or 0.82 ±0.25 degrees.
b) At the middle point along the aileron balance tab, make sure that the
dimension A is 0.065 ±0.070 in. (1.7 ±1.8 mm) or 0.60 ±0.25 degrees.
c) At the inboard end of the aileron balance tab, make sure that the dimension A
is 0.07 ±0.07 in. (1.8 ±1.8 mm) or 0.34 ±0.25 degrees.

Balance Tab Adjustment, TASK 27-11-00-820-803.

E. Do a Test of the Aileron Friction and Motion
SUBTASK 27-11-00-720-001
(1) Do a test of the aileron friction and motion:
NOTE: During this test, the force is positive (+) if you need to push the aileron to get it to a
specified position. The force is negative (-) if you need to hold the aileron to keep it at
a specified position.
(a) Move the aileron surface to the rig position and release.
NOTE: The aileron rig position is measured 3.0 ±0.1 in. (76.2 ±2.5 mm) forward of the
aft, inboard corner of the fixed lower panel, and 3.0 ±0.1 in. (76.2 ±2.5 mm)
forward of the aft, outboard corner of the aileron. At this location, the distance
between the lower surface of the fixed lower panel and the lower surface of the
aileron should be 0.19 ±0.03 in. (4.83 ±0.76 mm) (Figure 506 (Sheet 2)).
(b) If the aileron moves away from the rig position, do these steps:
1) Hold the aileron at the rig position with a force scale at 8.75 ±0.50 in.
(222.3 ±12.7 mm) aft of the hinge centerline and perpendicular to the aileron chord
plane. (held negative (-) force)
2) Slowly apply or relax the force as it is necessary until the aileron moves up and
down from the rig position.
a) Measure the force that is necessary to move the aileron up (up positive (+)
force).
b) Measure the force that is necessary to move the aileron down (down positive
(+) force).
3) Add the up force with the down force.
NOTE: Add the forces with the same signs. Subtract forces with the opposite signs.
4) Make sure the total of the two values is not more than 5 lbf (22.2 N).
(c) If the aileron does not move away from the rig position, do these steps;
1) Slowly apply a force perpendicular to the aileron chord plane 8.75 ±0.50 in.
(222.3 ±12.7 mm) aft of the hinge centerline.
2) Measure the force that is necessary to move the aileron up (up force).
3) Measure the force that is necessary to move the aileron down (down force).
4) Add the up force with the down force.
NOTE: Add the forces with the same signs. Subtract forces with the opposite signs.
5) Make sure the total of the two forces is not more than 5 lbf (22.2 N).
(d) Measure the maximum positive force necessary to move the aileron to these specified
positions:
1) Make sure that the aileron moves smoothly throughout its travel, and that there is
no binding at the aileron hinges and seals.
2) Move the aileron from the rig position to the full down position.
3) Move the aileron from the full down position to the full up position.
4) Move the aileron from the full up position to the rig position.
(e) Make sure the force is not more than 13 lbf (58 N) for aileron down.
(f) Make sure the force is not more than 3 lbf (13 N) aileron up.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(g) Measure the aileron travel before the aileron touches the wing structure at the upper and
lower limits of travel.
NOTE: Apply only enough force to maintain contact while you measure the aileron travel.
1) Make sure the aileron travels a minimum of 3.67 in. (93.2 mm) up before the aileron
touches the structure.
2) Make sure the aileron travels a minimum of 3.15 in. (80.0 mm) down before the
aileron touches the structure.

E. Manual Reversion Control Friction Test
SUBTASK 27-11-00-730-001
(1) Do the manual reversion control friction test:
(a) Use the torque wrench, STD-1019 on the adapter, SPL-1674 to measure the force that is
necessary to turn the captain's control wheels in the clockwise direction.
NOTE: If the adapter, SPL-1674 is not available, apply a tangent force to the captain's
control wheel at 6.5 in. (165 mm) radius.
1) Turn the control wheel clockwise until the ailerons start to move.
a) Make sure the force is not more than 33.1 lbf (147.2 N) or a torque of 215 in-lb
(24.3 N·m).
2) Continue to turn the control wheel to 20 degrees.
a) Make sure the force is not more than 37.4 lbf (166.4 N) or a torque of 243 in-lb
(27.5 N·m).
3) Continue to turn the control wheel to 40 degrees.
a) Make sure the force is not more than 42.9 lbf (190.8 N) or a torque of 279 in-lb
(31.5 N·m).
4) Continue to turn the control wheel to 75 degrees.
a) Make sure the force is not more than 51.2 lbf (227.7 N) or a torque of 333 in-lb
(37.6 N·m).
(b) Measure the force that is necessary to turn the captain's control wheel in the
counterclockwise direction.
NOTE: If the adapter, SPL-1674 is not available, apply a tangent force to the captain's
control wheel at 6.5 in. (165 mm) radius.
1) Turn the control wheel counterclockwise until the ailerons start to move.
a) Make sure the force is not more than 33.1 lbf (147.2 N) or a torque of 215 in-lb
(24.3 N·m).
2) Continue to turn the control wheel to 20 degrees.
a) Make sure the force is not more than 37.4 lbf (166.4 N) or a torque of 243 in-lb
(27.5 N·m).
3) Continue to turn the control wheel to 40 degrees.
a) Make sure the force is not more than 42.9 lbf (190.8 N) or a torque of 279 in-lb
(31.5 N·m).
4) Continue to turn the control wheel to 75 degrees.
a) Make sure the force is not more than 51.2 lbf (227.7 N) or a torque of 333 in-lb
(37.6 N·m).

D. Do the Aileron Response (Operational) Test
SUBTASK 27-11-00-710-002
(1) Do the aileron response test:
(a) Turn the aileron control wheel through full travel in each direction from the neutral
position.
1) Make sure the ailerons can move smoothly through the full range of travel.
(b) Remove pressure from the hydraulic system A, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B
Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805.
(c) Turn the aileron control wheel clockwise from the neutral position.
1) Make sure the trailing edges of the left aileron moves down and the aileron tab
moves up.
2) Make sure the trailing edges of the right aileron moves up and the aileron tab
moves down.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(d) Turn the aileron control wheel counterclockwise from the neutral position.
1) Make sure the trailing edges of the left aileron moves up and the aileron tab moves
down.
2) Make sure the trailing edges of the right aileron moves down and the aileron tab
moves up.
(e) Remove pressure from the hydraulic system B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B
Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805.
(f) Pressurize the hydraulic system A, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization,
TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
(g) Turn the aileron control wheel clockwise from the neutral position.
1) Make sure the trailing edges of the left aileron moves down and the aileron tab
moves up.
2) Make sure the trailing edges of the right aileron moves up and the aileron tab
moves down.
(h) Turn the aileron control wheel counterclockwise from the neutral position.
1) Make sure the trailing edges of the left aileron moves up and the aileron tab moves
down.
2) Make sure the trailing edges of the right aileron moves down and the aileron tab
moves up.

C. Prepare for the Check
SUBTASK 27-11-00-860-043
WARNING
MAKE SURE ALL PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT
CONTROLS SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING
GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY

D. Control Wheel Centering Check
SUBTASK 27-11-00-720-003
(1) Do the centering check:
(a) Turn the captain's control wheel clockwise from the neutral position (zero units) to 6 units
of trim.
(b) Turn the captain's control wheel back to 2 units of trim and release the control wheel.
(c) Make sure the control wheel goes back to the neutral position in 0.0 ±0.4 units of trim
(±2.4 degrees).
(d) Turn the captain's control wheel counterclockwise from the neutral position (zero units) to
6 units of trim.
(e) Turn the captain's control wheel back to 2 units of trim and release the control wheel.
(f) Make sure the control wheel goes back to the neutral position in 0.0 ±0.4 units of trim
(±2.4 degrees).

E. Do a Test of the Control Wheel Force
SUBTASK 27-11-00-730-002
(1) Do a check of the control wheel force:
(a) Set the indicator on the protractor, SPL-1680 to zero degrees.
(b) Turn the control wheel clockwise until the aileron starts to move.
1) Make sure the force to turn the control wheel is not more than 29.0 in-lb (3.3 N·m)
or 4.5 lbf (20.02 N).
(c) Continue to turn the control wheel clockwise to 5 degrees.
1) Make sure the force to turn the control wheel is not more than 35.5 in-lb (4.0 N·m)
or 5.5 lbf (24.47 N).
(d) Continue to turn the control wheel clockwise to 20 degrees.
1) Make sure the force to turn the control wheel is not more than 56.0 in-lb (6.3 N·m)
or 8.5 lbf (37.81 N).
(e) Continue to turn the control wheel clockwise to 40 degrees.
1) Make sure the force to turn the control wheel is not more than 89.5 in-lb (10.1 N·m)
or 14 lbf (62.28 N).
(f) Continue to turn the control wheel clockwise to 75 degrees.
1) Make sure the force to turn the control wheel is not more than 123.5 in-lb (14.0 N·m)
or 19 lbf (84.52 N).
(g) Release the control wheel.
1) Make sure the control wheel goes back to the neutral position.
(h) Turn the control wheel counterclockwise until the aileron starts to move.
1) Make sure the force to turn the control wheel is not more than 29.0 in-lb (3.3 N·m)
or 4.5 lbf (20.02 N).
(i) Continue to turn the control wheel counterclockwise to 5 degrees.
1) Make sure the force to turn the control wheel is not more than 35.5 in-lb (4.0 N·m)
or 5.5 lbf (24.47 N).
(j) Continue to turn the control wheel counterclockwise to 20 degrees.
1) Make sure the force to turn the control wheel is not more than 56.0 in-lb (6.3 N·m)
or 8.5 lbf (37.81 N).
(k) Continue to turn the control wheel counterclockwise to 40 degrees.
1) Make sure the force to turn the control wheel is not more than89.5 in-lb (10.1 N·m)
or 14 lbf (62.28 N).
(l) Continue to turn the control wheel counterclockwise to 75 degrees.
1) Make sure the force to turn the control wheel is not more than 123.5 in-lb (14.0 N·m)
or 19 lbf (84.52 N).
(m) Release the control wheel.
1) Make sure that the control wheel goes back to the neutral position.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

D. Aileron Trim Response Test
SUBTASK 27-11-00-860-048
(1) Do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811.
SUBTASK 27-11-00-860-049
WARNING
MAKE SURE ALL PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT
CONTROLS SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING
GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY
HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(2) Pressurize hydraulic systems A and B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization,
TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
SUBTASK 27-11-00-860-050
(3) Make sure you can freely install and remove the rig pin A/S-15, from the rigging pin kit,
SPL-1585, in the aileron trim actuator.
SUBTASK 27-11-00-480-023
(4) Install the adapter, SPL-1674 to the captain's control wheel.
NOTE: If the adapter is not available, put a tangent force to the captain's control wheel at a
6.5 inch (165 millimeters) radius.
SUBTASK 27-11-00-020-011
(5) Remove the map holder assembly from the first officer's control wheel.
SUBTASK 27-11-00-480-024
(6) Install the mount, SPL-1670 and the protractor, SPL-1680 to the first officer's control wheel.
SUBTASK 27-11-00-730-003
(7) Do a test of the aileron trim response:
(a) Shake the captain's control wheel to put the aileron control system at the center.
(b) Make sure the pointer decal on the captain's and first officer's control wheels aligns with
the aileron trim decal (zero unit) to a tolerance of 0.00 ±0.02 inches (0.00 ±0.5
millimeters).
(c) At the same time, operate the aileron trim switches, on the control stand, in the LEFT
WING DOWN direction until the trim actuator stops.
1) Measure the movement of the captain's and first officer's control wheels from the
neutral position.
2) Make sure the two control wheels turn counterclockwise a minimum of 9.5 trim
indicator units in 25.5 ±3 seconds.
NOTE: When you read the control wheel position - with the trim actuator fully
extended, shake the captain's control wheel to make sure that the control
system is centered in the trim detent.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(d) Move the control wheels to the zero unit position to a tolerance of 0.00 ±0.02 inches (0.0
±0.5 millimeters).
(e) Shake the captain's control wheel to put the aileron control system at the center.
(f) At the same time, operate the aileron trim switches in the RIGHT WING DOWN direction
until the trim actuator stops.
1) Measure the movement of the captain's and first officer's control wheels from the
neutral position.
2) Make sure the two control wheels turn clockwise a minimum of 9.5 trim indicator
units in 25.5 ±3 seconds.
NOTE: When you read the control wheel position - with the trim actuator fully
retracted, shake the captain's control wheel to make sure that the control
system is centered in the trim detent.
(g) Move the aileron trim switches to make sure the aileron trim is at the RIGHT WING
DOWN stop.
(h) Manually turn the captain's control wheel 105 degrees clockwise.
(i) Turn the captain's control wheel back to the neutral position.
(j) Turn and hold the captain's control wheel at 75 degrees counterclockwise.
1) Make sure the control wheel moves freely through travel.
2) Make sure the force to hold the control wheel is not more than 137.0 in-lb
(15.5 N·m) or 21.0 lbf (93.4 N) at 6.5 in. (165 mm) radius.
(k) Release the captain's control wheel.
1) Make sure the control wheel goes back to the trim position of 57 degrees minimum
clockwise.
(l) At the same time, operate the aileron trim switches in the LEFT WING DOWN direction
until the trim actuator stops.
1) Make sure the control wheel turns counterclockwise a minimum of 9.5 trim indicator
units.
(m) Manually turn the captain's control wheel 105 degrees counterclockwise.
(n) Turn the captain's control wheel back to the neutral position.
(o) Turn and hold the captain's control wheel at 75 degrees clockwise.
1) Make sure the control wheel moves freely through travel.
2) Make sure the force to hold the control wheel is not more than 137.0 in-lb
(15.5 N·m) or 21.0 lbf (93.4 N) at 6.5 in. (165 mm) radius.
(p) Release the captain's control wheel.
1) Make sure the control wheel goes back to the trim position of 57 degrees minimum
counterclockwise.
(q) At the same time, operate the aileron trim switches to put the control wheels at
approximately 0 units of trim.
(r) Operate one aileron trim switch in the LEFT WING DOWN direction then the RIGHT
WING DOWN direction.
1) Make sure the control wheels do not move.
(s) Operate the other aileron trim switch in the LEFT WING DOWN direction then the RIGHT
WING DOWN direction.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Make sure the control wheels do not move.

E. Aileron Spring Cartridge and Transfer Mechanism Operational Test
SUBTASK 27-11-00-710-003
(1) Do the operational test of the spring cartridge [17] and transfer mechanism.
(a) Operate the two aileron trim switches to put the aileron control wheels to the neutral (zero
unit) position.
(b) Shake the control wheel to center the aileron system.
(c) Turn the captain's control wheel fully clockwise and hold.
(d) Turn the first officer's control wheel counterclockwise through neutral and beyond 10 units
left aileron, and return the control wheel to neutral.
1) After the initial breakout, the force required to continue wheel movement must
increase steadily and smoothly.
a) Make sure that there is no binding or sudden increase in the force required to
turn the wheel.
2) Make sure that the drain holes on the aileron spring cartridge [17] are down.
3) Make sure that the aileron spring cartridge [17] extends and can move freely while
you turn the control wheel.
(e) Turn the captain's control wheel fully counterclockwise and hold.
(f) Turn the first officer's control wheel clockwise through neutral and beyond 10 units right
aileron, and return the control wheel to neutral.
1) After the initial breakout, the force required to continue wheel movement must
increase steadily and smoothly.
a) Make sure that there is no binding or sudden increase in the force required to
turn the wheel.
2) Make sure that the drain holes on the aileron spring cartridge [17] are down.
3) Make sure that the aileron spring cartridge [17] compresses and can move freely
while you turn the control wheel.
(g) Return the captain's control wheel to neutral.
(h) Put the inspection pin, STD-23326, or equivalent a minimum distance of 0.50 in.
(12.7 mm) into the inspection hole in the aileron input crank [16] to make sure that the
crank [16] does not move on the shaft and the shear rivets in the crank [16] are not
sheared (Figure 501).
NOTE: Any pin or equivalent tool that meets the dimensional requirement is acceptable
to use.
1) If the pin cannot be inserted into the inspection hole minimum 0.50 in. (12.7 mm),
replace the Spoiler Control Quadrant (PAGEBLOCK 27-61-41/401).
(i) Remove the pin from the inspection hole.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
F. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 27-11-00-860-067
(1) Remove power from hydraulic systems A and B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power
Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805.

E. Aileron Spring Cartridge and Transfer Mechanism Functional Test
SUBTASK 27-11-00-720-004
(1) Do the functional test of the aileron spring cartridge [17] and transfer mechanism:
(a) Operate the two aileron trim switches to put the aileron control wheels to the neutral (zero
unit) position.
(b) Shake the control wheel to center the aileron system.
(c) Hold the first officer's control wheel at the neutral position.
(d) Turn the captain's control wheel clockwise to 75 degrees from the neutral position.
1) Make sure the aileron spring cartridge [17] extends while you turn the control wheel.
2) Make sure the maximum breakout force is 67 lbf (298 N) or a torque of 436 in-lb
(49 N·m).
NOTE: The “breakout” force occurs when the captain's control wheel starts to move
with the first officer's control wheel hold in the neutral position.
3) Make sure the maximum force at 75 degrees is 104 lbf (463 N) or a torque of
676 in-lb (76 N·m).
(e) Turn the captain's control wheel counterclockwise to 75 degrees from the neutral position.
1) Make sure the aileron spring cartridge [17] compresses while you turn the control
wheel.
2) Make sure the maximum breakout force is 67 lbf (298 N) or a torque of 436 in-lb
(49 N·m).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
3) Make sure the maximum force at 75 degrees is 104 lbf (463 N) or a torque of
676 in-lb (76 N·m).
(f) Turn and hold the first officer's control wheel clockwise at 80 degrees from the neutral
position.
(g) Turn the captain's control wheel counterclockwise until the transfer mechanism stops
touch.
1) Make sure the captain's control wheel turns a minimum of 138 degrees from the
starting position.
2) Make sure the transfer mechanism can move freely when you turn the control
wheel.
(h) Turn and hold the first officer's control wheel counterclockwise at 80 degrees from the
neutral position.
(i) Turn the captain's control wheel clockwise until the transfer mechanism stops touch.
1) Make sure the captain's control wheel turns a minimum of 138 degrees from the
starting position.
2) Make sure the transfer mechanism can move freely when you turn the control
wheel.
(j) Turn and hold the first officer's control wheel clockwise at 80 degrees from the neutral
position.
(k) Turn the captain's control wheel counterclockwise 130 degrees from the starting position
(80 degrees clockwise).
1) Make sure the aileron spring cartridge [17] compresses and can move freely while
you turn the control wheel.
2) Make sure the maximum force to turn the captain's control wheel is 154 lbf (685 N)
or a torque of 1000 in-lb (113 N·m).
(l) Turn and hold the first officer's control wheel counterclockwise at 80 degrees from the
neutral position.
(m) Turn the captain's control wheel clockwise 130 degrees from the starting position (80
degrees counterclockwise).
1) Make sure the aileron spring cartridge [17] extends and can move freely while you
turn the control wheel.
2) Make sure the maximum force to turn the captain's control wheel is 154 lbf (685 N)
or a torque of 1000 in-lb (113 N·m).
(n) Return both control wheels to neutral.
(o) Put the inspection pin, STD-23326, or equivalent a minimum distance of 0.50 in.
(12.7 mm) into the inspection hole in the aileron input crank [16] (Figure 501) to verify
that the crank has not moved on the shaft and the shear rivets in the crank are not
sheared.
NOTE: Any pin that meets the dimensional requirements is acceptable to use.
1) If the pin cannot be inserted into the inspection hole minimum 0.50 in. (12.7 mm),
replace the Spoiler Control Quadrant (PAGEBLOCK 27-61-41/401).
(p) Remove the pin from the inspection hole.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

SUBTASK 27-11-00-720-005
(4) Do the test of the control wheel travel stop:
(a) Turn the captain's control wheel clockwise until the control wheel stops.
1) Make sure the first officer's control wheel turns a minimum of 105 degrees.
NOTE: A minimum of 105 degrees control wheel travel is required for the captain's
control wheel to touch the forward stop. This large deflection can be
necessary for certain flight conditions in manual reversion.
The system reaches the aft quadrant stop at approximately 90 degrees.
Additional force will be necessary to stretch the control cable past 90
degrees until the control wheel stops.
(b) Turn the captain's control wheel counterclockwise until the control wheel stops.
1) Make sure the first officer's control wheel moves freely and turns a minimum of 105
degrees.
NOTE: Turn the control wheel 105 degrees clockwise to make sure the minimum
travel requirements of the control wheel are met and that there are no
obstructions in the control column and control wheel installations. A
minimum of 105 degrees control wheel travel is required for the captain's
control wheel to touch the forward stop. This large deflection can be
necessary for certain flight conditions in manual reversion. The system
reaches the aft stops at approximately 90 degrees. Apply additional force to
turn the control wheel more than 90-95 degrees. The control cables stretch
slightly when the control wheels are turned beyond 90 degrees.
SUBTASK 27-11-00-860-096
(5) Do this task: Remove Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-812.

SUBTASK 27-11-00-730-004
(1) Do a test of the aileron travel:
(a) Operate the captain's aileron control wheel through at least 6 full cycles then return the
wheel to neutral position.
(b) Turn the captain's aileron control wheel more than 87 degrees counterclockwise from the
neutral position and hold.
(c) Measure and record the distance between the outboard lower trailing edge of the aileron
and the lower trailing edge of the adjacent fixed trailing structure for both the left and right
ailerons.
1) Make sure that the left aileron moves up 4.83 ±0.20 in. (122.7 ±5.1 mm).
2) Make sure that the right aileron moves down 3.63 ±0.20 in. (92.2 ±5.1 mm).
3) Make sure the aileron balance tab moves in the opposite direction to the aileron.
(d) Turn the captain's aileron control wheel more than 87 degrees clockwise from the neutral
position and hold.
(e) Measure and record the distance between the outboard lower trailing edge of the aileron
and the lower trailing edge of the adjacent fixed trailing structure for both the left and right
ailerons.
1) Make sure that the right aileron moves up 4.83 ±0.20 in. (122.7 ±5.1 mm).
2) Make sure that the left aileron moves down 3.63 ±0.20 in. (92.2 ±5.1 mm).
3) Make sure that the aileron balance tab moves in the opposite direction to the
aileron.

27-11-00-750-801Flight Test to Find and Correct Asymmetrical Flight Control ForcesPDF p. 463
21. Flight Test to Find and Correct Asymmetrical Flight Control Forces
A. General
(1) An aileron system flight test to find and correct asymmetrical flight control forces is necessary
after any of the following maintenance procedures:
(a) For the aileron:
1) Installation of a replacement aileron.
NOTE: Replacement of a new aileron, or one that is not the same as the one that
was originally on the airplane, requires an aileron system flight test.
NOTE: A flight test is not required if the same ailerons that were removed from the
airplane are re-installed without adjustment, modification, or repair.
2) Installation of an aileron that was repaired, repainted, or reworked and was
subsequently rebalanced, either by on-jig or calculation method, and required
adjustment of the aileron balance adjust weights (SRM 51-60).
NOTE: Any aileron which has been repaired, repainted, or reworked must meet the
aerodynamic smoothness requirements of SRM 51-10-01.
3) Removal or replacement of the aileron front spar hinge bearing nearest to the tab
control rods.
4) Replacement of any of the following components of the hinge bearing support fitting
within the aileron front spar:
a) Installation of a replacement hinge at any of the aileron positions.
b) Installation of a replacement bearing support fitting at any of the aileron
positions.
c) Installation of a replacement bearing in the aileron front support hinge at the
inboard position, nearest the tab control rods.
NOTE: Installation of new aileron hinge bearings (except the one nearest the
tab control rods) does not make a flight test necessary if the original
bearing support fittings are installed in their original locations.
5) Installation of a replacement aileron rear spar tab hinge bearing support fitting.
NOTE: Installation of new tab hinge bearings does not make a flight test necessary
if the original bearing support fittings are installed in their original locations.
(b) For the aileron tab:
1) Installation of a replacement aileron balance tab.
NOTE: Replacement of a new aileron tab, or one that is not the same as the one
that was originally on the airplane, requires an aileron system flight test.
NOTE: A flight test is not required if the same aileron tab that was removed is
re-installed without adjustment, modification, or repair.
2) Installation of a replacement front spar hinge of the aileron balance tab.
3) Installation of replacement bushings on the aileron balance tab front spar hinge
nearest the aileron tab control rods.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
4) After an adjustment or replacement of an aileron tab control rod.
NOTE: For each aileron balance tab, if both control rods are adjusted, then flight
test is necessary.
NOTE: If only one control rod is adjusted, and you can verify that the remaining rod
had not been replaced or adjusted since the last flight test, then flight test is
not necessary.
NOTE: If only one control rod is adjusted, and you can not verify that the remaining
rod had not been replaced or adjusted since the last flight test, then flight
test is necessary.
5) Installation of an aileron tab that was repaired, repainted, or reworked and required
adjustment of the aileron tab adjust weights (SRM 51-60).
NOTE: Any aileron tab which has been repaired, repainted, or reworked must meet
the aerodynamic smoothness requirements of SRM 51-10-01.

E. Prepare for the Test
SUBTASK 27-11-00-820-019
(1) Adjust the applicable system or systems before the flight test if you get these conditions
(Table 27-09-71-993-811):
(a) With the gear up and flaps up, the aileron trim is more than 3/4 unit at .78 mach and more
than 37,000 feet, 3/4 unit at 250 knots and 10,000 to 17,000 feet.
(b) With the gear up, the aileron trim is more than 1 unit at flaps 1, maneuver speed and
10,000 to 17,000 feet.
(c) With the landing gear extended, the aileron trim is more than 1 unit at flaps 15, maneuver
speed and 10,000 to 17,000 feet.
(d) With the landing gear extended, the aileron trim is more than 1.3 units at Vref+5, and
10,000 to 17,000 feet.
(e) The rudder trim is more than 1/2 unit left or 1 unit right at .78 mach and more than 37,000
feet, 3/4 units at 250 knots and 10,000 to 17,000 feet, or 1 unit at any configuration other
than gear up and flaps up.
SUBTASK 27-11-00-210-006
(2) Make sure that the airspeed is 250 knots.
SUBTASK 27-11-00-860-070
(3) Make sure that the flight altitude is 10,000 to 17,000 feet.
SUBTASK 27-11-00-860-073
(4) Make sure that the flaps are up.
SUBTASK 27-11-00-860-074
(5) Make sure that all persons are seated.
SUBTASK 27-11-00-860-109
(6) Make sure that the aileron trim is not more than 3/4 unit.
SUBTASK 27-11-00-860-110
(7) Make sure that the rudder trim is not more than 3/4 unit.
F. Flight Test
SUBTASK 27-11-00-860-075
(1) Move the control wheel to the neutral position.
SUBTASK 27-11-00-860-076
(2) Set the SPOILER A and B switches to OFF.
SUBTASK 27-11-00-860-077
(3) Make sure that the FLT CONTROL A and FLT CONTROL B switches are ON.
SUBTASK 27-11-00-860-078
(4) Set the FLT CONTROL A switch to OFF.
NOTE: The airplane may pitch up or down during transition.
SUBTASK 27-11-00-860-079
(5) Carefully move the elevators, ailerons, and rudder.
(a) Make sure that the control forces and operation do not change.
SUBTASK 27-11-00-860-080
(6) Set the FLT CONTROL A switch to ON.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-11-00-860-081
(7) Set the FLT CONTROL B switch to OFF.
NOTE: The airplane may pitch up or down during transition.
SUBTASK 27-11-00-860-082
(8) Carefully move the elevators, ailerons, and rudder.
(a) Make sure that the control forces and operation do not change.
SUBTASK 27-11-00-860-083
(9) Set the FLT CONTROL B switch to STBY RUD.
SUBTASK 27-11-00-860-084
(10) Set the FLT CONTROL A switch to OFF.
NOTE: The airplane may pitch up or down during transition.
SUBTASK 27-11-00-280-004
(11) When hydraulics are switched off for the test, apply pitch and roll control input as required to
maintain steady level flight.
SUBTASK 27-11-00-750-002
(12) Do these steps to find and correct asymmetrical flight control forces:
(a) Trim the airplane with the rudder to keep wings level flight.
(b) Make sure that the rudder trim does not change by more than 2 units.
1) If the change is more than 2 units, do this task: Control Rod for Standby Rudder
Power Control Unit Adjustment, TASK 27-21-00-820-810-002.
2) If the standby rudder is in adjustment, do this task: Aileron Balance Tab Adjustment,
TASK 27-11-00-820-803.
(c) Make a note if there is a roll tendency.
(d) Turn the control wheel clockwise 30 degrees.
(e) Turn the control wheel counterclockwise 30 degrees.
(f) Make sure that the control wheel forces are symmetrical.
1) If the control wheel forces are not symmetrical by a ratio of 2 to 1 or more, then use
the tool to measure the control wheel forces.
a) Use a force gauge, COM-1557, to push down on the right handgrip knob of the
control wheel, until the wheel is turned 30 degrees clockwise.
b) Measure the control wheel force.
c) Use a force gauge, COM-1557, to push down on the left handgrip knob of the
control wheel, until the wheel is turned 30 degrees counterclockwise.
d) Measure the control wheel force.
e) If the control wheel force in one direction is 2 or more times the force in the
other direction, do this task: Aileron Balance Tab Adjustment to Equalize
Lateral Manual Reversion Forces, TASK 27-09-71-820-802.
f) If the control wheel force in one direction is less than 2 times the force in the
other direction, no action is necessary.
SUBTASK 27-11-00-860-103
(13) Set the FLT CONTROL A switch to STBY RUD.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-11-00-860-085
(14) Set the FLT CONTROL B switch to OFF.
SUBTASK 27-11-00-750-003
(15) Do all the steps to find and correct asymmetrical flight control forces again.
SUBTASK 27-11-00-860-087
(16) Set the SPOILER A and B, FLT CONTROL A and B switches back to ON.
SUBTASK 27-11-00-860-104
(17) Set the Yaw Damper switch, on the forward overhead panel, to the ON position.

following:

(b) Pogo inputs.
 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131,
132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304,
306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-530 PRE SB 737-29-1128
SUBTASK 27-11-00-210-009
(7) Examine the support assembly and lower hose assembly.
(a) Look for any chafing damage on the support assembly from the lower hose assembly.
(b) If damage is found, check the allowable limits are listed below:
1) Location - Any location along the support assembly
2) Depth - less than 0.125 in. (3.175 mm)
3) Length - 0.80 in. (20.32 mm) maximum
4) Width - equal to the width of the flange on the support assembly
5) If the support assembly is out of tolerance, repair or replace the part.
(c) Look for any chafing to the lower hose assembly where contact with the support
assembly could have occurred.
1) Replace the lower hose assembly if chafing is found.
 ALL

 ALL

F. Aileron Removal
SUBTASK 27-11-11-480-001
(1) Remove the aileron and tab assembly [1] with the sling, SPL-2042 (Figure 401).
(a) Install the sling, SPL-2042, on the aileron and tab assembly [1].
1) At hinge 2, do these steps (View C, Figure 402):
a) Remove the bolts [35], washers [14], radial seal retainer [37], and radial
seal [39].
b) Remove the bolts [29], washers [14], radial seal retainer [33], and radial
seal [31].
c) Remove and discard the pin [17].
d) Remove and keep the nut [18], washer [19], bushing [20], washer [21], and
bolt [22].
2) At hinge 5, do these steps (View E, Figure 402):
a) If installed, remove the bolts [61], washers [14], and radial seal retainer [62].
b) Remove the bolts [52], washers [14], radial seal retainer [53], and radial
seal [54].
c) Remove and discard the pin [55].
d) Remove and keep the nut [56], washer [57], bushing [58], washer [59], and
bolt [60].
3) Attach the outboard C-bracket to the outboard clevis with the ball lock pin.
4) Attach the inboard C-bracket to the inboard clevis with the ball lock pin.
5) Put the sling in position around the TE of the aileron and tab assembly [1].
6) Attach the inboard clevis to hinge 5 with the attached ball lock pins.
7) Attach the outboard clevis to hinge 2 with the attached pins.
8) Lift the sling with a cable and hook to hold the aileron and tab assembly [1].
SUBTASK 27-11-11-020-007
(2) Remove the aileron and tab assembly [1] with the sling, SPL-2042, attached.
(a) At hinge 6, do these steps (View F, Figure 402):
1) Remove the bolt [73] that attach the removable fairing [74] to the aileron and tab
assembly [1].
2) Remove the removable fairing [74].
3) Remove and discard the pin [77].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
4) Remove and keep the nut [78], washer [76], bushing [75], washer [72], and bolt [71]
to disconnect the aileron control rod [67] from the aileron and tab assembly [1].
5) Remove the nut [82] and washer [83] to disconnect the bonding jumper [84] from
the structure.
(b) At hinge 1, do these steps (View B, Figure 402):
1) Remove the bolts [23], washers [14], radial seal retainer [24], and radial seal [25].
2) If installed, remove the bolts [15], washers [14], and radial seal retainer [16].
3) Remove the nut [11] and washer [12] to disconnect the bonding jumper [13] from
the structure.
(c) At hinge 3, do these steps (View C, Figure 402):
1) Remove the bolts [36], washers [14], radial seal retainer [38], and radial seal [40].
2) Remove the bolts [30], washers [14], radial seal retainer [34], and radial seal [32].
(d) At hinge 4, do these steps (View D, Figure 402):
1) Remove the bolts [86], washers [14], radial seal retainer [85], and radial seal [87].
2) Remove the bolts [43], washers [14], radial seal retainer [44], and radial seal [42].
3) Remove and discard the pins [45].
4) Remove and keep the nuts [46], washers [47], bushings [48], washers [49], and
bolts [50] to disconnect the tab control rods [41] from the forward fittings.
(e) Remove the hinge seals [7] from the balance panels [5] (View G, Figure 402):
1) Remove the bolts [4], bolts [6], bolts [27], bolts [88], washers [89], nuts [90], and
balance weights [26].
2) Remove the bolts [3] and balance weight [28].
3) Remove the hinge seal [7] from the balance panels [5].
4) Remove and discard the pins [63].
5) Remove and keep the nuts [64], washers [65] (under the nut), and bolts [66] to
remove the aileron and tab assembly [1] from the aileron balance panels [5].
NOTE: The washer under the bolt is bonded to the hinge half.
(f) At hinge 6, do these steps:
1) Remove and discard the pin [81].
2) Remove and keep the nut [80], washer [79], bushing [68], washer [69], and bolt [70].
(g) At hinges 1, 3, and 4, do these steps:
1) Remove and discard the pins [17].
2) Remove and keep the nuts [18], washers [19], bushings [20], washers [21], and
bolts [22].
(h) Remove the aileron and tab assembly [1] from the structure.
SUBTASK 27-11-11-020-001
(3) Remove the aileron and tab assembly [1] without the sling, SPL-2042 (Figure 402).
(a) Disconnect the aileron control rod [67] and bonding jumper [84].
1) At hinge 6, do these steps:
a) Remove the bolts [73] that attach the removable fairing [74] to the aileron and
tab assembly [1].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
b) Remove the removable fairing [74].
c) Remove and discard the pin [77].
d) Remove and keep the nut [78], washer [76], bushing [75], washer [72], and
bolt [71] to disconnect the aileron control rod [67] from the aileron and tab
assembly [1].
e) Remove the nut [82] and washer [83] to disconnect the bonding jumper [84]
from the structure.
(b) Remove the radial seals and radial seal retainers to get access to the aileron hinge and
control rods connections.
1) At hinge 1, do these steps:
a) Remove the bolts [23], washers [14], radial seal retainer [24], and radial
seal [25].
b) If installed, remove the bolts [15], washer [14], and radial seal retainer [16].
c) Remove the nut [11] and washer [12] to disconnect the bonding jumper [13]
from the structure.
2) At hinge 2, do these steps:
a) Remove the bolts [35], washers [14], radial seal retainer [37], and radial
seal [39].
b) Remove the bolts [29], washers [14], radial seal retainer [33], and radial
seal [31].
3) At hinge 3, do these steps:
a) Remove the bolts [36], washers [14], radial seal retainer [38], and radial
seal [40].
b) Remove the bolts [30], washers [14], radial seal retainer [34], and radial
seal [32].
4) At hinge 4, do these steps:
a) Remove the bolts [86], washers [14], radial seal retainer [85], and radial
seal [87].
b) Remove the bolts [43], washers [14], radial seal retainer [44], and radial
seal [42].
c) Remove and discard the pins [45].
d) Remove and keep the nuts [46], washers [47], bushings [48], washers [49],
and bolts [50] to disconnect the tab control rods [41] from the forward fittings.
5) At hinge 5, do these steps:
a) If installed, remove the bolts [61], washers [14], and radial seal retainer [62].
b) Remove the bolts [52], washers [14], radial seal retainer [53], and radial
seal [54].
(c) Remove the hinge seal [7] from the balance panels [5].
1) Remove the bolts [4], bolts [6], bolts [27], bolts [88], washers [89], nuts [90], and
balance weights [26].
2) Remove the bolts [3] and balance weights [28].
3) Remove the hinge seals [7] from the balance panels [5].
4) Remove and discard the pins [63].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
5) Remove and keep the nuts [64], washer [65] (under the nut), and bolts [66] to
remove the aileron and tab assembly [1] from the balance panels [5].
NOTE: The washer under the bolt is bonded to the hinge half.
(d) Hold the aileron and tab assembly [1] while you remove aileron and tab assembly [1]
from the structure.
1) At hinges 1, 2, 3, and 4, remove and discard the pins [17].
a) Remove and keep the nuts [18], washers [19], bushings [20], washers [21],
and bolts [22].
2) At hinge 5, remove and discard the pin [55].
a) Remove and keep the nut [56], washer [57], bushing [58], washer [59], and
bolt [60].
3) At hinge 6, remove and discard the pin [81].
a) Remove and keep the nut [80], washer [79], bushing [68], washer [69], and
bolt [70].
(e) Remove the aileron and tab assembly [1] from the structure.
SUBTASK 27-11-11-020-002
(4) If it is necessary to remove the aileron balance tab [2], do this task: Aileron Balance Tab

SUBTASK 27-11-11-220-001
(1) If you install used bolts, bushings, bearings, or other components with worn areas, do this task:
Aileron Inspection, TASK 27-11-11-200-801.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-11-11-420-001
(2) If you removed the aileron balance tab [2], do this task: Aileron Balance Tab Installation,
TASK 27-11-21-400-801 or Aileron Tab Control Rods Installation, TASK 27-11-34-400-801.
SUBTASK 27-11-11-280-001
(3) Make sure that the correct number of the balance weights [28] are installed on the lower
surface of the aileron balance panels 3 and 4 (SRM 51-60-03).
SUBTASK 27-11-11-820-001
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT YOU HAVE THE AILERONS BALANCED. IF NOT
BALANCED, THE AILERONS CAN CAUSE UNWANTED FLUTTER AND
INSTABILITY OF THE AIRPLANE. THIS CAN CAUSE AN IN-FLIGHT
EMERGENCY. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THESE INSTRUCTIONS, INJURY TO
PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(4) Balance and stamp the aileron assembly with the new static balance hinge moment if you
install a reworked, repaired, repainted, or new aileron assembly (SRM 51-60-01).
SUBTASK 27-11-11-400-001
(5) Install the aileron and tab assembly [1] with the sling, SPL-2042 (Figure 401, Figure 402).
(a) Make sure that the sling, SPL-2042, is installed on the aileron and tab assembly [1]
(Figure 401).
(b) If the sling, SPL-2042, is not installed, do these steps to install it (Figure 401):
1) Attach the outboard C-bracket to the outboard clevis with the ball lock pin
(Figure 401).
2) Attach the inboard C-bracket to the inboard clevis with the ball lock pin (Figure 401).
3) Put the sling in position around the Trailing Edge (TE) of the aileron and tab
assembly [1] (Figure 401).
4) Attach the inboard clevis to hinge 5 with the attached ball lock pins (Figure 401).
5) Attach the outboard clevis to hinge 2 with the attached ball lock pins (Figure 401).
6) Lift the sling with a cable and hook to hold the aileron and tab assembly [1]
(Figure 401).
SUBTASK 27-11-11-420-005
(6) Install the aileron and tab assembly [1] on the hinges (Figure 402):
(a) Apply grease, D00633, to the outer diameters of all hinge bolts and bushings and inner
diameters of bearings.
(b) Put the aileron and tab assembly [1] in position to install.
(c) Align the hinges with the support fittings.
(d) Connect the aileron and tab assembly [1] at hinge 6.
1) Install the bolt [70], washer [69], bushing [68], washer [79], and nut [80].
2) Tighten the nut [80] to 160 in-lb (18.1 N·m) - 240 in-lb (27.1 N·m).
a) Tighten the nut [80] to the lower end of the torque range.
b) Continue to tighten the nut [80] until the next castellation aligns with the hole in
the bolt [70].
3) Install the new pin [81].
(e) Connect the aileron and tab assembly [1], in the sequence that follows, at hinges 1, 4,
and 3.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) To install the pin in hinge 4, hold the aileron from below.
2) Install the bolts [22], washers [21], bushings [20], washers [19], and nuts [18].
3) Tighten the nuts [18] to 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m) - 80 in-lb (9.0 N·m).
a) Tighten the nut [18] to the lower end of the torque range.
b) Continue to tighten the nut [18] until the next castellation aligns with the hole in
the bolt [22].
4) Install the new pin [17].
(f) Remove the sling, SPL-2042, from the aileron and tab assembly [1] (Figure 401).
1) Remove the outboard clevis from hinge 2.
2) Remove the inboard clevis from hinge 5.
3) Remove the sling, SPL-2042, from the TE of the aileron and tab assembly [1].
4) Remove the ball lock pin and disconnect the outboard clevis from the outboard
C-bracket.
5) Remove the ball lock pin and disconnect the inboard clevis from the inboard
C-bracket.
(g) Connect the aileron and tab assembly [1] at hinge 5.
1) Install the bolt [60], washer [59], bushing [58], washer [57], and nut [56].
2) Tighten the nut [56] to 160 in-lb (18.1 N·m) - 240 in-lb (27.1 N·m).
a) Tighten the nut [56] to the lower end of the torque range.
b) Continue to tighten the nut [56] until the next castellation aligns with the hole in
the bolt [60].
3) Install the new pin [55].
(h) Connect the aileron and tab assembly [1] at hinge 2.
1) Install the bolts [22], washers [21], bushings [20], washers [19], and nuts [18].
2) Tighten the nuts [18] to 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m) - 80 in-lb (9.0 N·m).
a) Tighten the nut [18] to the lower end of the torque range.
b) Continue to tighten the nut [18] until the next castellation aligns with the hole in
the bolt [22].
3) Install the new pins [17].
(i) Align the aileron and tab assembly [1] with the balance panels [5].
1) Make sure that the washer under the bolt is bonded to the hinge half.
a) If it is necessary, bond the washer to the hinge half with sealant, A00247.
2) Install the bolts [66], washers [65], and nuts [64].
3) Tighten the nuts [64] to 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m) - 35 in-lb (4.0 N·m).
a) Tighten the nut [64] to the lower end of the torque range.
b) Continue to tighten the nut [64] until the next castellation aligns with the hole in
the bolt [66].
4) Make sure that the gap between the bushings and the washers [65] is 0.01 in.
(0.25 mm) minimum.
5) Install the new pin [63].
(j) Attach the hinge seals [7] to the aileron balance panels [5].

 ALL

SUBTASK 27-11-11-720-001
(10) Do the aileron surface friction and motion test.
(a) With a push/pull scale 0-25 pound (0-11 kilogram), STD-753, measure the force at
8.75 ±0.25 in. (222.25 ±6.35 mm) aft of the hinge centerline and perpendicular to the
aileron chord plane.
(b) Write down the (positive) forces necessary to move each aileron through the neutral
position.
(c) Write down the (negative) forces necessary to prevent movement of the aileron through
the neutral position.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(d) Add these forces together.
(e) Make sure that the result is not more than 5 lbf (22.2 N).
1) If the result is more than 5 lbf (22.2 N), do these checks:
a) Make sure that all the hinge bolts are sufficiently lubricated.
b) Make sure that the torque values of the hinge bolts are as specified.
(f) Measure the force necessary to move the aileron through full travel in each direction,
then back to the neutral position.
NOTE: The movement of the aileron must be free and smooth.
1) Apply the force perpendicular to the aileron chord plane 8.75 ±0.25 in.
(222.25 ±6.35 mm) aft of the aileron hinge line.
2) Make sure that the maximum force is not more than 13 lbf (57.8 N) for aileron down
and 3 lbf (13.3 N) for aileron up.

(13) Use the aileron control wheel to manually operate the aileron through a minimum of two full
cycles, to full travel.
(a) Make sure that the aileron can move smoothly and freely.
SUBTASK 27-11-11-220-002
(14) Do a check of the aileron clearances and mismatch (Figure 403).
(a) Make sure that the clearances for the upper and lower surfaces of the aileron and the
fixed TE are not out of tolerance.
1) At the support beams for the aileron balance panel, make sure that the clearance is
0.350 in. (8.89 mm) - 0.500 in. (12.7 mm).
2) At the blade seals, make sure that the clearance is 0.010 in. (0.25 mm) - 0.050 in.
(1.27 mm).
(b) Make sure that the mismatch for the upper and lower surfaces of the aileron and the fixed
TE are not out of tolerance.
1) For the aileron outside of the wing contour, make sure that the maximum mismatch
is 0.100 in. (2.54 mm).
2) For the aileron inside of the wing contour, make sure that the maximum mismatch is
0.050 in. (1.27 mm).
(c) Make sure that the clearance at the inboard end of the aileron is 0.100 in. (2.54 mm) -
0.200 in. (5.08 mm).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(d) Make sure that the clearance at the outboard end of the aileron is 0.250 in. (6.35 mm) -
0.350 in. (8.89 mm).
(e) Make sure that the aileron balance tab aligns with the aileron:
1) Measure the distance between the rig position of the aileron balance tab [2] to the
aileron lower surface (dimension A) at these three positions.
NOTE: You must measure from the lower aft most point of the aileron balance tab.
a) At the outboard end of the aileron balance tab, make sure that the dimension
A is 0.06 ±0.07 in. (1.5 ±1.8 mm) or 0.82 ±0.25 degrees.
b) At the middle point along the aileron balance tab, make sure that the
dimension A is 0.065 ±0.070 in. (1.7 ±1.8 mm) or 0.60 ±0.25 degrees.
c) At the inboard end of the aileron balance tab, make sure that the dimension A
is 0.07 ±0.07 in. (1.8 ±1.8 mm) or 0.34 ±0.25 degrees.
2) If the aileron balance tab does not align with the aileron, do this task: Aileron
Balance Tab Adjustment, TASK 27-11-00-820-803.

D. Aileron Power Control Unit Linkage Removal
SUBTASK 27-11-14-020-002
(1) Remove the linkage [1] or linkage [2]:
(a) Disconnect cable ABSA [22] and cable ABSB [19] at the turnbuckles [3].
(b) Remove the nuts [18], washers [17], washers [16] and bolts [15] to remove the retaining
plates [14] from the aileron bus drum [20] (Control Cable End Retaining Plate - Removal,
TASK 20-10-96-000-801).
(c) Disengage cable ABSA [22] and cable ABSB [19] from the aileron bus drum [20].
(d) Safety the disconnected cable ABSA [22] and cable ABSB [19] to secure them.
(e) Remove the cotter pin [6], washers [5] to remove the cable retention pins [4] between the
support frames [7] and [21].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(f) Remove the nuts [23] and screws [25] to disconnect the System B upper quadrant
assembly from the System A lower quadrant assembly.
(g) For system A, do these steps:
1) Remove the nut [47], washer [46], washer [45] and bolt [44] to disconnect the
diagonal support [39] from the structure.
2) Remove the nut [34], washer [33], washer [32] and bolt [31] to remove the diagonal
support [39] from the support frame [21].
3) Remove the nuts [49] to remove the hydraulic fittings.
4) Remove the nut [30], washer [29], washer [28], bolt [27], nut [38], washer [37],
washer [36], and bolt [35] to remove the support frame [21] from the structure.
(h) For system B, do these steps:
1) Remove the nut [12], washer [11], bushing [10], washer [9] and bolt [8] from the
fitting [24] to disconnect the spring cartridge [13] at the inboard end.
2) Remove the nut [68], washer [69], bushing [70], shims [67], washer [72] and bolt
[71] to disconnect the diagonal support [62] from the structure.
3) Remove the nut [55], washer [54], washer [53] and bolt [52] to remove the diagonal
support [62] from the support assembly [56].
4) Remove the nut [30], washer [29], washer [28], bolt [27] and nut [66], washer [65],
washer [64], bolt [63] to remove the support frame [7] from the structure.
(i) For system A, do these steps:
1) Remove the nuts [43], washers [42], washers [41] and bolts [40] to disconnect the
support assembly [50] from the structure.
2) Remove the linkage [1] from the airplane.
(j) For system B, do these steps:
1) Remove the nuts [43], washers [42], washers [41] and bolts [40] to disconnect the
support assembly [56] from the structure.
2) Remove the linkage [2] from the airplane.

SUBTASK 27-11-14-420-002
(1) Install the linkage [1] or linkage [2]:
(a) Put the linkage [1] or linkage [2] in its position.
(b) Apply sealant, A00247 to the bolts [40].
(c) Install the bolts [40], washers [41], washer [42] and nuts [43] to connect the support
assembly [50] or [56] to the structure.
(d) For system A, do these steps:
1) Apply sealant, A00247 to the bolts [31], [44], [27] and [35].
2) Install the diagonal support [39] to the support frame [21] with bolt [31], washer [32],
washer [33] and nut [34].
3) Connect the diagonal support [39] to the structure with bolt [44], washer [45],
washer [46] and nut [47].
4) Install the hydraulic fittings with nuts [49].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
5) Install the bolt [27], washer [28], washer [29], nut [30] and bolt [35], washer [36],
washer [37], nut [38] to connect the support frame [21] to the structure.
(e) For system B, do these steps:
1) Apply sealant, A00247 to the bolts [52], [71], [27] and [63], shims [67] and bushing
[70].
2) Install the diagonal support [62] to the support assembly [56] bolt [52], washer [53],
washer [54] and nut [55].
3) Install the diagonal support [62] to the structure with bolt [71], washer [72], shims
[67], bushing [70], washer [69] and nut [68].
a) Install or remove the taper shim [67] as necessary to decrease the gap to
0.003 in. (0.07 mm) or less, between the diagonal support [62] and the
bulkhead support structure to which the diagonal support attaches.
4) Install the bolt [27], washer [28], washer [29], nut [30] and bolt [63], washer [64],
washer [65], nut [66] to connect the support frame [7] to the structure.

SUBTASK 27-11-14-420-004
(3) Install the screws [25] and nuts [23].
(a) Make sure that the gap between the screw [25] and the aileron bus drum [20] is 0.04 in.
(1.02 mm) to 0.06 in. (1.52 mm).
(b) Install the MS20995NC40 lockwire, G02436 with one continuous twist on the two screws
[25].
SUBTASK 27-11-14-480-002
(4) Install the rig pin A/S-4, from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, in the aileron bus drum.

(5) Install the rig pin A/S-3, from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, in the right shaft of the aileron
control quadrant.
SUBTASK 27-11-14-420-005
(6) For system B, install the bolt [8], washer [9], bushing [10], through the top of the fork of fitting
[24], and the washer [11], and nut [12] to connect the spring cartridge [13] to the linkage [2].
SUBTASK 27-11-14-420-006
(7) Connect cable ABSA [22] and cable ABSB [19]:
(a) Connect cable ABSA [22] and cable ABSB [19] on the aileron bus drum [20].
1) Install the retaining plates [14] with bolts [15], washers [16], washers [17] and nuts
[18] (Control Cable End Retaining Plate - Installation, TASK 20-10-96-400-801).
(b) Install the cable retention pins [4], washers [5] and cotter pins [6].
1) Apply a maximum preload of 35 in-lb (4 N·m) during installation.
(c) Connect cable ABSA [22] and cable ABSB [19] at the turnbuckles [3].
(d) Tighten the turnbuckles [3] but keep the cables tension at zero.
(e) Adjust cable ABSA [22] and cable ABSB [19]. To adjust cable ABSA [22] and cable
ABSB [19], do this task: Aileron Cables Adjustment, TASK 27-11-00-820-801.
(f) Install turnbuckles clip locks.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

SUBTASK 27-11-21-860-001
(1) Do this task: Pressure from the Aileron Hydraulic Systems A and B - Deactivation,
TASK 27-11-00-860-801.
SUBTASK 27-11-21-020-001
(2) Remove the aileron balance tab assembly [2] (Figure 401):
(a) Remove the bolts [8] that attach the forward removable fairing [9] to the aileron [1].
1) Remove the forward removable fairing [9].
(b) Remove the bolts [6] that attach the aft removable fairing [7] to the aileron balance tab
assembly [2].
1) Remove the aft removable fairing [7].
(c) Remove the pin [12], nuts [11], washers [13], bushings [16], washers [15], and bolts [14]
that attach the aileron tab control rods [10] to the tab mast.
(d) Turn the trailing edge of the aileron balance tab assembly [2] up until you can see the
bolts [3] that attach the hinge covers [5] to the nose cap.
(e) Remove the bolts [3] and washers [4].
(f) Remove the hinge covers [5].
(g) Disconnect the bonding jumpers [29] that are adjacent to the tab hinges No. 1 and No. 5.
1) Remove the nuts [32], washers [31], and bolts [30] to disconnect the bonding
jumpers [29].
(h) Hold and remove the aileron balance tab assembly [2] from the aileron [1]:
1) Remove the pin [37], nuts [38], washers [39], bushings [35], washers [34], and
bolts [33].
a) Discard the pin [37].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
2) Remove the pin [22], nut [17], washer [21], bushing [18], washer [20], and bolt [19].
a) Discard the pin [22].
3) Remove the pin [23], nut [28], washer [27], bushings [26], washers [25], and
bolt [24].
a) Discard the pin [23].
(i) Carefully remove the aileron balance tab assembly [2] from the hinge assemblies.
(j) Remove the aileron balance tab assembly [2] from the aileron [1].

F. Aileron Balance Tab Installation
SUBTASK 27-11-21-220-001
(1) If you install used bearings, bushings and bolts, do this task: Aileron Balance Tab Inspection,
TASK 27-11-21-200-801.
SUBTASK 27-11-21-210-001
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT YOU HAVE THE AILERON TABS BALANCED. IF NOT
BALANCED, THE AILERON TABS CAN CAUSE UNWANTED FLUTTER AND
INSTABILITY OF THE AIRPLANE. THIS CAN CAUSE AN IN-FLIGHT
EMERGENCY. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THESE INSTRUCTIONS, INJURY TO
PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(2) Make sure that the balance panels have the correct number of the tab adjust weights
(Figure 402).
(a) If it is necessary, add or remove tab adjust weights (SRM 51-60-03).
SUBTASK 27-11-21-640-001
(3) Lubricate the hinge bearings, bushing [18], bushings [26], bushings [35], bolt [19], bolt [24],
and bolt [33] with grease, D00633, except on the threads (Figure 401).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-11-21-420-001
(4) Install the aileron balance tab assembly [2]:
(a) Put the aileron balance tab assembly [2] in its position.
(b) Install the hinge fittings on the aileron balance tab assembly [2] with the fittings on the
aileron [1].
1) Do these steps at tab hinges 1, 4, and 5:
a) Install the bolts [33], washers [34], bushings [35], bushings [36], washers [39],
and nuts [38].
b) Tighten the nuts [38] to the lower end of the torque range 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m) -
80 in-lb (9.0 N·m).
<1> Continue to tighten the nuts [38] until the first castellation aligns with the
hole in the bolt [33].
c) Install a new pin [37].
2) Do these steps at tab hinges 3:
a) Install the bolt [24], washer [25], bushings [26], washer [27], and nut [28].
b) Tighten the nut [28] to the lower end of the torque range 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m) -
80 in-lb (9.0 N·m).
<1> Continue to tighten the nut [28] until the first castellation aligns with the
hole in the bolt [24].
c) Install a new pin [23].
3) Do these steps at tab hinge No. 2:
a) Install the bolt [19], washer [20], bushing [18], washer [21], and nut [17].
b) Make sure that there is a minimum 0.015 in. (0.38 mm) gap between the
bushing and washer (View A-A, Figure 401).
c) Tighten the nut [17] to the lower end of the torque range 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m) -
80 in-lb (9.0 N·m).
<1> Continue to tighten the nut [17] until the first castellation aligns with the
hole in the bolt [19].
d) Install a new pin [22].
(c) Install the bonding jumper [29] at tab hinges No. 1 and No. 5 as follows:
1) Use cotton wiper, G00034, moist in alcohol, B00130, or solvent, B00148, to clean
the hole of the bolt [30], washers [31], and bonding jumper [29].
2) Install the bonding jumper [29] through the slot in the hinge cover [5].
3) Install bolt [30], washers [31], and nut [32] that attach the bonding jumper [29].
4) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the head of the bolt [30] and tab
assembly [2] (SWPM 20-20-00).
a) Use intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550.
b) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 300 000 ohm or less.
5) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the nut [32] and bonding
jumper [29] (SWPM 20-20-00).
a) Use intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
b) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 1.0 ohm (1000 milliohm) or
less.
6) Fillet seal the nut [32], washer [31], and terminal of the bonding jumper [29] with
sealant, A00247, or sealant, A00767.
(d) Install the hinge covers [5] to close the hinge bolt access areas.
1) Install the hinge covers [5] with washers [4] and bolts [3].
2) Make sure that the washer [4] touches the aileron balance tab assembly [2] on a
minimum of two edges.
3) Tighten the bolts [3] to 22 in-lb (2.5 N·m) - 28 in-lb (3.2 N·m).
(e) Connect the control rods [10] to the aileron balance tab assembly [2]:
1) Install bolts [14], washers [15], bushings [16], washers [13], and nuts [11].
a) Make sure that there is a minimum 0.0150 in. (0.38 mm) gap between the
bushing [16] and washer [15] (View A-A, Figure 401).
2) Tighten the nuts [11] to 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m) - 80 in-lb (9.0 N·m).
3) Install the pin [12].
SUBTASK 27-11-21-420-002
(5) Install the bolts [6] to attach the aft removable fairing [7] to the aileron balance tab
assembly [2].
SUBTASK 27-11-21-420-003
(6) Install the bolts [8] to attach the forward removable fairing [9] to the aileron [1].
(a) Apply sealant, A02315, to the upper edge of the forward removable fairing [9] to get
aerodynamic smoothing.
SUBTASK 27-11-21-710-001
(7) Operate the aileron control wheel through full travel.
(a) Make sure that the aileron balance tab assembly [2] moves freely in the opposite
direction to the aileron [1].
SUBTASK 27-11-21-860-002
(8) Do this task: Pressure to the Aileron Hydraulic Systems A and B - Activation,
TASK 27-11-00-860-802.
SUBTASK 27-11-21-820-001
(9) Do this task: Aileron Balance Tab Adjustment, TASK 27-11-00-820-803.
SUBTASK 27-11-21-730-001
(10) Do this task: Aileron Balance Tab Position Test, TASK 27-11-00-700-808.

A. General

B. References

Reference Description

D. Location Zones
Zone Area
572 Left Wing - Aileron
672 Right Wing - Aileron
E. Procedure
SUBTASK 27-11-21-020-002
(1) Do this task: Aileron Balance Tab Removal, TASK 27-11-21-000-801 or Aileron Tab Control
Rods Removal, TASK 27-11-34-000-801.
SUBTASK 27-11-21-020-003
(2) Use these tools to do a check for wear on the parts of the aileron balance tab:
(a) micrometer (0-1 inch, readable to 1/1000 inch), STD-1096
(b) vernier caliper (0 - 6 inch, readable to 1/1000 inch), STD-1097.

SUBTASK 27-11-24-020-001
(1) Remove the aileron wing quadrant assembly [9]:
(a) Disconnect cable ABSA [2] and cable ABSB [4] at the turnbuckles [1].
(b) Safety the disconnected cable ABSA [2] and cable cable ABSB [4].
(c) Remove the nuts [39], washers [38], and bolts [37] to remove the cable guard [36].
(d) Remove the nuts [8], washers [7], washers [6], and bolts [5] to remove the cable retaining
plates [19] from the aileron wing quadrant assembly [9] (Control Cable End Retaining
Plate - Removal, TASK 20-10-96-000-801).
(e) Disengage cable ABSA [2] and cable ABSB [4] from the aileron wing quadrant
assembly [9].
(f) Open the applicable access panel to get access to the bolt [23].
For the left wing, open this access panel:
Number Name/Location
571AT Upper Outboard Fixed Trailing Edge, Quadrant Bolt Access Panel
For the right wing, open this access panel:
Number Name/Location
671AT Upper Outboard Fixed Trailing Edge, Quadrant Bolt Access Panel
(g) Remove the bolt [31] and washer [32] to disconnect the aileron position transmitter rod
from the aileron wing quadrant assembly [9].
(h) Remove the pin [13], nut [14], washer [15], bushing [12], washer [11], and bolt [10] to
remove the aileron control rod [17] from the aileron [16]. Discard the pin [13].
(i) Disconnect the aileron wing quadrant assembly [9] from the aileron hinge support [18].
1) Remove the pin [26], nut [27], washer [25], bushing [24], washer [35], and bolt [23]
to disconnect the aileron wing quadrant assembly [9] from the aileron hinge
support [18]. Discard the pin [26].
(j) Remove the aileron wing quadrant assembly [9].
(k) Disassemble the aileron wing quadrant assembly [9] if it is necessary;

 ALL
1) Remove the bushing [41] and bearings [40].

to disconnect the aileron control rod [17] from the aileron wing quadrant
assembly [9]. Discard the pin [28].

F. Aileron Wing Installation
SUBTASK 27-11-24-420-001
(1) Install the aileron wing quadrant assembly [9]:
(a) Assemble the aileron wing quadrant assembly [9] if it is necessary:
1) Apply sealant, A00247 to the top bearing [40].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
2) Roller swage the top bearing [40].
WARNING
USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE
COR-BAN 27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE
IT WITH WATER. IF THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES,
IMMEDIATELY FLUSH YOUR EYES WITH WATER. GET MEDICAL
AID. THIS MATERIAL CONTAINS FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN
CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL.
3) Apply Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (preferred), or corrosion inhibiting material,
G50136 (alternate), to the bottom bearing [40].
4) Install the bearings [40] and bushing [41] in the aileron wing quadrant assembly [9].
5) Install the bolt [20], washer [21], bushing [22], washer [30], nut [29], and new
pin [28] to connect the aileron wing quadrant assembly [9] to the aileron control
rod [17].
(b) Connect the aileron wing quadrant assembly [9] to the aileron hinge support [18].
1) Install the bolt [23], washer [35], bushing [24], washer [25], nut [27], and new
pin [26].
(c) Install the bolt [10], washer [11], bushing [12], washer [15], nut [14], and new pin [13] to
connect the aileron control rod [17] to the aileron [16].
(d) Install the bolt [31] and washer [32] to connect the aileron position transmitter rod to the
aileron wing quadrant assembly [9].
1) Make sure that the aileron position transmitter rod is 17.01 in. (432.05 mm) from
bolt center to bolt center.
2) If adjustment of the aileron position transmitter rod is necessary, do this task:
Aileron Position Transmitter Installation Test, TASK 31-31-31-700-801.
(e) Put cable ABSA [2] (for the left wing) and cable ABSB [4] (for the right wing) in the bottom
groove of the aileron wing quadrant assembly [9].
(f) Put cable ABSB [4] (for the left wing) and cable ABSA [2] (for the right wing) in the top
groove of the aileron wing quadrant assembly [9].
(g) Install the cable terminations through the cable retaining plate [19].
(h) Install the cable retaining plate [19] with the bolts [5], washers [6], washers [7], and
nuts [8] (Control Cable End Retaining Plate - Installation, TASK 20-10-96-400-801).
(i) Install the cable guard [36] with bolts [37], washers [38], and nut [39].
1) Adjust the cable guard [36] until the gap between the cable guard [36] and the
aileron wing quadrant assembly [9] is 0.030 in. (0.76 mm) to 0.050 in. (1.27 mm).
(j) Connect cable ABSA [2] and cable ABSB [4] to the turnbuckles [1], but keep the cable
tension at zero.

seal [20].

G. Aileron Balance Panels Installation
SUBTASK 27-11-31-220-001
(1) If you install used bolts, bushings, or other components that have worn areas, do this task:
Aileron Balance Panel Seals Detailed Visual Inspection, TASK 27-11-31-210-801.
SUBTASK 27-11-31-420-001
(2) Install the balance panel [22], balance panel [23], balance panel [24], or balance panel [25].
(a) Install the bolts [26], washers [7], washers [8], and nuts [9] to attach the balance
panel [22], balance panel [23], balance panel [24], or balance panel [25] to the wing
structure.
(b) Tighten the nuts [9] to 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m) - 35 in-lb (4 N·m).
1) Tighten the nuts [9] to the lower end of the torque range.
2) Continue to tighten the nuts [9] until the next castellation aligns with the hole in the
bolts [26].
3) Make sure that the gap between the bushing face and washer [8] under the nut [9]
is 0.010 in. (0.25 mm) minimum after torque up.
(c) Install the pins [10].
(d) Make sure that the washers [7] are bonded to the hinge half.
1) If it is necessary, bond the washers [7] to the hinge half with sealant, A00247.
(e) Install the bolts [6], washers [7], washers [8], and nuts [9] to attach the balance
panel [22], balance panel [23], balance panel [24], or balance panel [25] to the aileron.
(f) Tighten the nuts [9] to 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m) - 35 in-lb (4 N·m).
1) Tighten the nuts [9] to the lower end of the torque range.
2) Continue to tighten the nuts [9] until the next castellation aligns with the hole in the
bolts [6].
3) Make sure the gap between the bushing face and washer [8] under the nut [9] is
0.010 in. (0.25 mm) minimum after torque up.
(g) Install the pins [10].
(h) Make sure that the aerodynamic seals [15], hinge seal [20], and hinge seal [29] are not
damaged.
(i) Install the seal retainer [18] to the hinge seal [20] with the bolts [16] and washers [17].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(j) Attach the hinge seal [29] to the balance panel [22], balance panel [23], balance
panel [24], or balance panel [25].
(k) Install the balance weights [19] to the balance panel with the bolts [21], bolts [4], bolts [5],
and bolts [2] with collars [3].
1) Apply primer, C00259, to the holes of the balance weights [19].
2) Apply compound, C00528, to the bolts [2], bolts [4], bolts [5], and bolts [21].
3) Tighten the bolts [2], bolts [4], bolts [5], and bolts [21] to 35 in-lb (4 N·m) - 50 in-lb
(6 N·m).
(l) Make sure that there are the same number of balance weights [11] on the new balance
panel as on the removed balance panel [24] or balance panel [25].
(m) Install the balance weights [11] to the balance panel assembly with bolts [12].
1) Apply primer, C00259, to the holes of the balance weights [11].
2) Apply compound, C00528, to the bolts [12].
3) Tighten the bolts [12] to 35 in-lb (4 N·m) - 40 in-lb (5 N·m).
(n) Install the seal retainer [27] and seal retainer [30] on the aerodynamic seals [15] with the
bolts [1] and bolts [14].
SUBTASK 27-11-31-860-004
(3) Apply compound, C00528, to the bolts [32].
SUBTASK 27-11-31-420-002
(4) Install the bolts [32], nuts [33], and washers [31] to attach the hinge seal [29] and aerodynamic
seals [15].
NOTE: It is permitted to install the hinge seal below the aerodynamic seal or aerodynamic seal
below the hinge seal.
(a) Make sure that one seal is on top of the other across the bolts [32], nuts [33], and
washers [31].

hinge seal [20], and hinge seal [29].
