E. Aileron Tab Control Rods Removal
SUBTASK 27-11-34-020-001
(1) Remove the bolts [6] that attach the forward removable fairing [2] to the aileron [1].
(a) Remove the forward removable fairing [2].
SUBTASK 27-11-34-020-002
(2) Remove the bolts [4] that attach the aft removable fairing [3] to the aileron balance tab [5].
(a) Remove the aft removable fairing [3].
SUBTASK 27-11-34-020-003
(3) Remove the control rod assembly [17]:
(a) Lift up the aileron Trailing Edge (TE).
(b) Remove the bolts [13] and washers [14] that attach the radial seal [16] to the radial seal
retainer [15] to the structure.
(c) Remove the radial seal [16] and radial seal retainer [15].
(d) Remove the pins [12], nuts [11], washers [10], bushings [9], washers [8] and bolts [7] that
connect the control rod assembly [17] to the forward fittings.
1) Discard the pins [12].
(e) Move the aileron TE down.
(f) Remove the pins [12], nuts [11], washers [10], bushings [18], washers [8], and bolts [19]
that connect the control rod assembly [17] to the tab mast.
1) Discard the pins [12].
(g) Remove the control rod assembly [17] from the airplane.
SUBTASK 27-11-34-970-001
(4) Write down the length of the control rod assembly [17].

F. Aileron Tab Control Rods Installation
SUBTASK 27-11-34-420-001
(1) Install the control rod assembly [17]:
(a) Lift up the aileron Trailing Edge (TE).
(b) Put the two control rod assemblies [17] in position, align the rod ends with the attach
fittings.
NOTE: The length of the control rod assembly must be the same as those written down
after the removal.
(c) Install the bolts [7], washers [8], bushings [9], washers [10], and nuts [11] to connect the
control rod assembly [17] to the forward fittings.
1) Tighten the nut [11] to 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m) - 80 in-lb (9.0 N·m) until the next nut
castellation aligns with the hole in the bolt.
2) Install the pins [12].
(d) Install the radial seal [16] and radial seal retainer [15] to the structure with the bolts [13]
and washers [14].
(e) Move the aileron TE down.
(f) Connect the control rod assembly [17] to the tab mast with the bolts [19], washers [8],
bushings [18], washers [10], and nuts [11].
NOTE: You must adjust the aileron tab control rods the same amount.
1) If there is binding between the aileron tab control rod assemblies [17] and bolt [19],
adjust the length of the aileron tab control rod assemblies [17].
2) Make sure that there is a minimum of 0.0150 in. (0.38 mm) gap between the
bushing [20] and washer [8].
3) Tighten the nuts [11] to 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m) - 80 in-lb (9.0 N·m).
4) Install the new pins [12].
SUBTASK 27-11-34-220-003
(2) Make sure that the distance from the tab TE to the extension of the aileron bottom surface is
correct.
(a) To measure the distance from the tab TE to the extension of the aileron bottom surface,
do this task: Aileron Balance Tab Adjustment, TASK 27-11-00-820-803.
SUBTASK 27-11-34-410-001
(3) On the left wing, install this access panel:

F. Aileron Control Wheel Removal
SUBTASK 27-11-41-020-001
(1) Remove the aileron control wheel [3] (Figure 402):
(a) Remove the screws [5] that attach the medallion [6] to the aileron control wheel [3].
(b) Remove the medallion [6] from the aileron control wheel [3].
(c) Remove the pin [10], nut [4], washer [8], guide washer [21], washer [7], spacer [9], and
bolt [11].
1) Discard the pin [10].
(d) Remove the screws [12], and washers [13] to remove the terminal cover [16].
(e) Remove the screws [19], washers [18] and washers [2] to disconnect the wires from the
terminal block [17].
(f) Write down and make a mark of the configuration of the identified color wires.
(g) Remove the terminal block [17] from the hub of the wheel.
(h) Remove the control wheel Push-To-Talk (PTT) switch (TASK 23-51-04-000-801) to
disconnect the wires necessary to remove the control wheel.
(i) Remove the memory device lamp (TASK 33-11-00-960-803) to disconnect the wires
necessary to remove the control wheel.
(j) Disconnect the autopilot disengage switch wiring at the jiffy junctions
(TASK 22-11-41-000-801).
(k) Carefully remove the aileron control wheel [3] from the control column.
(l) Make a mark of the positions of the aileron control wheel [3] and the gear and sleeve
assembly [1].
(m) Make a mark on the wire bundle to identify the clamp [15] location in the control wheel
hub.
(n) Remove the screw [14] to remove the clamp [15] from the aileron control wheel [3].
(o) Carefully disengage the wire bundle from the aileron control wheel [3].
SUBTASK 27-11-41-020-002
(2) If it is necessary, remove the stabilizer trim control switch. Do this task: Stabilizer Trim Control
Switch Removal, TASK 27-41-97-000-801.
SUBTASK 27-11-41-020-003
(3) If it is necessary, remove the autopilot disengage switch. Do this task: Autopilot Disengage
Switch Removal, TASK 22-11-41-000-801.

G. Aileron Control Wheel Installation
SUBTASK 27-11-41-020-005
(1) If you removed the stabilizer trim control switch, do this task: Stabilizer Trim Control Switch
Installation, TASK 27-41-97-400-801.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-11-41-020-006
(2) If you removed the autopilot disengage switch, do this task: Autopilot Disengage Switch
Installation, TASK 22-11-41-400-801.
SUBTASK 27-11-41-020-007
(3) If you removed the control wheel Push-To-Talk (PTT) switch, do this task: Control Wheel PTT
Switch Installation, TASK 23-51-04-400-801.
SUBTASK 27-11-41-420-001
(4) Install the aileron control wheel [3] (Figure 402):
(a) Connect the autopilot disengage switch wiring at the jiffy junctions
(TASK 22-11-41-400-801).
NOTE: These jiffy junctions were disconnected to remove the control wheel.
(b) Install the memory device lamp (TASK 33-11-00-960-803).
NOTE: The memory device lamp was removed to disconnect the wiring to remove the
control wheel.
(c) Install the terminal block [17] in the hub of the wheel.
(d) Install the screws [19], washers [18], and washers [2] to connect the terminals of the
switch wires to the terminal block [17].
(e) Make sure the terminals of the switch wires are installed correctly.
(f) Attach the terminal cover [16] to the aileron control wheel [3] with washers [13] and
screws [12].
(g) Apply a small amount of the compound, G50550 to the wire bundle and the inside of the
hub of the control wheel splines.
(h) Use a wire leader to put the electrical wires in the aileron control wheel [3].
(i) Put a clamp [15] at the mark on the wire bundle.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE WIRE BUNDLE LENGTH IS CORRECT
BETWEEN THE AILERON CONTROL COLUMN AND THE AILERON
CONTROL WHEEL. THE AILERON CONTROL WHEEL CANNOT MOVE
FREELY IF THE WIRE BUNDLE IS NOT CORRECT. THIS CAN CAUSE
DAMAGE TO THE WIRE BUNDLE.
(j) Make sure the length of the wire bundle is approximately 27 in. (686 mm) between the
clamp [15] in the aileron control wheel [3] and the hole in the housing.
(k) Make sure the aileron control wheel [3] moves an equal distance each direction from the
neutral position.
(l) Install the clamp [15] with the screw [14] to hold the wire bundle to the aileron control
wheel [3].
(m) Wind the wire bundle four times around the control wheel hub.
NOTE: As you look forward into the control wheel upper cavity, wind the wire bundle
counterclockwise for the captain's aileron control wheel. For the first officer's
aileron control wheel, wind the wire bundle clockwise. Fig. 402, Detail (B).
(n) Engage the splines on the aileron control wheel [3] to the control column at the identified
positions.
(o) Install the bolt [11], spacer [9], washer [7], guide washer [21], washer [8], and nut [4].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(p) Torque the nut [4] to 85 in-lb (10 N·m) - 140 in-lb (16 N·m) until the next nut castelation
aligns with the hole in the bolt.
(q) Install the new pin [10].
SUBTASK 27-11-41-720-001
(5) Do a check of the operation of the aileron control wheel [3]:
(a) Make sure the captain's and the first officer's aileron control wheels [3] are in the neutral
position.
(b) Put the straight edge, SPL-1671 across the top end of the aileron control wheels.
1) Make sure that one end of the first officer's aileron control wheel [3] is not farther
than 0.20 in. (5.08 mm) from the straightedge.
(c) Remove the straight edge, SPL-1671 from the aileron control wheels.
(d) Install the adapter, SPL-1674 to the captain's control wheel.
(e) Remove the map holder assembly from the first officer's control wheel.
(f) Install the mount, SPL-1670 and the protractor, SPL-1680 to the first officer's control
wheel.
(g) Remove the rig pins A/S-1, A/S-1A and A/S-15 from the transfer mechanism (Figure 401).
CAUTION
DO NOT LET THE AILERON CONTROL WHEEL TURN MORE THAN 110
DEGREES IN EACH DIRECTION FROM NEUTRAL. IF THE AILERON
CONTROL WHEEL TURNS MORE THAN 110 DEGREES DAMAGE TO
THE WIRE BUNDLE CAN OCCUR.
(h) Make sure the aileron control wheel [3] can turn 108 degrees in each direction from the
neutral position.
(i) Make slow and deliberate inputs, one direction at a time.
(j) Make sure the aileron control wheel [3] moves freely and smoothly.
(k) Remove the adapter, SPL-1674 from the captain's control wheel.
(l) Remove the mount, SPL-1670 and the protractor, SPL-1680 from the first officer's control
wheel.
(m) Install the map holder assembly on the first officer's control wheel.
SUBTASK 27-11-41-720-002
(6) Do a test of the electrical circuits for continuity changed during the replacement of the aileron
control wheel [3].
SUBTASK 27-11-41-720-003
(7) Use the insulation resistance tester, COM-1276 to do a test of the terminal block [17] while you
turn the aileron control wheel [3] from stop to stop.
(a) Do a test on the terminal block for resistance to ground, and wire to wire for a minimum
insulation value of 100 megohms.

WARNING
MAKE SURE TO USE THE CORRECT NUT THAT CONNECTS THE FORK TO
THE CONTROL WHEEL DRUM. USE ONLY THE SELF-LOCKING SHEAR-NUT
AND NOT THE TENSION-TYPE SELF-LOCKING NUT. IF YOU INSTALL THE
INCORRECT NUT, THE CAPTAIN'S CONTROL COLUMN CAN BECOME
DISENGAGED FROM THE FORK. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, THIS CAN CAUSE
INJURY TO PERSONNEL OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(1) Make sure that the fork is connected to the control wheel drum with correct self-locking shear
nut.
NOTE: You must see a completed bolt chamfer at the end of the nut.

SUBTASK 27-11-54-020-001
(1) Disconnect the electrical connector from the aileron trim actuator [1].

option.

CONNECTORS IN THE MAIN WHEEL WELL. THE ELECTRICAL
CONNECTORS ARE IN A SYSTEM THAT IS NECESSARY FOR SAFE
FLIGHT.

E. Aileron Power Control Unit Linkage Removal
SUBTASK 27-11-71-020-001
(1) Disconnect the hydraulic lines [4] at the inlet and outlet ports of the power control unit [1].
(a) Use a oil resistant container, STD-203, to contain any hydraulic fluid leakage.
(b) Disconnect the hydraulic lines [4] from the union [3] and union [5].
(c) If necessary, remove the union [3] and union [5] from the power control unit [1].
1) Discard the packing [2] and packing [6].
(d) Install the caps and plugs on the hydraulic lines [4] and ports.
SUBTASK 27-11-71-020-002
(2) Remove the power control unit [1].
(a) Remove the pin [13], nut [12], washer [11], bushing [10], washer [9], and bolt [8] to
disconnect the pogo [7] from the power control unit [1].
1) Discard the pin [13].
(b) Remove the bolts [30], washers [31], bolts [32], and washers [33] to disconnect the
bracket assemblies from the power control unit [1].
(c) Remove the pin [23], nut [22], washer [21], nut [24], washer [25], bushing [26],
washers [28], and bolt assembly [14] to disconnect the power control unit [1] from the
reaction support assembly [27].
1) Discard the pin [23].
(d) Remove the nut [20], washer [19], washers [17], spacer [16], and bolt [15] to disconnect
the safety link [18] from the reaction support assembly [27].
(e) Move the reaction link [29] aft to get access to the power control unit [1].
(f) Remove the pin [37], nut [38], washer [39], washer [35], and bolt [34] to disconnect the
power control unit [1] from the output lever assembly [36].
1) Discard the pin [37].
(g) Remove the power control unit [1].

F. Aileron Power Control Unit Installation
SUBTASK 27-11-71-420-001
(1) If they are not installed, install the union [3], union [5], new packing [2], and new packing [6].
(a) Apply hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the new packing [2] and new packing [6].
(b) Install the union [3], packing [2] and union [5], packing [6] in the ports on the power
control unit [1].
1) Tighten the union [3] to 161 in-lb (18.2 N·m) - 179 in-lb (20.2 N·m).
2) Tighten the union [5] to 104 in-lb (11.8 N·m) - 116 in-lb (13.1 N·m).
SUBTASK 27-11-71-860-002
(2) Make sure that the power control unit [1] is filled with hydraulic fluid, D00153.
SUBTASK 27-11-71-820-002
(3) Remove the oil resistant container, STD-203.
SUBTASK 27-11-71-420-002
(4) Install the power control unit [1].
(a) Put the power control unit [1] in its position.
(b) Install the bolt [34], washer [35], washer [39], and nut [38] to connect the power control
unit [1] to the output lever assembly [36].
(c) Tighten the nut [38] to the lower end of the torque range 300 in-lb (33.9 N·m) - 410 in-lb
(46.3 N·m).
1) Continue to tighten the nut [38] until the next castellation aligns with the hole in the
bolt [34].
(d) Install the new pin [37].
(e) Move the reaction link [29] to put the power control unit [1] between the fork end of the
reaction link [29].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(f) Connect the power control unit [1] to the reaction support assembly [27].
1) Install the bolt assembly [14], washers [25], bushings [26], washers [28], and
nut [24].
2) Tighten the nut [24] to 300 in-lb (33.9 N·m) - 350 in-lb (39.5 N·m).
3) Install the washer [21] and nut [22].
4) Tighten the nut [22] to the lower end of the torque range 220 in-lb (24.9 N·m) -
308 in-lb (34.8 N·m).
a) Continue to tighten the nut [22] until the next castellation aligns with the hole in
the bolt assembly [14].
5) Install the new pin [23].
(g) Apply sealant, A00247, to the bolt [15] and spacer [16].
(h) Install the bolt [15], spacer [16], washers [17], washer [19], and nut [20] to connect the
safety link [18] to the reaction support assembly [27].
(i) Connect the bracket assemblies to the power control unit [1] with bolts [30], washers [31],
bolts [32], and washers [33].
(j) Apply grease, D00633, to the bolt [8] and nut [12].
(k) Connect the pogo [7] to the power control unit [1] with bolt [8], washer [9], bushing [10],
washer [11], and nut [12].
(l) Tighten the nut [12] to the lower end of the torque range 60 in-lb (6.8 N·m) - 90 in-lb
(10.2 N·m).
1) Continue to tighten the nut [12] until the next castellation aligns with the hole in the
bolt [8].
(m) Install the new pin [13].

(5) Remove the caps and plugs from the hydraulic lines [4] and ports.
SUBTASK 27-11-71-420-003

E. Aileron Feel and Centering Unit Removal
SUBTASK 27-11-81-020-003
(1) Remove the aileron feel and centering unit [11] (Figure 402):
(a) Remove the electrical connector from the aileron trim actuator [15].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) Remove the pin [32], nuts [61], washers [33], nuts [34], washers [35], bushings [36],
washers [37], and bolt assemblies [27] from the reaction links [29]. Discard the pin [32].
NOTE: The four bushings [36] in the reaction support assemblies are free floating and
concealed by the washers above and below them. They can be easily misplaced
or lost during disassembly.
(c) Make sure that the four concealed bushings [36] are captured on the disassembly and
retained for reassembly of the reaction support assembly to the reaction link.
(d) Remove the nut [41], washer [42], washer [44] and bolt [45] to disconnect the autopilot
actuator rod [43] from the aileron feel and centering unit [11].
(e) Remove the bolt [46], washer [62] and washer [39] to remove the aileron position sensor
rod [38] from the aileron feel and centering unit [11].
NOTE: Record the position and orientation of the aileron position sensor rod [38] before
removal as an aid for installation.
(f) Remove the pin [25], nuts [24], washers [23], bushings [21], washers [20], and bolts [19]
to disconnect the pogos [22] from the lever assemblies [26]. Discard the pin [25].
(g) Disconnect the aileron feel and centering unit [11] from the airplane structure.
1) Remove the nut [4], washer [5], bushing [6], washer [7], and bolt [8].
2) Remove the nuts [16], washers [17], washers [31], bushings [28], washers [13] and
bolts [14].
(h) Remove the aileron control quadrant [47] from the shaft.
1) Remove the cable AA [2] and cable AB [1] from the aileron control quadrant [47]:
a) Disconnect the left cable AA [2] and cable AB [1] at the turnbuckles.
b) Remove the nuts [59], washers [58], and bolts [57] to remove retaining
plates [60] from the aileron control quadrant [47] (Control Cable End Retaining
Plate - Removal, TASK 20-10-96-000-801).
c) Remove the cable AA [2] and cable AB [1] from the aileron control
quadrant [47].
d) Secure the disconnected cable AA [2] and cable AB [1] with clamps.
e) Attach the identification tags to the disconnected cables for easier assembly.
2) Remove the nuts [51], washers [49], and bolts [48] to disconnect the aileron control
quadrant [47] from the shaft.
3) Remove the aileron control quadrant [47] from the shaft.
(i) Remove the nuts [56], washers [55], washers [53] and bolts [52] to disconnect the
bearing housing [54] from the pressure deck.
(j) Carefully lower and remove the aileron feel and centering unit [11].

F. Aileron Feel and Centering Unit Installation
SUBTASK 27-11-81-420-001
(1) Install the aileron feel and centering unit [11] (Figure 402).
(a) If the aileron control quadrant [47] is attached to the new aileron feel and centering
unit [11], remove the aileron control quadrant [47]:
1) Remove and keep the nuts [51], washers [49], and bolts [48].
(b) Apply AeroShell Grease 33, D50180, to the bearings (View A, Figure 402).
(c) Make sure that the spherical race of the bearing housing [54] does not bind in the outer
housing.
(d) Apply a fillet seal between the bearing housing [54] and pressure deck with sealant,
A00247 (TASK 51-31-00-390-804).
(e) Put the aileron feel and centering unit [11] in position with the shaft through the pressure
deck.
(f) Install the bolts [52], washers [53], washers [55], and nuts [56].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Torque the nuts [56] to 20 in-lb (2.26 N·m) - 25 in-lb (2.82 N·m).
NOTE: If necessary, the aileron control quadrant can be installed before the aileron
feel and centering unit fasteners.
(g) Install the aileron control quadrant [47] on the shaft:
1) If it is necessary, apply sealant, A00247, on the disk of the aileron control quadrant.
2) Engage the aileron control quadrant [47] on the shaft:
a) Make sure that the tip of the aileron control quadrant [47] points in the
outboard direction.
3) Install the bolts [48], washers [49], washers [50], and nuts [51].
(h) Attach the reaction support assemblys [30] to the structure (View D, Figure 402):
1) Install the bolts [14], washers [13], bushings [28], washers [31], washers [17], and
nuts [16].
a) Install the washers [31] between the lug and the clevis.
NOTE: There must be a minimum of one washer on each side of the lug.
(i) Attach the aileron feel and centering unit [11] to the structure (View B, Figure 402):
1) Install the bolt [8], washer [7], bushing [6], washer [5], and nut [4].
2) Do this task: Aileron Trim Actuator Installation, TASK 27-11-54-400-801.
3) Connect the electrical connector to the aileron trim actuator [15].
(j) Connect the reaction links [29] to the reaction support assemblys [30]:
1) Install the bolt assemblies [27], washers [35], bushings [36], washers [37], and
nuts [34].
2) Torque the nuts [34] to 300 in-lb (33.90 N·m) - 350 in-lb (39.54 N·m).
3) Install the washers [33], nuts [61] and new pin [32].
(k) Connect the pogos [22] to the aileron feel and centering unit [11] with the bolts [19],
washers [20], bushings [21], washers [23], nuts [24], and new pin [25].
1) Make sure to install the bolts [19] and bushings [21] with the head up.
(l) Make sure that the top and bottom pogos [22] on each power control unit are at the
center between the stops.
1) If it is necessary to adjust the pogos [22], do this task: Pogo and Power Control Unit
(PCU) Adjustment, TASK 27-11-00-820-802.
(m) Connect the autopilot actuator rod [43] with the bolt [45], washer [44], washer [42], and
nut [41].
CAUTION
POSITION AND ORIENT AILERON POSITION SENSOR ROD AS
RECORDED IN REMOVAL. UPON INSTALLATION OF THE AILERON
POSITION SENSOR, PLACE THE AILERON POSITION SENSOR ROD
AND CRANK SUCH THAT THEY ARE POINTED FORWARD RELATIVE TO
THE FUSELAGE. AN INCORRECT INSTALLATION OF THE ROD CAN
CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT WHEN AUTOPILOT IS ENGAGED.
(n) Connect the aileron position sensor rod [38] with the bolt [46], washer [62], washer [39],
and nut [40] (Figure 402).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Adjust the aileron position sensor, do this task: Aileron Position Sensor Adjustment,

correctly.

(29.36-29.69 millimeters) from the top of the baseplate [6] to the end of the rudder

C. Rudder Hydraulic System A, B, or Standby Pressurization
NOTE: This task supply the steps to pressurize either hydraulic system A or B, both systems A and
B, or to pressurize the standby hydraulic system.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-21-00-860-002
CAUTION
DO NOT OPERATE SYSTEM A OR B HYDRAULIC PUMPS FOR MORE THAN
TWO MINUTES WITHOUT FUEL IN THE FUEL TANKS. THE NO. 1 (FOR
SYSTEM A) AND NO. 2 (FOR SYSTEM B) FUEL TANKS MUST HAVE A
MINIMUM OF 250 GALLONS (1675 POUNDS/760 KILOGRAMS) OF FUEL IN
THEM. IF THERE IS NOT SUFFICIENT FUEL IN THE FUEL TANKS, THE
HYDRAULIC FLUID WILL BECOME TOO HOT.
(1) Make sure that the No. 1 and No. 2 fuel tanks each have 250 gallons (1675 pounds/760
kilograms) of fuel in them.
SUBTASK 27-21-00-210-001
(2) Make sure that the hydraulic reservoirs are full.
(a) If it is necessary, fill the reservoirs (TASK 12-12-00-610-801).
SUBTASK 27-21-00-860-065
(3) Make sure that these circuit breakers are closed:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2
Row Col Number Name
B 13 C00363 FLIGHT CONT SHUTOFF VALVES FLT CONT
C 11 C00362 FLIGHT CONT SHUTOFF VALVES STBY RUD
C 13 C01074 FLIGHT CONT SHUTOFF VALVES FLT CONT
SUBTASK 27-21-00-860-004
(4) Set the parking brake.
SUBTASK 27-21-00-480-001
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT THE GROUND LOCKS ARE INSTALLED IN ALL THE
LANDING GEARS BEFORE YOU PRESSURIZE THE HYDRAULIC SYSTEM.
WITHOUT THE GROUND LOCKS, THE LANDING GEARS CAN RETRACT
AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(5) If the downlock pins are not installed in the nose and main landing gear, do this task: Landing
Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801.
SUBTASK 27-21-00-860-005
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT ALL PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE
FLIGHT CONTROLS SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE
LANDING GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU
SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE INBOARD FAN COWL PANEL AND THE INBOARD
AND OUTBOARD THRUST REVERSERS ARE CLOSED, AND IN THE
STOWED POSITION, OR REMOVED BEFORE YOU EXTEND THE LEADING
EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS. THERE IS NOT SUFFICIENT CLEARANCE FOR
THE FLAPS AND SLATS TO EXTEND IF THE INBOARD FAN COWL PANEL
AND THE INBOARD AND OUTBOARD THRUST REVERSERS ARE IN THE
OPEN POSITION. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(6) Pressurize the rudder hydraulic system A, B or Standby (Figure 201):
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Set the ELEC 2, HYD PUMPS A or ELEC 1, HYD PUMPS B switch on the forward
overhead panel to the ON position.
NOTE: Intermittent system A or B electric pump operation must be kept to a limit of five
starts in a 5 minutes period. After the fifth start, it is necessary to operate the
pump for more than 5 minutes or turn the pump off for a minimum of 5 minutes.
(b) For the hydraulic system A pressurization, set the FLT CONTROL A switch on the forward
overhead panel to the ON position.
(c) For the hydraulic system B pressurization, set the FLT CONTROL B switch on the
forward overhead panel to the ON position.
(d) For the standby hydraulic system, set the FLT CONTROL A or B switch on the forward
overhead panel to the STDBY RUD position.

(6) Install the flight controls ground locks to the flight controls shutoff valves (Figure 202,
Figure 203):
(a) Disconnect the electrical connector from the flight controls shutoff valve at the flight
controls hydraulic modules A and B.
NOTE: The flight controls shutoff valve is part of the flight controls hydraulic module. The
hydraulic module for hydraulic system A is found in the left main wheel well. The
hydraulic module for hydraulic system B is found in the right main wheel well.
(b) Disconnect the electrical connector from the standby flight controls shutoff valve at the
standby flight controls hydraulic module.
(c) After you disconnect the electrical connector(s), examine the connector(s) for corrosion.
NOTE: The inspection of the electrical connector(s) can be done after the removal step
or before the installation step of the electrical connector(s). This is an operator
option.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
WARNING
DO THE STEPS BELOW IF THE AIRPLANE OPERATES WHERE
DEICING FLUID THAT CONTAINS POTASSIUM FORMATE OR
POTASSIUM ACETATE IS USED. ALSO, DO THE STEPS FOR ALL
AIRPLANES THAT YOU FOUND CORROSION IN THE ELECTRICAL
CONNECTORS IN THE MAIN WHEEL WELL. THE ELECTRICAL
CONNECTORS ARE IN A SYSTEM THAT IS NECESSARY FOR SAFE
FLIGHT.
(d) If there was corrosion, refer to (SWPM 20-60-03) to correct the problem.
(e) Put the manual override lever at the flight control A and B shutoff valves in the position 2
(OFF position). Leave the Standby valve in the position 1 (OFF position).
NOTE: In normal condition, the A and B valves are in position 1 (ON position) and the
Standby valve is in position 1 (OFF position).
(f) Install the lock, SPL-1675 on the three flight controls shutoff valves.
1) Install the detent pins.

H. Rudder Forward Quadrant Adjustment
SUBTASK 27-21-00-710-070-002
(1) Do the rudder forward quadrant adjustment:
(a) Do these steps to set the jackshaft yoke to the middle position:
NOTE: The middle position of the jackshaft yoke is where the number of turns of the
shaft from the full forward and full aft adjustment are the same.
1) Turn the rudder pedal adjustment crank to move the rudder pedals full forward.
2) Turn the rudder pedal adjustment crank to move the rudder pedals full aft.
a) Record the number of turns.
3) Turn the rudder pedal adjustment crank half the recorded number of turns forward.
(b) Install the rig pin R-3 from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, in the forward hole in the
captain's rudder forward quadrant.
Config 2
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(c) Install the rig pin R-4 from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, in the forward hole in the first
officer's rudder forward quadrant.
(d) If you can not install rig pins R-3 or R-4, adjust the bus rod [6] (Figure 501):
1) Turn the turnbuckles to release the tension of rudder control cables RA and RB.
2) Remove the pin [5], nut [4], washer [3], spacers [2], and bolt [1] to disconnect the
bus rod [6] from the rudder forward quadrant.
a) Discard the pin [5].
3) Install the rig pin R-3 from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, in the forward hole in the
captain's rudder forward quadrant.
4) Install the rig pin R-4 from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, in the forward hole in the
first officer's rudder forward quadrant.
5) Adjust the bus rod [6] until you can install the bolt [1] through the rudder forward
quadrant.
6) Install the spacers [2], washer [3], nut [4], and new pin [5].
7) If it is necessary, adjust the brake pushrods [12] to the nose wheel steering
(TASK 32-51-00-820-802).
8) Make sure that the control cables RA and RB are at the correct tension
(TASK 27-09-14-860-802).
(e) Make sure that the clearance between the cable guard blocks and the rudder forward
quadrants is 0.030 in. (0.76 mm) – 0.050 in. (1.27 mm) through full travel.
(f) Remove the rig pins R-3 and R-4.
(g) Remove the nut [50], washer [49], washer [48], and bolt assembly [47] to disconnect the
standby rudder PCU control rod [34] from the rudder control torque tube [33]
(Figure 502).
(h) For each main rudder PCU control rod [36] do this task:
1) Remove the nut [45], washer [44], washer [43], and bolt assembly [42] to disconnect
the main rudder PCU control rod [36] from the rudder control torque tube [33].
(i) Move the captain's rudder forward quadrant until you can install the rig pin R-3 in the aft
rig pin hole.
(j) Make sure that there is no clearance between the captain's forward quadrant and
quadrant stop.
1) Add or subtract shims as needed to bring the clearance to zero.
(k) Remove the rig pin R-3.
(l) Move the first officer's rudder forward quadrant until you can install the rig pin R-4 in the
aft rig pin hole.
(m) Make sure that there is no clearance between the first officer's forward quadrant and
quadrant stop.
1) Add or subtract shims as needed to bring the clearance to zero.
(n) Remove the rig pin R-4.
(o) Connect the main rudder PCU control rod [36] to the center crank [41].
1) Install the bolt assembly [42] with the bolt head end up and washer [43].
2) Tighten the outer bolt of the bolt assembly [42] to 70 in-lb (7.9 N·m) – 85 in-lb
(9.6 N·m).
Config 2
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
3) Install the washer [44] and nut [45].
CAUTION
DO NOT TIGHTEN THE OUTER BOLT OF THE BOLT ASSEMBLY [42]
AFTER YOU TIGHTEN THE NUT [45]. DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT
CAN OCCUR.
4) Tighten the nut [45] to 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m) – 30 in-lb (3.4 N·m).
(p) Install the bolt assembly [47] with the bolt head end up, washer [48] (under bolt),
washer [49] (under nut), and nut [50] to connect the standby rudder PCU control rod [34]
to the upper crank [46].

G. Procedure
SUBTASK 27-21-00-710-071-002
(1) Do the rudder pedals adjustment:
(a) Install the rig pin R-5 from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585 in the rudder feel and centering
unit (Figure 502).
(b) Install the rig pin R-3 from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585 in the captain's rudder forward
quadrant (Figure 501).
(c) Install the rig pin R-4 from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585 in the first officer's rudder forward
quadrant (Figure 501).
(d) Do these steps to set the jackshaft yoke to the middle position:
NOTE: The middle position of the jackshaft yoke is where the number of turns of the
shaft from the full forward and full aft adjustment are the same.
1) Turn the rudder pedal adjustment crank to move the rudder pedals full forward.
2) Turn the rudder pedal adjustment crank to move the rudder pedals full aft. Record
the number of turns.
3) Turn the rudder pedal adjustment crank half the recorded number of turns forward.
(e) Make sure that you can install these rig pins from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585:
1) Rig pin R-1 on the captain's rudder pedals.
2) Rig pin R-2 on the first officer's rudder pedals.
(f) If you can not install the rig pins R-1 and R-2 freely, then do these steps:
1) Determine which pedal arm is out-of-line with the rigging pin hole.
a) If you have problem with installing rig pin R-1, then adjust the captain's side.
b) If you have problem with installing rig pin R-2, then adjust the first officer's
side.
c) If you have problem with installing both rig pins R-1 and R-2, then adjust both
sides.
2) Loosen both jamnuts [8] on the rudder pedal tension rods [7].
3) Remove the bolts [9], washers [10], and nuts [11] to disconnect the rudder pedal
tension rods [7] at the forward end.
4) Adjust the length of rudder pedal tension rods [7] until you can install rig pin R-1 or
R-2 easily.
a) Turn the rod end or rod body of the rudder pedal tension rod [7] as necessary
to adjust the length.
b) Keep the lube fitting on the rudder pedal tension rod [7] down.
Config 2
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
5) Install the bolts [9], washers [10], and nuts [11] to connect the rudder pedal tension
rods [7].
6) Tighten the jamnuts [8].
7) Make sure you can see the threads through the holes on the rudder pedal tension
rods [7].
(g) Remove the rig pins R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, and R-5.

27-21-00-820-808-002Rudder Control Cables RA and RB AdjustmentPDF p. 706
4. Rudder Control Cables RA and RB Adjustment
(Figure 501, Figure 502)
NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. General
(1) Use this task to adjust the rudder control cables RA and RB. This task includes steps to adjust
the rudder forward quadrant and rudder pedals.
(2) Before you do cable adjustment, permit a minimum of one hour at a constant ambient
temperature of ± 5 degrees F (± 2.8 degrees C) for the airframe temperature to become stable.
(a) The cable tension values will not be correct when there are temperature differences along
the cable run.
(3) It is recommended that airplanes supplied with the cables that contain higher zinc coating
(Grade D or Grade K) be re-tensioned 3 to 4 months into service. This will bring the tension of
the control cables within the desired range. After the cables are re-tensioned the high zinc
cables (Grade D or Grade K) will continue to relax at a rate that is equivalent to the Grade B
cables. To identify the grade of the cable, refer to the table below:

H. Rudder Control Cables RA and RB Adjustment
SUBTASK 27-21-00-820-008-002
(1) If you install new rudder control cables RA and RB, do these steps to stretch the cables:
(a) Operate the rudder trim indicator until you can install the rig pin R-5 in the rudder feel and
centering unit easily (View D, Figure 502).
(b) Adjust the turnbuckles in the cables RA and RB to get a tension of 300 lbf (1334 N)
±20 lbf (89 N) each.
1) Make sure that you can install the rig pin R-3 from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585,
freely in the captain's rudder forward quadrant.
(c) Remove the rig pins R-3 and R-5.
(d) Adjust the pressure seals at the aft pressure bulkhead with the control cables RA and RB
(TASK 27-09-17-860-801).
(e) Make sure that the cables RA and RB do not touch the pulley or the quadrant flanges for
the total cable travel.
(f) Make sure that the cables RA and RB are in less than 2 degrees of the plane of the
pulley or the quadrant.
(g) Make sure that you install the cables through the grommets in the structure.
(h) Make sure that the cables do not move from the neutral rig position.
(i) Make sure that the pulleys turn freely with sufficient clearance with the guards.
(j) Remove the nut [50], washer [49], washer [48], and bolt assembly [47] to disconnect the
standby rudder PCU control rod [34] from the rudder control torque tube [33].
(k) Remove the nut [45], washer [44], washer [43], and bolt assembly [42] to disconnect the
main rudder PCU control rod [36] from the rudder control torque tube [33].
(l) Move the rudder pedals 25 times through full travel.
(m) Connect the main rudder PCU control rod [36] to the center crank [41].
1) Install the bolt assembly [42] with the bolt head end up and washer [43].
2) Torque the outer bolt of the bolt assembly [42] to 70 in-lb (7.9 N·m) – 85 in-lb
(9.6 N·m).
3) Install the washer [44] and nut [45].
CAUTION
DO NOT TIGHTEN THE OUTER BOLT OF THE BOLT ASSEMBLY [42]
AFTER YOU TIGHTEN THE NUT [45]. DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT
CAN OCCUR.
4) Torque the nut [45] to 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m) – 30 in-lb (3.4 N·m).
(n) Install the bolt assembly [47] with the bolt head end up, washer [48] (under bolt),
washer [49] (under nut), and nut [50] to connect the standby rudder PCU control rod [34]
to the upper crank [46].
SUBTASK 27-21-00-820-029-002
(2) Adjust the control cables RA and RB to their correct cable rigging tension:
Config 2
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Use a high tension cable tensiometer, COM-1554, or low tension cable tensiometer,
COM-1553, to get the tension measurement (TASK 27-09-14-860-802).
(b) Install the rig pin R-5 from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, in the rudder feel and centering
unit.
(c) Adjust the turnbuckles in the cables RA and RB to get the cable tension
(TASK 27-09-14-860-802).
NOTE: Adjust the tensions close to the maximum values in the table. The cables will
stretch over a period of time.
(d) Make sure that you can install these rig pins from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585
(Figure 501):
1) Rig pin R-3 in the captain's rudder forward quadrant
2) Rig pin R-4 in the first officer's rudder forward quadrant.
(e) If you can not install the rig pins R-3 and R-4 freely, do these steps:
1) Turn the turnbuckles to release the tension of the control cables RA and RB.
2) Remove the pin [5], nut [4], washer [3], spacers [2], and bolt [1] to disconnect one
end of the bus rod [6] from the rudder forward quadrant.
a) Discard the pin [5].
3) Install the rig pins R-3 in the captain's rudder forward quadrant.
4) Install the rig pin R-4 in the first officer's rudder forward quadrant.
5) Adjust the bus rod [6] until you can install the bolt [1] easily.
6) Install the bolt [1], spacers [2], washer [3], nut [4], and new pin [5] to connect the
bus rod [6] to the rudder forward quadrant.
7) Adjust the turnbuckles on the control cables RA and RB to get the correct tension
(TASK 27-09-14-860-802).
(f) Do these steps to adjust the captain's and first officer's pedals to the neutral adjustment
position:
NOTE: The middle position of the rudder pedals is where the number of turns of the
shaft from the full forward and full aft adjustment are the same.
1) Turn the rudder pedal adjustment crank to move the rudder pedals full forward.
2) Turn the rudder pedal adjustment crank to move the rudder pedals full aft.
a) Record the number of turns.
3) Turn the rudder pedal adjustment crank half the number of turns forward.
(g) Install these rig pins from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585:
1) Rig pin R-1 on the captain's rudder pedals
2) Rig pin R-2 on the first officer's rudder pedals.
(h) If you cannot install the rig pin R-1 or R-2 freely, do these steps:
1) Loosen the jam nuts [8] from the applicable rudder pedal tension rod [7].
NOTE: If you cannot install the rig pin R-1, adjust the captain's rudder pedal tension
rods. If you cannot install the rig pin R-2, adjust the first officer's rudder
pedal tension rods. You are only required to adjust the applicable rudder
pedal tension rod that is out of rig.
2) Remove the nut [11], washer [10], and bolt [9] from the forward end of the rudder
pedal tension rod [7].
Config 2
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
3) Adjust the rudder pedal tension rod [7] until you can install the applicable rig pin
freely.
a) Make sure that you keep the lube fitting on the rudder pedal tension rod [7] is
in the down direction.
4) Install the bolt [9], washer [10], and nut [11].
5) Tighten the jam nut [8].
(i) Do a check on the rudder forward quadrant bus rod [6] and the four rudder pedal tension
rod [7]:
1) Make sure that the rod ends cover at least 50 percent of the inspection holes at two
end of the rods (10 locations).
(j) Remove the rig pins R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, and R-5.
(k) Operate the rudder pedals through one full travel cycle.
1) Make sure that the control cables RA and RB are at the correct tension
(TASK 27-09-14-860-802).
(l) Install the locking clips on the turnbuckles.

F. Control Rod of the Standby Rudder PCU Adjustment
SUBTASK 27-21-00-710-072-002
(1) Adjust the standby rudder PCU control rod [34]:
(a) Set FLT CONTROL A and B switches to the STBY RUD position.
(b) Set the YAW DAMPER switch on the P5-3 overhead panel to the ON position.
1) Make sure the YAW DAMPER light goes out after approximately 2 seconds.
(c) Move the control wheel full right clockwise.
1) Make sure the rudder moves to the right.
(d) Release the control wheel.
(e) Do these steps to initiate a zero yaw damper command output from the stall Management
Yaw Damper No. 2 (SMYD No. 2), M1748:
NOTE: The SMYD No. 2 is installed on the E3-2 electrical equipment rack.
1) Push and release the ON/OFF button on the front BITE display of the SMYD No. 2.
2) Push and release the up arrow or down arrow button until the GROUND TEST
shows on the display.
3) Push the YES button to get access to the ground test option.
Config 2
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
4) Push and release the up arrow or down arrow button until the SERVO TEST?
shows on the display.
5) Push the YES button to start the servo test.
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF
THE RUDDER. THE RUDDER CAN MOVE QUICKLY WHEN YOU
PUSH THE `YES` BUTTON ON THE SMYD NO. 2. THIS CAN CAUSE
INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
6) Push the YES button when the RUDDER CLEARED? shows on the display.
7) Push the YES button when the FLT CTRL A STBY? shows on the display.
8) Push the YES button when the FLT CTRL B STBY? shows on the display.
9) Push the YES button when YAW DMPR ENGAGED? shows on the display.
10) Push the YES button when the ZERO COMMAND? shows on the display.
NOTE: A yaw damper command value and LVDT position will show for 10 seconds
each, then the END ZERO COMMAND? will show on the display. You can
push the NO button to show these values again.
 ALL; AIRPLANES WITH 251A3495-7 CONTROL ROD

27-21-00-700-813-002Rudder Pedal Adjustment and Limit Travel TestPDF p. 730
7. Rudder Pedal Adjustment and Limit Travel Test
(Figure 503)
A. General
(1) Use this test to make sure that the rudder pedals can move through their full travel and pedal
adjustment crank operates correctly.
(2) It is recommended to measure pedal travel by projecting a line from the pivot point of the pedal
normal to the heel rest wear plate at each pedal position and marking the pedal position on a
piece of masking tape that applied to the heel rest. Measuring the distance between marks is
the measured pedal travel.

The nose gear steering does not need to be disconnected if the airplane is jacked up
such that the nose gear is fully extended.

SUBTASK 27-21-00-730-030-002
(3) Do these steps to set the jackshaft yokes to the middle positions:
NOTE: The middle positions of the jackshaft yokes is where the number of turns of the shaft
from the full forward and full aft adjustment are the same.
(a) Turn the rudder pedal adjustment cranks for both the captain and first officer to move the
rudder pedals full forward.
(b) Turn the rudder pedal adjustment cranks to move the rudder pedals full aft.
1) Keep a record of number of turns.
(c) Turn the rudder pedal adjustment cranks back half of the number of recorded turns to set
the jackshaft yoke to the middle position.
(d) Make sure that you can install rig pins R-1 and R-2 easily.
(e) Remove the rig pins R-1 and R-2.
SUBTASK 27-21-00-730-028-002
(4) Do the captain's rudder pedal adjustment and the limit travel.
(a) Make sure that the rudder trim indicator is at the zero unit of trim.
(b) Turn the rudder pedal adjustment crank to move the captain's pedals full forward.
(c) Push the captain's left pedal forward until it touches the stop and hold.
1) Measure the forward travel of the captain's left pedal from the middle position of the
pedal adjustment.
2) Make sure that the forward travel, which measured at the pedal pivot point is at a
minimum of 6.58 in. (167.1 mm).
3) Release the captain's left pedal.
(d) Push the captain's right pedal forward until it touches the stop and hold.
1) Measure the forward travel of the captain's right pedal from the middle position of
the pedal adjustment.
2) Make sure that the forward travel, which measured at the pedal pivot point is at a
minimum of 6.58 in. (167.1 mm).
3) Release the captain's right pedal.
(e) Push forward on both the captain's left and right pedals at the same time.
1) Apply approximately 2.5 pounds on each pedal simultaneously.
(f) Turn the rudder pedal adjustment crank to move the captain's pedals to full aft position.
1) Turn the crank at a rate of one revolution (turn) per second.

EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(g) Make sure that the adjustment crank moves smooth and without any chatter.
(h) Push the captain's left pedal forward until it touches the stop and hold.
1) Measure the aft travel of the captain's right pedal from the middle position of the
pedal adjustment.
2) Make sure that the aft travel, which measured at the pedal pivot point is at a
minimum of 6.61 in. (167.9 mm).
3) Release the captain's left pedal.
(i) Push the captain's right pedal forward until it touches the stop and hold.
1) Measure the aft travel of the captain's left pedal from the middle position of the
pedal adjustment.
2) Make sure that the aft travel, which measured at the pedal pivot point is at a
minimum of 6.61 in. (167.9 mm).
3) Release the captain's right pedal.
(j) Turn the rudder pedal adjustment crank to move the captain's pedals to full forward
position.
1) Turn the crank at a rate of one revolution (turn) per second.
(k) Make sure that the adjustment crank only chattered slightly and there is no binding when
the crank is turned.
NOTE: The tendency to chatter will increase as the rate of adjustment increases.

(3) Do the rudder hinge bearing and Power Control Unit (PCU) bearing freeplay:
(a) Make sure the rudder and rudder pedals are in the neutral position.
(b) Make sure the rudder trim indicator is at zero units of trim.

rudder trailing edge.
CAUTION
USE A LOADING BLOCK AND DO NOT PUT MORE THAN 50 LBF (222 N)
ON THE RUDDER WHEN YOU MOVE THE RUDDER SURFACE BY AN
EXTERNAL FORCE. APPLY THE EXTERNAL FORCE APPROXIMATELY
BETWEEN 6 TO 8 INCHES (150 TO 200 MILLIMETERS) FROM THE
BOTTOM OF THE TRAILING EDGE AND APPROXIMATELY 3 INCHES (80
MILLIMETERS) FORWARD OF THE TRAILING EDGE. IF YOU DO NOT
APPLY FORCE AT THIS LOCATION, YOU CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE
RUDDER.
(d) Use a block, STD-1278 and push/pull scale 0-25 pound (0-11 kilogram), STD-753 to
move the rudder to the left side with a force of 12 lbf (53.4 N) ±4.0 lbf (17.8 N) and
release slowly.
1) Make a record of the rudder position on the dial indicator.
(e) Use a block, STD-1278 and push/pull scale 0-25 pound (0-11 kilogram), STD-753 to
move the rudder to the right side with a force of 12 lbf (53.4 N) ±4.0 lbf (17.8 N) and
release slowly.
1) Make a record of the rudder position on the dial indicator.
(f) Make sure that the total left and right freeplay between the left and right positions is not
more than 0.05 in. (1.3 mm).
1) If the total left and right freeplay is more than 0.05 in. (1.3 mm), Then replace the
bearings on the rudder hinge or power control units and repeat this test.
(g) Use a block, STD-1278 and push/pull scale 0-25 pound (0-11 kilogram), STD-753 to
move the rudder to the left side with a force of 12 lbf (53.4 N) ±4.0 lbf (17.8 N) and
release slowly.
NOTE: This check compares the two left positions to verify that the dial indicator did not
move during the test. If the check shows that the dial indicator had moved, the
test has to be repeated.
1) Make a record of the rudder position on the dial indicator.
(h) Make sure the difference between the two left positions is not more than 0.03 in.
(0.8 mm).

 ALL
1) If the difference is more than 0.03 in. (0.8 mm), then repeat the freeplay check.

27-21-00-700-816-002Rudder Pedal Forces TestPDF p. 743
10. Rudder Pedal Forces Test
(Figure 505)
A. General
(1) Use this test to make sure the rudder pedals operate with the correct forces.
NOTE: You must measure the forces with the pedal moving away from the neutral position. If
the pedal moves more than the specified distances, you must repeat the test and start
with the pedal at neutral position.
(2) You may need two people to do the test. One person can sit in one of the seats and push on
the tool. The other person can measure the rudder pedal movement and record the results.
(3) It may be useful to take three readings on each rudder pedal for better accuracy on the rudder
pedal forces test.

F. Procedure
SUBTASK 27-21-00-730-020-002
(1) Do the test of the rudder travel test:
(a) Set the FLT CONTROL A switch to the ON position and FLT CONTROL B switch to the
OFF position.
(b) Set the captain's and first officer's rudder pedal adjustment cranks to the middle position
(Figure 501).
(c) Make sure the rudder pedals are in the neutral position.
(d) Push and hold captain's left pedal until it touches the forward quadrant stop.
1) Measure the rudder travel (Figure 507).
2) Make sure that the dimension is 26.97 in. (685.0 mm) ±0.91 in. (23.1 mm) (29.00 +/-
1.00 degrees) rudder trailing edge left.
3) Release the captain's left pedal.
(e) Push and hold the captain's right pedal until it touches the forward quadrant stop.
1) Measure the rudder travel (Figure 507).
2) Make sure that the dimension is 26.97 in. (685.0 mm) ±0.91 in. (23.1 mm) (29.00 +/-
1.00 degrees) rudder trailing edge right.
3) Release the captain's right pedal.
(f) Make sure that the wire bundle W443 has a minimum clearance of 0.5 in. (12.700 mm)
from left forward rudder quadrant full travel motion, while operating the rudder pedals
(Figure 506)
(g) Set the FLT CONTROL B switch to the ON position and FLT CONTROL A switch to the
OFF position.
(h) Push and hold captain's left pedal until it touches the forward quadrant stop.
1) Measure the rudder travel (Figure 507).
2) Make sure that the dimension is 26.97 in. (685.0 mm) ±0.91 in. (23.1 mm) (29.00 +/-
1.00 degrees) rudder trailing edge left.
3) Release the captain's left pedal.
(i) Push and hold the captain's right pedal until it touches the forward quadrant stop.
1) Measure the rudder travel (Figure 507).
2) Make sure that the dimension is 26.97 in. (685.0 mm) ±0.91 in. (23.1 mm) (29.00 +/-
1.00 degrees) rudder trailing edge right.
3) Release the captain's right pedal.
(j) Make sure that the wire bundle W443 has a minimum clearance of 0.5 in. (12.700 mm)
from left forward rudder quadrant full travel motion, while operating the rudder pedals
(Figure 506).
(k) Set the FLT CONTROL B switch to the STBY position.
(l) Push and hold captain's left pedal until it touches the forward quadrant stop.
1) Measure the rudder travel (Figure 507).
2) Make sure that the dimension is 26.97 in. (685.0 mm) ±0.91 in. (23.1 mm) (29.00 +/-
1.00 degrees) rudder trailing edge left.
3) Release the captain's left pedal.

(m) Push and hold the captain's right pedal until it touches the forward quadrant stop.

1.00 degrees) rudder trailing edge right.

SUBTASK 27-21-00-860-114-002
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF ALL
CONTROL SURFACES BEFORE YOU REMOVE OR INSTALL HYDRAULIC
POWER. AILERONS, RUDDERS, ELEVATORS, FLAPS, SLATS, SPOILERS,
LANDING GEAR, AND THRUST REVERSERS CAN MOVE QUICKLY WHEN
YOU REMOVE HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO
PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(2) Pressurize the standby rudder hydraulic system. To pressurize it, do this task: Rudder
Hydraulic System A, B, or Standby Pressurization, TASK 27-21-00-800-801.
SUBTASK 27-21-00-860-115-002
(3) Move the rudder pedals through ten cycles to flush and bleed the standby rudder PCU.
SUBTASK 27-21-00-860-116-002
(4) Set the FLT CONTROL A and B switches to the ON position.
SUBTASK 27-21-00-730-021-002
(5) Do the test of the standby rudder PCU deadband test:
(a) Make sure the rudder is in the neutral position.
1) If it is necessary, move the rudder pedals lightly to put the rudder to the neutral
position.
2) Make sure the rudder trim indicator is at 0.00 +/- 0.25 unit of trim.
(b) Set the FLT CONTROL A and B to the STANDBY RUD position.
(c) Use your hands to push the rudder to the right, then slowly remove the load.
1) Move your hands away from the rudder.
2) Measure the rudder right position from the center of the rudder trailing edge to the
centerline of the index plate.
3) Record this measurement as A.
(d) Push the rudder by hands to the left, then slowly remove the load.
1) Move your hands away from the rudder.
2) Measure the rudder left position from the center of the rudder trailing edge to the
centerline of the index plate.
3) Record this measurement as B.
(e) Make sure the difference between A and B is not greater than 0.2 in. (5 mm).
1) If the difference is greater than 0.2 in. (5 mm), do this task: Control Rod for Standby
Rudder Power Control Unit Adjustment, TASK 27-21-00-820-810-002
SUBTASK 27-21-00-860-117-002
(6) Do this task: Put the Rudder Hydraulic systems A, B, and Standby Back to the Condition
Before the Pressurization, TASK 27-21-00-840-801.
SUBTASK 27-21-00-020-007-002
(7) Remove the NLG towing lever pin, SPL-1499, from the nose wheel steering mechanism
(Landing Gear Downlock Pins Removal, TASK 32-00-01-080-801).

E. Rudder Hinge Friction Test
SUBTASK 27-21-00-860-125-002
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF ALL
CONTROL SURFACES BEFORE YOU REMOVE OR INSTALL HYDRAULIC
POWER. AILERONS, RUDDERS, ELEVATORS, FLAPS, SLATS, SPOILERS,
LANDING GEAR, AND THRUST REVERSERS CAN MOVE QUICKLY WHEN
YOU REMOVE HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO
PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(1) If hydraulic pressure is powered, do this step to turn off hydraulic power:
(a) Do this task: Pressure from the Rudder Hydraulic Systems A, B, and Standby -
Deactivation, TASK 27-21-00-800-802.
SUBTASK 27-21-00-730-024-002
CAUTION
DO NOT USE A LOAD OF MORE THAN 50 POUNDS ON THE RUDDER
SURFACE DURING THE TEST. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
CAUTION
USE A LOADING BLOCK AND DO NOT PUT MORE THAN 50 LBF (222 N) ON
THE RUDDER WHEN YOU MOVE THE RUDDER SURFACE BY AN
EXTERNAL FORCE. APPLY THE EXTERNAL FORCE APPROXIMATELY
BETWEEN 6 TO 8 INCHES (150 TO 200 MILLIMETERS) FROM THE BOTTOM
OF THE TRAILING EDGE AND APPROXIMATELY 3 INCHES (80
MILLIMETERS) FORWARD OF THE TRAILING EDGE. IF YOU DO NOT APPLY
FORCE AT THIS LOCATION, YOU CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE RUDDER.
(2) Do the rudder hinge friction check:
NOTE: If the dial indicator is not available, you can use a ruler to measure the rudder trailing
edge placement in this test.
NOTE: If the test is unsatisfactory, you can remove the seals between the vertical fin and the
rudder surface.
(a) Make sure the rudder and rudder pedals are in the neutral position.
(b) Make sure the rudder trim indicator is at zero units of trim.
(c) Use your hand to move the rudder slowly through full travel to the left side.
1) Make sure that there is no sign of binding, rough spots or excessive friction at any
point of travel.
Config 2
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
a) If binding or excessive friction exist, the bearings can be out of alignment,
damaged or improperly installed. Correct this condition and repeat this check.
(d) Use your hand to move the rudder slowly through full travel to the right side.
1) Make sure that there is no sign of binding, rough spots or excessive friction at any
point of travel.
a) If binding or excessive friction exist, the bearings can be out of alignment,
damaged or improperly installed. Correct this condition and repeat this check.
(e) Attach the mount, STD-1279 on the tail cone.
(f) Place the pointer of the dial indicator, STD-1238 at the lower aft corner of the rudder
trailing edge.
(g) Use a block, STD-1278 and push/pull scale 0-25 pound (0-11 kilogram), STD-753 to
move the rudder 2.25 in. (5.72 cm) ± 0.1 in. (0.25 cm) to the left side.
1) Make sure that the force to move the rudder is less than 16.30 lbf (73 N).
(h) Use a block, STD-1278 and push/pull scale 0-25 pound (0-11 kilogram), STD-753 to
move the rudder 2.25 in. (5.72 cm) ± 0.1 in. (0.25 cm) to the right side.
1) Make sure that the force to move the rudder is less than 16.30 lbf (73 N).
(i) Remove the dial indicator, STD-1238 and block, STD-1278 from the rudder.
(j) Remove the mount, STD-1279, from the tailcone.
(k) If the force to move the rudder is greater than 16.3 lbf (72.5 N), do these steps:
1) Disconnect the two ends of the standby Power Control Unit (PCU):
a) Disconnect the two ends of the PCU.
b) Move the PCU forward and to one side to let the rudder travel without
interference.
2) Disconnect the two ends of the main PCU:
a) Disconnect the two ends of the PCU.
b) Move the PCU forward and to one side to let the rudder travel without
interference.
3) Use your hand to move the rudder slowly through full travel to the left side.
a) Make sure that there is no sign of binding, rough spots or excessive friction at
any point of travel.
<1> If binding or excessive friction exist, the bearings can be out of
alignment, damaged or improperly installed. Correct this condition and
repeat this check.
4) Use your hand to move the rudder slowly through full travel to the right side.
a) Make sure that there is no sign of binding, rough spots or excessive friction at
any point of travel.
<1> If binding or excessive friction exist, the bearings can be out of
alignment, damaged or improperly installed. Correct this condition and
repeat this check.
5) Attach the mount, STD-1279, on the tailcone.
6) Place the pointer of the dial indicator, STD-1238, at the lower aft corner of the
rudder trailing edge.
Config 2
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
7) Use a block, STD-1278 and push/pull scale 0-25 pound (0-11 kilogram), STD-753 to
move the rudder:
a) Move the rudder 2.25 in. (5.72 cm) ± 0.1 in. (0.25 cm) to the left side.
b) Measure the force required to move the rudder.
c) Record this value.
d) Move the rudder 2.25 in. (5.72 cm) ± 0.1 in. (0.25 cm) to the right side.
e) Measure the force required to move the rudder.
f) Record this value.
g) If the two recorded values are more than 1 lbf (4.4 N), do these steps:
<1> Correct the faulty condition.
<2> Connect the two ends of the main PCU.
<3> Connect the two ends of the standby PCU.
<4> Do the Rudder Hinge Friction Test again from the start of the test.
h) If one of the two recorded values is less than 1 lbf (4.4 N), connect the two
ends of the main PCU.
8) Use a block, STD-1278 and push/pull scale 0-25 pound (0-11 kilogram), STD-753 to
move the rudder:
a) Move the rudder 2.25 in. (5.72 cm) ± 0.1 in. (0.25 cm) to the right side.
b) Measure the force required to move the rudder.
c) Record this value.
d) Move the rudder 2.25 in. (5.72 cm) ± 0.1 in. (0.25 cm) to the left side.
e) Measure the force required to move the rudder.
f) Record this value.
g) If the two recorded values are more than 11.49 lbf (51.1 N), the friction in the
main PCU is too high. Do these steps:
<1> Correct the faulty condition.
<2> Connect the two ends of the main PCU.
<3> Do the Rudder Hinge Friction Test again from the start of the test.
h) If the two recorded values are less than 11.49 lbf (51.1 N), the friction in the
standby PCU is too high. Do these steps:
<1> Correct the faulty condition.
<2> Connect the two ends of the standby PCU.
<3> Do the Rudder Hinge Friction Test again from the start of the test.
(l) Remove the dial indicator, STD-1238, and block, STD-1278, from the rudder.
(m) Remove the mount, STD-1279, from the tailcone.

NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. General
WARNING
FOLLOW THE STEPS IN THIS TASK IN THE ORDER THAT THEY ARE
WRITTEN. FAILURE TO DO SO CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(1) Use this test to verify that the override mechanisms installed on the torque tube are

(3) Do the rudder override operational test:
(a) Make sure the rudder and rudder pedals are in the neutral position.
(b) Manually hold the rudder aft edge in the centered position.
(c) Observe the torque tube override assemblies and do these steps:.
1) Slowly push on the captain's left rudder pedal forward full travel then return the
pedal to the neutral position.
NOTE: It will require more force than normal operation for the override mechanism
to breakout of the detent position.
2) Verify that all 3 override assemblies breakout of their detent positions.
3) Verify that there is no sign of binding or interferences at any point of travel on the
three override assemblies.
a) If binding or excessive friction exist, the override assemblies may be damaged
or improperly installed. Correct this condition and repeat this check.
(d) Observe the torque tube override assemblies and do these steps:.
Config 2

to breakout of the detent position.
2) Verify that all 3 override assemblies breakout of their detent positions.
3) Verify that there is no sign of binding or interferences at any point of travel on the
three override assemblies.
a) If binding or excessive friction exist, the override assemblies may be damaged
or improperly installed. Correct this condition and repeat this check.

E. Rudder Removal
SUBTASK 27-21-11-480-001
(1) Do these steps to install sling equipment, SPL-2033 (Figure 401):
NOTE: If you use the crane, do this step when you have enough room for the crane.
(a) Attach the master link to a load cell with a minimum capacity of 500 lb (227 kg).
(b) Install the hoist fittings on the rudder [1] with a ¼ in. (6.4 mm) drive socket.
(c) Install four ropes to make sure the rudder does not rotate and hit the airplane.
(d) Attach the sling to the hoist fittings installed on the rudder [1].
SUBTASK 27-21-11-020-003
(2) Remove the nut [46], washers [45], and bolt [44] to disconnect the bonding jumper [47] from
the vertical fin at hinge 9 (Figure 402).
SUBTASK 27-21-11-020-004
(3) Disconnect the control rod of the rudder position transmitter from the vertical fin:
(a) Remove the bolt [23], washer [24], and washer [25].
(b) Disconnect the control rod.
SUBTASK 27-21-11-020-005
CAUTION
REMOVE THE CONTROL ROD FROM THE PCU BEFORE YOU DISCONNECT
THE PCU FROM THE RUDDER. IF YOU DO NOT REMOVE THE CONTROL
ROD FIRST, DAMAGE TO THE CONTROL ROD CAN OCCUR DURING THE
CHECK.
(4) Do this step to disconnect the rudder main Power Control Unit (PCU) from the rudder [1]:
(a) Disconnect and remove the control rod (or rods) from the main PCU
(TASK 27-21-91-000-803-002).
(b) Remove the nut [15], washer [14], nut [13], washer [12], bushing [11], bolt [10], and
bolt [9].
SUBTASK 27-21-11-020-006
(5) Do this step to disconnect the rudder standby PCU from the rudder [1]:
(a) Remove the nut [29], washer [28], bushing [50], washer [27], and bolt [26].
SUBTASK 27-21-11-020-007
(6) Move the rudder [1] to the neutral position.
SUBTASK 27-21-11-020-014
WARNING
DO NOT LIFT THE RUDDER WITH A FORCE THAT IS MORE THAN 257-LBS.
IF YOU USE A FORCE THAT IS MORE THAN 257-LBS, IT CAN CAUSE
DAMAGE TO THE AIRPLANE AND INJURY TO PERSONNEL.
(7) Lift the rudder [1] until the load is removed from its hinges.
SUBTASK 27-21-11-020-008
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT THE CRANE WILL HOLD THE RUDDER IN A STABLE
POSITION WHEN YOU REMOVE THE HINGE BOLTS. ACCIDENTAL RUDDER
MOVEMENT WHEN YOU DISCONNECT IT FROM THE AIRPLANE CAN
CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(8) Remove the hinge bolts from the hinges:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) At hinges 1, 4, 5, 6, and 8, remove the pins [35], nuts [34], washers [33], bushings [32],
washers [31], and bolts [30] from the hinges.
1) Discard the pins [35].
(b) At hinge 7, remove the pin [43], nut [42], washer [41], washer [39], bushing [38],
washer [37], and bolt [36] from the hinge.
1) Discard the pin [43].
(c) At hinge 2, remove the pin [2], nut [3], washer [4], spacer [5], bushing [6], washer [7], and
bolt [8] from the hinge.
1) Discard the pin [2].
(d) At hinge 3, remove the pin [22], nut [21], washer [20], adjustment bushing [19],
bushing [18], washer [17], and bolt [16] from the hinge.
1) Discard the pin [22].
(e) At hinge 9, remove the pin [35], nut [34], washer [33], bushing [32], washer [31], and
bolt [30] from the hinge.
1) Discard the pin [35].
SUBTASK 27-21-11-020-009
CAUTION
YOU MUST MOVE THE RUDDER UP BEFORE YOU REMOVE IT FROM THE
VERTICAL FIN. IF YOU DO NOT MOVE THE RUDDER UP, YOU CAN CAUSE
DAMAGE TO THE RUDDER TIP.
(9) Do this step to remove the rudder [1]:
(a) Use the load cell to make sure that the force used to lift the rudder [1] is not more than
257 lb (117 kg).
(b) Move the rudder [1] up and aft from the vertical fin and lower to the ground.

F. Rudder Installation
CAUTION
BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU MOVE THE RUDDER. IF THE CONTROL ROD
HITS THE VERTICAL STABILIZER, DAMAGE CAN OCCUR.
SUBTASK 27-21-11-820-004
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT YOU HAVE THE RUDDER BALANCED. IF NOT
BALANCED, THE RUDDER CAN CAUSE UNWANTED FLUTTER AND
INSTABILITY OF THE AIRPLANE. THIS CAN CAUSE AN IN-FLIGHT
EMERGENCY. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THESE INSTRUCTIONS, INJURY TO
PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(1) Balance and stamp the rudder assembly with the new static balance hinge moment if you
install a reworked, repaired, repainted, or new rudder assembly (SRM 51-60-07).
SUBTASK 27-21-11-860-003
(2) Loosen all the seals at the trailing edge of the fin and move them fully forward.
SUBTASK 27-21-11-420-001
(3) Do these steps to put the rudder [1] in its position and connect the hinges:
NOTE: A maximum of two washers are allowed under the bolt head or two washers under the
nut. No more than three washers are allowed on any individual bolt unless relief for the
bolt is necessary. A maximum of four washers are allowed on an individual bolt if one
each is used for fillet distortion compensation, fillet relief, finish protection, and grip
adjustment or counterbore substitution.
(a) Apply a thin layer of grease, D00633, to the smooth surfaces of all the hinge bolts (outer
diameter), bushings (inner diameter), and bearings before you install them.
(b) Put sling equipment, SPL-2033, in its position and connect it to the rudder [1]
(Figure 401).
1) Make sure that a load cell with a minimum capacity of 500 lb (227 kg) is attached to
the master link.
WARNING
DO NOT LIFT THE RUDDER WITH A FORCE THAT IS MORE THAN 257-
LBS. IF YOU USE A FORCE THAT IS MORE THAN 257-LBS, IT CAN
CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE AIRPLANE AND INJURY TO PERSONNEL.
(c) Lift the rudder [1] to its position on the vertical fin.
1) Use the load cell to make sure that the force used to lift the rudder [1] is not more
than 257 lb (117 kg).
2) Use the ropes to make sure that the rudder does not hit the airplane.
(d) Install the bolts, washers, spacers, and bushings that follow (Figure 402):
1) At hinges 1, 4, 5, 6, 8, and 9, install the bushings [32], washers [31], and bolts [30]
to the hinge fittings.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
2) At hinge 2, install the spacer [5] (under the fitting), bushing [6], washer [7], and
bolt [8] to the hinge fitting.
3) At hinge 3, install the bushing [18], washer [17], and bolt [16] to the hinge fitting.
4) At hinge 7, install the bushing [38], washer [37], and bolt [36] to the hinge fitting.
(e) Release the rudder [1] slowly until the load is on its hinges.
(f) Make sure that the torque required to rotate the bolts is less than 100 in-lb (11.3 N·m).
(g) Install the nuts, washers, and pins in the order that follow:
1) At hinge 2, install the washer [4] (above the fitting) and nut [3].
a) Tighten the nut [3] to 150 in-lb (16.9 N·m) – 200 in-lb (22.6 N·m).
NOTE: Tighten the nut [3] to the lower end of the torque range. Continue to
tighten the nut until the next castellation aligns with the hole in the
bolt [8].
b) Install the new pin [2].
2) At hinges 1, 4, 5, 6, 8, and 9, install the washers [33] and nuts [34].
a) Tighten the nuts [34] to 150 in-lb (16.9 N·m) – 200 in-lb (22.6 N·m).
NOTE: Tighten the nuts [34] to the lower end of the torque range. Continue to
tighten the nut until the next castellation aligns with the hole in the
bolts [30].
b) Install the new pin [35].
3) At hinge 3, do these steps:
a) Install the bushing [19] at hinge 3.
b) Adjust the bushing until it is against the fin bearing with finger tight pressure
only.
c) Install the washers [20] and nut [21].
d) Tighten the nut [21] to 150 in-lb (16.9 N·m) – 200 in-lb (22.6 N·m).
NOTE: Tighten the nut [21] to the lower end of the torque range. Continue to
tighten the nut until the next castellation aligns with the hole in the
bolts [16].
e) Install the new pin [22].
f) Install MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, from the bushing [19] to hinge fitting.
g) Fill the holes of MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, with sealant, A00247.
4) At hinge 7, install the washer [39], washer [41], and nut [42].
a) Tighten the nut [42] to 150 in-lb (16.9 N·m) – 200 in-lb (22.6 N·m).
NOTE: Tighten the nut [42] to the lower end of the torque range. Continue to
tighten the nut until the next castellation aligns with the hole in the
bolt [36].
b) Install the new pin [43].
SUBTASK 27-21-11-420-002
(4) Connect the control rod for the rudder position transmitter to the vertical fin:
(a) Install the washer [25], washer [24], and bolt [23].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-21-11-420-003
(5) Install the bolt [44], washers [45], and nut [46] to connect the bonding jumper [47] to the
vertical fin at hinge 9.
(a) Use the intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550, ohmmeter to make sure
there is a maximum of 0.010 ohm between the vertical fin and the rudder [1].
SUBTASK 27-21-11-620-001
(6) Apply sealant, A00247, to both ends of the bonding jumper [47] and their fasteners.
SUBTASK 27-21-11-080-002
(7) Remove sling equipment, SPL-2033.
(a) Remove the load cell from the master link.
SUBTASK 27-21-11-080-003
(8) Remove the hoist fittings.
SUBTASK 27-21-11-220-004
(9) Make sure that there is clearance between all the seals and the forward part of the rudder and
the balance weight.
(a) Manually move the rudder approximately 7 degrees in each direction to examine the
clearance.
SUBTASK 27-21-11-710-001
(10) Move the rudder to the left and right from the neutral position.
(a) Make sure that rudder moves left and right a minimum of 30 degrees from the neutral
position.
SUBTASK 27-21-11-420-004
(11) Do this step to connect the rudder standby Power Control Unit (PCU) to the rudder [1]:
(a) Install the bolt [26], washer [27], bushing [50], washer [28], and nut [29].
1) Tighten the nut [29] to 350 in-lb (39.5 N·m) – 400 in-lb (45.2 N·m).
SUBTASK 27-21-11-420-005
(12) Do these steps to connect the rudder main PCU to the rudder [1]:
(a) Install the bushing [11], bolt [10], bolt [9], washer [12], and nut [13].
1) Tighten the nut [13] to 900 in-lb (102 N·m) – 1050 in-lb (119 N·m).
CAUTION
DO NOT TIGHTEN THE NUT [13] AFTER YOU TIGHTEN THE NUT[15].
YOU CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(b) Install the washer [14] and nut [15].
1) Tighten the nut [15] to 450 in-lb (51 N·m) – 550 in-lb (62 N·m).
(c) Install the control rod (or rods) that you removed between the torque tube and the main
PCU (TASK 27-21-91-400-803-002).
SUBTASK 27-21-11-220-005
(13) Make sure that the mismatch between the rudder and the vertical fin is correct at each of rib
locations (View C-C, Figure 402).
SUBTASK 27-21-11-820-001
(14) Adjust the seals at the trailing edge of the vertical fin and tighten them (View J, View K and
View D-D, Figure 402).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-21-11-820-002
(15) Adjust the balance weight seals on the vertical fin and tighten the seal retainers (View I and
View B-B, Figure 402).
SUBTASK 27-21-11-820-003
(16) Adjust the seal compression for the lower (rudder to body) seal (View K, View D-D, and View
E-E, Figure 402):
(a) Move the rudder to its neutral position.
(b) Make sure that the seals contact and that the seal compression is 0.00 in. (0.00 mm) –
-0.04 in. (-1.02 mm).
(c) If it is necessary, do these steps to adjust the seal:
1) Loosen the bolts [48] and bolts [49] from the seal.
2) Adjust the seal until they both contact and the seal compression is 0.00 in.
(0.00 mm) – -0.04 in. (-1.02 mm).
3) Tighten the bolts [48] and bolts [49].
(d) Make sure that the seal does not cause a blockage at the left and right rudder drain
holes.
SUBTASK 27-21-11-860-004

SUBTASK 27-21-24-020-001
(1) Disconnect the hydraulic lines [12] from the power control unit [4].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU CAREFULLY DRAIN HYDRAULIC FLUID INTO A
SUITABLE CONTAINER. CAREFULLY CLEAN, DRY, AND DISPOSE OF
ALL LEAKAGE. HYDRAULIC FLUID CAUSES DAMAGE TO RUBBER,
COPPER, PLASTICS, PAINTS, AND MANY OTHER MATERIALS.
(a) Put a oil resistant container, STD-203, below the hydraulic connections.
(b) Disconnect the hydraulic lines [12] from the power control unit [4].
(c) Install the plugs and caps to the hydraulic lines [12] and ports.
(d) Install a tag on the hydraulic lines [12] to make sure that you install them correctly.
1) Discard the packing [3] and packing [11].
SUBTASK 27-21-24-020-002
(2) Disconnect the electrical connector [1] from the power control unit [4].
SUBTASK 27-21-24-020-003
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU REMOVE THE VERNIER CONTROL ROD FROM THE
PCU BEFORE YOU DISCONNECT THE PCU FROM THE RUDDER. IF YOU
DO NOT REMOVE THE VERNIER CONTROL ROD FIRST, IT CAN CAUSE
DAMAGE TO THE VERNIER CONTROL ROD.
(3) Disconnect the vernier control rod [9] from the power control unit [4].
(a) Remove the nut [8], washer [7], washer [6], and bolt [5] to disconnect the control rod [9]
from the power control unit [4].
(b) Remove the nut [28], washer [27], washer [26], and bolt [25] to disconnect the control
rod [9] from the power control unit [4].
(c) Remove the control rod [9] from the airplane.
SUBTASK 27-21-24-020-004
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU MOVE THE PCU CAREFULLY DURING THE
REMOVAL OR INSTALLATION OF THE PCU. THE PCU CAN HIT THE BOLTS.
THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE BOLTS.
(4) Remove the power control unit [4].
(a) Remove the nut [24], washer [23], bushing [22], washer [21], and bolt [20] to disconnect
the power control unit [4] from the rudder.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU HOLD THE STANDBY RUDDER PCU DURING
THE REMOVAL OF THE STANDBY RUDDER PCU. THE STANDBY
RUDDER PCU CAN FALL AND CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE STANDBY
RUDDER PCU.
(b) Remove the nut [19], washer [18], washer [17], bushing [16], bushing [15], washer [14],
and bolt [13] that attach the power control unit [4] to the airplane structure.
(c) Remove the power control unit [4] from the airplane.

F. Rudder Pedals Installation
SUBTASK 27-21-31-480-003
(1) Make sure that the rig pin R-3 from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585 is installed in the captain's
rudder forward quadrant.
SUBTASK 27-21-31-480-004
(2) Make sure that the rig pin R-4 from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585 is installed in the first officer's
rudder forward quadrant.
SUBTASK 27-21-31-420-001
(3) Install the rudder pedals [12]:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Put the spacers [15] and bearings [18] into the rudder pedals [12].
(b) Put the inboard rudder pedal between the support structure and align the holes.
(c) Put the washer [17] on the support shaft [16].
(d) Install the support shaft [16] from the inboard side through the hole in the support
structures and through the bushing [14] and rudder pedal [12].
(e) Install the bushing [14] on the support shaft [16].
(f) Install the washer [17] and nut [13] on the support shaft [16].
1) Tighten the nut [13] to 200 in-lb (22.6 N·m) -500 in-lb (56.5 N·m).
(g) Make sure the support shaft [16] is not free to turn in the support structures.
SUBTASK 27-21-31-820-001
(4) Do these steps to adjust the rudder pedal position:
(a) Turn the rudder pedal adjustment crank full clockwise for the installed rudder pedals until
the jackshaft is in its full forward position.
(b) Turn the rudder pedal adjustment crank 4 turns counterclockwise.
(c) If you install the captain's rudder pedals [12], then install the rig pin R-1 from the test set
rigging pin kit, SPL-1585 in the captain's rudder pedals [12].
(d) If you install the first officer's rudder pedals [12], then install the rig pin R-2 from the test
set rigging pin kit, SPL-1585 in the first officer's rudder pedals [12].
SUBTASK 27-21-31-820-002
(5) Do these steps to adjust the two rudder pedal tension rods [4]:
(a) Loosen the jamnuts [5] on the two rudder pedal tension rods [4].
(b) Turn the rudder pedal tension rods [4] until you can attach them to the rudder pedals [12].
(c) Make sure you can see the rod end threads through the inspection holes at two ends of
the rudder pedal tension rods [4] after the adjustment.
(d) Make sure that the threads show in at least one-half of the inspection hole.
(e) Tighten the jamnuts [5] on the rudder pedal tension rods [4].
SUBTASK 27-21-31-420-002
(6) Install the bolts [1], washers [2], nuts [3] and pin [3A] to connect the two rudder pedal tension
rods [4] to the rudder pedals [12].
SUBTASK 27-21-31-420-009
(7) Install the brackets [20] and the screws [19] on the rudder pedals [12].
SUBTASK 27-21-31-420-003
(8) Install the bolts [7], bushings [8], washers [9], and nuts [10] to connect the two brake
pushrods [11] to the bellcranks [6].
(a) Adjust the length of the brake pushrods [11] if it is necessary.
 ALL PRE SB 737-27A1314
SUBTASK 27-21-31-420-004
(9) Install top cover and shrouds. Do the following steps:
(a) Put the top cover [21] on the lower cover [32].
(b) Attach the pedal adjustment cable to the top cover [21].
1) Install bolt [34] through clamp on pedal adjustment cable [35] and into cable
standoff on top cover [21].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
 ALL PRE SB 737-27A1314 (Continued)
(c) Install screws [22], screws [29] and washers [23] to attach the top cover [21] to the lower
cover [32].
WARNING
MAKE SURE THE SCREWS THAT ATTACH THE PEDAL SHROUDS ARE
INSTALLED, SEATED, AND TIGHTENED TO THE CORRECT TORQUE. IF
THE SCREWS ARE NOT INSTALLED CORRECTLY, THEY CAN CAUSE
INTERFERENCE WITH THE MOTION OF THE RUDDER PEDALS. THIS
CAUSES A DANGEROUS FLIGHT CONDITION.
(d) Install screws [24] to attach the outboard pedal shroud [26] to the top cover [21].
1) Tighten the screws to a torque of 35 ±1 in-lb (4 ±0 N·m) (Standard Torque Values,
TASK 20-50-11-910-801).
2) Make sure there is no gap between the outboard pedal shroud [26] and the top
cover [21] at each screw [24] location.
NOTE: Pedal shroud is flexible and can push back from top cover during
installation of fasteners.
WARNING
MAKE SURE THE SCREWS THAT ATTACH THE PEDAL SHROUDS ARE
INSTALLED, SEATED, AND TIGHTENED TO THE CORRECT TORQUE. IF
THE SCREWS ARE NOT INSTALLED CORRECTLY, THEY CAN CAUSE

2) Make sure there is no gap between the inboard pedal shroud [27] and the top

NOTE: Pedal shroud is flexible and can push back from top cover during

D. Crank Assembly Removal
SUBTASK 27-21-41-020-001
(1) Do these steps to remove the crank lever [10]:
(a) Remove the nut [8] and washer [9] from the crank lever [10].
(b) Remove the crank lever [10] from the bearing retainer [12].
(c) Remove the spacer [11].
SUBTASK 27-21-41-020-002
(2) Do these steps to remove the rudder pedal adjustment cable [1] from the crank lever [10]:
(a) Remove the lockwire from the cable retaining nut [13].
(b) Loosen the cable retaining nut [13].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

support bracket [7].
SUBTASK 27-21-41-020-003
(3) Do these steps to disconnect the rudder pedal adjustment cable [1] from the rudder
jackshaft [4]:
(a) Loosen the retaining nut [3] at the rudder jackshaft [4].
(b) Hold the retaining nut [3] and pull the rudder pedal adjustment cable [1] from the rudder
jackshaft [4].
(c) Remove the retaining nut [3] and washer [2].
SUBTASK 27-21-41-020-004
(4) Do these steps to remove the rudder pedal adjustment cable [1]:
(a) Remove the bolts [5] from the cable clamps [6].
(b) Remove the cable clamps [6] and keep a record of their locations.
(c) Remove the elastic grommet.
(d) Pull the rudder pedal adjustment cable [1] through the grommet hole.
(e) Remove the rudder pedal adjustment cable [1].
