F. Rudder Pedal Adjustment Crank Installation
SUBTASK 27-21-41-420-001
(1) Do these steps to install the rudder pedal adjustment cable [1]:
(a) Install the grommet on the rudder pedal adjustment cable [1].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) Push the rudder pedal adjustment cable [1] through the grommet hole.
NOTE: One end of the cable should reach the crank lever and the other end should
reach the rudder jackshaft.
(c) Install the cable clamps [6] and bolts [5] on the rudder pedal adjustment cable [1].
1) Make sure that the cable radius is more than 5.0 in. (127 mm) for all the curves in
the cable.
NOTE: If the rudder pedal adjustment cable radius is less than 5.0 in. (127 mm),
the rudder pedal adjustment will not operate correctly.
SUBTASK 27-21-41-420-002
(2) Connect the rudder pedal adjustment cable [1] to the rudder jackshaft [4]:
(a) Put the washer [2] and retaining nut [3] on the rudder pedal adjustment cable [1].
(b) Put the rudder pedal adjustment cable [1] through the rudder jackshaft [4].
(c) Apply a thin layer of grease, D00013, to the outside diameter of the rudder pedal
adjustment cable [1] before it is installed in the rudder jackshaft [4].
(d) Do these steps:
1) Install the alignment tool alignment tool, B27064-5, SPL-1689, through the hole in
the bottom of the rudder jackshaft [4] to hold the jackshaft universal joint in its
position.
2) Turn the rudder pedal adjustment cable [1] end until it engages the jackshaft pin.
3) Use the crowfoot wrench, B27064-13, SPL-11751, or crowfoot wrench, STD-24936,
to hold the retaining nut [3].
4) Use the flare nut wrench, B27064-14, SPL-11752, or crowfoot wrench, STD-24937,
to hold the sleeve of the rudder pedal adjustment cable [1].
(e) Tighten the retaining nut [3].
1) Tighten the retaining nut [3] to 90 in-lb (10.2 N·m) - 400 in-lb (45.2 N·m) before it
touches the jackshaft support.
2) Turn the retaining nut [3] 1/4 to 1/2 of a turn more when it touches the jackshaft
support.
SUBTASK 27-21-41-420-003
(3) Do these steps to connect the rudder pedal adjustment cable [1] to the crank lever [10]:
(a) Put the cable retaining nut [13] on one end of the rudder pedal adjustment cable [1].
(b) Push the rudder pedal adjustment cable [1] through the bearing retainer [12].
(c) Tighten the cable retaining nut [13].
1) Tighten the cable retaining nut [13] finger tight plus one quarter turn.
(d) Install the MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, on the retaining nut [13].
NOTE: To get the best lockwire angle, make sure that the aft cable assembly can turn
easily and smoothly.
SUBTASK 27-21-41-420-004
(4) Do these steps to install the crank lever [10]:
(a) Install the spacer [11] on the rudder pedal adjustment cable [1].
(b) Install the crank lever [10], washer [9], and nut [8].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-21-41-410-001
(5) Close the main instrument panel module assembly [14].
SUBTASK 27-21-41-410-002
WARNING
MAKE SURE THE SCREWS THAT ATTACH THE PEDAL SHROUDS ARE
INSTALLED, SEATED, AND TIGHTENED TO THE CORRECT TORQUE. IF THE
SCREWS ARE NOT INSTALLED CORRECTLY, THEY CAN CAUSE
INTERFERENCE WITH THE MOTION OF THE RUDDER PEDALS. THIS
CAUSES A DANGEROUS FLIGHT CONDITION.

F. Rudder Forward Quadrant Removal
(Figure 402, Figure 403)
SUBTASK 27-21-51-010-004
WARNING
YOU MUST LOOSEN AND DISCONNECT THE RUDDER CABLES FROM THE
RUDDER FORWARD QUADRANTS BEFORE YOU DISCONNECT THE BUS
ROD. RELIEVE TENSION UNIFORMLY IN THE TWO RUDDER CABLES. IF
YOU DO NOT LOOSEN THE RUDDER CABLES EQUALLY, IT CAN CAUSE
INJURY TO PERSONNEL OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(1) Loosen the turnbuckles [91] for the rudder cable RB [21] and rudder cable RA [22]
(Figure 403).
SUBTASK 27-21-51-020-002
(2) Disconnect the applicable rudder cable from the rudder forward quadrant [39] that you will
remove (Figure 402):
(a) Remove the bolt [30] and washer [31] from the cable retainer [32] (Control Cable End
Retaining Plate - Removal, TASK 20-10-96-000-801).
(b) Remove the cable RB [21] or cable RA [22] from the rudder forward quadrant [39].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-21-51-020-003
(3) Remove the pins [44], nuts [43], washers [42], and bolts [41] to disconnect the rudder pedal
tension rods [40] from the rudder forward quadrant [39]. Discard the pins [44].

rod [50] from the rudder forward quadrant [39]. Discard the pin [49].

floor beam structure.
SUBTASK 27-21-51-020-005

bracket [74] from the structure.
SUBTASK 27-21-51-020-006
(7) Pull the adjustment shaft [75] and the adjustment shaft support bracket [74] forward to
disengage the adjustment shaft [75] from the rudder forward quadrant [39].
SUBTASK 27-21-51-020-007
(8) Remove the nuts [54], washers [53], and screws [52] to remove the cable guard [51].
SUBTASK 27-21-51-020-008
(9) If you remove the captain's rudder forward quadrant [39], then do these steps:
(a) Remove the lockwire from the rudder pedal steering arm [24].
(b) Remove the screws [68] and washers [69] to disconnect the rudder pedal steering arm
[24] from the rudder forward quadrant [39].
(c) Move the rudder pedal steering arm [24] out of the way.
(d) Hold the rudder forward quadrant [39] and remove the jackshaft support channel [70]:
NOTE: The rudder forward quadrant is free to fall from the upper bearing housing after
you remove the screws.
1) Remove the nuts [60], washers [59], and screws [58].
2) Remove the nut [63], washer [62], and screw [61].
(e) Remove the rudder forward quadrant [39] from the airplane:
1) Move the rudder forward quadrant [39] in an aft and outboard direction to clear the
floor beam penetration, and remove it from the airplane.
(f) Do these steps to remove the lower bearing housing [67] from the jackshaft support
channel [74]:
1) Remove the nuts [57], washers [56], and bolts [55].
2) Remove the nut [66], washer [65], and bolt [64].
SUBTASK 27-21-51-020-009

quadrant [23] from the rudder forward quadrant [39].
(c) Hold the rudder forward quadrant [39] and remove the jackshaft support channel [76]:
NOTE: The rudder forward quadrant [39] is free to fall from the upper bearing housing
after you remove the bolts and screws.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Remove the nuts [60], washers [59], and screws [58].
2) Remove the nuts [85], washers [84], and bolts [83].
3) Remove the support [86].
4) Remove the nut [63], washer [62], and screw [61].
(d) Remove the rudder forward quadrant [39] from the airplane:
1) Move the rudder forward quadrant [39] in an aft and outboard direction to clear the
floor beam penetration, and remove it from the airplane.
(e) Do these steps to remove the lower bearing housing [67] from the jackshaft support
channel [39]:
1) Remove the nuts [57], washers [56], and bolts [55].
2) Remove the nut [66], washer [65], and bolt [64].

SUBTASK 27-21-51-420-001
(1) If you install the captain's rudder forward quadrant [39], then do these steps (Figure 402):

 ALL

thru the floor beam penetration.

2) Install the screw [61], washer [62], and nut [63].
(d) Install the screws [68] and washers [69] to connect the rudder pedal steering arm [24] to
the rudder forward quadrant [39].
1) Install the MS20995NC32 lockwire, G01912.
(e) Install the screws [52], washers [53], and nuts [5] to attach the cable guard [51] to the
jackshaft support channel [70].
SUBTASK 27-21-51-420-002
(2) If you install the first officer's rudder forward quadrant [3], then do these steps:
(a) Install the lower bearing housing [67] to the jackshaft support channel [76] if it is
necessary:
1) Put the lower bearing housing [67] on the jackshaft support channel [76].
2) Install the bolts [55], washers [56], and nuts [57].
3) Install the bolt [64], washer [65], and nut [66].
(b) Put the rudder forward quadrant [39] in the upper bearing housing and quadrant arm thru
the floor beam penetration.
(c) Attach the jackshaft support channel [76] to the airplane structure:
1) Install the screws [58], washers [59], and nuts [60].
2) Install the screw [61], washer [62], and nut [63].
(d) Attach the support [86] to the jackshaft support channel [76]:
1) Install the bolts [83], washers [84], and nuts [85].
(e) Connect the rudder pedal position sensor quadrant [23] to the rudder forward quadrant
[39].
1) Install the screws [77] and washers [78].
2) Install the MS20995NC32 lockwire, G01912.
(f) Install the screws [52], washers [53], and nuts [54] to attach the cable guard [51] to the
jackshaft support channel [76].
SUBTASK 27-21-51-480-001
(3) Install the rig pin R-3 from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585 in the forward rig pin hole of the
captain's rudder forward quadrant [39].
SUBTASK 27-21-51-480-002
(4) Install rig pin R-4 from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585 in the forward rig pin hole of the first
officer's rudder forward quadrant [39].
SUBTASK 27-21-51-820-006
(5) Make sure that the clearance between the cable guard block [26] and the rudder forward
quadrant [39] is 0.030 in. (0.762 mm) to 0.050 in. (1.270 mm).
(a) If it is necessary, add or remove the shims [27]:
1) Remove the nuts [29], washers [28], and bolts [25] from the cable guard block [26].
2) Add or remove the shims [27] laminations.

 ALL
3) Install the bolts [25], washers [28], and nuts [29] to the cable guard block [26].
SUBTASK 27-21-51-420-003
(6) Temporarily install the bolt [45] to connect the bus rod [50] to the rudder forward quadrant [39].
(a) If it is necessary, adjust the bus rod [50] until the rig pins R-3 and R-4 move freely.
SUBTASK 27-21-51-420-004
(7) Install the bolts [41], washers [42], nuts [43], and pins [44] to connect the rudder pedal tension
rods [40] to the rudder forward quadrant [39].
(a) If it is necessary, adjust the length of the rudder pedal tension rods.
SUBTASK 27-21-51-080-002
(8) Remove the rig pins R-3, R-4.
SUBTASK 27-21-51-420-011
(9) If you install the captain's rudder forward quadrant, then do these steps:
(a) Move the captain's rudder forward quadrant [39] until it touches the quadrant stop [35].
(b) Make sure that you can install the rig pin R-3 easily in the aft rig pin hole.
1) If it is necessary, add or remove the shims [34]:
a) Remove the nuts [38], washers [37], bolts [36], and fillers [33] from the
quadrant stops [35].
b) Add or remove the shims [34] laminations.
c) Install the fillers [33], bolts [36], washers [37], and nuts [38] to the quadrant
stops [35].
(c) Remove the rig pin R-3.
SUBTASK 27-21-51-420-012
(10) If you install the first officer's rudder forward quadrant, then do these steps:
(a) Move the first officer's rudder forward quadrant [39] until it touches the quadrant stop [35].
(b) Make sure that you can install the rig pin R-4 easily in the aft rig pin hole.
1) If it is necessary, add or remove the shims [34]:
a) Remove the nuts [38], washers [37], bolts [36], and fillers [33] from the
quadrant stops [35].
b) Add or remove the shims [34] laminations.
c) Install the fillers [33], bolts [36], washers [37], and nuts [38] to the quadrant
stops [35].
(c) Remove the rig pin R-4.
SUBTASK 27-21-51-480-005
(11) Install the rig pin R-3 in the forward rig pin hole of the captain's rudder forward quadrant.
SUBTASK 27-21-51-480-006
(12) Install the rig pin R-4 in the forward rig pin hole of the first officer's rudder forward quadrant.
SUBTASK 27-21-51-420-005
(13) Connect the adjustment shaft [75] to the rudder forward quadrant [39]:
(a) Put the adjustment shaft [75] into the rudder forward quadrant's universal joint [39].
NOTE: The slot in the adjustment shaft must engage with the pin in the hole.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-21-51-420-006
(14) Install the bolts [71], washers [72], and nuts [73] to attach the adjustment shaft support bracket
[74] to the structure.
SUBTASK 27-21-51-420-013
(15) Install the bolts [88], washers [89], and nuts [90] to attach the cover assembly [87] to the floor
beam structure.
SUBTASK 27-21-51-860-002
(16) Do these steps to put the rudder pedals to the neutral position:
(a) Turn the adjustment crank clockwise for the rudder pedals to the full forward position.
(b) Turn the adjustment crank back four turns from the full forward position, to get to the
neutral position.
SUBTASK 27-21-51-820-004
(17) Do this task: Rudder Pedals Adjustment, TASK 27-21-00-820-807-002.
SUBTASK 27-21-51-420-007
(18) Connect the bus rod [50] to the rudder forward quadrant [39]:

(b) Turn the bus rod [50] two full turns to make it shorter.
(c) Make sure that you can see the threads of the two bus rod [50] ends through the holes in

(d) Install the bolt [45], spacers [46], washer [47], nut [48], and pin [49] to connect the bus
rod [50] to the rudder forward quadrant [39].
SUBTASK 27-21-51-420-008
(19) Install the bolt [30], washer [31], and cable retainer [32] to connect the applicable rudder cable
to the rudder forward quadrant [39] (Control Cable End Retaining Plate - Installation,
TASK 20-10-96-400-801).
SUBTASK 27-21-51-420-009

SUBTASK 27-21-61-860-002
(1) Make sure that pressure to the rudder hydraulic systems A, B, and Standby is removed, do this
task: Pressure from the Rudder Hydraulic Systems A, B, and Standby - Deactivation,
TASK 27-21-00-800-802.
SUBTASK 27-21-61-420-001
(2) Install the rudder aft quadrant, do these steps:
(a) Put the washer [21], plate [18], and right bearing housing [27] on the right side of the
quadrant shaft [17].
1) Make sure that the countersunk side of the washer [21] points to the center of the
quadrant shaft [17].
(b) Install the washer [22] and nut [23] on the right side of the quadrant shaft [17].
1) Torque the nut [23] to 190 in-lb (21.5 N·m) - 280 in-lb (31.6 N·m).
(c) Install a new cotter pin [24].
(d) Put all the parts through the access hole.
(e) Move the quadrant [20] onto the quadrant shaft [17].

 ALL
(f) Install the bolts [4], spacers [8], washers [5], washers [6], and nuts [7] to attach the
quadrant [20] to the quadrant shaft [17].
(g) Put the left bearing housing [19] on the left side of the quadrant shaft [17].
(h) Put the quadrant shaft [17] and plate [18] in its position.
(i) Install the bolts [25] and washers [26] to attach the left bearing housing [19] and right
bearing housing [27] to the airplane structure.
SUBTASK 27-21-61-420-002
(3) Turn the quadrant shaft [17].
(a) Make sure that the quadrant shaft [17] moves freely in the left bearing housing [19] and
right bearing housing [27].
SUBTASK 27-21-61-420-003
(4) Connect the cable RA [2] and cable RB [1] to the quadrant [20].
(a) Install the cable retainers [10], bolts [9], washers [11], and nuts [12]
(TASK 20-10-96-400-801).
SUBTASK 27-21-61-420-004
(5) Tighten the turnbuckles [3] until the cable RA [2] and cable RB [1] are not loose.
SUBTASK 27-21-61-420-005

rudder PCU control rod [3] from the center crank [29].

E. Rudder Control Torque Tube Installation
SUBTASK 27-21-71-420-006-002
(1) Install the rudder control torque tube [1]:
(a) Make sure that the plate [40], lower bearing housing [21], retainer [41], and plate [42] are
in their positions on the rudder control torque tube [1].
(b) Put the rudder control torque tube [1] through the structural cutouts, center crank [29],
upper crank [34], and upper bearing housing [35]].
(c) Install the bolts [37], washers [38], and nuts [39] to attach the lower bearing housing [21]
to the airplane structure.
(d) Install the center crank [29] on the rudder control torque tube [1]:
1) Put the center cranks [29] in the original position on the rudder control torque
tube [1].
2) Install the bolts [24], bolts [28], washers [25], washers [26], and nuts [27] to attach
the center cranks [29] to the rudder control torque tube [1].
3) Tighten the nuts [27] to 15 in-lb (1.69 N·m)–25 in-lb (2.82 N·m) above the run-on
torque.
(e) Install the upper crank [34] to the rudder control torque tube [1]:
1) Put the upper crank [34] in the original position on the rudder control torque tube [1].
2) Install the bolt [24], bolt [28], washers [25], washers [26], and nuts [27] to attach the
upper crank [34] to the rudder control torque tube [1].
Config 2
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
3) Tighten the nuts [27] to 15 in-lb (1.69 N·m)-25 in-lb (2.82 N·m) above the run-on
torque.
SUBTASK 27-21-71-710-004-002
(2) Make sure the rudder control torque tube [1] turns freely and that there is no play in the
horizontal and vertical directions.
(a) If the rudder control torque tube [1] does not turn freely, do a check of the lower bearing
housing [21] and upper bearing housing [35] installation.
SUBTASK 27-21-71-420-007-002
(3) Install the bolt assembly [30], washer [31] (under the bolt), washer [32] (under the nut), and
nut [33] to connect the standby rudder PCU control rod [2] to the upper crank [34].
SUBTASK 27-21-71-420-008-002
(4) Install the bolt assemblies [30], washers [31] (under the bolt), washers [32] (under the nut), and
nut [33] to connect the main rudder PCU control rods [3] to the center cranks [29].
SUBTASK 27-21-71-420-009-002
(5) Install the rudder trim actuator [18], do this task: Rudder Trim Actuator Installation,
TASK 27-21-87-400-801.
SUBTASK 27-21-71-420-010-002
(6) Install the bolt [9], washer [10], and nut [11] to connect the aft quadrant control rod [12] to the
lower crank [20].
SUBTASK 27-21-71-420-011-002
(7) Connect the control rod [8] to the lower crank [20]:

1) Tighten the nut [6] to 45 in-lb (5.1 N·m)-60 in-lb (6.8 N·m).
CAUTION
DO NOT TRY TO TIGHTEN THE NUT [6] AGAIN AFTER YOU TIGHTEN
THE NUT [7]. YOU CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT.

SUBTASK 27-21-82-020-002
(1) Disconnect the nose gear steering from the rudder system by rotating the towing handle,
located on the left-hand side of the nose gear, to the TOW Position. (NOSE WHEEL
STEERING SYSTEM - ADJUSTMENT/TEST, PAGEBLOCK 32-51-00/501)
NOTE: It is not necessary to disconnect the steering if the airplane is on jacks and the nose
landing gear is fully extended.
SUBTASK 27-21-82-860-004

TASK 27-21-00-800-801.
SUBTASK 27-21-82-700-001
(3) Test the Feel and Centering System:
(a) Operate the rudder pedals through their full travel range three times.
(b) Make sure the rudder trim indicator shows zero units of trim.
(c) Push the captain's left rudder pedal forward approximately 0.5 in. (13 mm) and release it.
1) Make sure each side of the rudder trailing edge aligns with the tab on the rudder
index plate.
(d) Push the captain's right rudder pedal forward approximately 0.5 in. (13 mm) and release
it.
1) Make sure each side of the rudder trailing edge aligns with the tab on the rudder
index plate.
SUBTASK 27-21-82-730-002

E. Spring Assembly Removal
SUBTASK 27-21-82-860-009
(1) Do the steps to reduce the preload on the spring assembly [50]:
(a) Make sure the roller that is in the arm assembly of the rudder feel and centering unit is
centered within the detent of the cam.
NOTE: The cam is attached to the main shaft of the rudder feel and centering unit.
(b) If necessary, move the rudder by hand in the LEFT direction to center the roller within the
cam.

E. Spring Assembly Installation
SUBTASK 27-21-82-420-005
(1) Do these steps to install the spring assembly [50]:
(a) Lubricate the bearing [59] with grease, D00633.
1) Make sure to apply grease, D00633 on the bearing [59] surface that contacts the
bearing seat [58].
(b) Lubricate the spring slider shaft [60]. To lubricate it, do this task: Spring Slider Shaft
Lubrication, TASK 12-22-21-600-802.
(c) Insert the spring assembly [50] through the bearing seat [58].
(d) Install the bolt [53], washer [54] and nut [55].
1) Tighten the nut [55] to 55 ±5 in-lb (6 ±1 N·m).
(e) Install the washer [56] and nut [57].
1) Tighten the nut [57] to 13.5 ±1.5 in-lb (1.5 ±0.2 N·m).
2) Do not try to tighten nut [55] after you tighten nut [57], it may cause damage to the
equipment.
(f) On the rudder feel and centering unit, use a black marker or rubber stamp to mark the R
after the serial number.
NOTE: The suffix R indicates the springs have been changed out.
1) Apply protective coating, C00032 or equivalent that is resistant to hydraulic fluid.

 ALL

trim.

index plate.
(d) Push the captain's right rudder pedal forward approximately 0.5 inch and release it.
1) Make sure each side of the rudder trailing edge aligns with the tab on the rudder
index plate.

F. Main Rudder PCU Removal
SUBTASK 27-21-91-020-011-002
CAUTION
REMOVE THE CONTROL ROD FROM THE PCU BEFORE YOU DISCONNECT
THE PCU FROM THE RUDDER. IF YOU DO NOT REMOVE THE CONTROL
ROD FIRST, DAMAGE TO THE CONTROL ROD CAN OCCUR DURING THE
CHECK.
(1) To remove the control rods [8], do these steps:
(a) Remove the nuts [7], washers [6], washers [5], and bolts [4] to disconnect the control
rods [8] from the external summing levers [3].
(b) Remove the nuts [44], washers [43], washers [42], and bolts [41] to disconnect the
control rods [8] from the input cranks [10].
(c) Remove the control rods [8] from the airplane.
SUBTASK 27-21-91-480-005-002
(2) Install the equipment, SPL-1732 (Figure 402).
(a) Install the bracket assembly [56] with screws [51] and washers [52] to the vertical fin.
1) Tighten the screws [51] to 18 in-lb (2.0 N·m) - 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m).
(b) Install the beam assembly [55] with screws [53] and washers [54] to the main rudder
power control unit [1].
1) Tighten the screws [53] to 45 in-lb (5.1 N·m) - 60 in-lb (6.8 N·m).
(c) Install the arm assembly [58] to the bracket assembly [56].
SUBTASK 27-21-91-020-012-002
(3) Remove the nut [32], washer [31], nut [30], washer [29], and bolt assembly [28] to disconnect
the rod assembly [2] from the rudder.
SUBTASK 27-21-91-020-013-002
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU HOLD THE MAIN RUDDER PCU DURING THE
REMOVAL OF THE FORWARD MANIFOLD. IF THE MAIN RUDDER PCU
FALLS, IT CAN CAUSE DAMAGE.
(4) Remove the nut [27], washer [26], nut [25], washer [24], washer [34], bushing [23], and bolt
assembly [22] to disconnect the forward manifold [11] from vertical fin structure.
SUBTASK 27-21-91-020-014-002
(5) Disconnect the electrical connectors [9] from the main rudder power control unit [1].
SUBTASK 27-21-91-020-015-002
(6) Disconnect the hydraulic lines from the main rudder power control unit [1].
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU CAREFULLY DRAIN HYDRAULIC FLUID INTO A
SUITABLE CONTAINER. CAREFULLY CLEAN, DRY, AND DISPOSE OF
ALL LEAKAGE. HYDRAULIC FLUID CAUSES DAMAGE TO RUBBER,
COPPER, PLASTICS, PAINTS, AND MANY OTHER MATERIALS.
(a) Put the oil resistant container, STD-203, container below the hydraulic connections.
(b) Disconnect the return line hydraulic system A [12] from the main rudder power control
unit [1].
Config 2
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(c) Disconnect the pressure line hydraulic system A [21] from the main rudder power control
unit [1].
(d) Disconnect the return line hydraulic system B [14] from the main rudder power control
unit [1].
(e) Disconnect the pressure line hydraulic system B [13] from the main rudder power control
unit [1].
(f) Install the plugs and caps to the hydraulic lines and ports.
(g) Install a tag on the hydraulic lines to make sure you install them correctly.
SUBTASK 27-21-91-020-016-002
CAUTION
THE PCU SHOULD NEVER BE SET DIRECTLY ON A HARD SURFACE
WITHOUT SUPPORTS OR OTHER METHODS TO PREVENT CONTACT WITH
THE SUMMING LEVER BOLTS. IF NOT, IT CAN CAUSE DAMAGE.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU MOVE THE PCU CAREFULLY DURING THE
REMOVAL OR INSTALLATION OF THE PCU. THE PCU CAN HIT THE BOLTS.
THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE BOLTS.
(7) Use the fishpole hoist, COM-1563, to remove the main rudder power control unit [1] from the
airplane.
SUBTASK 27-21-91-480-006-002
(8) Install the lock, SPL-1727, to hold the rudder in its position.

SUBTASK 27-31-00-860-002
CAUTION
DO NOT OPERATE SYSTEM A OR B HYDRAULIC PUMPS FOR MORE THAN
TWO MINUTES WITHOUT FUEL IN THE FUEL TANKS. THE NO. 1 (FOR
SYSTEM A) AND NO. 2 (FOR SYSTEM B) FUEL TANKS MUST HAVE A
MINIMUM OF 250 GALLONS (1675 POUNDS/760 KILOGRAMS) OF FUEL IN
THEM. IF THERE IS NOT SUFFICIENT FUEL IN THE FUEL TANKS, THE
HYDRAULIC FLUID WILL BECOME TOO HOT.
(1) Make sure that the No. 1 and No. 2 fuel tanks each have 250 gallons (1675 pounds/760
kilograms) of fuel in them.
SUBTASK 27-31-00-210-001
(2) Make sure that the hydraulic reservoirs are full.

 ALL

10. Elevator and Tab Control System - Deactivation
(Figure 208)
A. General
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT YOU DO NOT DO MAINTENANCE ON THE ELEVATOR OR
TAB CONTROL SURFACES WHEN THERE IS A HIGH WIND CONDITION. THE
ELEMENTS FROM THE ELEVATOR SYSTEM CAN MOVE SUDDENLY, IF THE
AIRCRAFT IS OPEN TO HIGH WINDS. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, INJURY TO
PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(1) Use this task to deactivate the elevator and tab control system.
B. Tools/Equipment
NOTE: When more than one tool part number is listed under the same "Reference" number, the
tools shown are alternates to each other within the same airplane series. Tool part numbers
that are replaced or non-procurable are preceded by "Opt:", which stands for Optional.
Reference Description
SPL-1675 Lock Assembly - Flight Controls (used on valve p/n 10-60581-2 and
10-60581-3)
Part #: F80049-83 Supplier: 81205
Opt Part #: F80049-56 Supplier: 81205
Opt Part #: F80049-65 Supplier: 81205
STD-858 Tag - DO NOT OPERATE

Zone Area

134 Main Landing Gear Wheel Well, Body Station 663.75 to Body Station 727.00 - Right
210 Subzone - Control Compartment - Body Station 178.00 to Body Station 259.50
211 Flight Compartment - Left
212 Flight Compartment - Right
D. Elevator and Tab Control System Deactivation
SUBTASK 27-31-00-860-242
(1) Set the FLT CONTROL A and B switches, on the P5 forward overhead panel, to the OFF
position.
SUBTASK 27-31-00-860-243
(2) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2
Row Col Number Name
B 13 C00363 FLIGHT CONT SHUTOFF VALVES FLT CONT
C 11 C00362 FLIGHT CONT SHUTOFF VALVES STBY RUD
C 13 C01074 FLIGHT CONT SHUTOFF VALVES FLT CONT
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-31-00-860-244
(3) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag:
CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1
Row Col Number Name
C 4 C00456 AFCS SYS A MACH TRIM AC
SUBTASK 27-31-00-040-003
(4) Install the flight controls lock assembly:
(a) Disconnect the electrical connector from the flight controls shutoff valve at the flight
controls hydraulic modules A and B.
NOTE: For the hydraulic system A, the flight control shutoff valve is mounted on the
inboard side of hydraulic module A in the left main wheel well. For hydraulic
system B, the flight control shutoff valve is mounted on the outboard side of
hydraulic module B in the right wheel well.
(b) Put the manual override lever at the two flight controls shutoff valves in position 2 (OFF
position).
(c) Install the lock, SPL-1675, on the two flight controls shutoff valves.
1) Install the detent pins.
SUBTASK 27-31-00-780-004
(5) Move the control column forward and aft to decrease the remaining hydraulic system pressure
until the display unit shows less than 60 psi (414 kPa) for System Hydraulics A and B.
NOTE: You can view the hydraulic pressure, for the applicable system, on the display unit for
the engine display.
SUBTASK 27-31-00-210-002
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT THERE IS NO PRESSURE IN THE HYDRAULIC SYSTEM.
PRESSURE IN THE HYDRAULIC SYSTEM CAN MOVE THE CONTROL
SURFACES, CABLES, LANDING GEARS, AND LANDING GEAR DOORS
QUICKLY. THEIR MOVEMENT CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL, AND
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(6) Elevator and Tab Control System - Tryout
NOTE: This tryout is to make sure the elevator and tab control system is in a zero energy
state.
(a) Move the captain's control column forward and aft.
1) Make sure that the column forces are much higher than usual and that a small dead
band condition exist when the direction is changed.
(b) Install the DO NOT OPERATE tags, STD-858, on the captain's and first officer's control
wheels.

A. General

SUBTASK 27-31-00-860-099
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF ALL
CONTROL SURFACES BEFORE YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER.
AILERONS, RUDDERS, ELEVATORS, FLAPS, SPOILERS, SLATS, AND
THRUST REVERSERS CAN MOVE QUICKLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY
HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(1) Do this task: Elevator Hydraulic System A and B - Pressurization, TASK 27-31-00-800-801.
SUBTASK 27-31-00-710-003
(2) Operate the control column with the systems A and B hydraulic power:
(a) Set the FLT CONTROL A and B switches on the forward overhead panel, P5, to the ON
position.
(b) Move the control column full aft.
1) Make sure that the elevators move full up and the system operates smoothly.
(c) Move the control column full forward.
1) Make sure that the elevators move full down and the system operates smoothly.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-31-00-710-004
(3) Operate the control column with the system B hydraulic power:
(a) Set the FLT CONTROL A switch on the forward overhead panel, P5, to the OFF position.
(b) Move the control column full aft.
1) Make sure that the elevators move full up and the system operates smoothly.
(c) Move the control column full forward.
1) Make sure that the elevators move full down and the system operates smoothly.
SUBTASK 27-31-00-710-005
(4) Operate the control column with the system A hydraulic power:
(a) Set the FLT CONTROL A switch on the forward overhead panel, P5, to the ON position.
(b) Set the FLT CONTROL B switch on the forward overhead panel, P5, to the OFF position.
(c) Move the control column full aft.
1) Make sure that the elevators move full up and the system operates smoothly.
(d) Move the control column full forward.
1) Make sure that the elevators move full down and the system operates smoothly.
SUBTASK 27-31-00-860-100
(5) Do this task: Put the Elevator Hydraulic systems A and B Back to the Condition Before the
Pressurization, TASK 27-31-00-840-801.

SUBTASK 27-31-00-860-101
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF ALL
CONTROL SURFACES BEFORE YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER.
AILERONS, RUDDERS, ELEVATORS, FLAPS, SPOILERS, SLATS, AND
THRUST REVERSERS CAN MOVE QUICKLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY
HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(1) Do this task: Elevator Hydraulic System A and B - Pressurization, TASK 27-31-00-800-801.
SUBTASK 27-31-00-710-006
(2) Do an operational test of the elevator control column override:
(a) Override Test of the First Officer's Control Column:
1) Push the captain's and first officer's control columns forward.
2) Hold the captain's control column forward (against the forward stop).
3) Pull the first officer's control column aft.
4) Make sure that you can pull the first officer's control column aft.
5) Release the captain's and first officer's control columns go to the neutral position.
(b) Override Test of the Captain's Control Column:
1) Push the captain's and first officer's control columns forward.
2) Hold the first officer's control column forward (against the forward stop).
3) Pull the captain's control column aft.
4) Make sure that you can pull the captain's control column aft.
5) Release the captain's and first officer's control columns go to the neutral position.
SUBTASK 27-31-00-860-102
(3) Do this task: Put the Elevator Hydraulic systems A and B Back to the Condition Before the
Pressurization, TASK 27-31-00-840-801.

E. Elevator Control Column Override Functional Test
SUBTASK 27-31-00-860-122
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF ALL
CONTROL SURFACES BEFORE YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THE
AILERONS, RUDDER, ELEVATORS, FLAPS, SLATS, SPOILERS, LANDING
GEAR, AND THRUST REVERSERS CAN MOVE QUICKLY WHEN YOU
SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(1) Do this task: Elevator Hydraulic System A and B - Pressurization, TASK 27-31-00-800-801.
SUBTASK 27-31-00-710-010
(2) Do functional test of the elevator control column override:
(a) Do this task: Null Procedure - Mach Trim Actuator, TASK 27-31-00-700-801.
1) Put a 6 in. (152 mm) strip of adhesive tape vertically on the right elevator index
plate.
2) Make a mark on the tape where the upper surface of the right elevator trailing edge
would extend to the tape.
3) Attach the spring scale, STD-755, and adapter, SPL-1674, to the captain's control
column.
NOTE: The force gage is a push pull scale for measuring control column loads.
4) Block the first officer's control column in the neutral position.
NOTE: One mechanic can hold the first officer's control column steady in the
neutral position.
5) Slowly pull the captain's control column aft and hold at a minimum right elevator
position of 1.9 in. (48 mm) - 2 in. (51 mm).
6) Make sure that the captain's control column force is 40 lbf (178 N) - 100 lbf (445 N).
7) Release the captain's control column slowly to center the system.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) Push the captains's control column slowly forward and hold at a minimum right elevator
position of 1.9 in. (48 mm) - 2 in. (51 mm).
(c) Make sure that the captain's control column force is 32 lbf (142 N) - 102 lbf (454 N).
(d) Remove the spring scale, STD-755, and adapter, SPL-1674, from the captain's control
column.
(e) Remove the strip of adhesive tape from the right elevator index plate.

Pressurization, TASK 27-31-00-840-801.
27-31-00-820-801Elevator Control Cables EA and EB and Pitch Force Transducers - AdjustmentPDF p. 1020
6. Elevator Control Cables EA and EB and Pitch Force Transducers - Adjustment
(Figure 501, Figure 502, Figure 503)
NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. General
(1) Use this task to adjust the elevator control cables and pitch force transducers.
(2) Before you do cable adjustment, permit a minimum of one hour at a constant ambient
temperature of ± 5 degrees F (± 2.8 degrees C) for the airframe temperature to become stable.
(a) The cable tension values will not be correct when there are temperature differences along
the cable run.
(3) It is recommended that airplanes supplied with the cables that contain higher zinc coating
(Grade D or Grade K) be re-tensioned 3 to 4 months into service. This will bring the tension of
the control cables within the desired range. After the cables are re-tensioned the high zinc
cables (Grade D or Grade K) will continue to relax at a rate that is equivalent to the Grade B
cables. To identify the grade of the cable, refer to the table below:

wire rope, 7 X 7 RT, per BMS7-265.

*[4] It is not necessary to adjust the Grade D 0.188 (3/16) cables (6J) 3 to 4 months after installation.

time using the same cable grade material in order to minimize asymmetric relaxation.

G. Elevator Control Cables EA and EB and Pitch Force Transducers Adjustment
SUBTASK 27-31-00-020-001
(1) Remove the nuts [3], washers [2], and bolts [1] from the adjustable end of the two pitch force
transducers (Figure 501).
NOTE: The bolts will be installed when you complete the adjustment of the pitch force
transducers.
SUBTASK 27-31-00-710-001
(2) Adjust the elevator control cables EA and EB and the pitch force transducers:
(a) Install the rig pin E-5 from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, in the elevator aft quadrant
(Figure 503).
1) Make sure that you can move the rig pin freely.
2) If it is necessary, move the elevator by hand until you can install the rig pin E-5.
(b) Install the rig pin E-1 from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, in the elevator left forward
quadrant (Figure 501).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Make sure that you can move the rig pin E-1 freely.
(c) Remove the nuts [6], washers [5], and bolts [4] from the two elevator forward quadrants.
NOTE: The bolts will be installed when you complete the adjustment of the pitch force
transducers.
(d) Install the rig pins E-2 and E-3 from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, through the installation
holes of the bolts [4] (Figure 501).
1) Make sure that you can move the rig pins E-2 and E-3 freely.
(e) Use a high tension cable tensiometer, COM-1554, or low tension cable tensiometer,
COM-1553, to check the tension measurement (TASK 27-09-14-860-802).
(f) If you install new elevator control cables EA and EB, then do these steps to stretch the
cables:
1) Adjust the turnbuckles on the EAL, EAR, EBL, and EBR cables to 300 ±20 lbf
(1334 ±89 N) or 136.0 ±9.1 kg.
2) Adjust the seals in the pressure bulkhead, if it is necessary, to keep the cables
straight.
3) Remove the rig pin E-1 from the elevator left forward quadrant.
4) Remove the rig pin E-5 from the elevator aft quadrant.
5) Move the control column 25 times through full travel.
6) Install the rig pin E-5 to the elevator aft quadrant.
a) Make sure that you can move the rig pin E-5 freely.
b) If it is necessary, move the elevator by hand until the rig pin holes align.
7) Install the rig pin E-1 to the elevator left forward quadrant.
a) Make sure that you can move the rig pin E-1 freely.
8) Make sure that the rig pins E-2 and E-3 move freely through the installation holes of
the bolts [4].
(g) Adjust the control cables EA and EB to their correct cable rigging tension:
1) Adjust the turnbuckles to get the cable tension (TASK 27-09-14-860-802).
NOTE: Adjust the tension close to the maximum values in the table. The cables will
stretch over a period of time.
(h) Adjust the pitch force transducers, do this task: Pitch Force Transducer Adjustment
(DFCS BITE Test), TASK 22-11-92-820-801.
(i) Make sure that the control cables EA and EB are at the correct tension
(TASK 27-09-14-860-802).
(j) Make sure that you can move the rig pins E-1, E-2, E-3, and E-5 freely.
(k) Remove the rig pins E-2 and E-3.
(l) Install the bolts [1], washers [2], and nuts [3].
(m) Install the bolts [4], washers [5], and nuts [6].
1) Torque the nuts [6] to 200 ±40 in-lb (23 ±5 N·m).
(n) Install the locking clips on the turnbuckles.
(o) Remove the rig pins E-1 and E-5.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

H. Elevator Control Pushrods Adjustment
SUBTASK 27-31-00-860-023
(1) Push down on the trailing edge of the right elevator to fully bottom out the elevator PCU's in
the extended position.
SUBTASK 27-31-00-710-002
(2) Make sure that the left elevator is in the “Y' dimension limit of 10.84 +0.09 / -0.32 in.
(275.34 +2.29 / -8.13 mm) (Figure 519).
(a) Remove the nut [27], washer [26], nut [25], washers [24], and bolt [23] to disconnect the
left elevator control pushrod [28] from the elevator buss crank [22].
(b) Loosen the checknut [29] on the left elevator control pushrod [28].
(c) Adjust the left elevator control pushrod [28] until the elevator is in the “Y” dimension limit
of 10.84 +0.09 / -0.32 in. (275.34 +2.29 / -8.13 mm).
NOTE: One half turn of the elevator control pushrod is equal to 0.20 inch (5.1 mm) at the
elevator trailing edge.
(d) Install the bolt [23], washers [24] (under the nut), and nut [25] (Figure 504).
1) Tighten the nut [25] by hand.
SUBTASK 27-31-00-980-002
(3) Push down on the trailing edge of the left elevator to fully bottom out of the elevator PCU's in
the extended position.
SUBTASK 27-31-00-820-016
(4) Make sure that the right elevator is in the “Y” dimension limit of 10.84 +0.09 / -0.32 in.
(275.34 +2.29 / -8.13 mm) (Figure 519).
(a) Remove the nut [27], washer [26], nut [25], washers [24], and bolt [23] to disconnect the
right elevator control pushrod [28] from the elevator buss crank [22].
(b) Loosen the checknut [29] on the right elevator control pushrod [28].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(c) Adjust the right elevator control pushrod [28] until the right elevator is in the “Y”
dimension limit of 10.84 +0.09 / -0.32 in. (275.34 +2.29 / -8.13 mm).
NOTE: One half turn of the elevator control pushrod is equal to 0.2 in. (5.1 mm) at the
elevator trailing edge.
(d) Install the bolt [23], washers [24] (under the nut), nut [25] (Figure 504).
1) Tighten the nut [25] by hand.
SUBTASK 27-31-00-970-005
(5) Make sure that the final dimension in the full down position of the left elevator is 0.00 ±0.12 in.
(0.00 ±3.05 mm) of the final dimension in the full down position of the right elevator.
(a) If necessary, re-adjust the right elevator to the “Y” dimension limit of
10.84 +0.09 / -0.32 in. (275.34 +2.29 / -8.13 mm) (Figure 519).
SUBTASK 27-31-00-420-003
(6) Tighten the checknut [29] on the left and right elevator control pushrod [28] to 750 in-lb
(85 N·m) - 900 in-lb (102 N·m).
(a) Install the MS20995NC32 lockwire, G01912, on the checknut [29].
SUBTASK 27-31-00-420-004
(7) Tighten the nuts [25] to 500 in-lb (56 N·m) - 600 in-lb (68 N·m).
SUBTASK 27-31-00-420-005
CAUTION
DO NOT TRY TO TIGHTEN THE NUT [25] AGAIN AFTER YOU TIGHTEN THE
NUT [27]. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN
OCCUR.
(8) Install the washers [26] and nuts [27].
(a) Tighten the nuts [27] to 150 in-lb (17 N·m) - 220 in-lb (25 N·m).

the checknut. The tightening of the checknut can cause the dimension to
change.
10) Install lockwire on the checknuts of the input rods.

direction.

 ALL; AIRPLANES WITH SIX HINGE ELEVATOR TABS

 ALL

(c) To use the C27028, rigging bar, SPL-10345, do the steps that follow:
1) Move the digital micrometer to the bottom of the slide.
2) Push the button on the micrometer to zero the micrometer reading.
3) Move the digital micrometer up until it gives the same reading as the calibration
value stamped on the side of the tool.
NOTE: This brings the pointer on the micrometer up to approximately 0.3 in.
(7.6 mm) below the trailing edge of the elevator tab.
NOTE: The C27028 rigging bar requires the micrometer be zeroed to the elevator
neutral position which is located by the dimension stamped on the tool
above the full down position. Refer to the tool placard for information.
4) Without moving the micrometer, push the button on the micrometer to zero the
micrometer reading.
a) This is the elevator tab neutral/faired position.
NOTE: The micrometer must be zeroed at the neutral position to prevent tab
misalignment and large pitch upset during manual reversion.

(12) Make sure that the forward and aft tab rod end bearings are aligned in the correct alignment :
NOTE: See Figure 508 or Figure 509.
(a) Rotate each tab rod counterclockwise (when facing forward) until contact is made
between the tab rod end and surrounding structure.
1) This initial contact point is the start of the measurement of the rod end bearing
alignment.
(b) Rotate each tab rod clockwise (when facing forward) until contact is made between the
tab rod end and surrounding structure.
1) Measure the distance travelled between the contact points as the tab rod was
rotated clockwise from contact point to contact point.
(c) There should be a minimum of 0.040 in. (1.016 mm) travel from contact point to contact
point.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) If there is less than 0.040 in. (1.016 mm) of travel from contact point to contact
point, adjust the tab rod end until a minimum travel of 0.040 in. (1.016 mm) is
achieved.
a) If it was necessary to adjust the tab rods, make sure you torque the check nuts
to the proper torque and do a check of the rod end rotation from contact point
to contact point.
 ALL; AIRPLANES WITH THE SIX HINGE ELEVATOR TAB WITH RECTANGULAR HEAD BOLTS
SUBTASK 27-31-00-420-010
(13) Install lockwire on the checknuts [103] and checknuts [105] (Figure 508 or Figure 509).
 ALL

G. Elevator Surface Friction and Balance Test
SUBTASK 27-31-00-730-001
CAUTION
DO NOT PUT A LOAD OF MORE THAN 65 POUNDS (290 NEWTONS) ON THE
ELEVATORS AT ONE TIME. IF THE LOAD IS TOO HEAVY, IT CAN CAUSE
DAMAGE TO THE ELEVATORS.
(1) Do the elevator surface friction and balance test:
(a) Hold the captain's control columns at the neutral position.
(b) Move the elevator with your hand until the right elevator trailing edge aligns with the
elevator neutral index mark (Figure 505).
1) Release the elevator trailing edge.
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT YOU HAVE THE ELEVATORS BALANCED. IF NOT
BALANCED, THE ELEVATORS CAN CAUSE UNWANTED FLUTTER AND
INSTABILITY OF THE AIRPLANE. THIS CAN CAUSE AN IN-FLIGHT
EMERGENCY. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THESE INSTRUCTIONS, INJURY
TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(c) If the right elevator trailing edge moves down from the index mark, then do the elevator
balance adjustment (SRM 51-61-04).
(d) If the right elevator trailing edge moves up from the index mark, then do these steps:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF
ALL CONTROL SURFACES BEFORE YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC
POWER. AILERONS, RUDDER, ELEVATORS, FLAPS, SPOILERS,
SLATS, AND THRUST REVERSERS CAN MOVE QUICKLY WHEN
YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO
PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
1) Turn on the A and B hydraulic systems to center the elevator, do this task: Elevator
Hydraulic System A and B - Pressurization, TASK 27-31-00-800-801.
2) Do this task: Remove Pressure from the Elevator Hydraulic Systems A and B,
TASK 27-31-00-800-802.
3) Hold the captain's control column in the neutral position.
4) Use the block, STD-1278, and force gauge, COM-1557, to measure the minimum
force required to move the elevator trailing edge down 0.75 ±0.15 in.
(19.05 ±3.81 mm) (1.25 ±0.24 degrees) from the neutral index mark (this force is
referred to as the "down force").
a) Make a record of this down force.
5) Hold the captain' control column in the neutral position.
6) Use the block, STD-1278, and force gauge, COM-1557, to measure the minimum
force required to hold the elevator trailing edge at the index mark (which is referred
to as the "up force").
a) Make a record of this up force.
7) Make sure that the difference between the down force and up force is equal or less
than 20 lbf (89 N).
8) If the difference between the down force and up force is greater than 20 lbf (89 N),
then do this task: FIM 27-31 TASK 810.
(e) If the right elevator trailing edge stays at the index mark, then do these steps:
1) Hold the captain's control column in the neutral position.
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF
ALL CONTROL SURFACES BEFORE YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC
POWER. AILERONS, RUDDER, ELEVATORS, FLAPS, SPOILERS,
SLATS, AND THRUST REVERSERS CAN MOVE QUICKLY WHEN
YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO
PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
2) Turn on the A and B hydraulic systems to center the elevator, do this task: Elevator
Hydraulic System A and B - Pressurization, TASK 27-31-00-800-801.
3) Do this task: Remove Pressure from the Elevator Hydraulic Systems A and B,
TASK 27-31-00-800-802.
4) Use the force gauge, COM-1557, to measure the force required to move the
elevator trailing edge down 0.75 ±0.15 in. (19.05 ±3.81 mm) (1.25 ±0.24 degrees)
from the index mark (which is referred to as the "down force").
a) Make a record of this down force.
5) Use the force gauge, COM-1557, to measure the force required to move the
elevator trailing edge up 0.75 ±0.15 in. (19.05 ±3.81 mm) (1.25 ±0.24 degrees) from
the index mark (which is referred to as the "up force").
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
a) Make a record of this up force.
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT YOU HAVE THE ELEVATORS BALANCED. IF
NOT BALANCED, THE ELEVATORS CAN CAUSE UNWANTED
FLUTTER AND INSTABILITY OF THE AIRPLANE. THIS CAN CAUSE
AN IN-FLIGHT EMERGENCY. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THESE
INSTRUCTIONS, INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
6) If the down force is less than the up force, then do a check of the elevator balance
adjustment (SRM 51-61-04).
7) Calculate the sum of the down force and the up force.
8) Make sure that the sum of the down force and the up force is equal or less than
32 lbf (142 N).
9) If the sum of the down force and the up force is greater than 32 lbf (142 N), then, do
this task: FIM 27-31 TASK 810.

G. Elevator Travel Limit Test
SUBTASK 27-31-00-730-003
CAUTION
DO NOT PUT A LOAD OF MORE THAN 65 POUNDS (290 NEWTONS) ON THE
ELEVATORS AT ONE TIME. IF THE LOAD IS TOO HEAVY, IT CAN CAUSE
DAMAGE TO THE ELEVATORS.
(1) Do the elevator travel limit test with hydraulics off:
(a) Check for binding at the left and right elevators:
1) Use your hand to move the right elevator through the full travel.
a) Make sure that there is no binding through the full travel.
2) Use your hand to move the left elevator through the full travel.
a) Make sure that there is no binding through the full travel.
(b) Move and hold the captain's control column aft until it touches the stops.
1) Make sure that the right elevator moves 13.16 in. (334.26 mm) - 14.87 in.
(377.70 mm) up from the index mark (Figure 519).
(c) Move and hold the captain's control column forward until it touches the stops.
1) Make sure that the right elevator moves 9.9 in. (251.46 mm) - 11.08 in. (281.43 mm)
down from the index mark.
(d) Move and hold the captain's control column aft until it touches the stops.
1) Make sure that the left elevator moves 13.16 in. (334.26 mm) - 14.87 in.
(377.70 mm) up from the index mark (Figure 519).
(e) Move and hold the captain's control column forward until it touches the stops.
1) Make sure that the left elevator moves 9.9 in. (251.46 mm) - 11.08 in. (281.43 mm)
down from the index mark (Figure 519).
(f) Do this task: Put the Elevator Systems A and B Back to the Condition Before the
Pressure Removal, TASK 27-31-00-840-802.
SUBTASK 27-31-00-730-016
(2) Do the elevator travel limit test with hydraulics on:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF ALL
CONTROL SURFACES BEFORE YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER.
AILERONS, RUDDERS, ELEVATORS, FLAPS, SLATS, SPOILERS,
LANDING GEAR, AND THRUST REVERSERS CAN MOVE QUICKLY
WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY
TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(a) Pressurize the elevator hydraulic system A, do this task: Elevator Hydraulic System A and
B - Pressurization, TASK 27-31-00-800-801.
(b) Move and hold the captain's control column aft until it touches the stops.
1) Make sure that the right elevator moves up 13.73 in. (348.74 mm) - 14.87 in.
(377.70 mm) from the index mark (Figure 519).
(c) Move and hold the captain's control column forward until it touches the stops.
1) Make sure that the right elevator moves down 10.18 in. (258.57 mm) - 11.08 in.
(281.43 mm) from the index mark (Figure 519).
(d) Set the FLT CONTROL B switch, on the P5 forward overhead panel, to the ON position.
(e) Set the FLT CONTROL A switch, on the P5 forward overhead panel, to the OFF position.
(f) Remove pressure from the elevator hydraulic system A, do this task: Remove Pressure
from the Elevator Hydraulic Systems A and B, TASK 27-31-00-800-802.
(g) Pressurize the elevator hydraulic system B, do this task: Elevator Hydraulic System A and
B - Pressurization, TASK 27-31-00-800-801.
(h) Move and hold the captain's control column aft until it touches the stops.
1) Make sure that the right elevator moves up 13.73 in. (348.74 mm) - 14.87 in.
(377.70 mm) from the index mark (Figure 519).
(i) Move and hold the captain's control column forward until it touches the stops.
1) Make sure that the right elevator moves down 10.18 in. (258.57 mm) - 11.08 in.
(281.43 mm) from the index mark (Figure 519).

CAUTION

(a) Set the FLT CONTROL A switch on the forward overhead panel, P5, to the OFF position.
(b) Make sure that the FLT CONTROL B switch on the forward overhead panel, P5, is in the
ON position.
(c) Use a block, STD-1278 and force gauge, COM-1557 to apply a downward force of
15 ±1 lbf (67 ±5 N) to the right elevator trailing edge.
1) Slowly release the force.
2) Make a mark of the elevator position on the tailcone after you remove the force.
(d) Use a block, STD-1278 and force gauge, COM-1557 to apply an upward force of
10 ±1 lbf (44 ±5 N) to the right elevator trailing edge.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Hold the elevator in this position with the force you have applied.

a) Make sure that the distance between the up and down position of the right
elevator is not greater than 0.21 in. (5.33 mm).
(e) Set the FLT CONTROL A switch on the forward overhead panel, P5, to the ON position.
(f) Set the FLT CONTROL B switch on the forward overhead panel, P5, to the OFF position.
(g) Use a block, STD-1278 and force gauge, COM-1557 to apply a downward force of
15 ±1 lbf (67 ±5 N) to the left elevator trailing edge.
1) Slowly release the force.
2) Make a mark of the elevator position on the tailcone after you remove the force.
(h) Use a block, STD-1278 and force gauge, COM-1557 to apply an upward force of
10 ±1 lbf (44 ±5 N) to the left elevator trailing edge.
1) Hold the elevator in this position with the force you have applied.
2) Make a mark of the elevator position on the tailcone before you remove the force.
3) Slowly remove the force.
a) Make sure that the distance between the up and down position of the left
elevator is not greater than 0.21 in. (5.33 mm).

 ALL

 ALL
(h) To use the C27083, rigging bar, SPL-10345, do the steps that follow:
1) Make sure that the cross bar on the rigging bar, SPL-10345, touches the lower
surface of the elevator trailing edge.
2) Push the rigging bar, SPL-10345, FWD until elevator stop indexes on the AFT edge
of elevator near elevator rear spar.
3) Slide step gage FWD under elevator tab to obtain reading.
(i) To use the C27028, rigging bar, SPL-10345, do the steps that follow:
1) Move the digital micrometer to the bottom of the slide.
2) Push the button on the micrometer to zero the micrometer reading.
3) Move the digital micrometer up until it gives the same reading as the calibration
value stamped on the side of the tool.
NOTE: This brings the pointer on the micrometer up to approximately 0.3 in.
(7.6 mm) below the trailing edge of the elevator tab.
NOTE: The C27028 rigging bar requires the micrometer be zeroed to the elevator
neutral position which is located by the dimension stamped on the tool
above the full down position. Refer to the tool placard for information.
4) Without moving the micrometer, push the button on the micrometer to zero the
micrometer reading.
a) This is the elevator tab neutral/faired position.
NOTE: The micrometer must be zeroed at the neutral position to prevent tab
misalignment and large pitch upset during manual reversion.

(1) Use this test to make sure that the control columns can move through their full travel. This also
includes a centering test of the control columns.

(b) Total stop to stop travel.
(3) Use this test to do a check for the Power Control Unit (PCU) force fight between A and B
systems.

G. Control Column Travel and Centering Test
SUBTASK 27-31-00-730-007
(1) Do the control column travel test (Figure 513).
(a) Attach the adapter, SPL-18559, and protractor, SPL-1680, to the captain's control column
(Figure 513).
(b) Move the captain's control column full aft until it touches the stop and hold it in that
position.
NOTE: This measures the minimum aft travel.
1) Make sure that the right elevator trailing edge moves to 13.16 in. (334.26 mm) -
14.87 in. (377.70 mm) up from the index mark (Figure 519).
2) Make sure that the position of the captain's control column is at a minimum of 14
degrees aft of the column neutral rig position (Figure 513).
(c) Move the captain's control column full forward until it touches the stop and hold it in that
position.
NOTE: This measures the minimum forward travel.
1) Make sure that the right elevator trailing edge moves to 9.9 in. (251.46 mm) -
11.08 in. (281.43 mm) down from the index mark (Figure 519).
2) Make sure that the position of the captain's control column is at a minimum of 12.8
degrees forward of the column neutral rig position.
a) Release the control column.
(d) Move the captain's control column full forward and note the degree forward
measurement.
NOTE: Enough force is required to stretch the control cables allowing the column to hit
the forward stop.
(e) Move the captain's control column full aft and note the degree aft measurement.
NOTE: Enough force is required to stretch the control cables allowing the column to hit
the aft stop.
1) Release the control column.
2) Make sure that the total stop to stop travel of the captain's control column is a
minimum of 28.4 degrees (Figure 513).
NOTE: This measures the total stop to stop travel.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF ALL

WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY
TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(f) Do this task: Put the Elevator Systems A and B Back to the Condition Before the
Pressure Removal, TASK 27-31-00-840-802.
(g) Do this task: Elevator Hydraulic System A and B - Pressurization,
TASK 27-31-00-800-801.
(h) Move the captain's control column lightly forward and aft to make sure that it is in the
neutral position.
1) Make sure that the position of the captain's control column is in 6.1 - 7.7 degrees of
the vertical position (90 degrees).
(i) Remove the adapter, SPL-18559, and protractor, SPL-1680, from the captain's control
column.
(j) Attach the adapter, SPL-18559, and protractor, SPL-1680, to the first officer's control
column (Figure 513).
(k) Move the first officer's control column lightly forward and aft to make sure that it is in the
neutral position (Figure 513).
1) Make sure that the position of the first officer's control column is in 6.1 - 7.7 degrees

(l) Remove the adapter, SPL-18559, and protractor, SPL-1680, from the first officer's control

F. Pitot System Leak Test
SUBTASK 27-31-00-480-017
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE PITOT PROBE HAS NO ADDED WEIGHT ON IT
FROM THE TEST HOSE. THE WEIGHT OF THE TEST HOSE CAN BEND OR
TWIST THE PITOT PROBE OUT OF TOLERANCE.
(1) Connect the regulator, SPL-1742, or equivalent air data model test set, COM-1914, to the two
pitot probes on the vertical fin.
(a) Do this step for the regulator, SPL-1742:
1) Connect the pressure lines from the regulator, SPL-1742, with the pitot test adapter,
COM-1916, to the pitot probes.
(b) Do this step for the air data model test set, COM-1914:
1) Use the air data accessory kit, COM-25177, to connect the air data model test set,
COM-1914, to the pitot test adapter, COM-1916.
NOTE: The air data accessory kit, COM-25177, contains hoses to connect to the
air data model test set, COM-1914, and pitot test adapter, COM-1916.
SUBTASK 27-31-00-480-018
(2) Inside the aft unpressurized compartment, below the elevator feel computer, do the following:
(a) Remove the restrictor valves from the bottom of the pitot lines.
(b) If you are using the regulator, SPL-1742, for the leak test, do the following:
1) Connect the pressure gage lines from the regulator, SPL-1742, to the bottom of the
pitot lines.
(c) If you are using the air data model test set, COM-1914, for the leak test, do the following:
1) Install pitot plugs, COM-16577, to the bottom of the pitot lines.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
2) Install a highly visible streamer on the opening of the aft unpressurized
compartment.
a) Make sure that you can easily see the streamer from the ground.
NOTE: This is to remind you to remove the plugs and install the restrictor
valves again when the test is completed.
SUBTASK 27-31-00-790-002
(3) Do the pitot system leak test:
CAUTION
DO NOT INCREASE THE PRESSURE TO MORE THAN 5 PSIG (34.5 KPA)
(437 KNOTS OF COMPUTED AIRSPEED (KCAS)), DURING THE TEST. IF
THE PRESSURE IS MORE THAN 5 PSIG (34.5 KPA) (437 KCAS), IT CAN
CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ELEVATOR FEEL COMPUTER.
(a) Operate the air data model test set, COM-1914, or regulator, SPL-1742, to apply
pressure of 0.90 +0.07 / -0.00 psig (6.21 +0.48 / -0.00 kPa) to simulate 194 to 201 kcas.
(b) Set the shutoff valve in the air data model test set, COM-1914, or regulator, SPL-1742, to
the OFF position.
(c) Make sure that the pressure does not decrease more than 0.2 psig (1.4 kPa) (8 kcas)
during a 2-minute time.
NOTE: The low pressure pressurization steps above ensure that there is no significant
system leak before you apply full pressure in the following steps. If there is a leak
in the pitot system or the pressurization equipment, you can exceed the full
pressure of 5 psig (437 kcas) and cause damage to the feel computer bellows.
1) Fix any pitot system or pressurization equipment leaks, as necessary.
(d) Operate the air data model test set, COM-1914, or regulator, SPL-1742, to apply
pressure of 4.8 ±0.1 psig (33.1 ±0.7 kPa) to simulate 425 to 433 kcas.
(e) Set the shutoff valve in the air data model test set, COM-1914, or regulator, SPL-1742, to
the OFF position.
(f) Make sure that the pressure does not decrease more than 0.3 psig (2.1 kPa) (12 kcas)
during a 2-minute time.
(g) Operate the air data model test set, COM-1914, or regulator, SPL-1742, to put the
system back to ambient pressure (0 psig (0.0 kPa)).
SUBTASK 27-31-00-080-012
(4) At the two pitot probes on the vertical fin, do the following:
(a) Remove the pressure lines with the pitot test adapter, COM-1916, from the air data model
test set, COM-1914, or regulator, SPL-1742.
(b) Remove the pitot test adapter, COM-1916, from the pitot probes.
(c) Remove the seal from the drain hole in each pitot probe.
SUBTASK 27-31-00-080-013
(5) Inside the aft unpressurized compartment, below the elevator feel computer, do the following:
(a) If you used the regulator, SPL-1742, for the leak test, do the following:
1) Disconnect the pressure gage lines of the regulator, SPL-1742, from the bottom of
the pitot lines.
(b) If you used the air data model test set, COM-1914, for the leak test, do the following:
1) Remove the pitot plugs, COM-16577, from the bottom of the pitot lines.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
2) Remove the highly visible streamer on the opening of the aft unpressurized
compartment.
(c) Install the restrictor valves on the bottom of the pitot lines.

27-31-00-710-803Elevator Power-Off Flight - TestPDF p. 1125
26. Elevator Power-Off Flight - Test
(Figure 517)
NOTE: See Figure 516.
A. General
(1) The flight test is necessary because the maintenance action can affect the flight characteristics
of the airplane and incorrect adjustment can cause a pitch and attitude upset in the event of a
dual simultaneous hydraulic system loss. Since the magnitude and attitude of this pitch upset
cannot be predicted to sufficient accuracy or verified on the ground, a flight test is necessary to
determine the unbalanced moment. The unbalanced moment is reflected in terms of the
number and direction the pilot must turn the stabilizer trim wheel to return the airplane to level
flight after initiating manual reversion. If the number and direction of stabilizer trim wheel turns
are not within limits, then the elevator tab pushrods need to be re-adjusted and a subsequent
flight test performed. The number and direction of stabilizer trim wheel turns should be
recorded during the manual reversion flight test since this information is needed to correctly
re-adjust the pushrods.
(2) This flight test is necessary after you have completed one of the following maintenance tasks:
(a) For the elevator:
1) After a replacement of an elevator.
NOTE: Replacement of an elevator with a new elevator, or with one that is not the
same as the one that was originally on the airplane, requires a flight test.
NOTE: If the elevator which was removed from the airplane is reinstalled without
repair, adjustment, or modification, a flight test is not required.
2) After a replacement or adjustment of an elevator control pushrod.
NOTE: Replacement of the elevator output torque tube crank arm bearing does not
require a flight test.
NOTE: Replacement of the elevator mast arm bearing does not require a flight test.
3) After a replacement of an elevator hinge bearing plate (Figure 517).
NOTE: Flight test is not required if all of the following conditions are met:
- The elevator is not removed from the airplane during replacement of the
elevator bearing plate(s).
- Adjacent elevator bearing plates are not removed at the same time.
- No more than two elevator bearing plates are removed at the same time
on the same side.
NOTE: Flight test is not required if only the bearing is replaced and the original
elevator bearing plate is reinstalled in its original location.
4) After a replacement of an elevator hinge fitting plate (Figure 517).
5) After a maintenance where re-balance of the elevator is necessary regardless of
procedure used, either on-jig or by calculation (SRM 51-61-04).
NOTE: A flight test is not necessary following repair and/or repainting of the
elevator if the re-balance method used does not result in adjustment of the
balance weights.
(b) For the elevator tab:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) After a replacement of an elevator tab.
NOTE: A flight test is not necessary if the same elevator tab is removed and
reinstalled after it was repaired, repainted, and rebalanced and the following
conditions are met:
- The elevator tab stays within the balance limits for Center of Gravity (CG)
and weight after it was repaired, repainted, and rebalanced (SRM 51-60-00)
and no adjustment of the elevator tab adjust weights is necessary following
repair and/or repaint.
- Any repair and/or paint application to the elevator tab provides a smooth
continuous finish to all edges.
2) After a replacement or adjustment of one or both of the elevator tab pushrods.
NOTE: If only one pushrod is replaced or adjusted and you can verify that the
remaining pushrod was not replaced or adjusted since the last flight test,
then a flight test is not necessary.
NOTE: If only one pushrod is replaced or adjusted and you cannot verify that the
remaining pushrod was not replaced or adjusted since the last flight test,
then a flight test is necessary.
NOTE: If the same elevator tab pushrods are removed and re-installed without
adjustment in the same left and right locations on the same elevator tab, a
flight test is not required.
3) After a replacement of an elevator tab hinge bearing.
NOTE: It is not necessary to do a flight test if you do not remove the elevator tab
hinge fitting assemblies from the elevator when you replace the bearing.
4) After a replacement of an elevator tab hinge fitting.
 ALL; AIRPLANES WITH THE SIX HINGE ELEVATOR TAB WITH RECTANGULAR HEAD BOLTS
5) After replacement of the inboard elevator tab hinge bushing (Figure 518).
NOTE: It is not necessary to do a flight test if you replace bolts at any elevator tab
hinge location, or if you replace bushings at any other tab hinge location.
 ALL
6) After the replacement of a new or repaired elevator tab control mechanism.
(c) For the stabilizer:
1) After a replacement of the horizontal stabilizer.
NOTE: A power-off flight test is not necessary if the horizontal stabilizer is removed
and the same stabilizer, elevator, and elevator tab are re-installed (without
elevator or elevator tab rework or adjustment).
(d) For the tailcone:
1) After a replacement of the tailcone.
NOTE: A power-off flight test is not required if the following conditions are met:
- The same tailcone is removed and re-installed (without elevator or
elevator tab rework or adjustment).
- The elevator and rudder position is recorded prior to removal (relative to
the respective index plates).
- The elevator and rudder position remains the same after re-installation.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(3) Dual Hydraulics Failure: Please read the following instructions before you perform the flight
test.
(a) Sudden dual hydraulic failure or selection of both flight control switches to off or standby
will put the airplane in manual reversion and cause elevator movement to a deflection
that balances the air load. The intent of the airplane design and Aircraft Maintenance
Manual procedures is to have the resultant pitch upset be easily manageable, but if an
out of tolerance elevator tab rigging exists on the airplane, the pitch upset could be
significant. Flight Crews, especially for check flights after elevator tab maintenance,
should be prepared in the event of a large upset.
(b) Upset recovery techniques are discussed in the maneuvers section of the Flight Crew
Training Maneuvers. These techniques provide good guidance in the case of a large
upset. Additional items to consider for a dual hydraulic failure are:
1) Elevator forces will be high and elevator control authority reduced in manual
reversion hydraulics should not be restored with large column inputs present.
(c) If the pitch upset is significant, immediately accomplish the Upset Recovery maneuver
found in the non-normal maneuvers section in the Quick Reference Handbook. For
example, the use of bank angle in the event of large nose up pitch rate, described in this
section, may be beneficial.
(d) If performing a maintenance check (where hydraulics are available to be restored), the
pilot’s should coordinate the restoration of hydraulics to ensure that column input is small
at time hydraulics are restored. Restoring hydraulics with large column input will result in
a large sudden elevator command that may generate a pitch upset in the opposite
direction. The pilot flying should reduce column input at the time hydraulics are restored
by using stabilizer trim or by momentarily allowing the airplane to maneuver. At the time
hydraulics are restored, the pilot flying should be prepared to apply column inputs to
maintain control as normal column feel forces return.

SUBTASK 27-31-00-860-109
(1) Before doing a flight test to verify the elevator tab pushrod adjustment, make sure that you
adjust the appropriate system if either of the following conditions exist:
(a) Aileron trim requirement is more than 3/4 unit.
NOTE: If the aileron trim requirement is more than 3/4 unit, you need to adjust the
aileron trim per the applicable section of PAGEBLOCK 27-09-71/501 before
doing an elevator tab adjustment power-off flight test.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) Rudder trim requirement is more than 3/4 unit.
NOTE: If the rudder trim requirement is more than 3/4 unit, you need to adjust the rudder
trim per the applicable section of PAGEBLOCK 27-09-71/501 before doing an
elevator tab adjustment power-off flight test.
SUBTASK 27-31-00-820-017

E. Flight Test Procedure
SUBTASK 27-31-00-710-008
(1) Make sure you satisfy these flight conditions:
(a) Indicated Airspeed: 250 kcas.
(b) Altitude: Flight Level 15,000 ft (4572 m).
NOTE: The altitude should be within 500 ft (152 m) of the 15,000 ft (4572 m) level to get
good flight results. Altitude variation more than 500 ft (152 m) is large enough to
cause misleading test results.
(c) Weight requirement:
 ALL; 737-800
1) less than 135,000 lb (61,235 kg).
 ALL
(d) Percentage of MAC center of gravity.
NOTE: See Figure 516.
NOTE: The Center of Gravity (CG) percentage Mean Aerodynamic Chord (MAC) is
calculated by dispatch based on fuel loads, cargo loading, and passenger
loading. This information is calculated for the pilot to enter into the Flight
Management Computer (FMC) to get the recommended stabilizer setting for
takeoff.
Because the percent MAC center of gravity (for this test) is being used for a flight
test with minimal flight crew, no cargo, and a normal fuel burn is anticipated;
recording the CG in percent of MAC at takeoff is sufficient for proper adjustment
of the tabs.
(e) N1 equal for both engines.
(f) Wing fuel loads equal.
(g) Flaps up.
SUBTASK 27-31-00-860-128
(2) Set the autopilot stabilizer trim cutout switch to the CUTOUT position.
NOTE: A speed trim fail master caution annunciation may occur if thresholds are exceeded.
NOTE: As soon as you complete the power off flight test, you must move the autopilot
stabilizer trim cutout switch to the NORMAL position.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-31-00-710-009
(3) Set the SPOILER A and B switches on the forward overhead panel, P5, to the OFF position.
NOTE: Hold control wheel firmly when you turn the SPOILER A and B switches OFF to control
any upset which might occur in pitch or roll direction. If wheel input required to
maintain steady flight increases when SPOILER A and B switches are turned off, this
could indicate unusual spoiler movement. If the required wheel input increases more
than approximately 2 units, higher than normal wheel forces may occur when the FLT
CONTROL A and B are turned to STBY RUD.
SUBTASK 27-31-00-860-110
(4) Set the FLT CONTROL A and B switches on the forward overhead panel, P5, to the STDBY
RUD position.
NOTE: To successfully complete the test, the airplane must be re-trimmed to the same
airspeed. To provide a greater precision for the maneuver, someone other than the
pilot in command should set the switches.
SUBTASK 27-31-00-860-111
(5) If the airplane pitches, use the elevator to re-trim the airplane to the same airspeed:
(a) Manually turn the stabilizer trim wheel to reduce column force to zero.
(b) Keep a record of the number of turns required to re-trim the airplane.
NOTE: During the initial rotation of the stabilizer trim wheel, there might be some
freeplay. Do not count the turns until you remove the freeplay.
(c) Keep a record of the center of gravity of the airplane.
SUBTASK 27-31-00-860-161
(6) After completing the elevator power-off flight test portion of the flight, return the switches (that
were moved for the power-off flight test) to their normal flight positions.
SUBTASK 27-31-00-700-005
(7) Make sure the number of turns of the stabilizer trim wheel in the airplane Nose Up or Nose
Down direction, are within the limits of the corresponding region in the referenced figure.
SUBTASK 27-31-00-700-002
(8) If the number of turns of the stabilizer trim wheel in the airplane Nose Up or Nose Down
direction, are more than the limits, do the steps that follow:
(a) Make sure the rigging of the elevator control pushrods, the input rod of the elevator
power control unit (PCU), and the output rod of the elevator feel and centering unit is
correct.
(b) If the rigging of the elevator control pushrods, the input rod of the elevator PCU, and the
output rod of the elevator feel and centering unit is satisfactory, then, do this task:
Elevator Tab Pushrod - Adjustment after the Elevator Power-Off Flight Test,
TASK 27-31-00-820-808.
(c) If the rigging of the elevator control pushrods, the input rod of the elevator PCU, or the
output rod of the elevator feel and centering unit is not correct, do these tasks:
1) Elevator Control Pushrods - Adjustment, TASK 27-31-00-820-802.
2) Input Rods of the Elevator Power Control Unit - Adjustment,
TASK 27-31-00-820-803.
3) Input Rods of the Elevator Neutral Shift Mechanism and Output Rod of the Feel and
Centering Unit - Adjustment, TASK 27-31-00-820-804.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

 ALL

(Figure 403).

(c) Install the forward sling fittings on the elevator [1].
1) Install the fasteners to attach each sling fitting to the elevator [1].

(e) Attach the straps from the forward sling fittings to the aft sling fitting.
(f) Attach the sling equipment, SPL-2034, to the forward sling fittings and aft sling fitting.
(g) Connect an overhead crane to the primary support sling on the sling equipment,
SPL-2034.
(h) Connect a tether line to the aft sling fitting.

(b) Remove the washers [63] and bolts [62].

EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-31-11-000-001
(9) If it is necessary, remove the applicable bulb seal (Figure 406).
(a) Remove the bolts [101] and washers [100].
SUBTASK 27-31-11-020-005
(10) Remove the elevator [1] in the following order (Figure 405):
(a) At elevator hinge 2, remove the pin [78], nut [79], washer [77], bushing [73], bolt [74],
washer [75], and bushing [76].
1) Discard the pin [78].
(b) At elevator hinges 3 and 4, remove the pins [85], nuts [84], washers [83], bushings [82],
washers [81], and bolts [80].
1) Discard the pin [85].
(c) At elevator hinge 5, remove pin [90], nut [91], washer [89], bushing [88], washer [87], and
bolt [86].
1) Discard the pin [90].
(d) Remove the nuts [99] and washers [100] to disconnect the bonding jumper [98] from the
horizontal stabilizer [2].
(e) At elevator hinges 6, 7, and 8, remove the pins [97], nuts [96], washers [95], bolts [92],
washers [93], and bushings [94].
NOTE: If it is necessary, pull on the tether line to remove the bolts.
1) Discard the pin [97].
(f) At elevator hinge 1, remove the lockwire, pin [72], nut [71], washer [70], bushing [69],
bolt [66], washer [67], and bushing [68].
1) If it is necessary, pull on the tether line to remove the bolt.
2) Discard the pin [72].
(g) Remove the lockwire from the secondary bushing and remove the secondary bushing
from hinge 1.
(h) Remove the elevator [1] from the airplane.
