G. Elevator Installation
SUBTASK 27-31-11-820-013
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT YOU HAVE THE ELEVATORS BALANCED. IF NOT
BALANCED, THE ELEVATORS CAN CAUSE UNWANTED FLUTTER AND
INSTABILITY OF THE AIRPLANE. THIS CAN CAUSE AN IN-FLIGHT
EMERGENCY. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THESE INSTRUCTIONS, INJURY TO
PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(1) Balance and stamp the elevator assembly with the new static balance hinge moment if you
install a reworked, repaired, repainted, or new elevator assembly (SRM 51-61-04).
SUBTASK 27-31-11-640-001
(2) Lubricate the bolts and bushings with grease, D00633.
SUBTASK 27-31-11-420-001
(3) Install the elevator [1], do the following steps (Figure 405):
(a) Put the elevator [1] at the stabilizer trailing edge using the sling equipment, SPL-2034.
(b) At the elevator hinges 1 and 2, do these steps:
1) If it is necessary, install the secondary bushing at the hinge 1.
2) Install the hinge 1 bushing [68], washer [67], and bolt [66] with the bolt head
outboard.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
a) Make sure that the clearance between the hinge 1 washer [67] and flanged
bushing on the elevator hinge is not less than 0.015 in. (0.381 mm).
3) Loosely install the hinge 1 bushing [69].
NOTE: Do not tighten the hinge 1 bushing until it seats against the horizontal
stabilizer bearing. If you tighten the hinge 1 bushing before you tighten the
hinge 2 nut [79], the elevator axial freeplay will not be correct.
4) Loosely install the hinge 1 washer [70] and nut [71].
 ALL; AIRPLANES WITH THE SIX HINGE ELEVATOR TAB WITH RECTANGULAR HEAD BOLTS
5) Install the hinge 2 bushing [76], bushing [73], washer [75], and bolt [74] with the bolt
head outboard.
a) Do not install the hinge 2 washer [77], nut [79], or pin [78] at this time.
 ALL
(c) At the elevator hinges 8, 7, and 6, do the following steps starting at the hinge 8, then
hinge 7, and then hinge 6:
1) Install the bushings [94], washers [93], and bolts [92] with the bolt head outboard.
a) Make sure that the clearance between the washer [93] and bushing on the
elevator hinge is not less than 0.015 in. (0.381 mm).
2) Install the washers [95] and nuts [96].
a) Tighten the nuts [96] to 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m) - 75 in-lb (8.5 N·m).
3) Install the new pin [97].
(d) At the elevator hinges 3 and 4, do these steps:
1) Install the bushings [82], washers [81], and bolts [80] with the bolt heads outboard.
a) Make sure that the clearance between the washer [81] and bushing on the
elevator hinge is not less than 0.015 in. (0.381 mm).
2) Install the washers [83] and nuts [84].
a) Tighten the nuts [84] to 90 in-lb (10.2 N·m) - 125 in-lb (14.1 N·m).
3) Install the new pins [85].
(e) At the elevator hinge 5, do these steps:
1) Install the bushing [88], washer [87], and bolt [86] with the bolt head outboard.
a) Make sure that the clearance between the washer [87] and bushing on the
elevator hinge is not less than 0.015 in. (0.381 mm).
2) Install the washer [89] and nut [91].
a) Tighten the nut [91] to 90 in-lb (10.2 N·m) - 125 in-lb (14.1 N·m).
3) Install the new pin [90].
(f) Connect the bonding jumper [98] to the horizontal stabilizer [2].
1) Clean the fay surfaces of the elevator [1], horizontal stabilizer [2], and bonding
jumpers [98] (SWPM 20-20-00, Paragraph 2).
2) Install the washers [100] and nuts [99] to attach the bonding jumpers [98] to the
horizontal stabilizer [2].
3) Measure the resistance between the horizontal stabilizer [2] and elevator [1].
a) Use the intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550, to measure the
resistance.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
b) Make sure that the bonding resistance is 0.010 ohm (10 milliohms) or less.
c) Make sure that the measured resistance is less than the maximum bonding
resistance (SWPM 20-20-10, Paragraph 5).
4) Seal the bonding jumper [98] ends, nuts [99], and washers [100] with sealant,
A00247.
SUBTASK 27-31-11-080-001
(4) If the sling equipment, SPL-2034, was used for installation of the elevator, remove it from the
elevator [1], do the following steps (Figure 403):
(a) Remove the fasteners to disconnect the forward sling fittings from the elevator [1].
(b) Remove the forward sling fittings from the elevator [1].
(c) Install the bolts [3] on the elevator [1].
(d) Remove the aft sling fitting from the elevator [1].
SUBTASK 27-31-11-710-002
(5) Do an initial check of the elevator full travel by turning the elevator [1] full up and full down by
hand.
(a) Make sure that the elevator [1] moves a minimum of 25.87 degrees trailing edge up from
the neutral index mark and minimum of 19.53 degrees trailing edge down from the
neutral index mark.
(b) Use the digital protractor, STD-1232, to measure the angle.
SUBTASK 27-31-11-400-002
(6) If it was removed, install the applicable bulb seal (Figure 406).
(a) Apply Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237, (preferred) or corrosion preventive compound,
C00308, (alternative) to all areas of the holes for the bolts [101].
(b) Install the washers [102] and bolts [101].
(c) Tighten the bolts [101] to 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m).
SUBTASK 27-31-11-420-002
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE IDLER HINGE MOVES DOWN FROM THE
STABILIZER SUPPORT BEAM WHEN YOU ATTACH THE BALANCE PANELS
TO THE ELEVATOR. IF YOU DO NOT INSTALL THE BALANCE PANELS
CORRECTLY, IT CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(7) Connect the balance panels to the elevator [1] (Figure 405):
(a) Install the washers [65] and bolts [64].
(b) Install the washers [63] and bolts [62].
(c) Check the elevator balance panel seal gap (TASK 27-31-41-400-801).
(d) Make sure that the hinge seals are installed correctly before you tighten the bolts [64] and
bolts [62].
 ALL; AIRPLANES WITH THE SIX HINGE ELEVATOR TAB WITH RECTANGULAR HEAD BOLTS
SUBTASK 27-31-11-020-015
(8) Connect the elevator tab control mechanism [34] to the elevator [1] and tab pushrod [26]
(Figure 404).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
 ALL; AIRPLANES WITH THE SIX HINGE ELEVATOR TAB WITH RECTANGULAR HEAD BOLTS
(Continued)
(a) Install the pin assemblies [21], washers [32], and nuts [31] that attach the elevator tab
control mechanism [34] to the elevator [1].
NOTE: You possibly have to move the hinge 2 bolt [74] outboard to tighten the nut of the
outboard tab mechanism attach point.
(b) Tighten the nuts [31] to 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m) - 35 in-lb (4.0 N·m).
(c) Install the spacers [23], bolts [22], washers [27], and new nuts [28] to attach the tab
pushrods [26] to the elevator tab control mechanism [34].
1) Make sure that the new nuts [28] are installed.
NOTE: If you loosened or removed the nuts, they must be replaced with new nuts.
Using new nuts will make sure that they have the required run-on torque.
(d) Tighten the nuts [28] to 70 in-lb (7.9 N·m) - 80 in-lb (9.0 N·m).
(e) Install the pin retainers [30] with the screws [29].
(f) Remove the clamps that prevent movement of the elevator tab control mechanism [34].
SUBTASK 27-31-11-420-007
(9) At the elevator hinge 2, do these steps:
(a) Make sure that the clearance between the hinge 2 washer [75] and flanged bushing on
the elevator hinge is not less than 0.015 in. (0.381 mm).
(b) Install washer [77] and nut [79].
1) Tighten the hinge 2 nut [79] by tightening the head of the bolt [74] to 113 in-lb
(12.8 N·m) - 138 in-lb (15.6 N·m) when using a wrench to keep the nut [79] from
rotating.
NOTE: The normal torque for the nut is 90 in-lb (10.2 N·m) - 125 in-lb (14.1 N·m). It
is hard to access the nut with a torque wrench. It is necessary to tighten the
head of the bolt to the upper torque value of the nut, +/- 10 percent of that
upper torque value. That torque value will be 113 in-lb (12.8 N·m) - 138 in-lb
(15.6 N·m).
(c) Install the new pin [78].
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-31-11-420-008
(10) At the elevator hinge 1, do these steps:
(a) Tighten the hinge 1 bushing [69] until it seats against the horizontal stabilizer bearing.
NOTE: Use only hand pressure to tighten the hinge 1 bushing.
(b) Tighten the hinge 1 nut [71] to 90 in-lb (10.2 N·m) - 125 in-lb (14.1 N·m).
1) Install the new pin [72].
2) Install the MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, from the bushing [69] to the elevator [1]
to prevent clockwise and counterclockwise rotation.
SUBTASK 27-31-11-710-024
(11) Do a final check of the elevator full travel by turning the elevator [1] full up and full down by
hand.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Make sure that the moves a minimum of 25.87 degrees trailing edge up from the neutral
index mark and minimum of 19.53 degrees trailing edge down from the neutral index
mark.
(b) Use the digital protractor, STD-1232, to measure the angle.
SUBTASK 27-31-11-420-004
(12) Connect the pushrod [52] of the elevator position transmitter [51] to the elevator [1]
(Figure 405).
(a) Make sure that the joint between the pushrod [52] and arm [52A] is located forward from
the elevator position transmitter [51].
(b) Install the screw [56], washer [55], and spacer [54] to the pushrod [52].
(c) Connect the electrical connector [53] to the elevator position transmitter [51].
SUBTASK 27-31-11-420-005
(13) Connect the elevator control pushrod [60] to the elevator [1] (Figure 405).
(a) Move the elevator [1] to the neutral position.
(b) Install the pin assembly [59] with the pin head inboard, nut [58].
1) Tighten the nut [58] to 500 in-lb (56.5 N·m) - 600 in-lb (67.8 N·m).
CAUTION
DO NOT TIGHTEN NUT [58] AFTER YOU TIGHTEN THE NUT [57]. BOLT
PROTRUSION THROUGH NUT [57] CAN BE 0.01 INCHES MINIMUM,
FOR THE BOLT ASSEMBLY. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, THIS CAN CAUSE
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(c) Install the nut [57].
1) Tighten the nut [57] to 150 in-lb (16.9 N·m) - 220 in-lb (24.9 N·m).
SUBTASK 27-31-11-080-002
(14) Remove the rig pin E-5 of the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, from the elevator aft quadrant.
SUBTASK 27-31-11-700-005
(15) Check the adjustment of the elevator blade seal gaps:
(a) Make sure that the stabilizer and elevator are at their neutral positions.
(b) Make sure that the elevator blade seal gap is within the tolerance of 0.01 in. (0.25 mm) -
0.05 in. (1.27 mm) (Figure 407).
SUBTASK 27-31-11-640-002
(16) Do this task: Elevator Buss Crank and Master Arm Fitting - Lubrication,

G. Elevator Control Pushrod Installation
SUBTASK 27-31-11-640-003
(1) Lubricate the bolts and bushings with grease, D00633.
SUBTASK 27-31-11-420-006
(2) Install the elevator control pushrod [113]:
(a) Make sure that the elevator [1] is in the neutral position (Figure 403).
(b) Connect the elevator control pushrod [113] to the elevator buss crank [120] (Figure 408):
NOTE: It is necessary to connect the AFT end of the pushrod to the elevator mast arm.
1) Make sure that the bushings [121] are installed on the elevator control
pushrod [113].
a) If it is necessary, install the bushings [121] with sealant, A00247
(TASK 20-10-02-900-801).
2) Install the bolt assembly [119] (with the bolt head inboard) washers [118], and
nut [117].
3) Tighten the nut [117] to 500 in-lb (56.5 N·m) to 600 in-lb (67.8 N·m).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
CAUTION
DO NOT TIGHTEN NUT [117] AFTER YOU TIGHTEN THE NUT [115].
BOLT PROTRUSION THROUGH NUT [115] CAN BE 0.01 INCHES
MINIMUM, FOR THE BOLT ASSEMBLY. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, THIS
CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
4) Install the washer [116] and nut [115].
5) Tighten the nut [115] to 150 in-lb (16.9 N·m) to 220 in-lb (24.9 N·m).
(c) Connect the elevator control pushrod [113] to the elevator mast arm [114]:
1) Make sure that the bushing [121] and washer [122] are installed on the elevator
control pushrod [113].
a) If it is necessary, install the bushing [121] with sealant, A00247
(TASK 20-10-02-900-801).
b) If it is necessary, install the washer [122] as follows:
<1> Use cotton wiper, G00034, moist in alcohol, B00130, to clean the
mating surfaces of the washer [122] and elevator control pushrod [113].
<2> Clean the mating surface of the elevator control pushrod [113] with 150
grit abrasive paper, G02428.
<3> Clean the mating surface of the elevator control pushrod [113] with
cotton wiper, G00034, moist in alcohol, B00130.
<4> If it is necessary, use dry cotton wiper, G00034, to remove remaining
solvent.
<5> Bond the washer [122] to the elevator control pushrod [113] with
sealant, A00767.
<6> If it is necessary, remove the excess of sealant with cotton wiper,
G00034, moist in alcohol, B00130.
2) Install the bolt assembly [112] with the bolt head inboard and nut [111].
NOTE: The bolt assembly is installed through the circular access hole in the
tailcone.
3) Tighten the nut [111] to 500 in-lb (56.5 N·m) to 600 in-lb (67.8 N·m).
CAUTION
DO NOT TIGHTEN NUT [111] AFTER YOU TIGHTEN THE NUT [110].
BOLT PROTRUSION THROUGH NUT [110] CAN BE 0.01 INCHES
MINIMUM, FOR THE BOLT ASSEMBLY. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, THIS
CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
4) Install the nut [110].
5) Tighten the nut nut [110] to 150 in-lb (16.9 N·m) to 220 in-lb (24.9 N·m).
SUBTASK 27-31-11-080-003

 ALL

F. Elevator PCU Removal
SUBTASK 27-31-14-020-002
(1) Remove the nuts [22], washers [21], washers [20], and bolts [19] to disconnect the four input
rods [23] from the four input cranks [18] (two on each elevator Power Control Unit (PCU)).
(a) Move the control column to move the quadrant out of the way when there are clearance
problems with the lower input rod attach bolt.
SUBTASK 27-31-14-020-004
(2) Move the four input cranks [18] forward.
SUBTASK 27-31-14-480-003
(3) Install the rig pin E-5 from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, in the elevator aft control quadrant
(Figure 402).
NOTE: To easily get access to the lower connection, set the input cranks on the rig pin E-5.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) If necessary, disconnect the vernier control rod [30] and vernier control rod [31] so that
the torque tube can be rotated to gain access to the PCU attach bolt, do these steps
(View D, Figure 402):
1) Remove the nut [39], washer [38], washer [37], and bolt [36], to disconnect the
vernier control rod [30].
2) Remove the nut [35], washer [34], washer [33], and bolt [32] to disconnect the
vernier control rod [31].
SUBTASK 27-31-14-020-003
(4) Remove the elevator PCU [6]:
(a) Remove the nut [17], washer [16], nut [15], washer [14], bolt [12], and bushing [13] that
attach the elevator PCU [6] to the mounting brackets.
1) If it is necessary, move the control quadrant to rotate the input cranks out of the way
of the PCU attachment bolt head.
WARNING
RELEASE THE HYDRAULIC CONNECTION SLOWLY AND LET THE
PRESSURE DECREASE BEFORE YOU FULLY REMOVE THE
HYDRAULIC LINES. IF YOU DISCONNECT THE HYDRAULIC LINE WHEN
IT HAS PRESSURE, A SPRAY OF HYDRAULIC FLUID CAN CAUSE
INJURY TO PERSONS.
(b) Disconnect the hydraulic lines from the applicable elevator PCU [6].
1) Install caps and plugs on the hydraulic lines and ports.
(c) Remove the nut [11], washer [10], washer [9], and bolt [8] that attach the elevator PCU [6]
to the output torque tube [7].
(d) Remove the elevator PCU [6] from the airplane.
SUBTASK 27-31-14-480-002
(5) If you remove the two elevator PCUs at the same time, install the fixture, SPL-1683, in the
position of the right elevator PCU [6] (Figure 403).
(a) Put the fixture, SPL-1683, between the output torque tube and input crank.
(b) Install the pins of the fixture, SPL-1683, to hold the fixture, SPL-1683, in position.

H. Elevator PCU Installation
SUBTASK 27-31-14-420-001
(1) If the packings and unions are not installed in the elevator PCU [6], do these steps:
(a) Lubricate the new packing [1] and new packing [5] with hydraulic fluid, D00153.
(b) Install the packing [1], union [2], packing [5], and union [4] in the elevator PCU [6].
SUBTASK 27-31-14-420-002
(2) Install the elevator PCU [6]:
(a) Apply grease, D00633, to the bolt [8] and bolt [12].
(b) Put the elevator PCU [6] in its position.
(c) Install the bolt [8] with the bolt head inboard, washer [9], washer [10], and nut [11] to
attach the elevator PCU [6] to the output torque tube [7].
1) Tighten the nut [11] to 558 in-lb (63.0 N·m) - 592 in-lb (66.9 N·m).
(d) Install the bushing [13], bolt [12], washer [14], and nut [15] to attach the elevator PCU [6]
to the mounting bracket.
1) For the right elevator Power Control Unit (PCU), install the bolt [12] with the bolt
head inboard.
2) For the left elevator PCU, install the bolt [12] with the bolt head inboard.
3) Tighten the nut [15] to 550 in-lb (62.1 N·m) - 600 in-lb (67.8 N·m).
CAUTION
DO NOT TIGHTEN THE NUT [15] AGAIN AFTER YOU TIGHTEN THE NUT
[17]. YOU CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT.
(e) Install the washer [16] and nut [17].
1) Tighten the nut [17] to 225 in-lb (25.4 N·m) - 250 in-lb (28.2 N·m).
SUBTASK 27-31-14-080-003
(3) Remove the rig pin E-5 of the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, from the elevator aft control quadrant.
(a) If the vernier control rod [30] and vernier control rod [31] were disconnected to give
access to the PCU attach bolt, connect them, do these steps:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
CAUTION
DO NOT TRY TO TIGHTEN THE BOLT AGAIN AFTER YOU TIGHTEN
THE NUT. YOU CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
1) Install the nut [39], washer [38] (under the nut [39]), washer [37] (under the
bolt [36]), and bolt [36] to connect the vernier control rod [30].
a) Tighten the nut [39] to 76 in-lb (8.6 N·m) - 80 in-lb (9.0 N·m).
2) Install the nut [35], washer [34] (under the nut [35]), washer [33] (under the
bolt [32]), and bolt [32] to connect the vernier control rod [31].
a) Tighten the outer bolt of the bolt [32] to 75 in-lb (8.5 N·m) - 85 in-lb (9.6 N·m).
b) Tighten the nut [35] to 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m) - 35 in-lb (4.0 N·m).
SUBTASK 27-31-14-860-004
(4) Move the elevator PCU [6] to the fully retracted position.
SUBTASK 27-31-14-420-003

(b) Install the bolts [19], washers [20], washers [21], and nuts [22].

2) For the inboard bolt, install the bolt [19] with the bolt head inboard.
SUBTASK 27-31-14-420-004

(a) Remove hydraulic fluid that falls on the floor.

E. Procedure
SUBTASK 27-31-14-020-005
(1) Remove the elevator power control unit (PCU). To remove it, do this task: Elevator Power
Control Unit - Removal, TASK 27-31-14-000-801.
SUBTASK 27-31-14-020-006
(2) Use these tools to check for wear on the parts of the elevator PCU connections:
(a) micrometer (0-1 inch, readable to 1/1000 inch), STD-1096
(b) vernier caliper (0 - 6 inch, readable to 1/1000 inch), STD-1097.
SUBTASK 27-31-14-020-007
(3) Examine the parts of the elevator PCU connections for worn areas:
(a) Remove the parts to be checked.
(b) Measure the parts as necessary with a micrometer (0-1 inch, readable to 1/1000 inch),
STD-1096 or a vernier caliper (0 - 6 inch, readable to 1/1000 inch), STD-1097.
(c) Compare the dimensions you measured with the permitted wear dimensions that follow.
(d) If the parts are not in the tolerance, replace or repair the part as required.

H. Elevator Pitot-Static System Flushing
SUBTASK 27-31-17-170-001
(1) Flush the pitot system, do these steps:
(a) Inspect the pitot probes, do this task: Elevator Pitot Probe - Inspection,
TASK 27-31-17-200-802.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU DISCONNECT THE FEEL COMPUTER LINES
BEFORE YOU FLUSH THE LINES WITH A DRY FILTERED AIR SOURCE
OF 20-30 PSIG, STD-1280. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(b) Disconnect the left and right pitot lines [4] from the elevator feel computer [5].
(c) Install plugs on the elevator feel computer [5] ports.
(d) Remove the left and right restrictor valves [3] from the pitot lines [4].
(e) Clean the restrictor valves [3] with degreasing solvent, B50126, or solvent, B00062
(TASK 27-31-17-200-801).
(f) Put a 5 gallon (19 liter) container, STD-1154, below the pitot lines [4] to catch any debris.
(g) Install the pitot plug, COM-16577, on the pitot line [4] for the left elevator feel
computer [5].
(h) Install the pitot test adapter, COM-1916, on the left pitot probe.
(i) From the left pitot probe, flush the left pitot line [4] with 20 psig (137.9 kPa) - 30 psig
(206.8 kPa) of air constantly for 3 minutes and no unwanted material comes out from the
tubes using a 0-30 psig dry filtered regulated air source, STD-1280.
1) Make sure that the pitot line [4] is not blocked and air flows out of the other open
end.
2) If air does not flow out of the other end from the left pitot system, do these steps:
a) Remove the elevator pitot probe, do this task: Feel System Pitot Probe
Removal, TASK 27-31-94-000-801.
b) Clean the elevator pitot probe, do this task: Pitot Probe Cleaning,
TASK 34-11-01-100-801.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
c) Install the elevator pitot probe, do this task: Feel System Pitot Probe
Installation, TASK 27-31-94-400-801.
(j) Remove the pitot plug, COM-16577, from the pitot line [4] for the left elevator feel
computer [5].
(k) Install the pitot plug, COM-16577, on the pitot line [4] for the left restrictor valve [3].
(l) From the left pitot probe, flush the left pitot line [4] with 20 psig (137.9 kPa) - 30 psig
(206.8 kPa) of air constantly for 3 minutes and no unwanted material comes out from the
tubes using a 0-30 psig dry filtered regulated air source, STD-1280.
1) Make sure that the pitot line [4] is not blocked and air flows out of the other open
end.
(m) Remove the pitot plug, COM-16577, from the pitot line [4] for the left restrictor valve [3].
(n) Remove the pitot test adapter, COM-1916, on the left pitot probe.
(o) Install the pitot test adapter, COM-1916, on the right pitot probe.
(p) Install the pitot plug, COM-16577, on the pitot line for the right elevator feel computer [5].
(q) From the right pitot probe, flush the right pitot line [4] with 20 psig (137.9 kPa) - 30 psig
(206.8 kPa) of air constantly for 3 minutes and no unwanted material comes out from the
tubes using a 0-30 psig dry filtered regulated air source, STD-1280.
1) Make sure that the pitot line [4] is not blocked and air flows out of the other open
end.
2) If air does not flow out of the other end from the left pitot system, do these steps:
a) Remove the elevator pitot probe, do this task: Feel System Pitot Probe
Removal, TASK 27-31-94-000-801.
b) Clean the elevator pitot probe, do this task: Pitot Probe Cleaning,
TASK 34-11-01-100-801.
c) Install the elevator pitot probe, do this task: Feel System Pitot Probe
Installation, TASK 27-31-94-400-801.
(r) Remove the pitot plug, COM-16577, from the pitot line [4] for the right elevator feel
computer [5].
(s) Install the pitot plug, COM-16577, on pitot line [4] for the right restrictor valve [3].
(t) From the right pitot probe, flush the right pitot line [4] with 20 psig (137.9 kPa) - 30 psig
(206.8 kPa) of air constantly for 3 minutes and no unwanted material comes out from the
tubes using a 0-30 psig dry filtered regulated air source, STD-1280.
1) Make sure that the pitot line [4] is not blocked and air flows out of the other open
end.
(u) Remove the pitot test adapter, COM-1916, on the right pitot probe.
(v) Remove the pitot plug, COM-16577, from the pitot line [4] for the right restrictor valve [3].
(w) Check the 5 gallon (19 liter) container, STD-1154, for unwanted material from the pitot
line [4].
1) If unwanted material is found in the container, examine the pitot lines [4].
(x) Remove the plugs from the elevator feel computer [5] ports.
(y) Connect the pitot lines [4] to the elevator feel computer [5].
1) Tighten the pitot lines [4] to 170.0 ±8.5 in-lb (19.2 ±1.0 N·m).
(z) Install the restrictor valves [3] on the pitot lines [4].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Tighten the restrictor valves [3] to 170.0 ±8.5 in-lb (19.2 ±1.0 N·m).
SUBTASK 27-31-17-170-002
(2) Flush the static system, do these steps:
(a) Disconnect the static lines [2] from the elevator feel computer [5].
(b) Install plugs on the elevator feel computer [5] ports.
(c) Flush the static lines [2] from each ends with 20 psig (137.9 kPa) - 30 psig (206.8 kPa) of
air for 3 minutes and no unwanted material comes out from the tubes using a 0-30 psig
dry filtered regulated air source, STD-1280.
1) Make sure that the static lines [2] are not blocked and air flows out of the other open
end.
(d) Remove the plugs from the elevator feel computer [5] ports.
(e) Connect the static lines [2] to the elevator feel computer [5].
1) Tighten the B-nuts on the static lines [2] to 170.0 ±8.5 in-lb (19.2 ±1.0 N·m).

SUBTASK 27-31-17-170-003
(1) Drain the pitot system, do these steps:
(a) Remove the restrictor valves [3] from the pitot lines [4].
(b) Make sure that the pitot lines [4] have proper drainage (Figure 201).
1) Check the hoses between the elevator feel system pitot-static probes and
associated rigid metal tubing.
2) Make sure that the hoses loop upward.
NOTE: The hoses are looped upward to avoid accumulation of water.
(c) If it is necessary, flush the pitot system, do this task: Elevator Pitot-Static System
Flushing, TASK 27-31-17-170-801.
(d) Clean the restrictor valves [3] with solvent, B00074, or solvent, B00062.
NOTE: Use dry-cleaning solvent, B00074, or solvent, B00062, and ultrasonic cleaning, if
available.
(e) Install the restrictor valves [3].
1) Tighten the restrictor valves [3] to 170.0 ±8.5 in-lb (19.2 ±1.0 N·m).
SUBTASK 27-31-17-170-004
(2) Do the following steps to check the static system:
(a) Disconnect the static lines [2] from the elevator feel computer [5].
(b) Make sure that the static lines [2] have proper drainage.
1) If it is necessary, flush the static system, do this task: Elevator Pitot-Static System
Flushing, TASK 27-31-17-170-801.
(c) Connect the static lines [2].
1) Tighten the B-nuts on the static lines [2] to 170.0 ±8.5 in-lb (19.2 ±1.0 N·m).

H. Elevator Pitot System Leak Test
NOTE: Use a pitot test adapter, COM-1916 if necessary.
SUBTASK 27-31-17-390-001
WARNING
WHEN THE PITOT PROBES HAVE COVERS ON THEM, MAKE SURE THAT A
PERSON ON THE GROUND CAN SEE THE COVERS. ALSO MAKE SURE
YOU ATTACH A TAG TO THE LEFT CONTROL WHEEL IN THE FLIGHT
COMPARTMENT AS A REMINDER THAT THE PITOT PROBES HAVE COVERS
ON THEM. IF THE COVERS ARE NOT REMOVED FROM THE PITOT
PROBES, INCORRECT AIRSPEED-SENSING AND ALTITUDE-SENSING
SIGNALS CAN OCCUR. THIS CAN CAUSE DANGEROUS FLIGHT
CONDITIONS.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE PITOT PROBE HAS NO ADDED WEIGHT ON IT
FROM THE TEST HOSE. THE WEIGHT OF THE TEST HOSE CAN BEND OR
TWIST THE PITOT PROBE OUT OF TOLERANCE.
(1) Connect the regulator, SPL-1742, or equivalent air data model test set, COM-1914, to the two
pitot probes on the vertical fin.
(a) Do this step for the regulator, SPL-1742:
1) Connect the pressure lines from the regulator, SPL-1742, with the pitot test adapter,
COM-1916, to the pitot probes.
(b) Do this step for the air data model test set, COM-1914:
1) Use the air data accessory kit, COM-25177, to connect the air data model test set,
COM-1914, to the pitot test adapter, COM-1916.
NOTE: The air data accessory kit, COM-25177, contains hoses to connect to the
air data model test set, COM-1914, and the pitot test adapter, COM-1916.
SUBTASK 27-31-17-020-001
(2) Inside the aft unpressurized compartment, below the elevator feel computer, do the following:
(a) Remove the restrictor valves [3] from the bottom of the pitot lines [4].
(b) If it is necessary, clean the restrictor valves [3] with degreasing solvent, B50126, or
solvent, B00062 (TASK 27-31-17-200-801).
(c) If you are using the regulator, SPL-1742, or equivalent, for the leak test, do the following:
NOTE: The DPS 400 Test Set can be used as an alternate tool to the DPS 500.
1) Connect the pressure gage lines from the regulator, SPL-1742, or equivalent, to the
drain holes of the pitot lines [4].
(d) If you are using the air data model test set, COM-1914, for the leak test, do the following:
1) Install pitot plugs, COM-16577, over the ends of the pitot lines [4].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
2) Install a highly visible streamer on the opening of the aft unpressurized
compartment.
a) Make sure that you can easily see the streamer from the ground.
NOTE: This is to remind you to remove the plugs and install the restrictor
valves again when the test is completed.
SUBTASK 27-31-17-790-002
(3) Do the pitot system leak test:
CAUTION
DO NOT INCREASE THE PRESSURE TO MORE THAN 5 PSIG (34.5 KPA)
(437 KNOTS OF COMPUTED AIRSPEED (KCAS)), DURING THE TEST. IF
THE PRESSURE IS MORE THAN 5 PSIG (34.5 KPA) (437 KCAS), IT CAN
CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ELEVATOR FEEL COMPUTER.
(a) Operate the air data model test set, COM-1914, or regulator, SPL-1742, or equivalent, to
apply pressure between 0.90 +0.07 / -0.00 psig (6.21 +0.48 / -0.00 kPa) to simulate 194
to 201 kcas.
(b) Set the shutoff valve in the air data model test set, COM-1914, or regulator, SPL-1742, or
equivalent to the OFF position.
(c) Make sure that the pressure does not decrease more than 0.2 psig (1.4 kPa) (8 kcas)
during a 2-minute time.
NOTE: The low pressure pressurization steps above ensure that there is no significant
system leak before you apply full pressure in the following steps. If there is a leak
in the pitot system or the pressurization equipment, you can exceed the full
pressure of 5 psig (437 kcas) and cause damage to the feel computer bellows.
1) Fix any pitot system or pressurization equipment leaks, as necessary.
(d) Operate the air data model test set, COM-1914, or regulator, SPL-1742, or equivalent, to
apply pressure of 4.8 ±0.1 psig (33.1 ±0.7 kPa) to simulate 425 to 433 kcas.
(e) Set the shutoff valve in the air data model test set, COM-1914, or regulator, SPL-1742, or
equivalent to the OFF position.
(f) Make sure that the pressure does not decrease more than 0.3 psig (2.1 kPa) (12 kcas)
during a 2-minute time.
(g) Operate the air data model test set, COM-1914, or regulator, SPL-1742, or equivalent, to
put the system back to ambient pressure (0 psig (0.0 kPa)).
SUBTASK 27-31-17-160-001
(4) At the two pitot probes on the vertical fin, do the following:
(a) Remove the pressure lines with the pitot test adapter, COM-1916, from the air data model
test set, COM-1914, or regulator, SPL-1742, or equivalent to the pitot probes.
(b) Remove the pitot test adapter, COM-1916, to the two pitot probes.
SUBTASK 27-31-17-080-001
(5) Inside the aft unpressurized compartment, below the elevator feel computer, do the following:
(a) If you used the regulator, SPL-1742, or equivalent, for the leak test, do the following:
1) Disconnect the pressure gage lines of the regulator, SPL-1742, or equivalent, from
the drain holes of the pitot lines [4].
(b) If you used the air data model test set, COM-1914, for the leak test, do the following:
1) Remove the plugs that were installed over the ends of the pitot lines [4].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
2) Remove the highly visible streamer on the opening of the aft unpressurized
compartment.
(c) Install the restrictor valves [3] on the bottom of the pitot lines [4].
1) Tighten the restrictor valves [3] to 170.0 ±8.5 in-lb (19.2 ±1.0 N·m).

E. Elevator Pitot System Pressurization
SUBTASK 27-31-17-480-003
(1) Do the following to prepare the elevator pitot system for pressurization:
NOTE: The following two steps do not need to be completed if you are using the air data
model test set, COM-1914.
(a) Remove the restrictor valves [3] from the pitot lines [4].
(b) If it is necessary, clean the restrictor valves [3] with degreasing solvent, B50126, or
solvent, B00062 (TASK 27-31-17-200-801).
(c) Connect the pressure gage lines from the regulator, SPL-1742, or equivalent to the drain
holes of the pitot lines [4].
NOTE: The DPS 400 Test Set can be used as an alternate tool to the DPS 500.
WARNING
WHEN THE PITOT PROBES HAVE COVERS ON THEM, MAKE SURE
THAT A PERSON ON THE GROUND CAN SEE THE COVERS. ALSO
MAKE SURE YOU ATTACH A TAG TO THE LEFT CONTROL WHEEL IN
THE FLIGHT COMPARTMENT AS A REMINDER THAT THE PITOT
PROBES HAVE COVERS ON THEM. IF THE COVERS ARE NOT
REMOVED FROM THE PITOT PROBES, INCORRECT AIRSPEED￾SENSING AND ALTITUDE-SENSING SIGNALS CAN OCCUR. THIS CAN
CAUSE DANGEROUS FLIGHT CONDITIONS.
(d) Seal the drain hole in each pitot probe on the vertical fin.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE WEIGHT OF THE TEST HOSE IS NOT ON THE
PITOT PROBE. THE WEIGHT OF THE HOSE CAN BEND OR TWIST THE
PROBE UNTIL IT IS NOT IN TOLERANCE.
(e) Connect the regulator, SPL-1742, or equivalent air data model test set, COM-1914, to the
two pitot probes on the vertical fin.
1) Do this step for the regulator, SPL-1742:
a) Connect the pressure lines from the regulator, SPL-1742, with the pitot test
adapter, COM-1916, to the pitot probes.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
2) Do this step for the air data model test set, COM-1914:
a) Use the air data accessory kit, COM-25177, to connect the air data model test
set, COM-1914, to the pitot test adapter, COM-1916.
NOTE: The air data accessory kit, COM-25177, contains hoses to connect to
the air data model test set, COM-1914, and pitot test adapter,
COM-1916.
SUBTASK 27-31-17-480-004
CAUTION
DO NOT LET THE PRESSURE BECOME MORE THAN 5 PSIG (34.5 KPA).
DAMAGE TO THE COMPONENT COULD OCCUR.
(2) Pressurize the elevator pitot system:
(a) Operate the air data model test set, COM-1914, or regulator, SPL-1742, to pressurize the
system, as necessary, to obtain the system test data.
(b) When testing is complete, slowly operate the air data model test set, COM-1914, or
regulator, SPL-1742, to remove pressure from the system until it is at zero.
SUBTASK 27-31-17-010-007
(3) Remove the pressurization equipment from the airplane:
(a) Remove the pressure gage lines from the air data model test set, COM-1914, or
regulator, SPL-1742, or equivalent to the drain holes.
(b) Install the restrictor valves [3] in each of the pitot lines [4].
1) Tighten the restrictor valves [3] to 170.0 ±8.5 in-lb (19.2 ±1.0 N·m).
(c) Remove the pressure lines from the air data model test set, COM-1914, or regulator,
SPL-1742, or equivalent, from the pitot probes.
(d) Remove the pitot test adapter, COM-1916, from the pitot probes.

G. Elevator Feel Shift Module Installation
SUBTASK 27-31-20-420-001
(1) Install the elevator feel shift module [1].
(a) Install the washers [3] and bolts [2] to attach the elevator feel shift module [1] to the
bracket.
1) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the elevator feel shift module [1]
and bracket (SWPM 20-20-00).
a) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550.
b) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 0.005 ohm (5.0 milliohm) or
less.
2) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the elevator feel shift module [1]
and airplane structure (SWPM 20-20-00).
a) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550.
b) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 0.005 ohm (5.0 milliohm) or
less.
3) If the electrical bonding resistance at the two locations is more than 0.005 ohm (5.0
milliohm), remove the elevator feel shift module [1] and prepare the electrical faying
surfaces.
(b) Apply a fillet seal with sealant, A00247, along the joint edges, do this task: Fillet Seal
Application, TASK 51-31-00-390-804.
SUBTASK 27-31-20-420-002

SUBTASK 27-31-20-420-005

G. Prepare for the Installation
SUBTASK 27-31-31-860-003
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT YOU HAVE THE ELEVATOR TABS BALANCED. IF NOT
BALANCED, THE ELEVATOR TABS CAN CAUSE UNWANTED FLUTTER AND
INSTABILITY OF THE AIRPLANE. THIS CAN CAUSE AN IN-FLIGHT
EMERGENCY. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THESE INSTRUCTIONS, INJURY TO
PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(1) Examine the data plate on the elevator tab for the necessary number of the tab adjust weights
(SRM 51-60-06 or SRM 51-61-06).
SUBTASK 27-31-31-860-004
(2) Make sure that the elevator has the correct number of the tab adjust weights.
(a) Add or remove weights on the elevator balance panels as applicable.
H. Elevator Tab Installation
SUBTASK 27-31-31-020-005
(1) Do the following steps to install the elevator tab assembly [22] (Figure 402):
(a) Clean the elevator locations where bonding jumper [28] and bonding jumper [36] will be
attached.
(b) If bonding jumper [28] or bonding jumper [36] was removed from the elevator tab
assembly [22], reinstall them.
1) Measure the resistance between the bonding jumper [28] or bonding jumper [36]
and elevator tab assembly [22] after piercing the painted surface to the conductive
graphite layer of the elevator tab assembly [22].
a) Use the bonding meter, COM-15065.
b) Make sure that there is maximum of 100 ohms (100,000 milliohms) resistance.
2) Repair the paint of the elevator tab assembly [22] where the ohmmeter readings
were taken.
3) Seal the bonding jumper ends and fasteners with sealant, A00247.
(c) Apply compound, D50004, to the threads of the bolts [40] and bolts [47].
NOTE: It is not necessary to apply compound, D50004, to the unthreaded part of the
bolts.
(d) Put the elevator tab assembly [22] near its position behind the elevator [21].
CAUTION
DO NOT LET THE BONDING JUMPERS HOLD THE WEIGHT OF THE
ELEVATOR TAB ASSEMBLY. IF YOU DO, YOU CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO
THE BONDING JUMPERS.
(e) Connect the bonding jumper [28] to the elevator [21]:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Install the bolt [29], washers [27] and nut [26] to attach the bonding jumper [28] to
the elevator [21].
2) Measure the resistance between the bonding jumper [28] and elevator [21] after
piercing the painted surface to the conductive graphite layer of the elevator [21].
a) Use the bonding meter, COM-15065.
b) Make sure that there is maximum of 100 ohms (100,000 milliohms) resistance.
3) Seal the bonding jumper [28], bolt [29], washers [27], and nut [26] with sealant,
A00247.
(f) Connect the bonding jumper [36] to the elevator [21]:
1) Install the bolt [37], washers [35] and nut [34] to attach the bonding jumper [36] to
the elevator [21].
2) Measure the resistance between the bonding jumper [36] and elevator [21] after
piercing the painted surface to the conductive graphite layer of the elevator [21].
a) Use the bonding meter, COM-15065.
b) Make sure that there is maximum of 100 ohms (100,000 milliohms) resistance.
3) Seal the bonding jumper [36], bolt [37], washers [35], and nut [34] with sealant,
A00247.
SUBTASK 27-31-31-420-004
(2) Connect the elevator tab assembly [22] to the elevator [21]:
NOTE: If you loosened or removed the nuts [30], nuts [45] or nuts [52], they need to be
replaced with new nuts. Using new nuts will make sure that they have the required
run-on torque.
(a) Install the bolts [47], washers [50], bushings [49], washers [48], and new nuts [52] on the
outboard hinges (hinges 3, 4, 5 and 6).
NOTE: If it is necessary, you can install up to two additional washers under the nut.
1) Tighten the nuts [52] to 90 in-lb (10 N·m) - 100 in-lb (11 N·m) and install the new
pins [51] in the end of the bolts [47].
(b) Install the bolts [40], washers [41], bushing [42] on hinge 1, bushings [42] on hinge 2,
washers [43], and new nuts [45] on inboard hinges (hinges 1 and 2).
NOTE: If it is necessary, you can install up to two additional washers under the nut.
1) Tighten the nuts [45] to 90 in-lb (10 N·m) - 100 in-lb (11 N·m) and install the new
pins [44] in the end of the bolts [40].
(c) Install the bolts [33], bushings [32], washers [31], and new nuts [30] to connect the
elevator tab pushrods [25] to the elevator tab assembly [22].
NOTE: The inboard bolt is installed with the head inboard and outboard bolt is installed
with the head outboard.
CAUTION
TIGHTEN THE NEW NUTS CORRECTLY. IF YOU TIGHTEN THEM
INCORRECTLY, THE PUSHRODS CAN BECOME DISCONNECTED.
THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ELEVATOR AND STABILIZER.
1) Tighten the nuts [30] to 70 in-lb (8 N·m) - 80 in-lb (9 N·m) and install the new
pins [54] in the anti-rotation boss at the head of the bolts [33].
SUBTASK 27-31-31-610-001
(3) Do this task: Elevator Tab Hinge Lubrication, TASK 12-22-31-640-802.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-31-31-080-001

G. Prepare for the Check
SUBTASK 27-31-32-860-019
WARNING
KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE FLIGHT CONTROL
SURFACES. THE AILERONS, ELEVATORS, RUDDER, FLAPS, SLATS,
SPOILERS, STABILIZER AND NOSE GEAR CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN
YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO
PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE INBOARD FAN COWL PANEL AND THE INBOARD
AND OUTBOARD THRUST REVERSERS ARE CLOSED AND IN THE
STOWED POSITION OR REMOVED BEFORE YOU EXTEND THE LEADING
EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS. THERE IS NOT SUFFICIENT CLEARANCE FOR
THE FLAPS AND SLATS TO EXTEND IF THE INBOARD FAN COWL PANEL
AND THE INBOARD AND OUTBOARD THRUST REVERSERS ARE IN THE
OPEN POSITION. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(1) Pressurize the elevator hydraulic systems A and B. To pressurize them, do this task: Elevator
Hydraulic System A and B - Pressurization, TASK 27-31-00-800-801.
SUBTASK 27-31-32-860-020
(2) Make sure the flaps are in the full up position, do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System
Operation With Primary Control, TASK 27-51-00-860-801.
SUBTASK 27-31-32-010-004
(3) Open this access panel:
Number Name/Location
311BL Stabilizer Trim Access Door
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-31-32-860-021
CAUTION
MAKE SURE TO GIVE PROTECTION TO THE WIRE BUNDLES WHEN YOU
USE THE TRAMMEL BAR, SPL-1677. THE TRAMMEL BAR HAS SHARP
EDGES THAT CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE WIRE BUNDLE INSULATION.
(4) Use the trammel bar, SPL-1677 to set the "B" dimension at 39.89 ±0.03 in.
(1013.21 ±0.77 mm) or use the trim system to move the stabilizer to 4 units of trim.
(Figure 601)
SUBTASK 27-31-32-860-022
(5) Operate the elevator in the full travel 6 times.
SUBTASK 27-31-32-860-023
(6) Make sure the control column is in the neutral position.
H. Do a Check of the Buss Linkage of the Elevator Output Torque Tube
SUBTASK 27-31-32-220-010
CAUTION
DO NOT PUT A LOAD OF MORE THAN 65 POUNDS (290 NEWTONS) ON THE
ELEVATORS AT ONE TIME. IF THE LOAD IS TOO HEAVY, IT CAN CAUSE
DAMAGE TO THE ELEVATORS.
(1) Set the FLT CONTROL A switch on the forward overhead panel, P5, to the OFF position.
(2) Make sure the FLT CONTROL B switch on the forward overhead panel, P5, is in the ON
position.
(3) Put a piece of adhesive tape, G50393 over the right elevator index plate.
(4) Use a block, STD-1278 and force gauge, COM-1557 to apply a force of 15 ±1 lbf (67 ±5 N) to
the right elevator trailing edge in the down direction and release slowly.
(a) Apply the force approximately 0.5 in. (12.7 mm) forward of the trailing edge and 1 in.
(25 mm) outboard of the inboard edge of the elevator (next to the tailcone).
(b) Slowly remove the force from the elevator.
(c) Make a mark of the right elevator position on the tape.
(5) Use a block, STD-1278 and force gauge, COM-1557 to apply a force of 10 ±1 lbf (44 ±5 N) to
right elevator trailing edge in the up direction.
(a) Apply the force approximately 0.5 in. (12.7 mm) forward of the trailing edge and 1 in.
(25 mm) outboard of the inboard edge of the elevator (next to the tailcone).
(b) Hold the force of 10 ±1 lbf (44 ±5 N) on the elevator.
(c) Make a mark of the right elevator position on the tape.
(d) Slowly remove the force from the elevator.
(6) Make sure that the total up and down freeplay between the up and down position of the right
elevator is not greater than 0.21 in. (5.33 mm).
(a) If the total up and down freeplay is more than 0.21 in. (5.33 mm), check torque tube and
the torque tube crank arm bearing for excessive wear, do these tasks: Control Crank
Bearing and Sleeve Removal, TASK 27-31-74-000-802 and Control Crank Bearing and
Sleeving Installation, TASK 27-31-74-400-802.
(7) Remove the tape.
(8) Set the FLT CONTROL A switch on the forward overhead panel, P5, to the ON position.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(9) Set the FLT CONTROL B switch on the forward overhead panel, P5, to the OFF position.
(10) Put a piece of tape over the left elevator index plate [1].
(11) Use a block, STD-1278 and force gauge, COM-1557 to apply a force of 15 ±1 lbf (67 ±5 N) to
left elevator trailing edge in the down direction and release slowly.
(a) Apply the force approximately 0.5 in. (12.7 mm) forward of the trailing edge and 1 in.
(25 mm) outboard of the inboard edge of the elevator (next to the tailcone).
(b) Slowly remove the force from the elevator.
(c) Make a mark of the left elevator position on the tape.
(12) Use a block, STD-1278 and force gauge, COM-1557 to apply a force of 10 ±1 lbf (44 ±5 N) to
left elevator trailing edge in the up direction.
(a) Apply the force approximately 0.5 in. (12.7 mm) forward of the elevator trailing edge and
1 in. (25 mm) outboard of the inboard edge of the elevator (next to the tailcone).
(b) Hold the force of 10 ±1 lbf (44 ±5 N) on the elevator.
(c) Make a mark of the left elevator position on the tape.
(d) Slowly remove the force from the elevator.
(13) Make sure that the total up and down freeplay between the up and down position of the left
elevator is not greater than 0.21 in. (5.33 mm).
(a) If the total up and down freeplay is more than 0.21 in. (5.33 mm), check torque tube and
the torque tube crank arm bearing for excessive wear, do these tasks: Control Crank
Bearing and Sleeve Removal, TASK 27-31-74-000-802 and Control Crank Bearing and
Sleeving Installation, TASK 27-31-74-400-802.
(14) Remove the tape.
(15) Set the FLT CONTROL B switch on the forward overhead panel, P5, to the ON position.

YOU DO NOT INSTALL IT CORRECTLY.
(e) Attach a mounting plate to the elevator trailing edge forward of the elevator tab hinge 2.
1) If double-back tape is used to secure the mounting plate, make sure that it is not
made of compressible foam.
2) Attach the mount, STD-1279, and the dial indicator, STD-1238, plunger on the top
of the elevator tab, approximately 0.1 in. (3 mm) forward of the trailing edge of the
elevator tab and within 0.5 in. (13 mm) of the inboard side of the hinge 2 centerline.
3) Adjust the dial indicator, STD-1238, to zero.
(f) Use a block, STD-1278, and force gauge, COM-1557, to push down on the top of the
elevator tab with a force of 10.0 ±0.2 lbf (44.5 ±0.9 N).
1) Apply the force on the elevator tab at the trailing edge, as close as possible to the
tab hinge 2 centerline.
2) Make a record of the travel shown on the dial indicator, STD-1238.
3) Slowly remove the force.
(g) Do not adjust the dial indicator, STD-1238.
(h) Push up on the bottom surface of the elevator tab with a force of 10.0 ±0.2 lbf
(44.5 ±0.9 N), directly below the force applied before.
1) Make a record of the travel shown on the dial indicator, STD-1238.
2) Slowly remove the force.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(i) Make sure that the sum of the two travel records is not more than 0.03 in. (0.76 mm).
1) If the sum of the two travel records is more than 0.03 in. (0.76 mm), check the
hinges for excessive wear and replace, as necessary.
(j) Remove the mount, STD-1279, and the dial indicator, STD-1238.
(k) Remove the mounting plate.
(l) If no other checks are necessary, remove the wood block from between the inboard edge
of the elevator and the tail cone.
H. Do a Check of the Elevator Tab Hinge Axial Freeplay
SUBTASK 27-31-32-220-013
(1) Do a check of the elevator tab hinge axial freeplay (Figure 602).
(a) Remove pressure from the elevator hydraulic systems A and B, do this task: Remove
Pressure from the Elevator Hydraulic Systems A and B, TASK 27-31-00-800-802.
(b) Make sure that the flaps are retracted to the full up position.
(c) Make sure that the stabilizer is set at 4.0 +/- 0.5 units of trim.
CAUTION
DO NOT USE MORE THAN HAND PRESSURE WHEN YOU INSTALL THE
WOOD BLOCK. IF YOU USE MORE THAN HAND PRESSURE, YOU CAN
CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ELEVATOR OR TAIL CONE.
(d) Keep the elevator from moving by installing a wood block between the inboard edge of
the elevator and the tail cone (Figure 602).
1) Make sure that you cover the wood block with duct tape or equivalent so that you do
not damage the paint of the elevator or tail cone.
(e) Do these steps to make sure that the axial play (inboard - outboard direction) of the tab is
not more than 0.036 in. (0.91 mm).
1) Hold the elevator tab at the trailing edge and move it outboard using hand pressure.
2) Use a 0.0 - 0.5 Inch feeler gauge, STD-1107, or a dial caliper, STD-1303, to
measure the clearance between the elevator and the outboard end of the elevator
tab.
a) If it is necessary, insert a flat metal filler block between the elevator and the
elevator tab to help in this measurement.
b) Make a record of the clearance dimension.
3) Hold the elevator tab at the trailing edge and move it inboard using hand pressure.
4) Measure the clearance between the elevator and the outboard end of the elevator
tab.
a) Make a record of the clearance dimension.
5) Make sure that the difference between the two measured clearances, or the axial
freeplay, is less than 0.036 in. (0.91 mm).
(f) If no other checks are necessary, remove the wood block from between the inboard edge
of the elevator and the tail cone.
I. Do a Check of the Elevator Tab Hinge Line Freeplay
SUBTASK 27-31-32-220-014
(1) Do a check of the elevator tab hinge line freeplay (Figure 602):
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) If it is necessary, remove pressure from the elevator hydraulic systems A and B, do this

TASK 27-31-00-800-802.
(b) Make sure that the stabilizer is set at 4.0 +/- 0.5 units of trim.
(c) Make sure that the flaps are retracted to the full up position.
CAUTION
DO NOT USE MORE THAN HAND PRESSURE WHEN YOU INSTALL THE
WOOD BLOCK. IF YOU USE MORE THAN HAND PRESSURE, YOU CAN
CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ELEVATOR OR TAIL CONE.
(d) Keep the elevator from moving by installing a wood block between the inboard edge of
the elevator and the tail cone (Figure 602).
1) Make sure that you cover the wood block with duct tape or equivalent so that you do
not damage the paint of the elevator or tail cone.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU INSTALL THE MOUNTING PLATE CORRECTLY.
THE MOUNTING PLATE CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ELEVATOR IF
YOU DO NOT INSTALL IT CORRECTLY.
(e) Attach a mounting plate to the elevator trailing edge, forward of elevator tab hinge 3.
1) If double-back tape is used to secure the mounting plate, make sure that it is not
made of compressible foam.
(f) Attach the mount, STD-1279, and the dial indicator, STD-1238, plunger on the elevator
tab leading edge directly over the top of the tab hinge centerline (Figure 602, sheet 6).
(g) Adjust the dial indicator, STD-1238, to zero once there is contact with the elevator tab
leading edge.
(h) Use a block, STD-1278, and force gauge, COM-1557, to apply a 10.0 ±0.5 lbf
(44.5 ±2.2 N) in the up direction.
1) Apply the force in line with the plunger on the bottom side of the tab leading edge.
(i) Make a record of the travel shown on the dial indicator, STD-1238.
(j) Slowly remove the force.
(k) Do not adjust the dial indicator, STD-1238.
(l) Use a block, STD-1278, and force gauge, COM-1557, to apply a 10.0 ±0.5 lbf
(44.5 ±2.2 N) in the down direction.
1) Apply the force to the top side of the tab leading edge.
(m) Make a record of the travel shown on the dial indicator, STD-1238.
(n) Slowly remove the force.
(o) Make sure that the sum of the two travel records is not more than 0.03 in. (0.76 mm).
1) If the sum of the two travel records is more than 0.03 in. (0.76 mm) check the
hinges for excessive wear and replace, as necessary.
(p) Move the mount, STD-1279, the dial indicator, STD-1238, and the mounting plate to the
next hinge centerline.
(q) Repeat the above steps for the other three outboard tab hinges (hinges 4, 5, and 6).
(r) Remove the mount, STD-1279, and the dial indicator, STD-1238.
(s) Remove the mounting plate.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(t) Remove the wood block from between the inboard edge of the elevator and the tail cone.

(7) Measure and record the elevator tab position in relation to the elevator.
NOTE: Measuring and recording the elevator tab position before you remove the tab may
improve the manual reversion success rate, if the tab needs to be adjusted after
installation. The tab position can be measured with the elevator tab rigging bar,
SPL-10345, installed on the third elevator tab hinge (from inboard).
(a) Push the elevator trailing edge up by hand.
(b) While you move the elevator trailing edge down, align the projected center of the elevator
trailing edge with the index mark within +/- 0.04 in. (1.02 mm), or less.
1) Install the rigging bar, SPL-10345 (Figure 27-31-00-990-811).
a) To use the rigging bar, SPL-10345, do the steps that follow:
<1> Move the digital micrometer to the bottom of the slide.
<2> Push the button on the micrometer to zero the micrometer reading.
<3> Move the digital micrometer up until it gives the same reading as the
calibration value stamped on the side of the tool.
NOTE: This brings the pointer on the micrometer up to approximately
0.3 in. (7.6 mm) below the trailing edge of the elevator tab.
NOTE: The C27028 rigging bar requires the micrometer be zeroed to
the elevator neutral position which is located by the dimension
stamped on the tool above the full down position. Refer to the
tool placard for information.
<4> Without moving the micrometer, push the button on the micrometer to
zero the micrometer reading.
<a> This is the elevator tab neutral/faired position.
NOTE: The micrometer must be zeroed at the neutral position to
prevent tab misalignment and large pitch upset during
manual reversion.
b) Install the rigging bar, SPL-10345, below the elevator and elevator tab at the
third elevator tab hinge (from inboard).
c) Make sure that the cross bar on the rigging bar, SPL-10345, touches the lower
surface of the elevator trailing edge.
2) Measure and record the elevator tab position.
3) Make sure that the distance between the left elevator tab and rigging bar,
SPL-10345, is within 0.20 in. (5.08 mm) - 0.50 in. (12.70 mm).
4) Make sure that the distance between the right elevator tab and rigging bar,
SPL-10345, is within 0.20 in. (5.08 mm) - 0.50 in. (12.70 mm).

 ALL

E. Elevator Tab Control Mechanism Installation
SUBTASK 27-31-34-860-004
(1) Make sure that the hydraulic power is removed from the elevator hydraulic systems A and B
(TASK 27-31-00-800-802).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
 ALL; AIRPLANES WITH THE SIX HINGE ELEVATOR TAB WITH RECTANGULAR HEAD BOLTS
SUBTASK 27-31-34-420-009
 ALL
(2) Do the following steps to install the tab mechanism [32]:
(a) Put the tab mechanism [32] in its position.
(b) Do these steps to connect the tab pushrods [29] to the tab mechanism [32]:
1) Apply compound, D50004, to the threads of the bolts [41] and outer surface of the
spacers [54].
2) Install the bolts [41], washers [46], spacers [54], and new nuts [47] to connect the
tab pushrods [29] to the tab mechanism [32].
NOTE: The inboard bolt is installed with the head inboard and outboard bolt is
installed with the head outboard.
a) Tighten the nuts [47] to 70 in-lb (8 N·m) - 80 in-lb (9 N·m).
NOTE: If you loosened or removed the nuts, they need to be replaced and not
re-installed. Using new nuts will make sure that they have the required
run-on torque of 3.5 in-lb (0.4 N·m).
(c) Apply compound, D50004, to the threads of the pin assembly [40].
(d) Install the pin assembly [40] with the head at the inside of the tab mechanism [32],
washer [51], and nut [52] to connect the tab mechanism [32] to elevator [21].
NOTE: You must use a Phillips screwdriver set-up to hold the heads of the pin assembly
when tightening the nut.
1) Tighten the nut [52] to 35 in-lb (4 N·m).
(e) Apply compound, D50004, to the threads of the pin assembly [42].
(f) Install the pin assembly [42] with the head at the inside of the tab mechanism [32],
washer [43], and nut [45] to connect the tab mechanism [32] to the elevator [21].
1) Make sure that the longer tab mechanism pin assembly [42] installs inboard
(Figure 402).
2) Tighten the nut [45] to 35 in-lb (4 N·m).
(g) Rotate the pin retainer [49] arms down and install the screws [48] and washers [55] to
attach the pin retainers [49] to the tab mechanism [32].
(h) Apply compound, D50004, to the threads of the bolt assemblies [39] and outer surface of
the bushings [38].
(i) Install the bushings [38], bolt assemblies [39], washers [34], and nuts [35] to connect the
tab mechanism [32] to the horizontal stabilizer [33].
NOTE: The bolts are installed with the heads at the outside of the tab mechanism.
1) Tighten the nuts [35] to 50 in-lb (6 N·m) - 60 in-lb (7 N·m).
CAUTION
DO NOT TIGHTEN THE NUTS [35] AGAIN AFTER YOU TIGHTEN THE
NUT [37]. YOU CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(j) Install the washers [36] and nuts [37].
1) Tighten the nuts [37] to 12 in-lb (1 N·m) - 15 in-lb (2 N·m).
(k) Connect the hydraulic line [31] to the tab mechanism [32].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(l) Connect the electrical line and electrical line clamp [30] to the tab mechanism [32].
(m) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [31] to 140 ±7 in-lb (16 ±1 N·m).

2) Push the button on the micrometer to zero the micrometer reading.

value stamped on the side of the tool.
NOTE: This brings the pointer on the micrometer up to approximately 0.3 in.

the elevator trailing edge.

G. Tab Pushrod Removal
SUBTASK 27-31-34-020-008
(1) Remove the bolts [24] that attach the access panel [23] to the elevator [21].
SUBTASK 27-31-34-020-009
(2) Remove the tab pushrod [29]:
(a) Remove the screws [48], washers [55] from the pin retainer [49].
(b) Remove the pin [53], nut [25], washer [26], bushing [27], and bolt [28] from the tab
pushrod [29] and elevator tab [22].
1) Discard the pin [53].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(c) Remove the upper access panels to disconnect the tab mechanism [32] from the elevator
by removing the nut [52], nut [45], washer [51], washer [43], bushings [50], pin
assembly [40], pin assembly [42], if it is required to remove bolts [41].
NOTE: For ease of removal of pin assembly [40] and pin assembly [42] use
removal/installation equipment, SPL-12558.
 ALL; AIRPLANES WITH THE SIX HINGE ELEVATOR TAB WITH RECTANGULAR HEAD BOLTS
(d) Remove the nut [47], washer [46], spacer [54], and the bolt [41] from the tab
mechanism [32] and tab pushrod [29].
 ALL
(e) Disconnect the tab pushrod [29] from the tab mechanism [32].
(f) Remove the tab pushrod [29] from the airplane.
SUBTASK 27-31-34-420-014
(3) Use the fixture, SPL-11021, to assist in measuring and replacing the new or replacement tab
pushrods to match the removed old tab pushrods (Figure 27-31-00-990-853):
NOTE: Measuring the new or replacement tab pushrod using fixture, SPL-11021, is optional.
The tool is used to adjust the new or replacement tab rods off the airplane to the same
length as the removed tab rods. This adjustment will reduce the chance that a second
flight test will be required.
NOTE: Use the previously recorded elevator tab dimension obtained using
Figure 27-31-00-990-811.
(a) Make sure no changes to the recorded elevator tab dimensions are made after removal.
(b) Install the old removed tab pushrods onto the fixture, SPL-11021.
(c) Set the digital scales to zero.
(d) Remove the old tab pushrods.
(e) Install the new or replacement tab pushrods onto the fixture, SPL-11021.
NOTE: The inboard and outboard pushrod must be identified prior to adjustment. The
slot in the retainer that attaches the pushrod is on the inboard for the RH elevator
and outboard for the LH elevator.
(f) Record readings from the scale.
(g) Adjust the new or replacement tab pushrods by coarse or fine method until scale is back
to 0 +0.0005/-0.0005 inches (TASK 27-31-00-820-805).
NOTE: The fine adjustments may be made with the pushrod installed on the tool. The
coarse adjustments must be made with the pushrods removed from the tool.
(h) Tighten the checknut to prevent movement of the rod end prior to installation.
NOTE: Do not lockwire the checknuts until final adjustment is done on the airplane.
(i) Remove the new or replacement tab pushrods from fixture, SPL-11021.
(j) Using the information from the previously recorded old elevator tab dimension, tag the
new tab pushrods with the same information.
(k) Install the new or replacement tab pushrods onto the fixture, SPL-11021.
(l) Verify the scales read 0 +0.0005/-0.0005 inches.
(m) Remove the tab pushrods.
1) Make sure that no adjustment is made to tab pushrods when removing from fixture,
SPL-11021.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(n) Tighten the checknuts on the tab pushrods (TASK 27-31-00-820-805.).
(o) Install the new or replacement tab pushrods onto the airplane, do this task: Elevator Tab
Pushrod - Installation, TASK 27-31-34-400-803.
(p) Verify the tab position is the same as the tab dimension first obtained from the old tab
pushrods rigging bar, SPL-10345 readings within 0.00 ±0.01 in. (0.00 ±0.25 mm).
1) If it is necessary, adjust the pushrods on the airplane.

E. Tab Pushrod Installation
SUBTASK 27-31-34-860-006
(1) Make sure that hydraulic power is removed from the elevator hydraulic systems A and B
(TASK 27-31-00-800-802).
SUBTASK 27-31-34-420-004
(2) Do the following steps to install the tab pushrods [29]:
(a) Put the tab pushrods [29] in its position.
(b) Make sure that the orientation of the tab pushrods [29] is correct.
NOTE: This orientation is applicable to the left and right elevator tab mechanisms.
1) For the left tab pushrod [29], the HI-LOK collars must be in the 3 o'clock and 6
o'clock positions at each end.
2) For the right tab pushrod [29], the HI-LOK collars must be in the 6 o'clock and 9
o'clock positions at each end.
(c) If you loosened or removed the nuts [47] or nuts [25], replace them with the new nuts [47]
or new nuts [25].
NOTE: Using new nuts will make sure that they have the required run-on torque.
(d) If the bolt [41] was removed, do this step (Figure 402):
1) Install the pin assembly [40], bushing [50], washer [51], and nut [52] to install the tab
mechanism [32] to the elevator [21].
 ALL; AIRPLANES WITH THE SIX HINGE ELEVATOR TAB WITH RECTANGULAR HEAD BOLTS
(e) Install the spacers [54], bolts [41], washers [46], and nuts [47] to connect the tab
pushrods [29] to the tab mechanism [32].
NOTE: The inboard bolt is installed with the head inboard and outboard bolt is installed
with the head outboard.
 ALL
CAUTION
IF THE NEW NUTS [47] ARE NOT TIGHTENED CORRECTLY, THEN THE
PUSHRODS CAN BECOME DISCONNECTED AND CAUSE DAMAGE TO
THE ELEVATOR AND STABILIZER.
(f) Tighten the nuts [47] to 70 in-lb (7.9 N·m) - 80 in-lb (9.0 N·m).
(g) Install the screws [48] and washers [55] to attach the pin retainers [49] to the tab
mechanism [32].
(h) Install the bushings [27], bolts [28], washers [26] and nuts [25] to connect the tab
pushrods [29] to the elevator tab [22].
NOTE: The inboard bolt is installed with the head inboard and outboard bolt is installed
with the head outboard.
CAUTION
IF THE NEW NUTS [25] ARE NOT TIGHTENED CORRECTLY, THEN THE
PUSHRODS CAN BECOME DISCONNECTED AND CAUSE DAMAGE TO
THE ELEVATOR AND STABILIZER.
(i) Tighten the nuts [25] to 70 in-lb (7.9 N·m) - 80 in-lb (9.0 N·m) and install the new pins [53]
in the anti-rotation boss at the head of the bolt [28].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-31-34-820-002
(3) Adjust the tab pushrods [29] until you get the same tab position that you measured before you

F. Elevator Tab Control Mechanism Spring Removal
SUBTASK 27-31-34-020-020
(1) Do these steps to remove one or both of the aft springs [83]:
(a) Install the hook assembly and tool handle from the removal/installation equipment,
SPL-13742, on the short fitting assembly from the removal/installation equipment,
SPL-13742, in the correct position for the aft springs [83] to be removed.
1) If both aft springs [83] are installed, attach the hook assembly on the center of the
aft bushing [85].
2) If one of the aft springs [83] is missing or broken, attach the hook assembly on the
aft bushing [85] around the remaining aft spring [83].
(b) Install the removal/installation equipment, SPL-13742, on the elevator control tab
mechanism assembly.
(c) Put a socket wrench, COM-6048, or equivalent on the bolt [87].
WARNING
DO NOT TIGHTEN THE TOOL HANDLE TOOL MUCH. THIS CAN CAUSE
DAMAGE TO THE TOOL, AIRPLANE STRUCTURE OR INJURY TO
PERSONNEL.
(d) At the same time, slowly turn the tool handle and the socket wrench, COM-6048, until the
bolt [87] starts to come loose.
1) Make sure that you do not tighten the tool handle too much, it should take
approximately 1/4 turn to loosen the bolt [87].
(e) After the bolt [87] is loose, remove the nut [92], washer [91], bolt [87], nut [90].
washer [89], and bolt [88].
(f) Loosen the tool handle.
(g) Remove one or both of the aft springs [83] as necessary.
SUBTASK 27-31-34-020-021
(2) Do these steps to remove one or both of the forward springs [84]:
(a) Install the hook assembly and tool handle from the removal/installation equipment,
SPL-13742, on the long fitting assembly from the removal/installation equipment,
SPL-13742, in the correct position for the forward springs [84] to be removed.
1) If both forward springs [84] are installed, attach the hook assembly on the center of
the forward bushing [86].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
2) If one of the forward springs [84] is missing or broken, attach the hook assembly on
the forward bushing [86] around the remaining forward spring [84].
(b) Install the removal/installation equipment, SPL-13742, on the elevator control tab
mechanism assembly.
(c) Put a socket wrench, COM-6048, or equivalent on the bolt [87].
WARNING
DO NOT TIGHTEN THE TOOL HANDLE TOOL MUCH. THIS CAN CAUSE
DAMAGE TO THE TOOL, AIRPLANE STRUCTURE OR INJURY TO
PERSONNEL.
(d) At the same time, slowly turn the tool handle and the socket wrench, COM-6048, until the
bolt [87] starts to come loose.
1) Make sure that you do not tighten the tool handle too much, it should take
approximately 1/4 turn to loosen the bolt [87].
(e) After the bolt [87] is loose, remove the nut [92], washer [91], bolt [87], nut [90].
washer [89], and bolt [88].
(f) Loosen the tool handle.
(g) Remove one or both of the forward springs [84] as necessary.

NOTE: The “B” dimension is measured between the center of the upper and lower Gimbal

(b) Use the trammel bar, SPL-1677, to measure the “B” dimension at 39.89 ±0.03 in.

MAKE SURE TO PREVENT DAMAGE TO THE WIRE BUNDLES
WHEN YOU USE THE TRAMMEL BAR, SPL-1677. THE TRAMMEL
BAR HAS SHARP EDGES THAT CAN CHAFE OR CAN CAUSE
DAMAGE THE WIRES OR BUNDLE INSULATION.

F. Elevator Feel Computer Removal
SUBTASK 27-31-37-020-001
CAUTION
DO NOT LIFT THE ELEVATOR FEEL COMPUTER BY THE INPUT ARM, OR
APPLY A TORQUE OF MORE THAN 300 POUND-INCHES (33.9 NEWTON￾METERS) TO THE INPUT ARM. THE ELEVATOR FEEL COMPUTER IS VERY
SENSITIVE AND IT CAN BE DAMAGED.
(1) Remove the elevator feel computer assembly [1].
(a) Disconnect the spring [16] from the crank [25].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) Remove the nut [26], washer [27], and screw [28] to disconnect the crank [25] from the
elevator feel computer assembly [1].
(c) Remove the nut [23], washer [22], and bolt [21] to disconnect the stabilizer pushrod [2]
from the input arm [8].
(d) Disconnect the electrical connector [7] from the elevator feel computer assembly [1].
(e) Put an applicable container below the elevator feel computer assembly [1].
NOTE: Hydraulic fluid leakage can occur when you disconnect the hydraulic lines from
the elevator feel computer assembly.
WARNING
RELEASE THE CONNECTION SLOWLY AND LET THE PRESSURE
DECREASE BEFORE YOU COMPLETELY REMOVE THE HYDRAULIC
LINE. IF YOU DISCONNECT THE HYDRAULIC LINE WHEN IT HAS
PRESSURE, A SPRAY OF HYDRAULIC FLUID CAN CAUSE INJURY TO
PERSONS.
(f) Disconnect the hydraulic lines [29] and hydraulic lines [30] from the elevator feel
computer assembly [1] as follows:
1) Install tags on lines and port fittings to clearly show the correct connection location
(TASK 20-10-51-000-801).
2) Remove the packings [9] and reducers [10] from the computer pressure line fittings.
3) Remove the filters [11], packings [12], and unions [13] from the hydraulic line
fittings.
4) Remove the packings [14] and unions [15] from the return line fittings.
5) Remove the packings [17] and unions [18] from the static line fittings.
6) Remove the packings [19] and unions [20] from the pitot line fittings.
(g) Install caps to the hydraulic lines, pitot lines, and static lines.
(h) Install plugs to all ports.
(i) Remove the nuts [6], washers [5], washers [4], and bolts [3] that attach the elevator feel
computer assembly [1] to the airplane structure.
(j) Remove the elevator feel computer assembly [1] from the airplane.
SUBTASK 27-31-37-540-001
(2) Discard the packings [9], packings [12], packings [14], packings [17], and packings [19].

G. Elevator Feel Computer Installation
SUBTASK 27-31-37-020-021
(1) For a new elevator feel computer assembly [1], do these steps:
(a) Remove the transport/storage strings from the input arm [8] and elevator feel computer
assembly [1].
CAUTION
YOU MUST INSTALL THE SAFETY PIN IN THE RIG PIN HOLE OF THE
ELEVATOR FEEL COMPUTER. IF YOU DO NOT ATTACH THE ELEVATOR
FEEL COMPUTER TO THE INPUT ARM, DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT
CAN OCCUR.
(b) Install the pin, SPL-1673, in the input arm [8] and elevator feel computer assembly [1].
SUBTASK 27-31-37-860-004
(2) Make sure that pressure is removed from the elevator hydraulic systems A and B.
(a) If it is necessary, do this task: Remove Pressure from the Elevator Hydraulic Systems A
and B, TASK 27-31-00-800-802.
SUBTASK 27-31-37-860-005
CAUTION
MAKE SURE TO PREVENT DAMAGE TO THE WIRE BUNDLES WHEN YOU
USE THE TRAMMEL BAR, SPL-1677. THE TRAMMEL BAR HAS SHARP
EDGES THAT CAN CHAF OR CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE WIRES OR
BUNDLE INSULATION.
(3) Use the trammel bar, SPL-1677, to make sure that the “B” dimension is at 39.86 in.
(1012.44 mm) - 39.92 in. (1013.97 mm).
SUBTASK 27-31-37-420-001
(4) If the packings [9], packings [12], packings [14], packings [17], packings [19], reducers [10],
filters [11], unions [13], unions [15], unions [18], and unions [20] are not installed in the elevator
feel computer assembly [1], do these steps:
(a) Lightly lubricate the new packings [9], new packings [12], new packings [14], new
packings [17], and new packings [19] with hydraulic fluid, D00153.
(b) Install these items in the elevator feel computer assembly [1]:
1) The packings [9] and reducers [10] to the fittings for the computer pressure lines.
a) Tighten the reducers [10] on the computer pressure lines to 255 in-lb (29 N·m)
- 285 in-lb (32 N·m).
2) The filters [11], packings [12], and unions [13] to the fittings for the hydraulic lines.
a) Tighten the unions [13] on the hydraulic lines to 135 in-lb (15 N·m) - 150 in-lb
(17 N·m).
3) The packings [14] and unions [15] to the fittings for the return lines.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
a) Tighten the unions [15] on the return lines to 255 in-lb (29 N·m) - 285 in-lb
(32 N·m).
4) The packings [17] and unions [18] to the fittings for the static lines.
a) Tighten the unions [18] on the static lines to 75 in-lb (8 N·m) - 125 in-lb
(14 N·m).
5) The packings [19] and unions [20] to the fittings for the pitot lines.
a) Tighten the unions [20] on the pitot lines to 75 in-lb (8 N·m) - 125 in-lb
(14 N·m).
SUBTASK 27-31-37-080-001
(5) Remove the pin, SPL-1673, from the input arm [8] and elevator feel computer assembly [1].
SUBTASK 27-31-37-480-002
(6) Install the rig pin E-4 from the test set rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, in the input arm [8] and
elevator feel computer assembly [1].
SUBTASK 27-31-37-420-002
(7) Install the elevator feel computer assembly [1].
(a) Put the elevator feel computer assembly [1] in its position.
(b) Install the bolts [3], washers [4] (under the bolt), washers [5] (under the nut), and nuts [6]
to attach the elevator feel computer assembly [1] to the airplane structure.
(c) Connect the stabilizer pushrod [2] to the input arm [8]:
1) If the bolt [21] cannot be installed, do these steps to adjust the length of the
stabilizer pushrod [2]:
a) Loosen the checknut [24] on the stabilizer pushrod [2].
b) Turn the rod end fitting of the stabilizer pushrod [2] until the bolt [21] can be
installed easily by hand.
c) Make sure that the rod end extends more than half of the distance across the
inspection hole in the stabilizer pushrod [2].
d) Tighten the checknut [24].
2) Install the washer [22] and nut [23] to the bolt [21].
(d) Connect the crank [25] to the elevator feel computer assembly [1].
(e) Install the screw [28], washer [27], and nut [26].
(f) Connect the spring [16] to the crank [25].
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU CONNECT THE HYDRAULIC LINES TO THE
CORRECT PORTS. IF YOU INSTALL THE HYDRAULIC LINES TO
INCORRECT PORTS, YOU CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ELEVATOR
FEEL COMPUTER.
(g) Connect the hydraulic lines to the elevator feel computer assembly [1]
(TASK 20-10-51-400-804).
1) Remove the caps and plugs.
2) Connect the hydraulic lines [29] and hydraulic lines [30] to the elevator feel
computer assembly [1].
3) Tighten the B-nuts on the hydraulic lines [29] to 170 ±9 in-lb (19 ±1 N·m).
4) Tighten the B-nuts on the hydraulic lines [30] to 140 ±7 in-lb (16 ±1 N·m).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(h) Remove the caps and plugs from pitot lines, static line.
(i) Connect the pitot lines and static lines to the fittings on the elevator feel computer
assembly [1].
1) Tighten the pitot lines to 170.0 ±8.5 in-lb (19.2 ±1.0 N·m).
(j) Connect the electrical connector [7] to the elevator feel computer assembly [1].
SUBTASK 27-31-37-080-002
(8) Remove the rig pin E-4 of the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, from the input arm [8] and elevator feel
computer assembly [1].
SUBTASK 27-31-37-860-006
(9) Do this task: Put the Elevator Systems A and B Back to the Condition Before the Pressure
Removal, TASK 27-31-00-840-802.
SUBTASK 27-31-37-410-004
(10) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers:

Row Col Number Name
B 2 C01064 AFCS SYS B MACH TRIM DC
B 4 C00716 AFCS SYS B ENGAGE INTLK

SUBTASK 27-31-37-860-041
(11) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2
Row Col Number Name
B 3 C01046 AFCS SYS B FCC DC
SUBTASK 27-31-37-870-001
(12) Bleed the elevator control system:
(a) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2
Row Col Number Name
B 10 C00207 FLIGHT CONTROL STAB TRIM CONT
D 10 C00840 FLIGHT CONTROL STAB TRIM ACTUATOR
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT ALL PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT ARE AWAY
FROM THE HORIZONTAL STABILIZER AND CONTROL CABLES IN THE
FORWARD EQUIPMENT COMPARTMENT OR AREA AFT OF THE
BULKHEAD. THE MOVEMENT OF THE HORIZONTAL STABILIZER
DURING MAINTENANCE CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONNEL AND
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(b) Move the stabilizer to the maximum leading edge up (APL NOSE DOWN) position (the
mechanical limits).
NOTE: This can be done with the control wheel STAB TRIM switches or the stabilizer
trim control wheel.
1) Make sure that the ballnut is against the jackscrew upstop.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(c) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags:
CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-3
Row Col Number Name
C 4 C00236 HEATERS ELEV PITOT LEFT
D 4 C00237 HEATERS ELEV PITOT RIGHT
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE PITOT PROBE HAS NO ADDED WEIGHT ON IT
FROM THE TEST HOSE. THE WEIGHT OF THE TEST HOSE CAN BEND
OR TWIST THE PITOT PROBE OUT OF TOLERANCE.
(d) Connect the regulator, SPL-1742, or equivalent air data model test set, COM-1914, to the
two pitot probes on the vertical fin.
1) Do this step for the regulator, SPL-1742:
a) Connect the pressure lines from the regulator, SPL-1742, with the pitot test
adapter, COM-1916, to the pitot probes.
2) Do this step for the air data model test set, COM-1914:
a) Use the air data accessory kit, COM-25177, to connect the air data model test
set, COM-1914, to the pitot test adapter, COM-1916.
NOTE: The air data accessory kit, COM-25177, contains hoses to connect to
the air data model test set, COM-1914, and the pitot test adapter,
COM-1916.
(e) Remove the restrictor valves from the bottom of the pitot lines.
(f) If the regulator, SPL-1742, or equivalent is used, do this step:
1) Connect the pressure gauge lines from the regulator, SPL-1742, or equivalent, to
the drain holes of the pitot lines.
(g) If the air data model test set, COM-1914, is used, do these steps:
1) Install plugs over the ends of the pitot lines.
2) Install a highly visible streamer on the opening of the aft unpressurized
compartment.
a) Make sure that the streamer can be easily seen from the ground.
NOTE: This is to remind to remove the plugs and install the restrictor valves
again when the test is completed.
(h) Use the regulator, SPL-1742, or air data model test set, COM-1914, to raise the airspeed
to 2.46 psig (300 knots).
NOTE: When pressure to the pitot system is applied or removed, the rate must not be
more than 2.46 psig (300 knots) for each minute.
WARNING
KEEP PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE FLIGHT
CONTROL SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING
GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU
SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO
PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(i) Pressurize the Hydraulic Systems A and B, do one of these steps:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) If a Portable Hydraulic Cart is used, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B
Pressurization with a Portable Hydraulic Cart, TASK 29-11-00-860-802.
NOTE: Two carts are recommended.
a) If only one cart is available, bleed hydraulic system A and B, as follows:
<1> Pressurize the hydraulic system A with a cart and hydraulic systems B
with the Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP).
<2> Pressurize the hydraulic system B with a cart and hydraulic systems A
with the EMDP.
2) If a Portable Hydraulic Cart is not used, do these tasks:
NOTE: Both the Engine Driven Pump (EDP) and EMDP should be operated at the
same time.
• Hydraulic System Pressurization with an Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP),
TASK 29-11-00-860-803
• Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization with an Engine-Driven Pump (EDP),
TASK 29-11-00-860-804.
(j) Do these steps to cycle the power between Hydraulic Systems A and B:
1) Set the flight controls hydraulic power switches as follows:
a) Set the FLT CONTROL B switch to OFF position.
b) Set the FLT CONTROL A switch to A ON position.
c) Wait for 2 seconds.
d) Set the FLT CONTROL A switch to OFF position.
e) Set the FLT CONTROL B switch to B ON position.
f) Wait for 2 seconds.
2) Repeat the cycle 10 times.
(k) Slowly, do column sweeps with pitot pressure applied.
(l) Do these steps to cycle pitot pressure:
1) Use the regulator, SPL-1742, or air data model test set, COM-1914, connected at
the elevator pitot probes on the vertical stabilizer, to lower the airspeed to 0 psig (0
knots)
2) Use the regulator, SPL-1742, or air data model test set, COM-1914, connected at
the elevator pitot probes on the vertical stabilizer, to increase the airspeed to 2.46
psig (300 knots).
3) Use the regulator, SPL-1742, or air data model test set, COM-1914, connected at
the elevator pitot probes on the vertical stabilizer, to lower the airspeed to 0 psig (0
knots).
SUBTASK 27-31-37-860-010
(13) Remove the pressure from the Hydraulic systems A and B (TASK 29-11-00-860-805).
SUBTASK 27-31-37-210-001
(14) Make sure that there is no hydraulic leakage from the elevator feel computer.
(a) If it is necessary, do this task: Elevator Feel Computer - Leakage Check,
TASK 27-31-37-200-802.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-31-37-860-008
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT ALL PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT ARE AWAY FROM
THE HORIZONTAL STABILIZER AND CONTROL CABLES IN THE FORWARD
EQUIPMENT COMPARTMENT OR AREA AFT OF THE BULKHEAD. THE
MOVEMENT OF THE HORIZONTAL STABILIZER DURING MAINTENANCE
CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(15) Move the horizontal stabilizer to the neutral stabilizer position (zero degrees or 4 units of trim).
NOTE: This can be done with the control wheel STAB TRIM switches or the stabilizer trim
control wheel.
