2. Elevator Feel Computer - Leakage Check
(Figure 27-31-37-990-801)
A. General
(1) Use this task to check for leakage at the elevator feel computer.
B. References
Reference Title
20-10-51-400-804 Flareless Tubing Assembly Installation (P/B 401)
27-31-00-800-801 Elevator Hydraulic System A and B - Pressurization (P/B 201)
27-31-00-800-802 Remove Pressure from the Elevator Hydraulic Systems A and B
(P/B 201)
27-31-37 P/B 401 ELEVATOR FEEL COMPUTER - REMOVAL/INSTALLATION
27-31-37-990-801 Figure: Elevator Feel Computer Installation (P/B 401)
C. Consumable Materials
Reference Description Specification
G01043 Cloth - Lint-free
G50641 Swab - ITW Texwipe TX762 Absorbond Swab
With Long Handle
D. Procedure
SUBTASK 27-31-37-200-001
(1) Do these steps to check for leakage:
(a) Clean any residual hydraulic fluid from the elevator feel computer with a lint-free cloth,
G01043.
WARNING
KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE FLIGHT CONTROL
SURFACES. THE AILERONS, ELEVATORS, RUDDER, FLAPS, SLATS,
SPOILERS, STABILIZER AND NOSE GEAR CAN MOVE SUDDENLY
WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY
TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(b) Pressurize the elevator hydraulic system A and B for one minute and verify that there is
no leakage: Elevator Hydraulic System A and B - Pressurization,
TASK 27-31-00-800-801.
(c) Visually examine the external surface of the elevator feel computer static tubes for signs
of hydraulic fluid.
(d) Visually examine the supply, return and feel pressure tubing B-nuts connection to the
elevator feel computer.
(e) Remove pressure from elevator hydraulic system A and B: Remove Pressure from the
Elevator Hydraulic Systems A and B, TASK 27-31-00-800-802.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(f) If there is no sign of hydraulic fluid at these locations, then continue.
(g) If there is a sign of hydraulic fluid at these locations, the B-nuts may not be correctly
installed or may have become loose.
1) Check that the B-nut is seated and tightened: Flareless Tubing Assembly
Installation, TASK 20-10-51-400-804.
(h) Use a lint-free cloth, G01043, to clean off the ends of the static lines of hydraulic fluid.
(i) From the open end of the static lines, carefully put a Texwipe TX762 swab, G50641
(Q-tip), approximately 1 in. (25 mm) or more into the static lines.
1) Wipe the inside surface in the static lines.
2) Remove the Texwipe TX762 swab, G50641 (Q-tip), and visually examine it for signs
of hydraulic fluid.
a) If the leakage rate exceeds 1 drop per hour, replace the elevator feel
computer: ELEVATOR FEEL COMPUTER - REMOVAL/INSTALLATION,
PAGEBLOCK 27-31-37/401.
SUBTASK 27-31-37-840-001
(2) Put the airplane back to its usual condition.

SUBTASK 27-31-41-020-001
CAUTION
DO NOT MIX THE ELEVATOR BALANCE PANELS. IF YOU MIX THE
ELEVATOR BALANCE PANELS, DAMAGE TO THE AIRCRAFT CAN OCCUR.
(1) Remove the balance panel [10] (bays 2, 3, and 4).

balance panel [10].
(b) Remove the washers [14] and bolts [13] that attach the balance panel [10] to the idler
hinge [18].
(c) Remove the washers [11] and bolts [12] that attach the balance panel [10] to the
elevator [6].
(d) Remove the washer [20] and bolt [21] that attach the balance panel [10] to the
elevator [6]

 ALL

(c) Remove the washers [4] and bolts [3] that attach the hinge half [2] to the balance panel

G. Elevator Balance Panel Installation
SUBTASK 27-31-41-860-002
(1) Make sure that the pressure from the elevator hydraulic system A and B is removed.
(a) If it is necessary, do this task: Remove Pressure from the Elevator Hydraulic Systems A
and B, TASK 27-31-00-800-802.
SUBTASK 27-31-41-420-001
(2) Install the idler hinge [18] (bays 2, 3, and 4).
(a) If you install new balance panel assemblies or seals, apply corrosion inhibiting
compound, G00009, as necessary (Figure 402).
NOTE: If you use the same parts that you removed, it is not necessary to apply corrosion
inhibiting compound, G00009.
(b) Position one loose end of the seal cloth [19] between the hinge half [2] and balance panel
support [1].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(c) Install the bolts [3] and washers [4] that attach the hinge half [2] to the balance panel
support [1].
(d) Tighten the bolt [3] to 23 in-lb (3 N·m) - 27 in-lb (3 N·m).
(e) Install the bolts [7] and washers [8] to attach the flat seals [5] to the idler hinge [18].
1) Do not tighten the bolts [7] until the clearance between the flat seals [5] and the
stabilizer trailing edge rib is adjusted.
(f) Make sure that the clearance between the flat seals [5] and the stabilizer trailing edge rib
is 0.01 +0.06 / -0.00 in. (0.25 +1.53 / -0.00 mm).
(g) Tighten the bolts [7] (TASK 20-50-11-910-801).
SUBTASK 27-31-41-420-002
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU INSTALL THE CORRECT BALANCE PANEL IN THE
CORRECT BAY. BALANCE PANELS IN BAYS 2, 3, AND 4 ARE NOT
INTERCHANGEABLE. IF YOU DO NOT FOLLOW THIS CAUTION, DAMAGE
TO THE AIRCRAFT CAN OCCUR.
(3) Install the balance panel [10].
(a) If you install new balance panel assemblies or seals, apply corrosion inhibiting
compound, G00009, as necessary (Figure 402).
NOTE: If you use the same parts that you removed, it is not necessary to apply corrosion
inhibiting compound, G00009.
(b) Put and hold the balance panel [10] in its position.
(c) Position one loose end of the seal cloth [24] between the balance panel [10] and
hinge [9].
(d) Install the bolt [21] and washer [20] to attach the balance panel [10] and hinge [9] to the
elevator [6].
(e) Install the bolts [12] and washers [11] to attach the balance panel [10] and hinge [9] to the
elevator [6].
1) Do not tighten the bolts [12] and bolt [21] until the gap between the balance
panel [10] and hinge [9] is adjusted.
2) Carefully install the seal cloth [24] between the hinge [9] and balance panel [10].
3) Make sure that the gap between the balance panel [10] and hinge [9] for the seal
cloth [24] does not allow either of the following conditions:
a) Pinching of the seal material
b) Movement of the seal inboard or outboard.
NOTE: The nominal design dimension for the gap between the balance panel
and hinge for the seal cloth that meets this condition is 0.05 ±0.02 in.
(1.3 ±0.5 mm).
(f) Tighten the bolts [12] to 68 in-lb (8 N·m) - 82 in-lb (9 N·m).
(g) Tighten the bolt [21] to 23 in-lb (3 N·m) - 27 in-lb (3 N·m).
(h) Make sure that the idler hinge [18] is turned down from the balance panel support [1].
(i) Position one loose end of the seal cloth [19] between the hinge half [23] and balance
panel [10].
(j) Install the bolts [13] and washers [14] to attach the balance panel [10] to the hinge
half [23].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Do not tighten the bolts [13] until the elevator has moved through the full range of
travel.
(k) Manually move the elevator through the full range of travel.
1) Make sure that the seal cloth [19] is not tight for all elevator positions.
(l) Tighten the bolts [13] to 23 in-lb (3 N·m) - 27 in-lb (3 N·m).
(m) Install the bulb seals [17].
1) Install the bolts [15], bolts [22], and washers [16] to attach the bulb seals [17] to the
balance panel [10].
a) Do not tighten the bolts [15] and bolts [22] until the clearance between the flat
seals [5] and stabilizer trailing edge rib is adjusted.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU ADJUST THE BULB SEALS CORRECTLY. IF
YOU DO NOT ADJUST THE BULB SEALS CORRECTLY, DAMAGE TO
THE TRAILING EDGE RIBS CAN OCCUR.
(n) Make sure that the clearance between the bulb seals [17] and stabilizer rib is
0.02 ±0.01 in. (0.51 ±0.26 mm).
(o) Tighten the bolts [15] and bolts [22] to 23 in-lb (3 N·m) - 27 in-lb (3 N·m).
SUBTASK 27-31-41-080-001

2. Elevator Balance Panel - Inspection
(Figure 601)
A. General
(1) This procedure gives wear limits and repair data for the elevator balance panel.
(2) This procedure also inspects the elevator balance panel for loose or missing attached
fasteners.
B. References
Reference Title
27-31-41-000-801 Elevator Balance Panel - Removal (P/B 401)
27-31-41-400-801 Elevator Balance Panel - Installation (P/B 401)
C. Tools/Equipment
Reference Description
STD-1096 Micrometer - Depth, 0-1 inch, Readable to 1/1000 inch
STD-1097 Caliper - Vernier, 0-6 inch, Readable to 1/1000 inch
D. Location Zones
Zone Area
334 Left Horizontal Stabilizer - Elevator
344 Right Horizontal Stabilizer - Elevator
E. Procedure
SUBTASK 27-31-41-020-005
(1) Remove the elevator balance panel. To remove it, do this task: Elevator Balance Panel -
Removal, TASK 27-31-41-000-801.
(a) Prior to removal, examine balance panels for missing or loose fasteners.
1) If any fastener is loose or missing, replace with a new fastener.
SUBTASK 27-31-41-020-006
(2) Use these tools to check for wear on the parts of the elevator balance panel connections:
(a) micrometer (0-1 inch, readable to 1/1000 inch), STD-1096
(b) vernier caliper (0 - 6 inch, readable to 1/1000 inch), STD-1097.
SUBTASK 27-31-41-020-007
(3) Examine the parts of the elevator balance panel connections for worn areas:
(a) Remove the parts to be checked.
(b) Measure the parts, as necessary, with a micrometer (0-1 inch, readable to 1/1000 inch),
STD-1096 or a vernier caliper (0 - 6 inch, readable to 1/1000 inch), STD-1097.
(c) Compare the dimensions you measured with the permitted wear dimensions that follow:

F. Control Column Removal
SUBTASK 27-31-51-020-001
(1) Disconnect the electrical wire [11] for the control column shaker [13] from the terminal strip in
the lower nose compartment.
SUBTASK 27-31-51-020-004
(2) Disconnect the electrical wire [5] to the control column [1] from the terminal strip in the lower
nose compartment.
SUBTASK 27-31-51-020-002
(3) Remove the ring assemblies and dust seals.
(a) Remove the screws [15] and washers [16] from the forward ring assembly [14] and aft
ring assembly [17].
(b) Remove the forward ring assembly [14] and aft ring assembly [17].
(c) Remove the aft dust seal [18] and forward dust seal [19].
SUBTASK 27-31-51-020-003
(4) Remove the control column [1].
CAUTION
HOLD THE CONTROL COLUMN WHEN YOU REMOVE THE COUPLINGS.
THE CONTROL COLUMN CAN FALL AND CAUSE DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(a) Hold the control column while you remove the nuts [7], washers [8], and bolts [12] from
the outboard couplings [9].
(b) Remove the outboard couplings [9].
(c) Lift and remove the control column [1] from the forward quadrant assembly.

F. Control Column Installation
SUBTASK 27-31-51-420-001
(1) Put the control column [1] in its position.
(a) Clean the spade [4] and clevis [6](SOPM 20-30-03).
(b) Apply MS-122XD release agent, G50063, or solid film lubricant, D00113, or lubricant,
D50108, to the spade [4] and clevis [6].
(c) Set the control wheel to the neutral position to engage the spade [4] with the clevis [6].
SUBTASK 27-31-51-480-002
(2) Use the protractor, COM-1691, to set the control column to 6.9 +/- 0.8 degrees forward of a
vertical line from the floor (Figure 401).
SUBTASK 27-31-51-420-002
(3) Install the control column [1].
(a) Engage the face splines on the control column [1] with the splines on the forward
quadrant connector [10].
(b) Install the outboard couplings [9].
1) Install the bolts [12], washers [8], and nuts [7] on the outboard couplings [9].
a) Make sure that you use the same bolts [12] at both ends of the outboard
couplings [9].
b) Tighten the nuts [7] to 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m) - 80 in-lb (9.0 N·m).
(c) Do one of these steps to check the clearance at each end of the outboard couplings [9]:
1) Make sure that the gaps of each end of the outboard couplings [9] are equal or less
than 0.03 in. (0.76 mm).
2) Make sure that thread protrusion of the bolts [12] at both ends of the outboard
couplings [9] is one thread.
(d) Make sure that the control column angle is 6.9 +/- 0.8 degrees forward of the vertical line
from the floor.
(e) Connect the electrical wire [5] and electrical wire [11] to the terminal strip in the lower
nose compartment.
1) Make sure that there is a 5.0 in. (12.7 cm) length of the electrical wire [11] between
the two clamps.
SUBTASK 27-31-51-420-003
(4) Install the ring assemblies and dust seals.
(a) Install the forward dust seal [19], aft dust seal [18], forward ring assembly [14], and aft
ring assembly [17] with the screws [15] and washers [16].
CAUTION
DO NOT HOLD THE DUST CAP TOO TIGHTLY AGAINST THE WIRE
BUNDLE. IT CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ELECTRICAL WIRES.
(b) If it is necessary, adjust the dust cap [3] to set the edge of the dust seals lightly up against
the dust cap [3].
1) Loosen the clamp [2] to adjust the dust cap [3].
(c) Make sure that the gap between the two dust seals is 0.060 inch (1.52 millimeters).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(d) Fill the hole between the notch in the dust seals and the cutout in the floor with sealant,
A00247.
SUBTASK 27-31-51-080-001
(5) Remove the rig pin E-1 from the left forward quadrant.
(a) Move the control column [1] full forward then full aft.
1) Make sure that the electrical wire [5] and electrical wire [11] are free of any
interference.
SUBTASK 27-31-51-410-001
(6) Close this access panel:
Number Name/Location
112A Forward Access Door
SUBTASK 27-31-51-410-002
(7) If removed, install the captain or first officer seat, do this task: Captain's and First Officer's Seat
Installation, TASK 25-11-01-400-801.

(1) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers:

Row Col Number Name

C 13 C01074 FLIGHT CONT SHUTOFF VALVES FLT CONT

SUBTASK 27-31-51-710-010
(2) Do this task: Put the Elevator Systems A and B Back to the Condition Before the Pressure
Removal, TASK 27-31-00-840-802.
SUBTASK 27-31-51-710-001
(3) Do a check of the control column.
(a) Move the control column full forward then full aft.
1) Make sure that the control column operates correctly and smoothly.
(b) Turn the control wheel through full travel.
1) Make sure that the control wheel operates correctly and smoothly.
SUBTASK 27-31-51-710-006
(4) Do this task: Control Column Travel and Centering - Test, TASK 27-31-00-700-808.
SUBTASK 27-31-51-710-007
(5) Do this task: Manual Mode - Test, TASK 27-31-00-700-807.
SUBTASK 27-31-51-710-008
(6) Do this task: Elevator Travel Limit - Test, TASK 27-31-00-700-804.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-31-51-860-005
(7) Do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811.
SUBTASK 27-31-51-710-003
(8) Do the operational test of the PTT switch in this task: Control Wheel PTT Switch Installation,
TASK 23-51-04-400-801.
SUBTASK 27-31-51-710-004
(9) Do a test of the stabilizer trim control switch on the control wheel.
(a) Move the STAB TRIM CUTOUT switch to the NORMAL position.
(b) Move the STAB TRIM switches to APL NOSE UP and then to APL NOSE DOWN.
1) Make sure that the stabilizer moves correctly.
SUBTASK 27-31-51-740-001
(10) Do a test of the autopilot disengage switch on the control wheel.
(a) Push the CMD A or CMD B autopilot engage switch on the mode control panel to engage
the autopilot.
1) Make sure that the CMD A or CMD B autopilot engage switch light comes on.
(b) Push the captain or first officer autopilot disengage switch on the control wheel to
disengage the autopilot.
1) Make sure that the A/P warning lights flash.
2) Make sure that the A/P disengage warning sound comes on.
3) Push the captain or first officer autopilot disengage switch again.
a) Make sure that the A/P warning lights go off.
b) Make sure that there is no A/P disengage warning sound.
SUBTASK 27-31-51-710-009
(11) Do a post-installation check of the shaker.
(a) Push and hold the STALL WARNING TEST NO. 1 switch (for the captain's shaker) or NO.
2 switch (for the first officer's shaker) on the P5 panel.
(b) Make sure that the applicable shaker operates.
(c) Release the switch.
(d) Make sure that the shaker stops.
SUBTASK 27-31-51-750-001
(12) Make sure that the wire bundle W443 has a minimum clearance of 0.5 in. (12.700 mm) from
left forward rudder quadrant full travel motion, while operating the rudder pedals (Figure 402).

E. Control Column Support Bearing Installation
SUBTASK 27-31-54-420-001
(1) Install the bearing [12] in the bearing housing [15]:
(a) Put the bearing [12] at the right angle of the bearing housing [15].
(b) Move the bearing [12] in the bearing housing [15] slots. Turn the bearing [12] to the
correct position.
SUBTASK 27-31-54-420-002
(2) Install the bearing housing [15]:
(a) Put the bearing housing [15] and the shim [8] against the structure.
(b) Install the upper bolts [10], washers [9], and nuts [7] that attach the bearing housing [15]
to the structure.
(c) Install the lower bolts [13], washers [14], washers [16], and nuts [17] on the bearing
housing [15].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-31-54-420-003
(3) Install the forward control quadrant assembly [2] to the support bearing:
(a) Install the forward control connector [11] in the bearing housing [15].
(b) Align the spines of the elevator forward control quadrant assembly [2] with the forward
quadrant connector [11].
(c) Install inboard couplings [6] with the bolts [3], washers [4], and nuts [5].
(d) Do these steps to make the clearances equal at each end of each inboard coupling [6]:
1) Tighten the bolts [3] to 50 pound-inches (5.7 newton-meters) of torque.
2) Tighten the bolt [3] and then the other to 50-70 pound-inches (5.7-7.9
newton-meters) in approximately 10 pound-inch (1.1 newton-meters) increments
until you get the clearances equal to +/- 0.03 inch (+/- 0.76 millimeter) of each other.
(e) Adjust the shim [8] below the bearing housing [15]:
1) Make sure the clearance between the forward quadrant connector [11] and inner
race of the bearing [12] is 0.01-0.03 inch (0.25-0.76 millimeter).
2) Make sure the clearance between lower chord of the floor beam and each side of
the forward control quadrant assembly [2] is 0.06 inch (1.5 millimeters) minimum
through the full travel.
3) If necessary, add or remove shims [8] under the bearing housing [15].
SUBTASK 27-31-54-480-004
(4) Remove the support set, SPL-1747 from the forward control quadrant assembly [2].
SUBTASK 27-31-54-420-004
(5) Install the applicable control column. To install it, do this task: Control Column - Installation,
TASK 27-31-51-400-801.
SUBTASK 27-31-54-080-001
(6) Remove the rig pin E-1 of rigging pin kit, SPL-1585 from the left forward quadrant.
SUBTASK 27-31-54-080-002
(7) Remove the rig pin E-5 of the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585 from the aft control quadrant.
SUBTASK 27-31-54-710-001
(8) Do a check of the control column:
(a) Move the control column full forward then full aft.
1) Make sure the control column operates correctly and smoothly.
SUBTASK 27-31-54-820-001

Cables EA and EB and Pitch Force Transducers - Adjustment, TASK 27-31-00-820-801.

SUBTASK 27-31-61-480-003
(1) Use the protractor, SPL-1680 to set the control column to 6.9 +/- 0.8 degrees forward of a

SUBTASK 27-31-61-420-002
(4) Install the forward quadrant assembly [1]:
(a) Set the control wheels to the neutral position.
(b) Put the forward quadrant assembly [1] it its position.
(c) Move the control columns inboard and at the same time align the spines of the elevator
forward control quadrant assembly [1] with the forward quadrant connectors [14].
(d) Install inboard couplings [16] with the bolts [13], washers [17], and nuts [18].
NOTE: Make sure that you use the correct bolts.
(e) Do these steps to make the clearances equal at each end of each inboard coupling:
1) Tighten the bolts [13] to 50 inch-pounds (5.7 newton-meters) of torque.
2) Tighten the bolt [13] and then the other to 50-70 pound-inches (5.7-7.9
newton-meters) in approximately 10 pound-inch (1.1 newton-meters) increments
until you get the clearances equal to +/- 0.03 inch (+/- 0.76 millimeter) of each other.
SUBTASK 27-31-61-820-001
(5) Adjust the shim below the bearing housings:
(a) Make sure the clearance between lower chord of the floor beam and each side of the
forward quadrant assembly [1] is 0.06 inch (1.5 millimeters) minimum through the full
travel.
(b) Make sure the total clearance (sum of the clearances of the two side of forward quadrant
assembly) between the bearing and forward quadrant connector is 0.01-0.02 inch
(0.25-0.51 millimeter).
(c) Make sure the total side play of the control column assembly is 0.01-0.03 inch (0.25-0.76
millimeter).
(d) Make sure the outboard end of the stop on the left side of the forward quadrant assembly
[1] is clear of the inboard face of the bracket by 0.07-0.24 inch (1.8-6.1 millimeters).
(e) If necessary, add or remove shim under the bearing housing.
SUBTASK 27-31-61-420-003

 ALL

F. Elevator Feel and Centering Spring Removal
SUBTASK 27-31-64-000-001
(1) Disconnect the output rod [8] from the crank [3].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Remove nut [7], washer [6], washer [5], and bolt [4] to disconnect the output rod [8] from
the crank [3], then swing the output rod [8] out of the way.
SUBTASK 27-31-64-000-002
(2) Remove the elevator feel actuator [10] from the elevator feel and centering unit [1].
NOTE: Do not disconnect the hydraulic lines from the elevator feel actuator.
(a) Remove the nut [27], washer [28], nut [29], washer [30], and bolt assembly [31] from the
aft connection of the elevator feel actuator [10].
(b) Remove the nut [17], washer [16], nut [15], washer [14], antirotation fitting [13],
spacer [12], and bolt assembly [11] from the elevator feel actuator [10].
(c) Remove the elevator feel actuator [10].
(d) Set the elevator feel actuator [10] carefully on a piece of soft fabric to prevent damage of
the elevator feel actuator [10] or adjacent components.
1) Do not strain the hydraulic lines.
SUBTASK 27-31-64-000-003
(3) Remove the elevator feel and centering cover [9] from the elevator feel and centering unit [1].
NOTE: Removal of the cover is done only to increase visibility of the springs and is not
mandatory for this procedure.
SUBTASK 27-31-64-000-004
(4) Remove the inner and outer springs.
(a) Remove the bolts [24] to loosen the retainer [37].
(b) Turn the spring post adjustment wrench flats [23] to loosen the springs.
(c) Remove the aft hook of the outer spring [32] from the spring post assembly [34].
1) Use a non-metallic tie-wrap and/or cord and/or plastic tie-strap to pull the spring in
the aft direction until the outer spring [32] hook is completely removed from the
eccentric groove of the of the spring post assembly [34].
NOTE: Use a protective thin plastic to prevent rubbing the housing surface with the
springs.
(d) Remove the aft hook of the inner spring [33] from the spring post assembly [34].
1) Use a non-metallic tie-wrap and/or cord and/or plastic tie-strap to pull the spring in
the aft direction until the inner spring [33] hook is completely removed from the
eccentric groove of the spring post assembly [34].
NOTE: Use a protective thin plastic to prevent rubbing the housing surface with the
springs.
(e) Remove the forward hooks of the outer spring [32] and inner spring [33] from the cam
follower assembly [35].

(Figure 201)

E. Elevator Feel and Centering Spring Installation
SUBTASK 27-31-64-400-002
(1) Replace the two inner and outer springs.
(a) Install the forward spring hooks on the cam follower assembly [35].
1) Make sure that the hooks are put in the eccentric groove correctly.
(b) Use the same tie-wrap from the removal task to install the aft hooks.
1) Install the inner spring [33] by pulling the inner spring coil aft and bending it slightly.
a) Make sure that it fits correctly in the eccentric groove.
2) Install the outer spring [32] by pulling the outer spring coil aft and bending it slightly.
a) Make sure that it fits properly in the eccentric groove.
NOTE: The aft hooks of the springs must point up.
b) Make sure that the forward hooks stay in the cam follower assembly [35].
(c) Do a detailed visual inspection of the elevator feel and centering unit springs to make
sure that the hooks are put in the eccentric groove correctly.
SUBTASK 27-31-64-400-004
(2) Do a breakout test of the crank [3].
(a) Use the same tie-wrap from the removal task to cycle the crank [3] a minimum of three
times.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Measure the force needed to move the end of the crank 0.025 ±0.005 in.
(0.635 ±0.127 mm) in the directions that follow:
2) Use the 0-100 lbs. (0.5 lbs. resolution) mechanical force gauge, COM-1452, to pull
down on a non-metallic strap attached to the crank and note the force when the dial
indicator, STD-11969, shows 0.025 in. (0.635 mm) or until the crank arm moves.
a) Force must measure 13.0 ±3.0 lbf (57.8 ±13.4 N).
3) Relax the tension on the strap and note the force when the crank starts to move
upward.
a) Force must measure 12.0 ±3.0 lbf (53.4 ±13.4 N).
4) Use the 0-100 lbs. (0.5 lbs. resolution) mechanical force gauge, COM-1452, to pull
up on the non-metallic strap and note the force when the dial indicator, STD-11969,
shows 0.025 in. (0.635 mm) or until the crank arm moves.
a) Force must measure 11.5 ±3.0 lbf (51.2 ±13.4 N).
5) Relax the tension on the strap and note the force when the crank starts to move
downward.
a) Force must measure 10.5 ±3.0 lbf (46.7 ±13.4 N).
(b) If the force values exceed these limits, loosen the retainer [37] and rotate the spring post
assembly [34] in elevator feel and centering housing [36] if necessary.
1) Repeat the breakout test until the force measures in the specified limits.
(c) Install the bolts [24] to tighten the retainer [37].
SUBTASK 27-31-64-400-005
(3) Install the elevator feel actuator [10].
(a) Put and hold the elevator feel actuator [10] in its position.
(b) Install the bolt assembly [31], washer [30], and nut [29] to attach the aft connection of the
elevator feel actuator [10] to the elevator feel and centering unit [1].
1) Tighten the nut [29] to 85 in-lb (9.6 N·m) - 100 in-lb (11.3 N·m).
(c) Install the washer [28] and nut [27].
CAUTION
DO NOT TIGHTEN THE NUT [29] AGAIN AFTER YOU TIGHTEN THE
NUT [27]. YOU CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT.
1) Tighten the nut [27] to 30 in-lb (3.4 N·m) - 35 in-lb (4.0 N·m).
(d) Install the bolt assembly [11], spacer [12], antirotation fitting [13], washer [14], and the
nut [15] to attach the forward connection of the elevator feel actuator [10] to the elevator
feel and centering unit [1].
1) Tighten the nut [15] to 85 in-lb (9.6 N·m) - 100 in-lb (11.3 N·m).
(e) Install the washer [16] and nut [17].
CAUTION
DO NOT TIGHTEN THE NUT [15] AGAIN AFTER YOU TIGHTEN THE
NUT [17]. YOU CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT.
1) Tighten the nut [17] to 30 in-lb (3.4 N·m) - 35 in-lb (4.0 N·m).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-31-64-400-006
(4) Install the elevator feel and centering cover [9] if removed.
SUBTASK 27-31-64-400-007
(5) Install the elevator feel and centering unit output rod [8].
CAUTION
DO NOT TIGHTEN THE HEAD OF THE BOLT [4] AGAIN AFTER YOU
TIGHTEN THE NUT [7]. YOU CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE
EQUIPMENT.
(a) Install the bolt [4], washer [5] (under bolt [4]), washer [6] (under nut [7]), and nut [7] to the
crank [3].
1) Tighten the bolt [4] to 75 in-lb (8.5 N·m) - 85 in-lb (9.6 N·m).
2) Tighten the nut [7] to 15 in-lb (1.7 N·m) - 20 in-lb (2.3 N·m).
SUBTASK 27-31-64-210-001
(6) Make sure that the unions [19], reducer [20], and union [21] are installed correctly and there
are no leaks from the lines.
SUBTASK 27-31-64-400-010
(7) Remove “DO-NOT-OPERATE” tags from the control columns.
SUBTASK 27-31-64-400-008
(8) Remove rig pin E-5 of the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, from the rig pin E-5 hole [2].
SUBTASK 27-31-64-400-009
(9) Check the control column power force (TASK 27-31-00-700-809).

F. Elevator Feel Actuator Removal
SUBTASK 27-31-67-020-001
WARNING
RELEASE THE CONNECTION SLOWLY AND LET THE PRESSURE
DECREASE BEFORE YOU COMPLETELY REMOVE THE HYDRAULIC LINE.
IF YOU DISCONNECT THE HYDRAULIC LINE WHEN IT HAS PRESSURE, A
SPRAY OF HYDRAULIC FLUID CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS.
(1) Disconnect the hydraulic line [2], hydraulic line [25], hydraulic line [26], and hydraulic line [27]
from the elevator feel actuator [3] (Figure 401).
(a) Remove the unions [12], reducer [13], and union [14].
(b) Discard the packings [11] and packings [15].
(c) Install the caps and plugs on the open ports and hydraulic line [2], hydraulic line [25],
hydraulic line [26], and hydraulic line [27].
SUBTASK 27-31-67-020-002
(2) Remove the elevator feel actuator [3] from the elevator feel and centering unit [1]:
(a) Remove the nut [20], washer [21], nut [22], washer [23], and bolt assembly [24] from the
aft connection of the elevator feel actuator [3].
(b) Remove the nut [17], washer [18], bushing [19], and slide block [16] from the anti-rotation
fitting [6].
(c) Remove the nut [10], washer [9], nut [8], washer [7], spacer [5], anti-rotation fitting [6],

attach the forward connection of the elevator feel actuator [3] to the elevator feel and

(b) Connect the hydraulic line [2], hydraulic line [25], hydraulic line [26], and hydraulic

(c) Tighten the B-nuts on the hydraulic line [2] and hydraulic line [27] to 140 ±7 in-lb

WARNING

(a) Move the horizontal stabilizer to the maximum leading edge up (APL NOSE DOWN)
position (the mechanical limits).
NOTE: The horizontal stabilizer can be moved with the control wheel STAB TRIM

1) Make sure that the ballnut is against the jackscrew upstop.

MAKE SURE THAT THE PITOT PROBE HAS NO ADDED WEIGHT ON IT

(c) Connect the regulator, SPL-1742, or equivalent air data model test set, COM-1914, to the
two pitot probes on the vertical fin.
1) Do this step for the regulator, SPL-1742:
a) Connect the pressure lines from the regulator, SPL-1742, with the pitot test

2) Do this step for the air data model test set, COM-1914:

COM-1916.
(d) Use the regulator, SPL-1742, or air data model test set, COM-1914, to raise the airspeed
to 2.46 psig (300 knots).
1) Make sure that the rate is 2.46 psig (300 knots) or less for each minute.
WARNING
KEEP PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE FLIGHT
CONTROL SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING
GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU
SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO
PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(e) Pressurize the Hydraulic Systems A and B, do one of these steps:
1) If you will use a Portable Hydraulic Cart, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B
Pressurization with a Portable Hydraulic Cart, TASK 29-11-00-860-802.
NOTE: Two carts are recommended.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
a) If only one cart is available, bleed hydraulic system A and B, as follows:
<1> Pressurize the hydraulic system A with a cart and hydraulic systems B
with the Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP).
<2> Pressurize the hydraulic system B with a cart and hydraulic systems A
with the EMDP.
2) If you will not use a Portable Hydraulic Cart, do these tasks:
NOTE: Both the Engine Driven Pump (EDP) and EMDP should be operated at the
same time.
• Hydraulic System Pressurization with an Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP),
TASK 29-11-00-860-803
• Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization with an Engine-Driven Pump (EDP),
TASK 29-11-00-860-804.
(f) Do these steps to cycle the power between Hydraulic Systems A and B:
1) Set the flight controls hydraulic power switches as follows:
a) Set the FLT CONTROL B switch to the OFF position.
b) Set the FLT CONTROL A switch to the A ON position.
c) Wait for 2 seconds.
d) Set the FLT CONTROL A switch to the OFF position.
e) Set the FLT CONTROL B switch to the B ON position.
f) Wait for 2 seconds.
2) Repeat the cycle 10 times.
(g) Slowly, do column sweeps with pitot pressure applied.
(h) Do these steps to cycle pitot pressure:
• Use the regulator, SPL-1742, or air data model test set, COM-1914, connected at the
elevator pitot probes on the vertical stabilizer, to lower the airspeed to 0 psig (0 knots).
• Use the regulator, SPL-1742, or air data model test set, COM-1914, connected at the
elevator pitot probes on the vertical stabilizer, to increase the airspeed to 2.46 psig (300
knots).
• Use the regulator, SPL-1742, or air data model test set, COM-1914, connected at the
elevator pitot probes on the vertical stabilizer, to lower the airspeed to 0 psig (0 knots).

2. Elevator Feel Actuator - Differential Pressure Test
Figure 501
A. General
(1) This task gives instructions on how to diagnose an Elevator Feel System differential pressure
issue, and how to use the elevator feel computer test box, SPL-23206.
(2) This Predictive Maintenance & Enhanced Troubleshooting (PMET) procedure is optional and
the results are for analysis only. It is not necessary to do more steps as a result of this
procedure if there is no flight deck effect or no faults. The recommendations show 's
best practices to make sure that the aircraft can get maximum reliability. If there is a flight deck
effect or other faults, use accepted procedures to correct them.

G. Elevator Feel System Troubleshooting
SUBTASK 27-31-67-480-003
(1) Place the test box in the aft galley and connect the power plug.
SUBTASK 27-31-67-480-002
(2) Install Elevator Pitot System test equipment:
(a) Install the pitot adaptors on each of the elevator pitot probes.
(b) Using the Y hose, connect a hose to each pitot adaptor.
(c) Install the remaining end of the Y hose to the REGULATED AIR connection on the test
box.
SUBTASK 27-31-67-480-004
(3) Install the pressure return hose:
(a) Install one return line on the system A visco drain.
(b) Install one return line on the system B visco drain.
(c) Install the system A return line onto the PITOT A connection on the test box.
(d) Install the system B return line onto the PITOT B connection on the test box.
SUBTASK 27-31-67-410-002
(4) Install the pressure transducers:
(a) Access the DUAL FEEL ACTUATOR in the tail cone compartment.
(b) Remove the SYSTEM B METERED PRESSURE line from the DUAL FEEL ACTUATOR.
(c) Install a cap on the DUAL FEEL ACTUATOR where the SYSTEM B METERED
PRESSURE line was removed.
(d) Install one of the pressure transducers from the kit on the SYSTEM B METERED
PRESSURE line.
(e) Remove the SYSTEM A METERED PRESSURE line from the DUAL FEEL ACTUATOR.
(f) Install a cap on the DUAL FEEL ACTUATOR where the SYSTEM A METERED
PRESSURE line was removed.
(g) Install the remaining pressure transducer from the kit on the SYSTEM A METERED
PRESSURE line.
(h) Connect a wire harness to each of the pressure transducers.
(i) Connect the SYSTEM A METERED PRESSURE transducer wire harness to the
TRANSMITTER A port on the test box.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(j) Connect the SYSTEM B METERED PRESSURE transducer wire harness to the
TRANSMITTER B port on the test box.
SUBTASK 27-31-67-700-001
(5) Test Procedure:
(a) Do this task: Hydraulic System Pressurization with an Electric Motor-Driven Pump
(EMDP), TASK 29-11-00-860-803or Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization with an
Engine-Driven Pump (EDP), TASK 29-11-00-860-804
(b) Loosen the PRESSURE REGULATOR knob until it can spin freely.
(c) Push the SHUT OFF VALVE knob in.
(d) Turn on the test box with the POWER SUPPLY switch.
(e) Turn on the pitot pump with the PUMP switch.
(f) Monitor the PITOT PRESSURE A and B gages.
(g) Slowly tighten the PRESSURE REGULATOR knob until the PITOT PRESSURE gages
read 2.5 psig (2.5 psi).
NOTE: The pitot pressure gauges will increase in pressure at an identical rate. If either
gauge (A or B) lags behind, that is an indication of a restriction or blockage in that
pitot system.
(h) Observe the TRANSMITTER A and B HYDRAULIC PRESSURE gage.
1) Both values need to be within 20% of each other.
NOTE: If one of the transmitter pressures (A or B) is lower by at least 20%, that is
the system that has a restriction or blockage.
(i) Loosen the PRESSURE REGULATOR knob until the gauges read
0.09 +0.07 / --0.00 psig (0.09 +0.07 / --0.00 psi), and let the pressure stabilize.
(j) Pull the SHUTOFF VALVE knob.
(k) Make sure that the PITOT pressure does not decrease more than 0.2 psig (0.2 psi)
during a 2-minute time.
NOTE: If the pressure in either pitot gage A or B decreases more than the limit in that
time period, that system has a leak.
H. Return the Aircraft to its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 27-31-67-700-002
(1) Release the pressure in the pitot system
(a) Push in the SHUTOFF Valve knob.
(b) Loosen the PRESSURE REGULATOR knob until it can spin freely.
(c) Once the pitot pressure gauges read 0 psig (0 psi), turn off the PUMP switch.
NOTE: The pitot equipment should not be removed at this time.
SUBTASK 27-31-67-020-004
(2) Remove the pressure transducers.
(a) Do this task: Remove Pressure from the Elevator Hydraulic Systems A and B,
TASK 27-31-00-800-802
(b) Remove the pressure transducers from the SYSTEM B METERED PRESSURE line and
the SYSTEM A METERED PRESSURE line.
(c) Remove the caps from the DUAL FEEL ACTUATOR.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(d) Install the SYSTEM B METERED PRESSURE line and the SYSTEM A METERED
PRESSURE line on to the corresponding ports of the DUAL FEEL ACTUATOR.
SUBTASK 27-31-67-410-003
(3) Bleed the Elevator Control System
(a) Bleed the elevator control system per task: Elevator Feel Actuator Installation,
TASK 27-31-67-400-801
SUBTASK 27-31-67-020-005
(4) Remove the Pitot Static Equipment
(a) Remove the pitot adaptors from each of the elevator pitot probes.
(b) Disconnect the Y hose from the pressure adaptors.
(c) Remove the pressure return hoses from the visco drains.
SUBTASK 27-31-67-410-004

SUBTASK 27-31-71-020-002
(1) Remove the cables EAL, EBL, EAR, and EBR from the quadrants [5] (Figure 401, Figure 402):
(a) Install the clamps on the cables so the cables will not go through the aft pressure
bulkhead.
(b) Remove the turnbuckles locking clips.
(c) Loosen the turnbuckles for the elevator cables EAL, EBL, EAR, and EBR (Figure 401).
(d) Remove the nuts [4], washers [3], bolts [1], and cable retainers [2] from the quadrants [5]

sensor rod [13] from the torque tube [18] (Figure 402) (View B).

actuator rod [19] from the input crank [30] (Figure 402) (View C).

guide to drill out the lockbolts [32] and collars [33] from the center bearing retainer [31]
(Figure 402) (View D).
1) Make sure that the holes are not out of tolerance.

CAUTION
YOU MUST BE CAREFUL WITH THE ELEVATOR AFTER YOU REMOVE THE
TORQUE TUBES. IT IS POSSIBLE THAT THE ELEVATOR CAN HIT THE
HORIZONTAL STABILIZER TRAILING EDGE LOWER BEAM AND ELEVATOR
MAST ARM FITTING. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT
CAN OCCUR.
SUBTASK 27-31-74-020-003
(1) Remove the mounting bracket [31] of the elevator autopilot actuators:
(a) Remove the bolts [27] and washers [28] from the mounting bracket [31].
(b) Remove the bolts [29] and washers [30] from the mounting bracket [31].
(c) Remove the nuts [35], washers [34], washers [33], and bolts [32] from the mounting
bracket [31].
(d) Remove the nuts [39], washers [38], washers [37], and bolts [36]from the mounting
bracket [31].
(e) Remove the mounting bracket [31]from the airplane.
SUBTASK 27-31-74-480-001
(2) Install the rig pin E-5 from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585 in the elevator aft control quadrant.
SUBTASK 27-31-74-020-004
(3) Remove the torque tube assembly [1]:
(a) Remove nut [25], washer [24], nut [23], washers [22], and bolt [26] to disconnect the
elevator contol pushrods [4] from the torque tube assembly [1].
(b) Remove the nuts [9], washers [8], washers [7], and bolts [6] to disconnect the elevator
PCUs [5] from the torque tube assembly [1].
(c) Move the elevator PCUs [5] away from the aft bulkhead until the input cranks are in the
bottom.
(d) At each end of the torque tube assembly [1], remove the nut [20], washer [21], nut [15],
washer [14], bolt [11], bushing [12], and bushing [13] to disconnect the torque tube
assembly [1] from the inboard pivot brackets [2] and the reaction links [10].
(e) At each end of the torque tube assembly [1], remove nut [17], washer [18], washer [19],
and bolt [16] to disconnect the torque tube assembly [1] from the outboard pivot
brackets [3].
(f) Remove the torque tube assembly [1] from the airplane.

SUBTASK 27-31-74-420-001
(1) Install the torque tube [1]:
(a) Make sure the outboard pivot bearing is installed on the tube assembly [1].
1) If the outboard pivot bearing is not installed, use P/S 870 Class B-1/2 sealant,
A50250 for installation on the tube assembly [1].
(b) Put the torque tube assembly [1] in its position.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(c) Install the alignment pins to keep the bearing components in the inboard pivot clevis
fittings of the torque tube assembly [1].
(d) Lubricate the bushings, bolts, and bearings with grease, D00013.
(e) Connect the torque tube assembly [1] to the two outboard pivot brackets [3]:
1) At each of the torque tube assembly [1], install the bolts [16] with the bolt head
inboard, washers [19], washers [18], and nuts [17].
a) Tighten the nuts [17] 470 in-lb (53.10 N·m) to 790 in-lb (89.26 N·m).
CAUTION
BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU INSTALL THE BOLTS [11]. YOU CAN CAUSE
DAMAGE TO THE BEARING COMPONENTS IF YOU HIT THE BOLTS [11]
DURING THE INSTALLATION.
(f) Connect the torque tube assembly [1] to the two inboard pivot brackets [2] and two
reaction links [10]:
1) At each end of the torque tube assembly [1], install the bushing [12] (on the right
side only), bushings [13], bolts [11], washers [14], and nuts [15].
a) Tighten the nuts [15] to 500-600 pound-inches (56.5-67.8 newton-meters).
CAUTION
DO NOT TIGHTEN THE NUT [15] AGAIN AFTER YOU TIGHTEN THE
NUT [20], YOU CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
2) Install the washers [21] and nuts [20].
a) Tighten the nuts [20] to 150-220 pound-inches (16.9-24.9 newton-meters).

F. Neutral Shift Mechanism Removal
(Figure 401)
SUBTASK 27-31-91-020-001
(1) Remove the neutral shift mechanism [1]:
(a) Remove the nut [8], washer [9], nut [10], washers [7], and bolt [6] to disconnect the
neutral shift mechanism [1] from the mach trim actuator.
(b) Remove the nuts [28], washers [26], washers [24], and bolts [25] to disconnect control
rods [23] and control rods [27] from the neutral shift mechanism [1].
(c) Remove the nuts [4], washers [3], and bolts [2] that attach the neutral shift mechanism [1]
to the support brackets.
(d) Remove the nuts [13], washers [12], and bolts [11] that attach the neutral shift
mechanism [1] to the support brackets.
(e) Remove the neutral shift mechanism [1] and spacers [17] from the airplane.
NOTE: Note the quantity, orientation, and location of the spacers [17] before you remove
them from the neutral shift mechanism [1].

F. Neutral Shift Mechanism Installation
(Figure 401)
SUBTASK 27-31-91-640-001
(1) Do these steps to replace the bearings of the neutral shift mechanism [1]:
(a) Remove the outer housing bearing [15] from the short end of the neutral shift mechanism
[1].
(b) Remove the bearing [16] from the short end of the neutral shift mechanism [1].
(c) Remove the outer housing bearing [14] from the long end of the neutral shift mechanism
[1].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(d) Remove the nut [21], washer [20], washer [19], and bolt [18] from the long end of the
neutral shift mechanism [1].
(e) Remove the bearing retainer [22] and bearing [16] from the neutral shift mechanism [1].
(f) Apply sealant, A00247 between each new bearing, their bearing housings and bearing
retainer.
(g) Install the bearings [16], bearing housing [14], bearing housing [15], and bearing retainer
[22] back on the neutral shift mechanism [1].
(h) Turn the bearing retainer [22] until you can install the bolt [18], washer [19] (under the bolt
head), washer [20] (under the nut), and the nut [21].
SUBTASK 27-31-91-420-001
(2) Install the neutral shift mechanism [1]:
(a) Put the neutral shift mechanism [1] between the support brackets.
1) Align the neutral shift mechanism [1] with the mach trim actuator.
2) Install the spacers [17] between the neutral shift mechanism [1] and support
brackets.
a) Add or remove spacers [17], if necessary.
(b) Install the bolts [2], washers [3] (under the nuts), and nuts [4] to attach the left side of the
neutral shift mechanism [1] to the left support bracket.
(c) Install the bolts [11], washers [12] (under the nuts), and nuts [13] to attach the right side
of the neutral shift mechanism [1] to the right support bracket.
WARNING
MAKE SURE YOU TURN THE CRANK OF THE NEUTRAL SHIFT
MECHANISM IN THE UP DIRECTION. IF YOU INSTALL THE CRANK
INCORRECTLY, THE STABILIZER CAN MOVE QUICKLY WHEN YOU
ENGAGE THE AUTOPILOT. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS
AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(d) Make sure the crank of the neutral shift mechanism [1] is in the up direction and
connected to the mach trim actuator.
1) Install the bolt [6] from the left to the right side (bolt head on the left side).
2) Install the washers [7] (under the nut) and nut [8].
a) Tighten the nut [8] to 85-100 pound-inches (9.6-11.3 newton-meters).
CAUTION
DO NOT TIGHTEN THE NUT [10] AGAIN AFTER YOU TIGHTEN THE
NUT [8]. YOU CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE BOLT ASSEMBLY.
3) Install the washer [9] and nut [10].
a) Tighten the nut [10] to 30-35 pound-inches (3.4-3.9 newton-meters).
(e) Connect the controls rods [27] and control rods [23] to the neutral shift mechanism [1].
1) Install the bolts [25], washers [24], washers [26], and nuts [28].
SUBTASK 27-31-91-080-001
(3) Remove the rig pin E-5 of the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585 from the aft control quadrant.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

27-32-00-710-801Stall Warning System - Operational TestPDF p. 1553
2. Stall Warning System - Operational Test
(Figure 501)
NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. Location Zones
Zone Area
212 Flight Compartment - Right
B. Stall Warning System Test
SUBTASK 27-32-00-710-001
(1) Do a test of the number 1 stall warning system.
NOTE: The amber SPD LIM flag on the on-side Primary Flight Display will be displayed
momentarily during the test.
NOTE: If hydraulic power is off, the leading edge flaps can droop enough to cause a leading
edge asymmetry signal, this can cause a failure of the stall warning system test.
NOTE: The YAW DAMPER light may momentarily flash for older Stall Management Yaw
Damper (SMYD) (prior to 285A1010-7/-107). This condition can be considered a
nuisance and not a failure of the SMYD.
(a) Push and hold the STALL WARNING TEST NO. 1 switch, on the P5-18 stall warning test
module.
(b) Make sure that the captain's control column shaker operates for more than 5 seconds.
(c) Release the switch.
(d) Make sure that the shaker stops.
SUBTASK 27-32-00-710-002
(2) Do a test of the number 2 stall warning system.
NOTE: The amber SPD LIM flag on the on-side Primary Flight Display will be displayed
momentarily during the test.
NOTE: SPEED BRAKE DO NOT ARM light may momentarily turn on and off for SMYD
285A1010-112 and earlier.
NOTE: If hydraulic power is off, the leading edge flaps can droop enough to cause a leading
edge asymmetry signal, this can cause a failure of the stall warning system test.
(a) Push and hold the STALL WARNING TEST NO. 2 switch, on the P5-18 stall warning test
module.
(b) Make sure that the first officer's control column shaker operates for more than 5 seconds.
(c) Release the switch.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(d) Make sure that the shaker stops.
27-32-00-740-801Stall Management Yaw Damper (SMYD) BITE Test - Existing FaultsPDF p. 1556
3. Stall Management Yaw Damper (SMYD) BITE Test - Existing Faults
(Figure 502)
A. General
(1) This procedure does the EXISTING FAULTS portion of the Stall Management Yaw Damper
(SMYD) BITE.
(2) This procedure does and exchange of SMYD 1 and 2 if a maintenance message is present,
and NO FAULT is found.
(3) Do this BITE test for SMYD 1 and 2 to ensure all faults are found.
(4) For EXISTING FAULTS, the SMYD does internal tests, discrete output checks, sensor
interface checks, and checks of inputs to the SMYD. Any faults that are found during the
EXISTING FAULTS are active. A maintenance message identifies a specific failure which is
found by the SMYD.

SUBTASK 27-32-00-740-001

(b) Push the YES switch. The display will show:

2) Or the display will show NO FAULTS.
(c) If there are existing faults, then, do this task: FIM 27-32 TASK 801.
(d) If the display shows NO FAULTS, push the MENU switch to return to the EXISTING
FAULTS? display.
(e) If a maintenance message is present and the SMYD shows NO FAULTS:
1) Do an exchange check of the SMYD 1 and 2 to determine if a SMYD is damaged,
FIM 27-32 TASK 801.

27-32-00-740-802Stall Management Yaw Damper (SMYD) BITE Test - Fault HistoryPDF p. 1560
4. Stall Management Yaw Damper (SMYD) BITE Test - Fault History
(Figure 502)
A. General
(1) This procedure does the FAULT HISTORY? portion of the Stall Management Yaw Damper
(SMYD) BITE.
(2) The SMYD keeps a record of faults in FAULT HISTORY. The faults are grouped by flight leg.
Flight leg 0 (LEG 0) is the most recent flight and includes faults that occurred on the ground
after the most recent flight. Only flight legs with faults will be displayed.

24-22-00-860-814 Remove External Power (P/B 201)

117A Electronic Equipment Access Door

SUBTASK 27-32-00-010-002
(2) Open this access panel:
Number Name/Location
117A Electronic Equipment Access Door
F. Procedure
SUBTASK 27-32-00-740-002
(1) Do the FAULT HISTORY test on the SMYD BITE.
(a) Push the ON/OFF switch on the SMYD BITE display to turn the BITE display on.
NOTE: EXISTING FAULTS? will be displayed.
(b) Push the down arrow until the display shows FAULT HISTORY?.
1) Push the YES switch.
a) If there are faults in history, The display will show FLIGHT LEG -n where n is
the most recent flight with faults recorded.
b) If there are no faults, the message NO FAULT HISTORY will be displayed.
2) Push the up arrow or down arrow to go through the flight legs.
3) If you push YES at any flight leg display the message corresponding to the first fault
in the list will be displayed.
4) To display the faults for the flight leg use the up arrow and down arrow.
NOTE: To return to the FLIGHT LEG N display, push the MENU switch.
5) To return to the FAULT HISTORY display, push the MENU switch.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
6) Refer to FIM 27-32 TASK 801 to find the fault isolation task for the applicable
maintenance message.
G. If you are finished with the SMYD tests, return the airplane to normal.

27-32-00-740-803Stall Management Yaw Damper (SMYD) BITE TestPDF p. 1561
5. Stall Management Yaw Damper (SMYD) BITE Test
(Figure 502)
NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. General
(1) This procedure does the GROUND TEST? portion of the Stall Management Yaw Damper
(SMYD) BITE.
(2) For GROUND TEST, the SMYD has several menus:
(a) SELF TEST? - This performs a self test sequence of the SMYD.
(b) DISCRETE INPUTS? - Monitors the status of each displayed discrete inputs to the
SMYD.
(c) ARINC429 INPUTS? - Monitors the status of each ARINC429 input to the SMYD.
(d) ANALOG INPUTS? - Displays the status of these sensors:
1) AOA SENSOR?
2) FLAP SENSOR?
3) WHEEL SENSOR?
4) YD LVDT?
NOTE: This is only for the SMYD in the number 2 position.
(e) SERVO TEST? - Tests the integrity of the interface between the SMYD and the rudder
power control unit.
(f) DISPLAY TEST? Tests the SMYD display.
(3) This task has a procedure for each of these menu items.
(4) This task also contains the Input Signal Integrity Test procedure from the OTHER FUNCTION?
menu.

J. ARINC429 Test
SUBTASK 27-32-00-740-010
(1) Push the down arrow to display ARINC429 INPUTS?
SUBTASK 27-32-00-740-011
(2) Push the YES switch to start the ARINC429 test.
(a) The first input bus will be displayed: ON SIDE IR BUS?
(b) To display the other input busses, push the down arrow until the desired bus is displayed.
(c) A good data bus will display "BUS ACTIVE" and a bad bus will display "BUS INACTIVE".
(d) The busses are:
1) ON SIDE IR BUS
2) OFF SIDE IR BUS
3) ON SIDE ADR BUS
4) CDS DEU BUS
5) FMC BUS
6) DFCS MCP BUS
7) CROSS CHANNEL.
(e) Push YES at any display to activate the test for the bus.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(f) If there is no fault in the bus activity monitor, BUS ACTIVE will be displayed.
(g) If there are faults, BUS INACTIVE will be displayed.
NOTE: For some combinations of SMYD and FMC part numbers a nuisance BUS
INACTIVE fault message may occur for the FMC bus. If that occurs, push the up
arrow until EXISTING FAULTS?
(h) Use the MENU key to return to the ARINC429 TEST? display.
K. Sensor Test
SUBTASK 27-32-00-740-012
(1) Push the down arrow to display ANALOG INPUTS?
SUBTASK 27-32-00-740-013
(2) Push the YES switch to start the analog inputs test.
(a) The SMYD will display the status of these sensors:
1) AOA SENSOR
2) FLAP SENSOR
3) YD LVDT
4) WHEEL SENSOR.
NOTE: The WHEEL SENSOR is only on the SMYD installed in the number 2
position. The SMYD in position 1 will not have this sensor. If the sensor
value is bad, "WHEEL INVALID" will appear.
(b) To move through the sensors, push the up and down arrow until the desired sensor is
displayed.
(c) When the sensor is displayed, push the YES switch to show the status of that sensor.
The possible displays are:
1) AOA (sensor angle) or AOA INVALID.
a) When you check the AOA sensor status, move the sensor to different
positions.
NOTE: It is possible that the AOA sensor may be in a dead band position.
This will incorrectly cause an AOA INVALID status on the SMYD
display. This is why it is necessary to move the sensor to different
angle positions.
b) Make sure that SMYD display matches the different angle positions of the
AOA sensor.
2) FLAP DET (flap detent position), FLAP SYN (flap synchro angle), or FLAP INVALID.
NOTE: Use the down arrow to move from the FLAP DET nn display to the FLAP
SYN nn display.
3) YD LVDT (angle) or YD LVDT INVALID.
4) WHEEL (angle) or WHEEL INVALID.
NOTE: WHEEL and WHEEL INVALID is only on the SMYD installed in the number
2 position.
(d) Push the MENU key to return to the ANALOG INPUTS? display.
L. Servo Test
NOTE: The SERVO TEST can be run from SMYD 1 and SMYD 2. Do the steps below for either
SMYD.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-32-00-860-014
(1) Supply hydraulic power, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization,
TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
SUBTASK 27-32-00-740-014
(2) Push the down arrow switch until SERVO TEST? is displayed.
SUBTASK 27-32-00-740-015
(3) Push the YES switch to start the servo test.
(a) A series of warning messages will be displayed on the SMYD prior to the activation of
rudder commands. Be aware of what will happen next during the test.
(b) There are two subtests in the SERVO TEST selection. They are:
1) ZERO COMMAND?
2) SWEEP TEST?
(c) Use the up arrow and down arrow to display the test.
WARNING
KEEP PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE RUDDER. THE
RUDDER CAN MOVE WHEN YOU DO THIS TEST, INJURY TO
PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(d) Push the YES switch to start the displayed test.
(e) The ZERO COMMAND test does the following:
NOTE: There will be a delay between the displays. The delay can be up to 10 seconds.
1) RUDDER MOVING is displayed.
2) YD CMD (value) is displayed.
3) LVDT (value) is displayed.
4) END ZERO COMMAND? is displayed.
5) Push the YES switch to end the ZERO COMMAND test. The following will be
displayed:
a) RUDDER MOVING
b) TEST EXITING
c) ZERO COMMAND?
(f) Push the down arrow to continue the test, the following displays will show:
1) SWEEP TEST?
(g) Push the YES switch to end the servo test.
(h) The SWEEP TEST? displays the following when it is run:
1) RUD CMD LEFT
2) LVDT (value)
3) RUD CMD RIGHT
4) LVDT (value)
5) RUD CMD ZERO
6) LVDT (value).
(i) If the test passes:
1) TEST PASSED is displayed.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
2) Remove hydraulic power, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal,
TASK 29-11-00-860-805.
(j) If the test failed, TEST FAILED is displayed followed by a message for the first fault.
1) To isolate the fault, do this task: FIM 27-32 TASK 801.
(k) Use the MENU switch to return to the SERVO TEST? display.
M. Display Test
SUBTASK 27-32-00-740-085
(1) Push the ON/OFF switch to turn on the BITE display.
SUBTASK 27-32-00-740-086
(2) Push the down arrow until GROUND TESTS? shows on the display.
SUBTASK 27-32-00-740-087
(3) Push the YES button to select GROUND TESTS? on the SMYD.
SUBTASK 27-32-00-740-088
(4) Push the down arrow until DISPLAY TEST? shows on the display.
SUBTASK 27-32-00-740-089
(5) Push the YES button to select DISPLAY TEST? on the SMYD.
SUBTASK 27-32-00-740-090
(6) It is necessary to watch the SMYD display during this test.
SUBTASK 27-32-00-740-091
(7) Make sure that all pixels on the display come on during the test.
N. Input Signal Integrity Test
SUBTASK 27-32-00-740-016
(1) Push the MENU switch to display GROUND TESTS?
(a) Push the down arrow to display OTHER FUNCTNS?
(b) Push the YES switch.
(c) Push the down arrow to display I/O MONITOR?
(d) Push the YES switch to display ARINC429 INPUTS?
(e) Push the YES switch.
(f) Push the down arrow until CDS DEU BUS? is displayed.
(g) Push the YES switch to display WORD 017?
NOTE: Skip the next three steps if WORD 017? does not display.
(h) Push the YES switch.
(i) Verify the SMYD BITE readout values:
1) Between -39 and -29 when the speedbrake lever is in the FLIGHT DETENT
position.
2) Between -3 and +3 when the speedbrake lever is in the DOWN position.
3) If 'DATA INVALID' is shown, the speedbrake handle position sensor needs
adjustment, do this task: Speed Brake Lever Position Sensor Adjustment,
TASK 27-62-37-400-803.
a) Repeat the Input Signal Integrity Test.
(j) Push the MENU switch.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(k) Push the down arrow until WORD 352? is displayed.
(l) Push the YES switch until BIT 27 is displayed.
(m) Verify the SMYD BITE readout values:
1) 1, when the WING ANTI-ICE switch on the P5 Fwd Overhead panel is ON.
2) 0, when the WING ANTI-ICE switch on the P5 Fwd Overhead panel is OFF.
O. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 27-32-00-860-010
(1) Push the ON/OFF switch to turn the SMYD BITE display off.
SUBTASK 27-32-00-410-003
(2) Close this access panel:
Number Name/Location
117A Electronic Equipment Access Door

27-41-00-820-801Stabilizer Control Cable and Chain - AdjustmentPDF p. 1603
2. Stabilizer Control Cable and Chain - Adjustment
(Figure 501 and Figure 502)
A. General
(1) Use this task to adjust the horizontal stabilizer control cables and chain.
(2) Before the cable adjustment is done, permit a minimum of one hour at a constant ambient
temperature of ±5°F (±2.8°C) for the airframe temperature to become stable.
(a) The cable tension values will not be correct when there are temperature differences along
the cable run.
(3) If the cables need to be replaced, do this task: Stabilizer Control Cable - Removal,
TASK 27-41-82-000-801.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(4) It is recommended that airplanes supplied with the cables that contain higher zinc coating
(Grade D or Grade K) be re-tensioned 3 to 4 months into service. This will bring the tension of
the control cables within the desired range. After the cables are re-tensioned the high zinc
cables (Grade D or Grade K) will continue to relax at a rate that is equivalent to the Grade B
cables. To identify the grade of the cables, refer to the table below:

H. Stabilizer Control Cable and Chain Adjustment
SUBTASK 27-41-00-710-001
(1) Adjust the tension of the cable STA and cable STB:
NOTE: It is necessary to use the control wheel switches to move the stabilizer, since the stab
trim control wheel chain has been disconnected.
NOTE: If it is necessary, the pinion gear wrench, SPL-10319, can be used to operate the
stabilizer system. This method can only be used when it is not possible to use the
method specified in the note above. This method is highly impractical.
(a) If the new cables is installed, do these steps to stretch the cables:
NOTE: If the tension is adjusted on existing cables (cables that were already on the
aircraft), do not need to do these steps. Go to the steps to adjust the cable STA
and cable STB to the correct rigging tension.
1) Adjust the lower turnbuckle [9] to get the cable tension of 350 ±50 lbf
(1557 ±223 N).
2) Operate the stabilizer system through a full cycle.
3) Put the cables at the center of the forward cable drum.
4) Tighten the lower turnbuckle [9].
5) Use the high tension cable tensiometer, COM-1554, to make sure that the cable
tension is at 350 ±50 lbf (1557 ±223 N).
6) Operate the stabilizer system through a full cycle.
7) Put the cables at the center of the forward cable drum.
8) Make sure that the cable tension stays at 350 ±50 lbf (1557 ±223 N).
9) Operate the stabilizer system through 5 full cycles.
10) Make sure that the cable tension stays at 350 ±50 lbf (1557 ±223 N).
(b) Do these steps until the cable STA and the cable STB get the correct rigging tension:
1) Use the lower turnbuckle [9] to adjust cables tension to the correct tension specified
in the Table 501 for the current ambient temperature.
NOTE: For new cables, adjust the tensions close to the maximum values in the
table. The cables will stretch over a period of time.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
For cables that were already on the aircraft, adjust the tensions close to the
minimum values in the table.
2) Operate the stabilizer system through a full cycle.
3) Put the cables at the center of the forward cable drum.
4) Use the low tension cable tensiometer, COM-1553, to make sure that the cable
tension is in the range specified in Table 501.

direction.
a) Measure the chain [10] tension.

(Figure 503, Figure 504)
A. General
(1) Use this test to make sure that the horizontal stabilizer moves to the correct position when it is
operated from the stabilizer trim wheel. It also make sure that the stabilizer trim indicator
operates correctly.
(2) If this test is performed as part of stabilizer control cable STA/STB replacement or
removal/installation procedures, make sure that the forward and aft stabilizer cable drum wraps
of the control cables when the stabilizer is in the full airplane nose UP and airplane nose
DOWN positions.

E. Stabilizer Electric Trim System Test
SUBTASK 27-41-00-710-004
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT ALL PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE
HORIZONTAL STABILIZERS. THE HORIZONTAL STABILIZER WILL MOVE
WHEN YOU TURN THE CONTROL TRIM WHEELS (OR PUSH THE STAB
TRIM SWITCHES). THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE
TO EQUIPMENT.
(1) Do the test of the electrical trim system test.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Set the flaps to any position from 1-40 units (TASK 27-51-00-860-803).
1) Push and hold the STAB TRIM switches on the captain's control wheel to the NOSE
DOWN position.
a) Make sure that the stabilizer leading edge moves up.
b) Release the STAB TRIM switches.
2) Push and hold the STAB TRIM switches on the captain's control wheel to the NOSE
UP position.
a) Make sure that the stabilizer leading edge moves down.
b) Release the STAB TRIM switches.
3) Push and hold the STAB TRIM switches on the first officer's control wheel to the
NOSE DOWN position.
a) Make sure that the stabilizer leading edge moves up.
b) Release the STAB TRIM switches.
4) Push and hold the STAB TRIM switches on the first officer's control wheel to the
NOSE UP position.
a) Make sure that the stabilizer leading edge moves down.
b) Release the STAB TRIM switches.
5) Push the STAB TRIM switches on the captain's control wheel to the NOSE UP
position until it stops and then to the NOSE DOWN position until it stops.
a) Make sure that the time for the stabilizer to move from its lower limit of travel
to its upper limit of travel is between 31-39 seconds.
b) Make sure that the operation is smooth and there is no unusual noise.
6) Use the STAB TRIM switches on the captain's control wheel to move the stabilizer
many time in the two directions one after the other for 3 seconds each.
a) Make sure that the operation is smooth and there is no unusual noise.
7) Push and hold the STAB TRIM switches on the captain's control wheel to the NOSE
UP position until the system comes to the full trim speed.
a) Move the STAB TRIM switches momentarily to OFF and then to the NOSE
DOWN position.
b) Make sure that the stabilizer leading edge moves up immediately after the
STAB TRIM switches are moved to the NOSE DOWN position.
8) Push and hold the STAB TRIM switches on the captain's control wheel to the NOSE
DOWN position until the system comes to the full trim speed.
a) Move the STAB TRIM switches momentarily to OFF and then to the NOSE UP
position.
b) Make sure that the stabilizer leading edge moves down immediately after the
STAB TRIM switches are moved to the NOSE UP position.
(b) Set the flaps to the full up position (TASK 27-51-00-860-804).
1) Push and hold the STAB TRIM switches on the captain's control wheel to the NOSE
DOWN position.
a) Make sure that the stabilizer leading edge moves up.
b) Release the STAB TRIM switches.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
2) Push and hold the STAB TRIM switches on the captain's control wheel to the NOSE
UP position.
a) Make sure that the stabilizer leading edge moves down.
b) Release the STAB TRIM switches.
3) Push and hold the STAB TRIM switches on the first officer's control wheel to the
NOSE DOWN position.
a) Make sure that the stabilizer leading edge moves up.
b) Release the STAB TRIM switches.
4) Push and hold the STAB TRIM switches on the first officer's control wheel to the
NOSE UP position.
a) Make sure that the stabilizer leading edge moves down.
b) Release the STAB TRIM switches.
5) Push the STAB TRIM switches on the captain's control wheel to the NOSE UP
position until it stops and then to the NOSE DOWN position until it stops.
a) Make sure that the time for the stabilizer to move from its lower limit of travel
to its upper limit of travel is 47-58 seconds.
b) Make sure that the operation is smooth and there is no unusual noise.
6) Use the STAB TRIM switches on the captain's control wheel to move the stabilizer
many times in the two directions, one after the other, for 3 seconds each.
a) Make sure that the operation is smooth and there is no unusual noise.
7) Push and hold the STAB TRIM switches on the captain's control wheel to the NOSE
UP position until the system comes to the full trim speed.
a) Move the STAB TRIM switches momentarily to OFF and then to the NOSE
DOWN position.
b) Make sure that the stabilizer leading edge moves up immediately after the
STAB TRIM switches are moved to the NOSE DOWN position.
8) Push and hold the STAB TRIM switches on the captain's control wheel to the NOSE
DOWN position until the system comes to the full trim speed.
a) Move the STAB TRIM switches momentarily to OFF and then to the NOSE UP
position.
b) Make sure that the stabilizer leading edge moves down immediately after the
STAB TRIM switches are moved to the NOSE UP position.
9) Move and hold the STAB TRIM switches on the captain's control wheel to the NOSE
UP position.
a) Make sure that the stabilizer leading edge moves down.
b) Set the main cutout switch, S272, to the CUTOUT position.
c) Make sure that the movement of the stabilizer stops immediately.
d) Set the main cutout switch, S272, to the NORMAL position.
e) Make sure that the stabilizer continues to move.
f) Release the STAB TRIM switches.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

SUBTASK 27-41-00-860-070
(1) Remove hydraulic power from system B (TASK 29-00-00-800-801).

F. Procedure
SUBTASK 27-41-00-710-012
(1) Do the stabilizer trim cutout test:
(a) Make sure that the main cutout switch, S272 on the control stand is in the NORMAL
position.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) Set the STAB TRIM switch on the stab trim and cabin door, P8-47 module, to the NORM
position.
(c) Position the stabilizer to an intermediate position (Approximately 8 units of trim is
satisfactory).
(d) Move and hold the STAB TRIM switches on the captain's control wheel to the NOSE UP
position.
1) Make sure that the stabilizer leading edge moves down (APL NOSE UP).
2) While the stabilizer moves, push the captain's control column forward until the
column cutout switch stops the stabilizer.
3) Immediately release the control column to the neutral position with the two stab trim
switches still held in the nose up position.
4) With the control column in the neutral position, make sure the stabilizer leading
edge continues to move down.
5) Release the STAB TRIM switches.
(e) Move and hold the STAB TRIM switches on the captain's control wheel to the NOSE
DOWN position.
1) Make sure that the stabilizer leading edge moves up (APL NOSE DOWN).
2) While the stabilizer moves, pull the captain's control column aft until the column
cutout switch stops the stabilizer.
3) Immediately release the control column to the neutral position with the two stab trim
switches still held in the nose down position.
4) With the control column in the neutral position, make sure the stabilizer leading
edge continues to move up.
5) Release the STAB TRIM switches.
(f) Position the stabilizer to an intermediate position (Approximately 8 units of trim is
satisfactory).
(g) Move and hold the STAB TRIM switches on the captain's control wheel to the NOSE UP
position.
1) Make sure that the stabilizer leading edge moves down (APL NOSE UP).
2) While the stabilizer moves, push the captain's control column forward until the
column cutout switch stops the stabilizer.
3) Hold the captain's control column in this position and immediately release the STAB
TRIM switches.
4) Use aprotractor, COM-1691 to make sure the captain's control column is between
2.90 and 3.70 degrees forward from the neutral position.
5) Put the captain's control column back to the neutral position.
(h) Position the stabilizer to an intermediate position (Approximately 8 units of trim is
satisfactory).
(i) Move and hold the STAB TRIM switches on the captain's control wheel to the NOSE
DOWN position.
1) Make sure that the stabilizer leading edge moves up (APL NOSE DOWN).
2) While the stabilizer moves, pull the captain's control column aft until the column
cutout switch stops the stabilizer.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
3) Hold the captain's control column in this position and immediately release the STAB
TRIM switches.
4) Use aprotractor, COM-1691 to make sure the captain's control column is between
3.20 and 4.21 degrees aft from the neutral position.
5) Put the captain's control column back to the neutral position.
SUBTASK 27-41-00-860-022
(2) Do this task: Put the Elevator Hydraulic systems A and B Back to the Condition Before the
Pressurization, TASK 27-31-00-840-801.

G. Horizontal Stabilizer Removal
SUBTASK 27-41-11-480-002
(1) Install the sling equipment, SPL-2035 (Figure 404).
(a) Remove the bolts [1] and bolts [2] from the horizontal stabilizer [3] top surface.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE YOU INSTALL THE HOISTING SLING CORRECTLY WHEN
YOU REMOVE THE HORIZONTAL STABILIZER WITH OR WITHOUT THE
ELEVATOR INSTALLED. IF YOU DO NOT INSTALL THE HOISTING SLING
CORRECTLY FOR THE REMOVAL OF THE HORIZONTAL STABILIZER,
YOU CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(b) Attach the sling equipment, SPL-2035, to the horizontal stabilizer [3] with fasteners.
NOTE: Low clearance sling is used only with elevator removed.
(c) Attach the load cell, STD-12395, to the sling equipment, SPL-2035.
(d) Attach a hoist to the load cell, STD-12395.
CAUTION
YOU MUST CAREFULLY LIFT THE HOISTING SLING. A SUDDEN
MOVEMENT OF THE HOISTING SLING CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE
HORIZONTAL STABILIZER.
(e) Lift the weight of the horizontal stabilizer [3].
1) Use the load cell, STD-12395, on the sling to make sure that the force used when
lifting horizontal stabilizer [3] is not more than:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
• 888 lb (403 kg) (830 lb (376 kg) airplane part + 58 lb (26 kg) tool) with elevator
attached
• 688 lb (312 kg) (630 lb (286 kg) airplane part + 58 lb (26 kg) tool) without elevator
attached.
SUBTASK 27-41-11-020-001
WARNING
DECREASE THE PRESSURE BEFORE YOU DISCONNECT THE HYDRAULIC
LINE. PRESSURIZED FLUID CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL.
(2) Disconnect the hydraulic line [25] of the elevator tab installed aft of the stabilizer rear spar.

(a) Flight recorder position sensor
(b) Exterior logo light (if installed).

2) Remove the nuts [35] and washers [34] from the bolts [38].
3) Remove the bolt [28], washer [29], and washer [27].
a) If it is necessary, remove the seal support structure before you remove this
bolt.

4) Remove the bolts [38], washers [37], and washers [27].

bolts.

a) If it is necessary, adjust the tension of the sling to help remove the pins.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
6) Remove and inspect each bolt or pin.
NOTE: If an existing bolt or pin has missing plating, cracked, or flaking, prior to
further flight replace with new parts or repair in accordance with a method
approved by an Authorized Representative for the BCA Organization
Designation Authorization who has been authorized to make those findings.
a) If the bolts or pins show signs of damage: pitting, corrosion, no plating (pins
only), galling (bolts only) or wear beyond drawing tolerances, replace them
with the improved bolts or pins.
b) If the pins or bolts show no sign of damage, they can be reinstalled or
replaced with an improved front spar bolts or rear spar pins designed to resist
wear, galling, or corrosion.
(c) At the horizontal stabilizer front spar, do this step:
1) Remove the pins [44], nuts [43], washers [42], shims [45], washers [46],
washers [40], and bolts [41].
(d) Lift the horizontal stabilizer [3] out horizontally, then lower to the support stand.
(e) Remove and inspect each bolt or pin.
1) If the bolts or pins show signs of damage: pitting, corrosion, no plating (pins only),
galling (bolts only) or wear beyond drawing tolerances, replace them with the
improved bolts or pins.
2) If the pins or bolts show no sign of damage, they can be reinstalled or replaced with
an improved front spar bolts or rear spar pins designed to resist wear, galling, or
corrosion.
(f) If there is indication of hydraulic fluid contamination on the lugs or clevises, examine
these components in the vertical fin for external leakage:
• Main and standby rudder PCU
• Hydraulic hoses and tubing.
NOTE: An example of hydraulic fluid contamination is cracked, peeled, or blistered paint.

1) Make sure that you protect wire bundles when you use the trammel trammel bar,

(e) Make sure that the right elevator position, “Z”, is within ±0.06 in. (1.5 mm) of the neutral
mark on the right elevator index plate (Figure 403).
1) If it is necessary, adjust the Power Control Unit (PCU) input rods to achieve the
±0.06 in. (1.5 mm) measurement on the right elevator index plate, do this task: Input
Rods of the Elevator Power Control Unit - Adjustment, TASK 27-31-00-820-803.
(f) Do the following to verify correct stabilizer geometry:
1) Make sure that the left elevator is within 0.12 in. (3.0 mm) of the initial left elevator
position.
NOTE: The initial left elevator position is the position, “Z”, measured before the
removal of the stabilizer.
2) Make sure that the right elevator is within 0.12 in. (3.0 mm) of the initial right
elevator position.
NOTE: The initial right elevator position is the position, “Z”, measured before the
removal of the stabilizer.
3) Make sure that the left elevator is within 0.12 in. (3.0 mm) of the right elevator
position.
NOTE: This measurement compares the left and right stabilizer half positions after
the installation of both sides of the stabilizer. It assures that the left and right
elevators are within 0.12 in. (3.0 mm) of their original positions. The 0.12 in.
(3.0 mm) difference is calculated to have a negligible effect on manual
reversion.
(g) If the measurements in the above step are not within limits, the elevator system should
be adjusted and test flown for manual reversion.
NOTE: You cannot adjust the elevator control pushrod to make sure that the elevator is
within the limits. Adjustment of the elevator control pushrod is too coarse to
achieve the minimum tolerance of 0.12 in. (3.0 mm). One half turn of the elevator
control pushrod moves the trailing edge of the elevator up or down 0.20 in.
(5.1 mm).

F. Horizontal Stabilizer Leading Edge Installation
SUBTASK 27-41-21-420-001
(1) Install the leading edge [3].
(a) Lift and put the leading edge [3] in its position.
(b) Make sure that the clearance between the leading edge [3] and horizontal stabilizer [2] is
0.040 in. (1.02 mm) - 0.130 in. (3.30 mm).
CAUTION
ALIGN THE LEADING EDGE ASSEMBLY ALONG THE FULL LENGTH
OF THE EDGE BEFORE YOU INSTALL THE FASTENERS. IF YOU
PUSH THE ASSEMBLY INTO ITS POSITION AND INSTALL THE
FASTENERS, DAMAGE CAN OCCUR TO THE RIB CHORDS.
1) Make sure that the alignment of the leading edge assembly is checked along the full
length prior to installing the fasteners.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(c) Install the bolts [1] that attach the top surface of the leading edge [3] to the front spar.
1) Tighten the bolts [1] to 20 in-lb (2.3 N·m).
(d) Install the bolts [1] that attach the lower surface and inboard of the leading edge [3] to the
front spar.
1) Tighten the bolts [1] to 20 in-lb (2.3 N·m).
(e) Install the tip cap assembly [4], do this task: Horizontal Stabilizer Tip - Installation,
TASK 55-10-00-400-801.
(f) Fill the clearance between the leading edge [3] and horizontal stabilizer [2] with Dow
Corning 93-006-1 RF sealant, A00900, or sealant, A00247.
