D. Prepare for the Removal
SUBTASK 27-41-31-020-006
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT ALL PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT ARE AWAY FROM
THE HORIZONTAL STABILIZER AND CONTROL CABLES IN THE FORWARD
EQUIPMENT COMPARTMENT OR AREA AFT OF THE BULKHEAD. THE
MOVEMENT OF THE HORIZONTAL STABILIZER DURING MAINTENANCE
CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(1) Remove the horizontal stabilizers: Horizontal Stabilizer - Removal, TASK 27-41-11-000-801.
SUBTASK 27-41-31-020-007
(2) Remove the stabilizer to body front spar sliding seals and pedestals
(PAGEBLOCK 53-31-31/401 Config 1 or PAGEBLOCK 53-31-31/401 Config 2).
NOTE: This will provide additional space for the stabilizer center section to move forward.
E. Hinge Fitting Removal
SUBTASK 27-41-31-860-010
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT ALL PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT ARE AWAY FROM
THE HORIZONTAL STABILIZER AND CONTROL CABLES IN THE FORWARD
EQUIPMENT COMPARTMENT OR AREA AFT OF THE BULKHEAD. THE
MOVEMENT OF THE HORIZONTAL STABILIZER DURING MAINTENANCE
CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(1) Make sure that the horizontal stabilizer is in the neutral position, if not, do these steps:
(a) If installed, remove the lock assembly, SPL-1672 (Figure 27-31-91-990-802).
(b) On the control stand, set the stabilizer trim wheel to put the horizontal stabilizer at zero
degrees (4 units of trim).
(c) Do these steps to install the lock assembly, SPL-1672, on the stabilizer trim wheel at the
control stand (Figure 27-31-91-990-802):
1) Turn the trim wheel to put the handle at the top of the wheel.
2) Adjust the height of the trim lock to put the trim wheel handle correctly on the yoke.
3) Install the pin through the yoke.
4) Install the safety pin.
SUBTASK 27-41-31-010-006
(2) Remove skin filler [57], skin support zee [58], track assembly [59], track assembly [61], track
assembly [62] and wire bundle [60].
SUBTASK 27-41-31-480-003
(3) Use wood beam, STD-9463, or wood beams that are approximately 4 in. (10 cm) by 4 in.
(10 cm) cross-section to hold the horizontal stabilizer center section (Figure 402).
(a) Use as many wood beam, STD-9463, or wood beams as necessary to make sure that
the horizontal stabilizer center section is level and supported before the hinge pin [26] is
removed.
SUBTASK 27-41-31-010-007
(4) If necessary, improve access for the hinge fittings [24], do the following steps:
(a) Loosen the nut [63] on the hydraulic line [64] (View D, Figure 402).
NOTE: It is not necessary to fully remove the nut and hydraulic line.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) Move the hydraulic line [64] for access.
SUBTASK 27-41-31-020-008
(5) Remove the hinge fittings [24] from the bulkhead support structure as follows:
NOTE: Both hinge fittings are to be removed.
(a) Remove the pin [20], nut [19], and washer [21].
1) Discard the pin [20].
(b) Remove the pin [22], nut [18], bushing spacer [23].
1) Discard the pin [22].
(c) Remove the bolts [2] and washers [3] from the bushing retainer [1].
(d) Remove the bushing retainer [1].
(e) Use the set, SPL-2026, and push out these parts:
1) The hinge insert pin [27]
2) The bushing retainer [25]
3) The hinge pin [26].
(f) To remove the adjustable hinge bushing [28], bushing spacer [16], and hinge
bushing [17], do as follows:
1) Turn the adjustable hinge bushing [28] to remove.
NOTE: The adjustable hinge bushing has threads and must be turned for removal
or installation.
2) Remove the bushing spacer [16] and hinge bushing [17].
NOTE: The bushing spacer will come off when you remove the adjustable hinge
bushing.
SUBTASK 27-41-31-020-009
(6) Remove the upper thrust brace [38] and lower thrust brace [39] (Thrust Brace Links Removal,
TASK 55-10-10-000-801).
SUBTASK 27-41-31-020-010
(7) Remove the thrust brace fitting [51] from the hinge fitting [24]:
(a) Remove the nuts [50], washers [49], washers [48], and bolts [47] that attach the thrust
brace fitting [51] to the hinge fitting [24].
NOTE: Use a marker or pen to make marks on the thrust brace fitting, to help make the
installation easier. Do not use sharp objects to make marks.
(b) Remove the thrust brace fitting [51] and shim [46].
SUBTASK 27-41-31-020-011
(8) Remove the fail safe link [10] from the hinge fitting [24]:
(a) Remove the nuts [7], washers [5], washers [6], bolt [4], and bolt [9].
(b) Remove the bonding jumper [8].
(c) Remove the pin [56], nut [15], washer [14], washer [13], and bolt [12].
1) If it is necessary, use the offset wrench kit, SPL-24249.
2) Discard the pin [56].
(d) Remove the fail safe link [10] and filler [11].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-41-31-020-012
(9) Remove the hinge fitting [24]:
(a) Remove the hi-locs [52] from the bracket [53].
(b) Remove the hi-locs [54] from the bracket [55].
(c) Remove the pin [44], nut [43], washer [42], and bolt [40] from the hinge fitting [24].
1) If it is necessary, use the offset wrench kit, SPL-24249.
2) Discard the pin [32].
(d) Remove the pin [37], nut [36], washer [35], washer [34] and bolt [33] from the hinge
fitting [24].
1) If it is necessary, use the offset wrench kit, SPL-24249.
2) Discard the pin [37].
(e) With the boards in place, carefully move the horizontal stabilizer center section forward
as much as the cutout in the fuselage structure will let you.
NOTE: Use as many maintenance personnel as necessary on the left and right sides of
the rear spar connection, to lift and move forward.
NOTE: With the boards in place the Center Section will be able to move approximately
1.5 in. (3.8 cm) forward.
1) Make sure that the horizontal stabilizer center section does not hit the neutral shift
input rods.
NOTE: The neutral shift input rods can be damaged, if they are hit by the horizontal
stabilizer center section.
(f) Move the hinge fitting [24] in a clockwise or counterclockwise direction while you move it
back and forth until it is removed.
NOTE: If moved in either the clockwise or counterclockwise direction, alternate back and
forth until the hinge fitting comes out.
(g) Remove the hinge fitting [24] from the airplane.

F. Hinge Fitting Installation
SUBTASK 27-41-31-420-006
(1) Install each hinge fitting [24], do these steps:
(a) Lubricate the threads of bolt [33] and bolt [40] with grease, D00633.
(b) Put the hinge fittings [24] in their positions.
(c) Install the bolt [33], washer [34] (under the bolt), washer [35] (3 maximum under nut), and
nut [36].
1) Tighten the nut [36] to 2200 in-lb (248.6 N·m) - 3300 in-lb (372.8 N·m).
a) If it is necessary, use the offset wrench kit, SPL-24249.
2) Carefully move the horizontal stabilizer center section into its position.
3) Install the new pin [37].
a) If it is necessary, tighten the nut [36] to get the pin hole alignment but do not
exceed 5300 in-lb (598.8 N·m).
(d) Install the bolt [40], washer [41] (under the bolt), washer [42] (3 maximum under nut), and
nut [43].
1) Tighten the nut [43] to 5400 in-lb (610 N·m) - 6450 in-lb (728.7 N·m).
a) If it is necessary, use the offset wrench kit, SPL-24249.
2) Install the new pin [44].
a) If it is necessary, tighten the nut [43] to get the pin hole alignment but do not
exceed 8600 in-lb (971.7 N·m).
SUBTASK 27-41-31-420-007
(2) Install the fail safe link [10] for each hinge fitting [24], do these steps:
(a) Lubricate the bolt [12] and bolt threads with grease, D00633.
(b) Apply sealant, A00247, to the bolt [4] and bolt [9].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(c) Put the fail safe link [10] and filler [11] on the hinge fitting [24].
(d) Install the bolt [12], washer [13] (under the bolt), washer [14] (3 maximum under nut), and
nut [15].
1) Tighten the nut [15] to 1300 in-lb (146.9 N·m) - 1530 in-lb (172.9 N·m).
a) If it is necessary, use the offset wrench kit, SPL-24249.
2) Install the new pin [56].
a) If it is necessary, tighten the nut [15] to get the pin hole alignment but do not
exceed 2000 in-lb (226.0 N·m).
(e) Install the bolt [4], washers [5] (under the bolt), washers [6] (under the nut), and nuts [7].
1) Tighten the nuts [7] to 370 in-lb (41.8 N·m) - 690 in-lb (78.0 N·m).
(f) Install the bolt [9], washers [5] (under the bolt), washers [6] (under the nut), bonding
jumper [8] (between washers [6]), and nuts [7].
1) Tighten the nuts [7] to 370 in-lb (41.8 N·m) - 690 in-lb (78.0 N·m).
2) Use intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550, to make sure that the
resistance between the free end of the bonding jumper [8] and fail safe link [10] is
not greater than 0.00216 ohms (2.16 milliohms).
3) Apply sealant, A00247, at the end of the bonding jumper [8].
SUBTASK 27-41-31-420-008
(3) Install the thrust brace fitting [51] on each hinge fitting [24], do these steps:
(a) Lubricate the bolts [47] with sealant, A00247.
(b) Put the thrust brace fitting [51] and shim [46] on the hinge fitting [24].
1) Remove or add shim [46] until you can install the bolts [47] and nuts [50] easily.
(c) Install the bolts [47], washers [48] (under the bolt), washers [49] (under the nut), and
nuts [50].
1) Tighten the nuts [50] to 630 in-lb (71.2 N·m) - 1070 in-lb (120.9 N·m).
SUBTASK 27-41-31-420-009
(4) Connect the upper thrust brace [38] and lower thrust brace [39] to the thrust brace fitting
(Thrust Brace Link Installation, TASK 55-10-10-400-801).
SUBTASK 27-41-31-420-010
(5) Install the hinge fittings [24] to the bulkhead support structure.
(a) Install each adjustable hinge bushing [28], do these steps:
1) Install the adjustable hinge bushing [28] with the bushing spacer [16] to the
bulkhead support structure on the left side.
2) Loosen the adjustable hinge bushing [28] and put the hinge fitting [24] in the correct
position.
3) Tighten the adjustable hinge bushing [28] with your fingers until the end of the
adjustable hinge bushing [28] touches the mating surface of the bearing in the hinge
fitting housing.
4) Install the adjustable hinge bushing [28] to the bulkhead support structure on the
right side.
5) Tighten the adjustable hinge bushing [28] with your fingers until the end of the
adjustable hinge bushing [28] touches the mating surface of the bearing in the hinge
fitting housing.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
6) Install the bushing spacer [16], do these steps:
a) Use the 0-0.150 Inch (0-3.81 mm) feeler gauge set, STD-1337, to measure the
clearance between the adjustable hinge bushing [28] head and bulkhead
support structure.
b) Select a bushing spacer [16] of applicable thickness for the measured
clearance and install.
NOTE: A maximum of one bushing spacer is permitted for each side.
<1> The maximum permitted clearance between the bushing spacer [16]
and bulkhead support structure after spacer installation is 0.005 in.
(0.13 mm).
(b) Install the hinge bushing [17], do these steps:
NOTE: The steps to install the hinge bushing is same for the left side and right side.
1) Lubricate the hinge bushing [17] with compound, D50004.
2) Install the hinge bushing [17].
3) Make sure that the end of the hinge bushing [17] touches the mating surface of the
bearing in the hinge fitting housing.
4) Use the 0-0.150 Inch (0-3.81 mm) feeler gauge set, STD-1337, to measure the
clearance between the hinge bushing [17] head and bulkhead support structure.
5) Make sure that the measured clearance is 0.12 +0.07 / -0.08 in.
(3.05 +1.78 / -2.03 mm).
(c) Install the hinge pin [26], do these steps:
1) Lubricate the hinge pin [26] and protector, SPL-2036, with grease, D00633.
NOTE: The protector, SPL-2036, is used to protect the head of the hinge pin.
2) Use the protector, SPL-2036, to install the hinge pin [26].
CAUTION
DO NOT USE TOO MUCH FORCE WHEN YOU INSTALL THE
HINGE PIN. DAMAGE TO THE HINGE PIN CAN OCCUR.
a) Do not apply too much force to install the hinge pin [26].
(d) Install the bushing spacer [23] and nut [18].
1) Tighten the nut [18] with your fingers.
(e) Install the bushing retainer [1] to the bulkhead support structure with the washers [3] and
bolts [2].
(f) Tighten the bolts [2] to 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m) - 75 in-lb (8.5 N·m).
(g) Install the bushing retainer [25], do these steps:
1) Install the bushing retainer [25] on the hinge pin [26].
2) Put the bushing retainer [25] in a position to allow the locating bosses to engage on
the webs of the bulkhead support structure.
3) Rotate the adjustable hinge bushing [28] a minimum amount (7.5 degrees) to allow
mating of the adjustable hinge bushing [28] head with the bushing retainer [25]
notches.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
CAUTION
DO NOT APPLY TORQUE TO THE WRENCH FLATS ON THE HINGE
PINS. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT.
(h) Temporarily remove the bushing retainer [25].
(i) Tighten the nut [18] to 650 in-lb (73.4 N·m) - 850 in-lb (96.0 N·m).
(j) If the pin holes do not align, tighten the nut [18] maximum 30 degrees as necessary to
align the nearest pin hole.
(k) Use the dial indicator, STD-1238, to measure the clearance between the bushing
spacer [16] and bulkhead support structure.
1) Make sure that the clearance is the same as you measured before and after you
installed the adjustable hinge bushing [28] in ±0.005 in. (0.13 mm).
(l) Do a check of the clearance between the bulkhead support structure and hinge
bushing [17].
1) Remove the bolts [2] and washers [3] to remove the bushing retainer [1].
2) Do a check of the clearance between the bulkhead support structure and hinge
bushing [17].
3) Make sure that the clearance is 0.12 +0.07 / -0.08 in. (3.05 +1.78 / -2.03 mm).
4) Install the bushing retainer [1] to the bulkhead support structure with the washers [3]
and bolts [2].
5) Tighten the bolts [2] to 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m) - 75 in-lb (8.5 N·m).
(m) Install the bushing retainer [25] with the hinge insert pin [27].
1) Turn the hinge insert pin [27] until you align the pin holes.
CAUTION
DO NOT APPLY TORQUE TO THE WRENCH FLATS ON THE HINGE
PINS. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT.
(n) Install the washer [21] and nut [19].
1) Tighten the nut [19] to a maximum of 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m).
2) If the pin hole of the nut [19] does not align, loosen the nut [19] a maximum of 30
degrees as necessary to align the nearest pin hole of the nut [19].
(o) Install the new pin [22] and new pin [20].
(p) Install the hi-locs [52] to attach the bracket [53] to the bulkhead support structure.
(q) Install the hi-locs [54] to attach the bracket [55] to the bulkhead support structure.
(r) Remove the wood beams, STD-9463, that held the horizontal stabilizer center section
(Figure 402).
SUBTASK 27-41-31-410-010
(6) If the hydraulic line [64] was moved for access, do the following steps:
(a) Put the hydraulic line [64] in its usual position (View D, Figure 402).
(b) Tighten the nut [63] to 140 ±7 in-lb (15.8 ±0.8 N·m).
SUBTASK 27-41-31-410-006
(7) Install the skin filler [57], skin support zee [58], track assembly [59], track assembly [61], track
assembly [62] and wire bundle [60].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-41-31-420-012
(8) Install the stabilizer to body front spar sliding seals and pedestal
(PAGEBLOCK 53-31-31/401 Config 1 or PAGEBLOCK 53-31-31/401 Config 2).
SUBTASK 27-41-31-420-011
(9) Install the horizontal stabilizers (TASK 27-41-11-400-801).
SUBTASK 27-41-31-080-004
(10) Make sure that the lock assembly, SPL-1672, has been removed from the stabilizer trim wheel
at the control stand (Figure 401).
SUBTASK 27-41-31-710-002
(11) Move the trim control wheel to make sure that the stabilizer operates smoothly through the full
travel between the jackscrew stops.
SUBTASK 27-41-31-220-004
(12) Make sure that the clearance between the jackscrew support fitting and fuselage structure is
0.030 ±0.020 in. (0.76 ±0.51 mm) on the two sides of the stabilizer.

SUBTASK 27-41-31-410-007
(1) For the left hinge fitting, close this access panel:
Number Name/Location
333AB Horizontal Stabilizer, Gap Cover, Horizontal Stabilizer to Body
(a) Make sure that the blade seal is installed correctly into the forward track channel.
SUBTASK 27-41-31-410-003
(2) For the left hinge fitting, do this step:

G. Forward Mechanism Installation
SUBTASK 27-41-41-420-001
(1) Install the stabilizer forward control mechanism [43].
(a) Put the stabilizer forward control mechanism [43] in its position.
(b) Install the bolt [17], bushing [18], washer [19], and nut [20] to attach the aft support
link [22] to the structure.
(c) Install the bolt [13], bushing [14], washer [15], and nut [16] to attach the aft support
link [22] to the structure.
(d) Install the bolts [25], washers [26], bushings [27], washers [28], and nuts [29] to attach
the forward support link [37] to the structure.
(e) Install the bolt [2], washer [3], bushing [4], washer [5], washer [6], and nut [7] to connect
the lower turnbuckle [1] to the brackets.
SUBTASK 27-41-41-420-002
(2) Adjust the lower turnbuckle [1] to get approximately 12.43 in. (315.7 mm) between the
connections.
(a) Make sure that there is approximately equal extension of the screws on each side of the
sleeve.
SUBTASK 27-41-41-020-011
(3) Connect the chain [8].
(a) Put the chain [8] on the idler sprocket [9] and forward mechanism sprocket [10].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) If it is necessary, add or remove the links from the chain [8], to correct the length of the
chain [8].
1) Use the chain repair tool, COM-25414, to install or remove the links from the
chain [8].
a) Grind the pin head before pin removal from the chain [8].
b) Do not grind the chain [8].
(c) Connect the chain [8] at the connector link [11].
(d) Do one of the applicable steps:
1) Install the pins [12] on the outboard side of the chain [8].
2) Install the replacement connecting link [50] on the outboard side of the chain [8].
SUBTASK 27-41-41-820-002
(4) Adjust the chain [8] tension.
(a) Apply a 5 lbf (22.2 N) force at approximately 4.5 ±1.0 in. (114 ±26 mm) from where the
chain [8] touches the forward mechanism sprocket [10].
(b) Make sure that the movement of the chain [8] is 0.25 ±0.07 in. (6.4 ±1.8 mm).
(c) If it is necessary, do these steps to get the correct chain movement:
1) Adjust the upper adjusting nuts [24] and upper adjusting nut [38].
2) Make sure that all three A dimensions equal ± 0.06 in. (1.52 mm) from each other:
a) Measure the A dimensions of left and right aft support link [22].
NOTE: The A dimension is the distance of the aft support link between the
center of the two connection bolts.
b) Measure the A dimension of the forward support link [36].
NOTE: The A dimension is the distance of the forward support link between
the center of the two connection bolts.
c) Make sure that all three A dimensions are ± 0.06 in. (1.52 mm) from each
other.
d) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G01912.
SUBTASK 27-41-41-420-003
(5) Connect the STB cable.
(a) Attach the eye of the STB cable in the slot in the top of the cable drum [39].
(b) Turn the trim control wheel to wind the STB cable 28-1/2 turns on the front of the cable
drum [39].
SUBTASK 27-41-41-420-004
(6) Connect the STA cable.
(a) Attach the STA cable to the cable drum [39].
1) Use a force gauge, COM-1557, to put a 50 lbf (222 N) load on the trim control wheel
to pull on the STB cable and make installation of the cable STA easier.
(b) Wind the STA cable approximately 4-1/2 turns on the front of the cable drum [39].
SUBTASK 27-41-41-420-005
(7) Install the washers [41] and nuts [42] to attach the cable guard [40] to the stabilizer forward
control mechanism [43].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

D. Procedure
SUBTASK 27-41-71-710-001
(1) Do the test of the stabilizer trim motor:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
WARNING
KEEP PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE FLIGHT
CONTROL SURFACES AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE
COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY
HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL
AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT STAY AWAY FROM
THE LEADING EDGE SLATS, TRAILING EDGE FLAPS, AND DRIVE
MECHANISMS. THE FLAPS, SLATS, AND DRIVE MECHANISMS MOVE
QUICKLY. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE
TO EQUIPMENT.
(a) Supply system B hydraulic power, do this task: TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
(b) Set the flaps to any position from 1-40 units.
1) Push and hold the stabilizer trim control switches on the captain's control wheel to
the NOSE DOWN position.
a) Make sure the stabilizer leading edge moves up.
b) Release the stabilizer trim control switches.
2) Push and hold the stabilizer trim control switches on the captain's control wheel to
the NOSE UP position.
a) Make sure the stabilizer leading edge moves down.
b) Release the stabilizer trim control switches.
3) Push and hold the stabilizer trim control switches on the first officer's control wheel
to the NOSE DOWN position.
a) Make sure the stabilizer leading edge moves up.
b) Release the stabilizer trim control switches.
4) Push and hold the stabilizer trim control switches on the first officer's control wheel
to the NOSE UP position.
a) Make sure the stabilizer leading edge moves down.
b) Release the stabilizer trim control switches.
5) Push the stabilizer trim control switches on the captain's control wheel to the NOSE
UP position and then to the NOSE DOWN position.
a) Make sure the time for the stabilizer leading edge to move from its lower limit
of travel to the upper limit of travel is between 31-39 seconds.
b) Make sure the operation is smooth and there is no unusual noise.
6) Use the stabilizer trim control switches on the captain's control wheel to move the
stabilizer many times in the two directions, one after the other for 3 seconds each.
a) Make sure the operation is smooth and there is no unusual noise.
7) Push and hold the stabilizer trim control switches on the captain's control wheel to
the NOSE UP position until the system comes to the full trim speed.
a) Move the stabilizer trim control switches momentarily to OFF and then to the
NOSE DOWN position.
b) Make sure the stabilizer leading edge moves up immediately after you move
the stabilizer trim control switches to the NOSE DOWN position.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
8) Push and hold the stabilizer trim control switches on the captain's control wheel to
the NOSE DOWN position until the system comes to the full trim speed.
a) Move the stabilizer trim control switches momentarily to OFF and then to the
NOSE UP position.
b) Make sure the stabilizer leading edge moves down immediately after you
move the stabilizer trim control switches to the NOSE UP position.
9) Push and hold the stabilizer trim control switches on the captain's control wheel to
the NOSE UP position until the system comes to full trim speed.
a) Release the stabilizer trim control switches. Make sure the stabilizer trim
wheel moves not more than 2.5 turns (900 degrees).
10) Push and hold the stabilizer trim control switches on the captain's control wheel to
the NOSE DOWN position until the system comes to full trim speed.
a) Release the stabilizer trim control switches. Make sure the stabilizer trim
wheel moves not more than 2.5 turns (900 degrees).
(c) Set the flaps to the full up position.
1) Push and hold the stabilizer trim control switches on the captain's control wheel to
the NOSE DOWN position.
a) Make sure the stabilizer leading edge moves up.
b) Release the stabilizer trim control switches.
2) Push and hold the stabilizer trim control switches on the captain's control wheel to
the NOSE UP position.
a) Make sure the stabilizer leading edge moves down.
b) Release the stabilizer trim control switches.
3) Push the stabilizer trim control switches on the captain's control wheel to the NOSE
UP position and then to the NOSE DOWN position.
a) Make sure the time for the stabilizer to move from its lower limit of travel to the
upper limit of travel is 47-58 seconds.
b) Make sure the operation is smooth and there is no unusual noise.
4) Use the stabilizer trim control switches on the captain's control wheel to move the
stabilizer many time in the two directions one after the other for 3 seconds each.
a) Make sure the operation is smooth and there is no unusual noise.
5) Push and hold the stabilizer trim control switches on the captain's control wheel to
the NOSE UP position until the system comes to the full trim speed.
a) Move the stabilizer trim control switches momentarily to OFF and then to the
NOSE DOWN position.
b) Make sure the stabilizer leading edge moves up immediately after you move
the stabilizer trim control switches to the NOSE DOWN position.
6) Push and hold the stabilizer trim control switches on the captain's control wheel to
the NOSE DOWN position until the system comes to the full trim speed.
a) Move the stabilizer trim control switches momentarily to OFF and then to the
NOSE UP position.
b) Make sure the stabilizer leading edge moves down immediately after you
move the stabilizer trim control switches to the NOSE UP position.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
7) Push and hold the stabilizer trim control switches on the captain's control wheel to
the NOSE UP position until the system comes to full trim speed.
a) Release the stabilizer trim control switches. Make sure the stabilizer trim
wheel moves not more than 0.5 turns (180 degrees).
8) Push and hold the stabilizer trim control switches on the captain's control wheel to
the NOSE DOWN position until the system comes to full trim speed.
a) Release the stabilizer trim control switches. Make sure the stabilizer trim
wheel moves not more than 0.5 turns (180 degrees).
(d) Remove system B hydraulic power, do this task: TASK 29-11-00-860-805.
(e) Do this task: Stabilizer Trim Motor Autopilot Test, TASK 22-11-81-710-801.

H. Stabilizer Trim Actuator Removal
SUBTASK 27-41-81-020-003
(1) Remove the clamps [44] for the electrical connectors [47] from the jackscrew gearbox [24]
(Figure 402):
(a) Remove the nuts [46], washers [45], and bolts [43] to remove the clamps [44] from the
jackscrew gearbox [24].
(b) Remove the electrical connectors [47] from the jackscrew gearbox [24].
(c) Install the bolts [43], washers [45], and nuts [46] back to the jackscrew gearbox [24].
SUBTASK 27-41-81-020-004
(2) Remove the cable drum guard [67] and spacers [26] from the cable drum [27]:
(a) Remove the pin [83] and castellated nut [82] from the support plate [62] that is attached
to the cable drum [27].
1) Discard the pin [83].
(b) Remove the nut [60], washer [59], bolt [57], and washer [58] that attaches the cable drum
guard [67] to the support plate [62].
(c) Remove the bolts [63], washers [64], support plate [62], spacers [26], and washer [84]
from the cable drum [27].
NOTE: Because work space is small, keep the bolts [63] in the support plate [62] and
spacers [26] to help the removal procedure.
(d) Remove the bolts [48] and washers [49] that attach the cable drum guard [67] to the
cable drum [27].
(e) Remove the cable drum guard [67] from the cable drum [27].
SUBTASK 27-41-81-020-005
CAUTION
KEEP TENSION ON THE CABLE AT ALL TIMES. WHEN THE CABLE IS
DISCONNECTED FROM THE CABLE DRUM, TENSION NEEDS TO BE KEPT
ON THE CABLE SO THAT THE CABLE DOES NOT BECOME CAUGHT IN THE
CABLE GUARDS ON THE OTHER CABLE DRUM. THIS CAN CAUSE
DAMAGE TO THE CABLE AND THE CABLE MAY NEED TO BE REPLACED.
(3) Disconnect the STB cable [65] from the cable drum [27].
(a) Use the force gauge, COM-1557, on the stabilizer trim wheel handle to put a 50 lb
(22.7 kg) load on the STA cable [66].
NOTE: This will keep the STA cable [66] on the drum, which will make the removal of the
STB cable [65] easier.
SUBTASK 27-41-81-480-001
(4) Install the pinion gear wrench, SPL-10319, on the internal spline of the jackscrew gearbox [24].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-41-81-020-006
(5) Move the jackscrew [23] to put the stabilizer leading edge to the full up position.
CAUTION
DO NOT DAMAGE OR KINK THE CABLE WHILE YOU UNWIND IT FROM
THE FORWARD CABLE DRUM. THE CABLE CAN KINK BETWEEN THE
CABLE GUARD AND THE FORWARD CABLE DRUM WHEN YOU
REMOVE THE LAST WRAP OF CABLE. IF YOU REMOVE THE CABLE
TOO QUICKLY, YOU CAN CAUSE DAMAGE THE END OF THE CABLE.
(a) When the stabilizer starts to move, pull the STB cable [65] into the tail compartment and
wind it on a cable spool, STD-22106.
NOTE: It is necessary to use the cable spool, STD-22106, to prevent damage and
maintain tension on the cable.
NOTE: It is recommended that a mechanic watch the cable unwind from the forward
cable drum to make sure that no damage occurs to the cable as the last three
wraps of cable are slowly unwound from the cable drum.
(b) When the ball nut [28] touches the stops, keep a record of the number of turns of the STA
cable [66] on the cable drum [27].
(c) Disconnect the STA cable [66] from the cable drum [27].
SUBTASK 27-41-81-480-002
(6) Install the control cable clamp, SPL-1569, to the cables and attach DO NOT OPERATE tags,
STD-858, to the stabilizer trim wheels.
SUBTASK 27-41-81-480-003
WARNING
INSTALL THE HORIZONTAL STABILIZER LOCKS. THE STABILIZER LEADING
EDGE CAN MOVE UP QUICKLY WHEN YOU DISCONNECT THE
JACKSCREW. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL, AND DAMAGE
TO EQUIPMENT.
(7) Install the lock equipment, SPL-1678, on the jackscrew fitting [21] (Figure 403):
(a) Refer to the instructions for installation of the lock equipment, SPL-1678, on the placard
from the tooling storage box.
(b) Install the lower horizontal stabilizer lock.
1) The maximum torque for the lower lock assembly bolts is 12 in-lb (1 N·m).
(c) Remove the clamps that attach the Auxiliary Power Unit (APU) Integrated Drive
Generator (IDG) cables to the frame and place the cables away from the stabilizer lock.
NOTE: This will prevent contact of the cables with the stabilizer lock and reduce the risk
of damage to the cables.
CAUTION
DO NOT MOVE THE JACKSCREW FITTING INTO THE HORIZONTAL
STABILIZER LOCKS. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT.
(d) Turn the motor shaft or cable drum by hand to move the stabilizer leading edge down
until the stabilizer truss touches the horizontal stabilizer lock.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU CORRECTLY INSTALL THE CLAMP ASSEMBLY
FROM THE STABILIZER LOCK IN THE TWO POSITIONS ON THE UPPER
ASSEMBLY. IF YOU DO NOT DO THIS, IT CAN COME OFF AND CAUSE
DAMAGE TO THE JACKSCREW AND ADJACENT EQUIPMENT.
(e) Install the upper horizontal stabilizer lock.
1) Make sure that the adjustable leveling feet are adjusted so that they contact the
jackscrew fittings [21].
2) The maximum torque for the upper lock assembly bolts is 12 in-lb (1 N·m).
SUBTASK 27-41-81-480-004
(8) Install the equipment, SPL-1728, and fishpole hoist, COM-1563, to the stabilizer trim
actuator [53] (Figure 403):
(a) Install the hoist adapter on the jackscrew [23].
(b) Install the hoist bar between the frames at the top of the stabilizer trim compartment.
(c) Attach the hoist to the hoist bar and connect it to the hoist adapter.
SUBTASK 27-41-81-020-007
(9) Remove the stabilizer trim actuator [53] from the airplane (Figure 402).
(a) Remove the nut [42], washers [40], and bolt [39] to disconnect the bonding jumper [41]
from the jackscrew gearbox [24].
1) Install the bolt [39], washers [40], and nut [42] back in the jackscrew gearbox [24].
(b) Remove the bolt [72], washer [73], washer [74], and nut [75] from the safety strap [56].
(c) Remove the bolt [68], washer [69], washer [70], and nut [71] from the safety strap [56].
(d) Remove the bolt [54] and washer [55] from the safety strap [56].
(e) If it is necessary to remove the second safety strap [56], remove the bolt [72],
washer [73], washer [74], nut [75], bolt [68], washer [69], washer [70], nut [71], bolt [54]
and washer [55] from the safety strap [56].
NOTE: The second safety strap can be removed to have additional clearance for the
stabilizer trim actuator removal.
(f) Remove the pins [38], nuts [37], washers [36], washers [34], spacers [35], and bolts [33]
that attaches the ball nut [28] to the jackscrew fitting [21].
1) Discard the pins [38].
(g) Remove the bolts [29] and washers [30] to remove the upper gimbal pins [31] from the
upper gimbal fittings [22].
(h) Move the ball nut [28] down and adjust the jackscrew [23] until it is clear from the
jackscrew fitting [21].
(i) Install the washers [30] and bolts [29] to attach the upper gimbal pins [31] back in the
upper gimbal fittings [22].
(j) Remove the pins [52], nuts [51], washers [50], and lower gimbal pins [25] from the
stabilizer trim actuator [53].
1) Discard the pins [52].
(k) Lower the jackscrew [23] until it is clear of the stabilizer truss.
(l) Lower the stabilizer trim actuator [53] from the airplane.

SUBTASK 27-41-81-220-002
(1) Do this task: Upper and Lower Gimbal Wear Limits Inspection, TASK 27-41-81-200-802.
SUBTASK 27-41-81-020-008
(2) If the cable drum guard [67] and spacers [26] are installed on the cable drum [27], do these
steps (Figure 402):
(a) Remove the pin [83] and castellated nut [82] from the support plate [62] that is attached
to the cable drum [27].
1) Discard the pin [83].
(b) Remove the nut [60], washer [59], bolt [57], and washer [58] that attach the cable drum
guard [67] to the support plate [62].
(c) Remove the bolts [63] washers [64], support plate [62], spacers [26], and washer [84]
from the cable drum [27].
NOTE: Because work space is small, you must keep the bolt in the support plate and
spacers to help the removal procedure.
(d) Remove the bolts [48] and washers [49] that attach the cable drum guard [67] to the
cable drum [27].
(e) Remove the cable drum guard [67] from the cable drum [27].
SUBTASK 27-41-81-480-005
(3) Install the hoist adapter and hoist to the stabilizer trim actuator [53] (Figure 403).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-41-81-480-006
(4) Lift the stabilizer trim actuator [53] into the airplane (Figure 402).
I. Stabilizer Trim Actuator Installation
SUBTASK 27-41-81-420-001
(1) Install the Horizontal Stabilizer Trim Actuator (HSTA).
(a) Install the jackscrew [23] through the jackscrew fitting [21].
1) If it is necessary, lower the ball nut [28] to install the jackscrew [23] through the
jackscrew fitting [21].
a) Manually rotate the cable drum [27], while holding the ball nut [28].
NOTE: This will keep the correct timing of the cable drum.
(b) Align the stabilizer trim actuator [53] with structure.
(c) Apply grease, D00633, to the lower gimbal pins [25].
(d) Install the lower gimbal pins [25] with the grease fitting outboard, washers [50], and
nuts [51] to connect the stabilizer trim actuator [53] to the structure.
(e) Tighten the nuts [51] by hand, then tighten them to the nearest pin hole.
(f) Install the new pins [52].
(g) Install the bolt [54] and washer [55] with bolt head outboard to connect the stabilizer trim
actuator [53] to the safety strap [56].

connect the stabilizer trim actuator [53] to the safety strap [56].

washer [69], washer [70], nut [71], bolt [72], washer [73], washer [74], and nut [75] with
bolt heads outboard to connect the stabilizer trim actuator [53] to the safety strap [56].

1) Make sure that the ball nut [28] is installed with the grease fitting toward the access
door.
a) If it is necessary, rotate the ball nut half a turn.

SUBTASK 27-41-81-210-001
(1) Do these Horizontal Stabilizer Trim Actuator (HSTA) inspections:
NOTE: The HSTA does not have to be replaced if the phosphate coating on the ballscrew is
found worn.
(a) Do a detailed inspection of all attachment points to make sure that they are secure and
do not have damage.
1) Make sure that the HSTA is correctly attached to the airplane structure, do an
inspection of the components shown on Table 601 and Table 602 (Views C and D,
Figure 601).

a) Examine the components for damage, deformation, corrosion, or loose
hardware, unless otherwise specified.
<1> If it is necessary, use a flashlight, STD-14360, and inspection mirror,
STD-600, or borescope, STD-7028.
<2> If either condition is found, replace the component.
(b) Do a general visual inspection of the area below, on, and around the HSTA to see if
grease is released from the ballnut.
NOTE: Large quantities of grease around the HSTA can be that the leakage is from the
ballnut. The leakage can be because of a defective seal or a return tube was
lifted out of position.
1) If a defective seal or a return tube is the cause of the leakage, do a detailed
inspection.
2) Examine the ballnut tube retainers for a deformation, corrosion, or a return tube that
is lifted.
3) If the ballnut tube retainers have a deformation, corrosion, or the leakage is from the
return tube, remove and replace the actuator (TASK 27-41-81-000-801 and
TASK 27-41-81-400-801).
(c) Examine cable drum and cables for damage or binding.
(d) Examine the electrical connectors of the stabilizer trim motor for damage.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(e) Do a detailed inspection of the grease on and around the jackscrew and ballnut for
metallic particles, other solid particles, and corrosion products in the grease.
NOTE: Metallic particles in the grease can be an indication of degradation of the balls in
the ball nut. If metallic particles are found in the grease, remove for repair and
replace the stabilizer trim actuator.
1) If metallic particles, or other solid particles, or corrosion products are found in the
grease, do this step:
a) Remove for repair and replace the HSTA (TASK 27-41-81-000-801 and
TASK 27-41-81-400-801).
(f) Check if any of the ballnut bearings are found in the vicinity of the ballnut, on the
jackscrew, or directly below the HSTA.
NOTE: The ball bearings dimension is 0.21875 in. (5.55625 mm) diameter.
1) If ball bearings are found, do this step:
a) Remove for repair and replace the HSTA (TASK 27-41-81-000-801 and
TASK 27-41-81-400-801).
(g) Wipe the old grease and dirt from the jackscrew threads with a clean, dry, non-abrasive
cotton cloth, G50316.
(h) Do a detailed visual inspection of the upper and lower gimbals for cracks or damage
(View B, Figure 601).
1) Examine the areas around the holes and bushings.
2) If parts with damage are found, replace the HSTA (TASK 27-41-81-000-801 and
TASK 27-41-81-400-801).
(i) Do a detailed inspection of the jackscrew for these problems:
1) Examine the jackscrew threads for cross-threading, distortion, or stripping.
2) Check for metallic particles, pitting, gouging, corrosion, spalling, or brinelling in the
jackscrew threads.
NOTE: If metallic particles are observed in the grease, there can be damage in the
jackscrew/ball nut assembly. Normal wear of the jackscrew actuator can
occur but this will not release visible metallic particles in the grease.
3) Check the jackscrew for obvious differences in thread shape between thread
grooves in the lower, middle, and upper portions of the jackscrew.
4) Check the jackscrew for damage or cracking.
5) Remove the DO NOT OPERATE tag, STD-858, from the Main Cutout switch, S272.
6) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers:
CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1
Row Col Number Name
C 2 C00849 AFCS STABILIZER TRIM
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2
Row Col Number Name
B 10 C00207 FLIGHT CONTROL STAB TRIM CONT
D 10 C00840 FLIGHT CONTROL STAB TRIM ACTUATOR
7) Make sure that the STAB TRIM switch, on the stab trim and cabin door panel, P8-47
module, is in the NORM position.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
8) Set the Main Cutout switch, S272, located on the aft area of the control stand, to the
NORMAL position.
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT ALL PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT ARE AWAY
FROM THE HORIZONTAL STABILIZER AND CONTROL CABLES IN
THE FORWARD EQUIPMENT COMPARTMENT OR AREA AFT OF
THE BULKHEAD. THE MOVEMENT OF THE HORIZONTAL
STABILIZER DURING MAINTENANCE CAN CAUSE INJURY TO
PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
9) Push and hold the stabilizer trim control switches on the Captain’s Control Wheel
(NOSE UP or NOSE DOWN) to move the jackscrew to another location other than
the current setting.
10) Set the Main Cutout switch, S272, to the CUTOUT position.
11) Attach the DO NOT OPERATE tag, STD-858, to the Main Cutout switch, S272.
12) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags:
CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1
Row Col Number Name
C 2 C00849 AFCS STABILIZER TRIM
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2
Row Col Number Name
B 10 C00207 FLIGHT CONTROL STAB TRIM CONT
D 10 C00840 FLIGHT CONTROL STAB TRIM ACTUATOR
13) With the stabilizer jackscrew moved to another position:
a) Remove the old grease and dirt from the newly exposed jackscrew threads by
wiping them with a clean, dry, non-abrasive cotton cloth, G50316.
b) Examine the threads on the newly exposed area of the jackscrew for
cross-threading, distortion or stripping.
c) Check the newly exposed area of the jackscrew for metallic particles, pitting,
gouging, corrosion, spalling, or brinelling in the jackscrew threads.
NOTE: If metallic particles are observed in the grease, there can be damage
in the jackscrew/ball nut assembly. Normal wear of the jackscrew
actuator can happen but this will not release visible metallic particles
in the grease.
d) Check the newly exposed jackscrew for obvious differences in thread shape
between thread grooves in the lower, middle, and upper portions of the
jackscrew.
e) Check the newly exposed jackscrew for damage or cracking.
14) If damage is found, replace the stabilizer jackscrew actuator
(TASK 27-41-81-000-801 and TASK 27-41-81-400-801).
15) For the grease removed from the jackscrew prior to examining the threads for
damage, corrosion, and contamination, do this step:
a) Lubricate the stabilizer trim jackscrew (TASK 12-22-41-600-801).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

G. Stabilizer Control Cable Removal
SUBTASK 27-41-82-020-004
(1) Remove the cable drum guard [28] and spacers [14] from the aft cable drum [15]:
(a) Remove the pin [83] and castellated nut [82] from the support plate [25] that is attached
to the aft cable drum [15].
1) Discard the pin [83].
(b) Remove the nut [23], washer [22], washer [21], and bolt [20] that attach the cable drum
guard [28] to the support plate [25].
(c) Remove the bolts [26], washers [27], support plate [25], spacers [14], and washer [84]
from the aft cable drum [15].
NOTE: Because work space is small, you must keep the bolts in the support plate and
the spacers to help the removal procedure.
(d) Remove the bolts [16] and washers [17] that attach the cable drum guard [28] to the aft
cable drum [15].
(e) Remove the cable drum guard [28] from the aft cable drum [15].
SUBTASK 27-41-82-020-013
(2) Remove the cable guard spacers [14] from the forward cable drum [15].
(a) Remove the bolts [1], washers [10] (if installed), washers [2], and nuts [9] that secure the
right spacer [14], center spacer [14], and left spacer [14].
(b) Remove the pins [35] and washers [19] that secure the three other spacers [14].
(c) If required, loosen the cable drum guard [28].
SUBTASK 27-41-82-020-005
(3) Disconnect the STB cable [5] from the aft cable drum [15].
(a) Install the pinion gear wrench, SPL-10319, on the internal spline of the jackscrew
gearbox [12] (Figure 401).
NOTE: Insert the arm of the pinion gear wrench, SPL-10319, into the motor mount hole
to keep the internal spline of the jackscrew gearbox from turning.
(b) Use the force gauge, COM-1557, on the captain's or first officer's stabilizer trim wheel
handle to put a 50 lb (22.7 kg) load on the handle to stretch the STA cable [6].
NOTE: This will keep the STA cable on the drum and will make the removal of the STB
cable easier.
(c) Disconnect the STB cable [5] from the aft cable drum [15].
SUBTASK 27-41-82-020-006
(4) Remove the STB cable [5] from the cable run.
(a) Remove the arm of the pinion gear wrench, SPL-10319, from the stabilizer trim motor
mount hole.
(b) Remove the DO NOT OPERATE tag, from the stabilizer trim wheel at the control stand.
(c) Using the captain's or first officer's stabilizer trim control wheel, move the jackscrew [11]
to put the stabilizer leading edge to the full up (airplane nose down) position.

(d) When the stabilizer starts to move, pull the STB cable [5] into the tail compartment and
wind it on a spool or a reel.
NOTE: Tension must always be kept on the STB cable while pulling it into the tail
compartment. The best way to keep steady tension on the STB cable is to have a
mechanic pulling the cable into the tail compartment while another winds it onto a
spool or reel.
NOTE: To ensure the STB cable is not damaged or kinked as it is unwound from the
forward drum, it is best to have a mechanic in the forward compartment to watch
the cable as it unwinds from the forward cable drum. This will ensure that the
mechanic operating the stabilizer trim control wheel does not turn the forward
cable drum too far and kink the cable on the right cable guard (Figure 401).
(e) When the ballnut touches the upper stop, keep a record of the number of turns of the STA
cable [6] on the cable drum [15].
(f) Disconnect the STA cable [6] from the aft cable drum [15].
NOTE: Use a control cable clamp, SPL-1569, to keep tension on the STA cable to keep it
from unwinding on the forward cable drum.
(g) Disconnect the STB cable [5] from the forward cable drum [15].
1) Remove the nut and washer from the clevis bolt.
2) Remove the clevis bolt from the STB cable [5] eyelet.

27-41-82-400-801Stabilizer Control Cable - InstallationPDF p. 1870
3. Stabilizer Control Cable - Installation
(Figure 401, Figure 402)
A. General
(1) It is recommended that cable assemblies on each side of a cable loop be replaced at the same
time using the same grade material in order to minimize asymmetric relaxation.
(2) It is recommended that airplanes supplied with the cables that contain higher zinc coating
(Grade D or Grade K) be re-tensioned three to four months into service. This will bring the
tension of the control cables within the desired range. After the cables are re-tensioned the
high zinc cables (Grade D or Grade K) will continue to relax at a rate that is equivalent to the
Grade B cables.

H. Prepare for the Installation
SUBTASK 27-41-82-860-003
(1) Use the pinion gear wrench, SPL-10319, to set the stabilizer leading edge to the full down
(airplane nose up) position.
SUBTASK 27-41-82-100-001
(2) Use a clean cloth to clean the grease and dirt from the forward and the aft cable drums [15].
SUBTASK 27-41-82-420-001
(3) Install the STA cable [6] and STB cable [5] into the cable runs (Figure 402).
(a) Place the new, or used, cables in the forward mechanism compartment.
(b) Attach the lockstitch to the aft end of the STA cable [6] and STB cable [5].
(c) Pulling the lockstitch from the aft unpressurized compartment, guide the stabilizer control
cables through the cable runs of the airplane.
1) Make sure that the idler pulleys are removed.
2) Remove the aft pulley as required to let the end of the cable through the pulley
stations (Figure 402).
NOTE: The aft pulley must only be removed while the cable end passes through
the bracket to decrease the cable rubbing.
SUBTASK 27-41-82-420-002
(4) Wind the STA cable [6] and STB cable [5] onto a spool or reel in the aft unpressurized
compartment.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-41-82-420-003
(5) Install the idler pulleys in the idler pulley brackets (Figure 402).
(a) Make sure that the STA cable [6] and STB cable [5] are in the groove above each idler
pulley.
I. Stabilizer Control Cable Installation
SUBTASK 27-41-82-420-015
(1) Loosely install the bolts [32], washers [33], and nuts [34] to securely hold the forward cable
drum guard [28] in the correct orientation.
NOTE: This will prevent a STA cable and STB cable from slipping off the cable drum during
cables installation.
SUBTASK 27-41-82-420-004
(2) Connect the STA cable [6] to the bottom slot of the forward cable drum [15] (Figure 401):
(a) Using the captain's or first officer's stabilizer control wheel, rotate the forward cable
drum [15] so that the lower cable connection point is on the left side of the airplane.
1) Install the STA cable clevis bolt through the STA cable [6] eyelet, the washers (if
necessary) on the STA cable clevis bolt, the castle nut on the STA cable clevis bolt,
and a new cotter pin [18] through the STA cable clevis bolt (Figure 401).
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE CABLE WINDS ONTO THE DRUM GROOVES
CORRECTLY WITH EACH TURN OF THE DRUM. THE CABLE CAN JAM
BETWEEN THE CABLE AND THE CABLE DRUM GUARD. IF YOU DO
NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO THE CABLE WILL OCCUR.
(b) Use the captain's or first officer's stabilizer trim control wheel to wind the STA cable [6]
"completely" onto the forward cable drum [15] (Approximately 33 1/2 turns).
NOTE: Tension must always be kept on the STA cable [6] while winding it onto the
forward cable drum [15]. The best way to keep steady tension on the STA
cable [6] is to have a mechanic applying tension to the cable in the aft
unpressurized compartment while another mechanic keeps the cable in position
in the forward mechanism compartment.
NOTE: To ensure the STA cable [6] is not damaged or kinked as it is wound onto the
forward cable drum [15], it is recommended to have a mechanic in the forward
mechanism compartment to watch the cable as it slowly winds onto the forward
cable drum [15]. This will ensure that the mechanic that is turning the stabilizer
trim control wheel, does not turn the forward cable drum [15] too much and
damage or kink the cable.
SUBTASK 27-41-82-420-005
(3) Connect the STB cable [5] to the top slot of the forward cable drum [15] (Figure 401):
(a) While keeping tension on the STA cable [6], use the captain's or first officer's stabilizer
control wheel to rotate the forward cable drum [15] so that the upper cable connection
point is on the right side of the airplane.
1) Install the STB cable [5] eyelet in the location on the upper right side of the forward
cable drum [15].
a) Install the STB cable clevis bolt through the STB cable [5] eyelet and the
washer and nut on the STB cable clevis bolt.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE CABLE WINDS ONTO THE DRUM GROOVES
CORRECTLY WITH EACH TURN OF THE DRUM. THE CABLE CAN JAM
BETWEEN THE CABLE AND THE CABLE DRUM GUARD. IF YOU DO
NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO THE CABLE WILL OCCUR.
(b) Use the captain's or first officer's stabilizer trim control wheel to wind the STB cable [5]
onto the forward cable drum [15] approximately 2 turns.
NOTE: Tension must always be kept on the STA cable [6] and STB cable [5] while
winding them onto the forward cable drum [15]. The best way to keep steady
tension on the cables is to have a mechanic applying tension to the cable in the
aft unpressurized compartment while another mechanic keeps the cable in
position at the forward cable drum [15].
(c) Install non-metallic wedges between the STA cable [6] and STB cable [5] and the cable
guards on the left and right sides of the forward cable drum [15].
NOTE: The wedges are used to keep tension on the STA cable [6] and STB cable [5]
while the cables are rigged to the forward cable drum [15].
SUBTASK 27-41-82-420-006
(4) Install the STB cable [5] on the aft cable drum [15].
(a) Install the cable terminal in the top terminal slot of the aft cable drum [15].
(b) Install a new pin [61] to connect the cable terminal to the aft cable drum [15].
1) Install the ends of the pin [61] in the terminal slot.
(c) Place approximately 1.7 wraps of STB cable [5] on the aft cable drum [15].
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE STB CABLE IS IN THE GROOVE OF THE
FORWARD PULLEY AND AFT PULLEY BEFORE YOU TIGHTEN THE
CABLE. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN
OCCUR.
(d) Using the pinion gear wrench, SPL-10319, wind the STB cable [5] onto the aft cable
drum [15] until the ballscrew reaches the upper stops.
1) Use the pinion gear wrench, SPL-10319, to keep tension on the STB cable [5].
2) Make sure that the STB cable [5] is in the groove of the forward (STA 330) and aft
(STA 1038) pulley (Figure 402).
SUBTASK 27-41-82-420-007
(5) Install the STA cable [6] on the aft cable drum [15].
(a) Place approximately 1.8 wraps of cable around the aft cable drum [15] and install the
cable terminal in the bottom terminal slot of the aft cable drum [15].
(b) Attach a control cable clamp, SPL-1569, to the STA cable [6], forward of the aft cable
drum [15].
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT YOU DO NOT GET FINGERS OR HANDS CAUGHT
BETWEEN THE CABLE AND THE DRUM OR INTO A LOOP OF CABLE. IF
THE CABLE MOVES SUDDENLY, DANGEROUS INJURY TO
PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(WARNING PRECEDES)
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE STA CABLE IS IN THE GROOVE OF THE
FORWARD PULLEY AND AFT PULLEY BEFORE YOU TIGHTEN THE
CABLE. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN
OCCUR.
(c) Apply tension to STA cable [6] with the control cable clamp, SPL-1569, until there is
sufficient cable to complete the last wrapping around the aft cable drum [15].
1) If it is necessary, loosen the lower turnbuckle [3], on the forward mechanism, to get
sufficient play in the cable.
2) Make sure that the STA cable [6] is in the groove of the forward (STA 330) and the
aft (STA 1038) pulley (Figure 402).
(d) Install the new pin [61] to connect the cable terminal to the aft cable drum [15].
1) Install the ends of the pin [61] in the terminal slot.
(e) Remove the non-metallic wedges from the forward cable drum [15] while keeping tension
on the STA cable [6] at the aft cable drum [15].
SUBTASK 27-41-82-080-001
(6) Remove the control cable clamp, SPL-1569.
SUBTASK 27-41-82-420-008
(7) Install the spacers [14] and cable drum guard [28] to the aft cable drum [15].
(a) Apply grease, D00633, to bolts [16], bolt [20], and bolts [26].
(b) Install the bolts [16] and washers [17] to attach the cable drum guard [28] to the aft cable
drum [15].
1) Tighten the bolts [16].
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU INSTALL THE WASHER BETWEEN THE
SUPPORT PLATE AND THE CABLE DRUM. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, THE
CABLE DRUM WILL NOT TURN CORRECTLY DURING OPERATION.
(c) Install the washer [84] to the aft cable drum [15].
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU INSTALL THE SUPPORT PLATE CORRECTLY.
THE SUM OF TORQUE TO DISENGAGE THE MANUAL CLUTCH CAN BE
MORE THAN THE LIMITS. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE CAN
OCCUR.
(d) Install the bolts [26], washers [27], support plate [25], and spacers [14] to the aft cable
drum [15].
1) Install the bolts [26] to the washers [27], support plate [25], and spacers [14].
NOTE: The bearing assembly of the support plate [25] must be on the same side
as the aft cable drum [15].
2) Install the bolts [26] to the aft cable drum [15].
3) Tighten the bolts [26].
(e) Install the bolt [20], washer [21], washer [22], and nut [23] to attach the cable drum
guard [28] to the support plate [25].
1) Tighten the bolt [20].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(f) Install the castellated nut [82] to the aft cable drum [15].
1) Install the castellated nut [82] to the thread of the aft cable drum [15].
2) Hand tighten the castellated nut [82] against the support plate [25].
3) Align the castellated nut [82] back to the nearest pin hole.
(g) Install the new pin [83] to the castellated nut [82].
SUBTASK 27-41-82-420-012
(8) Install the spacers [14] on the forward cable drum [15].
(a) Install the bolts [1], washers [10] (if removed), washers [2], and nuts [9] that secure the

(b) Install the pins [35] and washers [19] that secure the three other spacers [14].

(a) If it is necessary, use a video camera on areas that are not visible.
(b) Make sure that the cable routing is correct.
(c) Operate the system along the full range of travel.
(d) Make sure that there is free movement in all directions of travel.
(e) Make sure that the flight control surfaces align correctly.
(f) Make sure that the flight control surfaces have the correct routing and clearances.
(g) Make sure that the bellcranks and control rods move correctly.
(h) Make sure that the detents align correctly for the full range of the cable control
mechanism.

mechanism.

NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. References

D. Main Cutout Switch Test
SUBTASK 27-41-91-710-001
(1) Do the test of the main cutout switch, S272:
(a) Set the main cutout switch to the NORMAL position.
1) Push and hold the STAB TRIM switches on the captain's control wheel to the NOSE
UP position.
2) Make sure the stabilizer leading edge moves down.
3) Set the main cutout switch to the CUTOUT position.
4) Make sure that the movement of the stabilizer stops immediately.
5) Release the STAB TRIM switches.
(b) Set the main cutout switch to the NORMAL position.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Push and hold the STAB TRIM switches on the captain's control wheel to the NOSE
DOWN position.
2) Make sure the stabilizer leading edge moves up.
3) Set the main cutout switch to the CUTOUT position.
4) Make sure that the movement of the stabilizer stops immediately.
5) Release the STAB TRIM switches.
(c) Set the main cutout switch back to the NORMAL position.

NORMAL position.
D. Autopilot Cutout Switch Test
SUBTASK 27-41-91-710-002
(1) Do the test of the autopilot switch, S149:
(a) Set the autopilot cutout switch to the NORMAL position.
1) Engage the autopilot.
2) Move the control column to the nose up and then to the nose down position.
3) Make sure the stabilizer leading edge moves down and then up.
(b) Set the autopilot cutout switch to the CUTOUT position.
1) Make sure the autopilot disengages.
2) Move the control column to the nose up and then to the nose down position.
3) Make sure the stabilizer leading edge does not move.
(c) Set the autopilot cutout switch to the NORMAL position.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Engage the autopilot.
2) Move the control column to the nose up and then to the nose down position.
3) Make sure the stabilizer leading edge moves down and then up.
4) Disengage the autopilot.

(c) Loosen the lockscrews [4].

(when you hear a click).

1) Move the stabilizer until the limit switch [1] does not touch the cam.

 ALL

3. Stabilizer Trim Limit Switches Test
(Figure 502)
A. General
(1) The trim system can move the stabilizer to a position more than the limits that were set during
the adjustment of the limit switches because of the coasting (coasting occurs when power has
been removed from the stab trim actuator but the ballscrew is still moving as it comes to a
stop). This condition is usual. Thus the "B" dimension tolerances for the test are larger than the
tolerance for the adjustment.
(2) This test is applicable only for limit switches S145, S844, and S144.
B. References
Reference Title
27-51-00-860-804 Retract the Trailing Edge Flaps (P/B 201)

G. Stabilizer Trim Limit Switches Test
SUBTASK 27-41-94-710-004
(1) Do the test of the limit switch S844:
(a) Set the main cutout switch, S272, in the CUTOUT position.
(b) Use the stabilizer trim wheel to move the stabilizer to the maximum leading edge up (APL
NOSE DOWN) position.
(c) Set the main cutout switch, S272, in the NORMAL position.
(d) Turn the captain's stabilizer trim wheel clockwise approximately 3 turns.
(e) Move and hold the STAB TRIM switches on the captain's control wheel to the NOSE
DOWN position.
1) Make sure that the stabilizer leading edge does not move.
2) Release the STAB TRIM switches.
(f) Move and hold the STAB TRIM switches on the captain's control wheel to the NOSE UP
position.
1) Make sure that stabilizer leading edge moves down (APL NOSE UP).
2) Release the STAB TRIM switches.
(g) Move the stabilizer to approximately 4 units of trim.
(h) Move the STAB TRIM switches on the captain's control wheel to the NOSE DOWN
position until the stabilizer stops automatically.
1) Use the trammel bar, SPL-1677, to measure the "B" dimension.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU ARE CAREFUL WITH THE WIRE
BUNDLES WHEN YOU USE THE TRAMMEL BAR, SPL-1677.
THE SHARP EDGES ON THE TRAMMEL BAR, SPL-1677 CAN
CAUSE CHAFING OR DAMAGE TO THE WIRES.
a) Make sure to protect wire bundles when using the trammel trammel bar,
SPL-1677.
2) Make sure that the "B" dimension is 39.96 ±0.05 in. (1015.0 ±1.3 mm).
SUBTASK 27-41-94-710-005
(2) Do the test of the limit switch, S145:
(a) If you use the standby hydraulic pump motor to move the flaps, do these steps:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF
THE LE AND TE FLAPS AND FLAP-DRIVE MECHANISMS. THE
FLAPS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
CAUTION
DO NOT OPERATE THE TRAILING EDGE FLAPS WITH
ELECTRICAL POWER MORE THAN ONE FULL EXTEND/RETRACT
CYCLE IN 25 MINUTES. YOU CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE FLAP
ELECTRIC MOTORS IF YOU OPERATE THEM TOO FREQUENTLY.
1) Put the ALTERNATE FLAP arm switch in the ARM position.
NOTE: The standby hydraulic pump motor will operate when the ALTERNATE
FLAP arm switch is in the ARM position.
2) Move the flap control lever to the 5-unit detent position.
3) Move the alternate flap drive control switch to extend the flaps to the 5-unit position.
(b) If you use the system B hydraulic power to move the flap, do these steps:
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF
ALL CONTROL SURFACES BEFORE YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC
POWER. THE AILERONS, RUDDER, ELEVATORS, FLAPS, SLATS,
SPOILERS, LANDING GEAR, AND THRUST REVERSERS CAN
MOVE QUICKLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS
CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
1) Pressurize hydraulic system B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization,
TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF
THE LE AND TE FLAPS AND FLAP-DRIVE MECHANISMS. THE
FLAPS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
2) Move the flap control lever to extend the flaps to the 5-unit position.
(c) Set the main cutout switch, S272, in the CUTOUT position.
(d) Use the stabilizer trim wheel to move the stabilizer to the maximum leading edge up (APL
NOSE DOWN) position.
(e) Set the main cutout switch, S272, in the NORMAL position.
(f) Turn the captain's stabilizer trim wheel clockwise approximately 2 +/- 0.25 turns.
(g) Move and hold the STAB TRIM switches on the captain's control wheel to the NOSE
DOWN position.
1) Make sure that the stabilizer leading edge does not move.
2) Release the STAB TRIM switches.
(h) Move and hold the STAB TRIM switches on the captain's control wheel to the NOSE UP
position.
1) Make sure that stabilizer leading edge moves down (APL NOSE UP).
2) Release the STAB TRIM switches.
(i) Move the stabilizer to approximately 1 units of trim.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(j) Move the STAB TRIM switches on the captain's control wheel to the NOSE DOWN
position until the stabilizer stops automatically.
1) Use the trammel bar, SPL-1677, to measure the "B" dimension.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU ARE CAREFUL WITH THE WIRE
BUNDLES WHEN YOU USE THE TRAMMEL BAR, SPL-1677.
THE SHARP EDGES ON THE TRAMMEL BAR, SPL-1677 CAN
CAUSE CHAFING OR DAMAGE TO THE WIRES.
a) Make sure to protect wire bundles when using the trammel trammel bar,
SPL-1677.
2) Make sure that the "B" dimension is 45.48 ±0.10 in. (1155.2 ±2.5 mm).
(k) Retract the trailing edge flaps (TASK 27-51-00-860-804).
1) If it is necessary, retract the leading edge flaps (TASK 27-81-00-800-802 or
TASK 27-81-00-860-804).
(l) Do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805.
SUBTASK 27-41-94-710-007
(3) Do the test of the limit switch S144:
(a) Move the stabilizer to the maximum leading edge down (APL NOSE UP) position.
(b) Turn the captain's stabilizer trim wheel counterclockwise approximately 3 turns.
(c) Move and hold the STAB TRIM switches on the captain's control wheel to the NOSE UP
position.
1) Make sure that the stabilizer leading edge does not move.
2) Release the STAB TRIM switches.
(d) Move and hold the STAB TRIM switches on the captain's control wheel to the NOSE
DOWN position.
1) Make sure that stabilizer leading edge moves up (APL NOSE DOWN).
2) Release the STAB TRIM switches.
(e) Move the stabilizer to approximately 12 units of trim.
(f) Move the STAB TRIM switches on the captain's control wheel to the NOSE UP position
until the stabilizer stops automatically.
1) Use the trammel bar, SPL-1677, to measure the "B" dimension.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU ARE CAREFUL WITH THE WIRE
BUNDLES WHEN YOU USE THE TRAMMEL BAR, SPL-1677.
THE SHARP EDGES ON THE TRAMMEL BAR, SPL-1677 CAN
CAUSE CHAFING OR DAMAGE TO THE WIRES.
a) Make sure to protect wire bundles when using the trammel trammel bar,
SPL-1677.
2) Make sure that the "B" dimension is 24.80 ±0.10 in. (629.9 ±2.6 mm).
SUBTASK 27-41-94-410-003

SUBTASK 27-41-97-020-001

 ALL

is necessary to use this threaded wire for installation.

D. Stabilizer Trim Control Switch Test
SUBTASK 27-41-97-710-001
(1) Do a test of the stabilizer trim control switches on the applicable control wheel:
(a) Push and hold the two stabilizer trim control switches on the applicable control wheel to
the NOSE DOWN position.
1) Make sure the stabilizer leading edge moves up.
2) Make sure the trim wheels turn in the nose down position.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
3) Make sure that the STAB TRIM indicator for the applicable control wheel moves in
the NOSE DOWN position.
4) Release the two stabilizer trim control switches.
(b) Push and hold the two stabilizer trim control switches on the applicable control wheel to
the NOSE UP position.
1) Make sure the stabilizer leading edge moves down.
2) Make sure the trim wheels turn in the nose up position.
3) Make sure that the STAB TRIM indicator for the applicable control wheel moves in
the NOSE UP position.
4) Release the two stabilizer trim control switches.
5) Move the horizontal stabilizer to the neutral position.
(c) Push and hold the left stabilizer trim control switch on the applicable control wheel to the
NOSE UP position.
1) Make sure the stabilizer leading edge does not move.
2) Release the left stabilizer trim control switch.
(d) Push and hold the left stabilizer trim control switch on the applicable control wheel to the
NOSE DOWN position.
1) Make sure the stabilizer leading edge does not move.
2) Release the left stabilizer trim control switch.
(e) Push and hold the right stabilizer trim control switch on the applicable control wheel to the
NOSE UP position.
1) Make sure the stabilizer leading edge does not move.
2) Release the right stabilizer trim control switch.
(f) Push and hold the right stabilizer trim control switch on the applicable control wheel to the
NOSE DOWN position.
1) Make sure the stabilizer leading edge does not move.
2) Release the right stabilizer trim control switch.

(21) Do a test of the high (flaps down) stabilizer trim rate:
(a) Move the stab trim switches on the control wheel to the NOSE UP (stabilizer leading
edge down) position and hold until the stabilizer stops.
(b) Do the following to measure the time it takes for the stabilizer to move from the leading
edge down position to the leading edge up position:
1) Move the stab trim switches on the control wheel to the NOSE DOWN position and
hold until the stabilizer stops.
2) Make sure that the time from the start to stop of stabilizer movement is between 31
and 39 seconds.
SUBTASK 27-41-98-020-014
(22) Do this task: Retract the Trailing Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-804.
SUBTASK 27-41-98-020-015
(23) Move the stabilizer to 4 units of trim, or more.
SUBTASK 27-41-98-700-003
(24) Do a test of the low (flaps up) stabilizer trim rate:
(a) Move the stab trim switches on the control wheel to the NOSE DOWN (stabilizer leading
edge up) position and hold until the stabilizer stops.
(b) Do the following to measure the time it takes for the stabilizer to move from the leading
edge up position to the leading edge down position:
1) Move the stab trim switches on the control wheel to the NOSE UP position and hold
until the stabilizer stops.
2) Make sure that the time from the start to stop of stabilizer movement is between 46
and 56 seconds.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

E. Flap Deactivation
SUBTASK 27-51-00-210-001
(1) Make sure that the ALTERNATE FLAPS ARM switch on the P5 overhead panel is in the OFF
position (Figure 201).
SUBTASK 27-51-00-860-001
(2) Open these circuit breakers and install safety locks:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2
Row Col Number Name
A 7 C00210 FLIGHT CONTROL FLAP SHUTOFF VALVES

SUBTASK 27-51-00-480-005
WARNING
MAKE SURE THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL THE LANDING
GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR CAN
RETRACT AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(3) If the downlock pins are not installed in the nose and main landing gear, do this task: Landing
Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-00-040-001
(4) Deactivate the trailing edge flap bypass valve (Figure 202):
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU PREVENT BENDS OR ABRASION OF THE
WIRES WHEN THE WIRING HARNESS FOR THE BYPASS VALVE IS
DISCONNECTED. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO THE WIRING
HARNESS COULD OCCUR.
(a) Disconnect the electrical connector from the bypass valve.
NOTE: If desired, inspect the connector for corrosion now. If there is corrosion, refer to
SWPM 20-60-03 to correct the problem. This step is also done in the installation
task.
(b) Move the manual override lever on the bypass valve to POSITION 2.
(c) Install the lock, SPL-1676 on the bypass valve.
SUBTASK 27-51-00-210-012
WARNING
KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL
SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE
COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC
POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(5) Trailing Edge Flap System - Tryout
NOTE: This tryout is to make sure that the trailing edge flap system is in zero energy state.
(a) Make sure that the trailing edge flaps do not move using primary flight controls:
1) Move the flap control lever to a minimum of one lever detent position away from the
current position.
2) Make sure that the trailing edge flaps do not move.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
3) Return the flap control lever to the detent position corresponding to the current flap
position.
(b) Make sure that the trailing edge flaps do not move using the alternate flight controls:
1) Set the alternate flaps arm switch to the ARM position.
a) If flaps are in retracted position, set the alternate flaps control switch to DOWN
position.
b) If flaps are in the extended position, set the alternate flaps control switch to UP
position.
2) Make sure that the trailing edge flaps do not move.
3) Return the alternate flaps control switch to OFF, and the alternate flaps arm switch
to OFF.
SUBTASK 27-51-00-420-006
(6) If the flaps are in the retracted position, do this task to install the flap control handle lockout
assembly: Flap Control Handle Lockout Assembly Installation, TASK 27-51-00-400-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-00-480-001
(7) Put DO-NOT-OPERATE tags on the ALTERNATE FLAPS switches.

D. Trailing Edge Flap System Operation With Alternate Control
SUBTASK 27-51-00-860-008
(1) Do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811.
SUBTASK 27-51-00-860-009
WARNING
MOVE ALL PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE TRAILING EDGE
FLAPS, AND THE LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS. THESE SURFACES
WILL MOVE AND CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
WARNING
KEEP PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE AREA AROUND THE
THRUST REVERSERS. THE THRUST REVERSERS EXTEND AND RETRACT
QUICKLY. INJURIES TO PERSONNEL, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN
OCCUR.
WARNING
KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE FLIGHT CONTROL
SURFACES. THE AILERONS, ELEVATORS, RUDDER, FLAPS, SLATS,
SPOILERS, STABILIZER AND NOSE GEAR CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN
YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO
PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
CAUTION
DO NOT OPERATE THE TRAILING EDGE FLAPS WITH ELECTRICAL POWER
MORE THAN ONE FULL EXTEND/RETRACT CYCLE IN 25 MINUTES. YOU
CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE FLAP ELECTRIC MOTORS IF YOU OPERATE
THEM TOO FREQUENTLY.
(2) Move the ALTERNATE FLAPS ARM switch on the P5 panel to arm the alternate control
system.
NOTE: The Standby Hydraulic System activates when the ALTERNATE FLAPS ARM switch is
set to arm. The Standby Hydraulic System also operates the rudder, thrust reversers,
leading edge flaps and slats.
SUBTASK 27-51-00-860-010
(3) Move the flap control lever to the 40-unit position.
NOTE: This will decrease the load on the flap electric (alternate) motor. You can move the
lever past where you will move the flaps to.
NOTE: For ground operations, do not operate the flap electric (alternate) motor for more than
4 minutes on and 25 minutes off. You can cause damage to the electric motor.
SUBTASK 27-51-00-860-011
WARNING
MOVE ALL PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE TRAILING EDGE
FLAPS, AND THE LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS. THESE SURFACES
WILL MOVE AND CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(WARNING PRECEDES)
CAUTION
WAIT A MINIMUM OF 15 SECONDS AFTER THE FLAPS STOP BEFORE YOU
USE THE ALTERNATE SYSTEM TO MOVE THE FLAPS AGAIN. YOU CAN
CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE FLAP ALTERNATE MOTOR.
(4) Move the ALTERNATE FLAPS control switch to UP or DOWN to extend or retract the flaps as
it is necessary.
NOTE: The leading edge flaps and slats will extend with alternate control. To deactivate the
leading edge flaps and slats do this task:Trailing Edge Flap System Operation With
Leading Edge Flaps and Slats Disabled, TASK 27-51-00-860-805
NOTE: The leading edge flaps and slats will not retract with alternate control.
SUBTASK 27-51-00-860-012
(5) Move the ALTERNATE FLAPS control switch to the OFF position.
E. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 27-51-00-860-013
WARNING
MAKE SURE THE POSITION OF THE FLAPS AGREES WITH THE POSITION
OF THE FLAP CONTROL LEVER. WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER,
THE FLAPS AND SLATS WILL MOVE AUTOMATICALLY TO THE POSITION
OF THE FLAP CONTROL LEVER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS
AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(1) Move the ALTERNATE FLAPS control switch until the flaps are in the same position as the flap
control lever or move the flap control lever to the position of the flaps.
SUBTASK 27-51-00-860-014
(2) Move the ALTERNATE FLAPS control switch to the OFF position.
SUBTASK 27-51-00-860-015
(3) Move the ALTERNATE FLAPS ARM switch to the OFF position to disarm the alternate control

9. Trailing Edge Flap System Operation With Leading Edge Flaps and Slats Disabled
(Figure 203, Figure 204, Figure 205)
A. General
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT FOR AIRPLANES WITH THE -1001 CRUISE
DEPRESSURIZATION VALVE, YOU REVIEW THIS WARNING. MAKE SURE
THAT YOU CLOSE THE FAN COWLS AND THRUST REVERSERS IF YOU
MOVE THE TRAILING EDGE FLAPS WHILE THE LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND
SLATS ARE DISCONNECTED. THE -1001 CRUISE DEPRESSURIZATION
CREEP CAN CAUSE MOVEMENT OF THE LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND
SLATS WHEN YOU MOVE THE FLAP CONTROL LEVER. IF YOU DO NOT
OBEY, INJURY TO PERSONNEL OR DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN
OCCUR.
(1) This task gives instructions to operate the Trailing Edge (TE) flap system with the Leading
Edge (LE) flaps and slats retracted and disabled.
(2) You can operate the TE flaps with primary or alternate control or manually after you do the
Prepare to Operate the Trailing Edge Flaps part of this task.
(3) A LE device creep condition has been associated with the -1001 cruise depressurization valve.
It can cause hydraulic pressure leakage through the valve when manually closed.
(a) This cruise depressurization creep condition can permit movement of the deactivated LE
flaps and slats when the TE flaps are moved.
(b) The redesigned -1003 cruise depressurization valve is not susceptible to this creep
condition.

E. Operational Test of the Trailing Edge Flap System
SUBTASK 27-51-00-710-001
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE LE
AND TE FLAPS AND FLAP-DRIVE MECHANISMS. THE FLAPS CAN CAUSE
INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE INBOARD FAN COWL PANEL AND THE INBOARD
AND OUTBOARD THRUST REVERSERS ARE CLOSED AND IN THE
STOWED POSITION OR REMOVED BEFORE YOU EXTEND THE LEADING
EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS. THERE IS NOT SUFFICIENT CLEARANCE FOR
THE FLAPS AND SLATS TO EXTEND IF THE INBOARD FAN COWL PANEL
AND THE INBOARD AND OUTBOARD THRUST REVERSERS ARE IN THE
OPEN POSITION. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(1) Do a test of the hydraulic operation of the flaps:
NOTE: Use the flap position indicator to find the position of the flaps.
(a) Move the flap control lever to the UP position and wait for the flaps to reach the UP
position.
(b) Make sure that the pointers on the flap position indicator are in the UP white band.
(c) Move the flap control lever to the 10-unit position and wait for the flaps to stop.
(d) Make sure that the pointers on the flap position indicator are in the 10-unit white band.
(e) Move the flap control lever to the 40-unit position and wait for the flaps to stop.
(f) Make sure that the pointers on the flap position indicator are in the 40-unit white band.
(g) Move the flap control lever to the UP position and wait for the flaps to reach the UP
position.
(h) Make sure that the pointers on the flap position indicator are in the UP white band.
SUBTASK 27-51-00-710-002
(2) Do a test of the alternate operation of the flaps:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
CAUTION
DO NOT OPERATE THE TRAILING EDGE FLAPS WITH ELECTRICAL
POWER MORE THAN ONE FULL EXTEND/RETRACT CYCLE IN 25
MINUTES. YOU CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE FLAP ELECTRIC
MOTORS IF YOU OPERATE THEM TOO FREQUENTLY.
(a) Move the ALTERNATE FLAPS ARM switch to the ARM position.
NOTE: The standby hydraulic pump motor will operate when the ALTERNATE FLAPS
ARM switch is in the ARM position.
CAUTION
DO NOT CONTINUOUSLY OPERATE THE FLAP ELECTRIC MOTOR FOR
MORE THAN 4 MINUTES. YOU MUST WAIT A MINIMUM OF 25 MINUTES
BETWEEN OPERATIONS OF THE FLAP ELECTRIC MOTOR. IF YOU DO
NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(b) Move the flap control lever to the 40-unit position.
NOTE: This will reduce the load on the flap electric (alternate) motor.
1) Make sure that the flaps do not move.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE INBOARD FAN COWL PANEL AND THE
INBOARD AND OUTBOARD THRUST REVERSERS ARE CLOSED AND IN
THE STOWED POSITION OR REMOVED BEFORE YOU EXTEND THE
LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS. THERE IS NOT SUFFICIENT
CLEARANCE FOR THE FLAPS AND SLATS TO EXTEND IF THE
INBOARD FAN COWL PANEL AND THE INBOARD AND OUTBOARD
THRUST REVERSERS ARE IN THE OPEN POSITION. THIS CAN CAUSE
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
CAUTION
WAIT A MINIMUM OF 15 SECONDS AFTER THE FLAPS STOP BEFORE
YOU USE THE ALTERNATE SYSTEM TO MOVE THE FLAPS AGAIN. YOU
CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE FLAP ALTERNATE MOTOR.
(c) Move the ALTERNATE FLAPS CONTROL switch to the DOWN position and hold it until
the trailing edge flaps stop.
NOTE: The flap extension is controlled by a limit switch.
(d) Make sure that the pointers on the flap position indicator are in the 40-unit white band.
(e) Move the ALTERNATE FLAPS CONTROL switch to the UP position.
NOTE: The flap retraction is controlled by a limit switch.
(f) Make sure that the pointers on the flap position indicator are in the UP white band.
(g) Move the flap control lever to the UP position.
(h) Move the ALTERNATE FLAPS CONTROL switch to the OFF position.
(i) Move the ALTERNATE FLAPS ARM switch to the OFF position.
(j) Move the flap control lever to the 10-unit position and wait for the flaps to stop.
(k) Make sure that the pointers on the flap position indicator are in the 10-unit white band.
(l) Move the flap control lever to the UP position and wait for the flaps to reach the UP
position.
(m) Make sure the pointers on the flap position indicator are in the UP white band.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

27-51-00-820-801Trailing Edge Flap Control System Adjustment and TestPDF p. 1978
3. Trailing Edge Flap Control System Adjustment and Test
(Figure 502)
A. General
(1) This task does an adjustment of the trailing edge flap control system.
(a) The trailing edge flap control system includes the flap control lever, the flap control unit,
the flap control valve, the control cables WFA and WFB, and the follow-up cables WFFA
and WFFB.
(2) It is recommended that airplanes supplied with the cables that contain higher zinc coating
(Grade D or Grade K) be re-tensioned 3 to 4 months into service. This will bring the tension of
the control cables within the desired range. After the cables are re-tensioned the high zinc
cables (Grade D or Grade K) will continue to relax at a rate that is equivalent to the Grade B
cables.
(3) It is recommended that cable assemblies on each side of a cable loop be replaced at the same
time using the same cable grade of material in order to minimize asymmetric relaxation.
(4) When you retract the trailing edge flaps with hydraulic power, it is necessary to stop for two
minutes after you move the flaps. The flaps can move a small distance for 2 minutes after
extension or retraction.
(5) The adjustment instructions included in this task are included in the Flap Actuation Rigging
Instructions drawing 256A3001.

CAUTION
