(1) If the flap drive system is not adjusted correctly, disconnect the torque tubes [18] from the
power drive unit [17]:
(a) Install clamp set, SPL-1726, on the torque tubes [18] on each side of the power drive
unit [17], see Figure 503:
NOTE: The clamp set can be used to stop inadvertent movement of the flap drive
system while the torque tubes are disconnected. If the flap drive system moves,
then it will be necessary to do the flap drive system adjustment.
1) Put the clamp assembly in its location on the applicable torque tube.
2) Turn the knob to tighten the clamp assembly on the torque tube.
3) Turn the rod until it touches the structure to make sure the clamp assembly does not
turn.
(b) Remove lockwire or safety cable from the screws [14].
(c) Remove the screws [14] that attach the coupling sleeves [15] to the splined
couplings [16].
(d) Move the coupling sleeves [15] off the splined couplings [16].
(e) Move the torque tubes [18] away from the flap power drive unit [17].

SUBTASK 27-51-00-820-001
(4) Do the adjustment of the flap control lever [7] and cable assemblies [1] WFA and WFB:
(a) Put the flap control lever [7] in the rigged position:
1) Move the flap control lever [7] aft until the detent pin is out of the UP detent.
2) Put a 0.19 in. (4.83 mm) thick rigging block between the detent pin on the flap
control lever [7] and upstop on the detent plate.
a) Make sure that the rigging block does not go into the flaps UP detent.
(b) Install a clamp to hold the quadrant [6] against the aft side of the stop [5] on the flap
control unit [4].
(c) Remove the clips [2] from the turnbuckles [3] on the cable assemblies [1] WFA and WFB.
(d) If you installed a new cable assembly [1], do these steps:
1) Use the turnbuckles [3] to adjust the tension in the cable assemblies [1] to
275 ±15 lbf (1.22 ±0.07 kN).
2) Remove the clamp from the quadrant [6].
3) Remove the rigging block from the flap control lever [7].
4) Move the flap control lever [7] through its full travel 25 times.
5) Put the flap control lever [7] in the rigged position with the rigging block.
6) Install the clamp to hold the quadrant [6] against the aft side of the stop [5] on the
flap control unit [4].
(e) Use the turnbuckles [3] to adjust the tension in the cable assemblies [1] WFA and WFB to
the limit shown in (Table 501).
NOTE: Adjust the tensions close to the maximum values in the table. The cables will
stretch over a period of time.
NOTE: During the adjustment, make sure the tension in the cable assemblies [1] is
never less than 50 lbf (0.22 kN).
NOTE: To make sure the tension is correct, the temperature of the airframe must be
constant in the limit of ±5 degrees for a minimum of one hour.
(f) Remove the clamp from the quadrant [6].
(g) Remove the rigging block from the flap control lever [7].
(h) Move the flap control lever [7] through its full travel a minimum of 5 times. Stop with the
flap control lever [7] in the 1-unit position.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(i) Carefully move the flap control lever [7] forward until you feel resistance.
(j) Measure the distance between the detent pin on the flap control lever [7] and the upstop
on the detent plate.
(k) If the distance is not in the limit of 0.19 in. (4.83 mm), then adjust the cable assembly [1]
and flap control lever [7] again.
(l) Install the clips [2] on the turnbuckles [3].

nut [33] is less than 0.94 in. (23.88 mm).

adjustable sleeve [31] is less than 0.19 in. (4.83 mm).

degrees (±0.25 inch) (±6.3 millimeters) from the upstop on the ballscrew yoke.
SUBTASK 27-51-00-820-008
(17) If you cannot install the rig pin [27], or if the ballscrew nuts are not in the correct position, then
do a final adjustment of the trailing edge flap control valve [19]:
NOTE: It can be necessary to adjust the trailing edge flap control valve [19] more than once to
get it to the correct position.
(a) Loosen the nut [30] and nut [33] on the adjustable sleeve [31].
CAUTION
ADJUST THE FLAP CONTROL VALVE A SMALL DISTANCE AT A TIME. IF
YOU ADJUST THE FLAP CONTROL VALVE TOO FAR, THE BALLSCREW
NUTS CAN HIT THE UPSTOPS. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(b) Turn the adjustable sleeve [31] to change the position of the valve slide [29].
NOTE: If the flaps did not retract far enough, adjust the valve slide [29] to be further out
of the trailing edge flap control valve [19]. If the flaps retracted too far, adjust the
valve slide [29] to be further in the trailing edge flap control valve [19].
(c) Tighten the nut [30] and nut [33] on the adjustable sleeve [31].
NOTE: Make sure the distance between the center of the rod end [24] and the nut [33] is
less than 0.94 in. (23.88 mm). Make sure the distance between the nut [30] and
the hex on the adjustable sleeve [31] is less than 0.19 in. (4.83 mm).
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU REMOVE THE HYDRAULIC POWER BEFORE
YOU DISCONNECT THE ROD END FROM THE SUMMING LEVER. IF
YOU DISCONNECT THE ROD END WITH HYDRAULIC POWER ON, YOU
CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE FLAP CONTROL UNIT.
(d) If it is necessary, disconnect the rod end [24] from the summing lever [20]:
NOTE: It is necessary to disconnect the rod end [24] if you cannot adjust the valve
slide [29] enough to get the flaps in the correct position.
1) Remove the nut [23], washer [22], and bolt [21] that attach the rod end [24] to the
summing lever [20].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
2) Change the position of the adjustable sleeve [31].
3) Install the bolt [21], washer [22], and nut [23] to attach the rod end [24] to the
summing lever [20].
(e) Tighten the nut [30] and nut [33].
WARNING
KEEP PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT
CONTROL SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING
GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU
SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO
PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(f) Supply system B hydraulic power, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization,
TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
(g) Use the primary system to fully extend and retract the trailing edge flaps a minimum of
five times.
1) To extend and retract the flaps, do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Operation
With Primary Control, TASK 27-51-00-860-801.
(h) Remove system B hydraulic power, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power
Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805.
(i) Make sure that you can install the rig pin [27] in the flap control unit [4].
(j) Make sure that the ballscrew nuts for transmission No. 4 and No. 5 are 1/2 turn ±10
degrees (±0.25 inch) (±6.3 millimeters) from the upstop on the ballscrew yoke.
SUBTASK 27-51-00-420-003
(18) Install lockwire on the nut [30], nut [33], and adjustable sleeve [31].

4. Trailing Edge Flap Drive System Adjustment
(Figure 504)
A. General
(1) This task does a check of the adjustment and an adjustment of the trailing edge flap drive
system. The procedure to adjust the inboard flaps is in TASK 27-51-11-820-801. The
procedure to adjust the outboard flaps is in TASK 27-51-21-820-801.
(a) The trailing edge flap drive system includes the flap transmissions, angle gearboxes,
torque tubes, and the flap power drive unit.

(3) Manually extend the flaps until the ballscrew nuts touch the downstops on the ballscrews.
(a) If the torque tubes are not connected to the flap power drive unit, manually extend the

1) If all of the torque tubes on the wing are connected, use a coupling sleeve wrench,
SPL-5384, on the torque tube couplings inboard of the tee-angle gearbox.
CAUTION
DO NOT MOVE ONE END OF A FLAP MORE THAN 1.4 INCHES (35.5
MILLIMETERS) OF BALLSCREW TRAVEL MORE THAN THE OTHER
END. YOU CAN CAUSE THE FLAP TO SKEW TO MUCH. THIS CAN
CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE FLAP.
2) If all of the torque tubes on the wing are not connected, use a coupling sleeve
wrench, SPL-5384, to drive each flap independently.
(b) If the torque tubes are connected to the flap power drive unit, and all of the torque tubes

Trailing Edge Flap System Manual Operation, TASK 27-51-00-980-801.

SUBTASK 27-51-00-220-001
(4) Do a check of the adjustment of the flap drive system on each wing.
NOTE: If all of the torque tubes on the wing are not connected, it is not necessary to do this
check.
(a) At all of the transmissions, measure and record the dimension from the downstop on the
ballscrew nut to the downstop on the ballscrew.
NOTE: This dimension is referred to as Dimension Y.
(b) Make sure that the Dimension Y for the transmission No. 4 and transmission No. 5 are in
these limits:
1) If the torque tubes are connected between the wings, Dimension Y must be 0.0 (the
ballscrew nut touches the downstop) for one transmission and in the limit of 0.0 in.
(0.00 mm) to 0.1 in. (2.54 mm) for the other transmission.
2) If the torque tubes are not connected between the wings, Dimension Y must be 0.0
(the ballscrew nut touches the downstop) for the two transmission.
(c) On the left wing flap drive system:
1) Make sure that the Dimension Y for transmissions No. 1 and No. 3 are in the limit of
0.0 in. (0.00 mm) to 0.2 in. (5.08 mm) more than Dimension Y at transmission No. 4.
2) Make sure that the Dimension Y for transmission No. 2 is in the limit of 0.0 in.
(0.00 mm) to 0.22 in. (5.59 mm) more than Dimension Y at transmission No. 1.
(d) On the right wing flap drive system:
1) Make sure that the Dimension Y for transmissions No. 6 and No. 8 are in the limit of
0.0 in. (0.00 mm) to 0.2 in. (5.08 mm) more than Dimension Y at transmission No. 5.
2) Make sure that the Dimension Y for transmission No. 7 is in the limit of 0.0 in.
(0.00 mm) to 0.22 in. (5.59 mm) more than Dimension Y at transmission No. 8.

system adjustment.
G. Trailing Edge Flap Drive System Adjustment
SUBTASK 27-51-00-020-003
(1) For the flap position transmitters on the left and right wings, do this task: Flap Position
Transmitter Removal, TASK 27-58-01-000-801.
NOTE: If you do not remove the flap position transmitters before you disconnect the torque
tubes, they will become incorrectly adjusted.
SUBTASK 27-51-00-020-004
(2) Disconnect the torque tubes [18] from the flap power drive unit [17] (Figure 502).
NOTE: This will disconnect the flap drive system for the left wing from the right wing. It is
necessary to adjust the left and the right wings independently, then connect them
together.
(a) Remove lockwire or safety cable from the screws [14].
(b) Remove the screws [14] that attach the coupling sleeves [15] to the splined
couplings [16].
(c) Move the coupling sleeves [15] off the splined couplings [16].
(d) Move the torque tubes [18] away from the flap power drive unit [17].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-51-00-020-005
(3) Disconnect the torque tube from the inboard side of transmission No. 2 or transmission No. 7
(Figure 504).
NOTE: This will disconnect the flap drive system for the outboard flaps from the inboard flaps.
(a) Remove lockwire or safety cable from the screws [14].
(b) Remove the screws [14] that attach the coupling sleeves [15] to the splined
couplings [16].
(c) Move the coupling sleeves [15] off the splined couplings [16].
(d) Move the torque tubes away from the transmission.
SUBTASK 27-51-00-820-010
(4) Adjust the flap drive system for the outboard flap.
NOTE: This procedure is applicable to the drive system for the outboard flap on the left wing
and the right wing.
CAUTION
DO NOT MOVE ONE END OF A FLAP MORE THAN 1.4 INCHES (35.5
MILLIMETERS) OF BALLSCREW TRAVEL MORE THAN THE OTHER
END. YOU CAN CAUSE THE FLAP TO SKEW TO MUCH. THIS CAN
CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE FLAP.
(a) Use a coupling sleeve wrench, SPL-5384, on the coupling on the inboard side of
transmission No. 2 to extend the outboard flap until one of the ballscrew nuts touch the
downstop on the ballscrew.
(b) Make sure that the ballscrew nut at transmission No. 1 touches the downstop (Dimension
Y = 0).
(c) Make sure that the Dimension Y for transmission No. 2 is in the limit of 0.0 in. (0.00 mm)
to 0.2 in. (5.08 mm).
(d) If the ballscrew nuts for transmissions No. 1 and No. 2 are not in the limits, adjust the
drive system for the outboard flap.
1) Disconnect the torque tubes between transmissions No. 1 and No. 2.
a) Remove lockwire or safety cable from the screws [14].
b) Remove the screws [14] that attach the coupling sleeves [15] to the splined
couplings [16].
c) Move the coupling sleeve [15] off the splined coupling [16].
d) Move the torque tube away from the transmission.
2) Manually extend the transmissions until the ballscrew nuts for transmissions No. 1
and transmission No. 2 touch the downstops.
3) Connect the torque tubes between the transmissions No. 1 and No. 2.
NOTE: To align the torque tube couplings, you can retract the transmission No. 2 a
maximum of 1/3 of a torque tube turn.
a) Apply grease, D00633, to the coupling sleeve [15].
b) Put the splined coupling [16] in the coupling sleeve [15].
c) Install the screws [14] to attach the torque tube to the transmission.
d) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G50347, or safety cable kit, G51490, on the
screw [14] (PAGEBLOCK 20-10-44/401).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-51-00-820-011
(5) Adjust the flap drive system for the inboard flap.
NOTE: This procedure is applicable to the drive system for the inboard flap on the left wing
and the right wing.
CAUTION
DO NOT MOVE ONE END OF A FLAP MORE THAN 1.4 INCHES (35.5
MILLIMETERS) OF BALLSCREW TRAVEL MORE THAN THE OTHER
END. YOU CAN CAUSE THE FLAP TO SKEW TO MUCH. THIS CAN
CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE FLAP.
(a) Use a coupling sleeve wrench, SPL-5384, on the coupling on the inboard side of
transmission No. 4 to extend the inboard flap until one of the ballscrew nuts touch the
downstop on the ballscrew.
(b) Make sure that the ballscrew nut at transmission No. 4 touches the downstop (Dimension
Y = 0).
(c) Make sure that the Dimension Y for transmission No. 3 is in the limit of 0.0 in. (0.00 mm)
to 0.18 in. (4.57 mm).
(d) If the ballscrew nuts for transmissions No. 3 and No. 4 are not in the limits, adjust the
drive system for the inboard flap.
1) Disconnect the torque tubes between transmissions No. 3 and No. 4.
a) Remove lockwire or safety cable from the screws [14].
b) Remove the screws [14] that attach the coupling sleeve [15] to the splined
coupling [16].
c) Move the coupling sleeve [15] off the splined coupling [16].
d) Move the torque tube away from the transmission.
2) Manually extend the transmissions until the ballscrew nuts for transmissions No. 3
and transmission No. 4 touch the downstops.
3) Connect the torque tubes between the transmissions No. 3 and No. 4.
NOTE: To align the torque tube couplings, you can retract the transmission No. 3 a
maximum of 1/3 of a torque tube turn.
a) Apply grease, D00633, to the coupling sleeve [15].
b) Put the splined coupling [16] in the coupling sleeve [15].
c) Install the screws [14] to attach the torque tube to the transmission.
d) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G50347, or safety cable kit, G51490, on the
screws [14] (PAGEBLOCK 20-10-44/401).

(b) Make sure that the Dimension Y for transmission No. 2 is in the limit of 0.0 in. (0.00 mm)

(c) Make sure that the Dimension Y for transmission No. 3 is in the limit of 0.0 in. (0.00 mm)
to 0.18 in. (4.57 mm).

 ALL

2) Put the splined coupling [16] in the coupling sleeve [15].
3) Install the screws [14] to attach the torque tube to the transmission.
4) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G50347, or safety cable kit, G51490, on the
screws [14] (PAGEBLOCK 20-10-44/401).

27-51-00-730-801Trailing Edge Flap System TestPDF p. 2014
5. Trailing Edge Flap System Test
(Figure 501)
A. General
(1) This task does a functional test of the trailing edge flap system. This task includes these parts:
(a) A test of the FSEU display and a check of existing faults
(b) A test of the asymmetry and skew systems
(c) A test of the load relief system
(d) A test of the primary operation
(e) A test of the power supply for the ALTERNATE FLAPS switches and the bypass valve
(f) A test of the power supply for the flap electric motor
(g) A test of the UP limit switch
(h) A test of the DOWN limit switch
(i) A test of the flap priority valve
(j) A test of the force required to move the flap control lever.

SUBTASK 27-51-00-720-026
(1) Put the Flap Control Lever between UP and 1 detent.
SUBTASK 27-51-00-720-027
(2) Lift up and move the Flap Control Lever forward to the UP detent.
SUBTASK 27-51-00-720-028
(3) Stow the Flap Control Lever from the lifted position into the UP detent.
(a) Make sure that axial movement is in the bottom direction
(b) Make sure that it is put at the bottom of the detent
(c) Make sure that the Lever goes into the stand smoothly.
NOTE: There will be some permitted resistance because of the cable load in the UP detent.
SUBTASK 27-51-00-720-029
(4) Move the Flap Control Lever from the UP detent.
(a) Make sure that axial movement is in the up direction.
SUBTASK 27-51-00-720-030
(5) Make sure that the Flap Control Lever is smooth when moved in the up direction.
NOTE: There will be some permitted resistance because of the cable load in the UP detent.
SUBTASK 27-51-00-720-031
(6) Stow and attach safely the Flap Control Lever back into the UP detent to complete the test.

 ALL

F. Procedure
SUBTASK 27-51-00-860-051
CAUTION
DO NOT OPERATE THE TRAILING EDGE FLAPS WITH ELECTRICAL POWER
MORE THAN ONE FULL EXTEND/RETRACT CYCLE IN 25 MINUTES. YOU
CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE FLAP ELECTRIC MOTORS IF YOU OPERATE
THEM TOO FREQUENTLY.
(1) Move the ALTERNATE FLAPS ARM switch to the ARM position.
NOTE: The standby hydraulic pump motor will operate when the ALTERNATE FLAPS ARM
switch is in the ARM position.
SUBTASK 27-51-00-860-052
CAUTION
DO NOT CONTINUOUSLY OPERATE THE FLAP ELECTRIC MOTOR FOR
MORE THAN 4 MINUTES. YOU MUST WAIT A MINIMUM OF 25 MINUTES
BETWEEN OPERATIONS OF THE FLAP ELECTRIC MOTOR. IF YOU DO NOT
OBEY, DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(2) Move the flap control lever to the 40-unit position.
NOTE: This will decrease the load on the flap electric motor.
(a) Make sure the flaps do not extend.
SUBTASK 27-51-00-710-005
CAUTION
WAIT A MINIMUM OF 15 SECONDS AFTER THE FLAPS STOP BEFORE YOU
USE THE ALTERNATE SYSTEM TO MOVE THE FLAPS AGAIN. YOU CAN
CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE FLAP ALTERNATE MOTOR.
(3) Hold the ALTERNATE FLAPS CONTROL switch in the DOWN position until the trailing edge
flaps stop.
NOTE: The leading edge flaps and slats will extend when you move the switch to the DOWN
position. The trailing edge flap extension is controlled by a limit switch.
(a) Make sure the pointers on the flap position indicator are in the 40-unit white band.
(4) Release the ALTERNATE FLAPS CONTROL switch to let it move to the OFF position.
SUBTASK 27-51-00-710-006
(5) Move the ALTERNATE FLAPS CONTROL switch to the UP position until the trailing edge flaps
stop.
NOTE: The flap retraction is controlled by a limit switch.
(a) Make sure the pointers on the flap position indicator are in the UP white band.
SUBTASK 27-51-00-860-084
(6) Move the flap control lever to the UP position.
SUBTASK 27-51-00-860-054
(7) Move the ALTERNATE FLAPS ARM switch to the OFF position.
NOTE: The leading edge flaps and slats will retract.
SUBTASK 27-51-00-710-007
(8) Move the ALTERNATE FLAPS ARM switch to the ARM position.
SUBTASK 27-51-00-860-055
(9) Move the flap control lever to the 1-unit position.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Make sure the flaps do not move.
(10) Hold the ALTERNATE FLAPS CONTROL switch in the DOWN position until the trailing edge
flaps are in the 1-unit position.
NOTE: The leading edge flaps and slats will extend.
(11) Release the ALTERNATE FLAPS CONTROL switch to the OFF position.
(12) Move the ALTERNATE FLAPS ARM switch to the OFF position.
SUBTASK 27-51-00-720-012
(13) Do a test of the time necessary to retract the trailing edge flaps from the 1-unit position:
(a) Move the ALTERNATE FLAPS ARM switch to the ARM position.
(b) Use a stopwatch, STD-1139 to measure the time necessary to retract the flaps to the UP
position.
(c) Move the ALTERNATE FLAPS CONTROL switch to the UP position until the trailing edge
flaps stop.
NOTE: The flap retraction is controlled by a limit switch.
(d) Make sure the time it takes for the flaps to move from the 1-unit position to the retracted
position is 47 to 58 seconds.
NOTE: The leading edge flaps and slats will retract.
(e) Move the ALTERNATE FLAPS CONTROL switch to the OFF position.
(f) Move the flap control lever to the UP position.
(g) Move the ALTERNATE FLAPS ARM switch to the OFF position.
G. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 27-51-00-860-074
WARNING

AND TE FLAPS AND FLAP DRIVE MECHANISMS. THE FLAPS CAN CAUSE
INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(1) Retract the flaps to the UP position, do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Operation With

SUBTASK 27-51-00-710-008
(2) Do a test of the no-back brake in the transmissions:
(a) Put a stethoscope, COM-1797, on the applicable transmission to listen for a ratchet
sound.

for a stethoscope.
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE LE
AND TE FLAPS AND FLAP DRIVE MECHANISMS. THE FLAPS CAN
CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(b) Extend the flaps to the 15 unit position and listen for a ratchet sound from the
transmissions, do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Operation With Primary Control,
TASK 27-51-00-860-801.
NOTE: The ratchet sound is the no-back brake inside the transmission. It is necessary to
do the test again for the additional transmissions, or have additional people listen
to the transmissions.
(c) If the ratchet sound cannot be heard on the outboard flaps transmission, install test
equipment, SPL-12536, and perform the test again.

 ALL

position, do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Operation With Primary Control,

1) For the inboard transmission replacement do this task: INBOARD FLAP
TRANSMISSIONS - REMOVAL/INSTALLATION, PAGEBLOCK 27-51-31/401.
2) For the outboard transmission replacement do this task: OUTBOARD FLAP
TRANSMISSIONS - REMOVAL/INSTALLATION, PAGEBLOCK 27-51-41/401.

SUBTASK 27-51-00-740-009
(1) Push the ON/OFF button on the front panel of the FSEU to turn on the display.

SUBTASK 27-51-00-740-012
WARNING
KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL
SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE
COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC

EQUIPMENT.
(2) Do the Built-In-Test Equipment (BITE) test of the load relief system:
(a) Push the down arrow until GROUND TESTS? shows on the display.
(b) Push the YES button to select GROUND TESTS? on the FSEU.
(c) Push the down arrow until TE FLAP LD REL? shows on the display.
(d) Push the YES button to select TE FLAP LD REL? from the menu.

that they be in a different position.

F. Outboard Flap Inspection
(Figure 602)
SUBTASK 27-51-00-010-013
(1) At the flap supports, remove the leading edge skin panel [2] from the main flap [1] forward of
the carriage:
(a) Remove the bolts [3] that attach the leading edge skin panel [2].
(b) Remove the leading edge skin panel [2] from the main flap [1].
Open these access panels:
Number Name/Location
567BT Flap, Forward Carriage Bearing And Fitting
567ET Flap, Forward Carriage Bearing And Fitting
667BT Flap, Forward Carriage Bearing And Fitting
667ET Flap, Forward Carriage Bearing And Fitting
SUBTASK 27-51-00-210-004
(2) Do a detailed visual inspection of these items at the flap supports:
NOTE: These are flap supports No. 1, 2, 7 and 8.
(a) Aft flap drive rod, push rod and bellcrank
NOTE: Some freeplay in the bellcrank is acceptable.
(b) Carriage rollers
(c) Aft link and fittings
(d) Forward carriage bearing and fitting.
SUBTASK 27-51-00-210-005
(3) Do a detailed visual inspection of the deflection control rollers between the inboard and
outboard flaps and at the outboard end of the outboard flap.
SUBTASK 27-51-00-210-006
(4) At the outboard aft flap, do a detailed visual inspection of these items:
(a) Aft flap track attachments.
NOTE: There are four aft flap tracks on the outboard flap.
(b) Inboard and outboard programming rollers.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(c) Inboard and outboard aft flap pushrods.
(d) Rubstrips common to the aft flap support tracks, and common to the inboard and
outboard edge program tracks.
(e) Inboard and outboard aft flap track rollers.
SUBTASK 27-51-00-410-012
(5) Install the leading edge skin panel [2] on the main flap [1] forward of the carriage:
(a) Close these access panels:
Number Name/Location
567BT Flap, Forward Carriage Bearing And Fitting
567ET Flap, Forward Carriage Bearing And Fitting
667BT Flap, Forward Carriage Bearing And Fitting
667ET Flap, Forward Carriage Bearing And Fitting
(b) Put the leading edge skin panel [2] in its location on the leading edge of the main flap [1].
(c) Apply compound, C00528 to the holes for the bolts [3].
(d) Install the bolts [3] to attach the leading edge skin panel [2].
(e) Apply sealant, A00247 to fill all of the clearances around the leading edge skin panel [2]
that are more than 0.05 inch (1.27 millimeters).
G. Inboard Flap Inspection
(Figure 603)
SUBTASK 27-51-00-210-007
(1) At the outboard flap support for the inboard flap, do a detailed visual inspection of these items:
NOTE: These are flap supports No. 3 and 6.
(a) Aft flap drive rod and crankshaft
(b) Carriage rollers
SUBTASK 27-51-00-210-008
(2) At the inboard flap support for the inboard flap, do a detailed visual inspection of these items:
NOTE: These are flap supports No. 4 and 5.
(a) Carriage rollers
SUBTASK 27-51-00-210-009
(3) At the inboard aft flap, do a detailed visual inspection of these items:
(a) Aft flap track attachments.
NOTE: There are two aft flap tracks on the inboard flap.
(b) Inboard and outboard programming rollers.
(c) Inboard and outboard aft flap pushrods.
(d) Rubstrips common to the aft flap support tracks, and common to the inboard and
outboard edge program tracks.
(e) Inboard and outboard aft flap track rollers.
SUBTASK 27-51-00-440-006
(4) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Reactivation, TASK 27-51-00-440-801.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-51-00-010-014
(5) Retract the trailing edge flaps to the retracted position. To retract the flaps, do this task: Retract
the Trailing Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-804.

E. Trailing Edge Flap Bypass Valve Assembly Removal
SUBTASK 27-51-02-020-001
(1) Disconnect the electrical connector [5] from the bypass valve assembly [4].
NOTE: If desired, inspect the connector for corrosion now. If there is corrosion, refer to SWPM
20-60-03 to correct the problem. This step is also done in the installation task.
SUBTASK 27-51-02-020-002
(2) Disconnect the hydraulic lines [1] from the bypass valve assembly [4]:
(a) Put a container below the bypass valve assembly [4] to hold the hydraulic fluid.
(b) Disconnect the hydraulic lines [1] from the bypass valve assembly [4].
(c) Install caps on the hydraulic lines [1] and plugs in the hydraulic ports.
SUBTASK 27-51-02-020-003
(3) Remove the flap bypass valve assembly [4]:
(a) Remove the bolts [6] and washers [7] that attach the bypass valve assembly [4] to the
bracket [2].
(b) Remove the bypass valve assembly [4] from the bracket [2].
SUBTASK 27-51-02-020-004
(4) If you will install a new bypass valve assembly [4], remove the unions [13] and packings [14]
from the bypass valve assembly [4].

SUBTASK 27-51-02-860-007
(1) Make sure that this circuit breaker is open:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2
Row Col Number Name
A 7 C00210 FLIGHT CONTROL FLAP SHUTOFF VALVES
SUBTASK 27-51-02-420-001
(2) If they are not installed, install the unions [13] in the bypass valve assembly [4]:
(a) Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054 or fluid, D00070 to the new packings [14].
(b) Put the packings [14] and the unions [13] in their location on the bypass valve
assembly [4].
SUBTASK 27-51-02-420-002
(3) Install the bypass valve assembly [4]:
(a) Make sure the mating surface of the bypass valve assembly [4] and the bracket [2] are
clean for electrical bonding.
(b) Put the bypass valve assembly [4] in its position on the bracket [2].
(c) Install the bolts [6] and washers [7] to attach the bypass valve assembly [4] to the
bracket [2].
(d) With the electrical bonding intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550, make
sure the bonding resistance between the bypass valve assembly [4] and the bracket [2] is
less than 0.0025 ohm.
SUBTASK 27-51-02-420-003
(4) Connect the hydraulic lines [1] to the bypass valve assembly [4]:
(a) Remove the caps from the hydraulic lines [1] and the plugs from the ports.
(b) Connect the hydraulic lines [1] to the bypass valve assembly [4].

 ALL
(c) Tighten the B-nuts on the hydraulic lines [1] to 500 ±25 in-lb (56 ±3 N·m).

WARNING
DO THE STEPS BELOW IF THE AIRPLANE OPERATES AT AIRPORTS
WHERE DEICING FLUID IS USED. ALSO DO THE STEPS FOR ALL
AIRPLANES THAT YOU FOUND CORROSION IN THE ELECTRICAL

WARNING

D. Trailing Edge Flap Bypass Valve Functional Test
SUBTASK 27-51-02-740-001
(1) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap Asymmetry Skew System BITE Test, TASK 27-51-00-740-802.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-51-02-720-001
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE LE
AND TE FLAPS AND FLAP DRIVE MECHANISMS. THE FLAPS CAN CAUSE
INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(2) Do a test of the operational speed of the trailing edge flaps:
(a) Move the flap control lever to the UP position and wait for the flaps to reach the UP
position.
(b) Measure the time it takes for the trailing edge flaps to extend from the UP position to the
1-unit position:
1) Move the flap control lever to the 1-unit position to extend the flaps.
2) Make sure the time it takes for the flaps to extend to the 1-unit position is 11 to 14
seconds.
NOTE: If you will use the system B EMDP only, the extension time will be 34 to 39
seconds.
(c) Measure the time it takes for the trailing edge flaps to retract from the 1-unit position to
the UP position:
1) Move the flap control lever to the UP position to retract the flaps.
2) Make sure the time it takes for the flaps to retract to the UP position is 11 to 14
seconds.
NOTE: If you will use the system B EMDP only, the retraction time will be 34 to 39
seconds.
SUBTASK 27-51-02-720-002
(3) Do a test of the operation of the bypass valve while the trailing edge flaps are moving:
NOTE: It is necessary to do the following two steps within approximately 10 seconds. The
flaps must still be extending when you do the second step.
(a) Move the flap control lever to the 1-unit position.
(b) While the trailing edge flaps are extending, move the ALTERNATE FLAPS ARM switch to
the ARM position.
(c) Make sure the flaps stop extending when you move the ARM switch.
SUBTASK 27-51-02-720-003
(4) Move the flap control lever to the UP position.
(a) Make sure the flaps do not move.
SUBTASK 27-51-02-720-004
(5) Put the ALTERNATE FLAPS ARM switch in the OFF position.
(a) Make sure the flaps retract to the retracted position.

WARNING
USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COR￾BAN 27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH

(a) Apply Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (preferred), or corrosion inhibiting material,

(h) Connect the flap flow limiter [6] to the flap priority valve [1].
(i) Tighten the nut of the flap flow limiter [6] to 900 ±45 in-lb (101.7 ±5.1 N·m).

C. Flap Control Lever Position Sensor Removal
SUBTASK 27-51-06-020-005
(1) Disconnect the electrical connector [9] for the flap control lever position sensor [20].
SUBTASK 27-51-06-020-006
(2) Remove the flap control lever position sensor assembly [2]:
NOTE: The position sensor assembly [2] includes the position sensor [20], bracket
assembly [23], bracket [24] and the crank [18].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Remove the bolt [15], washers [16] and clamp [14] that attach the wire for the electrical
connector [9].
(b) Remove the bolts [11], washers [12], nuts [13] and clamps [10] that attach the wire for the
electrical connector [9].
(c) Remove the bolt [22] and nut [21] that attach the link [17] to the crank [18].
(d) Remove the screws [19] that attach the flap control lever position sensor assembly [2] to
the control stand [7].
SUBTASK 27-51-06-020-007
(3) Remove the flap control lever position sensor [20] from the position sensor assembly [2]:
(a) Remove the screw [27], washers [28] and nut [29] that attach the crank [18] to the shaft
on the position sensor [20].
(b) Remove the screws [25] and washers [26] that attach the position sensor [20] to the

E. Flap Control Lever Position Sensor Adjustment
SUBTASK 27-51-06-860-016
(1) Move the flap control lever to the 10-unit position.
SUBTASK 27-51-06-740-003
(2) Use the FSEU to find the output of the flap control lever position sensor [20]:
(a) Push the ON/OFF button on the front panel of the FSEU to turn on the display.
(b) Push the down arrow until OTHER FUNCTNS? shows on the display.
(c) Push the YES button to select OTHER FUNCTNS? on the FSEU.
(d) Push the down arrow until I/O MONITOR? shows on the display.
(e) Push the YES button to select I/O MONITOR? from the menu.
(f) Push the down arrow until SYNCHRO INPUTS? shows on the display.
(g) Push the YES button to select SYNCHRO INPUTS? from the menu.
(h) Make sure that the LVR POS shows in the limit of 52.3 to 52.9 degrees.
SUBTASK 27-51-06-820-004
(3) If the output of the position sensor [20] shown on the FSEU is not in the limit, adjust the
position sensor [20] (Figure 201):
(a) Loosen the screws [19] that attach the flap control lever position sensor assembly [2] to
the control stand [7].
(b) Put a 1/4 inch flat head screwdriver in the drive slot on the position flap control lever
sensor assembly [2].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(c) Carefully turn the position sensor assembly [2] until the FSEU shows the LVR POS in the
limit of 52.3 to 52.9 degrees.
(d) Tighten the screws [19].
(e) Remove the 1/4 inch flat head screwdriver from the drive slot.
(f) Make sure that the LVR POS shows in the limit of 52.3 to 52.9 degrees.
SUBTASK 27-51-06-730-008
(4) Do this task: Flap Control Lever Position Sensor System Test, TASK 27-51-06-730-802.

F. Inboard Trailing Edge Flap Removal
SUBTASK 27-51-11-020-008
(1) Remove the support assembly [131] as follows (Figure 401):
(a) Remove the bolts [130].
1) Keep the bolts [130] for re-installation.
(b) Remove the support assembly [131].
SUBTASK 27-51-11-020-006
(2) Disconnect the skew control rods for the skew mechanisms from the carriages (Figure 401):
(a) At the outboard carriage [13], remove the nut [8], washer [7], washer [5], bolt [4], and
bushing [6] that attaches the skew control rod [3] to the outboard carriage [13].
(b) At the inboard carriage [52], remove the nut [47], washer [46], washer [44], bolt [43], and
bushing [45] that attaches the skew control rod [41] to the inboard carriage [52].
SUBTASK 27-51-11-020-002
(3) Disconnect the aft flap drive rod [25] from the crankshaft [18]:
(a) Remove the pin [24], nut [23], washer [22], washer [20], bolt [19], and bushing [21] from
the crankshaft [18].
(b) Move the aft flap drive rod [25] away from the inboard flap assembly [1].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-51-11-980-002
CAUTION
DO NOT USE A RIG PIN IN THE CRANKSHAFT TO HOLD THE AFT FLAP IN
THE RETRACTED POSITION. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE
CRANKSHAFT OR THE FITTING ON THE MAIN FLAP.
(4) If the aft flap [2] is installed, move the aft flap [2] to the retracted position on the inboard flap
assembly [1]:
(a) Move the crankshaft [18] aft until the aft flap [2] is in the retracted position.
(b) Install the restraint strap (part of the sling equipment, SPL-1729) to hold the aft flap [2] in
the retracted position.
SUBTASK 27-51-11-480-001
(5) Install the sling [82] on the inboard flap assembly [1] (Figure 402):
(a) Remove the existing bolts [85] at the inboard and outboard ends of the front spar on the
inboard flap assembly [1].
1) Keep these bolts [85] for re-installation.
(b) Install the sling fittings [81] in the location of the bolts [85].
(c) Remove the existing bolts [86] at the rear spar at the aft end of the inboard flap
assembly [1].
1) Keep these bolts [86] for re-installation.
(d) Install the sling fitting [84] in the location of the bolts [86].
(e) Connect the sling [82] to the sling fittings [81] and sling fitting [84].
(f) Connect the sling [82] to an overhead lifting device.
(g) Use the sling [82] to hold the weight of the inboard flap assembly [1].
SUBTASK 27-51-11-020-003
(6) Remove the stop fittings from the flap tracks (Figure 401):
(a) On the flap track [39], remove the nut [56], washer [55], bushings [54], and bolt [53] from
the end of the flap track [39].
(b) On the outboard flap track [14], remove the roller stop [30], roller stop [37], and aft fairing
support fitting [35]:
1) Remove the nuts [29], washers [28], bolt [27], and bolts [36] that attach the aft
fairing support fitting [35] to the flap track [14].
2) Remove the nuts [34], washers [33], washers [32], and bolts [31] that attach the aft
fairing support fitting [35], roller stop [30], and roller stop [37] to the flap track [14].
3) Remove the roller stop [30], roller stop [37], and aft fairing support fitting [35] from
the flap track [14].
SUBTASK 27-51-11-860-016
(7) Use the manual drive system to extend the trailing edge flaps to the stops on the ballscrews,
do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Manual Operation, TASK 27-51-00-980-801.
NOTE: During the manual operation of the trailing edge flap, it is not necessary to do this task:
Trailing Edge Flap System Reactivation, TASK 27-51-00-440-801.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-51-11-020-004
CAUTION
BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU LOWER THE FLAP TO THE GROUND. YOU CAN
CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE TRAILING EDGE OF THE FLAP.
(8) Remove the inboard flap assembly [1]:
(a) Hold the weight of the inboard flap assembly [1] with the sling [82] and overhead lifting
device.
(b) Disconnect the inboard carriage [52] from the gimbal [40]:
1) Install a support to hold the ballscrew [42] when it is disconnected from the inboard
carriage [52].
2) Remove the nuts [50], washers [49], and bolts [48] that attach the carriage
bushings [51] to the inboard carriage [52].
3) Remove the carriage bushings [51] from the inboard carriage [52].
4) Move the gimbal [40] away from the inboard carriage [52].
(c) Disconnect the outboard carriage [13] from the gimbal [16]:
1) Install a support to hold the ballscrew [17] when it is disconnected from the outboard
carriage [13].
2) Remove the nut [11], washer [10], and bolt [9] that attach the carriage bushing
assembly [15] and carriage bushing assembly [26] to the outboard carriage [13].
3) Remove the carriage bushing assembly [15] and carriage bushing [26] from the
outboard carriage [13].
4) Move the gimbal [16] away from the outboard carriage [13].
(d) Use the sling equipment, SPL-1729, to move the inboard flap assembly [1] aft and down
away from the flap tracks.
(e) Use the sling equipment, SPL-1729, to move the inboard flap assembly [1] outboard and
aft away from the airplane.
SUBTASK 27-51-11-210-004
(9) Do a check of the configuration of the inboard flap carriage roller cartridges, and inboard seals:
(a) Do a check of the position of the index marks [120] for the carriage roller cartridges on
the inboard and outboard carriages.
1) Make a record of the position to use during the installation.
 006, 007, 013, 014; AIRPLANES WITH SMALL BULLNOSE SEALS
(b) Do a check for undersize seals on the inboard end of the flap assembly [1].
1) If undersize seals are installed on the inboard end of the flap, make a record to be

G. Prepare for the Installation
SUBTASK 27-51-11-820-001
(1) If the eccentric bushings [115] are installed on the flap assembly, make sure that the carriage
roller cartridges are in the correct position (Figure 403):
NOTE: The eccentric bushings are not installed on every flap assembly. If they are not
installed, adjustment is not necessary.
(a) If you will install a different inboard flap assembly [1] than the one you removed, make
sure that the carriage roller cartridge [116] and cartridge [125] are in the same position as
the flap you removed.
(b) If you did not record the position of the carriage roller from the flap you removed, adjust
the carriage roller cartridge [116] and cartridge [125] to the nominal position.
NOTE: The nominal position for the carriage roller cartridges is -45 degrees for the left
wing, and +30 for the right wing.
NOTE: There is no mismatch or alignment dimension to the fixed structure or the
outboard flap that the flap is adjusted to meet. The carriage roller cartridges can
be changed from the nominal position to meet lateral trim tolerances.
(c) Make sure that the carriage roller cartridge [116] and cartridge [125] for the inboard flap
assembly [1] are in the same position.
(d) If it is necessary, adjust the cartridge [125] on the inboard carriage [52]:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Loosen the nut [127] on the roller [123].
2) Turn the eccentric bushing [115] until the index mark [120] is in the correct position.
3) Tighten the nut [127] to 160 in-lb (18.1 N·m) - 975 in-lb (110.2 N·m).
4) Install the pin [126] in the nut [127].
5) Install lockwire between the bolts that attach the cartridge [125].
(e) If it is necessary, adjust the cartridge [116] or cartridge [125] on the outboard
carriage [13]:
1) Adjust the outboard cartridge [116]:
a) Remove the bolts [113], washers [122], and rub block [121] from the
retainer [114].
b) Loosen the nut [118] on the roller [117].
c) Turn the eccentric bushing [115] until the index marks [120] are in the correct
position.
d) Tighten the nut [118] on the roller [117] to 160 in-lb (18.1 N·m) - 975 in-lb
(110.2 N·m).
e) Install the pin [119] in the nut [118].
f) Put the rub block [121] in its position on the retainer [114] and install the
bolts [113] and washers [122].
2) Adjust the inboard cartridge [125]:
a) Loosen the nut [127] on the roller [123].
b) Turn the eccentric bushing [115] until the index marks [120] are in the correct
position.
c) Tighten the nut [127] on the roller [123] to 160 in-lb (18.1 N·m) - 975 in-lb
(110.2 N·m).
d) Install the pin [126] in the nut [127].
e) Install lockwire between the bolts that attach the cartridge [125].
 006, 007, 013, 014
SUBTASK 27-51-11-210-006
(2) If undersize seals were installed on the inboard end of the flap assembly [1] that was removed,
make sure that the new flap assembly [1] has undersize seals also.

H. Inboard Trailing Edge Flap Installation
SUBTASK 27-51-11-420-001
(1) Install the inboard flap assembly [1] (Figure 401):
CAUTION
BE VERY CAREFUL WHEN YOU LIFT THE FLAP FROM THE GROUND.
IF YOU ARE NOT CAREFUL, YOU CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE
TRAILING EDGE OF THE FLAP.
(a) Use the sling equipment, SPL-1729, and the overhead lifting device to move the inboard
flap assembly [1] up into its position aft of the flap track [14] and flap track [39].
(b) Align the forward rollers [12] for the outboard carriage [13] with the flap track [14].
(c) Move the inboard flap track [39] to align with the forward rollers [38] for the inboard
carriage [52].
CAUTION
DO NOT USE THE SLING TO MOVE THE FLAP ON THE FLAP TRACK
AFTER THE AFT ROLLERS ENGAGE. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO
THE FLAP.
(d) Move the inboard flap assembly [1] up and forward on the flap tracks until the carriages
align with the gimbal [16] and gimbal [40].
(e) Connect the outboard carriage [13] to the gimbal [16]:
1) Remove the support from the ballscrew [17] and move the gimbal [16] to its position
in the outboard carriage [13].
2) On the left wing, make sure that the ball return [128] on the ballscrew nut [129] are
outboard.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
3) On the right wing, make sure that the ball return [128] on the ballscrew nut [129] are
inboard.
NOTE: This is the preferred position for maintenance.
 006, 007, 013, 014
(f) Apply grease, D00633, to the inside and outside of the carriage bushing assembly [15]
and carriage bushing assembly [26].
(g) Install the carriage bushing assembly [15] and carriage bushing assembly [26] to attach
the gimbal [16] to the outboard carriage [13].

 ALL

torque.
(k) Connect the inboard carriage [52] to the gimbal [40]:
1) Remove the support from the ballscrew [42] and move the gimbal [40] to its position
in the inboard carriage [52].
2) Apply grease, D00633, to the inside and outside of the carriage bushings [51].
3) Install the carriage bushings [51] to attach the gimbal [40] to the inboard

4) Install the bolts [48], washers [49], and nuts [50] that attach the carriage
bushings [51] to the inboard carriage [52].
5) Tighten the nuts [50] to 65 in-lb (7.3 N·m) - 75 in-lb (8.5 N·m) more than the run-on
torque.

G. Inboard Trailing Edge Flap Adjustment
NOTE: There is no mismatch, or alignment dimension to the outboard flap, or to fixed structure that
the inboard flap is adjusted to meet. The eccentric carriage rollers can be changed from the
nominal position to meet lateral trim tolerances.
NOTE: The eccentric bushing [10], eccentric bushing [19] and eccentric bushing [30] are not
installed on every inboard flap [2].
SUBTASK 27-51-11-860-005
(1) Do a check of the adjustment of the deflection control roller [12] on the outboard end of the
inboard flap [2] (Figure 501):
(a) Manually extend and retract the inboard flap [2] through its full travel. To extend and
retract it, do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Manual Operation,
TASK 27-51-00-980-801.
NOTE: While you retract the inboard flap [2], monitor the deflection control roller [12] to
see if there is preload when it engages the deflection control track [3].
(b) If there is preload when the deflection control roller [12] engages the deflection control
track [3], then adjust the deflection control roller [12]:
1) Manually extend the inboard flap [2] to get access to the deflection control
roller [12]. To extend it, do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Manual Operation,
TASK 27-51-00-980-801.
2) Remove the bolt [6] and washer [5] that hold the retainer [4] and retainer [13] to the
deflection control rib [14].
3) Remove the retainer [13] for the inboard eccentric bushing [10].
4) Remove the pin [7] and loosen the nut [8] on the bolt [11].
5) Turn the inboard eccentric bushing [10] to change the position of the inboard
deflection control roller [12].
NOTE: Make sure you do not change the position of the outboard deflection control
roller [9].
6) Install the retainer [13] for the inboard eccentric bushing [10].
7) Install the bolt [6] and washer [5] that hold the retainer [4] and retainer [13].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
8) Tighten the nut [8] finger tight and install the pin [7].
NOTE: If it is necessary, tighten nut [8] the minimum amount necessary to install
the pin [7].
SUBTASK 27-51-11-860-006
(2) Retract the trailing edge flaps to the retracted position. To retract them, do this task: Retract the
Trailing Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-804.
SUBTASK 27-51-11-820-004
(3) Make sure carriage roller cartridges are in the correct position (Figure 501):
NOTE: It is necessary to keep the position of the cartridges on the inboard carriage the same
as the cartridges on the outboard carriage.
(a) If you installed a different flap, then adjust the carriage roller cartridges to the same
position as the original flap.
NOTE: The position of the original flap may have been adjusted for lateral trim per
(TASK 27-09-71-820-801).
(b) If you do not know the original position of the carriage roller cartridges, then adjust them
make sure they are in the nominal position.
NOTE: The nominal position for the carriage roller cartridges is -45 degrees for the left
wing, and +30 for the right wing.
CAUTION
DO NOT REMOVE MORE THAN ONE CARTRIDGE FROM THE
CARRIAGE AT A TIME. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(c) If it is necessary, adjust the cartridge [24] and cartridge [31] on the outboard carriage:
NOTE: It is necessary to keep the position of the cartridges on the inboard carriage the
same as the cartridges on the outboard carriage.
1) Adjust the outboard cartridge [31]:
a) Remove the bolts [28], washers [39] and the rub block [38] from the
retainer [29].
b) Remove the bolts [36] and washers [37] that attach the cartridge [31] to the
carriage.
c) Remove the cartridge [31] from the carriage.
d) Loosen the nut [33] on the roller [32].
e) Turn the eccentric bushing [30] until the index marks [35] are in the correct
position.
f) Tighten the nut [33] on the roller [32] to 160 in-lb (18.1 N·m)-975 in-lb
(110.2 N·m).
g) Install the pin [34] in the nut [33].
h) Put the cartridge [31] in its position in the carriage.
i) Install the bolts [36] and washers [37] to attach the cartridge [31].
j) Tighten the bolts [36] to 95 in-lb (10.7 N·m)-110 in-lb (12.4 N·m).
k) Install lockwire between the bolts [36] and the retainer [29].
l) Put the rub block [38] in its position on the retainer [29] and install the
bolts [28] and washers [39].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
2) Adjust the inboard cartridge [24]:
a) Remove the bolts [21] and washers [22] that attach the cartridge [24] to the
carriage.
b) Remove the cartridge [24] from the carriage.
c) Loosen the nut [26] on the roller [27].
d) Turn the eccentric bushing [19] until the index marks [23] are in the correct
position.
e) Tighten the nut [26] on the roller [27] to 160 in-lb (18.1 N·m)-975 in-lb
(110.2 N·m).
f) Install the pin [25] in the nut [26].
g) Put the cartridge [24] in its position in the carriage.
h) Install the bolts [21] and washers [22] to attach the cartridge [24].
i) Tighten the bolts [21] to 95 in-lb (10.7 N·m)-110 in-lb (12.4 N·m).
j) Install lockwire between the bolts [21].
CAUTION
DO NOT REMOVE MORE THAN ONE CARTRIDGE FROM THE
CARRIAGE AT A TIME. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(d) If it is necessary, adjust the cartridges [24] on the inboard carriage:
NOTE: Adjust the cartridges [24] one at a time. It is necessary to keep the position of the
cartridges on the inboard carriage the same as the cartridges on the outboard
carriage.
1) Remove the bolts [21] and washers [22] that attach the cartridge [24] to the
carriage.
2) Remove the cartridge [24] from the carriage.
3) Loosen the nut [26] on the roller [27].
4) Turn the eccentric bushing [19] until the index marks [23] are in the correct position.
5) Tighten the nut [26] to 160 in-lb (18.1 N·m)-975 in-lb (110.2 N·m).
6) Install the pin [25] in the nut [26].
7) Put the cartridge [24] in its position in the carriage.
8) Install the bolts [21] and washers [22] to attach the cartridge [24]
9) Tighten the bolts [21] to 95 in-lb (10.7 N·m)-110 in-lb (12.4 N·m).
10) Install lockwire between the bolts [21].
11) Adjust the other cartridge [24] on the inboard carriage.

(8) Do this procedure to adjust the applicable seal [55] (Figure 502):
(a) Loosen the screws [67] that attach the seal [55] and the seal retainer [68] to the inboard

(e) Tighten the screws [67] for the retainer assemblies on the flap with the smallest

the seals until the symmetry and gap requirements are met, or until the maximum
adjustment limit is reached.

 ALL

(10) Do this procedure to adjust the coverplate [63] to the wing-to-body fairing panels (Figure 502):
(a) On airplanes with the seal [62] on the wing-to-body fairing, do these steps:
1) Make sure the gap between the coverplate [63] and the wing-to-body fairing is
0.1000 +0.1200 / -0.0000 in. (2.5400 +3.0480 / -0.0000 mm).
NOTE: This distance is referred to as dimension C.
2) If the measurement between the coverplate [63] and the wing-to-body fairing is not
within the tolerance, then adjust the coverplate [63] :
a) Loosen the screws that attach the coverplate [63] to the lower surface of the
inboard flap.
b) Apply sealant, A00247 to both sides of the coverplate [63] in the area of the
attach screws.
c) Adjust the position of the coverplate [63].
d) Apply sealant, A00247 in the slots before you install the screws.
e) Tighten the screws.
f) Fill and fair the exposed slots if and as required with sealant, A00247
(b) On airplanes without the seal [62] on the wing-to-body fairing, do these steps:
1) Make sure the gap between the coverplate [63] and the wing-to-body fairing is
0.1000 +0.1200 / -0.0000 in. (2.5400 +3.0480 / -0.0000 mm).
NOTE: This distance is referred to as dimension C.
2) If the measurement between the coverplate [63] and the wing-to-body fairing is not
within the tolerance, then adjust the coverplate [63]:
a) Loosen the screws that attach the coverplate [63] to the lower surface of the
inboard flap.
b) Apply sealant, A00247 to both sides of the coverplate [63] in the area of the
attach screws.
c) Adjust the position of the coverplate [63].
d) Apply the sealant, A00247 in the slots before you install the screws.
e) Tighten the screws.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
f) Fill and fair the exposed slots if and as required with the sealant, A00247.
NOTE: The gap between the coverplate [63] and the wing-to-body fairing in
the flaps retracted position should not be less than 0.1000 in.
(2.5400 mm), but can be increased up to 0.2200 in. (5.5880 mm) if
required for the coverplate [63] to clear the wing-to-body fairing panels
by at least 0.0200 in. (0.5080 mm) as flaps are extended.

C. Prepare for the Removal
SUBTASK 27-51-12-860-003
(1) Extend the trailing edge flaps to the 40-unit position. To extend them, do this task: Extend the
Trailing Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-803.
SUBTASK 27-51-12-040-001
(2) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Deactivation, TASK 27-51-00-040-801.
D. Inboard Aft Flap Removal
SUBTASK 27-51-12-020-001
(1) At the outboard flap support, disconnect the crankshaft [3] from the aft flap drive rod [10]:
(a) Remove the nut [8], washer [7], bushing [6], washer [5] and bolt [4] that attach the
crankshaft [3] to the aft flap drive rod [10].
SUBTASK 27-51-12-980-001
(2) Use the crankshaft [3] to manually move the aft flap assembly [2] to the extended position.
SUBTASK 27-51-12-020-002
(3) Disconnect the inboard and outboard aft flap pushrods [11]:
(a) Remove the nuts [18], washers [17], washers [15], bolts [14] and bushings [13] that
attach the aft flap pushrod [11] to the aft flap assembly [2].
(b) Move the aft flap pushrod [11] away from the aft flap assembly [2].
SUBTASK 27-51-12-020-003
(4) Remove the aft flap assembly [2]:
NOTE: The aft flap assembly [2] weighs approximately 60 pounds.
(a) Support the aft flap assembly [2].
(b) Disconnect the aft flap tracks [21] from the aft flap assembly [2]:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Remove the nuts [23], washers [24], washers [26], bolts [27] and bushings [25] that
attach the aft flap tracks [21] to the aft flap assembly [2].
2) Move the aft flap tracks [21] forward, away from the aft flap assembly [2].
(c) Move the trailing edge of the aft flap assembly [2] down, until it is perpendicular to the
main flap [1].
(d) Disengage the inboard and outboard rollers [28] from the programming tracks [38].
NOTE: Disengage the inboard roller [28] first.

F. Prepare for the Installation
SUBTASK 27-51-12-820-001
(1) If you will not install the same aft flap assembly [2] and main flap [1], make sure that the
inboard and outboard rollers [28] are in the most forward position (Figure 401):
NOTE: With the rollers [28] in the most forward position, the slot in the eccentric bushing [29]
will align with the index mark on the retainer plate [30].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Remove the nut [34], washer [35] and retainer plate [30] that hold the eccentric
bushing [29].
(b) Loosen the nut [33] on the roller [28].
(c) Turn the eccentric bushing [29] until the roller [28] is in the forward position and the slot
aligns with the bolt [36].
NOTE: The bolt [36] will stay in its position.
(d) Apply sealant, A00247 to the threads of the bolt [36].
(e) Install the retainer plate [30] with the washer [35] and nut [34].
(f) Torque the nut [33] on the roller [28] to 95 in-lb (11 N·m)-110 in-lb (12 N·m).
(g) If a tabbed washer [32] is installed, bend a minimum of two tabs of the washer [32] over
the nut [33].
SUBTASK 27-51-12-420-001
(2) Make sure that the aft flap tracks are installed on the main flap [1] and are in the retracted
position. If they are not installed, do this task: Inboard Aft Flap Track Installation,
TASK 27-51-16-400-801.
G. Inboard Aft Flap Installation
SUBTASK 27-51-12-420-002
(1) Install the aft flap assembly [2]:
(a) Hold the aft flap assembly [2] below and approximately perpendicular to the main flap [1].
(b) Engage the outboard roller [28] with the outboard programming track [38].
(c) Engage the inboard roller [28] with the inboard programming track [38].
(d) Lift the trailing edge of the aft flap assembly [2] and hold it in its usual position.
(e) Connect the aft flap assembly [2] to the aft flap tracks [21]:
1) Move the aft flap tracks [21] aft until they align with the aft flap assembly [2].
2) Install the bushings [25], bolts [27], washers [26], washers [24] and nuts [23] that
attach the aft flap tracks [21] to the aft flap assembly [2].
3) Torque the nuts [23] to 100 in-lb (11.3 N·m)-150 in-lb (16.9 N·m).
4) Install the pins [22] in the nuts [23].
SUBTASK 27-51-12-020-004
(2) Connect the inboard and outboard aft flap pushrod [11]:
(a) Carefully pull the aft flap pushrod [11] through the cutouts to move them to the extended
position.
NOTE: The crankshaft [3] will move when you pull on the aft flap pushrod [11].
(b) Install the bushings [13], bolts [14], washers [15], washers [17], and nuts [18] that attach
the aft flap pushrod [11] to the aft flap assembly [2].
(c) Torque the nuts [18] to 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m)-80 in-lb (9.0 N·m).
(d) Install the pins [19] in the nuts [18].
SUBTASK 27-51-12-980-002
(3) Use the crankshaft [3] to manually move the aft flap assembly [2] to the retracted position.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
H. Inboard Aft Flap Adjustment
SUBTASK 27-51-12-480-001
(1) Install the rig pin (rigging pin kit, SPL-1585) in the crankshaft [3].
NOTE: Use rig pin F70207–113.
SUBTASK 27-51-12-220-001
(2) Measure the distance between the trailing edge of the aft flap assembly [2] and the trailing
edge of the upper cove panel [61] on the main flap [1] (Figure 402).
NOTE: Measure the distance aft of the inboard and outboard aft flap pushrod [11].
(a) At the outboard aft flap pushrod [11], make sure that the distance is 9.2745 ±0.0600 in.
(235.57 ±1.52 mm).
(b) At the inboard aft flap pushrod [11], make sure that the distance is 9.2319 ±0.0600 in.
(234.49 ±1.52 mm).
SUBTASK 27-51-12-820-002
(3) If the distance at the inboard or outboard aft flap pushrod [11] is not in the limit, then adjust the
length of the applicable aft flap pushrod [11] (Figure 401):
(a) Remove the rig pin from the crankshaft [3].
(b) Use the crankshaft [3] to manually extend the aft flap assembly [2] to the extended
position.
(c) Adjust the length of the applicable aft flap pushrod [11]:
NOTE: For each 90 degree turn of the aft flap pushrod [11], the trailing edge of the aft
flap will move 0.04 in. (1.02 mm).
1) Loosen the nuts [20] on the aft flap pushrod [11].
2) Adjust the length of the aft flap pushrod [11].
WARNING
USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE
COR-BAN 27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE
IT WITH WATER. IF THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES,
IMMEDIATELY FLUSH YOUR EYES WITH WATER. GET MEDICAL
AID. THIS MATERIAL CONTAINS FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN
CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL.
3) Apply a thin layer of Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (preferred) or corrosion
inhibiting material, G50136 (optional) to the threads of the rod ends [16].
4) Tighten the nuts [20].
5) Install lockwire on the nuts [20] and the locking keys [12].
(d) Use the crankshaft [3] to manually retract the aft flap assembly [2] to the retracted
position.
(e) Install the rig pin in the crankshaft [3].
(f) Make sure that the distance from the trailing edge of the aft flap assembly [2] to the
trailing edge of the upper cove panel [61] is in the limit.
SUBTASK 27-51-12-980-003
(4) Give support to the aft flap assembly [2].
NOTE: This is the position the rollers will be in with airloads applied to the aft flap
assembly [2].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Do a visual inspection to make sure that the programming rollers [28] touch the bottom
surface of the programming tracks [38], and that the aft rollers on the aft flap tracks [21]
touch the top surface of the tracks.
NOTE: If necessary, use an inspection mirror, STD-600 or a borescope, STD-7028 to aid with
the inspection.
SUBTASK 27-51-12-220-002
(5) At the outboard end of the aft flap assembly [2], measure the vertical alignment at the trailing
edge of the aft flap assembly [2] and the main flap [1] (Figure 402).
SUBTASK 27-51-12-820-003
(6) If the vertical alignment of the trailing edge is not in the limit of 0.000 ±0.100 in.
(0.00 ±2.54 mm), then adjust the rollers [28] for the inboard and outboard programming
tracks [38] (Figure 401):
NOTE: Make sure that you keep the two rollers [28] adjusted to the same position.
(a) Remove the rig pin from the crankshaft [3].
(b) Use the crankshaft [3] to manually extend the aft flap assembly [2] to the extended
position.
(c) Adjust the position of the rollers [28]:
1) Remove the nut [34], washer [35] and retainer plate [30] that hold the eccentric
bushing [29].
2) Loosen the nut [33] on the roller [28].
3) Turn the eccentric bushing [29] to adjust the position of the roller [28].
NOTE: Refer to (Table 401) to determine how far you must turn the eccentric
bushing [29].
Table 401/27-51-12-993-803 Programming Roller Eccentric Bushing Adjustment
Eccentric Bushing Position Aft Flap Trailing Edge Movement Inches (Millimeters)
Nominal to +30 +0.046 (+1.168)
+30 to +60 +0.034 (+0.864)
+60 to +90 +0.013 (+0.330)
Nominal to -30 -0.046 (-1.168)
-30 to -60 -0.034 (-0.864)
-60 to -90 -0.013 (-0.330)
4) Apply sealant, A00247 to the threads of the bolt [36].
5) Install the retainer plate [30] with the washer [35] and nut [34].
6) Torque the nut [33] on the roller [28] to 95 in-lb (10.7 N·m)-110 in-lb (12.4 N·m).
(d) Use the crankshaft [3] to manually retract the aft flap assembly [2] to the retracted
position.
(e) Install the rig pin in the crankshaft [3].
(f) Make sure that the vertical alignment of the trailing edge of the aft flap assembly [2] and
the main flap [1] is in the limit.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-51-12-220-003
(7) Measure the clearance between the upper cove panel [61] on the main flap [1] and the upper
surface of the aft flap assembly [2] (Figure 402).
NOTE: Measure the clearance at all of the cove panel support [62] and at the aft flap roller
fitting [76].
SUBTASK 27-51-12-220-008
(8) Make sure that the teflon coating on the aft flap assembly [2] is not damaged.
(a) If the teflon coating is damaged, do this task: Apply The Abrasion-Resistant Teflon Finish,
BMS 10-86 Type I, TASK 51-21-81-370-801 or Apply The Abrasion-Resistant Teflon
Finish, BMS 10-86 Type II, TASK 51-21-81-370-802.
SUBTASK 27-51-12-820-004
(9) If the clearance between the main flap [1] and the aft flap assembly [2] is not in the limit of
0.010 +0.100 / -0.005 in. (0.254 +2.540 / -0.127 mm), then change the thickness of the
shims [75] on the cove panel support [62] and the aft flap roller fitting [76]:
(a) Remove the rig pin from the crankshaft [3].
(b) Use the crankshaft [3] to manually extend the aft flap assembly [2] until you can get
access to the fasteners for the shims [75] and shims [77].
(c) If it is necessary, change the thickness of the shims [75] on the cove panel supports [62]:
1) Remove the nuts [74], washers [73] and bolts [72] that attach the upper cove
panel [61] to the cove panel support [62].
2) Remove the shim [75] from the cove panel support [62] and the upper cove
panel [61].
3) Change the thickness of the shim [75].
NOTE: The maximum permitted thickness of the shim [75] is 0.10 in. (2.54 mm).
4) Apply sealant, A00247 to the mating surfaces of the shim [75].
5) Put the shim [75] in its position between the cove panel support [62] and the upper
cove panel [61].

6) Apply a layer of Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (preferred) or corrosion inhibiting
material, G50136 (optional) to the shank and threads of the bolts [72].
7) Install the bolts [72], washers [73] and nuts [74].
(d) If it is necessary, change the thickness of the shims [77] on the aft flap roller fittings [76]:
1) Remove the nuts [80], washers [79] and bolts [78] that attach the upper cove
panel [61] to the aft flap roller fitting [76].
2) Remove the shims [77] from the aft flap roller fitting [76] and the upper cove
panel [61].
3) Change the thickness of the shim [77].
NOTE: The maximum permitted thickness of the shim [77] is 0.10 in. (2.54 mm).

4) Apply sealant, A00247 to the mating surfaces of the shim [77].
5) Put the shim [77] in its position between the aft flap roller fitting [76] and the upper
cove panel [61].

7) Install the bolts [78], washers [79] and nuts [80].
(e) Use the crankshaft [3] to manually retract the aft flap assembly [2] to the retracted
position.
(f) Install the rig pin in the crankshaft [3].
(g) Make sure that the clearance between the main flap [1] and the aft flap assembly [2] is in
the limit.
SUBTASK 27-51-12-220-004
(10) Measure the clearance between the lower cove panel [68] on the main flap [1] and the lower
surface of the aft flap assembly [2].
NOTE: Measure the clearance at the two lower cove panel supports [62].
SUBTASK 27-51-12-820-005
(11) If the clearance between the main flap [1] and the aft flap assembly [2] is not in the limit of
0.00 ±0.06 in. (0.00 ±1.52 mm), then change the thickness of the shims [81] on the lower cove
panel [68] support:
(a) Remove the rig pin from the crankshaft [3].
(b) Use the crankshaft [3] to manually extend the aft flap assembly [2] until you can get
access to the fasteners for the shims [81].
(c) Change the thickness of the shim [81] on the cove panel supports [62]:
1) Remove the nuts [71], washers [70], and bolts [69] that attach the lower cove
panel [68] to the cove panel support [62].
2) Remove the shim [81] from the cove panel support [62] and the lower cove
panel [68].
3) Change the thickness of the shim [81].
NOTE: The maximum permitted thickness of the shim [81] is 0.10 in. (2.54 mm).
4) Apply sealant, A00247 to the mating surfaces of the shim [81].
5) Put the shim [81] in its position between the cove panel support [62] and the lower
cove panel [68].

6) Apply a layer of Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (preferred) or corrosion inhibiting

7) Install the bolts [69], washers [70] and nuts [71].
(d) Use the crankshaft [3] to manually retract the aft flap assembly [2] to the retracted

(e) Install the rig pin in the crankshaft [3].
(f) Make sure that the clearance between the main flap [1] and the aft flap assembly [2] is in

SUBTASK 27-51-12-220-005
(12) At the inboard end of the aft flap assembly [2], measure the compression of the seal [82] on
the aft side of the main flap [1]:
(a) Measure and record the distance between the trailing edge of the aft flap assembly [2]
and the lower cove panel [68].
NOTE: This distance is referred to as Dimension A.
(b) Remove the rig pin from the crankshaft [3].
(c) Use the crankshaft [3] to manually extend the aft flap assembly [2] until the seal [82] is
not compressed against the aft flap assembly [2].
(d) Measure and record the distance between the aft edge of the seal [82] and the lower
cove panel [68].
NOTE: This distance is referred to as Dimension B.
SUBTASK 27-51-12-820-006
(13) If Dimension A minus Dimension B is not in the limit of 12.8393 ±0.1000 in. (326.12 ±2.54 mm),
then adjust the position of the seal [82]:
(a) Use the crankshaft [3] to manually extend the aft flap assembly [2] until you can get
access to the fasteners for the seal [82].
(b) Loosen the nuts [86], washers [85] and bolts [84] that attach the retainer [83].
(c) Move the retainer [83] with the seal [82] to change the distance to the compression of the
seal [82].
NOTE: This will change the Dimension B.
(d) Tighten the bolts [84], washers [85] and nuts [86] that attach the retainer [83].
(e) Use the crankshaft [3] to manually retract the aft flap assembly [2] to the retracted
position.
(f) Install the rig pin in the crankshaft [3].
SUBTASK 27-51-12-220-006
(14) Outboard of the inboard aft flap track [21], measure the distance between the aft edge of the
seal [63] and the seam on the lower surface of the aft flap assembly [2].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) If the distance between the seam on the aft flap assembly [2] and the seal [63] is not in
the limit of 4.7091 ±0.1000 in. (119.61 ±2.54 mm), then adjust the position of the
seal [63]:
1) Remove the rig pin from the crankshaft [3].
2) Use the crankshaft [3] to manually extend the aft flap assembly [2] until you can get
access to the fasteners for the seal [63].
3) Loosen the nuts [66], washers [65] and bolts [64] that attach the retainer [67].
4) Move the retainer [67] with the seal [63] to change the distance to the seam on the
aft flap assembly [2].
5) Tighten the nuts [66], washers [65] and bolts [64] that attach the retainer [67].
6) Use the crankshaft [3] to manually retract the aft flap assembly [2] to the retracted
position.
7) Install the rig pin in the crankshaft [3].
(b) Make sure that the distance between the seam on the bottom surface of the aft flap
assembly [2] and the seal [63] is in the limit.
SUBTASK 27-51-12-220-007
(15) Do a check of the adjustment of the seals at the inboard and outboard ends of the aft flap
assembly [2]:
(a) On the inboard and outboard ends of the aft flap assembly [2], measure the distance
between the aft flap assembly [2] and the main flap [1].
(b) Remove the rig pin from the crankshaft [3].
(c) Use the crankshaft [3] to manually extend the aft flap assembly [2] until the seal [88] and
seal [93] are clear of the main flap [1].
(d) Measure the distance the seal [88] and seal [93] extends away from the aft flap
assembly [2].
(e) If the distance the seal [88] and seal [93] extends is not in the limit of the distance you
measured plus 0.150 ±0.100 in. (3.81 ±2.54 mm), then adjust the position of the
applicable seal [88] or seal [93]:
1) Loosen the nuts [87], washers [91] and bolts [92] that attach the retainer [90].
2) Move the retainer [90] and the seal [88] or seal [93] to change the distance the seal
extends past the aft flap assembly [2].
3) Tighten the nuts [87], washers [91] and bolts [92] that attach the retainer [90].
(f) Use the crankshaft [3] to manually retract the aft flap assembly [2] to the retracted
position.
NOTE: The seal [88] and seal [93] can extend a maximum of 0.5 in. (12.7 mm) below the
lower surface of the main flap [1] when the seals are compressed.
SUBTASK 27-51-12-080-001
(16) Remove the rig pin from the crankshaft [3] if it is necessary.
SUBTASK 27-51-12-420-003
(17) At the outboard flap support, connect the crankshaft [3] to the aft flap drive rod [10]
(Figure 401):
(a) Use the crankshaft [3] to manually extend the aft flap assembly [2] until the crankshaft [3]
aligns with the aft flap drive rod [10].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) Install the bolt [4], washer [5], bushing [6], washer [7] and nut [8] that attach the
crankshaft [3] to the aft flap drive rod [10].
1) Make sure that the head of the bolt [4] is on the inboard side.
(c) Torque the nut [8] to 30 in-lb (3.4 N·m)-50 in-lb (5.6 N·m).
(d) Install the pin [9] through the nut [8].
I. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 27-51-12-440-001
(1) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Reactivation, TASK 27-51-00-440-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-12-860-002
(2) Retract the trailing edge flaps to the retracted position. To retract the flaps, do this task: Retract
the Trailing Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-804.

D. Procedure
SUBTASK 27-51-12-020-005

SUBTASK 27-51-13-420-001
(2) Install the carriage assembly [2] on the main flap [1]:

(c) Put the carriage assembly [2] in its position on the main flap [1].
(d) Apply sealant, A00247 to the mating surface of the fillers [6] and the main flap [1].

(f) Apply sealant, A00247 to the shank and threads of the bolts [5], bolts [9], bolts [12] and
bolts [16].
(g) Install the bolts [5], washers [7] and nuts [8] to attach the forward end of the carriage
assembly [2] to the main flap [1].
(h) Install the bolts [9], washers [10] and nuts [11] at the forward end of the carriage
assembly [2].
NOTE: Install the bolts [9] with the heads down.
(i) Install the bolts [12], bolts [16], washers [13], washers [14] and nuts [15] to attach the aft
end of the carriage assembly [2] to the main flap [1].
SUBTASK 27-51-13-410-001
(3) Install the upper skin panel [3] on the main flap [1]:

flap [1].

(c) Install the bolts [4]:
1) Apply compound, C00528 to the forward and aft rows of holes in the upper skin
panel [3].
2) Install the bolts [4] in the forward and aft rows of holes.

flap [1].

SUBTASK 27-51-13-020-009
(1) Do this task: Inboard Flap Inboard Carriage Removal, TASK 27-51-13-000-802.
SUBTASK 27-51-13-020-015
(2) Inspect the rub pads [8] for wear.
(a) If the rub pads [8] are worn greater than 40%, they will need to be replaced.
SUBTASK 27-51-13-020-010
(3) Use these tools to do a check for wear on the part of the inboard flap inboard carriage:
(a) micrometer (0-1 inch, readable to 1/1000 inch), STD-1096
(b) vernier caliper (0 - 6 inch, readable to 1/1000 inch), STD-1097.
SUBTASK 27-51-13-020-011
(4) Examine the parts of the inboard flap inboard carriage (Table 602):
(a) Remove the parts that you will measure.
(b) Measure the parts with a micrometer (0-1 inch, readable to 1/1000 inch), STD-1096, or a
vernier caliper (0 - 6 inch, readable to 1/1000 inch), STD-1097.
(c) Compare the dimensions you measured with the permitted wear dimensions.
(d) If the parts are not in tolerance, replace or repair the parts.

C. Prepare for the Removal
SUBTASK 27-51-14-860-001
(1) Extend the trailing edge flaps to the 40-unit position. To extend them, do this task: Extend the
Trailing Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-803.
SUBTASK 27-51-14-040-001
(2) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Deactivation, TASK 27-51-00-040-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-14-010-001
(3) Do this task: Inboard Flap Support Aft Fairing Removal, TASK 27-51-18-000-802.
SUBTASK 27-51-14-010-002
(4) Remove the upper skin panel [4] from the outboard end of the main flap [1]:
(a) Remove the bolts [3] that attach the upper skin panel [4] to the main flap [1].
(b) Remove the upper skin panel [4].
SUBTASK 27-51-14-010-003
(5) Remove the lower skin panel [58] from the inboard end of the main flap [1]:
(a) Remove the bolts [57] that attach the lower skin panel [58] to the main flap [1].

 ALL

D. Inboard Aft Flap Mechanism Removal
SUBTASK 27-51-14-020-001
(1) Remove the aft flap drive rod assembly [43]:
(a) Remove the nuts [49], washers [48], bushings [47], washers [46] and bolts [45] that
attach the aft flap drive rod assembly [43] to the drive rod fitting [44] and the crankshaft
assembly [17].
(b) Remove the aft flap drive rod assembly [43].
SUBTASK 27-51-14-020-002
(2) Remove the interconnect push rod assembly [18]:
(a) Remove the nut [25], washer [24], washer [22], bolt [21] and bushing [23] that attach the
interconnect push rod assembly [18] to the crankshaft assembly [17].
(b) Remove the nut [15], washer [14], washer [12], bolt [11] and bushing [13] that attach the
interconnect push rod assembly [18] to the outboard bellcrank assembly [33].
(c) Remove the interconnect push rod assembly [18].
SUBTASK 27-51-14-020-003
(3) Remove the crankshaft assembly [17]:
(a) Remove the nut [55], washer [54], washers [52], bolts [51] and bushings [53] that attach
the crankshaft assembly [17] to the ribs [41].
(b) Remove the crankshaft assembly [17].
SUBTASK 27-51-14-020-004
(4) Remove the aft flap push rod assemblies [34]:
(a) Remove the nut [31], washer [30], washer [28], bolt [27] and bushing [29] that attach the
outboard aft flap push rod assembly [34] to the outboard bellcrank assembly [33].
(b) Remove the nut [31], washer [30], bushing [29], washer [28] and bolt [27] that attach the
inboard aft flap push rod assembly [34] to the inboard bellcrank assembly [67].
(c) Remove the nut [79], washer [78], washer [76], bolt [75] and bushing [77] that attach the
aft flap push rod assemblies [34] to the aft flap [2].
(d) Remove the aft flap push rod assemblies [34].
SUBTASK 27-51-14-020-005
(5) Remove the cable assemblies [19] and cable assemblies [64]:
(a) Remove the locking clips [66] from the turnbuckles [65].
(b) Turn the turnbuckles [65] to loosen the cable assemblies [19] and cable assemblies [64].
(c) Remove the nuts [62], washers [61], washers [60], teflon washers [90] (if installed) and
bolts [59] that attach the cable assemblies [64] to the inboard bellcrank assembly [67].
(d) Remove the nuts [38], washer [37], washers [36], teflon washers [90] (if installed) and
bolts [35] that attach the cable assemblies [19] to the outboard bellcrank assembly [33].
(e) Remove the cable assemblies [19] and cable assemblies [64].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-51-14-020-006
(6) Remove the outboard bellcrank assembly [33]:
(a) Remove the nut [9], washer [8], washer [6], bolt [5] and bushings [7] that attach the
outboard bellcrank assembly [33] to the main flap [1].
(b) Remove the outboard bellcrank assembly [33].
SUBTASK 27-51-14-020-007
(7) Remove the inboard bellcrank assembly [67]:
(a) Remove the nut [72], washer [71], washer [69], bolt [68] and bushings [70] that attach the
inboard bellcrank assembly [67] to the main flap [1].
(b) Remove the inboard bellcrank assembly [67].
