G. Prepare for the Installation
SUBTASK 27-51-24-820-001
(1) Make sure that the bellcrank assembly [17] is the correct length.
NOTE: The length of the bellcrank assembly can be changed to adjust for lateral trim
problems.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Measure the distance between the center of the bolt hole in the adjustment fitting [36]
and bellcrank assembly [17].
NOTE: This distance is referred to as Dimension A.
(b) Make sure that the Dimension A on the bellcrank assembly [17] you will install is the
same as the bellcrank assembly [17] that you removed.
NOTE: The nominal dimension of the inboard bellcrank assembly is 14.56 in.
(369.82 mm). The nominal dimension of the outboard bellcrank assembly is
13.74 in. (349.00 mm).
1) If the inboard and outboard bellcrank assembly [17] are not at the nominal length,
they should both be the same distance from the nominal dimension.
(c) If the bellcrank assembly [17] is not the correct length, adjust the bellcrank assembly [17].
1) Loosen the nuts [35] on the adjustment fitting [36] until the locking washer [34] is
disengaged from the bellcrank assembly [17].
2) Change the position of the adjustment fitting [36].
3) Engage the locking washer [34] with the bellcrank assembly [17].
4) Tighten the nuts [35] on the adjustment fitting [36].
5) Install MS20995C47 lockwire, G50356, on the nut [35].
H. Outboard Aft Flap Actuating Mechanism Installation
SUBTASK 27-51-24-420-001
(1) Install the bellcrank assembly [17] on the flap carriage [18].
(a) Apply grease, D00633, to the shank of the bolt [29].
NOTE: Make sure that you do not get grease, D00633, on the threads of the bolt.
(b) Install the bolts [28] in the bellcrank assembly [17].
(c) Put the bellcrank assembly [17] in its position on the flap carriage [18].
(d) Install the bolt [29] and washer [30] that attach the bellcrank assembly [17] to the flap
carriage [18].
(e) Carefully clean all of the grease, D00633, from the threads of the bolt [29].
(f) Install the washer [31] and nut [32] on the bolt [29].
 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187,
189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343,
346-999;  006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044 POST SB 737-57-1278
(g) Tighten the nut [32] to 760 in-lb (86 N·m) - 840 in-lb (95 N·m).
 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044 PRE SB 737-57-1278
(h) Tighten the nut [32] to 240 in-lb (27 N·m) - 410 in-lb (46 N·m).
 ALL
(i) Install the pin [33] in the nut [32].
(j) Attach the rubcap [25] to the bellcrank assembly [17] with the washers [27] and nuts [26].
SUBTASK 27-51-24-420-002
(2) Connect the aft rod assembly [2] and forward rod assembly [16] to the bellcrank assembly [17].
(a) Apply grease, D00633, to the shank of the bolts [3] and the inside of the bushings [5].
NOTE: Make sure that you do not get grease, D00633, on the threads of the bolts.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) Install the bolts [3], washers [4], and bushings [5] to attach the aft rod assembly [2] and
forward rod assembly [16] to the bellcrank assembly [17].
NOTE: Make sure that the heads of the bolts are inboard.
(c) Carefully clean all of the grease, D00633, from the threads of the bolts [3].
(d) Install the washers [6] and nuts [7] on the bolts [3].
(e) Tighten the nuts [7] to 65 in-lb (7 N·m) - 100 in-lb (11 N·m).
(f) Install the pins [8] in the nuts [7].
SUBTASK 27-51-24-420-003
(3) Connect the forward rod assembly [16] to the drive rod attach fitting [9].
(a) Apply grease, D00633, to the shank of the bolt [10] and the inside of the bushing [12].
NOTE: Make sure that you do not get grease, D00633, on the threads of the bolts.
(b) Install the bushing [12], bolt [10], and washer [11] to attach the forward rod assembly [16]
to the drive rod attach fitting [9].
NOTE: Make sure that the head of the bolt is inboard.
(c) Carefully clean all of the grease, D00633, from the threads of the bolt [10].
(d) Install the washer [13] and nut [14] on the bolt [10].
(e) Tighten the nut [14] to 65 in-lb (7 N·m) - 100 in-lb (11 N·m).
(f) Install the pin [15] in the nut [14].
SUBTASK 27-51-24-420-004
(4) Connect the aft rod assembly [2] to the aft flap [1].
(a) Apply grease, D00633, to the shank of the bolt [19] and the inside of the bushing [21].
NOTE: Make sure that you do not get grease, D00633, on the threads of the bolt.
(b) Install the bushing [21], bolt [19], and washer [20] to attach the aft rod assembly [2] to the
aft flap [1].
NOTE: Make sure that the head of the bolt is inboard.
(c) Carefully clean all of the grease, D00633, from the threads of the bolt [19].
(d) Install the washer [22] and nut [23] on the bolt [19].
(e) Tighten the nut [23] to 65 in-lb (7 N·m) - 100 in-lb (11 N·m).
(f) Install the pin [24] in the nut [23].
I. Aft Flap Drive Mechanism Adjustment
SUBTASK 27-51-24-440-001
(1) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Reactivation, TASK 27-51-00-440-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-24-860-002
(2) Retract the trailing edge flaps to the retracted position (TASK 27-51-00-860-804).
SUBTASK 27-51-24-480-001
(3) Install the rig pin from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, in the rig pin holes in the bellcrank
assembly [17] and flap carriage [18] (Figure 402).
NOTE: Use rig pin F70207-88.
(a) If it is necessary, move the aft flap [1] or the main flap until you can install the rig pins.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-51-24-220-001
(4) Measure the mismatch at the between the aft flap [1] and main flap at the inboard and
outboard ends of the aft flap [1].
SUBTASK 27-51-24-820-002
(5) If the mismatch at the inboard and outboard ends of the aft flap [1] is not in the limit of
0.00 ±0.06 in. (0.000 ±1.524 mm), then adjust the length of the applicable aft rod assembly [2].
(a) Loosen the nuts [51] on the aft rod assembly [2].
(b) Turn the applicable aft rod assembly [2] until the mismatch is in the limit at the inboard
and outboard ends of the aft flap [1].
NOTE: For each 1/4 turn of the aft rod assembly, the trailing edge of the aft flap will
move approximately 0.04 in. (1.02 mm).
(c) Tighten the nuts [51] on the aft rod assembly [2].
(d) Install lockwire on the nuts [51].
SUBTASK 27-51-24-080-001
(6) Remove the rig pin from the bellcrank assembly [17].
J. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 27-51-24-410-001
(1) Install the aft fairings on the flap supports.
(a) Do this task: Outboard Flap Outboard Support Aft Fairing Installation,
TASK 27-51-28-400-802.
(b) Do this task: Outboard Flap Inboard Support Aft Fairing Installation,
TASK 27-51-28-400-804.
SUBTASK 27-51-24-440-002
(2) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Reactivation, TASK 27-51-00-440-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-24-860-003
(3) If the trailing edge flaps are not in the retracted position, do this task: Retract the Trailing Edge
Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-804.

F. Outboard Flap Outboard Track Removal
NOTE: Make sure you support the flap track while you disconnect it. The outboard track for the
outboard flap weighs approximately 110 pounds (50 kilograms).
SUBTASK 27-51-25-480-001
(1) If you will use the adapter, SPL-1733, install it on the flap track [1]:
(a) Install the adapter, SPL-1733 on the flap track [1] approximately 33 inches (84 cm) aft of
the track attach fitting.
(b) Put a low profile hydraulic jack, COM-1568 below the adapter, SPL-1733 to support the
flap track [1].
SUBTASK 27-51-25-020-004
(2) Remove the nut [15], washer [14], washer [12] and bolt [13] to disconnect the jumper wire [16]
from the flap track [1].
SUBTASK 27-51-25-020-005
(3) Disconnect the forward end of the flap track [1]:
(a) Remove the bolts [18] and washers [17] that attach the failsafe fitting assembly [19] to the
track attach fitting.
(b) Remove the nut [22], washer [21] and fuse pin [20] from the forward end of the flap
track [1].
SUBTASK 27-51-25-020-006
(4) Disconnect the aft end of the flap track [1] from the structure:
(a) Remove the nut [6], washer [5], washer [4] and bolt [3] that attach the outboard side of
the flap track [1] to the structure.
(b) Remove the nut [7], washer [8], washer [10] and bolt [11] that attach the inboard side of
the flap track [1] to the structure.
(c) Measure the thickness of the shim [9].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Make sure to mark the track with this measurement data.
NOTE: This measurement data for the removal and replacement of the flap tracks
is an important step to obtain ample free movement in the fuse pin joint at
the forward end of the flap track and return of the flaps to former operating
condition.
SUBTASK 27-51-25-020-007
(5) If you will install a new flap track [1], remove the transmission attach fitting assembly [2] from
the flap track [1]:
(a) Remove the nuts [26], washers [24] and bolts [27] that attach the transmission attach
fitting assembly [2] to flap track [1].

G. Outboard Flap Outboard Track Installation
SUBTASK 27-51-25-420-001
(1) If it is not installed, install the transmission attach fitting assembly [2]:
(a) Put the transmission attach fitting assembly [2] in its location on the flap track [1].
(b) Install the bolts [27], washers [24] and nuts [26] that attach the transmission attach fitting
assembly [2] to the flap track [1].
(c) Install the pins [25] in the nuts [26].
SUBTASK 27-51-25-480-002
(2) If you will use the adapter, SPL-1733, install it on the flap track [1]:
(a) Install the adapter, SPL-1733 on the flap track [1] approximately33 in. (84 cm) aft of the
track attach fitting.
(b) Put a low profile hydraulic jack, COM-1568 below the adapter, SPL-1733 to support the
flap track [1].
SUBTASK 27-51-25-420-002
(3) Install the flap track [1]:
(a) If it is not installed, install the shim [9] on the structure:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Make sure the shim [9] is the same thickness as the shim [9] that you removed.
NOTE: The original thickness of the shim [9] is on a marker on the structure.
a) If it is necessary to replace the flap track [1] with a new unit then you may
need to make a new shim [9].
NOTE: This shim should be marked and checked after you torque the nuts
that attach the flap track to the structure.
<1> If you use the new shim [9], align it to make sure that the maximum gap
is no more than 0.005 inches.
<2> Make sure that the Anti-Fert (Phenolic) shim [9] is installed to the lower
wing skin.
2) Apply sealant, A00247 to the mating surface of the shim [9] and the track [1].
3) Put the shim [9] in its position.
4) Apply a fillet seal of sealant, A00247 around the shim [9].
(b) Attach the aft end of the flap track [1] to the structure:
1) Lift the flap track [1] to its location on the structure.
2) Install the bolt [11], washer [10], washer [8] and nut [7] that attaches the inboard
side of the flap track [1] to the structure.
3) Install the bolt [3], washer [4], washer [5] and nut [6] that attaches the outboard side
of the flap track [1] to the structure.
(c) Attach the forward end of the flap track [1]:
1) Apply grease, D00633 to the outside of the fuse pin [20] and the inside of the
bushings.
2) Install the fuse pin [20] that attaches the forward end of the flap track [1] to the track
attach fitting.
(d) Tighten the nut [7] 1300 in-lb (147 N·m) - 1800 in-lb (203 N·m).
(e) Tighten the nut [6] 870 in-lb (98 N·m) - 1300 in-lb (147 N·m).
(f) Make sure you can turn the fuse pin [20] in the joint with a maximum of 10 in-lb (1 N·m).
NOTE: You can push up on the forward end of the flap track [1] to take the weight off the
fuse pin [20] when you measure the torque.
(g) Install the washer [21] and nut [22] on the fuse pin [20].
(h) Tighten the nut [22] 110 in-lb (12 N·m) - 130 in-lb (15 N·m).
(i) Loosen the nut [22] to align the hole for the pin [23].
(j) Install the pin [23] in the nut [22].
SUBTASK 27-51-25-420-003
(4) Install the failsafe fitting assembly [19] on the track attach fitting:
(a) Put the failsafe fitting assembly [19] in its location on the track attach fitting.
(b) Install the bolts [18] and washers [17] to attach the failsafe fitting assembly [19].
SUBTASK 27-51-25-480-003
(5) If it is necessary, remove the adapter, SPL-1733 from the flap track [1].
SUBTASK 27-51-25-020-008
(6) Install the bolt [13], washer [12], washers [14] and nut [15] to connect the jumper wire [16] to
the flap track [1].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

SUBTASK 27-51-25-480-004
(1) If you will use the adapter, SPL-1733, install it on the flap track [41]:
(a) Install the adapter, SPL-1733 on the flap track [41] approximately 33 in. (84 cm) aft of the
track attach fitting.

flap track [41].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-51-25-020-012
(2) Remove the nut [56], washer [55], washer [54], washer [53] and bolt [52] to disconnect the
jumper wire [57] from the flap track [41].
SUBTASK 27-51-25-020-013
(3) Disconnect the forward end of the flap track [41]:
(a) Remove the bolts [59] and washers [58] that attach the failsafe fitting assembly [60] to the
track attach fitting.
(b) Remove the nut [63], washer [62] and fuse pin [61] from the forward end of the flap
track [41].
SUBTASK 27-51-25-020-014
(4) Disconnect the aft end of the flap track [41] from the structure:
(a) Remove the nut [46], washer [45], washer [44] and bolt [43] that attach the outboard side
of the flap track [41] to the structure.
(b) Remove the nut [47], washer [48], washer [50] and bolt [51] that attach the inboard side
of the flap track [41] to the structure.
(c) Measure the thickness of the shim [49].
1) Make sure to mark the track with this measurement data.
NOTE: This measurement data for the removal and replacement of the flap tracks
is an important step to obtain ample free movement in the fuse pin joint at
the forward end of the flap track and return of the flaps to former operating
condition.
SUBTASK 27-51-25-020-015
(5) If you will install a new flap track [41], remove the transmission attach fitting assembly [42] from
the flap track [41]:
(a) Remove the nuts [67], washers [66] and bolts [65] that attach the transmission attach
fitting assembly [42] to the flap track [41].
NOTE: The washers [66] are adjacent to the washers that are bonded to the
transmission attach fitting assembly [42].

2. Outboard Flap Outboard Track Inspection
(Figure 601)
A. General
(1) This task gives wear limits for the outboard track on the outboard flap.
(2) this task is applicable to the flap tracks at flap supports No. 1 and 8.
B. References
Reference Title
27-51-25-000-801 Outboard Flap Outboard Track Removal (P/B 401)
27-51-25-400-801 Outboard Flap Outboard Track Installation (P/B 401)
C. Tools/Equipment
Reference Description
STD-1096 Micrometer - Depth, 0-1 inch, Readable to 1/1000 inch
STD-1097 Caliper - Vernier, 0-6 inch, Readable to 1/1000 inch
D. Location Zones
Zone Area
544 Left Wing - Fairing Flap Support No. 1
644 Right Wing - Fairing Flap Support No. 8
E. Procedure
SUBTASK 27-51-25-020-017
(1) Do this task: Outboard Flap Outboard Track Removal, TASK 27-51-25-000-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-25-020-018
(2) Use these tools to do a check for wear on the part of the outboard flap outboard track:
(a) micrometer (0-1 inch, readable to 1/1000 inch), STD-1096
(b) vernier caliper (0 - 6 inch, readable to 1/1000 inch), STD-1097.
SUBTASK 27-51-25-020-019
(3) Examine the parts of the outboard flap outboard track (Table 601):

SUBTASK 27-51-26-020-001
(1) If it is necessary to remove more than two aft flap tracks and aft flap [2], do this task: Outboard
Aft Flap Removal, TASK 27-51-22-000-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-26-860-001
WARNING
IF YOU REMOVE ONE OR TWO AFT FLAP TRACKS WITH THE AFT FLAP
ATTACHED TO THE MAIN FLAP, MAKE SURE THE INBOARD AND
OUTBOARD AFT FLAP PROGRAMMING ROLLERS REMAIN ENGAGED IN
THEIR RELATED PROGRAMMING TRACKS. ROLLERS CAN BECOME
DISENGAGED FROM THE PROGRAMMING TRACKS AND CAN CAUSE
INJURY TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE THE AFT FLAP FAIRING.
(2) If it is necessary to remove one or two aft flap tracks and extend the trailing edge flaps to the
40-unit position, do this task: Extend the Trailing Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-803.
SUBTASK 27-51-26-040-001
(3) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Deactivation, TASK 27-51-00-040-801.
D. Outboard Aft Flap Track Removal
SUBTASK 27-51-26-020-002
(1) For the outboard aft flap track No. 1 [3], remove the cotter pin [12], nut [11], washer [10],
washer [8], bolt [7], and bushing [9] that attach it to the aft flap [2] (View A, Figure 401).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-51-26-020-003
(2) For the aft flap track No. 2 [4], aft flap track No. 3 [5], or aft flap track No. 4 [6], remove the
cotter pin [18], nut [17], washer [16], bushing [15], washer [14], and bolt [13] that attach it to the
aft flap [2] (View B, Figure 401).
SUBTASK 27-51-26-020-004
(3) Remove the aft flap track assembly from the main flap [1] (View D, Figure 401).
NOTE: The flap track assemblies at each of the track positions are similar in assembly. The rib
aft track support, aft flap track, and rub plate assembly part numbers are specific to
each of the track positions.
(a) Remove the lockwire or safety cable, bolts [19], and washers [20] that attach the
cartridge assemblies [21] to the track support rib [22] on the main flap [1] (View E,
Figure 401).
(b) Retain the barrel nuts [19A] and retainer clips [20A] in the aft flap rib support.
NOTE: If the barrel nuts and retainer clips come out, mark their location and keep them
for installation later.
(c) Remove the cartridge assemblies [21] from the track support rib [22].
NOTE: There are four cartridge assemblies in the track support rib at each track position.
(d) Remove the lockwire or safety cable, bolts [101], and washers [102] that attach the left
rub plate assembly [110] and right rub plate assembly [111] to the track support rib [22]
(View F, Figure 401).
(e) Carefully remove the aft flap track together with left rub plate assembly [110] and right rub
plate assembly [111] from the track support rib [22].
SUBTASK 27-51-26-000-001
(4) Remove the down stop from the forward end of the aft flap track assembly (View D,
Figure 401).
(a) Remove the bolt [26], washer [27], washer [29], bushings [28], and nut [30] from the aft
flap track.

F. Outboard Aft Flap Track Installation
SUBTASK 27-51-26-420-001
(1) If the downstop is not installed on the applicable aft flap track, do these steps:
(a) Install the bolt [26], bushings [28], washer [27], washer [29], and nut [30] on the aft flap
track.
(b) Tighten the nut [30] the minimum amount to necessary to hold the bushings [28] tight.
SUBTASK 27-51-26-420-002
(2) Install the aft flap track assembly in the main flap [1] (View D, Figure 401).
NOTE: The flap track assemblies at each of the track positions are similar in assembly. The rib
aft track support , aft flap track, and rub plate assembly part numbers are specific to
each of the track positions.
(a) Insert the left rub plate assembly [110] and right rub plate assembly [111] into the sides of
the aft flap track with the nutlock plates facing inward to the centerline of the track.
(b) Carefully place the aft track together with the rub plates in its position in the track support
rib [22] of the main flap [1].
(c) Install the bolts [101], washers [102] that attach the left rub plate assembly [110] and right
rub plate assembly [111] to either side of the track support rib [22] (View F, Figure 401).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(d) Install MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, or safety cable kit, G50375, on the bolts [101] at
each side of the track.
(e) Apply a layer of grease, D00633, to the outside of the cartridge assemblies [21] and
inside diameter of the track support rib [22].
(f) Put the cartridge assemblies [21] in position in the track support rib [22].
1) Install the forward cartridge assembly [21] first so that you can access the barrel
nuts [19A] and retainer clips [20A] if necessary.
(g) If the barrel nuts [19A] and retainer clips [20A] did not remain in the rib support, install
them in the track support rib [22] before installing the attaching bolts [19] (View E,
Figure 401).
(h) Install the bolts [19] and washers [20] that attach the cartridge assemblies [21] to the
track support rib [22] (View E, Figure 401).
1) Install MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, or safety cable kit, G50375, on the two
bolts [19] at each of the four cartridge assemblies [21].
SUBTASK 27-51-26-420-005
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT YOU ENGAGE THE INBOARD-AND-OUTBOARD AFT
FLAP-PROGRAMMING-ROLLERS IN THEIR RELATED PROGRAMMING
TRACKS. ROLLERS CAN DISENGAGE FROM THE PROGRAMMING TRACKS
AND CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE THE AFT FLAP
FAIRING.
(3) If the aft flap [2] is installed, connect the applicable aft flap track to the aft flap [2].
(a) Connect the aft flap track No. 1 [3] to the aft flap [2] as follows:
1) Move the aft flap track No. 1 [3] until it aligns with the aft flap [2].
2) Apply grease, D00633, to the shank of the bolt [7] and inside of the bushing [9].
a) Make sure that you do not get grease, D00633, on the threads of the bolt [7].
3) Install the bushing [9], bolt [7], and washer [8] that attach the aft flap track No. 1 [3]
to the aft flap [2].
4) Carefully clean all of grease, D00633, from the threads of the bolt [7].
5) Install the washer [10] and nut [11] on the bolt [7].
6) Tighten the nut [11] to 65 in-lb (7.3 N·m) - 100 in-lb (11.3 N·m).
7) Install the cotter pin [12] in the nut [11].
(b) Connect the aft flap track No. 2 [4], aft flap track No. 3 [5], or aft flap track No. 4 [6] to the
aft flap [2] as follows:
1) Move the applicable aft flap track until it aligns with the aft flap [2].
2) Apply grease, D00633, to the shank of the bolt [13] and the inside of the
bushing [15].
a) Make sure that you do not get grease, D00633, on the threads of the bolt [13].
3) Install the bolt [13], washer [14], and bushing [15] that attach the aft flap track No.
2 [4], aft flap track No. 3 [5], or aft flap track No. 4 [6] to the aft flap [2].
4) Carefully clean all of grease, D00633, from the threads of the bolt [13].
5) Install the washer [16] and nut [17] on the bolt [13].
6) Tighten the nut [17] to 130 in-lb (14.7 N·m) - 200 in-lb (22.6 N·m).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
7) Install the cotter pin [18] in the nut [17].
SUBTASK 27-51-26-420-006
(4) If it is not installed, install the aft flap [2], do this task: Outboard Aft Flap Installation,
TASK 27-51-22-400-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-26-640-001
(5) Lubricate the cartridge assemblies [21] with grease, D00633, do this task: Outboard Main Flap
and Aft Flap Roller and Linkage Lubrication, TASK 12-22-51-640-812.
SUBTASK 27-51-26-860-002
(6) If the trailing edge flaps are not in the retracted position, retract the flaps:
(a) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Reactivation, TASK 27-51-00-440-801.
(b) Retract the flaps to the retracted position, do this task: Retract the Trailing Edge Flaps,
TASK 27-51-00-860-804.
(c) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Deactivation, TASK 27-51-00-040-801.
G. Outboard Aft Flap Adjustment
SUBTASK 27-51-26-480-001
(1) On the inboard and outboard flap supports, install the rig pins (rigging pin kit, SPL-1585) in the
rig pin holes in the bellcrank [51] and the flap carriage (Figure 402).
(a) If it is necessary, move the aft flap [2] or main flap [1] until you can install the rig pins.
SUBTASK 27-51-26-980-001
(2) Support the aft flap [2] to make sure that the programming rollers touch the bottom surface of
the programming tracks and the aft rollers for the aft flap tracks touch the top surface of the
tracks.
NOTE: This is the position the rollers will be in with airloads applied to the flap.
SUBTASK 27-51-26-220-001
(3) Measure the clearance between the main flap [1] and the upper surface of the aft flap [2] (View
C, Figure 402).
(a) Measure the clearance at all of the cove panel supports [52] and at the track support
ribs [22].
SUBTASK 27-51-26-220-002
(4) Make sure that the rub strip [50] and Teflon coating on the upper surface of the aft flap [2] are
not damaged (View C, Figure 402).
(a) If the rub strip [50] is damaged or missing, do this task: Bonded Phenolic or Stainless
Steel Rub Pad Repair (Heat Source Available), TASK 51-51-00-340-802.
(b) If the Telfon coating is damaged, do this task: Apply The Abrasion-Resistant Teflon Finish,
BMS 10-86 Type I, TASK 51-21-81-370-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-26-820-001
(5) If the clearance between the main flap [1] and aft flap [2] is not in the limit of
0.010 +0.100 / -0.010 in. (0.25 +2.54 / -0.25 mm), change the thickness of the shims [61] on
the cove panel support [52] or the shims [61] on the track support rib [22].
(a) Remove the rig pins from the bellcranks [51].
(b) Extend the aft flap [2], until you can get access to the fasteners for the shim [57] and
shims [61], do this task: Extend the Trailing Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-803.
(c) If it is necessary, change the thickness of the shims [61] on the cove panel support [52]
as follows:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Remove the nuts [56], washers [55], and bolts [54] that attach the cove panel [53] to
the cove panel support [52].
2) Remove the shim [57] from the cove panel support [52] and cove panel [53].
3) Change the thickness of the shim [57].
NOTE: The maximum permitted thickness of the shim is 0.050 in. (1.27 mm).
4) Apply sealant, A00247, to the mating surfaces of the shim [57].
5) Put the shim [57] in its position between the cove panel support [52] and cove
panel [53].
6) Install the bolts [54], washers [55], and nuts [56].
(d) If it is necessary, change the thickness of the shims [61] on the track support rib [22] as
follows:
1) Remove the nuts [60], washers [59], and bolts [58] that attach the cove panel [53] to
the track support rib [22].
2) Remove the shims [61] from the track support rib [22] and cove panel [53].
3) Change the thickness of the shims [61].
NOTE: The maximum permitted thickness of the shim is 0.050 in. (1.27 mm).
4) Apply sealant, A00247, to the mating surfaces of the shims [61].
5) Put the shims [61] in their position between the track support rib [22] and cove
panel [53].
6) Install the bolts [58], washers [59], and nuts [60].
7) If it is necessary, trim the excess shim [61] that extends past the track support
rib [22].
(e) Retract the aft flap [2] until you can install the rig pins in the bellcranks [51], do this task:
Retract the Trailing Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-804.
(f) Install the rig pins in the bellcranks [51].
(g) Make sure that the clearance between the main flap [1] and upper surface of the aft
flap [2] is in the limit.
H. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 27-51-26-440-001
(1) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Reactivation, TASK 27-51-00-440-801.

(2) Use the primary system to extend and retract the flaps, do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System

SUBTASK 27-51-28-420-002

 ALL

(d) Apply primer, C00259, to all areas of the holes for the bolts [4] and bolts [6].

bolts [6].

1) Tighten the bolts [4] to 90 in-lb (10 N·m) - 125 in-lb (14 N·m).

H. Outboard Flap Outboard Support Aft Fairing Installation
SUBTASK 27-51-28-020-005
(1) If the fairing drive linkage is not installed on the aft fairing assembly [2], do these steps:
NOTE: The fairing drive linkage includes the drive rod assembly, adjust link assembly, adjust
rod assembly and the attach beam assembly.
(a) Connect the adjust rod assembly [42] to the adjust link assembly [41]:
1) Install the bushing [45], bolt [43], washer [44], washer [46], and nut [47] that attach
the adjust rod assembly [42] to the adjust link assembly [41].
a) For the left wing, install the bolt [43] with the head on the same side of the
adjust link assembly [41] as the bushing [45].
b) For the right wing, install the bolt [43] with the head on the opposite side of the
adjust link assembly [41] as the bushing [45].
2) Install the pin [48] in the nut [47].
(b) Connect the adjust link assembly [41] to the attach beam assembly [33]:
1) Put the adjust link assembly [41] in its position on the attach beam assembly [33].
2) Install the bushing [51], bolt [49], washer [50], washer [52], and nut [53] to attach the
adjust link assembly [41] to the attach beam assembly [33].
3) Tighten the nut [53]:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
a) Tighten the nut [53] to 370 in-lb (41.8 N·m) - 475 in-lb (53.7 N·m), if the
bolt [49] is not lubricated.
b) Tighten the nut [53] to 260 in-lb (29.4 N·m) - 310 in-lb (35.0 N·m), if the
bolt [49] is lubricated with grease, D00633, or grease, D00013.
4) Install the pin [54] in the nut [53].
(c) Connect the drive rod assembly [32] to the attach beam assembly [33]:
1) Put the drive rod assembly [32] in its position on the attach beam assembly [33].
2) Install the bushing [28], bolt [26], washer [27], washer [29], and nut [30] to attach the
drive rod assembly [32] to the attach beam assembly [33].
3) Install the pin [31] in the nut [30].
(d) Connect the adjust link assembly [41] to the aft fairing assembly [2]:
1) Put the adjust link assembly [41] in its location on the aft fairing assembly [2] with
the bolt [62], washer [55], washer [63], washer [64], washer [69], washers [58],
bushing [60], bushing [61], and nut [57].
a) Use the necessary quantity and/or location of washer [55], washer [64], and
washer [69], to achieve clearance from 0.010 in. (0.25 mm) to 0.025 in.
(0.64 mm) (View A-A, Figure 401).
b) Make sure that link assembly [41] is centered between the clevis.
NOTE: Install the same number of washers in the same location as you
removed them.
2) Tighten the nut [57]:
a) Tighten the nut [57] to 530 in-lb (59.9 N·m) - 690 in-lb (78.0 N·m), if the
bolt [62] is not lubricated.
b) Tighten the nut [57] to 345 in-lb (39.0 N·m) - 425 in-lb (48.0 N·m), if the
bolt [62] is lubricated with grease, D00633, or grease, D00013.
3) Measure the clearance between the washer [58] and the flange on the flanged
bushing [59].
4) If the clearance is not 0.010 in. (0.25 mm) to 0.025 in. (0.64 mm), do these steps:
a) Remove the nut [57], washers [58], washer [55], washer [69], washer [64],
washer [63], bolt [62], bushing [60], and bushing [61].
b) Change the quantity and/or location of the washer [55], washer [64], and
washer [69].
c) Install the bushing [60], bushing [61], bolt [62], washer [63], washer [64],
washer [55], washer [69], washers [58], and nut [57].
d) Make sure that the clearance between the washer [58] and the flange on the
flanged bushing [59] is in the limit of 0.010 in. (0.25 mm) to 0.025 in.
(0.64 mm).
e) Tighten the nut [57] to 530 in-lb (59.9 N·m) - 690 in-lb (78.0 N·m), if the
bolt [62] is not lubricated.
f) Tighten the nut [57] to 345 in-lb (39.0 N·m) - 425 in-lb (48.0 N·m), if the
bolt [62] is lubricated with grease, D00633, or grease, D00013.
5) Install the pin [56] in the nut [57].
(e) Connect the adjust rod assembly [42] to the aft fairing assembly [2]:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Install the bushing [45], bolt [43], washer [44], washer [46], and nut [47] that attach
the adjust rod assembly [42] to the aft fairing assembly [2].
2) Install the pin [48] in the nut [47].
SUBTASK 27-51-28-420-003
(2) Install the aft fairing assembly [2]:
(a) Connect the jumper wires [22]:
1) Lift the forward end of the aft fairing assembly [2] until you can put the jumper
wires [22] on the studs.
2) Install the washers [12] and nuts [11] to attach the jumper wires [22].
3) Apply sealant, A02315, to the nuts [11].
(b) Connect the forward end of the aft fairing assembly [2] to the transmission attach
fitting [10]:
1) Lift the forward end of the aft fairing assembly [2] until it aligns with the transmission
attach fitting [10].
2) Install the bushing [17], pivot bolt [15], washer [18], washer [16] and nut [19].
3) Tighten the nut [19]:
a) Tighten the nut [19] to 1200 in-lb (135.6 N·m) - 1410 in-lb (159.3 N·m), if the
bolt [15] is not lubricated.
b) Tighten the nut [19] to 920 in-lb (103.9 N·m) - 1000 in-lb (113.0 N·m), if the
bolt [15] is lubricated with grease, D00633, or grease, D00013.
(c) Connect the aft end of the aft fairing assembly [2]:
1) Move the attach beam assembly [33] until it aligns with the flap track [7].
2) Install the bushing [37], bolt [35], washer [36], washer [38], and nut [39].
3) Tighten the nut [39]:
a) Tighten the nut [39] to 870 in-lb (98.3 N·m) - 1070 in-lb (120.9 N·m), if the
bolt [35] is not lubricated.
b) Tighten the nut [39] to 555 in-lb (62.7 N·m) - 650 in-lb (73.4 N·m), if the
bolt [35] is lubricated with grease, D00633, or grease, D00013.
4) Install the pin [40] in the nut [39].
5) Align the drive rod assembly [32] with the carriage [25].
6) Install the bushing [28], bolt [26], washer [27], washer [29], and nut [30].
a) Install the bolt [26] with the head on the outboard side.
7) Install the pin [31] in the nut [30].

H. Outboard Flap Inboard Support Aft Fairing Installation
SUBTASK 27-51-28-020-010
(1) If the fairing drive linkage is not installed on the aft fairing assembly [82], do these steps:
NOTE: The fairing drive linkage includes the drive rod assembly, adjust link assembly, adjust
rod assembly and the attach beam assembly.
(a) Connect the adjust rod assembly [121] to the adjust link assembly [120]:
1) Install the bushing [124], bolt [122], washer [123], washer [125], and nut [126] that
attach the adjust rod assembly [121] to the adjust link assembly [120].
a) For the left wing, install the bolt [122] with the head on the same side of the
adjust link assembly [120] as the bushing [124].
b) For the right wing, install the bolt [122] with the head on the opposite side of
the adjust link assembly [120] as the bushing [124].
2) Install the pin [127] in the nut [126].
(b) Connect the adjust link assembly [120] to the attach beam assembly [134]:
1) Put the adjust link assembly [120] in its position on the attach beam assembly [134].
2) Install the bushing [130], bolt [128], washer [129], washer [131], and nut [132] to
attach the adjust link assembly [120] to the attach beam assembly [134].
3) Tighten the nut [132]:
a) Tighten the nut [132] to 370 in-lb (41.8 N·m) - 475 in-lb (53.7 N·m), if the
bolt [128] is not lubricated.
b) Tighten the nut [132] to 260 in-lb (29.4 N·m) - 310 in-lb (35.0 N·m), if the
bolt [128] is lubricated with grease, D00633, or grease, D00013.
4) Install the pin [133] in the nut [132].
(c) Connect the drive rod assembly [112] to the attach beam assembly [134]:
1) Put the drive rod assembly [112] in its position on the attach beam assembly [134].
2) Install the bushing [108], bolt [106], washer [107], washer [109], and nut [110] to
attach the drive rod assembly [112] to the attach beam assembly [134].
3) Install the pin [111] in the nut [110].
(d) Connect the adjust link assembly [120] to the aft fairing assembly [82]:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Put the adjust link assembly [120] in its location on the aft fairing assembly [82] with
the bolt [142], washer [143], washer [144], washer [135], washer [151],
washers [138], bushing [140], and bushing [141].
a) Use the necessary quantity and/or location of washer [144], washer [135], and
washer [151], to achieve clearance from 0.010 in. (0.25 mm) to 0.025 in.
(0.64 mm) (View A-A, Figure 402).
b) Make sure that the adjust link assembly [120] is centered between clevis.
NOTE: Install the same number of washers in the same location as you
removed them.
2) Tighten the nut [137]:
a) Tighten the nut [137] to 530 in-lb (59.9 N·m) - 690 in-lb (78.0 N·m), if the
bolt [142] is not lubricated.
b) Tighten the nut [137] to 345 in-lb (39.0 N·m) - 425 in-lb (48.0 N·m), if the
bolt [142] is lubricated with grease, D00633, or grease, D00013.
3) Measure the clearance between the washer [138] and the flange on the flanged
bushing [139].
4) If the clearance is not 0.010 in. (0.25 mm) to 0.025 in. (0.64 mm), do these steps:
a) Remove the nut [137], washers [138], washer [151], washer [135],
washer [144], washer [143], bolt [142], bushing [141], and bushing [140].
b) Change the quantity and/or location of the washer [151], washer [135], and
washer [144].
c) Install the bushing [140], bushing [141], bolt [142], washer [143], washer [144],
washer [135], washer [151], washers [138], and nut [137].
d) Make sure the clearance between the washer [138] and the flange on the
flanged bushing [139] is in the limit of 0.010 in. (0.25 mm) to 0.025 in.
(0.64 mm).
e) Tighten the nut [137] to 530 in-lb (59.9 N·m) - 690 in-lb (78.0 N·m), if the
bolt [142] is not lubricated.
f) Tighten the nut [137] to 345 in-lb (39.0 N·m) - 425 in-lb (48.0 N·m), if the
bolt [142] is lubricated with grease, D00633, or grease, D00013.
5) Install the cotter pin [136] in the nut [137].
(e) Connect the adjust rod assembly [121] to the aft fairing assembly [82]:
1) Install the bushing [124], bolt [122], washer [123], washer [125], and nut [126] that
attach the adjust rod assembly [121] to the aft fairing assembly [82].
2) Install the pin [127] in the nut [126].

EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

3) Tighten the nut [101]:

pivot bolt [97] is not lubricated.
b) Tighten the nut [101] to 920 in-lb (103.9 N·m) - 1000 in-lb (113.0 N·m), if the
pivot bolt [97] is lubricated with grease, D00633, or grease, D00013.
(c) Connect the aft end of the aft fairing assembly [82]:

2) Install the bushing [116], bolt [114], washer [115], washer [117], and nut [118].
3) Tighten the nut [118]:
a) Tighten the nut [118] to 1300 in-lb (146.9 N·m) - 1470 in-lb (166.1 N·m), if the

b) Tighten the nut [118] to 840 in-lb (94.9 N·m) - 920 in-lb (103.9 N·m), if the

4) Install the pin [119] in the nut [118].

G. Prepare for the Adjustment
SUBTASK 27-51-28-860-005
(1) If the trailing edge flaps are not in the retracted position, do this task: Retract the Trailing Edge

SUBTASK 27-51-28-040-005
(2) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Deactivation, TASK 27-51-00-040-801.
H. Outboard Flap Outboard Support Aft Fairing Adjustment
SUBTASK 27-51-28-480-001
(1) Apply the 150 lb (68 kg) weight to preload the aft fairing assembly [4].
(a) Put a strap across the top of the aft fairing assembly [4] at the line of fasteners for the
tailcone [5].
(b) Attach the 150 lb (68 kg) weight to the strap.
1) Make sure that the weight is evenly applied to the inboard and outboard sides of the
aft fairing assembly [4].
SUBTASK 27-51-28-820-005
(2) Move the preload pads [7] away from the aft flap [1].
NOTE: It is necessary to move the preload pads to correctly measure the clearance between
the aft flap and the aft fairing assembly.
(a) Loosen the bolts [8] that attach the preload pads [7] to the aft fairing assembly [4].
(b) Move the preload pads [7] away from the lower surface of the aft flap [1].
SUBTASK 27-51-28-220-001
(3) Measure the clearance between the top surface of the aft fairing assembly [4] and the aft
flap [1].
NOTE: It is necessary to measure the clearance at the aft edge of the aft flap on the sides of
the aft fairing assembly.
(a) Make sure that the clearance is in the limit of 0.2639 ±0.0500 in. (6.703 ±1.270 mm).
(b) Make sure that the clearance is approximately the same on the inboard and outboard
sides of the aft fairing assembly [4].
SUBTASK 27-51-28-820-006
(4) If the clearance is not in the limit, or if it is not the same on the inboard and outboard sides,
then adjust the position of the aft fairing assembly [4].
(a) On the side of the aft fairing assembly [4] open the applicable access panels:
Number Name/Location
544DR Flap Support No. 1 Access Door
644DL Flap Support No. 8, Access Door
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) If the clearance is not the same on the inboard and outboard sides, adjust the length of
the adjust rod [21].
1) Remove the weight from the aft fairing assembly [4].
2) Remove the nut [14], washer [13], washer [11], bolt [10], and bushing [12] that
attach the drive rod [17] to the carriage [9].
NOTE: Support the aft fairing assembly when you remove the bolt.
3) Lower the aft end of the aft fairing assembly [4] to get access to the adjust rod [21].
4) Loosen the locknuts [20] on the adjust rod [21].
5) Adjust the length of the adjust rod [21] until the clearance is the same on the
inboard and outboard sides of the aft fairing assembly [4].
6) Tighten the locknuts [20] on the adjust rod [21].
7) Install lockwire on the locknuts [20].
8) Lift the aft end of the aft fairing assembly [4] and align the drive rod [17] with the
carriage [9].
9) Install the bushing [12], bolt [10], washer [11], washer [13], and nut [14] to attach the
drive rod [17] to the carriage [9].
a) Make sure that you install the bolt [10] with the head on the outboard side.
10) Install the cotter pin [15] in the nut [14].
(c) If the clearance is not in the limit, adjust the length of the drive rod [17].
1) Loosen the locknuts [16] on the drive rod [17].
2) Adjust the length of the drive rod [17] until the clearance is in the limit.
3) Tighten the locknuts [16] on the drive rod [17].
4) Install the lockwire on the locknuts [16].
(d) Make sure that the clearance is in the limit and that it is the same on the inboard and
outboard sides of the aft fairing assembly [4].
SUBTASK 27-51-28-820-007
(5) Adjust the position of the preload pads [7].
(a) With the 150 lb (68 kg) weight applied to the aft fairing assembly [4], move the preload
pads [7] up until they touch the lower surface of the aft flap [1].
(b) Tighten the bolts [8] that attach the preload pads [7].
SUBTASK 27-51-28-080-001
(6) Remove the 150 lb (68 kg) weight and the strap from the aft fairing assembly [4].
SUBTASK 27-51-28-210-001
(7) Make sure that the seals [6] on the sides of the aft fairing assembly [4] are compressed 10 to
25 percent against the lower surface of the flap.
SUBTASK 27-51-28-820-008
(8) If the seals [6] are not compressed correctly against the lower surface of the flap, adjust the
position of the seals [6].
(a) Remove the nut [14], washer [13], washer [11], bolt [10], and bushing [12] that attach the
drive rod [17] to the carriage [9].
(b) Lower the aft end of the aft fairing assembly [4] to get access to the fasteners for the
seals [6].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(c) Loosen the nuts [18] on the retainer [19].
(d) Move the seal [6] and the retainer [19].
1) Make sure that you move the seal [6] and the retainer [19] together as a unit.
(e) Tighten the nuts [18] on the retainer [19].
(f) Lift the aft end of the aft fairing assembly [4] and align the drive rod [17] with the
carriage [9].
(g) Install the bushing [12], bolt [10], washer [11], washer [13], and nut [14] to attach the drive
rod [17] to the carriage [9].
1) Make sure that you install the bolt [10] with the head on the outboard side.
(h) Install the cotter pin [15] in the nut [14].
SUBTASK 27-51-28-410-007
(9) On the side of the aft fairing assembly [4] close the applicable access panels:
Number Name/Location
544DR Flap Support No. 1 Access Door
644DL Flap Support No. 8, Access Door
I. Outboard Flap Outboard Forward Fairing Adjustment
SUBTASK 27-51-28-220-002
(1) Measure the mismatch between the forward fairing assembly [3] and the aft fairing
assembly [4].
NOTE: It is necessary to measure the mismatch on the inboard side and on the bottom of the
forward fairing assembly.
(a) Make sure that the mismatch is in the limit of +0.03 in. (0.76 mm) to -0.01 in. (0.25 mm).
NOTE: A positive (+) mismatch is when the forward fairing assembly extends past the aft
fairing assembly. A negative (-) mismatch is when the aft fairing assembly
extends past the forward fairing assembly.
SUBTASK 27-51-28-220-003
(2) Make sure that the seals [26] on the sides of the forward fairing assembly [3] are compressed
10 to 25 percent against the lower surface of the wing.
SUBTASK 27-51-28-020-011
(3) If the mismatch is not in the limit or if the seals [26] are not compressed correctly, do this task:
Outboard Flap Outboard Support Forward Fairing Removal, TASK 27-51-28-000-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-28-820-009
(4) If the mismatch between the forward fairing assembly [3] and the aft fairing assembly [4] is not
in the limit, then adjust the position of the forward fairing assembly [3].
(a) If the mismatch is not in the limit on the inboard side of the forward fairing assembly [3],
then adjust the position of the fairing attach fitting [24].
1) Loosen the bolts [23] that attach the fairing attach fitting [24] to the transmission
attach fitting [22].
2) Move the fairing attach fitting [24] inboard or outboard to get the mismatch in the
clearance.
3) Tighten the bolts [23].
4) Install lockwire on bolts [23].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) If the mismatch is not in the limit on the bottom of the forward fairing assembly [3],
change the thickness of the shims [25].
1) Apply primer, C00259, to the mating surfaces of the shim [25] and the fairing attach
fitting [24].
SUBTASK 27-51-28-820-010
(5) If the seals [26] are not compressed evenly against the lower surface of the wing, then adjust
the position of the seals [26].
(a) Loosen the nuts [27] on the retainer [28].
(b) Move the seal [26] and the retainer [28].
(c) Tighten the nuts [27] that hold the retainer [28].
SUBTASK 27-51-28-420-007
(6) If you removed the forward fairing assembly [3], do this task: Outboard Flap Outboard Support
Forward Fairing Installation, TASK 27-51-28-400-801.
J. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

(1) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Reactivation, TASK 27-51-00-440-801.

attach the drive rod [57] to the carriage [49].
a) Support the aft fairing [44] when you remove the bolt [50].
3) Lower the aft end of the aft fairing [44] to get access to the adjust rod [60].
4) Loosen the locknuts [61] on the adjust rod [60].
5) Adjust the length of the adjust rod [60] until the clearance is the same on the
inboard and outboard sides of the aft fairing [44].
6) Tighten the locknuts [61] on the adjust rod [60].
7) Install the lockwire on the locknuts [61].
8) Lift the aft end of the aft fairing [44] and align the drive rod [57] with the
carriage [49].
9) Install the bushing [52], bolt [50], washer [51], washer [53], and nut [54] to attach the
drive rod [57] to the carriage [49].
a) Make sure that you install the bolt [50] with the head on the outboard side.
10) Install the cotter pin [55] in the nut [54].
(c) If the clearance is not in the limit, adjust the length of the drive rod [57].
1) Loosen the locknuts [56]l on the drive rod [57].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
2) Adjust the length of the drive rod [57] until the clearance is in the limit.
3) Tighten the locknuts [56] on the drive rod [57].
4) Instal the lockwire on the locknuts [56].
(d) Make sure that the clearance is in the limit and that it is the same on the inboard and
outboard sides of the aft fairing [44].
SUBTASK 27-51-28-820-013
(5) Adjust the position of the preload pads [59].
(a) With the 150 lb (68 kg) weight applied to the aft fairing [44], move the preload pads [59]
up until they touch the lower surface of the aft flap [41].
(b) Tighten the bolts [58] that attach the preload pads [59].
SUBTASK 27-51-28-080-002
(6) Remove the weight from the aft fairing [44].
SUBTASK 27-51-28-210-002
(7) Make sure that the seals [47] on the sides of the aft fairing [44] are compressed 10 to 25
percent against the lower surface of the flap.
SUBTASK 27-51-28-820-014
(8) If the seals [47] are not compressed correctly against the lower surface of the flap, adjust the
position of the seals [47].
(a) Remove the nut [54], washer [53], washer [51], bolt [50], and bushing [52] that attach the
drive rod [57] to the carriage [49].
(b) Lower the aft end of the aft fairing [44] to get access to the fasteners for the seals [47].
(c) Loosen the nuts [46] on the retainer [48].
(d) Move the seal [47] and retainer [48].
1) Make sure that you move the seal [47] and retainer [48] together as a unit.
(e) Tighten the nuts [46] on the retainer [48].
(f) Lift the aft end of the aft fairing [44] to align the drive rod [57] with the carriage [49].
(g) Install the bushing [52], bolt [50], washer [51], washer [53], and nut [54] to attach the
drive rod [57] to the carriage [49].
1) Make sure that you install the bolt [50] with the head on the outboard side.
(h) Install the cotter pin [55] in the nut [54].
SUBTASK 27-51-28-410-008
(9) On the side of the aft fairing [44] close the applicable access panels:
Number Name/Location
543DR Flap Support No. 2 Access Door
643DL Flap Support No. 7, Access Door
I. Outboard Flap Inboard Forward Fairing Adjustment
SUBTASK 27-51-28-220-005
(1) Measure the mismatch between the forward fairing [43] and aft fairing [44].
NOTE: It is necessary to measure the mismatch on the inboard side and on the bottom of the
forward fairing.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Make sure that the mismatch is in the limit of +0.03 in. (0.76 mm) to -0.01 in. (-0.25 mm).
NOTE: A positive (+) mismatch is when the forward fairing extends past the aft fairing. A
negative (-) mismatch is when the aft fairing extends past the forward fairing.
SUBTASK 27-51-28-220-006
(2) Make sure that the seals [66] on the sides of the forward fairing [43] are compressed 10 to 25
percent against the lower surface of the wing.
SUBTASK 27-51-28-020-012
(3) If the mismatch is not in the limit or if the seals [66] are not compressed correctly, do this task:
Outboard Flap Inboard Support Forward Fairing Removal, TASK 27-51-28-000-803.
SUBTASK 27-51-28-820-015
(4) If the mismatch between the forward fairing [43] and aft fairing [44] is not in the limit, adjust the
position of the forward fairing [43].
(a) If the mismatch is not in the limit on the inboard side of the forward fairing [43], adjust the
position of the fairing attach fitting [64].
1) Loosen the bolts [63] that attach the fairing attach fitting [64] to the transmission
attach fitting [62].
2) Move the fairing attach fitting [64] inboard or outboard to get the mismatch in the
clearance.
3) Tighten the bolts [63].
4) Install the lockwire on the bolts [63].
(b) If the mismatch is not in the limit on the bottom of the forward fairing [43], change the
thickness of the shims [65].
1) Apply primer, C00259, to the mating surfaces of the shim [65] and fairing attach
fitting [64].
SUBTASK 27-51-28-820-016
(5) If the seals [66] are not compressed evenly against the lower surface of the wing, adjust the
position of the seal [66].
(a) Loosen the nuts [67] on the retainer [68].
(b) Move the seal [66] and retainer [68].
(c) Tighten the nuts [67] that hold the retainer [68].
SUBTASK 27-51-28-420-008
(6) If you removed the forward fairing [43], do this task: Outboard Flap Inboard Support Forward
Fairing Installation, TASK 27-51-28-400-803.
J. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 27-51-28-440-006
(1) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Reactivation, TASK 27-51-00-440-801.

27-51-31-000-801Inboard Flap Outboard Transmission RemovalPDF p. 2649
2. Inboard Flap Outboard Transmission Removal
(Figure 401)
A. General
(1) This task is applicable to the transmissions at flap supports No. 3 and 6.
B. References
Reference Title
27-51-00-040-801 Trailing Edge Flap System Deactivation (P/B 201)
27-51-00-860-803 Extend the Trailing Edge Flaps (P/B 201)
27-51-00-980-801 Trailing Edge Flap System Manual Operation (P/B 201)
27-51-18-000-802 Inboard Flap Support Aft Fairing Removal (P/B 401)
32-00-01 P/B 201 LANDING GEAR DOWNLOCK PINS - MAINTENANCE
PRACTICES
C. Location Zones
Zone Area
542 Left Wing - Fairing Flap Support No. 3
553 Left Wing - Inboard Flap
642 Right Wing - Fairing Flap Support No. 6
653 Right Wing - Inboard Flap
D. Prepare for the Removal
SUBTASK 27-51-31-860-001
(1) Extend the trailing edge flaps to the 40-unit position, do this task: Extend the Trailing Edge
Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-803.
SUBTASK 27-51-31-480-005
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED IN ALL OF THE
LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR
CAN RETRACT AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(2) Make sure that the downlock pins are installed in the nose and main landing gear
(PAGEBLOCK 32-00-01/201).
SUBTASK 27-51-31-040-001
(3) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Deactivation, TASK 27-51-00-040-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-31-010-001
(4) Do this task: Inboard Flap Support Aft Fairing Removal, TASK 27-51-18-000-802.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
E. Inboard Flap Outboard Transmission Removal
SUBTASK 27-51-31-980-001
(1) Manually extend the trailing edge flaps to the downstop on the ballscrew
(TASK 27-51-00-980-801).
SUBTASK 27-51-31-020-001
(2) Disconnect the torque tubes [1] from the transmission assembly [4]:
(a) Remove lockwire or safety cable from the screws [3].
(b) Remove the screws [3] that attach the coupling sleeves [2] to the splined couplings [5] on
the torque tubes [1].
(c) Move the coupling sleeves [2] off the splined couplings [5].
SUBTASK 27-51-31-020-002
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU HOLD THE BALLSCREW WHILE YOU DISCONNECT
IT. IF THE U-JOINT IS ALLOWED TO SUPPORT THE WEIGHT OF THE
BALLSCREW, THIS WILL CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE U-JOINT.
(3) Disconnect the ballscrew assembly [6] with the gimbal [14] from the carriage [8]:
(a) Install a support to hold the ballscrew assembly [6] when it is disconnected from the
carriage [8].
(b) Remove the nuts [11], washers [12], and bolts [7] that attach the carriage bushing [9] and
carriage bushing [13] to the carriage [8].
(c) Remove the carriage bushing [9] and carriage bushing [13] from the carriage [8].
(d) Move the gimbal [14] away from the carriage [8].
SUBTASK 27-51-31-020-003
(4) Disconnect the ballscrew assembly [6] from the yoke [16] on the transmission assembly [4]:
(a) Remove the nuts [20], washers [19], washers [18], and bolts [17] that attach the ballscrew
assembly [6] to the yoke [16].
(b) Remove the ballscrew assembly [6] from the yoke [16].
1) If it is necessary, turn the ballscrew assembly [6] and gimbal [14] to remove the
ballscrew assembly [6].
(c) Remove the ballscrew assembly [6] with the gimbal [14].
SUBTASK 27-51-31-020-004
(5) Remove the transmission assembly [4]:
NOTE: The transmission weighs approximately 50 lb (23 kg).
(a) Support the transmission assembly [4] while you disconnect the transmission attach
fitting [15] from the sideplates.
(b) Remove the nuts [24], washers [23], washers [22], and bolts [21] that attach the
transmission attach fitting [15] to the sideplates.
(c) Carefully lower the transmission assembly [4].

F. Inboard Flap Outboard Transmission Installation
SUBTASK 27-51-31-420-001
(1) Install the transmission assembly [4]:
NOTE: The transmission assembly weighs approximately 50 lb (23 kg).
(a) Use sealant, A00247, to fay seal the mating surface of the transmission attach fitting [15]
and sideplates.
(b) Carefully lift the transmission assembly [4] and position the transmission attach fitting [15]
on the sideplates.
(c) Install the bolts [21], washers [22], washers [23], and nuts [24] to attach the transmission
attach fitting [15] to the sideplates.
(d) Tighten the nuts [24] to 220 in-lb (24.9 N·m) - 410 in-lb (46.3 N·m).
1) As an option, you can tighten the bolts [21] to 369 in-lb (41.7 N·m) - 451 in-lb
(51.0 N·m).
(e) Wait a minimum of ten minutes and tighten the nuts [24] again.
1) If you initially tightened the bolts [21], tighten the bolts [21] again.
SUBTASK 27-51-31-420-002
(2) Connect the ballscrew assembly [6] to the yoke [16] on the transmission assembly [4]:
(a) Turn the ballscrew nut [28] until it is at the forward end of the ballscrew assembly [6].
(b) Apply a layer of grease, D00633, to the mating surfaces of the yoke [16] and ballscrew
assembly [6].
(c) Put the ballscrew assembly [6] into the yoke [16].
(d) Apply a layer of grease, D00633, to the shank and threads of the bolts [17].
(e) Install the bolts [17], washers [18], washers [19], and nuts [20] to attach the ballscrew
assembly [6] to the yoke [16].
(f) Make sure that the ballscrew assembly [6] is installed correctly in the yoke [16]:
1) Turn the transmission assembly [4] until the nut [29] on the u-joint [26] is up.
2) Turn the ballscrew nut [28] until the upstop is 180° from the upstop [27] on the
yoke [16].
3) If the ball returns [10] on the ballscrew nut [28] are not in the correct position,
change the position of the ballscrew assembly [6]:
NOTE: On the transmission No. 3, the ball returns should be on the outboard side.
On the transmission No. 6, the ball returns should be on the inboard side.
a) Remove the nuts [20], washers [19], washers [18], and bolts [17] that attach
the ballscrew assembly [6] to the yoke [16].
b) Turn the ballscrew assembly [6] 180° in the yoke [16].
c) Install the bolts [17], washers [18], washers [19], and nuts [20].
(g) Tighten the nuts [20] to 100 in-lb (11.3 N·m) - 120 in-lb (13.6 N·m) above run on torque.
SUBTASK 27-51-31-420-003
(3) Connect the ballscrew assembly [6] with the gimbal [14] to the carriage [8]:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Move the gimbal [14] to the downstop on the ballscrew assembly [6].
NOTE: On the transmission No. 3, the ball returns on the ballscrew nut should be on the
outboard side. On the transmission No. 6, the ball returns on the ballscrew nut
should be on the inboard side.
(b) Move the carriage [8] to align with the gimbal [14].
 006, 007, 013, 014
(c) Apply grease, D00633, to the inside and outside surfaces of the carriage bushing [9] and
carriage bushing [13].
 ALL
(d) Install the carriage bushing [9] and carriage bushing [13] to attach the gimbal [14] to the
carriage [8].
(e) Install the bolts [7], washers [12], and nuts [11] that attach the carriage bushing [9] and
carriage bushing [13] to the gimbal [14].
(f) Tighten the nuts [11] to 65 in-lb (7.3 N·m) - 75 in-lb (8.5 N·m) more than the run-on
torque.
SUBTASK 27-51-31-420-004
(4) Connect the torque tubes [1] to the transmission assembly [4]:
(a) Apply grease, D00633, to the coupling sleeves [2].
(b) Put the splined couplings [5] in the coupling sleeves [2].
(c) Install the screws [3] to attach the torque tubes [1] to the transmission assembly [4].
(d) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G50347, or safety cable kit, G51490, on the screws [3]
(PAGEBLOCK 20-10-44/401).
SUBTASK 27-51-31-640-003
(5) Apply grease, D00633, to the end of the plunger on the torque trip indicator [25] and push it
down around the sides of the plunger.
NOTE: Not all transmissions have torque trip indicator installed.
SUBTASK 27-51-31-640-001
(6) Lubricate the transmission assembly [4], ballscrew assembly [6], and gimbal [14]
(TASK 12-22-51-610-803 and TASK 12-22-51-640-803).
SUBTASK 27-51-31-210-001
(7) Make sure that the torque trip indicator [25] on the transmission assembly [4] is set.
NOTE: Not all transmissions have torque trip indicator installed.
SUBTASK 27-51-31-820-001
(8) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap Drive System Adjustment, TASK 27-51-00-820-802.
G. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 27-51-31-410-001
(1) Do this task: Inboard Flap Support Aft Fairing Installation, TASK 27-51-18-400-802.
SUBTASK 27-51-31-440-001
(2) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Reactivation, TASK 27-51-00-440-801.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-51-31-860-011
WARNING
KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL
SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE
COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC
POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(3) Supply hydraulic system B power (TASK 29-11-00-860-801).
SUBTASK 27-51-31-860-003
(4) Use the primary system to retract the flaps to the retracted position (TASK 27-51-00-860-801).
SUBTASK 27-51-31-860-004
(5) Use the primary system to extend and retract the flaps (TASK 27-51-00-860-801).
SUBTASK 27-51-31-210-002
(6) Make sure that the torque trip indicator [25] on the transmission assembly [4] is set.
NOTE: Not all transmissions have torque trip indicator installed.
SUBTASK 27-51-31-860-012
(7) Remove hydraulic system B power (TASK 29-11-00-860-805).

(2) Remove the u joint assembly [70]:

the transmission assembly [49] and the tee angle gearbox [69].

SUBTASK 27-51-31-020-006
CAUTION
MAKE SURE YOU HOLD THE BALLSCREW WHILE YOU DISCONNECT IT. IF
YOU LET THE U-JOINT HOLD THE BALLSCREW, YOU WILL CAUSE
DAMAGE TO THE U-JOINT.
(3) Disconnect the ballscrew assembly [42] with the gimbal [43] from the carriage [47]:

carriage [47].
(b) Remove the nuts [44], washers [45] and bolts [41] that attach the carriage bushings [46]
to the carriage [47].
(c) Remove the carriage bushings [46] from the carriage [47].
(d) Move the gimbal [43] away from the carriage [47].
SUBTASK 27-51-31-020-007
(4) Disconnect the ballscrew assembly [42] from the yoke [53] on the transmission assembly [49]:
(a) Remove the nuts [59], washers [58], washers [57] and bolts [56] that attach the ballscrew
assembly [42] to the yoke [53].
(b) Remove the ballscrew assembly [42] from the yoke [53].
NOTE: You can turn the ballscrew assembly [42] and the gimbal [43] to get access to
remove the ballscrew assembly [42].
(c) Remove the ballscrew assembly [42] with the gimbal [43].
SUBTASK 27-51-31-020-008
(5) Remove the transmission assembly [49]:
NOTE: The transmission assembly [49] weighs approximately 50 pounds (23 kilograms).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Support the transmission assembly [49] while you disconnect it from the transmission
attach fitting [51].
(b) Remove the nuts [63], washers [62], washers [61], bolts [60], bolt [64] and bolt [65] that
attach the transmission assembly [49] to the transmission attach fitting [51].
(c) Carefully remove the transmission assembly [49].

F. Inboard Flap Inboard Transmission Installation
SUBTASK 27-51-31-420-005
(1) Install the transmission assembly [49]:
NOTE: The transmission assembly weighs approximately 50 lb (23 kg).
WARNING
USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COR￾BAN 27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH
WATER. IF THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH
YOUR EYES WITH WATER. GET MEDICAL AID. THIS MATERIAL
CONTAINS FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO
PERSONNEL.
(a) Apply a thin layer of Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (preferred), or corrosion inhibiting
material, G50136 (optional), to the mating surface of the transmission assembly [49] and
transmission attach fitting [51].
(b) Apply a layer of Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (preferred), or corrosion inhibiting
material, G50136 (optional), to the bolt holes in the transmission assembly [49].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(c) Apply a layer of Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (preferred), or corrosion inhibiting
material, G50136 (optional), to the shank and threads of the bolts [60], bolt [64], and
bolt [65].
(d) Carefully lift the transmission assembly [49] to its position on the transmission attach
fitting [51].
(e) Install the bolts [60], bolt [64], bolt [65], washers [61], washers [62], and nuts [63] to
attach the transmission assembly [49] to the transmission attach fitting [51].
(f) Tighten the nuts [63] to 500 in-lb (56.5 N·m) - 550 in-lb (62.1 N·m) more than the run-on
torque.
SUBTASK 27-51-31-420-006
(2) Connect the ballscrew assembly [42] to the yoke [53] on the transmission assembly [49]:
(a) Turn the ballscrew nut [55] until it is at the forward end of the ballscrew assembly [42].
(b) Apply a layer of grease, D00633, to the mating surfaces of the yoke [53] and ballscrew
assembly [42].
(c) Put the ballscrew assembly [42] into the yoke [53].
(d) Apply a layer of grease, D00633, to the shank and threads of the bolts [56].
(e) Install the bolts [56], washers [57], washers [58], and nuts [59] to attach the ballscrew
assembly [42] to the yoke [53].
(f) Make sure that the ballscrew assembly [42] is installed correctly in the yoke [53]:
1) Turn the transmission assembly [49] until the nut [50] on the U-Joint [52] is up.
2) Turn the ballscrew nut [55] until the upstop is 180° from the upstop [54] on the
yoke [53].
3) If the ball returns on the ballscrew nut [55] are not in the correct position, change
the position of the ballscrew assembly [42]:
NOTE: On transmission No. 4, the ball returns should be on the outboard side. On
transmission No. 5, the ball returns should be on the inboard side.
a) Remove the nuts [59], washers [58], washers [57], and bolts [56] that attach
the ballscrew assembly [42] to the yoke [53].
b) Turn the ballscrew assembly [42] 180° in the yoke [53].
c) Install the bolts [56], washers [57], washers [58], and nuts [59].
(g) Tighten the nuts [59] to 100 in-lb (11.3 N·m) - 120 in-lb (13.6 N·m) above run on torque.
SUBTASK 27-51-31-420-007
(3) Connect the ballscrew assembly [42] with the gimbal [43] to the carriage [47]:
(a) Move the gimbal [43] to the downstop on the ballscrew assembly [42].
NOTE: On transmission No. 4, the ball returns on the ballscrew nut should be on the
outboard side. On transmission No. 5, the ball returns on the ballscrew nut
should be on the inboard side.
(b) Move the carriage [47] to align with the gimbal [43].
(c) Install the carriage bushing [46] to attach the gimbal [43] to the carriage [47].
(d) Install the bolts [41], washers [45], and nuts [44] that attach the gimbal carriage
bushing [46] to the carriage [47].
(e) Tighten the nuts [44] to 65 in-lb (7.3 N·m) - 75 in-lb (8.5 N·m) more than the run-on
torque.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

H. Inboard Flap Transmission Coupling Seal Replacement
SUBTASK 27-51-31-480-004
(1) Install the clamp set, SPL-1726, on the torque tubes [1] on both sides of the transmission [4].
NOTE: The clamp set can be used to stop inadvertent movement of the flap drive system
while the torque tubes are disconnected. If the flap drive system moves, then it will be
necessary to do the flap drive system adjustment.
(a) Put the clamp assembly in its location on the applicable torque tube [1].
(b) Turn the knob to tighten the clamp assembly on the torque tube [1].
(c) Turn the rod until it touches the structure to make sure the clamp assembly does not turn.
SUBTASK 27-51-31-020-009
(2) Disconnect the torque tube [1] from the transmission [4]:
(a) Remove lockwire or safety cable from the screws [3].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) Remove the screws [3] that attach the coupling sleeve [2] to the splined coupling [5] on
the torque tube [1].
(c) Move the coupling sleeve [2] off the splined coupling [5].
SUBTASK 27-51-31-020-010
(3) Remove the coupling half [8] with coupling seal [9] from the pinion shaft [10]:
(a) Use the coupling sleeve wrench, SPL-5384, to hold the coupling sleeve [2].
(b) Remove the bolt [6], packing [7], coupling half [8] with the coupling seal [9], and coupling
sleeve [2].
1) Discard the packing [7] and coupling seal [9].
2) Do a detailed inspection of the coupling sleeve [2] and coupling half [8].
a) If the coupling sleeve [2] and coupling half [8] have worn areas, replace them
with new ones.
SUBTASK 27-51-31-420-009
(4) Install the coupling half [8] with the new coupling seal [9] on the pinion shaft [10]:
(a) Lubricate the coupling sleeve [2] and coupling half [8] with grease, D00633.
(b) Install the coupling sleeve [2] and coupling half [8] with the new coupling seal [9] on the
pinion shaft [10].
(c) Apply grease, D00633, to the new packing [7].
(d) Install the new packing [7] on the bolt [6].
(e) Apply grease, D00633, to the faying surface of the bolt [6].
(f) Use the coupling sleeve wrench, SPL-5384, to hold the coupling sleeve [2].
(g) Install the bolt [6] in the pinion shaft [10].
1) Tighten the bolt [6] to 600 in-lb (68 N·m) - 720 in-lb (81 N·m) above the run-on
torque.
SUBTASK 27-51-31-420-010
(5) Connect the torque tube [1] to the transmission [4]:
(a) Put the splined coupling [5] in the coupling sleeve [2].
(b) Install the screws [3] to attach the torque tube [1] to the transmission [4].
(c) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G50347, or safety cable kit, G51490, on the screws [3]
(PAGEBLOCK 20-10-44/401).
SUBTASK 27-51-31-080-001
(6) Remove the clamp set, SPL-1726, from the torque tubes [1].
SUBTASK 27-51-31-820-003
(7) If the disconnected torque tubes [1] moved, do this task: Trailing Edge Flap Drive System
Adjustment, TASK 27-51-00-820-802.

F. Inboard Flap Inboard Ballscrew and Gimbal Installation
SUBTASK 27-51-32-420-004
(1) If you removed it, install the gimbal assembly [45] on the ballscrew nut [58]:
(a) Apply grease, D00633, to the inside and outside mating surfaces of the gimbal
bushings [42].
 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169,
174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317,
322-341, 343, 346-999;  006, 007, 013, 014 POST 737-SL-57-077
(b) Apply grease, D00633, to the outside surfaces of the gimbal bushings [42].
 ALL
(c) Put the gimbal assembly [45] in its location on the ballscrew nut [58].
(d) Install the gimbal bushings [42] through the gimbal assembly [45] on the ballscrew
nut [58].
(e) Install the bolts [43], washers [41] and collars [51] to attach the gimbal bushing [42] to the
gimbal assembly [45].
SUBTASK 27-51-32-420-005
(2) Connect the ballscrew assembly [44] to the yoke [56] on the transmission [53]:
(a) Turn the ballscrew nut [58] until it is at the forward end of the ballscrew assembly [44].
(b) Apply a layer of grease, D00633, to the mating surfaces of the yoke [56] and the
ballscrew assembly [44].
(c) Put the ballscrew assembly [44] into the yoke [56].
(d) Apply a layer of grease, D00633, to the shank and threads of the bolts [59].
(e) Install the bolts [59], washers [60], washers [61] and nuts [62] to attach the ballscrew
assembly [44] to the yoke [56].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(f) Install the ballscrew assembly [44] in the yoke [56]:
NOTE: The ball return tubes can point inboard or outboard when you install the
ballscrew assembly. For easier access to lubricate the ballscrew assembly, you
can point the ball return tubes of transmission No.4 outboard, and transmission
No.5 inboard.
1) Disconnect the torque tube from the transmission assembly
(TASK 27-51-31-000-802).
2) Turn the transmission [53] until the nut [54] on the U-joint [55] is up.
3) Turn the ballscrew nut [58] until the upstop is 180° from the upstop [57] on the
yoke [56].
4) If necessary, change the position of the ballscrew assembly [44] ball return tubes:
NOTE: The ball return tubes can point inboard or outboard when you install the
ballscrew assembly. For easier access to lubricate the ballscrew assembly,
you can point the ball return tubes of transmission No.4 outboard, and
transmission No.5 inboard.
a) Remove the nuts [62], washers [61], washers [60] and bolts [59] that attach
the ballscrew assembly [44] to the yoke [56].
b) Turn the ballscrew assembly [44] 180° in the yoke [56].
c) Install the bolts [59], washers [60], washers [61] and nuts [62].
5) Connect the torque tube to the transmission assembly (TASK 27-51-31-400-802).
(g) Tighten the nuts [62] to 100 in-lb (11.3 N·m) - 120 in-lb (13.6 N·m) above the run on
torque.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-420-006
(3) Connect the ballscrew assembly [44] with the gimbal assembly [45] to the carriage [49]:
(a) Move the gimbal assembly [45] to the downstop on the ballscrew assembly [44].
(b) Move the carriage [49] to align with the gimbal assembly [45].
(c) Install the carriage bushings [48] to attach the gimbal assembly [45] to the carriage [49].
(d) Install the bolts [50], washers [47] and nuts [46] that attach the carriage bushing [48] to
the carriage [49].
(e) Tighten the nuts [46] to 65 in-lb (7.3 N·m) - 75 in-lb (8.5 N·m) more than the run-on
torque.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-210-006
(4) Make sure that the torque trip indicator [52] on the transmission [53] is set.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-640-004
(5) Apply grease, D00633, to the end of the plunger on the torque trip indicator [52] and push it
down around the sides of the plunger.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-640-002
(6) Lubricate the transmission [53] and ballscrew assembly [44], do this task: Inboard Flap Inboard
Ballscrew Lubrication and U-Joint Lubrication, TASK 12-22-51-640-802.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-820-002
(7) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap Drive System Adjustment, TASK 27-51-00-820-802.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

2. Inboard Flap Outboard Ballscrew Inspection
(Figure 601)
A. General
(1) This task is applicable to the ballscrew at flap supports No. 3 and 6.
(2) There are two methods that you can use to apply a load to the ballscrew nut to measure the
movement on the ballscrew. This procedure gives instructions for each method.
(a) You can push up on the trailing edge of the flap to apply the load.
(b) You can use the lever and clamp tool to apply the load to the ballscrew nut.
(3) It is not necessary to use the two methods to apply the load.

E. Prepare for the Inspection
SUBTASK 27-51-32-860-011
(1) Extend the trailing edge flaps to the 40-unit position. To extend them, do this task: Extend the
Trailing Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-803.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-480-009
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL THE
LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR
CAN RETRACT. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS, AND DAMAGE
TO EQUIPMENT.
(2) If the downlock pins are not installed in the nose and main landing gear, do this task: Landing
Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-040-003
(3) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Deactivation, TASK 27-51-00-040-801.
F. Inboard Flap Outboard Ballscrew Backlash Check Without the Lever and Clamp Tool
NOTE: With this method, you manually push on the trailing edge of the flap to apply the load to the
ballscrew nut.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-480-010
(1) Install the dial indicator assembly on the ballscrew:
NOTE: The dial indicator assembly is a part of the tester, SPL-1753
(a) Put the dial indicator assembly on the ballscrew.
NOTE: Make sure the pointer touches the forward end of the ballscrew nut.
(b) Put the strap around the ballscrew to help hold the dial indicator assembly on the
ballscrew.
(c) Adjust the dial indicator to zero.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-220-004
(2) Measure the backlash of the ballscrew and ballscrew nut:
(a) Push up on the outboard trailing edge end of the inboard flap.
NOTE: This will apply a load to the ballscrew nut, and move it forward on the ballscrew.
(b) Use the dial indicator to measure the movement of the ballscrew nut.
NOTE: The movement of the ballscrew nut is the backlash.
(c) Do these steps a total of five times to make sure the movement of the dial indicator is
repeatable.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-51-32-960-004
(3) If the backlash is more than 0.0073 in. (0.1854 mm), then replace the ballscrew assembly.
These are the tasks:
Inboard Flap Outboard Ballscrew and Gimbal Removal, TASK 27-51-32-000-801,
Inboard Flap Outboard Ballscrew and Gimbal Installation, TASK 27-51-32-400-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-080-004
(4) Remove the dial indicator assembly from the ballscrew.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-440-007
(5) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Reactivation, TASK 27-51-00-440-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-860-017
(6) Retract the trailing edge flaps to the retracted position, do this task: Retract the Trailing Edge
Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-804.
G. Inboard Flap Outboard Ballscrew Backlash Check with the lever and clamp tool
NOTE: With this method, you use the lever and clamp tool to apply the load to the ballscrew nut.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-020-007
(1) Do this task: Inboard Flap Support Aft Fairing Removal, TASK 27-51-18-000-802
SUBTASK 27-51-32-440-008
(2) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Reactivation, TASK 27-51-00-440-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-860-018
(3) Retract the trailing edge flaps to the 15-unit position, do this task: Retract the Trailing Edge
Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-804.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-040-006
(4) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Deactivation, TASK 27-51-00-040-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-480-001
(5) Install the lever and clamp tool on the ballscrew:
NOTE: The lever and clamp tool is a part of the tester, SPL-1753.
(a) Put the lever and clamp tool in its position on the ballscrew aft of the ballscrew nut.
NOTE: Make sure the load surfaces of the lever and clamp tool touch the aft side of the
ballscrew nut.
(b) Tighten the clamp-up bolt to 200-300 pound-inches (22.6 to 33.8 newton-meters).
NOTE: Make sure the handles of the lever and clamp tool are in the relaxed position.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-480-002
(6) Install the dial indicator assembly on the ballscrew:
NOTE: The dial indicator assembly is a part of the tester, SPL-1753.
(a) Put the dial indicator assembly on the ballscrew.
NOTE: Make sure the pointer touches the forward end of the ballscrew nut.
(b) Put the strap around the ballscrew to help hold the dial indicator assembly on the
ballscrew.
(c) Adjust the dial indicator to zero.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-220-001
(7) Measure the backlash of the ballscrew and ballscrew nut:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Move the handles of the lever and clamp tool together until the dial indicator stops.
NOTE: This will apply a load to the ballscrew nut, and move it forward on the ballscrew.
(b) Use the dial indicator to measure the movement of the ballscrew nut.
NOTE: The movement of the ballscrew nut is the backlash.
(c) Do these steps a total of five times to make sure the movement of the dial indicator is
repeatable.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-960-001
(8) If the backlash is more than 0.0073 in. (0.1854 mm), then replace the ballscrew assembly.
These are the tasks:
Inboard Flap Outboard Ballscrew and Gimbal Removal, TASK 27-51-32-000-801,
Inboard Flap Outboard Ballscrew and Gimbal Installation, TASK 27-51-32-400-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-080-001
(9) Remove the dial indicator assembly and the lever and clamp tool from the ballscrew.
H. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 27-51-32-410-002
(1) Do this task: Inboard Flap Support Aft Fairing Installation, TASK 27-51-18-400-802, if you
removed it.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-440-003
(2) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Reactivation, TASK 27-51-00-440-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-860-012
(3) Retract the trailing edge flaps to the retracted position, do this task: Retract the Trailing Edge
Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-804.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-020-008
(4) Do this task: Landing Gear Downlock Pins Removal, TASK 32-00-01-080-801, if not
necessary.
