(c) Do these steps a total of five times to make sure that the movement of the dial indicator is
repeatable.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-960-003
(3) If the backlash is more than 0.0073 in. (0.1854 mm), replace the ballscrew assembly.
(a) Do this task: Inboard Flap Inboard Ballscrew and Gimbal Removal,
TASK 27-51-32-000-802.
(b) Do this task: Inboard Flap Inboard Ballscrew and Gimbal Installation,
TASK 27-51-32-400-802.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-080-003
(4) Remove the dial indicator assembly from the ballscrew.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-440-005
(5) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Reactivation, TASK 27-51-00-440-801.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-51-32-860-015
(6) Retract the trailing edge flaps to the retracted position, do this task: Retract the Trailing Edge
Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-804.
H. Inboard Flap Inboard Ballscrew Backlash Check with the Lever and Clamp Tool
NOTE: With this method, you use the lever and clamp tool to apply the load to the ballscrew nut.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-000-002
(1) Open these access panels:
Number Name/Location
193CL Wheel Well Panel - Aft Outboard
193CR Wheel Well Panel - Aft Outboard
194CL Aft Wing To Body Fairing Panel
194CR Aft Wing To Body Fairing Panel
SUBTASK 27-51-32-440-011
(2) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Reactivation, TASK 27-51-00-440-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-860-016
(3) Retract the trailing edge flaps to the 15-unit position, do this task: Retract the Trailing Edge
Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-804.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-040-005
(4) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Deactivation, TASK 27-51-00-040-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-480-003
(5) Install the lever and clamp tool on the ballscrew:
NOTE: The lever and clamp tool is a part of the tester, SPL-1753.
(a) Put the lever and clamp tool in its position on the ballscrew aft of the ballscrew nut.
1) Make sure that the load surfaces of the lever and clamp tool touch the aft side of the
ballscrew nut.
(b) Tighten the clamp-up bolt to 200 in-lb (22.6 N·m) - 300 in-lb (33.9 N·m).
1) Make sure that the handles of the lever and clamp tool are in the relaxed position.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-480-004
(6) Install the dial indicator assembly on the ballscrew:
NOTE: The dial indicator assembly is a part of the tester, SPL-1753.
(a) Put the dial indicator assembly on the ballscrew.
1) Make sure that the pointer touches the forward end of the ballscrew nut.
(b) Put the strap around the ballscrew to help hold the dial indicator assembly on the
ballscrew.
(c) Adjust the dial indicator to zero.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-220-002
(7) Measure the backlash of the ballscrew and ballscrew nut:
(a) Move the handles of the lever and clamp tool together until the dial indicator stops.
NOTE: This will apply a load to the ballscrew nut, and move it forward on the ballscrew.
(b) Use the dial indicator to measure the movement of the ballscrew nut.
NOTE: The movement of the ballscrew nut is the backlash.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(c) Do these steps a total of five times to make sure that the movement of the dial indicator is
repeatable.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-960-002
(8) If the backlash is more than 0.0073 in. (0.1854 mm), replace the ballscrew assembly.
(a) Do this task: Inboard Flap Inboard Ballscrew and Gimbal Removal,
TASK 27-51-32-000-802.
(b) Do this task: Inboard Flap Inboard Ballscrew and Gimbal Installation,
TASK 27-51-32-400-802.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-080-002
(9) Remove the dial indicator assembly and the lever and clamp tool from the ballscrew.

F. Inboard Flap Outboard Gimbal Bushing and Carriage Bushing Freeplay Check
SUBTASK 27-51-32-000-004
(1) Do this task: Inboard Flap Support Aft Fairing Removal, TASK 27-51-18-000-802.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-220-005
(2) Measure the Gimbal Bushing Freeplay as follows:
(a) Push up (Y - axis) on the ballscrew.
NOTE: This will apply a load on the ballscrew nut and move it up.
(b) Measure between the ballnut flange and the gimbal bushing with a feeler gage,
STD-4872 or equivalent.
NOTE: The movement of the ballscrew nut is the freeplay.
(c) If the freeplay is less than 0.040 in. (1.02 mm) or more that 0.080 in. (2.03 mm), then
replace the gimbal bushing. (Inboard Flap Outboard Ballscrew and Gimbal Removal,
TASK 27-51-32-000-801, Inboard Flap Outboard Ballscrew and Gimbal Installation,
TASK 27-51-32-400-801)
NOTE: The freeplay tolerance for the gimbal bushing is 0.040 in. (1.02 mm) to 0.080 in.
(2.03 mm).
SUBTASK 27-51-32-220-006
(3) Measure the Carriage Bushing Freeplay as follows:
(a) Push left or right (X - axis) on the ballscrew.
NOTE: This will apply a load on the gimbal and move it to one side.
(b) Measure between the carriage flange and the carriage bushing with a feeler gage,
STD-4872 or equivalent.
NOTE: The movement of the gimbal is the freeplay.
(c) If the freeplay is less than 0.040 in. (1.02 mm) or more that 0.080 in. (2.03 mm), then
replace the carriage bushing. (Inboard Flap Outboard Ballscrew and Gimbal Removal,
TASK 27-51-32-000-801, Inboard Flap Outboard Ballscrew and Gimbal Installation,
TASK 27-51-32-400-801)
NOTE: The freeplay tolerance for the carriage bushing is 0.040 in. (1.02 mm) to 0.080 in.
(2.03 mm).

F. Inboard Flap Inboard Ballscrew Lubrication Inspection
(Table 601)
SUBTASK 27-51-32-640-007
(1) This table supplies data for the subsequent lubrication and inspection steps:
Table 601/27-51-32-993-802 Inboard Flap Inboard Ballscrew Servicing
Item No. Nomenclature Lubricant Method of
Application
Number of
Locations
- No. 4 Ballscrew Nut (No. 5 Ballscrew
Nut is Equivalent)
grease, D00633 Zerk 1
SUBTASK 27-51-32-840-001
WARNING
USE GLOVES AND EYE PROTECTION WHEN YOU LUBRICATE WITH A
GREASE GUN. LUBRICANT AT HIGH PRESSURE CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO
PERSONNEL.
(2) Put on the neoprene or nitrile glove, STD-6517, and eye protection goggles, STD-421.
SUBTASK 27-51-32-640-005
(3) Do these steps for the ballscrew nut lubrication and inspection:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Remove the old grease and dirt on and around the ballscrew nut and grease vent with a
lint-free cloth, G01043, or equivalent.
CAUTION
DO NOT USE A PNEUMATIC GREASE GUN TO SERVICE THE
BALLSCREWS, EXCESSIVE GREASE GUN NOZZLE PRESSURE AND
FLOW RATE CAN DAMAGE THE SEALS.
(b) Lubricate the ballscrew nut with grease, D00633.
NOTE: The ballscrew nut has two grease fittings. It is only necessary to lubricate one of
them.
NOTE: Accumulated grease and Foreign Object Damage (FOD) can be removed from
the vent opening, if necessary to make sure that the vent is clear.
NOTE: It is recommended to use a manual grease gun.
1) Make sure that clean grease comes out from the grease vent, to flush out the used
grease.
NOTE: If necessary, remove collected grease and FOD from the vent opening to
clean the vent.
a) If clean grease does not come out from the vent, then replace the ballscrew
assembly on or before the next interval inspection (INBOARD FLAP
BALLSCREWS AND GIMBALS - REMOVAL/INSTALLATION,
PAGEBLOCK 27-51-32/401).
2) Make sure that grease does not flow freely from the ballscrew nut seal.
NOTE: It is acceptable for a small quantity of grease to come out through the
ballscrew nut seal. This means that when applying new grease into the
ballscrew, the grease should come out mainly from the grease vent. If the
grease comes out more from the ballscrew nut seal than from the grease
vent, it is necessary to replace or repair the ballscrew to serviceable
condition.
a) If the grease flows freely from the ballscrew nut seal, then do this task on or
before the next interval inspection (Inboard Flap Inboard Ballscrew Inspection,
TASK 27-51-32-220-802).

(1) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Reactivation, TASK 27-51-00-440-801.

2. Outboard Flap Outboard Transmission Removal
(Figure 401)
A. General
(1) This task is applicable to the transmissions at flap supports No. 1 and 8.
B. References
Reference Title
27-51-00-980-801 Trailing Edge Flap System Manual Operation (P/B 201)
27-51-28-000-802 Outboard Flap Outboard Support Aft Fairing Removal (P/B 401)
27-58-01-000-801 Flap Position Transmitter Removal (P/B 401)

Zone Area

D. Prepare for the Removal
SUBTASK 27-51-41-010-001
(1) Do this task: Outboard Flap Outboard Support Aft Fairing Removal, TASK 27-51-28-000-802.
E. Outboard Flap Outboard Transmission Removal
SUBTASK 27-51-41-980-001
(1) Manually extend the trailing edge flaps to the downstop on the ballscrew
(TASK 27-51-00-980-801).
SUBTASK 27-51-41-020-001
(2) Do this task: Flap Position Transmitter Removal, TASK 27-58-01-000-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-41-020-002
(3) Disconnect the torque tube [9] from the transmission assembly [4]:
(a) Remove lockwire or safety cable from the screws [11].
(b) Remove the screws [11] that attach the coupling sleeve [8] to the splined coupling [10] on
the torque tube [9].
(c) Move the coupling sleeve [8] off the splined coupling [10].
SUBTASK 27-51-41-020-003
(4) Disconnect the aft flap drive rod [6] from the drive rod attach fitting [37]:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Remove the nut [35], washer [34], washer [32], bolt [31], and bushing [33] that attach the
aft flap drive rod [6] to the drive rod attach fitting [37].
(b) Move the aft flap drive rod [6] away from the drive rod attach fitting [37].
SUBTASK 27-51-41-020-004
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU HOLD THE BALLSCREW WHILE YOU DISCONNECT
IT. IF THE U-JOINT IS ALLOWED TO SUPPORT THE WEIGHT OF THE
BALLSCREW, THIS WILL CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE U-JOINT.
(5) Disconnect the ballscrew assembly [2] with the gimbal [13] from the carriage [1]:
NOTE: When you disconnect the ballscrew assembly from the carriage, the outboard flap can
move a small distance to the downstop on the flap track.
(a) Remove the nuts [15], washers [16], and bolts [17] from the carriage [1].
(b) Remove the inboard carriage bushing [20] and outboard carriage bushing [14] from the
gimbal [13] and carriage [1].
(c) Move the ballscrew assembly [2] and gimbal [13] away from the carriage [1].
SUBTASK 27-51-41-020-005
(6) Disconnect the ballscrew assembly [2] from the yoke [5] on the transmission assembly [4]:
(a) Remove the nuts [24], washers [22], washers [23], and bolts [21] that attach the ballscrew
assembly [2] to the yoke [5].
(b) Remove the ballscrew assembly [2] from the yoke [5].
NOTE: You can turn the ballscrew assembly and gimbal to get access to remove the
ballscrew assembly.
(c) Remove the ballscrew assembly [2] with the gimbal [13].
SUBTASK 27-51-41-020-014
(7) If it is necessary, remove the fairlead [48] from the transmission assembly [4]:

(8) Remove the transmission assembly [4]:
NOTE: It is not necessary to do this step if the transmission attach fitting will remain on the
sideplate.

fitting [3] from the sideplates.
(c) Remove the nuts [30], washers [29], washers [28], and bolts [27] that attach the
transmission attach fitting [3] to the sideplates.
(d) Carefully lower the transmission assembly [4] and wire bracket [26].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

(9) Remove the transmission assembly [4] from the transmission attach fitting [3]:
(a) Hold the transmission assembly [4] while you disconnect it from the transmission attach
fitting [3].
(b) Remove the nuts [45], washers [44], washers [43], bolts [42], and wire bracket [26] from
the transmission assembly [4].
(c) Remove the nuts [45], washers [44], washers [43], bolt [46], bolt [47], and drive rod attach
fitting [37] from the transmission assembly [4].
(d) Remove the transmission assembly [4] from the transmission attach fitting [3].

SUBTASK 27-51-41-420-012
(1) Install the transmission assembly [4] to the transmission attach fitting [3]:
WARNING
DO NOT GET THIS MATERIAL IN YOUR MOUTH, EYES, OR ON YOUR
SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM THIS MATERIAL. PUT ON
A RESPIRATOR, EYE PROTECTION (GOGGLES, OR OTHER
APPROVED PROTECTION), AND GLOVES BEFORE YOU USE THIS
MATERIAL. MAKE SURE THAT THERE IS SUFFICIENT AIRFLOW. KEEP
THIS MATERIAL AWAY FROM SPARKS, FLAME, AND HEAT. THIS
MATERIAL CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(a) Apply a thin layer of Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (recommended), or Mastinox 6856
K, C50056 (optional), to the mating surfaces of the transmission assembly [4],
transmission attach fitting [3], drive rod attach fitting [37], and wire bracket [26].
(b) Apply a layer of Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (recommended), or Mastinox 6856 K,
C50056 (optional), to the bolt holes in the transmission assembly [4] and the shank and
threads of the top two bolts [42], bottom bolt [46], and bolt [47].
(c) Hold the transmission assembly [4] in position on the transmission attach fitting [3].
(d) Put the bolts [42], washers [43], and wire bracket [26] in position on the transmission
assembly [4].
(e) Install the bolts [42], washers [43], washers [44], nuts [45], and wire bracket [26] to the
transmission assembly [4].
(f) Put the bolt [46], bolt [47], washers [43], and drive rod attach fitting [37] in position on the
transmission assembly [4].
(g) Install the bolt [46], bolt [47], washers [43], washers [44], nuts [45], and drive rod attach
fitting [37] to the transmission assembly [4].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(h) Tighten the nuts [45] to 394 in-lb (44.5 N·m) - 425 in-lb (48.0 N·m) if installed with
Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237.
(i) Tighten the nuts [45] to 640 in-lb (72 N·m) - 690 in-lb (78 N·m) if installed with Mastinox
6856 K, C50056.
SUBTASK 27-51-41-420-001
(2) Install the transmission assembly [4]:
NOTE: This step is not necessary if the transmission attach fitting remained on the sideplate.
NOTE: The transmission assembly weighs approximately 50 lb (23 kg).
(a) Apply a thin layer of sealant, A00247, to the mating surfaces of the transmission
assembly [4] and the sideplates.
(b) Apply a layer of sealant, A00247, to the bolt holes in the transmission assembly [4] and
the shank and threads of the bolts [27].
(c) Carefully lift the transmission assembly [4] and position the transmission attach fitting [3]
on the sideplates.
(d) Install the bolts [27], washers [28], washers [29], and nuts [30].
(e) Tighten the nuts [30] to 220 in-lb (25 N·m) - 410 in-lb (46 N·m).
1) When applicable, re-torque the nuts [30] to 220 in-lb (25 N·m) - 410 in-lb (46 N·m).
WARNING
USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COR￾BAN 27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH
WATER. IF THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH
YOUR EYES WITH WATER. GET MEDICAL AID. THIS MATERIAL
CONTAINS FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO
PERSONNEL.
(f) Apply a layer of Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (preferred), or corrosion inhibiting
material, G50136 (optional), to the shank and threads of the bolts [38].
(g) Install the bolts [38] to attach the wires to the wire bracket [26].
SUBTASK 27-51-41-420-014
(3) If removed, install the fairlead [48] to the transmission assembly [4].
(a) Install the fairlead [48] with the bolts [49] and washers [50].
(b) Put the cables back through the gaps of the fairlead [48].
SUBTASK 27-51-41-420-002
(4) Connect the ballscrew assembly [2] to the yoke [5] on the transmission assembly [4]:
(a) Turn the ballscrew nut [19] until it is at the forward end of the ballscrew assembly [2].
(b) Apply a layer of grease, D00633, to the mating surfaces of the yoke [5] and ballscrew
assembly [2].
(c) Put the ballscrew assembly [2] into the yoke [5].
(d) Apply a layer of grease, D00633, to the shank and threads of the bolts [21].
(e) Install the bolts [21], washers [22], washers [23], and nuts [24] to attach the ballscrew
assembly [2] to the yoke [5].
(f) Make sure that the ballscrew assembly [2] is installed correctly in the yoke [5]:
1) Turn the transmission assembly [4] until the nut [40] on the U-joint [25] is down.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
2) Turn the ballscrew nut [19] until the upstop is 180° from the upstop [41] on the
yoke [5].
3) On the transmission No. 1, make sure that the ball returns [18] on the ballscrew
nut [19] are oriented outboard.
4) On the transmission No. 8, make sure that the ball returns [18] on the ballscrew
nut [19] are oriented inboard.
5) If the ball returns [18] on the ballscrew nut [19] are not on the required side, change
the position of the ballscrew assembly [2]:
a) Remove the nuts [24], washers [23], washers [22], and bolts [21] that attach
the ballscrew assembly [2] to the yoke [5].
b) Turn the ballscrew assembly [2] 180° in the yoke [5].
c) Install the bolts [21], washers [22], washers [23], and nuts [24].
(g) Tighten the nuts [24] to 100 in-lb (11.3 N·m) - 120 in-lb (13.6 N·m) more than the run-on
torque.
SUBTASK 27-51-41-420-003
(5) Connect the ballscrew assembly [2] with the gimbal [13] to the carriage [1]:
(a) Move the gimbal [13] aft on the ballscrew assembly [2] until it is at the down stop [7].
(b) On the transmission No. 1, make sure that the ball returns [18] on the ballscrew nut [19]
are outboard and the grease vent is on the lower side.
(c) On the transmission No. 8, make sure that the ball returns [18] on the ballscrew nut [19]
are inboard and the grease vent is on the lower side.
NOTE: This is the preferred position for maintenance.
 006, 007, 013, 014
(d) Apply grease, D00633, to the inside and outside surfaces of the carriage bushing [14]
and carriage bushing [20].
 ALL
(e) Lift the outboard flap until the carriage [1] aligns with the gimbal [13].
(f) Install the carriage bushing [14] and carriage bushing [20] to attach the gimbal [13] to the
carriage [1].
(g) Install the bolts [17], washers [16], and nuts [15] to hold the carriage bushing [14] and
carriage bushing [20] in the carriage [1].
(h) Tighten the nuts [15] to 65 in-lb (7.3 N·m) - 75 in-lb (8.5 N·m) more than the run-on
torque.
SUBTASK 27-51-41-420-004
(6) Connect the aft flap drive rod [6] to the drive rod attach fitting [37]:
(a) Put the aft flap drive rod [6] in its position in the drive rod attach fitting [37].
(b) Apply a layer of grease, D00633, to the inside of the bushing [33] and shank of the
bolt [31].
(c) Install the bushing [33], bolt [31], and washer [32] to attach the aft flap drive rod [6] to the
drive rod attach fitting [37].
1) Install the bolt [31] with the head on the inboard side of the joint.
NOTE: It is necessary to prevent interfering with the flap track fairing during
deployment.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(d) Carefully clean the grease, D00633, from the threads of the bolt [31].
(e) Install the washer [34] and nut [35] on the bolt [31].
(f) Tighten the nut [35] to 65 in-lb (7.3 N·m) - 100 in-lb (11.3 N·m).
(g) Install the pin [36] in the nut [35].
SUBTASK 27-51-41-420-005
(7) Connect the torque tube [9] to the transmission assembly [4]:
(a) Apply grease, D00633, to the coupling sleeve [8].
(b) Put the splined coupling [10] in the coupling sleeve [8].
(c) Install the screws [11] to attach the torque tube [9] to the transmission assembly [4].
(d) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G50347, or safety cable kit, G51490, on the screws [11]
(PAGEBLOCK 20-10-44/401).
SUBTASK 27-51-41-420-006
(8) Do this task: Flap Position Transmitter Installation, TASK 27-58-01-400-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-41-640-003
(9) Apply grease, D00633, to the end of the plunger on the torque trip indicator [12] and push it
down around the sides of the plunger.
NOTE: Not all transmissions have torque trip indicator installed.
SUBTASK 27-51-41-210-001
(10) Make sure that the torque trip indicator [12] on the transmission assembly [4] is set.
NOTE: Not all transmissions have torque trip indicator installed.
SUBTASK 27-51-41-640-001
(11) Lubricate the transmission assembly [4], ballscrew assembly [2], and gimbal [13]
(TASK 12-22-51-610-803 and TASK 12-22-51-640-805).
SUBTASK 27-51-41-820-001
(12) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap Drive System Adjustment, TASK 27-51-00-820-802.

(1) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Reactivation, TASK 27-51-00-440-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-41-860-002
WARNING
KEEP PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL
SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE
COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC
POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(2) Supply system B hydraulic power, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization,
TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-41-860-003
(3) Use the primary system to retract the flaps to the retracted position, do this task: Trailing Edge
Flap System Operation With Primary Control, TASK 27-51-00-860-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-41-860-004
(4) Use the primary system to extend and retract the flaps, do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System
Operation With Primary Control, TASK 27-51-00-860-801.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-51-41-210-002
(5) Make sure that the torque trip indicator [12] on the transmission assembly [4] is set.
NOTE: Not all transmissions have torque trip indicator installed.
SUBTASK 27-51-41-210-003
(6) Make sure that the flap position indicator on the center instrument panel shows the UP
position.
SUBTASK 27-51-41-860-005

E. Outboard Flap Inboard Transmission Removal
SUBTASK 27-51-41-980-002
(1) Manually extend the trailing edge flaps to the downstop on the ballscrew
(TASK 27-51-00-980-801).
SUBTASK 27-51-41-020-007
(2) Disconnect the torque tubes [68] from the transmission assembly [64]:
(a) Remove lockwire or safety cable from the screws [70].
(b) Remove the screws [70] that attach the coupling sleeves [67] to the splined
couplings [69] on the torque tubes [68].
(c) Move the coupling sleeves [67] off the splined couplings [69].
SUBTASK 27-51-41-020-008
(3) Disconnect the aft flap drive rod [66] from the drive rod attach fitting [96]:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Remove the nut [94], washer [93], washer [91], bolt [90], and bushing [92] that attach the
aft flap drive rod [66] to the drive rod attach fitting [96].
(b) Move the aft flap drive rod [66] away from the drive rod attach fitting [96].
SUBTASK 27-51-41-020-009
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU HOLD THE BALLSCREW WHILE YOU DISCONNECT
IT. IF THE U-JOINT IS ALLOWED TO SUPPORT THE WEIGHT OF THE
BALLSCREW, THIS WILL CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE U-JOINT.
(4) Disconnect the ballscrew assembly [62] with the gimbal [72] from the carriage [61]:
NOTE: When you disconnect the ballscrew assembly from the carriage, the outboard flap can
move a small distance to the downstop on the flap track.
(a) Remove the nuts [74], washers [75], and bolts [76] from the carriage [61].
(b) Remove the inboard carriage bushing [79] and outboard carriage bushing [73] from the
gimbal [72] and carriage [61].
(c) Move the ballscrew assembly [62] and gimbal [72] away from the carriage [61].
SUBTASK 27-51-41-020-010
(5) Disconnect the ballscrew assembly [62] from the yoke [65] on the transmission assembly [64]:
(a) Remove the nuts [83], washers [82], washers [81], and bolts [80] that attach the ballscrew
assembly [62] to the yoke [65].
(b) Remove the ballscrew assembly [62] from the yoke [65].
NOTE: You can turn the ballscrew assembly and gimbal to get access to remove the
ballscrew assembly.
(c) Remove the ballscrew assembly [62] with the gimbal [72].
SUBTASK 27-51-41-020-011
(6) Remove the transmission assembly [64]:
NOTE: It is not necessary to do this step if the transmission attach fitting will remain on the
sideplate.
NOTE: The transmission assembly weighs approximately 50 lb (23 kg).
(a) Remove the bolts [97] that attach the wires to the wire bracket [85].
(b) Hold the transmission assembly [64] while you disconnect the transmission attach
fitting [63] from the sideplates.
(c) Remove the nuts [89], washers [88], washers [87], and bolts [86] that attach the
transmission attach fitting [63] to the sideplates.
(d) Carefully lower the transmission assembly [64] and wire bracket [85].
SUBTASK 27-51-41-020-013
(7) Remove the transmission assembly [64] from the transmission attach fitting [63]:
(a) Hold the transmission assembly [64] while you disconnect it from the transmission attach
fitting [63].
(b) Remove the nuts [104], washers [103], washers [102], bolts [101], and wire bracket [85]
from the transmission assembly [64].
(c) Remove the nuts [104], washers [103], washers [102], bolt [105], bolt [106], and drive rod
attach fitting [96] from the transmission assembly [64].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(d) Remove the transmission assembly [64] from the transmission attach fitting [63].

threads of the top two bolts [101], bottom bolt [105], and bolt [106].
(c) Hold the transmission assembly [64] in position on the transmission attach fitting [63].
(d) Put the bolts [101], washers [102], and wire bracket [85] in position on the transmission
assembly [64].
(e) Install the bolts [101], washers [102], washers [103], nuts [104], and wire bracket [85] to
the transmission assembly [64].
(f) Put the bolt [105], bolt [106], washers [102], and drive rod attach fitting [96] in position on
the transmission assembly [64].
(g) Install the bolt [105], bolt [106], washers [102], washers [103], nuts [104], and drive rod
attach fitting [96] to the transmission assembly [64].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(h) Tighten the nuts [104] to 394 in-lb (44.5 N·m) - 425 in-lb (48.0 N·m) if installed with
Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237.
(i) Tighten the nuts [104] to 640 in-lb (72 N·m) - 690 in-lb (78 N·m) if installed with Mastinox
6856 K, C50056.
SUBTASK 27-51-41-420-007
(2) Install the transmission assembly [64]:
NOTE: This step is not necessary if the transmission attach fitting remained on the sideplate.
NOTE: The transmission assembly weighs approximately 50 lb (23 kg).
(a) Apply a thin layer of sealant, A00247, to the mating surfaces of the transmission
assembly [64] and sideplates.
(b) Apply a layer of sealant, A00247, to the bolt holes in the transmission assembly [64] and
the shank and threads of the bolts [86].
(c) Carefully lift the transmission assembly [64] to its position on the transmission attach
fitting [63] on the sideplates.
(d) Install the bolts [86], washers [87], washers [88], and nuts [89].
(e) Tighten the nuts [89] to 350 in-lb (40 N·m) - 410 in-lb (46 N·m).
1) When applicable, re-torque the nuts [89] to 350 in-lb (40 N·m) - 410 in-lb (46 N·m).
WARNING
DO NOT GET THIS MATERIAL IN YOUR MOUTH, EYES, OR ON YOUR
SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM THIS MATERIAL. PUT ON
A RESPIRATOR, EYE PROTECTION (GOGGLES, OR OTHER
APPROVED PROTECTION), AND GLOVES BEFORE YOU USE THIS
MATERIAL. MAKE SURE THAT THERE IS SUFFICIENT AIRFLOW. KEEP
THIS MATERIAL AWAY FROM SPARKS, FLAME, AND HEAT. THIS
MATERIAL CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(f) Apply a layer of Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (recommended), or Mastinox 6856 K,
C50056 (optional), to the shank and threads of the bolts [97].
(g) Install the bolts [97] to attach the wires to the wire bracket [85].
SUBTASK 27-51-41-420-008
(3) Connect the ballscrew assembly [62] to the yoke [65] on the transmission assembly [64]:
(a) Turn the ballscrew nut [78] until it is at the forward end of the ballscrew assembly [62].
(b) Apply a layer of grease, D00633, to the mating surfaces of the yoke [65] and ballscrew
assembly [62].
(c) Put the ballscrew assembly [62] into the yoke [65].
(d) Apply a layer of grease, D00633, to the shank and threads of the bolts [80].
(e) Install the bolts [80], washers [81], washers [82], and nuts [83] to attach the ballscrew
assembly [62] to the yoke [65].
(f) Make sure that the ballscrew assembly [62] is installed correctly in the yoke [65]:
1) Turn the transmission assembly [64] until the nut [99] on the U-joint [84] is down.
2) Turn the ballscrew nut [78] until the upstop is 180° from the upstop [100] on the
yoke [65].
3) On the transmission No. 2, make sure that the ball returns [77] on the ballscrew
nut [78] are oriented outboard.

 ALL
4) On the transmission No. 7, make sure that the ball returns [77] on the ballscrew
nut [78] are oriented inboard.

the position of the ballscrew assembly [62]:
a) Remove the nuts [83], washers [82], washers [81], and bolts [80] that attach
the ballscrew assembly [62] to the yoke [65].
b) Turn the ballscrew assembly [62] 180° in the yoke [65].
c) Install the bolts [80], washers [81], washers [82], and nuts [83].

(2) Connect the ballscrew assembly [42] to the yoke [44] on the transmission [43]:

(b) Apply a layer of grease, D00633, to the mating surfaces of the yoke [44] and the
ballscrew assembly [42].
(c) Put the ballscrew assembly [42] into the yoke [44].
(d) Apply a layer of grease, D00633, to the shank and threads of the bolts [56].
(e) Install the bolts [56], washers [57], washers [58] and nuts [59] to attach the ballscrew
assembly [42] to the yoke [44].
(f) Install the ballscrew assembly [42] in the yoke [44]:
NOTE: The ball return tubes can point inboard or outboard when you install the
ballscrew assembly. For easier access to lubricate the ballscrew assembly, you
can point the ball return tubes of transmission No.2 outboard, and transmission
No.7 inboard.
1) Disconnect the torque tube from the transmission assembly
(TASK 27-51-41-000-802).
2) Turn the transmission [43] until the nut [61] on the U-joint [60] is down.
3) Turn the ballscrew nut [53] until the upstop is 180° from the upstop [62] on the
yoke [44].
4) If necessary, change the position of the ballscrew assembly [42] ball return tubes:
NOTE: The ball return tubes can point inboard or outboard when you install the
ballscrew assembly. For easier access to lubricate the ballscrew assembly,
you can point the ball return tubes of transmission No.2 outboard, and
transmission No.7 inboard.
a) Remove the nuts [59], washers [58], washers [57] and bolts [56] that attach
the ballscrew assembly [42] to the yoke [44].
b) Turn the ballscrew assembly [42] 180° in the yoke [44].
c) Install the bolts [56], washers [57], washers [58] and nuts [59].
5) Connect the torque tube to the transmission assembly (TASK 27-51-41-400-802).
(g) Tighten the nuts [59] to 100 in-lb (11.3 N·m) - 120 in-lb (13.6 N·m) above the run on
torque.

2. Outboard Flap Outboard Ballscrew Inspection
(Figure 601)
A. General
(1) This task is applicable to the ballscrew and ballscrew nut at flap supports No. 1 and 8.
(2) There are two methods that you can use to apply a load to the ballscrew nut to measure the
movement on the ballscrew. This procedure gives instructions for each method.
(a) You can push up on the trailing edge of the flap to apply the load.
(b) You can use the lever and clamp tool to apply the load to the ballscrew nut.
(3) It is not necessary to use the two methods to apply the load.
B. References

E. Prepare for the Inspection
SUBTASK 27-51-42-860-011
(1) Extend the trailing edge flaps to the 40-unit position. To extend them, do this task: Extend the
Trailing Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-803.
SUBTASK 27-51-42-480-007
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL THE
LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR
CAN RETRACT. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS, AND DAMAGE
TO EQUIPMENT.
(2) If the downlock pins are not installed in the nose and main landing gear, do this task: Landing
Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-42-040-003
(3) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Deactivation, TASK 27-51-00-040-801.
F. Outboard Flap Outboard Ballscrew Backlash Check Without the Lever and Clamp Tool
NOTE: With this method, you manually push on the trailing edge of the flap to apply the load to the
ballscrew nut.
SUBTASK 27-51-42-480-001
(1) Install the dial indicator assembly on the ballscrew:
NOTE: The dial indicator assembly is a part of the tester, SPL-1753.
(a) Put the dial indicator assembly on the ballscrew.
NOTE: Make sure the pointer touches the forward end of the ballscrew nut.
(b) Put the strap around the ballscrew to help hold the dial indicator assembly on the
ballscrew.
(c) Adjust the dial indicator to zero.
SUBTASK 27-51-42-220-001
(2) Measure the backlash of the ballscrew and ballscrew nut:
(a) Push up on the outboard trailing edge of the outboard flap.
NOTE: This will apply a load to the ballscrew nut, and move it forward on the ballscrew.
(b) Use the dial indicator to measure the movement of the ballscrew nut.
NOTE: The movement of the ballscrew nut is the backlash.
(c) Do these steps a total of five times to make sure the movement of the dial indicator is
repeatable.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-51-42-960-001
(3) If the backlash is more than 0.0073 in. (0.1854 mm), then replace the ballscrew assembly.
These are the tasks:
Outboard Flap Outboard Ballscrew and Gimbal Removal, TASK 27-51-42-000-801,
Outboard Flap Outboard Ballscrew and Gimbal Installation, TASK 27-51-42-400-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-42-080-001
(4) Remove the dial indicator assembly from the ballscrew.
SUBTASK 27-51-42-440-003
(5) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Reactivation, TASK 27-51-00-440-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-42-860-012
(6) Retract the trailing edge flaps to the retracted position, do this task: Retract the Trailing Edge
Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-804.
G. Outboard Flap Outboard Ballscrew Backlash Check With the Lever and Clamp Tool
NOTE: With this method, you use the lever and clamp tool to apply the load to the ballscrew nut.
SUBTASK 27-51-42-010-003
(1) Do this task: Outboard Flap Outboard Support Aft Fairing Removal, TASK 27-51-28-000-802.
SUBTASK 27-51-42-440-004
(2) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Reactivation, TASK 27-51-00-440-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-42-860-013
(3) Retract the trailing edge flaps to the 15-unit position, do this task: Retract the Trailing Edge
Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-804.
SUBTASK 27-51-42-040-004
(4) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Deactivation, TASK 27-51-00-040-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-42-480-002
(5) Install the lever and clamp tool on the ballscrew:
NOTE: The lever and clamp tool is a part of the tester, SPL-1753.
(a) Put the lever and clamp tool in its position on the ballscrew aft of the ballscrew nut.
NOTE: Make sure the load surfaces of the lever and clamp tool touch the aft side of the
ballscrew nut.
(b) Tighten the clamp-up bolt to 200-300 pound-inches (22.6-33.8 newton-meters).
NOTE: Make sure the handles of the lever and clamp tool are in the relaxed position.
SUBTASK 27-51-42-480-003
(6) Install the dial indicator assembly on the ballscrew:
NOTE: The dial indicator assembly is a part of the tester, SPL-1753.
(a) Put the dial indicator assembly on the ballscrew.
NOTE: Make sure the pointer touches the forward end of the ballscrew nut.
(b) Put the strap around the ballscrew to help hold the dial indicator assembly on the
ballscrew.
(c) Adjust the dial indicator to zero.
SUBTASK 27-51-42-220-002
(7) Measure the backlash of the ballscrew and ballscrew nut:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Move the handles of the lever and clamp tool together until the dial indicator stops.
NOTE: This will apply a load to the ballscrew nut, and move it forward on the ballscrew.
(b) Use the dial indicator to measure the movement of the ballscrew nut.
NOTE: The movement of the ballscrew nut is the backlash.
(c) Do these steps a total of five times to make sure the movement of the dial indicator is
repeatable.
SUBTASK 27-51-42-960-002
(8) If the backlash is more than 0.0073 in. (0.1854 mm), then replace the ballscrew assembly.
These are the tasks:
Outboard Flap Outboard Ballscrew and Gimbal Removal, TASK 27-51-42-000-801,
Outboard Flap Outboard Ballscrew and Gimbal Installation, TASK 27-51-42-400-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-42-080-002
(9) Remove the dial indicator assembly and the lever and clamp tool from the ballscrew.

(1) Do this task: Outboard Flap Outboard Support Aft Fairing Installation, TASK 27-51-28-400-802.

F. Outboard Flap Outboard Gimbal Bushing and Carriage Bushing Freeplay Check
SUBTASK 27-51-42-220-005
(1) Measure the Gimbal Bushing Freeplay as follows:
(a) Push up (Y - axis) on the ballscrew.
NOTE: This will apply a load on the ballscrew nut and move it up.
(b) Measure between the ballnut flange and the gimbal bushing with a feeler gage,
STD-4872 or equivalent.
NOTE: The movement of the ballscrew nut is the freeplay.
(c) If the freeplay is less than 0.040 in. (1.02 mm) or more than 0.080 in. (2.03 mm), then
replace the gimbal bushing (Outboard Flap Outboard Ballscrew and Gimbal Removal,
TASK 27-51-42-000-801,Outboard Flap Outboard Ballscrew and Gimbal Installation,
TASK 27-51-42-400-801).
NOTE: The freeplay tolerance for the gimbal bushing is 0.040 in. (1.02 mm) to 0.080 in.
(2.03 mm).
SUBTASK 27-51-42-220-006
(2) Measure the Carriage Bushing Freeplay as follows:
(a) Push left or right (X - axis) on the ballscrew.
NOTE: This will apply a load on the gimbal and move it to one side.
(b) Measure between the carriage flange and the carriage bushing with a feeler gage,
STD-4872 or equivalent.
NOTE: The movement of the gimbal is the freeplay.
(c) If the freeplay is less than 0.040 in. (1.02 mm) or more than 0.080 in. (2.03 mm), then
replace the carriage bushing (Outboard Flap Outboard Ballscrew and Gimbal Removal,
TASK 27-51-42-000-801, Outboard Flap Outboard Ballscrew and Gimbal Installation,
TASK 27-51-42-400-801).
NOTE: The freeplay tolerance for the carriage bushing is 0.040 in. (1.02 mm) to 0.080 in.
(2.03 mm).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

SUBTASK 27-51-42-020-007

(Table 601)
SUBTASK 27-51-42-640-004
(1) This table supplies data for the subsequent lubrication and inspection steps:
Table 601/27-51-42-993-802 Outboard Flap Inboard Ballscrew Servicing
Item No. Nomenclature Lubricant Method of
Application
Number of
Locations
- No. 2 Ballscrew Nut (No. 7
Ballscrew Nut is Equivalent)
grease, D00633 Zerk 1
EFFECTIVITY

SUBTASK 27-51-42-840-001
WARNING
USE GLOVES AND EYE PROTECTION WHEN YOU LUBRICATE WITH A
GREASE GUN. LUBRICANT AT HIGH PRESSURE CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO
PERSONNEL.
(2) Put on the neoprene or nitrile glove, STD-6517, and eye protection goggles, STD-421.
SUBTASK 27-51-42-640-003
(3) Do these steps for the ballscrew nut lubrication and inspection:
(a) Remove the old grease and dirt on and around the ballscrew nut and grease vent with a
lint-free cloth, G01043, or equivalent.
CAUTION
DO NOT USE A PNEUMATIC GREASE GUN TO SERVICE THE
BALLSCREWS, EXCESSIVE GREASE GUN NOZZLE PRESSURE AND
FLOW RATE CAN DAMAGE THE SEALS.
(b) Lubricate the ballscrew nut with grease, D00633.
NOTE: The ballscrew nut has two grease fittings. It is only necessary to lubricate one of
them.
NOTE: Accumulated grease and Foreign Object Damage (FOD) can be removed from
the vent opening, if necessary to make sure that the vent is clear.
NOTE: It is recommended to use a manual grease gun.
1) Make sure that clean grease comes out from the grease vent, to flush out the used
grease.
NOTE: If necessary, remove collected grease and FOD from the vent opening to
clean the vent.
a) If the clean grease does not come out from the vent, then replace the
ballscrew assembly on or before the next interval inspection (OUTBOARD
FLAP BALLSCREWS AND GIMBALS - REMOVAL/INSTALLATION,
PAGEBLOCK 27-51-42/401).
2) Make sure that grease does not freely come out through the ballscrew nut seal.
NOTE: It is acceptable for a small quantity of grease to come out through the
ballscrew nut seal. This means that when applying new grease into the
ballscrew, the grease should come out mainly from the grease vent. If the
grease comes out more from the ballscrew nut seal than from the grease
vent, it is necessary to replace or repair the ballscrew to serviceable
condition.
a) If the grease freely comes through the ballscrew nut seal, then do this task on
or before the next interval inspection (Outboard Flap Inboard Ballscrew
Inspection, TASK 27-51-42-220-802).

 ALL

WARNING

F. Flap Power Drive Unit Removal
SUBTASK 27-51-51-860-003
(1) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2
Row Col Number Name
D 13 C00841 FLIGHT CONTROL ALTN T.E. FLAP DRIVE
SUBTASK 27-51-51-020-001
(2) Disconnect the electrical connector [18] from the electric motor [19].
SUBTASK 27-51-51-020-002
(3) Disconnect the hydraulic line [1], hydraulic lines [71], and case drain line [20] from the
hydraulic motor [22].
(a) Disconnect the hydraulic line [1] and hydraulic lines [71].
(b) Install the cap/plug, STD-14686, on the hydraulic line [1] and hydraulic lines [71].
(c) Disconnect the case drain line [20].
(d) Install the cap/plug, STD-14686, on the case drain line [20].
(e) Install the cap/plug, STD-14686, in the ports on the hydraulic motor [22].
SUBTASK 27-51-51-020-003
(4) Remove the nut [17], washers [16], and screw [15] that attach the jumper wire [13] to the
electric motor [19].
SUBTASK 27-51-51-010-001
(5) Remove the lower pan [25] from the flap control unit [23].
(a) Remove the screws [24] and washers [38] that attach the lower pan [25] to the flap
control unit [23].
(b) Remove the lower pan [25].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-51-51-480-001
(6) Install the flap actuator rig pin, from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, through the cam follower
arm [27] and valve cam [26].
(a) Use a rig pin, F70207-116, SPL-12421.
SUBTASK 27-51-51-480-002
(7) Install the clamp set, SPL-1726, on the torque tubes [12] on both sides of the flap power drive
unit [21].
NOTE: The clamp set can be used to stop inadvertent movement of the flap drive system
while the torque tubes are disconnected. If the flap drive system moves, then it will be
necessary to do the flap drive system adjustment.
(a) Put the clamp assembly in its location on the applicable torque tube.
(b) Turn the knob to tighten the clamp assembly on the torque tube.
(c) Turn the rod until it touches the structure to make sure that the clamp assembly does not
turn.
SUBTASK 27-51-51-020-004
(8) Disconnect the torque tubes [12] from the flap power drive unit [21].
(a) Remove lockwire or safety cable from the screws [35].
(b) Remove the screws [35] that attach the coupling sleeves [36] to the splined
couplings [37] on the torque tubes [12].
(c) Move the coupling sleeves [36] off the splined couplings [37].
SUBTASK 27-51-51-020-005
(9) Disconnect the cables [6] from the cables [2] on the flap control unit [23].
NOTE: The lower cables are WFFA and upper cables are WFFB.
(a) Install a label on the cables [2] to identify them.
(b) Remove the locking clips [3] from the turnbuckles [4].
(c) Disconnect the turnbuckles [4].
SUBTASK 27-51-51-020-006
(10) Remove the flap power drive unit [21].
(a) Remove the nuts [10], washers [9], washers [8], bolts [14], and bolt [7] that attach the flap
power drive unit [21] to the structure.
(b) Remove the flap power drive unit [21].
SUBTASK 27-51-51-020-007
(11) If it is necessary, remove the cables [6] from the flap power drive unit [21].
(a) Remove the pins [33] that attach the cable [6] to the cable drum [34].
(b) Manually turn the output shaft one or more revolutions in each direction.
(c) Remove the cables [6] from the cable drum [34].

G. Flap Power Drive Unit Installation
SUBTASK 27-51-51-860-004
(1) Make sure that this circuit breaker is open and has safety tag:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2
Row Col Number Name
D 13 C00841 FLIGHT CONTROL ALTN T.E. FLAP DRIVE
SUBTASK 27-51-51-860-005
(2) Make sure that the flaps are in the retracted position.
SUBTASK 27-51-51-420-001
(3) If the cables [6] are not installed, install them on the flap power drive unit [21].
(a) Put the cables [6] in their position on the cable drum [34].
(b) Manually turn the output shaft of one or more revolutions in each direction.
(c) Install the pins [33] to attach the cable [6] to the cable drum [34].
SUBTASK 27-51-51-820-001
(4) Make sure that the cables [6] and cable drum [34] are in the correct position.
(a) Turn the flap power drive unit [21] until the black rig marks on the cable drum [34] align
with the white cable guard [11] on the flap power drive unit [21].
(b) Make sure that the lower cable [6] wraps around the cable drum [34] 2 to 2 1/2 turns.
NOTE: This is cable WFFA.
(c) Make sure that the upper cable [6] wraps around the cable drum [34] 0 to 1/2 turns.
NOTE: This is cable WFFB.
SUBTASK 27-51-51-420-002
(5) Install the flap power drive unit [21].
(a) Put the flap power drive unit [21] in its position on the structure.
WARNING
DO NOT GET THIS MATERIAL IN YOUR MOUTH, EYES, OR ON YOUR
SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM THIS MATERIAL. PUT ON
A RESPIRATOR, EYE PROTECTION (GOGGLES, OR OTHER
APPROVED PROTECTION), AND GLOVES BEFORE YOU USE THIS
MATERIAL. MAKE SURE THAT THERE IS SUFFICIENT AIRFLOW. KEEP
THIS MATERIAL AWAY FROM SPARKS, FLAME, AND HEAT. THIS
MATERIAL CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(b) Apply Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (preferred), or corrosion inhibiting material,
G50136 (optional), or Mastinox 6856 K, C50056 (optional) to the shank and threads of
the bolt [7] and bolts [14].
(c) Install the bolt [7], bolts [14], washers [8], washers [9], and nuts [10] to attach the flap
power drive unit [21].
SUBTASK 27-51-51-420-003
(6) Connect the cables [6] to the cables [2] for the flap control unit [23].
(a) Connect the cables [2] and cables [6] at the turnbuckles [4].
(b) Remove the labels from the cables [2].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(c) Tighten the cables [2] to 125 +10 / -0 lbf (556 +44 / -0 N).
NOTE: This is an initial cable tension. The cables will be adjusted to their final tension
during the trailing edge flap control system adjustment.
1) Use the low tension cable tensiometer, COM-1553, to measure the tension of the
cables [2].
(d) Install the locking clips [3] on the turnbuckles [4].
SUBTASK 27-51-51-420-004
(7) Connect the torque tubes [12] to the flap power drive unit [21].
(a) Do not rotate the torque tubes [12] more than 5 spline teeth, in either direction, to the
nearest position where the bolt holes align at the torque tube coupling connection.
(b) Do not rotate the flap power drive unit [21] at this step.
(c) Apply grease, D00633, to the coupling sleeves [36].
(d) Put the splined couplings [37] in the coupling sleeves [36].
(e) Install the screws [35] to attach the coupling sleeves [36] to the splined couplings [37].
(f) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G50347, or safety cable kit, G51490, on the screws [35]
(PAGEBLOCK 20-10-44/401).
SUBTASK 27-51-51-420-005
(8) Connect the jumper wire [13] for the electric motor [19].
(a) Install the screw [15], washers [16], and nut [17] that attach the jumper wire [13].
(b) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the jumper wire [13] and electric
motor [19] (SWPM 20-20-00).
NOTE: When you measure the resistance, the probe can be closer than 0.25 in.
(6.4 mm) to the jumper terminal.
1) Use the intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550.
2) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is less than 0.0004 ohm (0.4
milliohm).
(c) Put a fillet seal of sealant, A02315, or sealant, A00247, around the two ends of the
screw [15].
SUBTASK 27-51-51-080-001
(9) Remove the clamp set, SPL-1726, from the torque tubes [12].
SUBTASK 27-51-51-420-006
(10) Connect the hydraulic line [1], hydraulic lines [71], and case drain line [20] to the hydraulic
motor [22].
(a) Remove the cap/plug, STD-14686, from the ports on the hydraulic motor [22].
(b) Remove the cap/plug, STD-14686, from the hydraulic lines [1] and hydraulic lines [71].
(c) Connect the hydraulic lines [1] and hydraulic lines [71] to the hydraulic motor [22].
(d) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [1] to 170 ±9 in-lb (19 ±1 N·m).
(e) Tighten the B-nuts on the hydraulic lines [71] to 500 ±25 in-lb (56 ±3 N·m).
(f) Remove the cap/plug, STD-14686, from the case drain line [20].
(g) Connect the case drain line [20] to the flap power drive unit [21].
SUBTASK 27-51-51-420-007
(11) Connect the electrical connector [18] to the electric motor [19].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-51-51-610-002
(12) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap Power Drive Unit Servicing, TASK 12-22-51-610-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-51-080-003
(13) Remove the rig pin, F70207-116, SPL-12421, from the flap control unit [23].
SUBTASK 27-51-51-820-002
(14) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap Control System Adjustment and Test, TASK 27-51-00-820-801.
NOTE: This adjustment will include the final adjustment of the cables WFFA and WFFB.
SUBTASK 27-51-51-640-001
(15) Lubricate the torque tube couplings (TASK 12-22-51-640-801).
SUBTASK 27-51-51-410-001
(16) Install the lower pan [25] on the flap control unit [23].
(a) Put the lower pan [25] in its location on the flap control unit [23].
WARNING
DO NOT GET THIS MATERIAL IN YOUR MOUTH, EYES, OR ON YOUR
SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM THIS MATERIAL. PUT ON
A RESPIRATOR, EYE PROTECTION (GOGGLES, OR OTHER
APPROVED PROTECTION), AND GLOVES BEFORE YOU USE THIS
MATERIAL. MAKE SURE THAT THERE IS SUFFICIENT AIRFLOW. KEEP
THIS MATERIAL AWAY FROM SPARKS, FLAME, AND HEAT. THIS
MATERIAL CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(b) Apply a layer of Mastinox 6856 K, C50056 (recommended), or Cor-Ban 27L Compound,
G50237 (optional), or corrosion inhibiting material, G50136 (optional) to the shank and
threads of the screws [24].
(c) Install the screws [24] and washers [38] to attach the lower pan [25].
SUBTASK 27-51-51-860-006
(17) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2
Row Col Number Name
D 13 C00841 FLIGHT CONTROL ALTN T.E. FLAP DRIVE

H. Flap Power Drive Unit Manual Drive Shearout Replacement
SUBTASK 27-51-51-010-002
(1) Remove the manual drive manual drive cover [5] from the flap power drive unit [21]:
(a) Remove the bolts [29] and washers [28] that attach the manual drive manual drive
cover [5].
(b) Remove the manual drive manual drive cover [5] from the flap power drive unit [21].
SUBTASK 27-51-51-020-008
(2) Remove the shearout [31] from the flap power drive unit [21]:
(a) Install a screw, STD-1281 in the threaded part of the shearout [31].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) Pull on the screw, STD-1281 to remove the shearout [31] with the retainer [32] from the
flap power drive unit [21].
NOTE: It will take approximately 30 pounds (130 newtons) of force to remove the
shearout [31].
SUBTASK 27-51-51-420-008
(3) Install a new shearout [31] in the flap power drive unit [21]:
(a) Put a new retainer [32] on the shearout [31].
(b) Apply grease, D00633 to the splines on the shearout [31].
(c) Use a 3/8-inch square drive to push the shearout [31] in the flap power drive unit [21] until
you feel the retainer [32] engage.
SUBTASK 27-51-51-710-001
(4) Use the manual drive to extend and retract the trailing edge flaps. To extend and retract the
flaps, do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Manual Operation, TASK 27-51-00-980-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-51-410-002
(5) Install the manual drive manual drive cover [5] on the flap power drive unit [21]:
(a) Apply fluid, D00467 to the packing [30] on the manual drive manual drive cover [5].
WARNING
USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COR￾BAN 27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH
WATER. IF THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH
YOUR EYES WITH WATER. GET MEDICAL AID. THIS MATERIAL
CONTAINS FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO
PERSONNEL.
(b) Apply Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (preferred) or corrosion inhibiting material,
G50136 (optional) to the mating surface of the manual drive manual drive cover [5] and
the flap power drive unit [21].
(c) Apply Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (preferred) or corrosion inhibiting material,
G50136 (optional) to the shank and threads of the bolts [29].
(d) Put the manual drive manual drive cover [5] and the packing [30] on the flap power drive
unit [21].
(e) Install the bolts [29] and washers [28] to attach the manual drive manual drive cover [5].
SUBTASK 27-51-51-440-002
(6) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Reactivation, TASK 27-51-00-440-801.

E. Prepare for the Removal
SUBTASK 27-51-51-480-006
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED IN ALL OF THE
LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR
CAN RETRACT AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(1) Make sure that the downlock pins are installed in the nose and main landing gear
(PAGEBLOCK 32-00-01/201).
SUBTASK 27-51-51-040-003
(2) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Deactivation, TASK 27-51-00-040-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-51-860-013
(3) Remove the pressure from the system B hydraulic reservoir (TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or
TASK 29-09-00-860-808).
F. Input Seal Removal
SUBTASK 27-51-51-010-004
(1) To replace the seal [53] for the hydraulic motor [22], remove the hydraulic motor [22] from the
flap power drive unit [21] (TASK 27-51-52-000-801).
SUBTASK 27-51-51-010-005
(2) To replace the seal [53] for the electric motor [19], remove the electric motor [19] from the flap
power drive unit [21] (TASK 27-51-53-000-801).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-51-51-680-001
(3) Drain the fluid from the flap power drive unit [21]:
(a) Put a oil resistant container, STD-203 below the drain port to catch the fluid.
(b) Remove lockwire from the drain plug [51].
(c) Remove the drain plug [51] and the packing [52] from the drain port.
1) Discard the packing [52].
(d) Wait for the fluid to drain from the flap power drive unit [21].
SUBTASK 27-51-51-020-009
(4) Remove the seal [53] from the flap power drive unit [21]:
(a) Remove the screws [55] and the retainer [54] from the flap power drive unit [21].
CAUTION
USE CAUTION WHEN YOU REMOVE THE SEAL FROM THE POWER
DRIVE UNIT. YOU CAN SCRATCH THE PINION GEAR SHAFT, OR THE
PDU HOUSING. SCRATCHES, OR OTHER DAMAGE CAN CAUSE FLUID
LEAKS THROUGH THE NEW SEAL.
(b) Carefully remove the seal [53] from the output shaft on the flap power drive unit [21].
1) Discard the seal [53].
G. Output Seal Removal
SUBTASK 27-51-51-000-001
(1) To replace the seals [56] for the output shaft, remove the torque tubes [12] from the flap power
drive unit [21].
(a) If the trailing edge flaps are not in the retracted position, do this task:Retract the Trailing
Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-804
(b) Install the clamp set, SPL-1726, on the torque tubes [12] on both sides of the flap power
drive unit [21].
NOTE: The clamp set can be used to stop inadvertent movement of the flap drive
system while the torque tubes are disconnected. If the flap drive system moves,
then it will be necessary to do the flap drive system adjustment.
1) Put the clamp assembly in its location on the applicable torque tube.
2) Turn the knob to tighten the clamp assembly on the torque tube.
3) Turn the rod until it touches the structure to make sure that the clamp assembly
does not turn.
(c) Disconnect the torque tubes [12] from the flap power drive unit [21]:
1) Remove lockwire or safety cable from the screws [35].
2) Remove the screws [35] that attach the coupling sleeves [36] to the splined
couplings [37] on the torque tubes [12].
3) Move the coupling sleeves [36] off the splined couplings [37].
SUBTASK 27-51-51-680-003
(2) Drain the fluid from the flap power drive unit [21] :
(a) Put a oil resistant container, STD-203, below the drain port to catch the fluid.
(b) Remove lockwire from the drain plug [51].
(c) Remove the drain plug [51] and packing [52] from the drain port.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Discard the packing [52].
(d) Wait for the fluid to drain from the flap power drive unit [21].
SUBTASK 27-51-51-020-011
(3) Remove the seals [56] from the flap power drive unit [21]:
(a) Remove the coupling sleeves [65]:
1) Use the coupling sleeve wrench, SPL-5384, to hold the coupling sleeves [65] while
you remove the bolts [67] and packings [66].
2) Remove the coupling seals [63], coupling halves [64], coupling sleeves [65], and
seal shields [62].
3) Remove the bolts [61], washers [60], and retainers [59] from the flap power drive
unit [21].
CAUTION
USE SOFT TOOLS TO REMOVE THE SEALS OR SEAL RINGS
FROM THE COMPONENT. HARD TOOLS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO
THE COMPONENT MATING SURFACES AND LEAKAGE CAN
OCCUR.
4) Remove the seals [56], seal rings [57], and packings [58] from the flap power drive
unit [21].
a) Discard the seals [56] and packings [58].

E. Flap Power Drive Unit Functional Test
SUBTASK 27-51-51-730-001
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE LE
AND TE FLAPS AND FLAP DRIVE MECHANISMS. THE FLAPS CAN CAUSE
INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(1) Do a test of the primary operation of the trailing edge flaps.
(a) Move the flap control lever to the UP position and wait for the flaps to reach the UP
position.
(b) Push the ON/OFF button on the front panel of the FSEU to turn on the display.
NOTE: The display will show EXISTING FAULTS?
(c) Do a check of the flap lever sensor, position sensors and skew sensor inputs to the
FSEU.
1) Push the down arrow until OTHER FUNCTNS? shows on the display.
2) Push the YES button to select OTHER FUNCTNS? on the FSEU.
3) Push the down arrow until I/O MONITOR? shows on the display.
4) Push the YES button to select I/O MONITOR? from the menu.
5) Push the down arrow until SYNCHRO INPUTS? shows on the display.
6) Push the YES button to select SYNCHRO INPUTS? from the menu.
7) Make sure that the inputs for the sensors are in the limits for the UP position
(Table 501).
NOTE: Push the arrow keys to step through the sensor values.

(d) Move the flap control lever to the 1-unit position to extend the flaps.

 ALL
(e) Make sure that the inputs for the sensors are in the limits for the 1-unit position
(Table 501).
NOTE: Push the arrow keys to step through the sensor values.
(f) Move the flap control lever to the 40-unit position to extend the flaps.
1) Measure the time it takes for the trailing edge flaps to extend from the 1-unit
position to the 40-unit position.
(g) Make sure that the time it takes for the flaps to extend is 22 to 27 seconds.
(h) Make sure that the inputs for the sensors are in the limits for the 40-unit position
(Table 501).
NOTE: Push the arrow keys to step through the sensor values.
(i) Move the flap control lever to the 1-unit position to retract the flaps.
1) Measure the time it takes for the trailing edge flaps to retract from the 40-unit
position to the 1-unit position.
(j) Make sure that the time it takes for the flaps to retract is 22 to 27 seconds.
(k) Move the flap control lever to the UP position to retract the flaps.
SUBTASK 27-51-51-720-002
(2) Do a test of the power supply for the flap electric motor.
(a) Move the flap control lever to the 1-unit position to extend the flaps.
(b) Make sure that the pointers on the flap position indicator are in the 1-unit white band.
(c) Open this circuit breaker:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2
Row Col Number Name
D 13 C00841 FLIGHT CONTROL ALTN T.E. FLAP DRIVE
(d) Move the ALTERNATE FLAPS ARM switch to the ARM position.
(e) Move and hold the ALTERNATE FLAPS CONTROL switch in the UP position for 5
seconds.
NOTE: With the circuit breaker open, the electric motor will not operate.
(f) Make sure that the flaps do not retract.
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE
LEADING EDGE SLATS. THE LEADING EDGE SLATS CAN MOVE
QUICKLY. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO

seconds.

F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2
Row Col Number Name
D 13 C00841 FLIGHT CONTROL ALTN T.E. FLAP DRIVE

 ALL

E. Flap Hydraulic Motor Installation
SUBTASK 27-51-52-420-001
(1) If you install a new hydraulic motor [3], install the reducers [4], elbow [9], check valve [11],
packings [5], packing [12], drain plug [14], and packing [15] as follows:
(a) Apply MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the new packings [5], new
packing [12], and new packing [15].
(b) Install the packings [5] and reducers [4] in the hydraulic motor [3].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Tighten the reducers [4] to 550 in-lb (62 N·m) - 600 in-lb (68 N·m).
(c) Install the packing [12] and check valve [11] in the hydraulic motor [3].
1) Tighten the check valve [11] to 155 in-lb (18 N·m) - 165 in-lb (19 N·m).
(d) Install the elbow [9] in the check valve [11].
(e) If it is not installed, install the packing [15] and drain plug [14] in the hydraulic motor [3].
1) Install MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, using double twist method.
SUBTASK 27-51-52-420-002
(2) Install the hydraulic motor [3].
(a) Apply grease, D00633, to the splines on the output shaft [8] of the hydraulic motor [3]:
(b) Fill the space between the hydraulic motor [3] and power drive unit [2] with grease,

SUBTASK 27-51-57-020-001
(1) Disconnect the torque tubes [3] from the seal rib angle gear assembly [5]:
(a) Install clamp set, SPL-1726, on the torque tube [3] outboard of the seal rib angle gear
assembly [5].
NOTE: The clamp set can be used to stop inadvertent movement of the flap drive
system while the torque tubes are disconnected. If the flap drive system moves,
then it will be necessary to do the flap drive system adjustment.

gear assembly [5] to the rib [10].

F. Torque Tube Inspection
SUBTASK 27-51-58-480-006
(1) Install the clamp set, SPL-1726, on the torque tubes inboard and outboard of the applicable
torque tube (Figure 602):
NOTE: The clamp set can be used to stop inadvertent movement of the flap drive system
while the torque tubes are disconnected. If the flap drive system moves, then it will be
necessary to do the flap drive system adjustment.
(a) Put the clamp assembly in its location on the applicable torque tube.
(b) Turn the knob to tighten the clamp assembly on the torque tube.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(c) Turn the rod until it touches the structure to make sure that the clamp assembly does not
turn.
SUBTASK 27-51-58-220-001
(2) Examine the flap torque tube splined couplers (Figure 601).
(a) Remove the torque tube guards, if applicable.
(b) Remove lockwire or safety cable from the three screws that attach the coupling sleeve to
the spline coupling on the opposite end of the torque tube.
(c) Remove the three screws that attach the coupling sleeve to the spline coupling on the
opposite end of the torque tube.
(d) Move the coupling sleeve off the torque tube spline to disconnect the torque tube.
(e) Measure the angular backlash between the units coupling half and coupling sleeve.
1) Move the torque tube axially, the full length of the sleeve, to find the point of
maximum backlash.
NOTE: Since the wear on the coupler will not be uniform, the torque tube is moved
axially.
2) The maximum allowable angular backlash is no more than 2 degrees.
(f) If the angular backlash is not in tolerance, replace the applicable unit:
• Torque Tube Assembly (PAGEBLOCK 27-51-58/401)
• Inboard Flap Transmission (PAGEBLOCK 27-51-31/401)
• Outboard Flap Transmission (PAGEBLOCK 27-51-41/401)
• Power Drive Unit (PDU) (PAGEBLOCK 27-51-51/401)
• Tee Angle Gearbox (PAGEBLOCK 27-51-55/401)
• Main Landing Gear (MLG) Beam Angle Gearbox (PAGEBLOCK 27-51-56/401)
• Seal Rib Angle Gearbox (PAGEBLOCK 27-51-57/401).
(g) If the angular backlash is in tolerance, attach coupling sleeve as follows:
1) Wipe the old grease from the coupling sleeve and splines with a clean, dry,
non-abrasive cotton cloth, G50316.
2) Apply a layer of the grease, D00633 (Recommended), or grease, D00013
(Alternate) on the splines of the coupling sleeve.
3) Engage the coupling sleeve with the coupling.
4) Install the three screws to attach the coupling sleeve.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU INSTALL THE LOCKWIRE OR SAFETY
CABLE KIT ON THE COUPLING SCREWS. IF THE COUPLING
SCREWS COME OFF, THE TORQUE TUBE WILL DISCONNECT AND
CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE AIRPLANE.
5) Install the MS20995NC32 lockwire, G01912, or safety cable kit, G51490, on the
screws (PAGEBLOCK 20-10-44/401).
(h) Remove the clamp set, SPL-1726, from the torque tubes.
(i) Install the torque tube guards, if applicable.
(j) Make sure that the torque tube has free axial movement.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-51-58-220-002
(3) Examine the center sleeve bearings:
(a) Measure the radial depth of the worn areas at the center sleeve bearing.
1) Make sure that the worn area is less than 0.080 in. (2.03 mm) maximum radial
depth on the sleeve.
NOTE: This limit applies to torque tubes that use either phenolic or CRES torque
tube center bearings.
(b) Replace the torque tube if it is not in the limits (PAGEBLOCK 27-51-58/401).
SUBTASK 27-51-58-220-003
(4) Examine the torque tube for loose rivets:
(a) Make sure that there is no movement between the end fitting and the tube.
(b) If there is movement between the end fitting and the tube, do one of these procedures:
• Replace any torque tube which shows movement between the end fitting and the
torque tube (PAGEBLOCK 27-51-58/401).
• Repair any torque tube which shows movement between the end fitting and the torque
tube (PAGEBLOCK 27-51-58/401).
G. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 27-51-58-640-004
(1) For the applicable torque tube, do this task: Trailing Edge Flap Torque Tube and Torque Tube
Support Lubrication, TASK 12-22-51-640-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-58-440-004
(2) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Reactivation, TASK 27-51-00-440-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-58-710-009
(3) Use the primary system to retract the flaps, do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Operation
With Primary Control, TASK 27-51-00-860-801.
(a) Make sure that the pointers for the flap position indicators are in the UP white band.
SUBTASK 27-51-58-710-010
(4) Use the primary system to extend the flaps to the 40-unit position, do this task: Trailing Edge
Flap System Operation With Primary Control, TASK 27-51-00-860-801.
(a) Make sure that the pointers for the flap position indicators are in the 40-unit white band.
SUBTASK 27-51-58-710-011
(5) Use the primary system to retract the flaps, do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System Operation
With Primary Control, TASK 27-51-00-860-801.

G50136 (alternate), to the shank and threads of the bolts [7] and bolts [12].

the support assembly [6] to the spoiler actuator support [2].

right side of the support assembly [6] to the spoiler actuator support [2].
SUBTASK 27-51-59-420-002
(2) Connect the torque tubes [4] to the support assembly [6]:

(d) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G50347, or safety cable kit, G51490, on the screws [5]
(PAGEBLOCK 20-10-44/401).
(e) Remove the clamp set, SPL-1726, from the torque tubes [4] inboard and outboard of the
support assembly [6].

SUBTASK 27-51-61-020-001

WFA [1] and cable assembly WFB [1].

(d) Remove the straps [10] that attach the cable assembly WFA [1] and cable assembly
WFB [1] to the quadrant [5].
(e) Remove the pins [4] that attach the cable assembly WFA [1] and cable assembly WFB [1]
to the quadrant [5].
(f) Remove the cable assembly WFA [1] and cable assembly WFB [1] from the quadrant [5].

 ALL
SUBTASK 27-51-61-020-003
(3) Remove the flap limit switches [39] from the flap control unit [9] (Figure 402).
NOTE: It is not necessary to disconnect the wires for the flap limit switches.
(a) Remove the screws [40], washers [56], and switch cover [31] from the flap control unit [9].
(b) For the Flap UP limit switch, S245, Flap Up limit switch, S1051 and the Flap DOWN limit
switch, S246, do this task: Flap Limit Switch Removal, TASK 27-51-63-000-801.
(c) For the Landing Warning Switch, S138, do this task: Flap Landing Warning Switch
Removal, TASK 31-51-01-000-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-61-020-004

and cable WFFB [48].

(5) Disconnect the electrical connector [33] from the trailing edge control valve [34].

G. Prepare for the Installation
SUBTASK 27-51-61-820-001
(1) Install the rig pin [38] in the flap control unit [9] (Figure 402).
NOTE: This will make sure that the flap control unit is in the adjusted position.
(a) Remove the screws [36], washers [55], and lower pan [37] from the flap control unit [9].
(b) Use rig pin, F70207-116, SPL-12421, from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585.
(c) Install the rig pin [38] through the cam follower arm and the valve cam.
SUBTASK 27-51-61-420-001
(2) If the cable WFFA [48] and cable WFFB [48] are not installed, install them on the flap control
unit [9].
(a) Remove the bolts [45], washers [46], and drum guard [44] from the flap control unit [9].
(b) Put the cable WFFA [48] and cable WFFB [48] in their location on the cable drum [43].
1) Wrap the cable WFFA [48] around the cable drum [43] 1/2 turns.
2) Wrap the cable WFFB [48] around the cable drum [43] 1 1/2 turn.
(c) Install the cotter pins [47] to hold the cable WFFA [48] and cable WFFB [48] on the cable
drum [43].
(d) Put the drum guard [44] in its location on the flap control unit [9].
WARNING
USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COR￾BAN 27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH
WATER. IF THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH
YOUR EYES WITH WATER. GET MEDICAL AID. THIS MATERIAL
CONTAINS FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO
PERSONNEL.
(e) Apply Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (preferred), or corrosion inhibiting material,
G50136 (optional), to the shank and threads of the bolts [45].
(f) Install the bolts [45] and washers [46] to attach the drum guard [44].
H. Flap Control Unit Installation
SUBTASK 27-51-61-420-002
(1) Install the flap control unit [9].
(a) Make sure that the area around four of the seven holes for the bolts [15] on the flap
control unit [9] is clean for electrical bonding.
(b) Apply a layer of sealant, A00247, to the mating surface of the flap control unit [9] and the
structure.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
WARNING
USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COR￾BAN 27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH

(c) Apply a layer of Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (preferred), or corrosion inhibiting
material, G50136 (optional), to the shank and threads of the bolts [41].
(d) Lift the flap control unit [9] to its position.
(e) Install the bolts [41] and washers [42] to attach the flap control unit [9].
(f) Install the bolts [15] and washers [14] from above to attach the flap control unit [9]
(Figure 401).
(g) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the flap control unit [9] and structure.
1) Use intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550.
2) Make sure that resistance is maximum 0.008 ohm (8 milliohms).
(h) Apply a bead of sealant, A02315, to the heads of the bolt [15].
SUBTASK 27-51-61-420-003
(2) Install the quadrant [5] on the flap control unit [9] (Figure 401).
(a) Put the quadrant [5] in its position on the input shaft [12] for the flap control unit [9].
(b) Apply grease, D00633, to the threads on the input shaft [12].
(c) Install the washer [17] and nut [11] on the input shaft [12].
(d) Tighten the nut [11] to 250 in-lb (28.2 N·m) - 300 in-lb (33.9 N·m) more than the run-on
torque.
SUBTASK 27-51-61-420-004
(3) Connect the cable assembly WFA [1] and cable assembly WFB [1] to the quadrant [5].
(a) Put the flap control lever [18] in the rigged position.
1) Put a 0.19 ±0.005 inch (4.83 ±0.13 mm) thick rigging block between the detent pin
on the flap control lever [18] and the upstop on the detent plate.
a) Make sure that the rigging block does not go into the flap UP detent.
2) Install a clamp to hold the quadrant [5] against the aft side of the stop [13] on the
flap control unit [9].
(b) Put the cable assembly WFA [1] and cable assembly WFB [1] in their position on the
quadrant [5].
NOTE: The cable assembly attaches to the quadrant in two locations. There is a loop of
cable that goes through the straps.
(c) Install the pins [4] and straps [10] to attach the cable assembly WFA [1] and cable
assembly WFB [1] to the quadrant [5].
(d) Install the pin [6], spacers [7], and pin [8] on the quadrant [5].
(e) Use the turnbuckles [3] to tighten the cable assembly WFA [1] and cable assembly
WFB [1] until the tension is 275 ±15 lb (124.7 ±6.8 kg).
NOTE: You will adjust the cable assembly to the final tension and remove the tools from
the flap control unit during the flap control unit adjustment procedure.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

G. Flap Control Quadrant Installation
SUBTASK 27-51-62-820-001
(1) Install the rig pin [18] in the flap control unit [9].
NOTE: This will make sure the flap control unit [9] is in the adjusted position.
(a) Remove the screws [16], washers [21], and lower pan [17] from the flap control unit [9].
(b) Install the rig pin [18] through the cam follower arm and the valve cam.
1) Use rig pin, F70207-116, SPL-12421, from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585.
SUBTASK 27-51-62-420-001
(2) Install the quadrant [5] on the flap control unit [9].
(a) Put the quadrant [5] in its position on the input shaft [12] for the flap control unit [9].
(b) Apply grease, D00633, to the threads on the input shaft [12].
(c) Install the washer [15] and nut [11] on the input shaft [12].
(d) Tighten the nut [11] to 250 in-lb (28.2 N·m) - 300 in-lb (33.9 N·m) more than the run-on
torque.
SUBTASK 27-51-62-420-002
(3) Connect the cable assembly WFA [1] and cable assembly WFB [1] to the quadrant [5].
(a) Put the flap control lever [19] in the rigged position.
1) Put a 0.19 in. (4.83 mm) thick rigging block [20] between the detent pin on the flap
control lever [19] and the upstop on the detent plate.
a) Make sure that the rigging block [20] does not go into the flap UP detent.
2) Install a clamp to hold the quadrant [5] against the aft side of the stop [13] on the
flap control unit [9].
(b) Put the cable assembly WFA [1] and cable assembly WFB [1] in their positions on the
quadrant [5].
NOTE: The cable assembly WFA [1] and cable assembly WFB [1] attach to the
quadrant [5] in two locations. There is a loop of cable that goes through the
straps [10].
(c) Install the pins [4] and straps [10] to attach the cable assembly WFA [1] and cable
assembly WFB [1] to the quadrant [5].
(d) Install the pin [6], spacers [7], and pin [8] on the quadrant [5].
(e) Use the turnbuckles [3] to tighten the cable assembly WFA [1] and cable assembly
WFB [1] until the tension is 275 ±15 lbf (1223 ±67 N).
NOTE: You will adjust the cable assembly WFA [1] and cable assembly WFB [1] to the
final tension and remove the tools from the flap control unit during the flap control
system adjustment procedure.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-51-62-820-002
(4) Do this task: Trailing Edge Flap Control System Adjustment and Test, TASK 27-51-00-820-801.
NOTE: This task includes the removal of the rig pin and the clamp from the flap control unit [9]
and the removal of the rigging tool from the flap control lever.
SUBTASK 27-51-62-420-003
(5) Install the locking clips [2] on the turnbuckles [3] for cable assembly WFA [1] and cable
assembly WFB [1].

the cam [6].

control unit.

position.

I. Flaps Down Limit Switch S246 Adjustment
SUBTASK 27-51-63-860-011
(1) Move the trailing edge flaps until the Dimension X on the Number 4 or 5 ballscrew is
11.9 ±0.0 in. (302.26 ±0.76 mm), do this task: Extend the Trailing Edge Flaps,
TASK 27-51-00-860-803.
NOTE: The trailing edge flaps will be in approximately the 40-unit position. Do not disconnect
the torque tubes from the power drive unit to extend the flaps.
SUBTASK 27-51-63-820-004
(2) Adjust the position of the Flaps DOWN limit switch [5], S246.
NOTE: It is necessary to move the limit switch [5] away from the cam for the adjustment.
There should not be any continuity through the switch pins 1 and 3 when the flaps are
approximately in the 40-unit position.
(a) Remove the lockwire from the nuts [10].
(b) Loosen the nuts [10] on the limit switch [5].
(c) Use the nuts [10] to adjust the position of the limit switch [5] until the switch is depressed
against the cam [6] and there is continuity between pins 1 and 3 of the limit switch [5].
(d) Carefully loosen the inside nut [10], and then tighten the outside nut [10] to move the limit
switch [5] away from the cam [6] until there is not continuity through the pins.
(e) Make sure that the limit switch [5] is in the correct position.
1) Pull the cable WFFA [12] to the side to turn the cam [6] slightly in the retract
direction.
NOTE: Pull on the cable to deflect it approximately 1.2 in. (30.48 mm). The cable
WFFA [12] is the lower cable between the flap power drive unit and the flap
control unit.
2) Make sure that there is continuity between the pins.
3) Pull the cable WFFB [12] to the side to turn the cam [6] slightly in the extended
direction.
NOTE: Pull on the cable to deflect it approximately 1.2 in. (30.48 mm). The cable
WFFB [12] is the upper cable between the flap power drive unit and the flap
control unit.
4) Make sure that there is no continuity between the pins.
5) Make fine adjustments of the nuts [10] until the limit switch [5] is in the correct
position.
(f) Tighten the nuts [10] on the limit switch [5] to 15 in-lb (2 N·m) - 45 in-lb (5 N·m).
(g) Install MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, on the nuts [10] with double twist method
(TASK 20-10-44-400-801).
(h) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the limit switch [5] and the flap control
unit [1] (SWPM 20-20-00).
1) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550.
2) Make sure that the resistance is 0.0025 ohm (2.5 miliohm) or less.

 ALL

control valve assembly [6] to the cam follower arm [13].

flap control unit [1].
(e) Remove the flap control valve assembly [6] from the flap control unit [1].

SUBTASK 27-51-65-420-001
(1) Install the unions [5] and new packings [4], if they are not installed, in the ports of the flap
control valve assembly [6].
(a) Apply hydraulic fluid, D00153, or MCS 352B fluid, D00054, to the new packings [4].
(b) Put the new packings [4] and unions [5] in their location on the flap control valve
assembly [6].
SUBTASK 27-51-65-420-002
(2) Install the flap control valve assembly [6] in the flap control unit [1].
(a) Put the flap control valve assembly [6] in its location on the flap control unit [1].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
WARNING
USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COR￾BAN 27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH
WATER. IF THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH
YOUR EYES WITH WATER. GET MEDICAL AID. THIS MATERIAL
CONTAINS FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO
PERSONNEL.
(b) Apply Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (preferred), or corrosion inhibiting material,
G50136 (optional), to the shank and threads of the bolts [7].
(c) Install the bolts [7] and washers [8] to attach the flap control valve assembly [6].
(d) Install lockwire on the bolts [7].
(e) Connect the flap control valve assembly [6] to the cam follower arm [13].
1) Apply grease, D00633, to the inside of the bushings [17].
2) Install the bushings [17], washers [16], bolt [15], and nut [18] that attach the flap
control valve assembly [6] to the cam follower arm [13].
3) Install the plug [9] on the forward side of the flap control unit [1].
4) Apply a bead of sealant, A00247, around the plug [9].
(f) Connect the hydraulic lines [2] and hydraulic line [24] to the flap control valve
assembly [6].
1) Remove the caps from the hydraulic lines [2] and hydraulic line [24].
2) Remove the plugs from the hydraulic ports on the flap control valve assembly [6].
3) Connect the hydraulic lines [2] and hydraulic line [24] to the flap control valve
assembly [6].
4) Tighten the B-nuts on the hydraulic lines [2] to 500 ±25 in-lb (56.5 ±2.8 N·m).
5) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [24] to 280 ±14 in-lb (31.6 ±1.6 N·m).
(g) Before you connect the electrical connector [3], examine the connector for corrosion.
WARNING
DO THE STEPS BELOW IF THE AIRPLANE OPERATES WHERE
DEICING FLUID THAT CONTAINS POTASSIUM FORMATE OR
POTASSIUM ACETATE IS USED. ALSO, DO THE STEPS FOR ALL

CONNECTORS IN THE MAIN WHEEL WELL. THE ELECTRICAL
CONNECTORS ARE IN A SYSTEM THAT IS NECESSARY FOR SAFE
FLIGHT.
(h) If there was corrosion, correct the problem (SWPM 20-60-03).
(i) Apply the D5026NS or ZC-026 compound, G50171, to the connector (SWPM 20-60-03).
(j) Connect the electrical connector [3] to the flap control valve assembly [6].

connector [3].

SUBTASK 27-51-65-420-003
(1) Install solenoid valve assembly [21] in the flap control valve assembly [6]:
(a) Apply hydraulic fluid, D00153, or MCS 352B fluid, D00054 to the new packing [22].
(b) Put the packing [22] and gasket [19] in their locations on the solenoid valve
assembly [21].

NOTE: Make sure the electrical connector on the solenoid valve assembly [21] engages
the electrical connector in the flap control valve assembly [6].

assembly [6].

(f) Install lockwire on the screws [20].
