F. Prepare for the Adjustment
SUBTASK 27-51-65-860-011
WARNING
KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL
SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE
COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC
POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(1) Supply system B hydraulic power, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization,
TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-65-860-012
(2) Extend the trailing edge flaps to the 40-unit position, do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System
Operation With Primary Control, TASK 27-51-00-860-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-65-860-013
(3) Retract the trailing edge flaps to the UP position, do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System
Operation With Primary Control, TASK 27-51-00-860-801.
(a) Wait a minimum of 2 minutes before you remove the hydraulic power.
NOTE: The flaps can move a small distance during this time.
SUBTASK 27-51-65-860-014
(4) Remove system B hydraulic power, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal,
TASK 29-11-00-860-805.
SUBTASK 27-51-65-010-002
(5) Remove the lower pan [10] from the flap control unit [1].
(a) Remove the screws [11] and washers [21] that attach the lower pan [10] to the flap
control unit [1].
(b) Remove the lower pan [10] from the flap control unit [1].
G. Trailing Edge Flap Control Valve Adjustment
SUBTASK 27-51-65-820-002
(1) Do a check of the adjustment of the flap control valve assembly [4].
NOTE: This will make sure the flap power drive unit [20] and the flap control unit [1] moved to
the correct position when you retracted the flaps.
(a) Make sure that you can easily install the rig pin [14] (F70207-116) from the rigging pin kit,
SPL-1585, through the cam follower arm [13] and valve cam [12].
(b) Make sure that the black rig mark on the cable drum [18] for the flap power drive unit [20]
extends past the cable guard [19] a minimum of 0.03 in. (0.76 mm) on each side.
SUBTASK 27-51-65-820-003
(2) If you cannot easily install the rig pin [14] (F70207-116) from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, or if
the flap power drive unit [20] is not in the correct position, then adjust the flap control valve
assembly [4].
(a) Loosen the nut [16] and nut [17] on the adjustable sleeve [9].
(b) Turn the adjustable sleeve [9] to change the position of the rod end [8].
NOTE: This will change the alignment of the valve slide and index surface on the flap
control valve assembly.
(c) Tighten the nut [16] and nut [17] on the adjustable sleeve [9].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Make sure that the distance between the center of the rod end [8] and nut [17] is
less than 0.94 in. (23.88 mm).
2) Make sure that the distance between the nut [16] and the hex on the adjustable
sleeve [9] is less than 0.19 in. (4.83 mm).
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU REMOVE THE HYDRAULIC POWER BEFORE
YOU DISCONNECT THE ROD END FROM THE SUMMING LEVER. IF
YOU DISCONNECT THE ROD END WITH HYDRAULIC POWER ON, YOU
CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE FLAP CONTROL UNIT.
(d) If it is necessary, disconnect the rod end [8] from the summing lever [2].
NOTE: It is necessary to disconnect the rod end if you cannot adjust the flap control
valve assembly while the adjustable sleeve is in the limits.
1) Remove the nut [7], washer [6], and bolt [5] that attach the rod end [8] to the
summing lever [2].
2) Change the position of the adjustable sleeve [9].
3) Install the bolt [5], washer [6], and nut [7] to attach the rod end [8] to the summing
lever [2].
(e) Tighten the nut [16] and the nut [17].
(f) Install lockwire on the nut [16], nut [17], and adjustable sleeve [9].
SUBTASK 27-51-65-080-002
(3) Remove the rig pin [14] (F70207-116) from the cam follower arm [13] and the valve cam [12].
SUBTASK 27-51-65-860-015
WARNING
KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL
SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE
COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC
POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(4) Supply system B hydraulic power, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization,
TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
SUBTASK 27-51-65-860-016
(5) Extend and retract the trailing edge flaps five times, do this task: Trailing Edge Flap System
Operation With Primary Control, TASK 27-51-00-860-801.
(a) Wait a minimum of 2 minutes before you remove the hydraulic power.
NOTE: The flaps can move a small distance during this time.
SUBTASK 27-51-65-860-017
(6) Remove system B hydraulic power, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal,
TASK 29-11-00-860-805.
SUBTASK 27-51-65-820-004
(7) Do a check of the adjustment of the flap control valve assembly [4] again.
(a) Make sure that the black rig mark on the cable drum [18] for the flap power drive unit [20]
extends past the cable guard [19] a minimum of 0.03 in. (0.76 mm) on each side.
(b) Make sure that you can easily install the rig pin [14] through the cam follower arm [13]
and valve cam [12].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-51-65-480-002
(8) If you cannot easily install the rig pin [14] or if the flap power drive unit [20] is not in the correct
position, then adjust the trailing edge flap control valve assembly [4] again.

SUBTASK 27-51-65-410-002
(2) Install the lower pan [10] on the flap control unit [1].
(a) Put the lower pan [10] in its location on the flap control unit [1].

(b) Apply Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (preferred), or corrosion inhibiting material,

(10) Do this test of the flap control valve assembly [3]:
(a) Fully extend and retract the trailing edge flaps five times, do this task: Trailing Edge Flap
System Operation With Primary Control, TASK 27-51-00-860-801.
1) Wait a minimum of 2 minutes before you remove the hydraulic power.
NOTE: The flaps can move a small distance during this time.

1) Remove the screw [5] that attach the lower pan [4] to the flap control unit [1].

D. Trailing Edge Flap Flow Limiter Installation
SUBTASK 27-51-67-420-001
(1) Install the flap flow limiter [1]:
(a) Connect the flap flow limiter [1] to the priority valve [2].
(b) Hold the flap flow limiter [1] and priority valve [2] in their position.
NOTE: The 'REGULATED FLOW' arrow on the flap flow limiter must agree with the
'REGULATED FLOW' arrow on the pressure bulkhead.
(c) Tighten the nut [3] to 900 ±45 in-lb (101.7 ±5.1 N·m).
(d) Connect the hydraulic line [4] to the flap flow limiter [1].
(e) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [4] to 500 ±25 in-lb (56.5 ±2.8 N·m).

27-58-01-820-801Flap Position Transmitter Adjustment and TestPDF p. 3071
2. Flap Position Transmitter Adjustment and Test
(Figure 501)
A. General
(1) This task uses the Flap/Slat Electronics Unit (FSEU) to adjust the flap position transmitters.
(2) This task should only be used in the situation where the adjustment of a flap position
transmitter has been changed during the installation process.
(a) This adjustment is not as accurate as the installation process of a new flap position
transmitter due to these reasons:
1) The reliance on the ability of the trailing edge flap drive system to accurately drive
the flaps to the 15-unit position.
2) The reliance on the tolerances of the particular flap position transmitter at the
15-unit position.
3) The reliance on the ability of the FSEU to read the flap position transmitter at the
15-unit position.
(b) The flap position transmitter is capable of being used on the left and right wings. Because
of this, it is necessary to be careful not to set the position transmitter at the incorrect
15-unit position. If the flap position transmitter is set at the incorrect position for the wing
it is on, it will appear to operate backward.

(e) Move the ALTN FLAP control switch to the OFF position when the right pointer is in the
30-unit white band on the flap position indicator [1].
(f) Make sure that the left pointer is in the 40-unit white band.
(g) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2
Row Col Number Name
A 12 C00213 FC TE FLAP POS/SKEW SNSR & IND LEFT
(h) Make sure that the left pointer moves to the 30-unit white band.
(i) Make sure that the tips of the pointers align in the limit of 0.06 in. (1.52 mm).
(j) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2
Row Col Number Name
A 11 C01443 FC TE FLAP POS/SKEW SNSR & IND RIGHT
(k) Move the ALTN FLAP control switch to the DOWN position and hold it until the flaps stop
moving.
(l) Make sure that the left pointer is in the 40-unit white band and the right pointer is in the
30-unit white band.
(m) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2
Row Col Number Name
A 11 C01443 FC TE FLAP POS/SKEW SNSR & IND RIGHT
(n) Make sure that the right pointer moves to the 40-unit white band.
(o) Make sure that the tips of the pointers align in the limit of 0.06 in. (1.52 mm).
(p) Move the ALTN FLAPS ARM switch to the OFF position.
SUBTASK 27-58-02-860-007
(8) Move the flap control lever to the UP position to retract the flaps.
SUBTASK 27-58-02-710-003

(a) Make sure that the pointers on the flap position indicator [1] are in the UP white band.
(b) Make sure that the tips of the pointers on the flap position indicator [1] align in the limit of
0.06 in. (1.52 mm).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

H. Flap Skew Mechanism Adjustment
NOTE: This is applicable to the flap skew mechanisms on all of the flap supports.
SUBTASK 27-59-00-820-001
(1) If the ballscrew nut for the applicable flap support does not touch the downstop, do these steps
(Figure 501).
(a) For the flap position transmitters on the left and right wings, do this task: Flap Position
Transmitter Removal, TASK 27-58-01-000-801.
NOTE: If you do not remove the flap position transmitters before you disconnect the
torque tubes, they will become incorrectly adjusted.
(b) Disconnect the torque tubes [3] from the transmission.
1) Install a clamp set, SPL-1726, on a torque tube [3] outboard of the transmission.
NOTE: The clamp set can be used to stop inadvertent movement of the flap drive
system while the torque tubes are disconnected. If the flap drive system
moves, then it will be necessary to do the flap drive system adjustment.
a) Put the clamp assembly in its location on the applicable torque tube.
b) Turn the knob to tighten the clamp assembly on the torque tube.
c) Turn the rod until it touches the structure to make sure the clamp assembly
does not turn.
2) Remove the screws [2] that attach the coupling sleeves [1] to the splined
couplings [4].
3) Move the coupling sleeves [1] off the splined couplings [4].
4) Move the torque tubes [3] away from the transmission.
CAUTION
DO NOT MOVE ONE END OF A FLAP MORE THAN 1.4 INCHES (35.5
MILLIMETERS) OF BALLSCREW TRAVEL MORE THAN THE OTHER
END. YOU CAN CAUSE THE FLAP TO SKEW TO MUCH. THIS CAN
CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE FLAP.
(c) Use a coupling sleeve wrench, SPL-5384, on one of the couplings on the transmission to
extend the transmission until the ballscrew nut touches the downstop on the ballscrew.
SUBTASK 27-59-00-220-001
(2) Measure the mismatch between the crank arm [23] and the flat side of the rigging flange [21]
on the sensor input assembly [22] (Figure 502).
SUBTASK 27-59-00-820-002
(3) If the mismatch between the crank arm [23] and the rigging flange [21] is not in the limit of
0.005 in. (0.127 mm) to 0.015 in. (0.381 mm), then adjust the length of the skew control
rod [24] (Figure 502).
NOTE: The crank arm [23] must be past the rigging flange [21].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) To make a large adjustment to the length of the skew skew control rod [24], do these
steps:
1) Loosen the nut [26].
2) Remove the nut [33], washer [32], bushing [31], washer [30], and bolt [29] that
attach the rod end [34] to the crank arm [23].
3) Turn the adjustment sleeve [27] with the rod end [34] in the skew control rod [24] to
adjust the length of the skew control rod [24].
NOTE: Make sure that the threads of the adjustment sleeve [27] cover a minimum
of half the inspection hole in the skew control rod [24].
WARNING
USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE
COR-BAN 27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE
IT WITH WATER. IF THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES,
IMMEDIATELY FLUSH YOUR EYES WITH WATER. GET MEDICAL
AID. THIS MATERIAL CONTAINS FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN
CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL.
4) Apply Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (preferred), or corrosion inhibiting material,
G50136 (alternate), to the shank and threads of the bolt [29].
5) Put the skew control rod [24] in its position in the crank arm [23].
6) Install the bolt [29], washer [30], bushing [31], washer [32], and nut [33] to attach the
skew control rod [24] to the crank arm [23].
NOTE: Install the bolt [29] with the head toward the center of the flap track.
(b) To make a small adjustment to the length of the skew control rod [24], do these steps:
1) Loosen the nut [26] and the nut [35].
2) Turn the adjustment sleeve [27] in the skew control rod [24] with the rod end [34]
attached to the crank arm [23].
NOTE: Make sure that the threads of the adjustment sleeve [27] cover a minimum
of half the inspection hole in the skew control rod [24].
NOTE: Make sure that the threads of the rod end [34] cover a minimum of half the
inspection hole in the adjustment sleeve [27].
(c) Torque the nut [26] to 125 in-lb (14 N·m) - 175 in-lb (20 N·m).
(d) Torque the nut [35] to 30 in-lb (3 N·m) - 50 in-lb (6 N·m).
(e) Make sure that the mismatch between the crank arm [23] and the rigging flange [21] is in
the limit.
(f) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G50347 between the nut [35] and the locking key [28].
(g) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G50347 between the nut [26] and the locking key [25].

(1) Make sure that these circuit breakers are open:

Row Col Number Name

SUBTASK 27-59-01-420-001
(2) Install the flap skew sensor [5]:
(a) Apply grease, D00633 to the packing [9].
(b) Install the packing [9] on the flap skew sensor [5].
(c) Apply grease, D00633 to the shaft of the flap skew sensor [5] and the splines on the
sensor input assembly [10].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
WARNING
USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COR￾BAN 27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH
WATER. IF THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH
YOUR EYES WITH WATER. GET MEDICAL AID. THIS MATERIAL
CONTAINS FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO
PERSONNEL.
(d) Apply a thin layer of Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (preferred) or corrosion inhibiting
material, G50136 (optional) to the mating surface of the flap skew sensor [5] and the
sensor input assembly [10].
(e) Engage the shaft on the flap skew sensor [5] with the sensor input assembly [10].
NOTE: The shaft has a missing tooth on the splines.
(f) Engage the alignment pin on the sensor input assembly [10] with the hole in the flap
skew sensor [5].
WARNING
USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COR￾BAN 27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH
WATER. IF THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH
YOUR EYES WITH WATER. GET MEDICAL AID. THIS MATERIAL
CONTAINS FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO
PERSONNEL.
(g) Apply Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (preferred) or corrosion inhibiting material,
G50136 (optional) to the shank and threads of the bolts [6].
(h) Install the bolts [6] and washers [7] to attach the flap skew sensor [5].
(i) Install the bolt [4], washer [3], and washer [1] to attach thejumper wire [2] to the flap skew
sensor [5].
(j) With the electrical bonding intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550, make
sure that the bonding resistance between the flap skew sensor [5] and jumper wire [2] is
less than 1.0 milliohm.
(k) With the electrical bonding intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550, make
sure that the bonding resistance between the flap skew sensor [5] and airplane structure
is less than 8.0 milliohms.
(l) Apply a bead of sealant, A02315 or sealant, A00247 to the head of the bolt [4].

SUBTASK 27-61-00-860-055
CAUTION
DO NOT OPERATE THE SYSTEM A OR THE SYSTEM B EMDP FOR MORE
THAN 2 MINUTES IF THE NO. 1 OR THE NO. 2 FUEL TANK (RESPECTIVELY)
CONTAINS LESS THAN 250 GALLONS (1675 POUNDS, 760 KG) OF FUEL.
YOU MUST LET THE RESERVOIR TEMPERATURE DECREASE TO AMBIENT
TEMPERATURE BEFORE YOU OPERATE THE PUMP AGAIN. DAMAGE TO
THE EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(1) Make sure that the No. 1 and No. 2 fuel tanks each have 250 gallons (1675 pounds/760
kilograms) of fuel in them.

(3) Make sure that this circuit breaker is closed:

panel to the ON position.

±5°F (±2.8°C) for the airframe temperature to become stable.

the cable run.

(a) Remove the bolt [32], washer [33], washer [34] and nut [35] that connects the ratio
changer input rod [37] to the input crank [31].

(c) Loosen the checknut [38] on the ratio changer input rod [37].

 ALL

NOTE: It must be possible to install the bolt without excessive force.
(e) Install the bolt [32] with the head up, washer [33], washer [34] and nut [35].
(f) Tighten the checknut [38] on the ratio changer input rod [37].

27-61-00-820-803Flight Spoiler AdjustmentPDF p. 3209
5. Flight Spoiler Adjustment
(Figure 501, Figure 502, Figure 503)
NOTE: There are two different sets of values for the spoiler gaps. One set is called standard gaps. The
other set is called reduced gaps. Reduced gaps were introduced in production to help reduce
airplane drag. You may use either the standard or the reduced gaps for any airplane. However,
for each airplane, you must choose which set of values (standard gaps or reduced gaps) to use to
adjust the spoilers. You must use only one set of values for each airplane. Use of standard gaps
on some spoilers and reduced gaps on other spoilers on the same airplane is not allowed.

SUBTASK 27-61-00-860-020
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF ALL
CONTROL SURFACES BEFORE YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER.
AILERONS, RUDDERS, ELEVATORS, FLAPS, SPOILERS AND THE THRUST
REVERSERS CAN MOVE QUICKLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC
POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(3) Do this task: Speed Brake Hydraulic Systems A and B Pressurization,

SUBTASK 27-61-00-866-005
(4) Extend the flaps (TASK 27-51-00-860-803).
SUBTASK 27-61-00-860-021
(5) Move the speed brake lever to the full up position to fully extend the spoilers.
SUBTASK 27-61-00-020-037
(6) If installed, remove and discard the MS20995NC32 lockwire, G01912, from the check nut [52].
SUBTASK 27-61-00-010-004
(7) Loosen the check nut [52].
(a) Hold the adjustment screw [51] with a hexdrive allen wrench, STD-1330.
SUBTASK 27-61-00-820-007

(8) Turn adjustment screw [51] clockwise 2 full turns, or until the stop is reached.
(a) Tighten the check nut [52].

 ALL
SUBTASK 27-61-00-860-022
(9) Do this task: Retract the Trailing Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-804.
SUBTASK 27-61-00-860-023

F. Flight Spoiler Adjustment
SUBTASK 27-61-00-860-024
(1) Measure the clearance (Dimension X) between the trailing edge of the spoiler panels and flaps
near the centerline of the spoiler actuators.
(2) Make sure that the clearance (Dimension X) between the spoilers and flaps are within the
limits on the following Spoilers Gaps Table:
NOTE: Measure the clearance aft of the spoiler actuator rod end. A larger or smaller clearance
is permitted at other locations along the spoiler.
NOTE: The two tables represent the different sets of spoilers gaps. You must adjust the
spoilers to the values in only one table. Adjust some spoilers to one table and other
spoilers on the same airplane to a different table is not allowed.
STANDARD SPOILERS GAPS
DIMENSION X Figure 503
SPOILERS MINIMUM MAXIMUM
2, 11 0.290 in. (7.366 mm) 0.350 in. (8.890 mm)
3, 10 0.240 in. (6.096 mm) 0.300 in. (7.620 mm)
4, 9 0.240 in. (6.096 mm) 0.300 in. (7.620 mm)
5, 8 0.025 in. (0.635 mm) 0.085 in. (2.159 mm)
REDUCED SPOILERS GAPS
DIMENSION X Figure 503
SPOILERS MINIMUM MAXIMUM
2, 11 0.070 in. (1.778 mm) 0.130 in. (3.302 mm)
3, 10 0.080 in. (2.032 mm) 0.140 in. (3.556 mm)

5, 8 0.030 in. (0.762 mm) 0.090 in. (2.286 mm)
SUBTASK 27-61-00-860-028
(3) If the clearances (Dimension X) between the spoiler panels and flaps are not in the limits,
adjust the clearance:
(a) Make a record of the clearance.
(b) Lift the spoiler and extend the flaps to get access to the spoiler actuator:
1) Do this task: Extend the Trailing Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-803.
2) Move the speed brake lever to the UP position to lift the spoilers.
3) Do this task: Speed Brake Hydraulic Systems A and B - Pressure Removal,
TASK 27-62-00-800-802.
(c) Remove the locking device from the check nut [55] on the actuator rod end [56].
(d) Loosen the check nut [55] on the actuator rod end [56].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(e) Turn the piston rod on the spoiler actuator to adjust the clearance between the spoiler
and flaps.
NOTE: Turning the piston rod 1/4 turn will change the clearance by approximately
0.09 in. (2.29 mm).
(f) Tighten the check nut [55].
(g) Check the adjustment.
1) Do this task: Put the Speed Brake Systems A and B Back to the Condition Before
the Pressure Removal, TASK 27-62-00-840-802.
2) Do this task: Retract the Trailing Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-804.
3) Slowly move the speed brake lever to the DOWN position.
4) Make sure that the clearances between the spoilers and flaps are within the
tolerances.
5) Turn the control wheel fully clockwise.
a) Make sure that spoilers No. 2, 3, 4, and 5 do not move down.
b) If the spoilers move down, go back to the start of the task.
NOTE: You do not need to check the fit of the rig pins a second time.
6) Turn the control wheel back to neutral to retract the flight spoilers.
7) Turn the control wheel fully counterclockwise.
a) Make sure that spoilers No. 8, 9, 10, and 11 do not move down.
b) If the spoilers move down, go back to the start of the task.
NOTE: You do not need to check the fit of the rig pins a second time.
(h) Extend the flaps (TASK 27-51-00-860-803).
(i) Move the speed brake lever to the full up position to extend the spoilers.
(j) Clean all grease from the piston rod and actuator rod end [56] threads with Series 84
solvent, B01004 (TASK 20-30-84-910-801).
(k) Apply a layer of the corrosion preventive D5026NS or ZC-026 compound, G50171, to the
threads of the actuator rod end [56].
(l) Tighten the check nut [55] to 250.0 in-lb (28.2 N·m) - 300.0 in-lb (33.9 N·m).
(m) Install the locking device to the check nut [55] on the actuator rod end [56].
(n) Install the MS20995NC32 lockwire, G01912, on the check nut [55].
(o) Apply a bead of sealant, A00247, to the check nut [55].
SUBTASK 27-61-00-860-122
(4) Check the adjustment of the spoiler actuator linkage, do this task: Spoiler Actuator Linkage
Adjustment, TASK 27-61-00-820-804.
SUBTASK 27-61-00-820-038
(5) Do this task: Flight Spoiler System Test, TASK 27-61-00-730-801 or Flight Spoiler System Test,
TASK 27-61-00-730-803.

(2) Do this task: Retract the Trailing Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-804.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-61-00-860-031

Pressurization, TASK 27-62-00-840-801.

F. Spoiler Actuator Linkage Adjustment
SUBTASK 27-61-00-700-002
(1) Check the adjustment of the spoiler actuator linkages for spoilers No. 2, 3, 4, and 5.
(a) Turn the captain's aileron control wheel fully clockwise to make sure the spoilers No. 2, 3,
4, and 5 are in the fully retracted position.
(b) Turn the control wheel 30.0 ± 0.5 degrees counterclockwise from the neutral position.
NOTE: Do not turn the control wheel past 30.5 degrees. If you do this, return the control
wheel to neutral and move the control wheel slowly to 30.0 ± 0.5 degrees again.
1) Make sure the spoilers No. 2, 3, 4, and 5 are extended to the positions shown in
Table 502.
Table 502/27-61-00-993-811
Control Wheel Position (Degrees CCW) Spoiler Number Panel Position (Degrees)
30 2 3.5 +1.0/-0.0
30 3 5.5 +1.0/-0.0
30 4 10.5 +1.0/-0.0
30 5 10.5 +1.0/-0.0
SUBTASK 27-61-00-820-008
(2) If the spoilers panel positions are not in the specified limits, adjust the linkage for spoilers No.
2, 3, 4, and 5.
(a) Do this task: Extend the Trailing Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-803.
(b) Hold the control wheel 30.0 ± 0.5 degrees counterclockwise from the neutral position.
(c) Loosen the check nut [52] on the linkage (Figure 503).
1) Hold the screw [51] with a hex wrench when you loosen the check nut [52].
NOTE: You may have to turn the control wheel past 30.5 degrees to turn the check
nut or adjustment screw.
CAUTION
DO NOT TURN THE ADJUSTMENT SCREW MORE THAN THE LIMITS. IT
CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ADJUSTMENT-SCREW SPRING PIN AND
COLLAR. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN
OCCUR.
(d) Turn the adjustment screw [51] to adjust the actuator linkage.
NOTE: A 1/4 turn of the adjustment screw will change the panel position by
approximately 0.75 degrees.
(e) Tighten the check nut [52] to 63.0 in-lb (7.1 N·m) - 67.0 in-lb (7.6 N·m) on the linkage.
(f) Turn the control wheel to neutral and back to 30.0 ± 0.5 degrees counterclockwise.
(g) Make sure the spoilers No. 2, 3, 4, and 5 are extended to the positions shown in
Table 502.
NOTE: Each spoiler has a different full-down position. The measurements in the table
need to be made from that position.

 ALL

SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND

(2) Do this task: Speed Brake Hydraulic Systems A and B Pressurization,

D. Spoiler Mixer Adjustment
SUBTASK 27-61-00-010-002
(1) Remove the roller access covers [71] to get access to the roller on the spoiler mixer [72].
(a) Remove bolts [73] and washers [74].
SUBTASK 27-61-00-860-088
(2) Make sure the speedbrake lever is in the DOWN position.
SUBTASK 27-61-00-860-089
(3) Turn the control wheel counter-clockwise 87 degrees from the neutral position.
SUBTASK 27-61-00-700-004
(4) Look at the spoiler mixer [72] cam through the left roller access cover [71].
(a) Make sure the left cam is near the maximum rise part of the spoiler mixer [72].
SUBTASK 27-61-00-860-040
(5) Turn the control wheel to the neutral position.
SUBTASK 27-61-00-860-041
(6) Turn the control wheel clockwise 87 degrees from the neutral position.
SUBTASK 27-61-00-700-005
(7) Look at the spoiler mixer [72] cam through the right roller access cover [71].
(a) Make sure the right cam is near the maximum rise part of the spoiler mixer [72].
SUBTASK 27-61-00-860-042
(8) Turn the control wheel to the neutral position.
SUBTASK 27-61-00-820-010
(9) If the cam followers are not near the maximum rise when you turn the control wheel, adjust the
SBA and SBB cables.
(a) Use the turnbuckles to make the cable SBB shorter by one-half turn and make the cable
SBA longer by one-half turn.
NOTE: The cable SBB is the lower cable on the speed brake quadrant on the ratio
changer. When you look forward, the speed brake quadrant will turn clockwise
when you tighten the cable SBB.
(b) To check the adjustment of cables SBA and SBB, do this task: Speed Brake Control
Cable Adjustment, TASK 27-62-00-820-802.
NOTE: After the adjustment it is not necessary for the rig pin S/B-2 to fit in the rig pin
hole.
(c) Make sure the cam followers are near the maximum rise when you turn the control wheel.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-61-00-010-003
(10) Install washers [74] and bolts [73] to close the roller access covers [71] on the spoiler mixer
[72].
SUBTASK 27-61-00-730-001
(11) Do this task: Flight Spoiler System Test, TASK 27-61-00-730-801 or Flight Spoiler System Test,
TASK 27-61-00-730-803.

E. Spoiler Position Sensor Adjustment
SUBTASK 27-61-00-030-001
(1) Loosen the bolt on the mounting bracket until you can turn the spoiler position sensor.
NOTE: You do not have to remove the bolt, washer, washer, and nut.
SUBTASK 27-61-00-820-041
(2) Turn the spoiler position sensor until the tester shows 7735 to 0042.
SUBTASK 27-61-00-820-042
(3) Rotate the thumb nut on the adjustment rod until the tester shows a value as close to 0000 (or
7777) as possible.
SUBTASK 27-61-00-430-003
(4) Lockwire the thumbnut.
SUBTASK 27-61-00-430-004
(5) Tighten the bolt on the mounting bracket to 8 in-lb (0.9 N·m) - 12 in-lb (1.4 N·m).

E. Flight Spoiler System Test
SUBTASK 27-61-00-020-028
(1) Turn the control wheel to 30 (+/- 0.5) degrees clockwise.
(a) Make sure that the spoilers No. 8 and No. 9 are up 10.5 +1.0/-0.0 degrees.
(b) Make sure that the spoiler No. 10 is up 5.5 +1.0/-0.0 degrees.
(c) Make sure that the spoiler No. 11 is up 3.5 +1.0/-0.0 degrees.
SUBTASK 27-61-00-020-029
(2) Turn the control wheel to 87 (+/-1) degrees clockwise.
(a) Make sure that the spoiler No. 9 is up 37 ± 2 degrees.
(b) Make sure spoiler No. 9 and spoiler No. 8 align in the limit of ± 2 degrees.
(c) Make sure that the spoiler No. 10 is up 32 ± 2 degrees.
(d) Make sure spoiler No. 10 and spoiler No. 11 align in the limit of ± 2 degrees.
(e) Make sure that the spoilers No. 2, 3, 4 and 5 are in the fully down position.
SUBTASK 27-61-00-020-011
(3) Turn the wheel counterclockwise until the spoiler No. 9 starts to move down.

 ALL

WARNING

F. Flight Spoiler Actuator Override Quadrant Operational Test
SUBTASK 27-61-00-710-008
(1) Install a plastic tie strap through the open hole of the input lever [3] on the spoiler Power
Control Unit (PCU).
SUBTASK 27-61-00-710-009
(2) Pull the input lever [3] of the PCU aft, to the full limit of travel, and verify that the hub
assembly [1] rotates and that the follower arm [2] moves in the slot of the quadrant control
assembly [5].
(a) Verify that the spring [4] extends.
SUBTASK 27-61-00-710-010
(3) Release the PCU input lever [3].
(a) Verify that the hub assembly [1] rotates back to the neutral position.
(b) Verify that the follower arm [2] returns to center.
SUBTASK 27-61-00-700-020
(4) If the operational test is for the left wing:
(a) Repeat the procedure, as necessary, for spoilers 2, 3, 4 and 5.
SUBTASK 27-61-00-710-013
(5) If the operational test is for the right wing:
(a) Repeat the procedure, as necessary, for spoilers 8, 9, 10 and 11.

(1) Remove rig pin A/S-15 from the aileron feel and centering unit.
(2) Remove the plastic tie strap from the input lever [3].

WARNING

PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.

 ALL

SUBTASK 27-61-00-860-092

D. Spoiler Mixer Centering Mechanism Operational Test
SUBTASK 27-61-00-710-002
(1) Turn the captain's aileron control wheel fully counterclockwise.
(a) Make sure the override mechanism (within the spoiler mixer) is operating properly.
NOTE: This operational test checks the internal function of the spoiler mixer unit. The
ratio changer input rod and the left spoiler output quadrant should move together
through the full control wheel travel. If the quadrant stops moving while the input
rod continues to move or if the quadrant does not move at all, there is an
override breakout.
SUBTASK 27-61-00-710-005
(2) Turn the captain's aileron control wheel fully clockwise.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Make sure the override mechanism (within the spoiler mixer) is operating properly.
NOTE: This operational test checks the internal function of the spoiler mixer unit. The
ratio changer input rod and the right spoiler output quadrant should move
together through the full control wheel travel. If the quadrant stops moving while
the input rod continues to move or if the quadrant does not move at all, there is
an override breakout.
SUBTASK 27-61-00-710-003
(3) Turn the captain's aileron control wheel fully counterclockwise and hold.
(a) Make sure the No. 2, 3, 4, and 5 flight spoilers move to the up position.
SUBTASK 27-61-00-710-006
(4) Release the captain's control wheel.
(a) Make sure the No. 2, 3, 4, and 5 flight spoilers move to the down position.
SUBTASK 27-61-00-710-004
(5) Turn the captain's aileron control wheel fully clockwise and hold.
(a) Make sure the No. 8, 9, 10 and 11 flight spoilers move to the up position.
SUBTASK 27-61-00-710-007
(6) Release the captain's control wheel.
(a) Make sure the No. 8, 9, 10, and 11 flight spoilers move to the down position.

(1) Do this task: Put the Spoiler Hydraulic systems A and B Back to the Condition Before the
Pressurization, TASK 27-61-00-840-801.

structure.
1) Discard the nut [32] and washers [31].
(b) Remove the nut [60] and washers [59] to disconnect the bonding jumper [52] from the
structure.
1) Discard the nut [60] and washers [59].
(c) Disconnect the aft end of the control rod for the spoiler position transmitter from the flight
spoiler no. 3 [2] (View K, Figure 401).
1) Remove the bolt [77], washer [78], bushing [79], washer [80], and nut [81].
(d) Disconnect the aft end of the control rod for the spoiler position transmitter from the flight
spoiler no. 4 [3] (View K, Figure 401).
1) Remove the bolt [77], washer [78], bushing [79], washer [80], and nut [81].
(e) Disconnect the spoiler actuator [30] from the spoiler no. 3 [2], spoiler no. 4 [3], or spoiler
no. 5 [4] (TASK 27-61-51-000-801).
(f) Remove the cotter pin [38], nut [37], washer [36], bushing [35], washer [34], and bolt [33].
(g) Remove the cotter pin [45], nut [44], washer [43], bushing [42], washer [41], and bolt [40].
(h) Remove the cotter pin [51], nut [50], washer [49], bushing [48], washer [47], and bolt [46].
(i) Remove the cotter pin [58], nut [57], washer [56], bushing [55], washer [54], and bolt [53].
(j) Remove the flight spoiler no. 3 [2], spoiler no. 4 [3], or spoiler no. 5 [4] from the airplane.

SUBTASK 27-61-11-420-001
(1) Install the flight spoiler no. 2 [1], do these steps (View B, Figure 401):
(a) Put the flight spoiler no. 2 [1] in its position on the airplane.
(b) Install the bolt [8] with head outboard, washer [9], bushing [10], washer [11], nut [12], and
cotter pin [13].
(c) Install the bolt [15] with head inboard, washer [16], bushing [17], washer [18], nut [19],
and cotter pin [20].
(d) Install the bolt [24] with head outboard, washer [25], bushings [26], washer [27], nut [28],
and cotter pin [29].
(e) Connect the rod end of the spoiler actuator [5] to the spoiler no. 2 [1]
(TASK 27-61-51-400-801).
(f) Install the new nut [7] and new washers [6] to connect the bonding jumper [14] to the
structure.
1) Use cotton wiper, G00034, moist in solvent, B00184, to clean the mating surfaces of
the airplane structure, nut [7], washers [6], and bonding jumper [14].
2) Install the nut [7], washers [6], and bonding jumper [14].
3) Tighten the nut [7] to 28 in-lb (3 N·m) - 35 in-lb (4 N·m).

 ALL

structure (SWPM 20-20-00).

less.

F. Spoiler Shutoff Valve Removal
SUBTASK 27-61-12-020-001
(1) Remove the spoiler shutoff valve [12].
(a) Disconnect the electrical connector [1] from the spoiler shutoff valve motor [7].
(b) After you disconnect the electrical connector(s), examine the connector(s) for corrosion.
NOTE: The inspection of the electrical connector(s) can be done after the removal step
or before the installation step of the electrical connector(s). This is an operator
option.
WARNING
DO THE STEPS BELOW IF THE AIRPLANE OPERATES WHERE
DEICING FLUID THAT CONTAINS POTASSIUM FORMATE OR
POTASSIUM ACETATE IS USED. ALSO, DO THE STEPS FOR ALL
AIRPLANES THAT YOU FOUND CORROSION IN THE ELECTRICAL
CONNECTORS IN THE MAIN WHEEL WELL. THE ELECTRICAL
CONNECTORS ARE IN A SYSTEM THAT IS NECESSARY FOR SAFE
FLIGHT.
(c) If there was corrosion, correct the problem (SWPM 20-60-03).
(d) Remove the lockwires from the bolts [4].
(e) Put a 5 gallon (19 liter) container, STD-1154, below the spoiler shutoff valve [12]
assembly to catch hydraulic fluid.
(f) Remove the bolts [4] and washers [5] that attach the spoiler shutoff valve [12] assembly
to the flight controls hydraulic module housing [2].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(g) Carefully lift the spoiler shutoff valve [12] assembly straight up to remove it from the flight
controls hydraulic module housing [2].
(h) Put a cover on the flight controls hydraulic module housing [2] to keep contamination out
of the open valve hole.

F. Spoiler Shutoff Valve Installation
SUBTASK 27-61-12-420-001
(1) If the spoiler shutoff valve [12] does not have the packing [9], backup rings [8], packing [11],
and backup rings [10] installed, do these steps:
(a) Apply hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the packing [9], backup rings [8], packing [11], and
backup rings [10].
(b) Install the packing [9], backup rings [8], packing [11], and backup rings [10] to the spoiler
shutoff valve [12] assembly.
SUBTASK 27-61-12-420-002
(2) Carefully install the spoiler shutoff valve [12] assembly in the flight controls hydraulic module
housing [2].
(a) Install the bolts [4] and washers [5] to attach the spoiler shutoff valve [12] assembly to the
flight controls hydraulic module housing [2].
(b) Tighten the bolts [4] to 30 in-lb (3 N·m) - 40 in-lb (5 N·m).
(c) Install the lockwires on the bolts [4].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(d) If you did not examine the electrical connector(s) at the removal step, do these steps:
NOTE: The inspection of the electrical connector(s) can be done after the removal step
or before the installation step of the electrical connector(s). This is an operator
option.
1) Before you connect the electrical connector(s), examine the connector(s) for
corrosion.
WARNING
DO THE STEPS BELOW IF THE AIRPLANE OPERATES WHERE
DEICING FLUID THAT CONTAINS POTASSIUM FORMATE OR
POTASSIUM ACETATE IS USED. ALSO, DO THE STEPS FOR ALL
AIRPLANES THAT YOU FOUND CORROSION IN THE ELECTRICAL
CONNECTORS IN THE MAIN WHEEL WELL. THE ELECTRICAL
CONNECTORS ARE IN A SYSTEM THAT IS NECESSARY FOR SAFE
FLIGHT.
2) If there was corrosion, correct the problem (SWPM 20-60-03).
(e) Apply the D5026NS or ZC-026 compound, G50171, to the electrical connector [1]
(SWPM 20-60-03).
(f) Connect the electrical connector [1] to the spoiler shutoff valve motor [7].

E. Spoiler Shutoff Valve Motor Removal
SUBTASK 27-61-12-020-002
(1) Do these steps to remove the spoiler shutoff valve motor [7].
(a) Disconnect the electrical connector [1] from the spoiler shutoff valve motor [7].
(b) Examine the electrical connector [1] for corrosion.
NOTE: The inspection of the electrical connector can be done after the removal step or
before the installation step of the electrical connector. This is an operator option.
WARNING
DO THE STEPS BELOW IF THE AIRPLANE OPERATES WHERE
DEICING FLUID THAT CONTAINS POTASSIUM FORMATE OR
POTASSIUM ACETATE IS USED. ALSO, DO THE STEPS FOR ALL
AIRPLANES THAT YOU FOUND CORROSION IN THE ELECTRICAL
CONNECTORS IN THE MAIN WHEEL WELL. THE ELECTRICAL
CONNECTORS ARE IN A SYSTEM THAT IS NECESSARY FOR SAFE
FLIGHT.
(c) If there was corrosion, correct the problem (SWPM 20-60-03).
(d) Set the manual override lever on the spoiler shutoff valve motor [7] to position 2.
(e) Remove the lockwire from the screws [6].
(f) Remove the screws [6] that attach the spoiler shutoff valve motor [7] to the spoiler shutoff
valve [12].
(g) Remove the spoiler shutoff valve motor [7] from the spoiler shutoff valve [12].

D. Spoiler Shutoff Valve Test
SUBTASK 27-61-12-720-001
(1) Do the test of the spoiler shutoff valve [1]:
(a) Move the two SPOILER switches, on the P5-3 flights control panel, to the OFF position
and then to the ON position (Figure 501).
(b) Make sure that the manual override levers [2] of the two spoiler shutoff valves [1] are in
position 1 (Figure 502).
(c) Move one of the two aileron control wheels to bleed the hydraulic system.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(d) Make sure that there is no leakage of hydraulic fluid at the spoiler shutoff valves [1].
(e) Move the aileron control wheel to make sure that the flight spoilers operate correctly.
(f) Set the two SPOILER switches to the OFF position.
(g) Make sure that the manual override levers [2] of the two spoiler shutoff valves [1] are in
position 2.
(h) Move the aileron control wheel to make sure that the flight spoilers do not operate.
E. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 27-61-12-860-010
(1) Set the SPOILER switches to the ON position.
SUBTASK 27-61-12-820-001
(2) Make sure that the manual override levers [2] of the two spoiler shutoff valves [1] are in
position 1 (Figure 502).
SUBTASK 27-61-12-860-011

Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805.

F. Spoiler Control Quadrant Removal
SUBTASK 27-61-41-020-001
(1) Disconnect aileron control cable AA [1] and cable AB [3]:
(a) Install the turnbuckle clamps on the cable AA [1] and cable AB [3] to keep a small tension
when you disconnect the cable turnbuckles [2].
(b) Disconnect the cable turnbuckles [2].
(c) Remove the nuts, washers, and bolts to remove the retaining plates from the spoiler
cable quadrant [5] (Control Cable End Retaining Plate - Removal,
TASK 20-10-96-000-801).
(d) Remove cable AA [1] and cable AB [3] from the spoiler cable quadrant [5].
(e) Install a tag on cable AA [1] and cable AB [3] for identification during the installation.
SUBTASK 27-61-41-020-002
(2) Remove the spoiler cable quadrant [5].
(a) Remove the nuts [9], washers [8], washers [7], and bolts [6] that attach the spoiler cable
quadrant [5] to the quadrant shaft [36].
(b) Disconnect the spoiler cable quadrant [5] from the quadrant shaft [36] and remove it from
the airplane.
(c) Remove the nut [19], washer [18], washer [17], and bolt [16] that attaches the ratio
changer input rod [35] to the upper control crank [15].
(d) Remove the nut [30], washer [29], washer [28], and bolt [27] that attaches the aileron
spring cartridge [31] to the aileron input crank [26].
(e) Remove the nuts [24], washers [23], washers [22], and bolts [21] that attach the quadrant
shaft support bracket [25] to the wheel well forward bulkhead [20].
(f) Remove the nuts [14], washers [13], washers [12], and bolts [11] that attach the bearing
retainer [38] to the wheel well ceiling [37].
(g) Break the pressure seal between the bearing retainer [38] and the wheel well ceiling [37].
(h) Disconnect the quadrant shaft [36] from the spoiler cable quadrant [5].
(i) Lower the quadrant shaft [36] from the wheel well ceiling [37] and remove it from the
airplane.

F. Spoiler Control Quadrant Installation
SUBTASK 27-61-41-020-003
(1) If you will install a new spoiler control quadrant, remove the spoiler cable quadrant [5] from the
quadrant shaft [36].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-61-41-200-001
(2) Do a check of the shear rivets [32] on the quadrant shaft [36] at the aileron input crank [26]:
(a) Make sure that the witness hole in the aileron input crank [26] and the quadrant shaft [36]
align correctly.
NOTE: The marker instructions are located on the quadrant shaft [36].
SUBTASK 27-61-41-420-002
(3) Attach the quadrant shaft [36] to the wheel well ceiling [37]:
(a) Apply a pressure seal to the bearing retainer [38] and the wheel well ceiling [37], to apply
seal, do this task: Non-Removable Faying (Mated) Surface Seal Application,
TASK 51-31-00-390-801.
(b) Put the quadrant shaft [36] through the opening in the wheel well ceiling [37].
NOTE: Make sure that the bearing housing is aligned with the correct bolt holes in the
wheel well ceiling.
(c) Install the bolts [11] with the heads up through the wheel well ceiling [37] to attach the
bearing retainer [38].
(d) Install the washers [12], washers [13] and nuts [14] on the bolts [11].
(e) Torque the nuts [14] to 20 in-lb (2.3 N·m) - 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m).
SUBTASK 27-61-41-420-003
(4) Install the quadrant shaft support bracket [25] on the wheel well forward bulkhead [20]:
(a) Put the quadrant shaft support bracket [25] in its position.
(b) Install the bolts [21], washers [22], washers [23] and nuts [24]] to attach the quadrant
shaft support bracket [25].
SUBTASK 27-61-41-420-008
(5) Connect the spoiler cable quadrant [5] to the quadrant shaft [36]:
(a) Install the spoiler cable quadrant [5] on the quadrant shaft [36].
(b) Apply sealant, A00247, to the bolts [6].
(c) Install the bolts [6], washers [7], washer [8] and nuts [9] to attach the spoiler cable
quadrant [5] to the quadrant shaft [36].
(d) Torque the nuts [9] to 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m) - 80 in-lb (9.0 N·m).
SUBTASK 27-61-41-390-001
(6) Examine the sealant on the seal disk [42] at the top of the quadrant shaft [36] for damage.
(a) If the seal disk [42] has damage, apply sealant, A00247, to the shoulder of the shaft
(SEALS AND SEALING - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES, PAGEBLOCK 51-31-00/201).
(b) Push the seal disk [42] tightly on the shoulder of the shaft.
SUBTASK 27-61-41-420-009
(7) Connect the right aileron control cable AA [1] and cable AB [3]:
(a) Use the cable retaining plates to attach the cables to the spoiler cable quadrant [5]
(Control Cable End Retaining Plate - Installation, TASK 20-10-96-400-801).
(b) Connect aileron control cable AA [1] and cable AB [3] at the cable turnbuckles [2].
(c) Remove the cable clamps from aileron control cable AA [1] and cable AB [3].
SUBTASK 27-61-41-420-010
(8) Do this task: Aileron Cables Adjustment, TASK 27-11-00-820-801.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-61-41-420-004
(9) Install the aileron spring cartridge [31]:
(a) Do this task: Spoiler Hydraulic Systems A and B Pressurization, TASK 27-61-00-800-801.
(b) Install the rig pins A/S-4 and A/S-3 from the test set rigging pin kit, SPL-1585.
(c) If you cannot easily install and remove the rig pin A/S-3 adjust the aileron spring
cartridge [31].
1) Loosen the checknut [40].
2) Use the collar nut [41] to adjust the length of the aileron spring cartridge [31] until
you can easily install and remove rig pin A/S-3.
a) Make sure that the internal spring does not deflect.
b) Make sure that there is no backlash.
3) Torque the checknut [40] to 10 in-lb (1.1 N·m) - 20 in-lb (2.3 N·m).
4) Install MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, on the checknut [40] and collar nut [41].
(d) Connect the aileron spring cartridge [31] to the aileron input crank [26]:
1) Make sure that the drain holes [39] on the aileron spring cartridge [31] are down.
2) Install the bolt [27] with the bolt head up.
3) Install the washer [28], washer [29] and nut [30] on the bolt [27].
(e) Remove the rig pin A/S-4.
(f) Do this task: Pressure from the Aileron Hydraulic Systems A and B - Deactivation,
TASK 27-11-00-860-801
SUBTASK 27-61-41-420-005
(10) Connect the ratio changer input rod [35] to the upper control crank [15]:
(a) Install the rig pin A/S-14 from the test set rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, in the spoiler
mixer [33].
(b) Make sure that you can easily install the bolt [16] in the ratio changer input rod [35].
(c) If you cannot easily install the bolt [16], adjust the length of the rod:
1) Loosen the checknut on the ratio changer input rod [35].
2) Adjust the ratio changer input rod [35] end until you can easily install the bolt [16] in
the rod end.
3) Tighten the checknut on the ratio changer input rod [35].
(d) Install the bolt [16] to attach the ratio changer input rod [35] to the upper control
crank [15].
(e) Install the washer [17], washer [18] and nut [19] on the bolt [16].
(f) Remove the rig pin A/S-3 and A/S-14.
SUBTASK 27-61-41-720-001
(11) Do this task: Spoiler Control Quadrant Functional Test, TASK 27-61-41-000-802.

WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF ALL

AILERONS, RUDDERS, ELEVATORS, FLAPS, SLATS, SPOILERS, LANDING

E. Spoiler Control Quadrant Test
SUBTASK 27-61-41-020-004
(1) Turn the captain's aileron control wheel 87 degrees counterclockwise:
(a) Make sure that the spoiler No. 2 moves 32 +/-3 degrees up from the retracted position.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) Make sure that the spoiler No. 4 moves 37 +/-3 degrees up from the retracted position
SUBTASK 27-61-41-020-007
(2) Turn the wheel clockwise until the spoiler No. 2 starts to retract.
(a) Make sure that the control wheel is a minimum of 70 degrees counterclockwise.
SUBTASK 27-61-41-020-005
(3) Turn the captain's aileron control wheel 87 degrees clockwise:
(a) Make sure that the spoiler No. 8 moves 37 +/-3 degrees up from the retracted position.
(b) Make sure that the spoiler No. 10 moves 32 +/-3 degrees up from the retracted position
SUBTASK 27-61-41-020-006
(4) Turn the wheel counterclockwise until the spoiler No. 8 starts to retract.
(a) Make sure that the control wheel is a minimum of 70 degrees clockwise.
SUBTASK 27-61-41-820-003
(5) Turn the captain's aileron control wheel to the neutral position.
(a) Make sure that the spoilers move to the retracted position.

SUBTASK 27-61-41-020-016
(4) Remove the protractor, COM-1691, from the upper surface of spoilers No. 2, 4, 8 and 10.

D. Flight Spoiler Actuator Quadrant Removal
SUBTASK 27-61-61-020-001
(1) Disconnect the wing spoiler cables WSA [2] and WSB [4] from the applicable quadrant:
(a) Install the turnbuckle clamps to keep a small tension on the wing spoiler cables WSA [2]
and WSB [4].
(b) Loosen the turnbuckles [3] for the cables.
(c) Remove the guard pin [34], guard [35] (if applicable), and pin [36].
(d) Remove the cotter pin [38].
NOTE: For ground spoilers 1 and 6 for the left wing and spoilers 7 and 12 on the right
wing, it is also necessary to remove the nuts [28], washers [27], bolts [26] and
retainers [29] (Control Cable End Retaining Plate - Removal,
TASK 20-10-96-000-801).
(e) Remove the wing spoiler cables WSA [2] and WSB [4] from the quadrant [37].
SUBTASK 27-61-61-020-002
(2) Remove the flight spoiler actuator quadrant [37]:
(a) Remove the pin [33], nut [32], washer [31], and bolt [30] to disconnect the quadrant [37]
from the actuator input arm [21].
(b) Remove the nut [25], washer [24], washer [23], and bolt [22] from the quadrant [37].
NOTE: Keep the bearings and bushing with the quadrant [37].
(c) Remove the quadrant [37] from the structure.

F. Speed Brake Control System Tryout
NOTE: This tryout is to make sure that the speed brake control system is in zero energy state.
SUBTASK 27-62-00-710-005
(1) Do these steps to check the spoiler control system:
(a) Move the speed brake lever from the DOWN position to the UP position.
1) Make sure that the speed brakes do not move.
(b) Move the speed brake lever from the UP position to the DOWN position.
1) Make sure that the speed brakes do not move.
(c) Turn the captain's control wheel a minimum of 4 units.
(d) Make sure that there is no movement from the spoiler and wheel forces are higher than
usual.
(e) Move the captain's control wheel back to the neutral position.

wheel.

HYDRAULIC FLUID WILL BECOME TOO HOT.

(1) Remove the flight controls hydraulic module locks from the spoiler shutoff valves.
(a) Remove the detent pins.
(b) Remove the lock, SPL-1675 from the two spoiler shutoff valves.
(c) Put the manual override lever at the two spoiler shutoff valves in the position 1 (ON
position).
(d) If you did not examine the electrical connector(s) at the removal step, do these steps:
NOTE: The inspection of the electrical connector(s) can be done after the removal step
or before the installation step of the electrical connector(s). This is an operator
option.
1) Before you connect the electrical connector(s), examine the connector(s) for
corrosion.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
WARNING
DO THE STEPS BELOW IF THE AIRPLANE OPERATES WHERE
DEICING FLUID THAT CONTAINS POTASSIUM FORMATE OR
POTASSIUM ACETATE IS USED. ALSO, DO THE STEPS FOR ALL
AIRPLANES THAT YOU FOUND CORROSION IN THE ELECTRICAL
CONNECTORS IN THE MAIN WHEEL WELL. THE ELECTRICAL
CONNECTORS ARE IN A SYSTEM THAT IS NECESSARY FOR SAFE
FLIGHT.
2) If there was corrosion, refer to (SWPM 20-60-03) to correct the problem.
(e) Apply the D5026NS or ZC-026 compound, G50171 to the connector (SWPM 20-60-03).
(f) Connect the electrical connector to the spoiler shutoff valve at the spoiler hydraulic
modules A and B.
SUBTASK 27-62-00-860-011

 ALL

2) Remove the nut [16], washer [15] and bolt [14] to disconnect the top end of the

4) Loosen the checknut [17] and adjust the lower control rod [18] end until you can
install the bolt [14].
5) Install the bolt [14], washer [15] and nut [16] to attach the lower control rod [18] end
to the idler link [13].

 ALL
7) Make sure you can see the rod end through the inspection hole on the lower control
rod [18].

detents on the indicator plate:
1) Move the speed brake control lever [8] to the DOWN position.
2) Make sure the pointer aligns with the DOWN marker on the indicator plate.
3) Move the speed brake control lever [8] to the ARMED position.
4) Make sure the pointer aligns with the ARMED marker on the indicator plate.
5) Move the speed brake control lever [8] to the FLIGHT DETENT position.
6) Make sure the pointer aligns with the FLIGHT DETENT marker on the indicator
plate.
7) Move the speed brake control lever [8] to the UP position.
8) Make sure the pointer aligns with the UP marker on the indicator plate.
9) Move the speed brake control lever [8] to the DOWN position.
(g) If the pointer does not align with the markers on the indicator plate or, adjust the speed
brake control lever [8]:
1) Make sure the lever latch is in the DOWN detent on the control stand.
2) If the pointer on the speed brake control lever [8] does not align with the center of
the DOWN detent, adjust the positions of the indicator plate:
a) Loosen the screws [19] that attach the indicator plate to the control stand.
b) Move the indicator plate until the center of the DOWN position aligns with the
pointer on the speed brake control lever [8].
c) Tighten the screws [19] on the indicator plate.
3) Do this task: Speed Brake Lever Position Sensor Adjustment,

Adjustment and Test, TASK 27-62-34-400-802.

on the cam.
6) Make sure the pointer aligns with the ARMED indicator on the indicator plate.
7) If the pointer does not align, adjust the indicator plate with the speed brake control
lever [8] in the DOWN position again.
8) Move the speed brake lever aft until the roller [6] is in the flight detent on the cam.
9) Make sure the pointer aligns with the FLIGHT DETENT indicator on indicator plate.
10) If the pointer does not align, adjust the position of the indicator plate with the speed
brake control lever [8] in the DOWN position again.

27-62-00-820-802Speed Brake Control Cable AdjustmentPDF p. 3465
5. Speed Brake Control Cable Adjustment
(Figure 501, Figure 502)
A. General
(1) Use this procedure to adjust the speed brake control cables SBA [35] and SBB [34].
(2) Before you do cable adjustment, permit a minimum of one hour at a constant ambient
temperature of ±5°F (+/- 2.8°C) for the airframe temperature to become stable.
(a) The cable tension values will not be correct when there are temperature differences along
the cable run.
(3) It is recommended that airplanes supplied with the cables that contain higher zinc coating
(Grade D or Grade K) be re-tensioned 3 to 4 months into service. This will bring the tension of
the control cables within the desired range. After the cables are re-tensioned the high zinc
cables (Grade D or Grade K) will continue to relax at a rate that is equivalent to Grade B
cables. To identify the grade of the cable, refer to: Aileron Cables Adjustment,
TASK 27-11-00-820-801.
(4) It is recommended that cable assemblies on each side of a cable loop be replaced at the same
time using the same grade material in order to minimize asymmetric relaxation.

AILERONS, RUDDERS, ELEVATORS, FLAPS, SLATS, SPOILERS, LANDING
GEAR, AND THRUST REVERSERS CAN MOVE QUICKLY WHEN YOU
SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(1) Do this task: Speed Brake Hydraulic Systems A and B Pressurization,
TASK 27-62-00-800-801.
SUBTASK 27-62-00-210-002
(2) Examine the hydraulic connections on the ground spoiler control valve [51] for leakage.
SUBTASK 27-62-00-870-002
(3) Move the speed brake lever through more than one full cycle to bleed the hydraulic system.
SUBTASK 27-62-00-820-003
(4) Do the ground spoiler control valve [51] adjustment:
(a) Make sure that the speed brake lever is in the DOWN position.
(b) Remove the bolt [52], washer [53] and nut [54] that attach the control rod [55] to the valve
lever [56].
(c) Use digital protractor, STD-1232, to position the speed brake lever to 29 +/-2 degrees aft
of the DOWN position.
NOTE: 29 +/-2 degrees is equivalent to 2.78 ±0.20 in. (70.6 ±5.1 mm) of the speed brake
lever travel from the DOWN position measured along the top surface of the aisle
stand light plate.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(d) By hand slowly move the valve lever [56] inboard until the inboard spoilers begin to
move.
NOTE: The inboard spoilers will move before the outboard spoilers.
(e) Adjust the control rod [55]:
1) Loosen the checknut on the control rod [55].
2) Adjust the length of the control rod [55] until you can install the bolt [52].
3) Install the washer [53], nut [54] and bolt [52].
4) Make sure that you can see the threads of the rod end through the inspection hole
in the control rod [55].
5) Tighten the checknut.
(f) Move the speed brake lever to the DOWN position.
(g) Slowly move the speed brake lever aft.
(h) Make sure that the inboard spoilers begin to move at speed brake lever position of 29
+/-2 degrees aft of the DOWN position.
(i) Adjust the control rod [55] if necessary.
SUBTASK 27-62-00-860-016
(5) Do this task: Put the Speed Brake Hydraulic systems A and B Back to the Condition Before the
Pressurization, TASK 27-62-00-840-801.
SUBTASK 27-62-00-610-001
(6) If necessary to fill the hydraulic reservoir, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoir Servicing,
TASK 12-12-00-610-801.

9. Ground Spoiler Adjustment
(Figure 506)
NOTE: There are two different sets of values for the spoiler gaps. One set is called standard gaps. The
other set is called reduced gaps. Reduced gaps were introduced in production to help reduce
airplane drag. You may use either the standard or the reduced gaps for any airplane. However,
for each airplane, you must choose which set of values (standard gaps or reduced gaps) to use to
adjust the spoilers. You must use only one set of values for each airplane. Use of standard gaps
on some spoilers and reduced gaps on other spoilers on the same airplane is not allowed.

E. Ground Spoiler Adjustment
SUBTASK 27-62-00-860-023
(1) Measure the clearance (Dimension X) between the trailing edge of the spoiler panels and the
flaps near the centerline of the spoiler actuators.
(2) Make sure the clearance (Dimension X) between the spoilers and the flaps are within the limits
on the following Spoilers Gaps Table:
NOTE: You do not need to check the clearance at the inboard actuator.
NOTE: The two tables represent the different sets of spoiler gaps. You must adjust the
spoilers to the values in only one table. Adjust some spoilers to one table and other
spoilers on the same airplane to a different table is not allowed.
STANDARD SPOILERS GAPS
DIMENSION X Figure 506
SPOILERS MINIMUM MAXIMUM
1, 12 0.020 INCH (0.51 mm) 0.120 INCH (3.05 mm)
6, 7 0.005 INCH (0.13 mm) 0.100 INCH (2.54 mm)
REDUCED SPOILERS GAPS
DIMENSION X Figure 506
SPOILERS MINIMUM MAXIMUM
1, 12 0.030 INCH (0.76 mm) 0.130 INCH (3.30 mm)
6, 7 0.030 INCH (0.76 mm) 0.125 INCH (3.17 mm)
(3) Make sure there is clearance between the trailing edge of the spoiler panels and the flaps for
the full span of the spoiler.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-62-00-860-027
(4) If the clearances (Dimension X) between the ground spoiler panels and the flaps are not in the
limits, adjust the clearance:
(a) Make a record of the clearance.
(b) Lift the spoiler or extend the flaps to get access to the spoiler actuator:
1) Do this task: Extend the Trailing Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-803.
2) Move the speed brake lever to the UP position to lift the spoilers.
3) Do this task: Speed Brake Hydraulic Systems A and B - Pressure Removal,
TASK 27-62-00-800-802.
(c) Loosen the checknut on the rod end of the ground spoiler actuator.
(d) Remove the locking key from the piston rod.
(e) Do the following to adjust the Outboard Ground Spoilers (No. 1 and 12):
1) Turn the piston rod on the spoiler actuator to adjust the clearance between the
spoiler and the flaps to the correct tolerance.
2) Temporarily torque the actuator check nut to 100 - 200 pound-inches (11.3 - 22.6
newton-meters).
3) Move the speedbrake lever to the UP position.
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF
ALL CONTROL SURFACES BEFORE YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC
POWER. AILERONS, RUDDERS, ELEVATORS, FLAPS, SLATS,
SPOILERS, LANDING GEAR, AND THRUST REVERSERS CAN
MOVE QUICKLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS
CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
4) Do this task: Speed Brake Hydraulic Systems A and B Pressurization,
TASK 27-62-00-800-801.
5) Do this task: Retract the Trailing Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-804.
6) Move the speedbrake lever to the DOWN position.
7) Check the clearance at the trailing edge of the ground spoilers.
a) Make sure the clearance is within the limits (Figure 506).
8) If the clearance of the ground spoiler is not in the limits, do the following to adjust
the actuator:
a) Do this task: Extend the Trailing Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-803.
b) Do this task: Speed Brake Hydraulic Systems A and B - Pressure Removal,
TASK 27-62-00-800-802.
c) Adjust the spoiler actuator again, as necessary.
9) If the clearance of the ground spoiler is in the limits, do the following:
a) Do this task: Extend the Trailing Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-803.
b) Move the speed brake lever to the UP position to extend the spoilers.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR
OF ALL CONTROL SURFACES BEFORE YOU SUPPLY
HYDRAULIC POWER. AILERONS, RUDDERS, ELEVATORS,
FLAPS, SLATS, SPOILERS, LANDING GEAR, AND THRUST
REVERSERS CAN MOVE QUICKLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY
HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS
AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
c) Do this task: Speed Brake Hydraulic Systems A and B - Pressure Removal,
TASK 27-62-00-800-802.
d) Clean all grease from the piston rod and the rod end threads with Series 84
solvent, B01004 (TASK 20-30-84-910-801).
e) Apply a layer of the corrosion preventive D5026NS or ZC-026 compound,
G50171 to the threads of the piston rod end.
f) Install the locking key in the actuator rod end.
g) Torque the checknut to 250-300 pound-inches (28.25-33.90 newton-meters).
h) Install the MS20995NC32 lockwire, G01912 on the checknut.
i) Apply a bead of sealant, A00247 to the rod end checknut.
(f) Do the following to adjust the Inboard Ground Spoilers (No. 6 and 7):
1) Turn the piston rod on the outboard spoiler actuator to adjust the clearance between
the spoiler and the flaps to the correct tolerance.
2) Turn the piston rod on the inboard spoiler actuator until the pin that connects the rod
end to the spoiler panel moves freely or is loose.
NOTE: Make sure there is no force fight between the inboard and outboard
actuators.
3) Temporarily torque the actuator check nut to 100 - 200 pound-inches (11.3 - 22.6
newton-meters).
4) Move the speedbrake lever to the UP position.
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF
ALL CONTROL SURFACES BEFORE YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC
POWER. AILERONS, RUDDERS, ELEVATORS, FLAPS, SLATS,

5) Do this task: Speed Brake Hydraulic Systems A and B Pressurization,

6) Do this task: Retract the Trailing Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-804.
7) Move the speedbrake lever to the DOWN position.
8) Check the clearance at the trailing edge of the ground spoilers.
a) Make sure the clearance is within the limits (Figure 506).
9) If the clearance of the ground spoiler is not in the limits, do the following to adjust

a) Do this task: Extend the Trailing Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-803.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
b) Do this task: Speed Brake Hydraulic Systems A and B - Pressure Removal,

c) Adjust the spoiler actuator again, as necessary.
10) If the clearance of the ground spoiler is in the limits, do the following:

b) Move the speed brake lever to the UP position to extend the spoilers.

F. Speed Brake Lever Brake Adjustment
SUBTASK 27-62-00-200-003
(1) Adjust the secondary backlash of the speed brake lever brake.
(a) Apply a 4.5 lbf (20.0 N) load to setscrew C so that setscrew A touches the drive
(Figure 508).
(b) Put a 0-0.150 Inch (0-3.81 mm) feeler gauge set, STD-1337, adjusted to 0.036 in.
(0.914 mm) - 0.037 in. (0.940 mm) between the drive and setscrew B.
(c) Adjust setscrew B until it is tight against the 0-0.150 Inch (0-3.81 mm) feeler gauge set,
STD-1337.
(d) Remove the 0-0.150 Inch (0-3.81 mm) feeler gauge set, STD-1337.
SUBTASK 27-62-00-200-004
(2) Adjust the setscrew D primary backlash of the speed brake lever brake.
(a) Put a 0-0.150 Inch (0-3.81 mm) feeler gauge set, STD-1337, adjusted to 0.018 in.
(0.457 mm) between the drive and setscrew A.
(b) Apply a 1.5 lbf (6.7 N) load to setscrew C.
(c) Put the 0-0.150 Inch (0-3.81 mm) feeler gauge set, STD-1337, adjusted to 0.010 in.
(0.254 mm) - 0.011 in. (0.279 mm) between setscrew D and the adjacent shoe face.
(d) Adjust setscrew D until it is tight against the 0-0.150 Inch (0-3.81 mm) feeler gauge set,
STD-1337.
(e) With the 0-0.150 Inch (0-3.81 mm) feeler gauge set, STD-1337, in position, tighten the
locknut of setscrew D.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(f) Remove the 0-0.150 Inch (0-3.81 mm) feeler gauge sets, STD-1337, between the drive
and setscrew A, and between setscrew D and the adjacent shoe face.
SUBTASK 27-62-00-200-005
(3) Adjust the setscrew C primary backlash of the speed brake lever brake.
(a) Put a 0-0.150 Inch (0-3.81 mm) feeler gauge set, STD-1337, adjusted to 0.018 in.
(0.457 mm) between the drive and setscrew B.
(b) Apply a 1.5 lbf (6.7 N) load to setscrew D.
(c) Put a 0-0.150 Inch (0-3.81 mm) feeler gauge set, STD-1337, adjusted to 0.010 in.
(0.254 mm) - 0.011 in. (0.279 mm) between setscrew C and the adjacent shoe face.
(d) Adjust setscrew C until it is tight against the 0-0.150 Inch (0-3.81 mm) feeler gauge set,
STD-1337.
(e) With the 0-0.150 Inch (0-3.81 mm) feeler gauge set, STD-1337, in position, tighten the
locknut of setscrew C.
(f) Remove the 0-0.150 Inch (0-3.81 mm) feeler gauge sets, STD-1337, between the drive
and setscrew B, and between setscrew C and the adjacent shoe face.
SUBTASK 27-62-00-200-002
(4) Do a check of the total primary backlash of the speed brake lever brake.
(a) Apply a 1.5 lbf (6.7 N) load to setscrew D.
(b) Make sure that the total primary backlash at setscrew C is 0.020 in. (0.508 mm) -
0.023 in. (0.584 mm).
(c) Apply a 1.5 lbf (6.7 N) load to setscrew C.
(d) Make sure that the total primary backlash at setscrew D is 0.020 in. (0.508 mm) -
0.023 in. (0.584 mm).
(e) If the total primary backlash at setscrew C or setscrew D is not 0.020 in. (0.508 mm) -
0.023 in. (0.584 mm), do the secondary backlash adjustment procedure again until the
total primary backlash is in the limits.
SUBTASK 27-62-00-860-222
(5) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker:

SUBTASK 27-62-00-010-007
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF ALL
CONTROL SURFACES BEFORE YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER.
AILERONS, RUDDERS, ELEVATORS, FLAPS, SLATS, SPOILERS, LANDING
GEAR, AND THRUST REVERSERS CAN MOVE QUICKLY WHEN YOU
SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(1) Do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
SUBTASK 27-62-00-860-258
(2) Move the flap control lever to the 30-unit position to extend the flaps.
SUBTASK 27-62-00-860-187
(3) Move the speed brake lever from the DOWN position to the UP position.
SUBTASK 27-62-00-860-253
(4) Attach a DO NOT OPERATE tag, STD-858 on the flap control lever and speed brake lever.
SUBTASK 27-62-00-860-254
(5) Do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-62-00-210-005

SUBTASK 27-62-00-860-255
(7) Do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801
SUBTASK 27-62-00-860-256
(8) Remove the DO NOT OPERATE tag, STD-858 from the flap control lever and speed brake
lever.
SUBTASK 27-62-00-860-257
(9) Move the flap control lever to the UP position to retract the flaps.
SUBTASK 27-62-00-860-188
(10) Move the speed brake lever from the UP position to the DOWN position.
SUBTASK 27-62-00-860-189
(11) If the hydraulic power is not needed, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal,
TASK 29-11-00-860-805.

F. Speed Brake Forward Drum and Lever Brake Installation.
SUBTASK 27-62-21-420-001
(1) Install the lever brake assembly [11]:
(a) Install the lever brake assembly [11] into position.
(b) Apply a layer of grease, D00633, to the inner diameter of bearing [19] and bearing [20].
(c) Install the bearing [19], bearing [20], and nut [21] at the end of the lever brake shaft.
(d) Install the bolt [7], washer [8], nut [9], and cotter pin [10] to connect the actuator [6] to the
lever brake assembly [11].
(e) Install the bolt [12], washer [13], and nut [14] to connect the input rod [15] to the lever
brake assembly [11].
(f) Hand tighten the nut [21] to 60 in-lb (6.8 N·m) - 100 in-lb (11.3 N·m).
SUBTASK 27-62-21-420-002
(2) Install the speed brake forward drum [1]:
(a) Install the speed brake forward drum [1] on the lever brake shaft.
1) Hold the cam roller lever arm assembly [16] away from the speed brake forward
drum [1].
(b) Install the quadrant bolt [18] and washer [17].
1) Hand tighten the quadrant bolt [18] to 40 in-lb (4.5 N·m) - 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m).
(c) Install MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, between the quadrant bolt [18] and speed brake
forward drum [1].
SUBTASK 27-62-21-420-003
(3) Connect the speed brake control cables SBA and SBB:
(a) Install the cable retainers and the cables on the speed brake forward drum [1]
(TASK 20-10-96-400-801).
(b) Connect the turnbuckles installed in the aft part of the lower nose compartment.
(c) Remove the clamps on the cables.
(d) Remove the tags on the cables.
SUBTASK 27-62-21-420-004
(4) Install the bushing [5], bolt [3], and washer [4] to connect the lever arm assembly [2] to the
speed brake forward drum [1].
SUBTASK 27-62-21-860-004
(5) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker:

(13) Do these tasks to get access to the speed brake lever in the control stand (Figure 401):

1) Remove four screws [9].
2) Apply masking tape to prevent damage to the surface of the stabilizer trim switch
panel [10].
3) Move the stabilizer trim switch panel [10] on to the mat.
E. Disconnect the Control Stand Components
SUBTASK 27-62-22-020-002
(1) Disconnect the flap indicator assembly:
(a) Go to the right side of the control stand.
(b) Remove the nut [16], the washer [14], the washer [15], and the bolt [17] from the lower
end of the link assembly [13].
(c) Safety the link assembly to the control stand.
SUBTASK 27-62-22-020-003
(2) Disconnect the flap lever position synchro assembly:
(a) Remove the nut [18] and the bolt [19] from the link assembly [20].
(b) Safety link assembly to the control stand.
SUBTASK 27-62-22-020-004
(3) Disconnect the stabilizer trim controls:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Turn the left trim wheel until you find the link in the trim chain (Figure 402).
NOTE: This will help if it becomes necessary to disconnect the chain during installation.
(b) Safety the chain [31] to the stabilizer trim sprocket [32].
NOTE: Do not remove the chain from the sprocket.
(c) Move to the forward bay below the flight compartment to do this step:
1) To release the tension from the stabilizer control chain, do this task: Stabilizer
Control Cable and Chain - Adjustment, TASK 27-41-00-820-801.
SUBTASK 27-62-22-020-005
(4) Do these steps to remove the control shaft components (Figure 401):
(a) Remove the bolt [8]and left stabilizer trim wheel [11].
(b) Remove the three screws [50] and the upper left cover [12].
(c) Carefully move the stabilizer trim shaft [27] to the left side of the control stand and do
these steps at the same time (Figure 402):
1) Remove the bearing [35].
2) Remove the clamp-up bushing [36].
3) Be prepared to catch and remove the bushing [33] as the shaft is moved to the left.
NOTE: The bushing [33] is between the bearing [34] and the sprocket [32].
4) Be prepared to catch and move the sprocket and chain.
5) Move the shaft [27] to the left side until the sprocket [32] is clear of the shaft.
6) Move the sprocket and chain to the bottom of the control stand.
(d) Reach inside the short shaft [37] from the left side and remove the inside bearing [34].
(e) Remove the stabilizer trim shaft [27] from the control stand.
1) Remove the bearing [28].
2) Remove the long bushing [29].
3) Remove the clamp-up bushing [30].
SUBTASK 27-62-22-020-006
(5) Do these steps to remove the chain guard (Figure 403):
(a) Go to the opening where the switch panel [10] for the stabilizer trim cutout is found.
(b) Use the 90 degree screwdriver from the tool set, SPL-2411 to hold the screw [44].
(c) Remove the nut [42], the washer [43], and the screw [44].
(d) Remove the upper center screw [39] and the washer [38].
(e) Remove the forward screw [41] and the washer [40].
(f) Remove the chain guard [45].
F. Remove the speed brake lever
SUBTASK 27-62-22-030-001
(1) Do these steps to disconnect the speed brake lever [22] from the link assembly [23]
(Figure 401).
(a) Remove the bolt [24], the washer [25], and the nut [26] from the speed brake lever [22].
SUBTASK 27-62-22-020-007
(2) Do these steps to disconnect the lockwasher and nut from the control shaft (Figure 404):
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Find the bent tab on the lockwasher [47].
(b) Use the lockwasher removal tool from the tool set, SPL-2411 to bend the tab.
(c) Bend the tab out of the notch in the nut [48].
(d) Put one control shaft wrench from the tool set, SPL-2411 on the left side of the long
shaft [46] to hold it in position.
(e) Put one control shaft nut wrench from the tool set, SPL-2411 in position and remove the
nut [48] from the long shaft [46].
(f) Remove and discard the lockwasher [47].
SUBTASK 27-62-22-020-008
(3) Do the steps to remove the speed brake lever [22] (Figure 404):
(a) Put the dowel set, SPL-2409 against the right side end of the long shaft [46].
(b) Hit lightly (carefully tap) on the dowel.
NOTE: This will move the long control shaft off the control levers.
1) Move the dowel until the speed brake lever [22] is on the dowel.
(c) Do not move the long shaft [46] from this position.
NOTE: More movement will let the speed brake lever fall.
(d) Hold the speed brake lever [22] and move the dowel from the lever.
1) Stop the dowel movement when you can lift up the lever.
2) Make sure the washers [49] are still held by the dowel and control shaft.
(e) Remove the speed brake lever [22] through the top of the control stand.
(f) Make sure the that the washers [49] do not fall in to the control stand.
(g) Do not move the dowel from this position.
