F. Install the Speed Brake Lever
SUBTASK 27-62-22-420-002
(1) Do these steps to install the speed brake lever [22] in the control stand (Figure 404):
(a) Apply grease, D00013 to the inside of the speed brake lever [22].
(b) Apply a thin layer of grease, D00013 to each side of the washers [49] you install.
NOTE: The application of grease, D00013 will help to hold the washers to the speed
brake lever.
(c) Hold the speed brake lever [22] and washers in the correct position.
(d) Move the long shaft [46] through the speed brake lever [22] and washers [49].
(e) Put the long shaft [46] against the right side end of the dowel set, SPL-2409.
(f) Move the speed brake lever [22] forward and aft.
NOTE: The lever and washers must move freely when you move them from the dowel to
the long control shaft.
(g) Move the long shaft [46] and the dowel to the right until all the lever assemblies and
washers are on the long shaft [46].
(h) Remove the dowel.
SUBTASK 27-62-22-420-003
(2) Do these steps to lock the speed brake lever:
(a) Set the keyway on the long shaft [46] at the top.
(b) Install a new lockwasher [47], but do not bend the tab at this time.
NOTE: Align the key tab on the lockwasher with the keyway on the long shaft.
(c) Put one control shaft wrench from the tool set, SPL-2411 on the left side of the long
shaft [46] to hold it in position.
(d) Install the nut [48].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Use one control shaft nut wrench from the tool set, SPL-2411 to tighten the nut [48].
2) Tighten the nut [48] to 100 in-lb (11.3 N·m) - 150 in-lb (16.9 N·m).
SUBTASK 27-62-22-020-010
(3) Measure the gap after the lever is installed (Figure 405):
(a) If the gap is not in the limits, follow the instructions in Table A to get the correct limits:
1) Use the applicable steps in the removal and installation task to adjust the
washer [49] on the long shaft [46].
SUBTASK 27-62-22-420-004
(4) After the speed brake lever [22] is set correctly, lock the assembly in its position (Figure 404):
(a) Make sure that the nut is tightened to 100 in-lb (11.3 N·m) - 150 in-lb (16.9 N·m).
(b) Bend the rim of the lockwasher [47] into one of the notches on the nut [48].
1) Use a chisel or the lockwasher break tool from the tool set, SPL-2411 to bend the
rim of the lockwasher [47].
2) Make sure that the bend in the lockwasher is not more than 0.15 in. (3.8 mm) into
the notch on the nut.
SUBTASK 27-62-22-420-008
(5) Connect the speed brake lever to the link assembly.
(a) Install the bolt [24], washer [25], and nut [26] in the speed brake lever [22] and link
assembly [23] (Figure 401).
G. Install the control stand components
SUBTASK 27-62-22-020-011
(1) Do these steps to install the chain guard (Figure 403):
(a) Put the chain guard [45] in its position.
(b) Install the upper screw [39] and the washer [38].
(c) Install the forward screw [41] and washer [40].
(d) Install the screw [44] through the thrust lever opening.
(e) Use the 90 degree screwdriver from the tool set, SPL-2411 to hold the screw [44].
(f) Install the nut [42] and the washer [43].
SUBTASK 27-62-22-020-012
(2) Do these steps to install the control shaft components (Figure 402):
(a) Install the clamp-up bushing [30] and the long bushing [29] on the stabilizer trim
shaft [27].
NOTE: Put the clamp-up bushing on the end with the longest splines.
(b) Put the bearing [34] into the inside end of the short shaft [37].
(c) Move the stabilizer trim shaft [27] into the control stand from the left side.
NOTE: Put the end of the shaft with the longest splines in first.
(d) Move the sprocket [32] and chain [31] up from the bottom of the control stand.
1) Put the sprocket [32] on the splined end of the shaft [27].
2) Move the shaft through the sprocket.
(e) Put the bushing [33] on the splined end of the shaft [27].
1) Move the shaft through the bushing.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(f) Move the shaft [27] through the bearing [34] until the end is moved out through the short
shaft [37].
(g) Install the bearing [28] on the left side of the shaft.
(h) Install the clamp-up bushing [36] on the right side of the stabilizer trim shaft [27].
(i) Install the bearing [35] on the right side of the shaft [27].
(j) Lightly tap the shaft [27] from the left side.
NOTE: Do this step to make sure that the assembled parts are tight and in the correct
position.
SUBTASK 27-62-22-420-005
(3) Do these steps to activate and adjust the stabilizer trim assembly:
(a) Remove the temporary wire tie from the chain [31] and sprocket [32].
(b) To adjust the stabilizer control chain, do this task: Stabilizer Control Cable and Chain -
Adjustment, TASK 27-41-00-820-801.
SUBTASK 27-62-22-410-001
(4) Do these steps to connect the flap lever synchro assembly (Figure 401):
(a) Put the link assembly [20] in the clevis for the flap lever position synchro assembly.
(b) Install the nut [18] and the bolt [19].
SUBTASK 27-62-22-410-007
(5) Do this step to connect the flap indicator assembly:
(a) Install the bolt [17], washer [15], washer [14], and nut [16] in the link assembly [13] and
indicator assembly arm.
SUBTASK 27-62-22-040-006
(6) Do these steps to activate the speed brake lever:
(a) Go into the access area under the forward flight compartment floor.
1) Remove the rig pin from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585 from the forward drum of the
speed brake assembly.
2) Do this task: Speed Brake Control Lever Adjustment, TASK 27-62-00-820-801.
SUBTASK 27-62-22-420-006
(7) Install these covers on the control stand.
(a) Install the upper left cover [12].
1) Install the three screws [50].
(b) Install the upper right cover [21].
1) Install the three screws [51].
SUBTASK 27-62-22-010-007
(8) Install the control stand access covers:
(a) The left upper side panel [1].
1) Attach with four screws [2].
(b) The left lower side panel [5]:
1) Attach with five screws [2]
(c) The right upper side panel [3]:
1) Attach with four screws [2].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(d) The right lower side panel [4]:
1) Attach with four screws [2].
SUBTASK 27-62-22-420-007
(9) Install the stabilizer trim wheel assemblies:
(a) Install the right stabilizer trim wheel [7].
1) Install the right bolt [8].
2) Tighten the bolt [8] to 150 in-lb (16.9 N·m) - 170 in-lb (19.2 N·m)
(b) Install the left stabilizer trim wheel [11]:
1) Set the crank of the left stabilizer trim wheel [11] 75 to 105 degrees away from the
setting of the crank on the right wheel.
NOTE: This can be set in either direction.
2) Install the left bolt [8].

(VDC) to the auto speedbrake actuator [16].
1) Apply 28 VDC to pins 1 and 7 on the auto speedbrake actuator [16].

a) Use pin 1 as the ground (SSM 27-62-11).

 ALL

1) Extend the actuator (TASK 27-62-00-820-806 or TASK 27-62-00-820-812).
SUBTASK 27-62-31-420-001
(3) Install the auto speedbrake actuator [16], do these steps:
(a) Put the auto speedbrake actuator [16] in its position on the airplane.
(b) Install the bolt [1], washer [2], and lockwire or safety cable [3] that attaches the auto
speedbrake actuator [16] to the structure.
(c) Manually turn the brake lever [15] forward until the internal stop touches.
(d) Adjust the rod end fitting on the auto speedbrake actuator [16], do these steps:
1) Remove the lockwire or safety cable [3] from the checknut [9].
2) Loosen the checknut [9] on the auto speedbrake actuator [16] rod end.
3) Adjust the auto speedbrake actuator [16] rod end until you can install the bolt [10]
through the brake lever [15] and auto speedbrake actuator [16].
NOTE: To make the alignment easier, you can loosen the brake lever a distance
equal to one-half turn of the auto speed brake actuator rod end.
4) Install the bolt [10] to attach the auto speedbrake actuator [16] to the brake
lever [15].
5) Hand tighten the checknut [9] on the auto speedbrake actuator [16] rod end.
6) Remove the bolt [10] from the auto speedbrake actuator [16] rod end and brake
lever [15].
7) Loosen the checknut [9].
a) Make sure that the rod end doesn't turn while loosening the checknut [9].
8) Turn the auto speedbrake actuator [16] rod end in one full turn.
NOTE: The function of the full turn clockwise is to decrease the length of the
actuator rod. This retracts the speedbrake lever no-back clutch to the stops
and moves the lever to the down detent position.
9) Tighten the checknut [9].
10) Install the lockwire or safety cable [3] in the checknut [9].
(e) Manually turn the brake lever [15] until it aligns with the auto speedbrake actuator [16]
rod end.

B. RTO Switch Adjustment
SUBTASK 27-62-32-820-003
(1) Adjust the RTO switch [13]:
(a) Make sure that the thrust levers are at idle and the reverse thrust levers are down and
stowed.
(b) Make sure that the speed brake lever is in the DOWN position.
(c) Disconnect the D5148P connector from the D5148J connector.
(d) Loosen screw [9] and screw [10].
(e) Turn the RTO switch [13] as far aft as possible.
(f) Make sure that there is no continuity between pin 8 and 9 of the D5148J connector.
(g) Move the left reverse thrust lever aft until there is a 0.0200 in. (0.5080 mm) to 0.0400 in.
(1.0160 mm) clearance between the speed brake lever dog [4] and the detent plate
assembly lip [5].
(h) Turn the RTO switch [13] until the roller [11] touches the actuator arm [12] and there is
continuity between pins 8 and 9 of the D5148J connector.
(i) Tighten the screw [9] and screw [10].
(j) Slowly move the left reverse thrust lever back to the down and stowed position.
1) Make sure that there is no continuity between pins 8 and 9.
(k) Slowly move the left reverse thrust lever aft until there is continuity between pins 8 and 9.
1) Make sure that the clearance between the speed brake lever dog [4] and the detent
plate assembly lip [5] is 0.0200 in. (0.5080 mm) to 0.0400 in. (1.0160 mm).
(l) Slowly move the left reverse thrust lever forward until there is no continuity between pins
8 and 9.
1) Make sure that the speed brake lever dog [4] is not less than 0.0100 in.
(0.2540 mm) above the detent plate assembly lip [5].
(m) Move the left reverse thrust lever to the down and stowed position.
1) Make sure that there is no continuity between pins 8 and 9.
(n) Slowly move the right reverse thrust lever aft until there is continuity between pins 8 and
9.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Make sure that the speed brake lever dog [4] is 0.0200 in. (0.5080 mm) to
0.0400 in. (1.0160 mm) above the detent plate assembly lip [5].
(o) Slowly move the right reverse thrust lever forward until there is no continuity between
pins 8 and 9.
1) Make sure that the speed brake lever dog [4] is not less than 0.0100 in.
(0.2540 mm) above the detent plate assembly lip [5].
(p) Move the right reverse thrust lever to the down and stowed position.
1) Make sure that there is no continuity between pins 8 and 9.
SUBTASK 27-62-32-420-002
(2) Connect the D5148P connector to the D5148J connector.
SUBTASK 27-62-32-410-002
(3) Install screws [1] and washers [2] to attach the cover plate [3] on the control stand.

F. Speedbrake Autostow Actuator Functional Test
SUBTASK 27-62-33-860-012
(1) Do the Stall Management Yaw Damper (SMYD) BITE test, do this task: FIM 27-32 TASK 801.
(a) Check the SMYD #2 for autostow faults.
NOTE: You can ignore any other faults.
SUBTASK 27-62-33-760-001
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT YOU OPEN THE CIRCUIT BREAKER FOR THE WEATHER
RADAR SYSTEM. THE FORWARD MOVEMENT OF A THRUST LEVER CAN
CAUSE THE AUTOMATIC OPERATION OF THE SYSTEM. THE OPERATION
OF THIS SYSTEM CAN CAUSE SERIOUS INJURY TO PERSONS AND
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT IN THE AREA OF THE NOSE RADOME.
(2) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1
Row Col Number Name
D 13 C00120 WEATHER RADAR RT
SUBTASK 27-62-33-860-014
(3) Move either thrust lever full forward to retract the speed brake actuator, if it has been
extended.
(a) After the speed brake actuator retracts, move the thrust lever back to idle.
EFFECTIVITY
 006, 007, 013, 014
SUBTASK 27-62-33-480-003
CAUTION
INSTALL THE PROTRACTOR ON THE SPOILER TOP SURFACE. IF THE
PROTRACTOR INSTALLED ON THE BOTTOM OF THE SPOILER, DAMAGE
TO AIRCRAFT CAN OCCUR.
(4) Install protractors, COM-1691, on the upper surface of spoilers 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 10, and 11.
(a) If all eight protractors are not available, install as many as you have on the spoilers.
NOTE: The task can be repeated as many times as is necessary to measure the
positions of each of the eight spoiler panels.
(b) Make sure that you measure each of the eight spoilers before you record the average
spoiler panel position.
(c) Zero the protractors.
SUBTASK 27-62-33-860-015
(5) Measure the speed brake lever handle forces using a spring scale, STD-758.
(a) Measure the force required to slowly move the speed brake lever to the FLIGHT DETENT
position.
NOTE: The force required to move the speedbrake lever to this position should not
exceed 20 lbf (89 N).
1) Make sure that you record this force.
(b) Measure the force required to slowly move the speed brake lever to the full UP position.
NOTE: The force required to move the speedbrake lever to this position should not
exceed 28 lbf (125 N).
1) Make sure that you record this force.
(c) Measure the force required to slowly move the speed brake lever to the DOWN position.
NOTE: The force required to move the speedbrake lever to this position should not
exceed 15 lbf (67 N).
1) Make sure that you record this force.
SUBTASK 27-62-33-860-016
(6) Move the speedbrake handle to the FLIGHT DETENT position.
(a) Make sure that the SPEED BRAKE ARMED light illuminates.
1) If the SPEED BRAKE ARMED light does not illuminate, do this task: SPEED
BRAKE ARMED Light Does Not Operate - Fault Isolation, FIM 27-62 TASK 803.
SUBTASK 27-62-33-860-017
(7) Do the autostow actuator test on the SMYD #2.
(a) Press and then release the ON/OFF button.
1) The display reads "EXISTING FAULTS?".
(b) Press and then release the up or down arrow until "GROUND TEST?" appears on the
display.
1) Press and release the YES button to access ground test options.
(c) Press and then release the up or down arrow until "AUTOSTOW?" appears on the
display.
EFFECTIVITY
 006, 007, 013, 014
1) Press and then release the YES button to start the autostow test.
NOTE: The SPEEDBRAKE DO NOT ARM light will illuminate.
NOTE: The SPEEDBRAKE ARMED light will remain illuminated.
(d) When "RUN AUTO TEST" appears on the display, press and then release the NO button.
(e) ”STARTING RIG TEST” and “TEST IN PROGRESS” will appear on the display.
(f) When "RETRACT ACTR" appears on the display, press and then release the YES button.
1) The autostow actuator will be commanded to retract.
NOTE: The actuator will be held in the retracted position until it is commanded to
extend by the test operator.
SUBTASK 27-62-33-860-018
(8) Measure the average spoiler panel position, do these steps:
(a) Do a shakeout of the lateral control system as follows:
1) Rotate the control wheel slowly clockwise to 1.5 units of trim.
2) Rotate the control wheel slowly counterclockwise to 1.5 units of trim.
3) Rotate the control wheel slowly clockwise to zero units of trim.
(b) Use the protractors, COM-1691, to measure and record the spoiler panel positions for
spoilers 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 10 and 11.
1) Make sure that the protractors, COM-1691, are put perpendicular to the spoiler
panel hinge line.
(c) Add the eight spoiler panel positions together from the previous step.
1) Divide the total of the panel positions by eight (8) to get the average spoiler panel
position.
a) The average spoiler panel position should be between 9.3 and 11.8 degrees.
(d) If the average spoiler position is more than 11.8 degrees or less than 9.3 degrees, do this
task: Speedbrake Autostow Actuator Rod End Adjustment, TASK 27-62-33-820-802.
SUBTASK 27-62-33-730-001
(9) Test the speedbrake handle forces, do these steps:
(a) Slowly move the speedbrake handle to the FLIGHT DETENT position while measuring
the handle force with a spring scale, STD-758.
NOTE: The handle force should not exceed 40 lbf (178 N).
1) Release the speedbrake handle.
NOTE: The speedbrake handle should move forward to the 50% position.
(b) Slowly move the speedbrake handle to the full UP position while measuring the handle
force with a spring scale, STD-758.
NOTE: The handle force should not exceed 55 lbf (245 N).
1) Release the speedbrake handle.
NOTE: The speedbrake handle should remain in the full UP position.
(c) Move the speedbrake handle to the DOWN position.
NOTE: The SPEEDBRAKE ARMED light should go out.
SUBTASK 27-62-33-010-001
(10) Go to the SMYD #2 and continue with the SMYD test.
EFFECTIVITY
 006, 007, 013, 014
(a) When "EXTEND ACTR?" is displayed, press and then release the YES button once the
actuator rigging is finished.
NOTE: If the SMYD detects a failure during the retract command, the SMYD will remove
the retract command and display "TEST FAILED" followed by a list of the

button to initiate the autostow test.

TEST" will be displayed for 4 seconds.

the shutdown of the display.

(4) Do the following to access the autostow actuator rod end:
(a) Remove the screws [1] and washers [2] from the lower cover plate [3] (Figure 502)

D. Autostow Actuator Rod End Adjustment
SUBTASK 27-62-33-020-028
(1) Remove the nut, washer, and bolt from the autostow actuator upper attach point.
SUBTASK 27-62-33-480-002
(2) Install the rig pin in the autostow actuator cam housing and cam (Figure 502).
SUBTASK 27-62-33-820-004
(3) Make sure the autostow actuator is fully retracted.
(a) Apply 28V to pin 3 and ground pin 1.
SUBTASK 27-62-33-820-005
(4) Adjust the autostow actuator rod end.
(a) Loosen the locknut on the actuator rod end.
(b) Adjust the rod end as needed to align with the autostow actuator upper attach point.
(c) Install the bolt, washer, and nut in the autostow actuator upper attach point.
(d) Tighten the locknut finger tight.
SUBTASK 27-62-33-080-001
(5) Remove the rig pins from the autostow actuator cam and the lower speedbrake quadrant.
SUBTASK 27-62-33-720-001
(6) Do this task: Speedbrake Autostow Actuator - Functional Test, TASK 27-62-33-010-801.
NOTE: You do not need to measure the speedbrake handle forces.
(a) If the measured average spoiler panel position is between 9.3 and 11.8 degrees, you
have correctly adjusted the autostow actuator rod end. Do the steps to Put the Airplane
Back to Its Usual Condition.
(b) If the measured average spoiler panel position is not between 9.3 and 11.8 degrees, the
autostow actuator rod end needs further adjustment. Do these steps to adjust the
autostow actuator rod end.
NOTE: The rod end may be adjusted up to two full turns (720 degrees) (from its initial
rigged position) in the clockwise or counterclockwise directions.
1) To adjust the spoiler panels in the down direction, loosen the locknut and rotate the
rod end clockwise.
NOTE: One full rotation of the rod end (360 degrees) is equal to approximately 1.0
degree of spoiler panel travel.
2) To adjust the spoiler panels in the up direction, loosen the locknut and rotate the rod
end counterclockwise.
NOTE: One full rotation of the rod end (360 degrees) is equal to approximately 1.0
degree of spoiler panel travel.
3) Tighten the locknut finger tight.
4) Repeat the Speedbrake Autostow Actuator - Functional Test,
TASK 27-62-33-010-801.
NOTE: You do not need to measure the speedbrake handle forces.
a) If the measured average spoiler panel position is still not between 9.3 and 11.8
degrees, do the Speed Brake Control Lever Adjustment,
TASK 27-62-00-820-801.
EFFECTIVITY
 006, 007, 013, 014

5. Speedbrake Autostow Actuator Tension Spring Adjustment
(Figure 502)
A. References
Reference Title
27-62-33-000-802 Speedbrake Autostow Actuator Cam Assembly Removal
(P/B 401)
27-62-33-400-802 Speed Brake Autostow Actuator Cam Assembly Installation
(P/B 401)

Zone Area
117 Electrical and Electronics Compartment - Left
118 Electrical and Electronics Compartment - Right
210 Subzone - Control Compartment - Body Station 178.00 to Body Station 259.50
C. Prepare for the Test
SUBTASK 27-62-33-860-031
(1) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2
Row Col Number Name
A 10 C01611 SPDBRK AUTOSTOW
SUBTASK 27-62-33-860-032
(2) Do this task: Speedbrake Autostow Actuator Cam Assembly Removal,
TASK 27-62-33-000-802.
SUBTASK 27-62-33-860-033
(3) Do the following to adjust the tension of the tension spring (Figure 502):
(a) With the cam housing assembly restrained, move the idler arm up until the cam assembly
contacts the cam roller bearing.
NOTE: All of the breakout force measurements must be reached within 5 degrees of
cam travel, after the cam roller bearing has made contact with the cam assembly.
(b) Attach a spring scale to the upper speedbrake control rod attach point of the idler arm.
(c) Use the spring scale to apply a tangential force to the idler arm until you move the idler
arm 5 degrees from the initial roller to cam contact point.
NOTE: This is the breakout force of the mechanism.
(d) Do the following to verify proper breakout force:
1) If the breakout force is between 60.2 pounds and 70.2 pounds (268 newtons and
312 newtons), it is within the tolerance and does not need to be adjusted.
2) If the breakout force is less than 60.2 pounds (268 newtons), then you need to add
washers to increase the breakout force of the cam assembly.
a) Remove the nut that attaches the upper force feel spring lug to the cam
housing and add washers, as necessary.
b) Install the nut.
c) Repeat the breakout force test until the breakout force is in the limits of 60.2
pounds and 70.2 pounds (268 newtons and 312 newtons).
EFFECTIVITY
 006, 007, 013, 014
3) If the breakout force is more than 70.2 pounds (312 newtons), then you need to
remove washers to decrease the breakout force of the cam assembly:
a) Remove the nut that attaches the upper force feel spring lug to the cam
housing and remove washers, as necessary.
b) Install the nut.
c) Repeat the breakout force test until the breakout force is in the limits of 60.2
pounds and 70.2 pounds (268 newtons and 312 newtons).
SUBTASK 27-62-33-860-034
(4) Do this task: Speed Brake Autostow Actuator Cam Assembly Installation,
TASK 27-62-33-400-802.

D. Speed Brake Armed Switch and Speed Brake Handle Position Switch Adjustment
SUBTASK 27-62-34-820-002
(1) Adjust the speed handle armed switch [6]:
(a) Move the speed brake lever to the DOWN detent position.
(b) Move the speed brake lever to the FLIGHT DETENT position.
(c) Loosen the nuts [5].
(d) Move the speed brake lever forward until the aft surface of the detent pin is 0.18 in.
(4.57 mm) - 0.22 in. (5.59 mm) from the aft edge of the DOWN detent.
CAUTION
DO NOT BEND THE SWITCH LEVER. TO ADJUST THE SWITCH, YOU
LOOSEN THE ATTACHMENT BOLTS UNTIL THE SWITCH TURNS
FREELY. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN
OCCUR.
(e) Adjust the speed handle armed switch [6] until there is continuity between the common
and normally open terminals.
NOTE: Always adjust the switch from the no continuity position to the continuity position.
SUBTASK 27-62-34-820-003
(2) Adjust the speed brake handle position switch [1]:
(a) Move the speed brake lever to the ARMED detent position.
(b) Slowly move the speed brake lever aft 0.25 in. (6.35 mm) - 0.3 in. (7.6 mm).
CAUTION
DO NOT BEND THE SWITCH LEVER. TO ADJUST THE SWITCH, YOU
LOOSEN THE ATTACHMENT BOLTS UNTIL THE SWITCH TURNS
FREELY. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN
OCCUR.
(c) Adjust the speed brake handle position switch [1] until the switch actuates and there is
continuity between the common and normally open terminals.
NOTE: Always adjust the switch from the no continuity position to the continuity position.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
CAUTION
DO NOT TIGHTEN THE SELF-LOCKING NUT TOO MUCH. IF YOU
TIGHTEN THE NUT MORE THAN 15 POUND-INCHES, DAMAGE TO THE
EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(d) Tighten the nuts [5].
SUBTASK 27-62-34-010-002
(3) Close this access panel:
Number Name/Location
112A Forward Access Door

E. Valve Installation
SUBTASK 27-62-41-800-001
(1) Make sure that the valve lever [19] moves smoothly through the full range of travel.
SUBTASK 27-62-41-420-001
(2) Install the valve assembly [10].
(a) Install the packing [4], packings [11], reducer [3], and reducers [12] in the hydraulic ports
on the valve assembly [10]:
1) Remove the caps from the ports in the valve assembly [10].
2) Apply a thin layer of hydraulic fluid, D00153, on the packing [4] and packings [11].
3) Install the packing [4], packings [11], reducer [3], and reducers [12] in the hydraulic
ports.
a) Tighten the reducer [3] and reducers [12] to 280 ±14 in-lb (31.6 ±1.6 N·m).
(b) Remove the plugs from the hydraulic line [2], hydraulic line [5], hydraulic line [6],
hydraulic line [13], and hydraulic line [14].
(c) Put the valve assembly [10] in its position on the bracket [1].
(d) Loosely install the connections for the hydraulic lines on the valve assembly [10].
(e) Install the bolts [7], washers [8], and nuts [9] that attach the valve assembly [10] to the
bracket [1].
NOTE: Some bracket assemblies come with permanent nutplates as an alternative to
nuts.
(f) Install the bolt [15], washer [16], and nut [17] that attaches the control rod [18] to the
valve lever [19].
NOTE: Some assemblies use a nut and pin as an alternative to self-locking nut.
(g) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [13], hydraulic line [5], hydraulic line [6], and
hydraulic line [14] to 270 ±14 in-lb (30.5 ±1.6 N·m).
1) Make sure that the wire bundles have a minimum separation of 0.5 in. (12.7 mm)
from the hydraulic tubing.
NOTE: The 0.5 in. (12.7 mm) minimum separation will prevent wear and fraying
between the wire/bundle and hydraulic tubing.
(h) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [2] to 140 ±7 in-lb (15.8 ±0.8 N·m).
SUBTASK 27-62-41-860-002
(3) Do this task: Put the Speed Brake Systems A and B Back to the Condition Before the Pressure

 ALL

SUBTASK 27-62-41-860-003
(1) Do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811.
SUBTASK 27-62-41-860-004

(3) Examine the hydraulic connections on the valve assembly [10] for leakage.
SUBTASK 27-62-41-870-001
(4) Move the speed brake lever through more than one full cycle to bleed the hydraulic system.
SUBTASK 27-62-41-720-002
(5) Do the test for the valve assembly [10]:
(a) Make sure the speed brake lever is in the DOWN position.
(b) Move the speed brake lever aft until the ground spoilers begin to move to the extended
position.
(c) Make sure the speed brake lever is 29 +/-2 degrees (2.78 +/-0.20 inches) (70.6 +/-5.1
millimeters) aft of the DOWN position.
(d) Move the speed brake lever to the UP position.
(e) Move the speed brake lever forward until the ground spoilers move to the retracted
position.
(f) Make sure the speed brake lever is 21 +/-4 degrees (2.00 +/-0.40 inches) (50.8 +/-10.2
millimeters) aft of the DOWN position.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(g) Move the speed brake lever to the DOWN position.

F. Ground Spoiler Interlock Valve Installation
SUBTASK 27-62-61-800-001
(1) Make sure that the valve [1] moves smoothly through its full travel.
SUBTASK 27-62-61-420-001
(2) Install the valve [1].
(a) Install the bracket [23] on the valve [1].
1) Put the bracket [23] into its position.
2) Install the screws [24] and washers [32].
3) Tighten the screws [24] to 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m) - 35 in-lb (4.0 N·m).
4) Install MS20995C20 lockwire, G50225 (or equivalent), between the screws [24].
(b) Install the reducers [13], reducer [38], new packings [14], and new packing [39] in the
ports of the valve [1]:
1) Remove the caps from the valve [1] ports.
2) Apply a thin layer of hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the packings [14] and packing [39].
3) Install the packings [14], reducers [13], packing [39], and reducer [38] in the ports.
a) Tighten the reducers [13] to 155 in-lb (17.5 N·m) - 165 in-lb (18.6 N·m).
b) Tighten the reducer [38] to 95 in-lb (10.7 N·m) - 105 in-lb (11.9 N·m).
(c) Clean the aft fay surface of the valve [1] and the fay surface of the bracket [31] (SWPM
20-20-00, Category 6 Fillet Sealed Fay Surface Bond).
(d) Put the valve [1] into its position.
1) Install the bolts [3] and washers [4].
(e) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the valve [1] and bracket [31] (SWPM
20-20-00).
1) Use the intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550.
2) Make sure that the resistance is 0.0025 Ohm (2.50 milliohm) or less.
(f) Fillet seal bonding location (SWPM 20-20-00, Category 6 Fillet Sealed Fay Surface
Bond).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(g) Apply Bonderite M-CR 600 Aero coating, C00862, to bare metal surface of the
bracket [31] (TASK 51-21-41-370-802).
(h) Apply primer, C00259, to the bracket [31] (TASK 51-21-72-370-804).
(i) Remove the plugs from the hydraulic line [12] and hydraulic lines [28].
(j) Connect the hydraulic line [12] and hydraulic lines [28] to the valve [1].
(k) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [12] to 133 in-lb (15.0 N·m) - 147 in-lb (16.6 N·m).
(l) Tighten the B-nuts on the hydraulic lines [28] to 256 in-lb (28.9 N·m) - 284 in-lb
(32.1 N·m).
(m) If you did not examine the electrical connector(s) at the removal step, do these steps:

option.
1) Before you connect the electrical connector(s), examine the connector(s) for
corrosion.

SUBTASK 27-62-61-420-006
(1) Put the sensor [17] in place in the bracket.

SUBTASK 27-62-61-420-008

SUBTASK 27-62-61-220-001
(4) Measure the gap between the sensor [17] and target [25].
(a) If the gap is not 0.0600 in. (1.524 mm) - 0.0800 in. (2.032 mm), do these steps:
1) Remove the nut [20], washer [19], and sensor [17].
2) Remove or install shims [18] as necessary to adjust the gap.
NOTE: Laminated layers can be removed from the shims for adjustment.
NOTE: Each layer of lamination on the shims is 0.003 in. (0.08 mm).
3) Put the sensor [17] in place in the bracket.
4) Install the washer [19] with the tab in the index slot of the sensor [17] and bracket.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
 466-999 (Continued)
5) Install the nut [20] finger tight.
6) Measure the gap between the sensor [17] and target [25].
a) If the gap is not 0.0600 in. (1.524 mm) - 0.0800 in. (2.032 mm), repeat the
adjustment until the gap is correct.
SUBTASK 27-62-61-390-001
(5) Use a layer of sealant, A00767, to bond the shims [18] to the bracket.
SUBTASK 27-62-61-430-001

E. Ground Spoiler Interlock Valve Functional Test
 466-999
SUBTASK 27-62-61-860-019
(1) Move the flap lever to the 1-unit position.
(a) Make sure that the flap moves to the 1-unit position.
NOTE: Speed brake lever stop is now disengaged.
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-62-61-860-059
(2) Move the speed brake lever to the UP position.
(a) Make sure that the ground spoilers do not move.
SUBTASK 27-62-61-020-012
(3) Deflate the shock strut for the right main landing gear.
(a) Remove the cap for the gas valve.
(b) Loosen the swivel nut on the gas valve a maximum of two turns.
NOTE: Fluid in the chock strut will have bubbles when the pressure is released. Deflate
the shock strut slowly to prevent the leakage of the fluid through the gas valve.
(c) Loosen the swivel nut on the gas valve fully when all the pressure in the shock strut is
released.
SUBTASK 27-62-61-860-020
(4) Use an automotive type jack, STD-6620, to slowly lift the right main gear axle to compress the
right main gear shock strut until the ground spoiler interlock valve [1] opens.
(a) Make sure that the ground spoilers move to the fully extended position.
(b) Make sure that the inner cylinder of the right main gear shock strut moved
1.5 +1.5 / -0.0 in. (38.1 +38.1 / -0.0 mm) from the fully extended position.
SUBTASK 27-62-61-860-021
(5) Move the speed brake lever to the DOWN position.
(a) Make sure that the ground spoilers retract.
SUBTASK 27-62-61-080-002
(6) Slowly lower the right main gear axle to extend the right main gear shock strut.
SUBTASK 27-62-61-020-013
(7) Inflate the shock strut for the right main landing gear (TASK 12-15-31-610-805).

D. Procedure
SUBTASK 27-62-61-860-050
(1) Make sure the airplane is in the Ground Mode.
(a) If the airplane is not in the Ground Mode, do this task: Return the Airplane to the Ground
Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-802.
SUBTASK 27-62-61-860-051
(2) Make sure the speedbrake lever is in the DOWN position.
SUBTASK 27-62-61-210-002
(3) Make sure the spoilers are in the down position.
SUBTASK 27-62-61-865-002
(4) If the SPEEDBRAKE DO NOT ARM light is illuminated, do this step:
(a) Open and close this circuit breaker:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2
Row Col Number Name
A 5 C01663 SPOILER PCU SOV SYS B
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
 466-999 (Continued)
SUBTASK 27-62-61-480-003
(5) Attach a deactuator from the sensor proximity test kit, SPL-22766 to the face of the sensor,
S01131.
(6) If the sensor proximity test kit, SPL-22766 is not available, make the deactuator with sheet
copper.
NOTE: The dimensions for the deactuator should approximately be 1 in. (25 mm) X 1 in.
(25 mm) X 0.025 in. (0.635 mm).
SUBTASK 27-62-61-860-052
(7) Do this task: Put the Airplane in the Air Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-801.
SUBTASK 27-62-61-210-003
(8) After 5 seconds, make sure the SPEEDBRAKE DO NOT ARM light is off.
SUBTASK 27-62-61-080-003
(9) Remove the deactuator (from the sensor proximity test kit, SPL-22766) from the face of the
sensor, S01131.
SUBTASK 27-62-61-21-001
(10) Make sure the SPEEDBRAKE DO NOT ARM light comes on within 5 seconds of removing the
deactuator.

TASK 32-09-00-840-802.
SUBTASK 27-62-61-865-003
(2) Open and close this circuit breaker:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2

SUBTASK 27-62-71-860-002
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF ALL
CONTROL SURFACES BEFORE YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER.
AILERONS, RUDDERS, ELEVATORS, FLAPS, SLATS, SPOILERS, LANDING
GEAR, AND THRUST REVERSERS CAN MOVE QUICKLY WHEN YOU
SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(1) Do this task: Speed Brake Hydraulic Systems A and B Pressurization,
TASK 27-62-00-800-801.
SUBTASK 27-62-71-860-003
(2) Put the SPOILER A and B switches in the OFF position to remove the hydraulic power from the
flight spoilers.
NOTE: SPOILER A and B switches are on the P5-3 flight control panel.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-62-71-860-004
(3) Do this task: Extend the Trailing Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-803.
SUBTASK 27-62-71-860-005
(4) Do this task: Speed Brake Hydraulic Systems A and B - Pressure Removal,
TASK 27-62-00-800-802.
SUBTASK 27-62-71-860-015
(5) If it is necessary, do this task: Inboard Fixed Trailing Edge Lower Panel Removal,
TASK 57-50-02-000-801.
E. Actuator Removal
SUBTASK 27-62-71-020-001
(1) Disconnect the hydraulic line [10] and hydraulic line [20] from the actuator [17]:
(a) Put a 5 gallon (19 liter) hydraulic fluid resistant container, STD-1110, below the
actuator [17] to catch the hydraulic fluid.
(b) Disconnect the hydraulic line [10] and hydraulic line [20] from the unions [19].
(c) Remove the unions [19] and packings [18] from the actuator [17].
(d) Install the plugs in the hydraulic line [10] and hydraulic line [20].
SUBTASK 27-62-71-020-002
(2) Remove the pin [7], nut [6], washer [5], bushing [4], washer [3], and bolt [2] that attach the
actuator [17] to the inboard ground spoiler [1].
SUBTASK 27-62-71-020-003
(3) Remove the pin [16], nut [15], washer [14], bushing [13], washer [12], and bolt [11] that
attaches the actuator [17] to the structure.
SUBTASK 27-62-71-480-001
(4) Install caps in the hydraulic ports of the actuator [17].

E. Actuator Installation
SUBTASK 27-62-71-420-001
(1) Install the actuator [17]:
(a) Remove the caps from the hydraulic ports of the actuator [17].
(b) Put the actuator [17] in its position.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Make sure that the hydraulic line [10] and hydraulic line [20] align with the fittings.
(c) Connect the actuator [17] rod end to the inboard ground spoiler [1]:
1) Apply grease, D00633, to the bolt [2].
2) Install the bolt [2] with the head outboard, washer [3], bushing [4], washer [5],
nut [6], and pin [7].
3) Tighten the nut [6] to 450 in-lb (50.8 N·m) - 690 in-lb (78.0 N·m).
(d) Connect the actuator [17] to the structure:
1) Apply grease, D00633, to the bolt [11].
2) Install the bolt [11] with the head outboard, washer [12], bushing [13], washer [14],
nut [15], and pin [16].
3) Tighten the nut [15] to 450 in-lb (50.8 N·m) - 690 in-lb (78.0 N·m).
SUBTASK 27-62-71-420-002
(2) Connect the hydraulic line [10] and hydraulic line [20] to the actuator [17]:
(a) Remove the plugs from the hydraulic line [10] and hydraulic line [20].
(b) Connect the hydraulic line [10] and hydraulic line [20] to the actuator [17].
1) Install the packings [18] on the unions [19].
2) Install the unions [19] in the actuator [17].
3) Tighten the unions [19] to 154 ±21 in-lb (17.4 ±2.4 N·m).
4) Connect the hydraulic line [10] and hydraulic line [20] to the unions [19].
5) Tighten the B-Nuts [21] to 140 ±7 in-lb (15.8 ±0.8 N·m).
SUBTASK 27-62-71-860-006
(3) Do this task: Put the Speed Brake Systems A and B Back to the Condition Before the Pressure

SUBTASK 27-62-71-860-007

E. Actuator Removal
SUBTASK 27-62-94-020-001
(1) Disconnect the piston rod end of the outboard ground spoiler actuator [10] from the outboard
ground spoiler [1]:
(a) Remove the pin [8], nut [7], washer [6], bushings [4], washer [6], washer [3], and bolt [2]
from the piston rod end.
(b) Discard the pin [8].
SUBTASK 27-62-94-020-002
(2) Disconnect the hydraulic lines [9] from the outboard ground spoiler actuator [10].
(a) Put a 5 gallon (19 liter) hydraulic fluid resistant container, STD-1110, below the outboard
ground spoiler actuator [10] to catch the hydraulic fluid.
(b) Disconnect the hydraulic lines [9] from the outboard ground spoiler actuator [10].
(c) Turn the hydraulic lines [9] at the swivel joints to access the outboard ground spoiler
actuator [10].
(d) Install the plugs in the hydraulic lines [9].
SUBTASK 27-62-94-020-003
(3) Remove the bolts [13], washers [14], pillow blocks [11], and split ball bearings [12] from the
structure.
SUBTASK 27-62-94-020-004
(4) Remove the outboard ground spoiler actuator [10] from the airplane.
SUBTASK 27-62-94-480-001
(5) Install caps in the hydraulic ports of the outboard ground spoiler actuator [10].

SUBTASK 27-62-94-020-013

SUBTASK 27-62-94-610-001

SUBTASK 27-62-94-410-002

SUBTASK 27-62-94-420-002

hydraulic line [9] align with the fittings.
(b) Install the pillow blocks [11] on the outboard ground spoiler actuator [10]:
1) Apply grease, D00633, to the split ball bearings [12].
2) Assemble the split ball bearings [12].
3) Install the split ball bearings [12] in the pillow blocks [11].
4) Make sure that the split ball bearings [12] move freely.
WARNING
DO NOT GET THIS MATERIAL IN YOUR MOUTH, EYES, OR ON
YOUR SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM THIS
MATERIAL. PUT ON A RESPIRATOR, EYE PROTECTION
(GOGGLES, OR OTHER APPROVED PROTECTION), AND GLOVES
BEFORE YOU USE THIS MATERIAL. MAKE SURE THAT THERE IS
SUFFICIENT AIRFLOW. KEEP THIS MATERIAL AWAY FROM
SPARKS, FLAME, AND HEAT. THIS MATERIAL CAN CAUSE
INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
WARNING
USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE
COR-BAN 27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE
IT WITH WATER. IF THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES,
IMMEDIATELY FLUSH YOUR EYES WITH WATER. GET MEDICAL
AID. THIS MATERIAL CONTAINS FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN
CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL.

2. Leading Edge Flaps and Slats Deactivation
(Figure 201, Figure 202, Figure 203)
A. General
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT FOR AIRPLANES WITH THE -1001 CRUISE
DEPRESSURIZATION VALVE, YOU REVIEW THIS WARNING. MAKE SURE
THAT YOU CLOSE THE FAN COWLS AND THRUST REVERSERS IF YOU
MOVE THE TRAILING EDGE FLAPS WHILE THE LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND
SLATS ARE DISCONNECTED. THE -1001 CRUISE DEPRESSURIZATION
CREEP CAN CAUSE MOVEMENT OF THE LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND
SLATS WHEN YOU MOVE THE FLAP CONTROL LEVER. IF YOU DO NOT
OBEY, INJURY TO PERSONNEL OR DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN
OCCUR.
WARNING
MAKE SURE ALL PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT
CONTROLS SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING
GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY
HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE INBOARD FAN COWL PANEL AND THE INBOARD
AND OUTBOARD THRUST REVERSERS ARE CLOSED AND IN THE
STOWED POSITION OR REMOVED BEFORE YOU EXTEND THE LEADING
EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS. THERE IS NOT SUFFICIENT CLEARANCE FOR
THE FLAPS AND SLATS TO EXTEND IF THE INBOARD FAN COWL PANEL
AND THE INBOARD AND OUTBOARD THRUST REVERSERS ARE IN THE
OPEN POSITION. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(1) Before you do maintenance on the Leading Edge (LE) flaps and slats, you must deactivate the
LE control surfaces. This is to prevent injury to persons and damage to equipment because of
accidental operation of the LE control surfaces.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(2) The -1001 cruise depressurization valve can cause a related creep condition of an LE device.
It can cause hydraulic pressure leakage through the valve when manually closed.
(a) This creep condition can let movement of the LE flaps and slats occur when you move
the Trailing Edge (TE) flaps.
(b) The -1003 cruise depressurization valve has changes that do not give this creep
condition.

 ALL

A. General
WARNING
MAKE SURE ALL PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT
CONTROLS SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING
GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY

DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
CAUTION

AND OUTBOARD THRUST REVERSERS ARE CLOSED AND IN THE
STOWED POSITION OR REMOVED BEFORE YOU EXTEND THE LEADING
EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS. THERE IS NOT SUFFICIENT CLEARANCE FOR

AND THE INBOARD AND OUTBOARD THRUST REVERSERS ARE IN THE

(1) If you do the deactivation procedure with the Leading Edge (LE) flaps and slats in the retract
position, then do the steps to reactivate the LE flaps and slats in the retract position.
(2) If you do the deactivation procedure with the LE flaps and slats in the extend (intermediate)
position, then do the steps to reactivate the LE flaps and slats in the extend (intermediate)
position.
(3) If you do the deactivation procedure with the LE flaps and slats in the full extend position, then
do the steps to reactivate the LE flaps and slats in the full extend position.

(9) Do this task: Leading Edge Standby Shutoff Valve Test, TASK 27-81-91-720-801.
H. Reactivate the Leading Edge Flaps and Slats in the Extend (intermediate) Position
SUBTASK 27-81-00-020-006
(1) Remove the DO-NOT-REMOVE tag from the lockout pin, SPL-1746, from the manual override
lever (handle) on the LE cruise depressurization valve.
SUBTASK 27-81-00-020-009
(2) Remove the lockout pin, SPL-1746, from the manual override lever on the LE cruise
depressurization valve (Figure 201).
NOTE: Do not force movement of the lever (handle) with tools. The lever should move with
very little force. If the lever is tight, you may need hydraulic pressure and the Flap/Slat
Electronics Unit (FSEU) to relieve the pressure on the LE CRUISE
DEPRESSURIZATION VALVE.
(a) If the lockout pin, SPL-1746, will not come out easily, then do the steps that follow:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) If necessary, supply system B hydraulic power and then use the FSEU to relieve the
pressure on the LE depressurization valve.
a) Use the FSEU procedure below but replace the selection of the LE UCM
SHUTOFF VALVE for the LE DEPR VALVE.
(b) Move the (LE cruise depressurization valve) manual override lever from the OFF position
to the ON position.
(c) Install MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, on the manual override lever on the LE cruise
depressurization valve (Lockwire, Cotter Pins, and Lockrings - Installation,
TASK 20-10-44-400-801).
SUBTASK 27-81-00-020-007
(3) Remove the DO-NOT-REMOVE tag from the lockout pin, SPL-1746, from the manual override
lever (handle) on the LE Uncommanded Motion (UCM) shutoff valve.
SUBTASK 27-81-00-020-010
(4) Remove the lockout pin, SPL-1746, from the manual override lever on the LE UCM shutoff
valve.
(a) Move the manual override lever on the UCM shutoff valve to the down (ON) position.
NOTE: The lever (handle) should move with very little force. If the handle is tight, you
may need hydraulic pressure and the FSEU to relieve the pressure on the LE
UCM SHUTOFF VALVE.
SUBTASK 27-81-00-020-011
(5) If the lockout pin, SPL-1746, will not come out easily, then do the steps that follow:
(a) Supply system B hydraulic power by doing this task: Leading Edge Flap and Slat System
Operation With Primary Control, TASK 27-81-00-860-801.
(b) Use the FSEU to relieve the pressure on the LE UCM SHUTOFF VALVE, as follows:
1) Push the ON/OFF button.
2) EXISTING FAULTS.....press NO.
3) Press NO until OTHER FUNCTIONS.
4) OTHER FUNCTIONS....press YES.
5) SET OUTPUTS.....press YES.
6) Press NO until LE UCM SHUTOFF VALVE.
7) LE UCM SHUTOFF VALVE....press YES.
8) SET ON.....press YES.
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT YOU MOVE THE MANUAL OVERRIDE HANDLE TO
THE OFF POSITION AND INSTALL THE RIG PIN IN LESS THAN 75
SECONDS. THE FSEU WILL AUTOMATICALLY CHANGE THE POSITION
OF THE VALVE AND THE OVERRIDE HANDLE AFTER 75 SECONDS.
THE MANUAL OVERRIDE HANDLE CAN MOVE SUDDENLY AND CAUSE
INJURY TO PERSONS.
(c) Remove the lockout pin, SPL-1746, from the LE UCM shutoff valve within 75 seconds of
pushing YES on the FSEU.
1) If the pin will not come out easily, then repeat the steps above pressurizing the
hydraulic system B before operating the FSEU.
2) Remove the B pressure after the valve has moved.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(d) Make sure that the LE UCM shutoff valve lever (handle) moves to the down position.
(6) Install the MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048 when the LE UCM shutoff lever is in the down
position (Lockwire, Cotter Pins, and Lockrings - Installation, TASK 20-10-44-400-801).

AND THE LANDING GEAR CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WITH THE
PRESSURIZATION OF A HYDRAULIC SYSTEM. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY
TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.

TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
NOTE: When operating the high lift devices on the ground with only the system B Electric
Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP) supplying power the pump low pressure light may
momentarily illuminate. This illumination and associated pressure drop should be
considered normal as long as the pressure recovers within 10 seconds of initiating
movement of the high lift devices.

LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS, AND THE TRAILING EDGE FLAPS. IF

EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS. THERE IS NOT SUFFICIENT CLEARANCE FOR

slats.

SUBTASK 27-81-00-860-011
WARNING
MAKE SURE THE POSITION OF THE FLAPS AGREES WITH THE POSITION
OF THE FLAP CONTROL LEVER. WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER,
THE FLAPS AND SLATS WILL MOVE AUTOMATICALLY TO THE POSITION
OF THE FLAP CONTROL LEVER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS
AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(1) Move the ALTERNATE FLAPS control switch until the flaps and slats are in the same position
as the flap control lever or move the flap control lever to the position of the flaps and slats.
SUBTASK 27-81-00-860-013
(2) Move the ALTERNATE FLAPS ARM switch to the OFF position to disarm the alternate control
system.

AND OUTBOARD THRUST REVERSERS ARE CLOSED AND IN THE

EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS. THERE IS NOT SUFFICIENT CLEARANCE FOR
THE FLAPS AND SLATS TO EXTEND IF THE INBOARD FAN COWL PANEL
AND THE INBOARD AND OUTBOARD THRUST REVERSERS ARE IN THE
OPEN POSITION. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.

G. Manual Leading Edge Flaps and Slats Retraction Procedure
SUBTASK 27-81-00-860-114
(1) If necessary, do these steps: (Figure 205).
NOTE: Pressurizing the hydraulic line to retract the flaps and slats will add hydraulic fluid to
Hydraulic Reservoir B. If the additional hydraulic fluid does not cause an overfill
condition then the following steps are not necessary. An overfill condition in the
reservoir can result in hydraulic fumes in the passenger cabin.
NOTE: Hydraulic fluid will be pushed back through the C1 and C2 lines during retraction.
(a) Disconnect the C1 line from the TEE fitting that is connected to the autoslat control valve.
1) Install a cap on the TEE fitting.
2) Put a container on the C1 line to catch the hydraulic fluid.
(b) Disconnect the C2 line from the autoslat control valve.
1) Install a cap on the open port of the autoslat control valve.
2) Put a container on the C1 line to catch the hydraulic fluid.
SUBTASK 27-81-00-860-115
(2) Do these steps to manually retract the LE flaps and slats: (Figure 205).
(a) Disconnect the hydraulic line from the CYL port on the LE Uncommanded Motion (UCM)
valve.
(b) Install a cap on the CYL port.
(c) Connect the portable hydraulic cart, COM-163, to the hydraulic line.
(d) Pressurize the hydraulic line with the portable hydraulic cart, COM-163, to retract the LE
flaps and slats.
NOTE: The LE surfaces may move slightly when hydraulic pressure is removed.
H. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 27-81-00-420-012
(1) Disconnect the hydraulic line from the portable hydraulic cart, COM-163.
(a) Connect the hydraulic line to the CYL port on the LE UCM.
SUBTASK 27-81-00-420-013
(2) If the C1 line and the C2 line were disconnected, do these steps:
(a) Connect the C1 line to the TEE fitting that is connected to the autoslat control valve.
(b) Connect the C2 line to the autoslat control valve.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

27-81-00-820-803Leading Edge Slats AdjustmentPDF p. 3860
4. Leading Edge Slats Adjustment
A. General
(1) You must adjust the leading edge slats with the wing unsupported outboard of the engine
nacelle. You can adjust the leading edge slats with the airplane on the gear or on jacks inboard
of the engine nacelle. The airplane must not have fuel in the wing fuel tanks located outboard
of the engine nacelle.
(2) It is recommended that all the steps in this task and full slat adjustment is done, for the most
consistent and lowest drag adjustment.
(3) Where time and/or airplane condition do not support the use of the full slat adjustment, a
minimum slat adjustment is permitted. Use of this minimum slat adjustment can result in
increased drag compared with the full slat adjustment. In this task, all the steps that are not
necessary for a minimum slat adjustment will be identified.

SUBTASK 27-81-00-200-001
WARNING
DO NOT LET OBJECTS GET IN THE HOUSING ASSEMBLY OF THE SLAT
TRACK. THIS WILL HELP PREVENT A PUNCTURE OF THE HOUSING
ASSEMBLY THAT COULD CAUSE A FUEL LEAK. THE FUEL LEAK COULD
CAUSE A FIRE AND POSSIBLE DEATH OR INJURY TO PERSONNEL.
(2) Keep the housing (can) assemblies of the slat main tracks clean and free of all Foreign Object
Debris (FOD) at all times.
SUBTASK 27-81-00-820-002
(3) Do a preliminary adjustment of the auxiliary track forward support (View A-A, Figure 503):
(a) Install the preload shim assembly, which is part of the rigging equipment, SPL-1739, at
the forward supports for the auxiliary tracks.
1) Remove the nuts [74] and washers [75] from the clevis [76].
2) Lift the auxiliary track [72] with the clevis [76] through the auxiliary track support.
3) Install the shims [77] as necessary to get the thickness 0.310 +0.030 / -0.010 in.
(7.87 +0.76 / -0.25 mm).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
4) Install the preload shim assembly, which is part of the rigging equipment, SPL-1739,
on the clevis [76].
5) Put the clevis [76] back in its position on the auxiliary track support.
6) Install the washers [75] and nuts [74] on the clevis [76].
7) Make sure that two BACW10P390TF, Polytetraflouroethylene (Teflon) (PTFE)
washers are installed in the clevis/auxiliary track/detent arm joint, if you
disconnected it. Use the applicable Illustrated Part Catalog for the required washers
at this location.
NOTE: If the washers are damaged or missing, stabilization of the detent arm is
reduced and it is possible for the detent arm to be deflected laterally during
slat extension or retraction and the possibility of misalignment between the
detent arm and the detent roller increases.
NOTE: If the washers are damaged or missing, it may be possible for the roller to
come out of the detent arm track, thus affecting the operation of the detent
system. Also extreme misalignment of the slat roller attachment could move
the slat down sensor target, causing fault indications or physical damage to
the sensor itself.
SUBTASK 27-81-00-820-003

(b) Loosen the jamnut [82].
(c) Loosen the nut [80] on the locking bolt [79].
(d) Turn the adjusting nut [81] of the aux track aft support to get the required trailing edge
clearance until the dimension A is as specified (Table 501).

corner of the track touches the locking bolt [91] at the upper aft auxiliary track

NOTE: This is only for the preliminary adjustment. The total shim thickness will be

SUBTASK 27-81-00-820-006
(7) Do a preliminary adjustment of the detent arm preload:
NOTE: If minimum slat adjustment will be done, preliminary adjustment of the detent arm
preload is not necessary.
NOTE: When measuring the 0.010 in. (0.254 mm) minimum clearance between the torsion rod
and the shorter shoulder bolt, the detent arm must be flush and in contact with the
shorter shoulder bolt. This dimension only applies during initial torsion rod installation.
This dimension will not apply after the torsion rod is preloaded during the slat
adjustment.
(a) Make sure that three (Corrosion Resistant Steel (CRES) material, 0.063 in. (1.600 mm)
nominal thickness) washers are installed in the detent roller/track/arm/sensor target joint
(one washer under the bolt head and two washers installed on both sides of the auxiliary
arm at the location shown in View B) per the applicable Illustrated Part Catalog.
NOTE: If the washers are thinner than 0.063 in. (1.600 mm), the lateral location of the
roller bearing will be changed and it will no longer align with the centerline of the
detent arm.
NOTE: The thinner washers will not support the torque preload and operating load
imposed on the joint. As the thinner washers deform, the fastener torque preload
is lost, and the joint may move under normal operating loads, inducing additional
misalignment of the bearing. This joint holds the slat sensor target, so a loosened
bolt will permit the sensor target to move. Target movement could lead to sensor
indication problems, and the loose target could physically contact the sensor as
the slat moves and cause additional damage.
(b) Adjust all preload on the detent arm to zero.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Turn the detent arm preload adjustment bolt [73] clockwise to increase preload or
counterclockwise to reduce preload.
2) Adjust the preload on all the detent arm [78] to zero pound.
SUBTASK 27-81-00-860-034
(8) Make sure that the bolt [102] on the skin tab [92] are loose on the slat auxiliary arms.
NOTE: This is to prevent damage to the fixed leading edge when the slat is retracted during
the adjustment.
H. Leading Edge Slats Adjustment
NOTE: The following operations may require slat position change to complete the adjustment
requirements and may result in dimensional changes when moving the slats.
SUBTASK 27-81-00-200-002
WARNING
DO NOT LET OBJECTS GET IN THE HOUSING ASSEMBLY OF THE SLAT
TRACK. THIS WILL HELP PREVENT A PUNCTURE OF THE HOUSING
ASSEMBLY THAT COULD CAUSE A FUEL LEAK. THE FUEL LEAK COULD
CAUSE A FIRE AND POSSIBLE DEATH OR INJURY TO PERSONNEL.
(1) Keep the housing (can) assemblies of the slat main tracks clean and free of all FOD at all
times.
SUBTASK 27-81-00-820-007
(2) Do the initial adjustment of the leading edge slat in the (intermediate) extend position:
NOTE: If minimum slat adjustment is done, initial adjustment of the slat in the (intermediate)
extend position is not necessary.
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT ALL PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF
THE LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS, AND THE TRAILING EDGE
FLAPS. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, THESE SURFACES WILL MOVE AND
CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONNEL OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE INBOARD FAN COWL PANEL AND THE
INBOARD AND OUTBOARD THRUST REVERSERS ARE CLOSED AND IN
THE STOWED POSITION OR REMOVED BEFORE YOU EXTEND THE
LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS. THERE IS NOT SUFFICIENT
CLEARANCE FOR THE FLAPS AND SLATS TO EXTEND IF THE
INBOARD FAN COWL PANEL AND THE INBOARD AND OUTBOARD
THRUST REVERSERS ARE IN THE OPEN POSITION. THIS CAN CAUSE
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(a) Extend the leading edge slat to the (intermediate) extend (1-unit detent) position with
hydraulic power, do this task: Leading Edge Flaps and Slats Extension,
TASK 27-81-00-860-803.
(b) Align the noses of the slats to get a mismatch of 0.0000 in. (0.00 mm) to 0.0600 in.
(1.52 mm) between the adjacent slats.
1) Dimension may apply at any one point within the 1.0000 in. (25.40 mm) band width
(Figure 504).
NOTE: This dimension is normal to the skin surface where the measurement is
taken. Vertical mismatch is permissible.
(c) Adjust the forward support of the auxiliary track [72].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Make sure that two BACW10P390TF, PTFE washers are installed in the
clevis/auxiliary track/ detent arm joint, if you disconnected it. Use the applicable
Illustrated Part Catalog for the required washers at this location.
NOTE: If the washers are damaged or missing, stabilization of the detent arm is
reduced and it is possible for the detent arm to be deflected laterally during
slat extension or retraction and the possibility of misalignment between the
detent arm and the detent roller increases.
NOTE: If the washers are damaged or missing, it may be possible for the roller to
come out of the detent arm track, thus affecting the operation of the detent
system. Also extreme misalignment of the slat roller attachment could move
the slat down sensor target, causing fault indications or physical damage to
the sensor itself.
2) Remove the nut [74] and washer [75] from the clevis [76].
3) Lift the auxiliary track [72] with the clevis [76] through the auxiliary track support.
4) Add or remove the shim [77] until the gap between the slat and fixed leading edge is
0.002 +0.006 / -0.000 in. (0.051 +0.152 / -0.000 mm).
a) Measure the clearance at the tightest point, within 2.00 in. (50.80 mm) on
either side of the each auxiliary track centerline.
b) Measure the clearance to a depth of 0.4000 in. (10.1600 mm) - 0.6000 in.
(15.2400 mm).
5) Move the slat, if required, to remove shims [77].
6) Make sure that the total shim thickness is 0.0300 in. (0.7620 mm) - 0.2700 in.
(6.8580 mm).
7) Re-align the noses of the slats to get a mismatch of 0.0000 in. (0.0000 mm) -
0.0600 in. (1.5240 mm) between the adjacent slats, if/as required.
8) Put the clevis [76] back in its positions on the auxiliary track support.
9) Install the washer [75] and nut [74] on the clevis [76].
(d) Adjust the cam plate [83].
NOTE: The cam plates are located on the forward end of the detent arm and are used to
align and hold the slats in the (intermediate) extend position.
1) Loosen the two nuts [84] that attach the cam plate [83] to the detent arm [78].
a) Adjust the cam plates to the dimension shown in View C-C.
<1> If the cam plate serrations do not mate with corresponding serrations on
the detent arm when located per the required dimension then moved
the cam plate aft into the next available serration.
2) Move the cam plate [83] forward or aft, as required, until you get these conditions:
a) Engage the serrations in the required position and torque the nuts [84] on the
cam plate [83] to 65 in-lb (7 N·m) - 100 in-lb (11 N·m) (preferred method) or
the bolts [90] to 90 in-lb (10 N·m) - 110 in-lb (12 N·m) (optional method).
b) The detent roller touch the root of each detent arm [78].
c) Make sure that the clearance between the detent roller and aft surface of the
cam plate is 0.000 in. (0.000 mm) - 0.030 in. (0.762 mm).
3) Cycle the slats and make sure that the 0.0020 +0.0060 / -0.0000 in.
(0.0508 +0.1524 / -0.0000 mm) clearance is kept.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
4) Adjust if/as required the alignment of the slat noses and detent arm cam plates.
(e) Move the slat from the (intermediate) extend position until the detent roller is completely
clear of the detent arm [78] and cam plate [83].
(f) On slats 1, 4, 5 and 8, adjust the detent arm preload to 75 lbf (334 N) - 85 lbf (378 N),
measured with a spring scale, STD-755, at the throat of the cam plate [83], and
0.1000 +0.0600 / -0.0400 in. (2.5400 +1.5240 / -1.0160 mm) dimension at the lower
portion of the detent arm [78].
NOTE: The arm preload adjustment bolt is located next to the auxiliary tracks at the far
end of the torsion rod and is used to change the preload tension of the torsion
rod and detent arm. Adjust the preload by rotating the preload adjustment bolt
clockwise for increased preload and counterclockwise for reduced preload.
1) If it is necessary, remove the nut at the lower auxiliary track attach bolt to see this
clearance.
(g) On slats 2, 3, 6 and 7, adjust the detent arm preload to 45 lbf (200 N) - 55 lbf (245 N),
measured with a spring scale, STD-755, at the throat of the cam plate [83], and
0.1000 +0.0600 / -0.0400 in. (2.5400 +1.5240 / -1.0160 mm) dimension at the lower
portion of the detent arm [78].
(h) Make sure that there is 0.0100 in. (0.2540 mm) minimum clearance between the torsion
rod and the longer shoulder bolt, if not, do the steps that follow ( View D-D, Figure 503):
NOTE: The longer shoulder bolt is installed through both of the flanges of the (auxiliary
track support) clevis.
NOTE: The clearance measurement is taken where the torsion rod exits the longer
shoulder bolt on the detent preload side of the mechanism. In other words, the
clearance measurement is taken on the (auxiliary track support) clevis side
toward the middle point of the torsion rod.
1) Remove the preload from the detent arm.
2) Adjust the bolt with the steps that follow:
a) Re-align the torsion rod by backing off the nut by adjusting the shorter
shoulder bolt up or down in the slotted hole in the torsion rod support bracket
assembly.
b) Torque the nut to 450 in-lb (51 N·m) - 600 in-lb (68 N·m).
3) Adjust the detent arm preload.
a) Adjust the preload by rotating the preload adjustment bolt clockwise for
increased preload and counterclockwise for reduced preload.
b) After final adjustment fasten the adjustment bolt to its lower trunnion with
safety wire (single wire method permissible).
4) Make sure that you get the correct clearance.
SUBTASK 27-81-00-820-008
(3) Do the initial adjustment of the leading edge slat in the retract position:
NOTE: If minimum slat adjustment is done, initial adjustment of the slat in the retract position
is not necessary.
(a) Do this task: Leading Edge Flaps and Slats Retraction, TASK 27-81-00-860-804.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) Position the ends of the slats using the end stop pad adjustments to get a 0.0000 in.
(0.0000 mm) - 0.0500 in. (1.2700 mm) fair between all adjacent slat ends; between the
outboard end of slats 1 and 8 and on the adjacent fixed leading edge; and between the
inboard end of slat 4 and 5 and adjacent fixed leading edge.
NOTE: The end stops are located near both ends of each slat and can be used to adjust
the trailing edge clearance near the slat center, clearance and misfair of the flex
skin to the lower fixed leading edge panels, and misfair at the slat ends. Each
stop location has a horizontal and vertical pad. To adjust each stop pad. add or
subtract in any combination of 0.0100 in. (0.2540 mm), 0.0200 in. (0.5080 mm),
0.0400 in. (1.0160 mm), and 0.0630 in. (1.6002 mm) thick solid shims. The total
permitted shim thickness is 0.0000 in. (0.0000 mm) to 0.1280 in. (3.2512 mm)
and must be such that the slat flex skin keeps solid contact with the fixed leading
edge.
(c) Make sure that the slat upstops touch the horizontal and vertical stop pads.
NOTE: The up stop pads are located 5.3 in. (134.6 mm) on either side of each actuator
and can be used to adjust the trailing edge clearance near the slat center,
clearance and misfair of the flex skin to the lower fixed leading edge panels, and
misfair at the slat ends. Each stop location has a horizontal and vertical pad.
(d) If the slat upstops do not touch the horizontal and vertical stop pads, adjust the stop pad:
NOTE: Use these stops to adjust the slat nose to match the adjacent slats.
1) Remove the retainers [85], nuts [86], and bolts [89].
2) Add or remove shim [87] as it is necessary until the slat fairs with the adjacent slat.
NOTE: Add or remove only a minimum amount of shim necessary for the slat
upstop to touch the stop pad. To adjust each stop pad, add or subtract in
any combination of 0.0100 in. (0.2540 mm), 0.0200 in. (0.5080 mm),
0.0400 in. (1.0160 mm), and 0.0630 in. (1.6002 mm) thick solid shims. The
total permitted shim thickness is 0.0000 in. (0.0000 mm) to 0.1280 in.
(3.2512 mm) and must be such that the slat flex skin keeps solid contact
with the fixed leading edge.
3) Install the bolts [89], nuts [86], and retainers [85].
(e) Adjust the aft support of the auxiliary track [72] per Views C-C and D-D:
1) Loosen the nut [103] on the bolt [91] at the upper aft aux track.
2) Loosen the jamnut [82].
3) Loosen the nut [80] on the locking bolt [79].
4) Turn the adjusting nut [81] until the clearance between the slat and fixed leading
edge is 0.0020 +0.0060 / -0.0000 in. (0.0508 +0.1524 / -0.0000 mm).
a) Measure the clearance at the tightest point, within 2.00 in. (50.80 mm) on
either side of the each auxiliary track centerline.
b) Measure the clearance to a depth of 0.4000 in. (10.1600 mm) - 0.6000 in.
(15.2400 mm).
5) Temporarily tighten the locking bolt [79].
6) Temporarily tighten the jamnut [82].
7) Temporarily tighten the locking bolt [91] at the upper aft aux track.
(f) Measure and calculate the weighted average misfair.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Measure the misfair at six locations for each specified gap (Table 502):
NOTE: There will be a total of 30 locations on each wing that you will need to
measure.
a) The gap between all adjacent slat ends
b) The clearance between the outboard end of slats 1 and 8 and adjacent fixed
leading edge
c) The clearance between the inboard end of slats 4 and 5 and adjacent fixed
leading edge.

2) Multiply all negative fair measurements by -0.5.
3) Add all the misfair values (positive and negative misfairs).
4) Divide the total misfair value by 6.
5) Make sure that the result is 0.0000 in. (0.0000 mm) - 0.0500 in. (1.2700 mm).
(g) Make sure that the slat endstops touch the horizontal and vertical stop pads.
(h) If the slat endstops do not touch the horizontal and vertical stop pads, adjust the stop
pad:
1) Remove the retainers [85], nuts [86], and bolts [89]].
2) Add or remove shim [87] as it is necessary until the slat fairs with the adjacent slat.
a) Add or remove only a minimum amount of shim necessary for the slat upstop
to touch the stop pad.
b) Add or subtract in any combination of 0.0100 in. (0.2540 mm), 0.0200 in.
(0.5080 mm), 0.0400 in. (1.0160 mm), and 0.0630 in. (1.6002 mm) thick solid
shims to adjust each stop pad.
NOTE: The total permitted shim thickness is 0.0000 in. (0.0000 mm) to
0.1280 in. (3.2512 mm) and must be such that the slat flex skin keeps
solid contact with the fixed leading edge.
3) Install the bolts [89], nuts [86], and retainers [85].
SUBTASK 27-81-00-820-009
(4) Do the final adjustment of the leading edge slat in the (intermediate) extend position:
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT ALL PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF
THE LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS, AND THE TRAILING EDGE
FLAPS. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, THESE SURFACES WILL MOVE AND
CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONNEL OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE INBOARD FAN COWL PANEL AND THE
INBOARD AND OUTBOARD THRUST REVERSERS ARE CLOSED AND IN
THE STOWED POSITION OR REMOVED BEFORE YOU EXTEND THE
LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS. THERE IS NOT SUFFICIENT
CLEARANCE FOR THE FLAPS AND SLATS TO EXTEND IF THE
INBOARD FAN COWL PANEL AND THE INBOARD AND OUTBOARD
THRUST REVERSERS ARE IN THE OPEN POSITION. THIS CAN CAUSE
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(a) To extend the leading edge slat to the (intermediate) extend (1-unit detent) position, do
this task: Leading Edge Flaps and Slats Extension, TASK 27-81-00-860-803.
(b) Align the noses of the slats to get a mismatch of 0.0000 in. (0.00 mm) to 0.0600 in.
(1.52 mm) between the adjacent slats.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Dimension may apply at any one point within the 1.0000 in. (25.40 mm) band width
(Figure 504).
NOTE: This dimension is normal to the skin surface where the measurement is
taken. Vertical mismatch is permissible.
(c) Make sure that the detent roller touch the root of each detent arm.
(d) Make sure that the clearance between the detent roller and aft surface of the cam plate is
0.0000 in. (0.0000 mm) to 0.0300 in. (0.7620 mm).
(e) If the detent roller does not touch the root of the detent arm and gap between the detent
roller and cam plate [83] is out of tolerance, adjust the cam plate [83]:
1) Loosen the two nuts [84] that attach the cam plate [83] to the detent arm [78].
2) Move the cam plate [83] forward or aft as it is necessary.
3) Temporarily tighten the two nuts [84].
(f) Make sure that the clearance between the slat and fixed leading edge is
0.0020 +0.0060 / -0.0000 in. (0.0508 +0.1524 / -0.0000 mm) (View C1, Figure 503).
NOTE: View C1 shows the slat in the retracted position. View C1 is dimensionally similar
to the slat in the intermediate position.
1) Measure the clearance at the tightest point, within 2.00 in. (50.80 mm) on either
side of each auxiliary track centerline.
2) Measure the clearance to a depth of 0.4000 in. (10.1600 mm) - 0.6000 in.
(15.2400 mm).
(g) If the clearance between the slat and fixed leading edge is not
0.0020 +0.0060 / -0.0000 in. (0.0508 +0.1524 / -0.0000 mm), adjust the forward support
of the auxiliary track:
1) Remove the nut [74] and washer [75] from the clevis [76].
2) Lift the auxiliary track [72] with the clevis [76] through the auxiliary track support.
3) Add or remove the shim [77] to a total thickness of 0.0300 in. (0.7620 mm) -
0.2700 in. (6.8580 mm).
4) Put the clevis [76] back in its position on the auxiliary track support.
5) Install the washer [75] and nut [74] on the clevis [76].
(h) Remove the preload shim assembly, which is part of the rigging equipment, SPL-1739, at
the forward supports for the auxiliary tracks:
1) Remove the nut [74] and washer [75] from the clevis [76].
2) Lift the auxiliary track [72] with the clevis [76] through the auxiliary track support.
3) Remove the preload shim assembly.
4) Put the clevis [76] back in its position on the auxiliary track support.
5) Install the washer [75] and nut [74] on the clevis [76].
(i) Make sure that the minimum clearance at these locations is 0.2000 in. (5.0800 mm):
1) The clearance between all adjacent slat ends.
2) The clearance between the outboard end of slats 1 and 8 and adjacent fixed leading
edge.
3) The clearance between the inboard end of slats 4 and 5 and adjacent fixed leading
edge.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(j) Extend the slat until the detent roller is completely clear of the detent arm [78] and cam
plate [83].
(k) On slats 1, 4, 5 and 8, make sure that the detent arm preload is 75 lbf (334 N) - 85 lbf
(378 N), measured with a spring scale, STD-755, at the throat of the cam plate [83], and
0.100 +0.060 / -0.040 in. (2.540 +1.524 / -1.016 mm) dimension at the lower portion of
the detent arm [78].
(l) On slats 2, 3, 6 and 7, make sure that the detent arm preload is 45 lbf (200 N) - 55 lbf
(245 N), measured with a spring scale, STD-755, at the throat of the cam plate [83], and
0.100 +0.060 / -0.040 in. (2.540 +1.524 / -1.016 mm) dimension at the lower portion of
the detent arm [78].

WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT ALL PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF
THE LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS, AND THE TRAILING EDGE
FLAPS. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, THESE SURFACES WILL MOVE AND
CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONNEL OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(a) Do this task: Leading Edge Flaps and Slats Retraction, TASK 27-81-00-860-804.
(b) Make sure that the slat upstops touch the horizontal and vertical stop pads.
(c) If the slat upstops do not touch the horizontal and vertical stop pads, adjust the stop pad:
1) Remove the retainers [85], nuts [86], and bolts [89].
2) Add or remove shim [87] as it is necessary until the slat fairs with the adjacent slat.
NOTE: Add or remove only a minimum amount of shim necessary for the slat
upstop to touch the stop pad. To adjust each stop pad, add or subtract in
any combination of 0.0100 in. (0.2540 mm), 0.02 in. (0.5080 mm),
0.0400 in. (1.0160 mm), and 0.0630 in. (1.6002 mm) thick solid shims. The
total permitted shim thickness is 0.0000 in. (0.0000 mm) to 0.1280 in.
(3.2512 mm) and must be such that the slat flex skin keeps solid contact
with the fixed leading edge.
3) Install the bolts [89], nuts [86], and retainers [85].
(d) Make sure that the clearance between the slat and fixed leading edge is
0.0020 +0.0060 / -0.0000 in. (0.0508 +0.1524 / -0.0000 mm).
1) Measure the clearance at the tightest point, within 2.00 in. (50.80 mm) on either
side of each auxiliary track centerline.
2) Measure the clearance to a depth of 0.4000 in. (10.1600 mm) - 0.6000 in.
(15.2400 mm).
(e) If the clearance between the slat and fixed leading edge is not
0.0020 +0.0060 / -0.0000 in. (0.0508 +0.1524 / -0.0000 mm), adjust the aft support of the
auxiliary track:
1) Loosen the nut [103] on the locking bolt [91] at the upper aft aux track.

 ALL
2) Loosen the jamnut [82].
3) Loosen the nut [80] on the locking bolt [79].

edge is 0.0020 +0.0060 / -0.0000 in. (0.0508 +0.1524 / -0.0000 mm).
5) Temporarily tighten the nut [80] on the locking bolt [79].
6) Temporarily tighten the jamnut [82].
(f) Reduce the dimension A by 0.0210 ±0.0030 in. (0.5334 ±0.0762 mm) to preload the slat
trailing edge:
1) Loosen the jamnut [82].
2) Loosen the nut [80] to loosen the locking bolt [79].

(h) Temporarily tighten the jamnut [82].
(i) Make sure that the weighted average misfair is 0.0000 in. (0.0000 mm) - 0.0500 in.

any combination of 0.0100 in. (0.2540 mm), 0.0200 in. (0.5080 mm),
0.0400 in. (1.0160 mm), and 0.0630 in. (1.6002 mm) thick solid shims. The
total permitted shim thickness is 0.0000 in. (0.0000 mm) to 0.1280 in.

with the fixed leading edge.
3) Install the bolts [89], nuts [86], and retainers [85].

D. Leading Edge Flap and Slat Timing Test in Primary Mode
SUBTASK 27-81-00-720-001
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE
LEADING EDGE AND TRAILING EDGE CONTROL SURFACES. THE LEADING
EDGE AND TRAILING EDGE CONTROLS SURFACES CAN EXTEND AND
RETRACT QUICKLY. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONNEL AND
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(1) Do a timing test of the leading edge flap and slat control system in primary mode:
NOTE: Measure the time intervals between the time the surfaces start to move to the time the
surfaces stop moving.
(a) If the flap control lever is not in the UP position, do these steps:
1) Move the flap control lever to the UP position.
2) Let the leading edge flaps and slats and the trailing edge flaps move to the retract
position.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) Move the flap control lever to the 5-unit detent position.
1) If hydraulic system B is pressurized with a portable hydraulic cart:
a) Make sure that the leading edge flaps extend fully in 5.5 to 7.5 seconds.
b) Make sure that the leading edge slats move to the extend position in 7.5 to 9.5
seconds.
2) If hydraulic system B is pressurized with the Electric Motor-Driven Pump (EMDP):
a) Make sure that the leading edge flaps extend fully in 7.0 to 9.0 seconds.
b) Make sure that the leading edge slats move to the extend position in 9.0 to
11.0 seconds.
(c) Move the flap control lever to the 30-unit detent.
 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131,
132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304,
306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-465
NOTE: For airplanes without Short Field Performance (SFP) the leading edge slats
move to the extend position at the 1-unit detent flap lever position and the
leading edge slats move to the full extend position at the 10-unit detent flap lever
position.
 ALL
1) If hydraulic system B is pressurized with a portable hydraulic cart:
a) Make sure that the leading edge slats move to the full extend position in 2.0 to
3.5 seconds.
2) If hydraulic system B is pressurized with the EMDP:
a) Make sure that the leading edge slats move to the full extend position in 3.5 to
5.5 seconds.
(d) Make sure that the LE indication flaps EXTEND and slats FULL EXTEND lights on the aft
overhead panel are on (Figure 506).
(e) Move the flap control lever to the 1-unit detent position.
1) If hydraulic system B is pressurized with a portable hydraulic cart:
a) Make sure that the leading edge slats move to the extend position in 3.5 to 5.5
seconds.
2) If hydraulic system B is pressurized with the EMDP:
a) Make sure that the leading edge slats move to the extend position in 4.5 to 6.5
seconds.
3) Let the trailing edge flaps move to the correct position.
(f) Move the flap control lever to the UP detent position.
1) If hydraulic system B is pressurized with a portable hydraulic cart:
a) Make sure that the leading edge flaps move to the retracted position in 7.0 to
9.0 seconds
b) Make sure that the leading edge slats move to the retracted position in 6.5 to
8.5 seconds.
2) If hydraulic system B is pressurized with the EMDP:
a) Make sure that the leading edge flaps move to the retracted position in 8.0 to
10.0 seconds.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
b) Make sure that the leading edge slats move to the retracted position in 7.0 to
9.0 seconds.
(g) Make sure that the LE indication flaps and slats TRANSIT, EXTEND and FULL EXTEND
lights on the aft overhead panel are off.

SUBTASK 27-81-00-710-001
(1) Do the leading edge flap and slat timing test in the standby mode:
NOTE: The leading edge flaps and slats do not retract in the standby mode.
(a) Put the ALTERNATE FLAPS arm switch, on the overhead panel, P5, in the ARM position
(Figure 507).
(b) Move the ALTERNATE FLAPS control switch to the DOWN position for 5 seconds, then
release.
(c) When the flaps and slats start to extend, make sure all the LE indication flaps and slats
TRANSIT lights, on the aft overhead panel, P5, come on.
(d) Make sure that the leading edge flaps extend in 29 to 37 seconds.
(e) Make sure that the leading edge slats extend in 43 to 55 seconds.
(f) Do these checks of the lights on the aft overhead panel (P5-12) when the leading edge
flaps and slats are in the full extended position (Figure 506):
1) Make sure that all the TRANSIT lights go off.
2) Make sure that the flaps EXT lights come on.
3) Make sure that the slats FULL EXT lights come on.
(g) Put the ALTERNATE FLAPS arm switch, on the overhead panel, P5, in the OFF position
(Figure 507).

SUBTASK 27-81-00-860-083
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE
LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS AND THE TRAILING EDGE FLAPS. THE
FLAPS AND SLATS WILL EXTEND. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS
