(1) Move the flap control lever to the 1-unit position to extend the leading edge flaps and slats and
the trailing edge flaps.
SUBTASK 27-81-00-740-004
(2) Do this test of the leading edge cruise depressurization valve:
(a) Move the ALTERNATE FLAPS ARM switch on the P5-3 panel to the ARM position.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) Use the Flap/Slat Electronics Unit (FSEU) to operate the leading edge cruise
depressurization valve:
1) Push the ON/OFF button on the front panel of the FSEU to turn on the display.
NOTE: The display will show EXISTING FAULTS?.
2) Push the down arrow until OTHER FUNCTNS? shows on the display.
3) Push the YES button to select OTHER FUNCTNS? on the FSEU.
4) Push the YES button to select SET OUTPUTS? from the OTHER FUNCTNS?
menu.
5) Push the YES button to select LE DEPR VALVE? from the menu.
6) Push the YES button to select SET ON? on the display.
7) The FSEU display will show CMD ON/SET OFF? for approximately 75 seconds.
(c) Make sure the leading edge flaps and slats do not move.
(d) Wait until the FSEU display shows LE DEPR VALVE?.
NOTE: This will take approximately 75 seconds from the time that CMD ON/SET OFF?
shows on the display.
(e) Move the flap control lever to the UP position.
(f) Make sure the leading edge flaps and slats and the trailing edge flaps do not move to the
retracted position.
(g) Push the YES button on the FSEU to display SET ON?.
(h) Push the YES button to select SET ON? on the display.
(i) Make sure the leading edge flaps and slats retract and that the trailing edge flaps stay
extended.
NOTE: The LE FLAPS TRANSIT lights will stay on.
(j) Wait until the FSEU display shows LE DEPR VALVE?.
NOTE: This will take approximately 75 seconds.
(k) Make sure the leading edge flaps and slats move to the extend position.
(l) Move the ALTERNATE FLAPS ARM switch to the OFF position.
(m) Make sure the leading edge flaps and slats, and the trailing edge flaps move to the
retracted position.

position.

(b) Make sure the STANDBY HYD LOW PRESSURE light on the P5 panel comes on and
quickly goes out.
NOTE: This makes sure that the standby system is pressurized.
SUBTASK 27-81-00-210-004
(2) Observe the leading edges on both the left and right wings:
(a) Make sure that the leading edges do not move when you pressurize the standby
hydraulic system.
NOTE: The leading edge flaps can slowly extend because of gravity.
F. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 27-81-00-860-075
(1) Move the ALTERNATE FLAPS ARM switch on the forward overhead panel to the OFF position.
NOTE: This will turn off the standby hydraulic system.
SUBTASK 27-81-00-860-076
(2) Do this task: Remove Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-812.

SUBTASK 27-81-11-860-001
WARNING
KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL
SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE
COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC
POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(1) To pressurize hydraulic system B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization,
TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-81-11-860-002
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE
LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS AND THE TRAILING EDGE FLAPS. THE
FLAPS AND SLATS WILL EXTEND. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS
AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU REMOVE OR CLOSE THE INBOARD FAN DUCT
COWL AND INBOARD AND OUTBOARD THRUST REVERSERS BEFORE
YOU EXTEND THE LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS. THERE IS NOT
SUFFICIENT CLEARANCE FOR THE FLAPS AND SLATS TO EXTEND. THIS
CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(2) Move the flap control lever to the 1-unit detent to extend the leading edge flaps.
SUBTASK 27-81-11-860-003
(3) To remove power from hydraulic system B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power
Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805.
SUBTASK 27-81-11-480-001
WARNING
MAKE SURE TO INSTALL THE LEADING EDGE FLAP AND SLAT ACTUATORS
LOCKOUT SET TO PREVENT ACCIDENTAL OPERATION OF THE LEADING
EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS. THE LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS CAN
MOVE QUICKLY. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(4) Install the lockout set, SPL-1734, on the actuator of the adjacent leading edge flap. To do this,
do this task: Leading Edge Flap and Slat Locks Installation, TASK 27-81-00-480-801.
E. Leading Edge Flap Removal
SUBTASK 27-81-11-020-001
(1) Disconnect the flap actuator [4] from the leading edge flap [1] or leading edge flap [2]:
(a) Remove the pin [6], nut [7], washer [8], bushing [11], washer [10] and bolt [9] to
disconnect the flap actuator [4] from the outboard leading edge flap [1].
(b) Remove the pin [15], nut [16], washer [17], bushing [12], washer [13] and bolt [14] to
disconnect the flap actuator [4] from the inboard leading edge flap [2].
SUBTASK 27-81-11-020-002
(2) Do these steps to remove the outboard leading edge flap [1] from the fixed leading edge:
(a) Disconnect the outboard bullnose linkage [53] from the fixed leading edge flap.
1) Remove the pin [55], nut [54], washer [56], anti-rotation washer [41], bushing [44],
washer [43] and bolt [42].
(b) Disconnect hinges 1 thru 4 on the leading edge flap [1] from the fixed leading edge.
1) At hinges 1 and 4, remove the pins pin [21], nuts [22], washers [20], bushings [19],
washers [24], and bolts [23].
2) At hinges 2 and 3, remove the pin [34], nuts [33], washers [25], bushings [26],
washers [28], and bolts [27].
(c) Remove the nut [32], washers [31], and bolt [30] to disconnect the bonding jumper [29]
from the fixed leading edge.
(d) Remove the leading edge flap [1] from the wing.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-81-11-020-003
(3) Do these steps to remove the inboard leading edge flap [2] from the fixed leading edge:
(a) Disconnect the mid and inboard bullnose linkages [53] from the fixed leading edge flap.
1) Remove the pin [55], nuts [54], washers [56], anti-rotation washers [41],
bushings [44], washers [43] and bolts [42].
(b) Disconnect hinges 5 thru 8 on the leading edge flap [2] from the fixed leading edge flap.
1) At hinge 5, remove the pin [21], nut [22], washer [20], bushing [19], washer [24], and
bolt [23].
2) At hinges 6 and 7, remove the pin [34], nuts [33], washers [25], bushings [26],
washers [28], and bolts [27].
3) At hinge 8, remove the pin [40], nut [39], washer [35], bushing [38], washer [36], and
bolt [37].
(c) Remove the nut [32], washers [31], and bolt [30] to disconnect the bonding jumper [29]
from the leading edge flap [2].
(d) Remove the leading edge flap [2] from the wing.

F. Leading Edge Flap Installation
SUBTASK 27-81-11-220-005
(1) If you install used bearings, bushings and bolts, do this task: Leading Edge Flap Inspection,
TASK 27-81-11-200-801.
SUBTASK 27-81-11-420-001
(2) If you removed the outboard leading edge flap [1], connect the outboard leading edge flap [1]
to the fixed leading edge:
(a) Connect hinges 1 thru 4 on the leading edge flap [1] to the fixed leading edge.
1) Apply grease, D00633, on the mating surfaces of the bolts [23] and bolts [27].
2) At hinges 1 and 4, install the bolts [23], washers [24], bushings [19], washers [20],
and nuts [22].
NOTE: Install the bolts [23] with the head outboard.
3) Tighten the nuts [22] to 60 in-lb (6.8 N·m) - 95 in-lb (10.7 N·m).
4) Install the pin [21].
5) At hinges 2 and 3, install the bolts [27], washers [28], bushings [26], washers [25],
and nuts [33].
NOTE: At hinge 2, install the bolt [27] with the head inboard. At hinge 3, install the
bolt [27] with the head outboard.
6) Tighten the nuts [33] to 290 in-lb (32.8 N·m) - 510 in-lb (57.6 N·m).
7) Install the pin [34].
(b) Connect the bonding jumper [29] to the fixed leading edge.
1) Install the bolt [30], washers [31], and nut [32] to attach the bonding jumper [29].
2) Tighten the nut [32] to 28 in-lb (3.2 N·m) - 35 in-lb (4.0 N·m).
3) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the bonding jumper [29] and
fixed leading edge.
a) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550.
b) Make sure that the resistance is less than 0.001 ohm.
4) Do these steps to make a fillet seal (SWPM 20-20-00):
a) Clean the area before you apply the sealant (TASK 51-31-00-160-801).
b) Apply the sealant, A02315, around the bolt [30], washers [31], nut [32], and
end of the bonding jumper [29].
(c) Connect the outboard bullnose linkage [53] to the fixed leading edge.
1) Install the bolt [42], washer [43], bushing [44], anti-rotation washers [41],
washer [56], and nut [54].
NOTE: Install the bolt [42] with the head inboard.
2) Tighten the nut [54] to 30 in-lb (3.4 N·m) - 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m).
3) Install the pin [55].
SUBTASK 27-81-11-420-002
(3) If you removed the inboard leading edge flap [2], connect the inboard leading edge flap [2] to
the fixed leading edge:
(a) Connect hinges 5 thru 8 on the leading edge flap [2] to the fixed leading edge.
1) Apply grease, D00633, on the mating surfaces of the bolts [23] and bolts [27].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
2) At hinge 5, install the bolt [23], washer [24], bushing [19], washer [20], and nut [22].
NOTE: Install the bolt [23] with the head outboard.
a) Tighten the nut [22] to 60 in-lb (6.8 N·m) - 95 in-lb (10.7 N·m).
b) Install the pin [21].
3) At hinges 6 and 7, install the bolts [27], washers [28], bushings [26], washers [25],
and nuts [33].
NOTE: At hinge 6, install the bolt [27] with the head inboard. At hinge 7, install the
bolt [27] with the head outboard.
a) Tighten the nuts [33] to 290 in-lb (32.8 N·m) - 510 in-lb (57.6 N·m).
b) Install the pin [34].
4) At hinge 8, install the bolt [37], washer [36], bushing [38], washer [35], and nut [39].
NOTE: Install the bolt [37] with the head inboard.
a) Tighten the nut [39] to 60 in-lb (6.8 N·m) - 95 in-lb (10.7 N·m).

(b) Connect the bonding jumper [29] to the fixed leading edge.
1) Install the bolt [30], washers [31], and nut [32] to attach the bonding jumper [29].

(c) Connect the mid and inboard bullnose linkages [53] to the fixed leading edge.
1) Install the bolts [42], washers [43], bushings [44], anti-rotation washers [41],

NOTE: Install the bolts [42] with the heads outboard.
2) Tighten the nuts [54] to 30 in-lb (3.4 N·m) - 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m).
3) Install the pin [55].

(d) Make sure that the full extend angle of the leading edge flap [2] or leading edge flap [1] is
98 +/- 0.5 degrees.
1) If the extend angle is out of tolerance, adjust the length of the flap actuator [4].
a) Loosen the jamnut [45] on the flap actuator rod end [3].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
b) Turn the flap actuator rod end [3] until you get the correct full extend angle.
NOTE: The limit for maximum adjustment is two full turns.
c) Tighten the jamnut [45] to 550 in-lb (62.1 N·m) - 650 in-lb (73.4 N·m).
d) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G01912, on the jamnut [45].
(e) Remove the protractor, COM-1691.
SUBTASK 27-81-11-220-002
(14) Make sure that the mismatch between the inboard leading edge flap [2] and the outboard
leading edge flap [1] is 0.000 ±0.040 in. (0.000 ±1.016 mm).
 352
SUBTASK 27-81-11-220-007
(15) Make sure that the mismatch between the inboard leading edge flap [2] and the outboard
leading edge flap [1] is 0.000 ±0.040 in. (0.000 ±1.016 mm) with a mismatch of up to -0.190 in.
(4.826 mm) as acceptable.
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-81-11-860-006
(16) Apply preload at the flap bullnose to the leading edge flap [2] or leading edge flap [1].
(a) Make sure that the flap bullnose touches the leading edge flap [2] or leading edge
flap [1].
NOTE: To apply the correct preload, the flap bullnose must first touch the leading edge
flap [2] or leading edge flap [1].
1) If the flap bullnose does not touch the leading edge flap [2] or leading edge flap [1],
adjust the flap rod [57].
(b) Adjust the flap rod [57] an additional 1/2 turn to apply the correct preload at the flap
bullnose to the leading edge flap [2] or leading edge flap [1].
(c) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G01912, on the flap rod [57].
SUBTASK 27-81-11-860-007
WARNING
MOVE ALL PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE TRAILING EDGE
FLAPS, AND THE LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS. THESE SURFACES
WILL MOVE AND CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(17) Move the flap control lever to the UP detent to retract the leading edge flaps.
SUBTASK 27-81-11-220-003
(18) Do a check of the gap at the edge of the leading edge flap [2] and leading edge flap [1] (View K
and View L, Figure 401).
(a) Check the gap at location 1-4, 6-10, 12-19 (Figure 402).
1) If all the measurements taken at locations 1-4, 6-10, 12-19 are less than 0.15 in.
(3.8 mm), then the gap is satisfactory.
2) If one or more of the gap measurements exceeds 0.15 in. (3.8 mm), convert each of
the measurements into a Net Effect Value (NEV).
a) Use the NET Effect Value Chart and NET Effect Value Table for the Trealing
Edge Gaps (Figure 402).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
3) Add the NEV measurements together and divide by the total number of
measurements.
NOTE: This gives the total NEV.
4) Make sure that the calculated total NEV is less than 1.0.
NOTE: The Net Effect Limit (NEL) for this measurement is 1.0.
SUBTASK 27-81-11-220-006
(19) Do a check of the mismatch at the forward edge of the leading edge flap [2] and leading edge
flap [1] (View K, Figure 401).
(a) Check the mismatch at the forward edge of the leading edge flap [2] and leading edge
flap [1] at locations 1-4 and 6-10 (Figure 402).
1) If all the measurements taken at locations 1-4 and 6-10 are within the range
-0.03 in. (-0.8 mm) - 0.02 in. (0.5 mm), the misfair at the forward edge of the
Krueger flap is acceptable as is without any additional adjustments.
NOTE: See the Figure 402 for definition of the negative and positive misfair
measurements.
2) If one or more of the misfair measurements is outside the range -0.03 in. (-0.8 mm)
- 0.02 in. (0.5 mm), convert each of the measurements into a NEV.
a) Use the NET Effect Value Chart and NET Effect Value Table for the Leading
(Forward) Edge Misfair only (Figure 402).
3) Add the NEV measurements together and divide by the total number of
measurements.
NOTE: This gives the total NEV.
4) Make sure that the calculated total NEV is less than 1.0.
NOTE: The NEL for this measurement is 1.0.
5) If it is necessary, adjust the mismatch dimension.
a) Loosen the jamnut [45] on the flap actuator rod end [3].
b) Turn the flap actuator rod end [3] to adjust the length of the flap actuator [4]
until you get the correct mismatch.
NOTE: The limit for maximum adjustment is two full turns.
c) Tighten the jamnut [45] to 550 in-lb (62.1 N·m) - 650 in-lb (73.4 N·m).
d) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G01912, on the jamnut [45].
SUBTASK 27-81-11-220-004
(20) Do a check of the mismatch at the aft edge of the leading edge flap [2] and leading edge
flap [1] (View L, Figure 401).
(a) Check the mismatch at the aft edge of the leading edge flap [2] and leading edge flap [1]
at locations 12-19 (Figure 402).

SUBTASK 27-81-11-020-004
(1) Do this task: Leading Edge Flap Removal, TASK 27-81-11-000-801.
SUBTASK 27-81-11-020-005
(2) Use these tools to do a check for wear on the parts of the leading edge flap:
(a) micrometer (0-1 inch, readable to 1/1000 inch), STD-1096
(b) vernier caliper (0 - 6 inch, readable to 1/1000 inch), STD-1097.
SUBTASK 27-81-11-020-006
(3) Examine the parts of the leading edge flap for worn areas:
NOTE: The Dacron cloth common to the leading edge (krueger) flap seals can be frayed
provided there is no damage to the silicon rubber portion of the seal. If the silicon
rubber portion is damaged then the seal should be repaired or replaced. Contact the
airplane manufacturer for repair instructions for the seal.
NOTE: Damage to the wear pads is permitted for continued service, but you must replace
them before through-thickness wear.
(a) Remove the parts you want to do a check.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) Measure the parts with a micrometer (0-1 inch, readable to 1/1000 inch), STD-1096, or a
vernier caliper (0 - 6 inch, readable to 1/1000 inch), STD-1097.
(c) Compare the dimensions you measured with the permitted wear dimensions.
(d) If the parts are out of tolerance, replace or repair the part if it is necessary.

B. Krueger Flap Inspection
SUBTASK 27-81-11-200-003
(1) Do a detailed inspection of Krueger Flaps no. 1, 2, 3, and 4.
NOTE: Reference Service Bulletin 737–57A1327 Rev 02.
(a) Check that the Krueger Flap installed on aircraft has had the one-time inspection
completed.
1) If verified that the one time inspection has been completed, no further action is
required.
2) If the inspection has not been completed or the status of completion cannot be
confirmed, then the one time inspection must be completed on the affected Krueger
Flap.
SUBTASK 27-81-11-200-004
(2) Do a detailed inspection in the bullnose attachment hardware of Krueger Flaps no. 1, 2, 3 and
4.
(a) If cracks or any deformation is found, replace the discrepant hardware or Krueger Flap.

F. Leading Edge Slat Removal
SUBTASK 27-81-21-020-001
(1) Disconnect the slat actuator [9] from the leading edge slat [17] (View B, Figure 401).
(a) Remove the bolt retainer [18] from the leading edge slat [17].
1) Remove the bolts [15] and washers [16] that attach the bolt retainer [18] to the
leading edge slat [17].
2) Remove the bolt retainer [18] from the leading edge slat [17].
WARNING
MAKE SURE YOU HOLD THE LEADING EDGE SLAT IN ITS POSITION.
THE LEADING EDGE SLAT CAN FALL TO THE FULL EXTEND POSITION.
THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(b) Hold the leading edge slat [17] while you remove the nut [12], washer [11], bushing [10],
washer [19], and bolt [20].
SUBTASK 27-81-21-980-001
(2) Carefully let the leading edge slat [17] move down to the full extend position.
SUBTASK 27-81-21-860-003
(3) Use hydraulic power to retract the slat actuator [9], do this task: Leading Edge Flaps and Slats
Retraction, TASK 27-81-00-860-804.
NOTE: The slat actuator can hang from the upper fitting.
SUBTASK 27-81-21-040-001
(4) Do this task: Leading Edge Flaps and Slats Deactivation, TASK 27-81-00-040-801.
SUBTASK 27-81-21-480-006
(5) If you use the sling, SPL-2041, to help with the removal of the leading edge slat [17], do these
steps to install the sling, SPL-2041, on the leading edge slat [17] (Figure 402):
(a) Remove the stowage A/P fastener (shown in the placard of the sling tool box) from the
holes of the slat structure that you will use to install the screws [64] and screw [67] of the
sling, SPL-2041, kit.
(b) Attach the wedges [69] on the trailing edge of the leading edge slat [17] where they will
line up with the main tracks [21].
(c) Attach the strap assembly [61] to the bottom of the leading edge slat [17] with screw [64],
washers [65], and nuts [66].
(d) Attach the end fitting [63] to the leading edge slat [17] with screws [67] and washers [68].
(e) Attach the strap assembly [61] to the end fitting [63], wedges [69], and spreader bar [62].
SUBTASK 27-81-21-480-007
(6) Connect the overhead hoist to the sling, SPL-2041.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-81-21-020-003
(7) Remove the leading edge slat [17].
(a) Disconnect the auxiliary arms [28] from the auxiliary tracks [29].
1) Remove the pins [40], nuts [41], washers [42], targets [43], spacers [48], detent arm
roller bearings [45], washers [47], and bolts [46].
2) Move the auxiliary arms [28] away from the auxiliary tracks [29].
NOTE: The auxiliary arms will remain attached to the leading edge slat structure.
3) Remove the auxiliary arm roller bearing [44] from the auxiliary tracks [29].
4) Disconnect the leading edge slat [17] from the main track [21].
NOTE: The main tracks will remain attached to the fixed leading edge structure.
a) Remove the bolt retainer [70] (attached to the leading edge slat [17] structure)
by removing two adjustable bolts [76] and two washers [77] at each of the
main track [21] attach locations.
b) Remove the nut [75], washer [74], plain bushing [73], washer [72], and
bolt [71] at each of the main track [21] attach locations.
(b) If it is necessary, remove the main tracks [21] from the fixed leading edge structure.
NOTE: Some airlines only keep slat box sub-assemblies (without main tracks attached)
for spares. By removing the entire slat final assembly it does then require that the
main tracks are transferred over if the slat box sub-assemblies do not have any
main tracks already attached.
1) Remove the cotter pins [53], nuts [52], washers [51], stop fitting [49], and bolts [50].
2) Align stop fitting [49] with the holes in the ribs.
SUBTASK 27-81-21-020-004
(8) If you remove slats No. 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 or 7, disconnect the telescoping anti-icing duct from the
leading edge slat [17] (TASK 30-11-31-000-801).
SUBTASK 27-81-21-200-003
WARNING
DO NOT LET OBJECTS GET IN THE HOUSING ASSEMBLY OF THE SLAT
TRACK. THIS WILL HELP PREVENT A PUNCTURE OF THE HOUSING
ASSEMBLY THAT COULD CAUSE A FUEL LEAK. THE FUEL LEAK COULD

FURTHER AFT AND DAMAGE THE SLAT CAN, CAUSING A FUEL LEAK.

G. Prepare for the Leading Edge Slat Installation
SUBTASK 27-81-21-200-002
WARNING
DO NOT LET OBJECTS GET IN THE HOUSING ASSEMBLY OF THE SLAT
TRACK. THIS WILL HELP PREVENT A PUNCTURE OF THE HOUSING
ASSEMBLY THAT COULD CAUSE A FUEL LEAK. THE FUEL LEAK COULD
CAUSE A FIRE AND POSSIBLE DEATH OR INJURY TO PERSONNEL.
(1) Keep clean and free of all Foreign Object Debris (FOD), the housing (can) assemblies of the
slat main tracks, at all time.
SUBTASK 27-81-21-860-016
(2) If you use the sling, SPL-2041, to help with the installation of the leading edge slat [17], make
sure that the sling, SPL-2041, is correctly installed on the leading edge slat [17]
(TASK 27-81-21-000-801).
SUBTASK 27-81-21-480-002
(3) If you disconnected the clevis [33], auxiliary track [29], and detent arm [35] joint then install the
preload shim assembly, C27045, that is part of the rigging equipment, SPL-1739, at the
forward supports for the auxiliary tracks [29] (View C-C, Figure 401).
NOTE: This step is necessary to make sure that the leading edge slat is not preloaded against
the fixed leading edge.
(a) Loosen the nut [31] on the clevis [33].
(b) Lift the auxiliary track [29] with the clevis [33] through the auxiliary track support.
(c) Install the preload shim assembly, C27045, that is part of the rigging equipment,
SPL-1739, with the shims [34] on the clevis [33].
(d) Put the clevis [33] back in its position on the auxiliary track support.
(e) Tighten the nut [31] on the clevis [33].
(f) Make sure that two BACW10P390TF, PTFE washers [54] are installed in the clevis [33],
auxiliary track [29], and detent arm [35] joint, if you disconnected it. Use the applicable
Aircraft Illustrated Parts Catalog (AIPC) for the required washers at this location.
NOTE: If the washers are damaged or missing, stabilization of the detent arm is reduced
and it is possible for the detent arm to be deflected laterally during slat extension
or retraction and the possibility of misalignment between the detent arm and the
detent roller increases.
NOTE: If the washers are damaged or missing, it may be possible for the roller to come
out of the detent arm track, thus affecting the operation of the detent system. Also
extreme misalignment of the slat roller attachment could move the slat down
sensor target, causing fault indications or physical damage to the sensor itself.
SUBTASK 27-81-21-860-004
(4) Prepare the auxiliary tracks [29] and detent arm [35] for the installation.
(a) Adjust the aft support for the auxiliary tracks [29] (View D-D, Figure 401).
1) Loosen the nut [39B] on the locking bolt [39A] at the upper aft auxiliary track.
2) Loosen the jam nut [39].
3) Loosen the nut [37] to loosen the locking bolt [36].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
4) Turn the adjusting nut [38] of the auxiliary track aft support to get the required
trailing edge clearance until the dimension A is as specified (Table 401).
NOTE: Optional. In order to adjust the auxiliary track aft support to the dimensions
given in the table below, adjust the auxiliary track up until the slot in the aft
upper corner of the track touches the locking bolt [39A] at the upper aft
auxiliary track.

(Millimeters)

5) Temporarily tighten the nut [37] on the locking bolt [36].
NOTE: You will apply final torque on the locking nut to 130 in-lb (14.7 N·m) -
200 in-lb (22.6 N·m) during the completion of the slat adjustment procedure
(TASK 27-81-00-820-803).
6) Finger tighten the jam nut [39] until in contact with the adjusting nut [38] of the aft
support.
7) Tighten the jam nut [39] an additional quarter turn.
8) Temporarily tighten the nut [39B] on the locking bolt [39A] at the upper aft auxiliary
track.
NOTE: You will apply final torque on the locking nut to 130 in-lb (14.7 N·m) -
200 in-lb (22.6 N·m) during the completion of the slat adjustment procedure
(TASK 27-81-00-820-803).
There is no lockwire required on the jam nut.
(b) If it is necessary, adjust the preload on the detent arm [35] to zero (View F, view B, view
C-C, Figure 401).
1) Turn the preload adjustment bolt [30] clockwise to increase preload or
counterclockwise to reduce preload.
2) Adjust the preload on all the detent arms [35] to zero pound.
(c) After final adjustment secure the preload adjustment bolt [30] to its lower trunnion [86]
with safety wire (View H-H, Figure 401, TASK 20-10-44-400-801).
SUBTASK 27-81-21-420-003
(5) If you removed slats No. 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 or 7, connect the telescoping anti-icing duct to the leading
edge slat [17] (TASK 30-11-31-400-801).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
H. Leading Edge Slat Installation
SUBTASK 27-81-21-400-001
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE LOWER SURFACE OF THE SLAT TRAILING EDGE
AND THE UPPER SKIN PANELS OF THE FIXED LEADING EDGE ARE
SMOOTH BEFORE YOU INSTALL THE LEADING EDGE SLATS. MAKE SURE
THAT THE SURFACE AND PANELS ARE ALSO CLEAN AND FREE OF
CONTAMINATIONS, NICKS, OR BURRS. DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN
OCCUR IF THE SURFACE AND PANELS ARE NOT SMOOTH AND THERE
ARE CONTAMINATIONS.
(1) Install the leading edge slat [17] (Figure 401).
WARNING
DO NOT LET OBJECTS GET IN THE HOUSING ASSEMBLY OF THE SLAT
TRACK. THIS WILL HELP PREVENT A PUNCTURE OF THE HOUSING
ASSEMBLY THAT COULD CAUSE A FUEL LEAK. THE FUEL LEAK
COULD CAUSE A FIRE AND POSSIBLE DEATH OR INJURY TO
PERSONNEL.
(a) Keep clean and free of all FOD, the housing (can) assemblies of the slat main tracks, at
all time.
(b) Install the main tracks [21] on the fixed leading edge structure, if you removed them.
1) Make sure that the clearance between the stop assembly is 0.220 in. (5.59 mm) -
0.250 in. (6.35 mm) (View B-B, Figure 401).
a) If the clearance is not within the specified limit, adjust the shims [95], as
necessary (TASK 27-81-21-400-802).
2) Apply a layer of grease, D00633, to the vertical web surfaces of the main tracks [21]
that contact the side guides.
NOTE: It is no longer required to grease the rolling surface, only the side guide
contact surface.
3) Install the stop fittings [49] to the main tracks [21]:
NOTE: The use of the optional production tool MIT002A0001-90 will ease the
installation of the downstop assembly and the cotter pin.
a) Make sure that you install all the necessary parts (use the AIPC) on the
installation of the stop fittings [49].
CAUTION
INSTALL THE WASHERS CORRECTLY. IF YOU DO NOT,
THE MAIN TRACK/STRUCTURE JOINT CAN BECOME
LOOSE AND THE DOWNSTOP ASSEMBLY CAN FALL.
THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE SLAT TRACK
HOUSING.
<1> Make sure that you install one washer [51] below the head of the
bolt [50] and one washer [51] below the nut [52].
NOTE: An additional washer is permitted under the bolt head, if
required.
<2> Make sure that the bolt [50] or the nut [52] are tighten to the required
torque value.
b) Get access to the stop fittings [49] through the access holes in the track ribs.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
c) Do a check on the fit of the bolt [50] in the hole in the slat main track [21].
<1> If the bolt [50] will not enter the hole in the main track [21] using hand
pressure (because the hole diameter is less than the bolt's shank
diameter), then do the steps that follow:
<a> Ream the hole up to a maximum of 0.4375 in. (11.11 mm).
<b> If it is necessary, remove the slat.
<c> Clean the area as necessary.
WARNING
USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION
WHEN YOU USE COR-BAN 27L. IF IT GETS ON
YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH
WATER. IF THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES,
IMMEDIATELY FLUSH YOUR EYES WITH WATER.
GET MEDICAL AID. THIS MATERIAL CONTAINS
FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN CAUSE
INJURIES TO PERSONNEL.
<d> Apply Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (preferred), or corrosion
inhibiting material, G50136 (alternate), to the reamed hole.
<2> If the bolt [50] has side-to-side play in the hole, measure the hole and
then do the steps that follow:
<a> If the hole diameter is 0.4421 in. (11.23 mm) - 0.5005 in.
(12.71 mm), then install a bushing.
<b> If the hole diameter is greater than 0.5005 in. (12.71 mm), then
replace the slat main track.
d) Coat the shank of the bolt [50], face of the first stop fitting [49], and all surface
of the hole in the main track [21] with Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237
(preferred), or corrosion inhibiting material, G50136 (alternate).
e) Install one washer [51] under the bolt head and the first stop fitting [49] on the
bolt [50].
NOTE: An additional washer is permitted under the bolt head, if required.
f) Install the bolt [50] attached to the washer [51] and the first stop fitting [49] to
the main track [21].
NOTE: The down stop assembly can be installed with the bolt head on either
the inboard side or the outboard side of the slat main track.
g) Install the second stop fitting [49], one washer [51], and nut [52] on the shank
of the bolt [50] that is installed on the main track [21].
NOTE: No grip length increase is permitted on the bolt.
h) Tighten the nut [52] (preferred) or bolt head to 180 in-lb (20.3 N·m) - 200 in-lb
(22.6 N·m).
NOTE: The recommended method is to tighten the nuts.
The optional method is to tighten the bolts.
i) Install the new cotter pin [53].
<1> Wrap the cotter pin [53] around the shank of the bolt [50].
j) Make sure by the visual inspection that the bolts [50], washers [51], stop
fittings [49], nut [52], and cotter pins [53] are all installed correctly.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
k) Make sure that the slat main track housing (can) is free of unwanted material.
(c) Attach the auxiliary arms [28] to the auxiliary tracks [29] (View G, Figure 401).
1) Apply a layer of grease, D00633, to the auxiliary tracks [29] and the side guards on
the auxiliary arms [28].
2) Install the auxiliary arm roller bearings [44] to the auxiliary tracks [29].
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE TARGET EDGES ALIGN WITH RELATED
SURFACES ON THE AUXILIARY TRACK. THE TARGET IS "U"
SHAPED AND YOU MUST ORIENT IT WITH THE BASE FACING
DOWN. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO THE TARGET CAN
OCCUR DURING MOVEMENT OF THE SLAT.
3) Install the bolts [46], washer [47], detent arm roller bearing [45], spacers [48],
targets [43], washers [42], and nuts [41].
a) Make sure that three (CRES material, 0.063 in. (1.60 mm) nominal thickness)
washers are installed in the detent roller/track/arm/sensor target joint (one
washer [47] under the head of the bolt [46] and two washers [42] installed on
both sides of the auxiliary arm) per the applicable AIPC.
NOTE: If the washers [42] and washers [47] are thinner than 0.063 in.
(1.60 mm), the lateral location of the roller bearing will be changed
and it will no longer align with the centerline of the detent arm.
NOTE: The thinner washers will not support the torque preload and operating
load imposed on the joint. As the thinner washers deform, the fastener
torque preload is lost, and the joint may move under normal operating
loads, inducing additional misalignment of the bearing. This joint holds
the slat sensor target, so a loosened bolt will permit the sensor target
to move. Target movement could lead to sensor indication problems,
and the loose target could physically contact the sensor as the slat
moves and cause additional damage.
b) Make sure that the head of the bolt [46] clears the fixed LE structure (auxiliary
ribs) on slats 1 and 8.
<1> If clearance is limited, make sure that the auxiliary track support is fully
adjusted up.
c) Make sure that the target [43] is in its correct location.
NOTE: The inboard and outboard targets have different shapes.
d) Add the washer [42] under the nut [41] if and as it is necessary to align the
cotter pin hole in the bolt [46] with the slot in the nut [41].
4) Tighten the nuts [41] to 95 in-lb (10.7 N·m) - 160 in-lb (18.1 N·m) or the bolts [46] to
144 in-lb (16.3 N·m) - 192 in-lb (21.7 N·m).
NOTE: The recommended method is to tighten the nuts.
The optional method is to tighten the bolts.
5) Install the pin [40].
(d) Attach the main tracks [21] to the leading edge slat [17] of the leading edge slat [17] at
each of the main track [21] locations with the steps that follow:
1) Apply grease, D00633, to the shank and threads before the installation of the
bolts [71].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
2) Install the plain bushing [73] in the main track [21].
3) Install the bolt [71], washer [72], washer [74], and nut [75].
NOTE: The slats 1 and 8 are attached with 0.500 in. (12.70 mm) nominal diameter
bolts. The slats 2 through 7 are attached with 0.625 in. (15.88 mm) nominal
diameter bolts.
a) For slats 2 through 7, tighten the nut [75] to 795 in-lb (89.8 N·m) - 845 in-lb
(95.5 N·m).
b) For slats 1 and 8, tighten the nut [75] to 388 in-lb (43.8 N·m) - 412 in-lb
(46.5 N·m).
4) Install the bolt retainer [70] with two adjustable bolts [76] and two washers [77] on
the leading edge slat [17] structure.
a) Make sure that there is a permitted clearance dimension between the bolt
retainer [70] and the head of the bolt [71] (Figure 401).
NOTE: For slats 1 and 8 is 0.030 in. (0.76 mm) - 0.125 in. (3.18 mm), for slats
2 through 7 is 0.030 in. (0.76 mm) - 0.100 in. (2.54 mm).
b) If it is necessary, adjust the clearance by loosening the two adjustable
bolts [76], moving the bolt retainer [70] along the slotted holes and tightening
the two adjustable bolts [76].
SUBTASK 27-81-21-440-001
(2) Do this task: Leading Edge Flaps and Slats - Activation, TASK 27-81-00-440-801.
SUBTASK 27-81-21-860-010
(3) Match the index mark [91] on torsion rod [79] with the index mark [91] on arm assembly [92]
(View H-H, Figure 401).
SUBTASK 27-81-21-860-011
(4) Match the index mark [91] on torsion rod [79] with the index mark [91] on detent arm [78] (View
G-G, Figure 401).
NOTE: Index mark on torsion rod is 180 degrees out of phase with index mark on detent arm.
SUBTASK 27-81-21-710-002
(5) Manually retract the leading edge slat [17].
(a) Make sure that the clearance between the slat and the fixed leading edge is
0.002 +0.006 / -0.000 in. (0.051 +0.153 / -0.000 mm).
NOTE: Slat must be in the 0-unit position to measure clearance.
1) Measure the clearance at the highest point, within 2.00 in. (50.80 mm) on either
side of the each auxiliary track centerline. Measure the clearance to a depth of
0.400 in. (10.16 mm) to 0.600 in. (15.24 mm).
(b) Make sure that the main tracks [21] move parallel with each other and non-binding
between main tracks [21] and side guides.
1) Make sure that the head of the bolt [46] clears the fixed LE structure (auxiliary ribs)
on slats 1 and 8.
a) If clearance is limited, make sure that the auxiliary track aft support is fully
adjusted up.
(c) Make sure that the main tracks can move freely on the rollers.
SUBTASK 27-81-21-980-002
(6) Manually extend the leading edge slat [17].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-81-21-860-006
(7) Use hydraulic power to extend the actuator to the 1-unit position, do this task: Leading Edge
Flaps and Slats Retraction, TASK 27-81-00-860-804.
NOTE: This will permit you to install the bolt.
SUBTASK 27-81-21-420-005
(8) Connect the slat actuator [9] to the leading edge slat [17] (View B, Figure 401).
(a) Move the leading edge slat [17] until it aligns with the slat actuator [9].
(b) Install the bushing [10], bolt [20], washer [19], washer [11], and nut [12] to attach the slat
actuator [9] to the leading edge slat [17].
1) Make sure that the head of the bolt [20] is on the outboard side of the slat
actuator [9].
(c) Tighten the nut [12] to 660 in-lb (74.6 N·m) - 980 in-lb (110.7 N·m) or the bolt [20] to
882 in-lb (99.7 N·m) - 1078 in-lb (121.8 N·m).
NOTE: The recommended method is to tighten the nuts.
The optional method is to tighten the bolts.
(d) Install the bolt retainer [18].
1) Apply compound, C00528, to the shank and threads of the bolts [15].
2) Install the bolts [15] and washers [16] to attach the bolt retainer [18].
SUBTASK 27-81-21-080-002
(9) If you installed the sling, SPL-2041, remove the sling, SPL-2041, from the leading edge
slat [17] (Figure 402).
(a) Hold and remove the spreader bar [62] from the overhead hoist.
(b) Remove the strap assembly [61] from end fittings [63] and wedges [69].
(c) Remove the screws [67] and washers [68] to remove the end fittings [63].
(d) Remove the nuts [66], washers [65], and screws [64] to remove the strap assembly [61]
from bottom of the leading edge slat [17].
(e) Remove the wedges [69] from the leading edge slat [17].
(f) Install the stowage A/P fastener (shown in the placard of the tool box) in the holes of the
slat structure that you use to install the screws [64] and screws [67] of the sling,
SPL-2041, kit.
SUBTASK 27-81-21-211-001
(10) Visually check that all leading edge slat [17] bull-noses align within 0.00 in. (0.00 mm) - 0.06 in.
(1.52 mm) when in the extended intermediate position.
(a) Dimension may apply at any one point within the 1.0000 in. (25.40 mm) band width.
NOTE: This dimension is normal to the skin surface where the measurement is taken.
Vertical mismatch is permissible.
(b) Make sure that the sum of all of the clearances is 0.0000 in. (0.00 mm) to 0.0600 in.
(1.52 mm).
(c) If not, make sure that all main tracks [21] are correctly installed.
NOTE: The part number of the main track is located on the forward lower non-wear
surface.
SUBTASK 27-81-21-820-002
(11) Do this task: Leading Edge Slats Adjustment, TASK 27-81-00-820-803.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

G. Leading Edge Slat Main Track Installation
SUBTASK 27-81-21-160-001
WARNING
DO NOT LET OBJECTS GET IN THE HOUSING ASSEMBLY OF THE SLAT
TRACK. THIS WILL HELP PREVENT A PUNCTURE OF THE HOUSING
ASSEMBLY THAT COULD CAUSE A FUEL LEAK. THE FUEL LEAK COULD
CAUSE A FIRE AND POSSIBLE DEATH OR INJURY TO PERSONNEL.
(1) Make sure that the housing assemblies and parts of the slat main tracks are clean and free of
unwanted materials.
SUBTASK 27-81-21-210-001
(2) Do a check on the fit of the bolt [50] in the aft hole in the main track [21].
(a) If the bolt [50] will not enter the hole in the main track [21] using hand pressure, then do
the steps that follow:
1) Ream the hole up to a maximum of 0.4375 in. (11.1125 mm).
2) Clean the area as necessary.
WARNING
USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE
COR-BAN 27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE
IT WITH WATER. IF THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES,
IMMEDIATELY FLUSH YOUR EYES WITH WATER. GET MEDICAL
AID. THIS MATERIAL CONTAINS FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN
CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL.
3) Apply Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (preferred), or corrosion inhibiting material,
G50136 (alternate), to the reamed hole.
(b) If the bolt [50] has side-to-side play in the hole, then measure the hole and do the steps
that follow:
1) If the hole diameter is 0.4421 in. (11.2293 mm) to 0.5005 in. (12.7127 mm), then
install a bushing.
2) If the hole diameter is greater than 0.5005 in. (12.7127 mm), then replace the slat
main track.
SUBTASK 27-81-21-420-006
(3) Install the new main track [21] in the housing assembly.
(a) Carefully lift the slat manually, to give clearance to install the main track [21].
(b) Make sure that the clearance between the stop assembly is 0.220 in. (5.588 mm) to
0.250 in. (6.350 mm) (View B-B, Figure 401).
1) If the clearance is not within the specified limit, adjust the shims [95], as necessary
(View B1-B1, Figure 401).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
a) Remove and discard the lockwire from the bolts [93].
b) Remove the bolts [93], washers [94], and stops [96] as necessary to adjust the
shims [95].
c) Apply primer, C00259, to all areas of the holes where the bolts [93] will be
installed.
d) Apply compound, C00528, to all areas of the holes where the bolts [93] will be
installed.
e) Install the stops [96], washers [94], and bolts [93].
f) Tighten the bolts [93] to 80.0 ±2.0 in-lb (9.0 ±0.2 N·m).
g) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G01912, on the bolts [93]
(TASK 20-10-44-400-801).
(c) Install the main track [21] in the housing assembly.
(d) Apply a layer of grease, D00633, to the vertical web surfaces of the main track [21] that
contact the side guides.
NOTE: It is not required to grease the rolling surface, only the side guide contact
surface.
(e) Lower the slat to align the main track [21] and the leading edge slat [17].
SUBTASK 27-81-21-420-007
(4) Install the stop fittings [49] to the main track [21]:
(a) Get access to the aft hole of the main track [21] through the access holes in the track
ribs.
(b) Coat the shank of the bolt [50], the face of the first stop fitting [49], and all the surface of
the hole in the main track [21] with Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (preferred), or
corrosion inhibiting material, G50136 (alternate).
CAUTION
INSTALL THE WASHERS CORRECTLY. IF YOU DO NOT, THE MAIN
TRACK/STRUCTURE JOINT CAN BECOME LOOSE AND THE
DOWNSTOP ASSEMBLY CAN FALL. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE
SLAT TRACK HOUSING.
(c) Install one washer [51] under the head of the bolt [50] and the first stop fitting [49] on the
bolt [50].
NOTE: An additional washer is permitted under the bolt head, if required.
(d) Install the bolt [50], attached to the washer [51] and the first stop fitting [49] to the main
track [21].
NOTE: The down stop assembly can be installed with the bolt head on either the inboard
side or the outboard side of the slat main track.
(e) Install the second stop fitting [49], one washer [51] and the nut [52] on the shank of the
bolt [50] that is installed on the main track [21].
NOTE: No grip length increase is permitted on the bolt.
(f) Tighten the nut [52] (preferred), or the bolt [50] head to 180 in-lb (20.3 N·m) - 200 in-lb
(22.6 N·m).
NOTE: The recommended method is to tighten the nuts.
The optional method is to tighten the bolts.
(g) Install the new cotter pin [53].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Wrap the cotter pin [53] around the shank of the bolt [50].
(h) Make sure by the visual inspection that the bolt [50], washers [51], stop fittings [49],
nut [52] and cotter pin [53] are all installed correctly.
(i) Make sure that the slat main track housing (can) is free of unwanted material.
SUBTASK 27-81-21-420-008
(5) Attach the main track [21] to the leading edge slat [17] with the steps that follow:
(a) Apply Mobilgrease 33, D50306, or AeroShell Grease 33, D50180, to the shank and
threads of the bolt [71] and outer diameter of plain bushing [73].
(b) Install the plain bushing [73] in the main track [21].
(c) Install the bolt [71], washer [72], washer [74], and the nut [75].
NOTE: The slats 1 and 8 are attached with 0.500 in. (12.700 mm) nominal diameter
bolts. The slats 2 through 7 are attached with 0.625 in. (15.875 mm) nominal
diameter bolts.
1) For slats 2 through 7, tighten the nut [75] to 795 in-lb (89.8 N·m) - 845 in-lb
(95.5 N·m).
2) For slats 1 and 8, tighten the nut [75] to 388 in-lb (43.8 N·m) - 412 in-lb (46.5 N·m).
(d) Install the bolt retainer [70] with two adjustable bolts [76] and two washers [77] on the
leading edge slat [17] structure.
1) Make sure that there is a permitted clearance dimension between the bolt
retainer [70] and the head of the bolt [71] (View H, (Figure 401).
2) If necessary, adjust the clearance by loosening the two adjustable bolts [76], moving
the bolt retainer [70] along the slotted holes and tightening the two adjustable
bolts [76].
SUBTASK 27-81-21-420-009
(6) If removed, install the bolt [20] to connect the slat actuator [9] to the leading edge slat [17].
(a) Install the bushing [10], bolt [20], washer [19], washer [11] and nut [12] to attach the slat
actuator [9] to the leading edge slat [17].
NOTE: Make sure the head of the bolt is on the outboard side of the slat actuator.
(b) Tighten the nut [12] to 660 in-lb (74.6 N·m) - 980 in-lb (110.7 N·m) or the bolt [20] to
882 in-lb (99.7 N·m) - 1078 in-lb (121.8 N·m).
NOTE: The recommended method is to tighten the nuts.
The optional method is to tighten the bolts.
(c) Install the bolt retainer [18]:
1) Apply compound, C00528, to the shank and threads of the bolts [15].
2) Install the bolts [15] and washers [16] to attach the bolt retainer [18].
SUBTASK 27-81-21-210-002
(7) Visually check that all leading edge slat [17], bull-noses align within 0.00 in. (0.00 mm) -
0.06 in. (1.52 mm) when in the extended intermediate position.
(a) If not, make sure that all main tracks [21] are correctly installed.
(b) If necessary, adjust the slat (TASK 27-81-00-820-803).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-81-21-860-018
WARNING
MAKE SURE ALL PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT
CONTROLS SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING
GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY
HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE INBOARD FAN COWL PANEL AND THE INBOARD
AND OUTBOARD THRUST REVERSERS ARE CLOSED AND IN THE
STOWED POSITION OR REMOVED BEFORE YOU EXTEND THE LEADING
EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS. THERE IS NOT SUFFICIENT CLEARANCE FOR
THE FLAPS AND SLATS TO EXTEND IF THE INBOARD FAN COWL PANEL
AND THE INBOARD AND OUTBOARD THRUST REVERSERS ARE IN THE
OPEN POSITION. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(8) To move the leading edge slats to the full extend position, do this task: Leading Edge Flaps
and Slats Extension, TASK 27-81-00-860-803.
SUBTASK 27-81-21-210-003
(9) With the slats extended, do these steps:
(a) Apply hand load to the end of the slat assembly, to make sure that preload exists.
(b) If no preload exists, do as follow:
1) Make sure that the possible under-travel dimension of the slat actuator [9] does not
exceed 0.02 in. (0.508 mm) maximum between the attach point at the rod end of the
slat actuator [9] and the clevis bores of the slat attach fittings.
NOTE: The under-travel dimension of the slat actuator indicates that there is no
preload of the slat actuator in relationship to the slat actuator attach fitting.
a) If the dimension is greater than 0.02 in. (0.508 mm), make sure that the part
numbers of the main track assemblies are correct.
NOTE: When the slat main tracks are incorrectly installed visual cues
(excessive mismatches, misalignment, skew, etc.) will sometimes
indicate a problem in advance depending on which slat is affected.
(c) If necessary, adjust the slat (TASK 27-81-00-820-803).
SUBTASK 27-81-21-440-002
(10) Do this task: Leading Edge Flaps and Slats - Activation, TASK 27-81-00-440-801.
SUBTASK 27-81-21-710-003
(11) Do this task: Leading Edge Flap and Slat System Operation With Primary Control,
TASK 27-81-00-860-801.

2. Leading Edge Slat Main Track Inspection
A. General
(1) This task has the steps to inspect the leading edge slat main tracks.

E. Procedure
SUBTASK 27-81-21-020-006
(1) Do this task to fully extend the leading edge slats: Leading Edge Flaps and Slats Extension,
TASK 27-81-00-860-803.
SUBTASK 27-81-21-860-015
WARNING
DO THE DEACTIVATION PROCEDURE FOR THE LEADING EDGE FLAPS
AND SLATS. THE FLAPS AND SLATS MOVE QUICKLY. INJURIES TO
PERSONNEL, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(2) Do this task: Leading Edge Flaps and Slats Deactivation, TASK 27-81-00-040-801.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-81-21-200-005
WARNING
DO NOT LET OBJECTS GET IN THE HOUSING ASSEMBLY OF THE SLAT
TRACK. THIS WILL HELP PREVENT A PUNCTURE OF THE HOUSING
ASSEMBLY THAT COULD CAUSE A FUEL LEAK. THE FUEL LEAK COULD
CAUSE A FIRE AND POSSIBLE DEATH OR INJURY TO PERSONNEL.
(3) Keep clean and free of all unwanted objects (FOD), the housing (can) assemblies of the slat
tracks, at all times.
SUBTASK 27-81-21-020-007
(4) Use these tools to do a check for wear on the parts of the leading edge slat main tracks:
(a) micrometer (0-1 inch, readable to 1/1000 inch), STD-1096
(b) vernier caliper (0 - 6 inch, readable to 1/1000 inch), STD-1097.
SUBTASK 27-81-21-020-008
(5) Do a detailed (on-wing) visual inspection of the slat main tracks for signs of corrosion or wear:
(a) If you find light corrosion on the roller bearing surface of the slat main track, lubricate the
main track (TASK 12-22-71-640-801).
(b) Go to the SRM 57-42-02 for the wear limits of the leading edge slat main tracks.
SUBTASK 27-81-21-860-014
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE
RUDDER AND THE LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS. THE RUDDER AND
THE LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS CAN MOVE QUICKLY. THIS CAN
CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(6) Do this task: Leading Edge Flaps and Slats - Activation, TASK 27-81-00-440-801.
SUBTASK 27-81-21-020-009
(7) Do this task: Leading Edge Flaps and Slats Retraction, TASK 27-81-00-860-804.

D. Prepare for the Removal
SUBTASK 27-81-31-860-001
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT EQUIPMENT AND PERSONNEL ARE CLEAR OF THE
FLIGHT CONTROLS SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE
LANDING GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU
SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(1) Pressurize the hydraulic system B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization,
TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-81-31-860-002
(2) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2
Row Col Number Name
A 15 C01081 HYDRAULIC SYSTEM PTU VALVE CONT 1
A 16 C01085 HYDRAULIC SYSTEM PTU VALVE CONT 2
SUBTASK 27-81-31-860-003
WARNING
MAKE SURE PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE LEADING
EDGE AND TRAILING EDGE CONTROL SURFACES. THE LEADING EDGE
AND TRAILING EDGE CONTROL SURFACES CAN EXTEND AND RETRACT
QUICKLY. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE INBOARD FAN COWL PANEL AND THE INBOARD
AND OUTBOARD THRUST REVERSERS ARE CLOSED AND IN THE
STOWED POSITION OR REMOVED BEFORE YOU EXTEND THE LEADING
EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS. THERE IS NOT SUFFICIENT CLEARANCE FOR
THE FLAPS AND SLATS TO EXTEND IF THE INBOARD FAN COWL PANEL
AND THE INBOARD AND OUTBOARD THRUST REVERSERS ARE IN THE
OPEN POSITION. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE TRAILING EDGE FLAPS ARE FULLY RETRACTED. IF
THEY ARE NOT FULLY RETRACTED, THE ACTUATOR WILL EXTEND. THE
ACTUATOR CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE WING RIB.
(3) Move the flap control lever to the 1-unit detent to extend the leading edge flaps.
SUBTASK 27-81-31-480-001
(4) Install the lockout set, SPL-1734, on the actuator for adjacent leading edge flap
(TASK 27-81-00-480-801).
E. Leading Edge Flap Actuator Removal
SUBTASK 27-81-31-020-001
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT YOU INSTALL THE LEADING EDGE FLAP AND SLAT
ACTUATORS LOCKOUT SET TO PREVENT ACCIDENTAL OPERATION. THE
LEADING EDGE FLAP AND SLAT CAN MOVE QUICKLY. THIS CAN CAUSE
INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(1) Disconnect the applicable leading edge flap actuator [11] or actuator [12] from the leading edge
flap.
(a) To remove the outboard leading edge flap actuator [11], do these steps:
1) Remove and discard the pin [19] from the bolt [18].
2) Remove the nut [24], washer [23], bolt [18], washer [20], and bushing [21] that
attach the actuator [11] to the leading edge flap [1].
3) Disconnect the actuator [11] and washer [22] from the leading edge flap [1].
(b) To remove the inboard leading edge flap actuator [12], do these steps:
1) Remove and discard the pin [26] from the bolt [25].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
2) Remove the nut [30], washer [29], bolt [25], washer [27], and bushing [28] that
attach the actuator [12] to the leading edge flap [2].
3) Disconnect the actuator [12] and washer [22] from the leading edge flap [2].
SUBTASK 27-81-31-860-004
(2) Move the flap control lever to the UP detent to retract the applicable actuator.
SUBTASK 27-81-31-860-010
(3) For the hydraulic system B, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization,
TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-808.
SUBTASK 27-81-31-020-002
(4) Remove the applicable leading edge flap actuator:
(a) Disconnect the hydraulic line [4], hydraulic line [9], and hydraulic line [10] from the
hydraulic fittings [3].
1) Remove lockwire between the B-nut of the hydraulic line [4] and hydraulic fitting [3].
2) Remove lockwire between the B-nuts of the hydraulic line [9] and hydraulic line [10].
3) Attach the identification tags or labels to the hydraulic lines and to their related
hydraulic fittings for correct connections during the installation.
4) Remove the nuts [7], screws [6], and clamps [5] that attach the hydraulic line [4] to
the bracket [8].
5) Disconnect the hydraulic line [4], hydraulic line [9], and hydraulic line [10] from the
hydraulic fittings [3].
6) Install the plugs in the open ends of the hydraulic lines.
7) Install the caps in the hydraulic fittings [3].
(b) Remove the nut [17], washer [16], bolt [13], washer [14], and bushing [15] that attach the
actuator to the structure.
(c) Remove the actuator from the structure.
NOTE: Remove the actuator with the attached hydraulic lines.
SUBTASK 27-81-31-020-003
(5) If you will install a new actuator, remove the hydraulic line [4], hydraulic line [9], and hydraulic
line [10] from the removed actuator.
(a) Remove lockwire between the B-nuts of the hydraulic line [4], hydraulic line [9], and
hydraulic line [10].
(b) Attach the identification tags or labels to the hydraulic lines and to their related hydraulic
ports for correct connections during the installation.
(c) Remove the hydraulic line [4], hydraulic line [9], and hydraulic line [10] from the actuator.
(d) Install the plugs in the open ends of the hydraulic lines.
(e) Install the caps in the hydraulic ports on the actuator.

F. Leading Edge Flap Actuator Installation
SUBTASK 27-81-31-820-001
(1) Make sure that the rod end of the leading edge flap actuator [11] or actuator [12] that will be
installed is the same length as the rod end of the actuator that was removed.
(a) If the lengths are not the same, adjust the rod end length of the actuator as follows:
1) Remove lockwire from the nut [31].
2) Loosen the nut [31] to adjust the rod end of the actuator to the correct length.
a) The limit for maximum adjustment is two full turns of the nut [31].
3) Tighten the nut [31] to 550 in-lb (62.1 N·m) - 650 in-lb (73.4 N·m).
4) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G01912, on the nut [31].
5) Seal the nut [31] as follows:
a) Clean the areas on the joints of the nut [31] with the actuator rod and rod end,
using a clean cloth wetted with technical grade methyl ethyl ketone, B50046,
or equivalent.
b) Apply P/S 870 Class B-1/2 sealant, A50250, or P/S 870 Class B-2 sealant,
A50479, to the joints of the nut [31] with the actuator rod and rod end.
SUBTASK 27-81-31-420-001
(2) If the hydraulic lines are not installed on the applicable leading edge flap actuator, connect the
hydraulic line [4], hydraulic line [9], and hydraulic line [10] to the actuator as follows:
(a) Remove the caps from the hydraulic ports on the actuator.
(b) Remove the plugs from the ends of the hydraulic line [4], hydraulic line [9], and hydraulic
line [10].
1) Remove the plugs only from the ends that will be connected to the actuator.
(c) Connect the hydraulic line [4], hydraulic line [9], and hydraulic line [10] to the related
hydraulic ports on the actuator.
(d) Tighten the B-nuts on the hydraulic line [4], hydraulic line [9], and hydraulic line [10] to
133 in-lb (15.0 N·m) - 147 in-lb (16.6 N·m).
(e) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G01912, between the B-nuts of the hydraulic line [4],
hydraulic line [9], and hydraulic line [10].
(f) Remove the identification tags or labels from the hydraulic lines and from their related
hydraulic ports on the actuator.
SUBTASK 27-81-31-420-002
(3) Do these steps to install the applicable leading edge flap actuator:
(a) Put the actuator in its location on the structure.
(b) To install the actuator on the left wing, do this step:
1) Install the bushing [15], washer [14], and bolt [13] on the outboard side of the
structure fitting.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
a) Make sure that you install the countersink washer [14] under the head of the
bolt [13].
(c) To install the actuator on the right wing, do these steps:
1) Install the bushing [15] on the inboard side of the structure fitting.
2) Install the washer [14] and bolt [13] on the inboard side or the outboard side of the
structure fitting.
NOTE: The bolt direction is optional for the right wing actuators.
a) Make sure that you install the countersink washer [14] under the head of the
bolt [13].
(d) Install the washer [16] and nut [17].
(e) Tighten the nut [17] to 660 in-lb (74.6 N·m) - 980 in-lb (110.7 N·m).
(f) Connect the hydraulic line [4], hydraulic line [9], and hydraulic line [10] to the hydraulic
fittings [3] as follows:
1) Remove the plugs from the hydraulic line [4], hydraulic line [9], and hydraulic
line [10].
2) Remove the caps from the hydraulic fittings [3].
3) Connect the hydraulic line [4], hydraulic line [9], and hydraulic line [10] to the related
hydraulic fittings [3].
4) Tighten the B-nuts on the hydraulic line [4], hydraulic line [9], and hydraulic line [10]
to 133 in-lb (15.0 N·m) - 147 in-lb (16.6 N·m).
5) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G01912, between the B-nut of the hydraulic line [4]
and hydraulic fitting [3].
6) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G01912, between the B-nuts of the hydraulic line [9]
and hydraulic line [10].
7) Remove the identification tags or labels from the hydraulic lines and from their
related hydraulic fittings.
(g) Install the clamps [5], screws [6], and nuts [7] to attach the hydraulic line [4] to the
bracket [8].

SUBTASK 27-81-31-420-003
(7) Connect the applicable actuator to the leading edge flap:
(a) To install the outboard leading edge flap actuator [11], do these steps:
1) Apply grease, D00633, on the mating surfaces of the bolt [18] and bushing [21].
2) Put the actuator [11] and washer [22] in their positions on the fitting of the leading
edge flap [1].
NOTE: You can bond the washer to the leading edge flap with sealant, A00247, for
easier installation.
3) Install the bushing [21], bolt [18], and washer [20], on the outboard side of the
leading edge flap fitting.
a) Make sure that you install the countersink washer [20] under the head of the
bolt [18].
4) Install the washer [23] and nut [24] to attach the actuator [11] to the leading edge
flap [1].
5) Tighten the nut [24] to 660 in-lb (74.6 N·m) - 980 in-lb (110.7 N·m).
a) Align the slot on the nut [24] with the cotter pin hole in the bolt [18].
6) Install the new pin [19] in the bolt [18].
(b) To install the inboard leading edge flap actuator [12], do these steps:
1) Apply grease, D00633, on the mating surfaces of the bolt [25] and bushing [28].
2) Put the actuator [12] and washer [22] in their positions on the fitting of the leading
edge flap [2].
NOTE: You can bond the washer to the leading edge flap with sealant, A00247, for
easier installation.
3) Install the bushing [28], bolt [25], and washer [27] on the inboard side of the leading
edge flap fitting.
a) Make sure that you install the countersink washer [27] under the head of the
bolt [25].
4) Install the washer [29] and nut [30] to attach the actuator [12] to the leading edge
flap [2].
5) Tighten the nut [30] to 660 in-lb (74.6 N·m) - 980 in-lb (110.7 N·m).
a) Align the slot on the nut [30] with the cotter pin hole in the bolt [25].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
6) Install the new pin [26] in the bolt [25].

F. Leading Edge Slat Actuator Removal
SUBTASK 27-81-41-020-002
(1) Remove the slat actuator door [3] from the slat actuator assembly [2]:
(a) For the slats 1 and 8, remove the bolts [14], washers [15], washers [16] and nuts [17] that
attach the slat actuator door [3] to the slat actuator assembly [2].
(b) For the slats 2 through 7, remove the bolts [14], washers [15], washers [16] and nuts [17]
that attach the slat actuator door [3] and clamp [52] to the actuator assembly [2].
(c) Remove the bolts [4], washers [5] and nuts [6] that attach the slat actuator door [3] and
the bracket [32] to the slat actuator assembly [2].
(d) Remove the slat actuator door [3].
(e) Temporarily install the bolts [4], washers [5] and nuts [6] to attach the bracket [32] to the
slat actuator assembly [2].
SUBTASK 27-81-41-860-008
(2) Depressurize the hydraulic system B, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization,
TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-808.
SUBTASK 27-81-41-020-003
(3) Remove the dropout links [7]:
(a) Remove the cotter pins [13], nuts [12], washers [11], washers [9], bolts [8] and
bushings [10].
NOTE: The 737-600/-700/-800 airplanes have castellated nuts and cotter pins installed
at all dropout link locations. The -900 airplanes have castellated nuts and cotter
pins installed at some locations and self locking nuts at other locations.
(b) Remove the dropout links [7].
SUBTASK 27-81-41-020-004
(4) Disconnect the slat actuator assembly [2] from the leading edge slat [1]:
(a) Remove the bolt retainer [23] from the leading edge slat [1]:
1) Remove the bolts [21]] and washers [22] that attach the bolt retainer [23] to the
leading edge slat [1].
2) Remove the bolt retainer [23] from the leading edge slat [1].
WARNING
MAKE SURE YOU HOLD THE LEADING EDGE SLAT IN ITS POSITION.
THE LEADING EDGE SLAT CAN FALL TO THE FULL EXTEND POSITION.
THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(b) Remove the nut [19], washer [20], washer [24], bolt [25] and bushing [18].
SUBTASK 27-81-41-980-001
(5) Manually move the applicable leading edge slat to the 10-unit detent (full extend) position while
you hold the slat actuator assembly [2].
(a) Remove the applicable access panels (TASK 57-41-02-000-801):
1) Remove the access panels 521WB and 521ZB for the slat 1.
2) Remove the access panels 521QB and 521TB for the slat 2.
3) Remove the access panels 521JB and 521MB for the slat 3.
4) Remove the access panels 521CB and 521FB for the slat 4.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
5) Remove the access panels 621CB and 621FB for the slat 5.
6) Remove the access panels 621HB and 621LB for the slat 6.
7) Remove the access panels 621PB and 621SB for the slat 7.
8) Remove the access panels 621VB and 621YB for the slat 8.
(b) Disconnect the actuator rod from the slat.
(c) Pull down on the two detent arms that are installed on each auxiliary track of the slats 1,
4, 5 or 8 with a hand pressure of 75 lbf (334 N) to 85 lbf (378 N) or with a hand pressure
of 45 lbf (200 N) to 55 lbf (245 N) on the slats 2, 3, 6 or 7 (TASK 27-81-00-820-803).
1) Measure the applied force with a spring force scale at the throat of the cam plate.
NOTE: It is acceptable to wrap rags around the detent arms for leverage to pull
down.
2) Pull the slat down to the 10-unit detent (full extended) position when the roller
bearings on the auxiliary track are out of detent.
SUBTASK 27-81-41-980-002
(6) Let the slat actuator assembly [2] hang from the support fitting [46].
SUBTASK 27-81-41-020-005
(7) Remove the slat actuator assembly [2]:
(a) Make sure that you attach identification tags or labels to the hydraulic lines and to their
corresponding swivel [31] ports (before disconnection) for correct re-connections during
the installation procedure.
(b) Disconnect the hydraulic line [29], hydraulic line [30], hydraulic line [40] and hydraulic
line [41] for the slats 1 and 8, hydraulic line [53], hydraulic line [54], hydraulic line [40] and
hydraulic line [41] for the slats 2 through 7 from the swivels [31].
NOTE: The hydraulic line [29], hydraulic line [30] or hydraulic line [53], hydraulic line [54]
with hydraulic line [40] and hydraulic line [41], bracket [32] and clamps [26] and
clamps [36] are removed from the airplane with the slat actuator assembly [2].
(c) Install caps on the swivels [31].
(d) Install plugs in the open ends of the hydraulic line [29], hydraulic line [30] or hydraulic
line [53], hydraulic line [54] with hydraulic line [40] and hydraulic line [41].
(e) Remove the nut [47] and washer [48] from the bolt [44].
1) Discard the nut [47].
(f) Hold the slat actuator assembly [2] while you remove the bolt [44], washer [45] and
bushing [43].
(g) Remove the slat actuator assembly [2] from the airplane.
SUBTASK 27-81-41-480-003
(8) Make sure that you attach identification tags or labels (as necessary) to the hydraulic lines and
to their corresponding actuator assembly [2] ports (before disconnection) for correct
re-connections during the installation procedure.
SUBTASK 27-81-41-020-006
(9) If it is necessary, remove the hydraulic line [29], hydraulic line [30] or hydraulic line [53],
hydraulic line [54] with hydraulic line [40], hydraulic line [41] and bracket [32] from the slat
actuator assembly [2]:
(a) Disconnect the hydraulic line [29], hydraulic line [30] or hydraulic line [53], hydraulic
line [54] with hydraulic line [40], hydraulic line [41] from the slat actuator assembly [2].

 ALL
(b) Remove the nuts [6], washers [5] and bolts [4] that attach the bracket [32] to the slat
actuator assembly [2].
(c) On the slats 1 and 8, remove the nut [28], bolt [27] and the clamps [26] that attach
hydraulic line [29] and hydraulic line [30] to the slat actuator assembly [2].
(d) On the slats 2 through 7, do these steps to remove hydraulic line [53] and hydraulic

1) Remove the nut [28], bolt [27] and the clamps [26].
(e) Remove the nuts [39], washers [38], bolts [37] and clamps [36] that attach the hydraulic

(f) Install caps on the hydraulic ports on the slat actuator assembly [2].
(g) Install plugs in the open ends of the hydraulic line [29], hydraulic line [30] or hydraulic

WARNING

EQUIPMENT.

Maintenance, TASK 78-31-00-040-802-F00.
SUBTASK 27-81-41-010-005
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE INBOARD FAN COWL PANEL AND THE INBOARD
AND OUTBOARD THRUST REVERSERS ARE CLOSED AND IN THE
STOWED POSITION OR REMOVED BEFORE YOU EXTEND THE LEADING
EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS. THERE IS NOT SUFFICIENT CLEARANCE FOR
THE FLAPS AND SLATS TO EXTEND IF THE INBOARD FAN COWL PANEL
AND THE INBOARD AND OUTBOARD THRUST REVERSERS ARE IN THE
OPEN POSITION. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.

closed in the stowed position or are removed.

G. Leading Edge Slat Actuator Installation
SUBTASK 27-81-41-200-003
WARNING
DO NOT LET OBJECTS GET IN THE HOUSING ASSEMBLY OF THE SLAT
TRACK. THIS WILL HELP PREVENT A PUNCTURE OF THE HOUSING
ASSEMBLY THAT COULD CAUSE A FUEL LEAK. THE FUEL LEAK COULD
CAUSE A FIRE AND POSSIBLE DEATH OR INJURY TO PERSONNEL.
(1) Keep clean and free of all unwanted objects (FOD), the housing (can) assemblies of the slat
main tracks, at all time.
SUBTASK 27-81-41-420-002
(2) If the hydraulic line [29], hydraulic line [30], or hydraulic line [53], hydraulic line [54] with
hydraulic line [40], hydraulic line [41] and bracket [32] are not installed on the slat actuator
assembly [2], do these steps:
(a) Remove the plugs from the end of the hydraulic line [29], hydraulic line [30] or hydraulic
line [53], hydraulic line [54] with hydraulic line [40], and hydraulic line [41] that attach to
the slat actuator assembly [2].
(b) Remove the caps from the hydraulic ports on the slat actuator assembly [2].
(c) Put the bracket [32] in its position on the slat actuator assembly [2].
(d) Install the bolts [4], washers [5], and nuts [6] to attach the bracket [32].
(e) Put the hydraulic line [29], hydraulic line [30] or hydraulic line [53], hydraulic line [54] with
hydraulic line [40], hydraulic line [41] in their position on the bracket [32].
(f) Install the clamp [36], bolt [37], washer [38], and nut [39] that attach the hydraulic
line [29], hydraulic line [30] or hydraulic line [53], hydraulic line [54] with hydraulic
line [40], hydraulic line [41] to the bracket [32].
(g) Connect the hydraulic line [29], hydraulic line [30] or hydraulic line [53], hydraulic line [54]
with hydraulic line [40], hydraulic line [41] to the ports in the slat actuator assembly [2].
(h) Tighten the B-nuts on the hydraulic line [29], hydraulic line [30] or hydraulic line [53],
hydraulic line [54] with hydraulic line [40], hydraulic line [41] to 140 ±7 in-lb (16 ±1 N·m).
(i) On the slats 1 and 8, put the clamp [26] on the hydraulic line [29] and hydraulic line [30].
1) Install the bolt [27] and nut [28].
(j) On the slats 2 through 7, do these steps:
1) Put the clamp [52] on the hydraulic line [53].
2) Put the clamp [26] on the hydraulic line [53] and hydraulic line [54].
3) Install the bolt [27] and nut [28].
(k) Remove the identification tags or labels you attached to the hydraulic lines and to their
corresponding actuator assemblies [2] ports during the disconnection task, if they are not
necessary anymore.
SUBTASK 27-81-41-980-003
(3) Make sure that the leading edge slat [1] is in the full extend position.
SUBTASK 27-81-41-420-003
(4) Connect the aft end of the slat actuator assembly [2] to the support fitting [46].
(a) If the washer [42] is not bonded to the support fitting [46], do these steps:
1) Make sure that the mating surface of the support fitting [46] is clean.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
2) Apply sealant, A00247, to the mating surface of the washer [42] and support
fitting [46].
3) Put the washer [42] in its position on the rib support fitting [46].
(b) Put the slat actuator assembly [2] in its position on the support fitting [46].
(c) Install the bushing [43], bolt [44], washer [45], washer [48], and new nut [47] to attach the
slat actuator assembly [2] to the support fitting [46].
1) Make sure that the bushing [43] and head of the bolt [44] are on the outboard side
of the slat actuator assembly [2].
(d) Tighten the nut [47] to 660 in-lb (75 N·m) to 980 in-lb (111 N·m) or bolt [44] to 882 in-lb
(100 N·m) to 1078 in-lb (122 N·m).

IF YOU TIGHTEN THE BOLTS AT THIS TIME, DAMAGE TO
THE HYDRAULIC LINES CAN OCCUR.
<2> Make sure that you loosely install the bolts [33] to let the swivel [31]
align correctly during the movement of the slats.

at the end of this slat actuator installation task.

MAKE SURE THAT YOU SAFELY CONNECT THE HYDRAULIC LINES TO
THE CORRECT PORTS AND FITTINGS. IF YOU CONNECT THE
HYDRAULIC LINES TO THE INCORRECT PORTS AND FITTINGS,
DAMAGE CAN OCCUR. IF YOU DO NOT CONNECT ALL OF THE
HYDRAULIC LINES, THEN DAMAGE TO THE ACTUATOR CAN OCCUR.
(f) Connect the hydraulic line [29], hydraulic line [30] or hydraulic line [53], hydraulic line [54]
with hydraulic line [40], hydraulic line [41] to the swivels [31].

 ALL

D. Leading Edge Flap and Slat Hydraulic Fuse Installation (LE System B or Standby System
Fuses)
SUBTASK 27-81-61-420-001
(1) If you install the two fuse assemblies [2] in system B, do these steps:
(a) Hold the two fuse assemblies [2] in their positions.
NOTE: The flow direction arrow on the two fuse assemblies must agree with the arrow
on the pressure bulkhead.
(b) Connect the hydraulic line [9], hydraulic line [10], hydraulic line [11], and hydraulic
line [12] to the two fuse assemblies [2].
(c) Tighten the nuts [1] on the hydraulic line [9] and hydraulic line [11] to 700 ±35 in-lb
(79.1 ±4.0 N·m).
(d) Tighten the nuts [3] on the hydraulic line [10] and hydraulic line [12] to 500 ±25 in-lb
(56.5 ±2.8 N·m).
SUBTASK 27-81-61-420-002
(2) If you install the standby hydraulic fuse [5] in the standby system, do these steps:
(a) Install the standby hydraulic fuse [5] to the flow limiting valve [4].
1) Install a new packing [8] between the standby hydraulic fuse [5] and flow limiting
valve [4].
2) Tighten the flow limiting valve [4] to the fuse assembly end fitting to 170.0 ±8.5 in-lb
(19.2 ±1.0 N·m).
(b) Hold the standby hydraulic fuse [5] and flow limiting valve [4] in their position.
NOTE: The flow direction arrow on the fuse assembly and valve must agree with the
arrow on the pressure bulkhead.
(c) Connect the hydraulic line [13] to the flow limiting valve [4].
(d) Tighten the nut [7] on the hydraulic line [13] to 140 ±7 in-lb (15.8 ±0.8 N·m).
(e) Connect the hydraulic line [14] to the standby hydraulic fuse [5].
(f) Tighten the nut [6] on the hydraulic line [14] to 270 ±14 in-lb (30.5 ±1.6 N·m).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-81-61-860-002
(3) To pressurize the hydraulic system B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization,
TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
(a) If you replaced the fuse assembly [2], you will need to pressurize the hydraulic system B.
SUBTASK 27-81-61-860-006
(4) To pressurize the standby hydraulic system, do this task: Standby Hydraulic System
Pressurization, TASK 29-21-00-000-801.
(a) If you replaced the standby hydraulic fuse [5], you will need to pressurize the standby
hydraulic system.
SUBTASK 27-81-61-210-001
(5) Do a visual check of the fuse assembly [2] or standby hydraulic fuse [5] for hydraulic leaks.
SUBTASK 27-81-61-710-001
(6) To extend or retract fuse (hydraulic system B fuses), do this task: Leading Edge Flap and Slat
Timing Test in Primary Mode, TASK 27-81-00-700-802.
SUBTASK 27-81-61-710-002
(7) Do this task: Leading Edge Flap and Slat Timing Test in the Standby Mode,
TASK 27-81-00-700-803.
SUBTASK 27-81-61-860-003
(8) To remove the power from hydraulic system B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power
Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805.
SUBTASK 27-81-61-860-007
(9) To remove the power from standby hydraulic system, do this task: Standby Hydraulic System
Power Removal, TASK 29-21-00-000-802.
SUBTASK 27-81-61-610-001
(10) If it is necessary to service the hydraulic reservoirs, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoir Servicing,
TASK 12-12-00-610-801.

D. Procedure
SUBTASK 27-81-61-860-004
(1) Do these steps to reset the hydraulic fuses [2] for system B:
(a) Make sure the flap control lever is in the UP position.
(b) Make sure there is no power on hydraulic system B. If it is necessary to remove power
from hydraulic system B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal,
TASK 29-11-00-860-805.
(c) Between the retract or extend hydraulic fuse [2] and the check valve upstream, loosen
the B-nut [1] sufficiently to bleed off the hydraulic fluid into a 5 gallon (19 liter) container,
STD-1154.
NOTE: The pressure difference across the hydraulic fuse [2] must be less than 5 psi
(34.5 kPa) for a minimum of 5 seconds to put the hydraulic fuse [2] back to the
open position.
(d) Tighten the B-nut [1] after you put the hydraulic fuse [2] back to the open position.
WARNING
MAKE SURE ALL PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE
FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE
LANDING GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN
YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO
PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(e) To pressurize the hydraulic system B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B
Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
(f) Do a check of the hydraulic fuse [2] for hydraulic leaks.
(g) To remove power from hydraulic system B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power
Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805.

D. Leading Edge Flap Flow Limiting Valve Installation
SUBTASK 27-81-71-420-001
(1) Install the flow limiting valve [1].
(a) Install the union [8] on the flow limiting valve [1].
1) Install the new packing [7] between the union [8] and flow limiting valve [1].
2) Tighten the union [8] to the 170.0 ±9.0 in-lb (19.2 ±1.0 N·m).
(b) Connect the flow limiting valve [1] to the hydraulic fuse [2].
1) Install the new packing [7] between the hydraulic fuse [2] and flow limiting valve [1].
2) Tighten the flow limiting valve [1] to the hydraulic fuse end fitting to 170.0 ±8.5 in-lb
(19.2 ±1.0 N·m).
(c) Hold the flow limiting valve [1] and hydraulic fuse [2] in their position.
NOTE: The flow direction arrow on the flow limiting valve and hydraulic fuse must agree
with the arrow on the pressure bulkhead.
(d) Connect the hydraulic line [5] to the flow limiting valve [1] and hydraulic line [6] to the
hydraulic fuse [2].
(e) Tighten the nut [3] on the hydraulic line [6] to 270 ±14 in-lb (30.5 ±1.6 N·m).
(f) Tighten the nut [4] on the hydraulic line [5] to 140 ±7 in-lb (15.8 ±0.8 N·m).
SUBTASK 27-81-71-610-001
(2) If it is necessary to service the hydraulic reservoirs, do this task: Hydraulic Reservoir Servicing,
TASK 12-12-00-610-801.
SUBTASK 27-81-71-710-001
(3) Do a test of the flow limiting valve [1]:
(a) Make sure that electrical power is supplied (TASK 24-22-00-860-811).
(b) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2
Row Col Number Name
D 13 C00841 FLIGHT CONTROL ALTN T.E. FLAP DRIVE
(c) To pressurize hydraulic system B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization,
TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
(d) If it is necessary, move the flap control lever to the FLAP UP detent position to retract the
leading edge flaps and slats.
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE
LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS AND THE TRAILING EDGE FLAPS.
THE FLAPS AND SLATS WILL EXTEND. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO
PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(WARNING PRECEDES)
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THE INBOARD FAN DUCT COWL AND THE INBOARD AND
OUTBOARD THRUST REVERSERS ARE CLOSED OR REMOVED
BEFORE YOU EXTEND THE LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS IN
THIS TEST. THERE IS NOT SUFFICIENT CLEARANCE FOR THE FLAPS
AND SLATS TO EXTEND IF THE INBOARD FAN DUCT COWL AND THE
THRUST REVERSERS ARE IN THE OPEN POSITION. THIS CAN CAUSE
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(e) Put the alternate flap arm switch in the ARM position.
(f) Put the alternate flap control switch in the DOWN position.
1) Make sure that the leading edge flaps and slats fully extend.
(g) Put the alternate flap control switch in the OFF position.
(h) Put the alternate flap arm switch in the OFF position.
1) Make sure that the leading edge flaps and slats fully retract.
(i) Examine the hydraulic fittings of the flow limiting valve [1] for leakage.

E. Leading Edge Flap and Slat Control Valve Removal
SUBTASK 27-81-81-020-001
(1) Remove the lower pan [8] from the flap control unit [6].
(a) Remove the screws [7] that attach the lower pan [8] to the flap control unit [6].
(b) Remove the lower pan [8] from the flap control unit [6].
SUBTASK 27-81-81-480-002
(2) Install the rig pin [16] through the cam follower arm [15] and trailing edge flap control valve
cam [14].
(a) Use the rig pin, F70207-116, SPL-12421, from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585.
SUBTASK 27-81-81-020-002
(3) Remove the leading edge flap and slat control valve [1].
CAUTION
DO NOT LET HYDRAULIC FLUID GET ON EQUIPMENT. IF HYDRAULIC
FLUID GETS ON EQUIPMENT, IMMEDIATELY CLEAN IT FROM THE
EQUIPMENT. HYDRAULIC FLUID CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(a) Put a 5 gallon (19 liter) container, STD-1154, below the leading edge flap and slat control
valve [1] to catch hydraulic fluid.
(b) Disconnect the hydraulic lines [3] from the reducers [2] and hydraulic line [5] from the
check valve [18].
1) Install the caps on the hydraulic lines [3] and hydraulic line [5].
2) Install the plugs in the hydraulic ports of the leading edge flap and slat control
valve [1].
(c) If it is necessary, remove the reducers [2] and check valve [18].
(d) If you removed the reducers [2], remove and discard the packings [4].
(e) Remove the nut [13], washer [12], washer [19], and bolt [11] that attach the leading edge
flap and slat control valve [1] to the leading edge cam link [17].
(f) Remove the lockwire from the bolts [9].
(g) Remove the bolts [9] and washers [10] that attach the leading edge flap and slat control
valve [1] to the flap control unit [6].
(h) Carefully remove the leading edge flap and slat control valve [1] from the flap control
unit [6].

more than 1.00 in. (25.4 mm) (View D, Figure 501).

 ALL
