F. Leading Edge Standby Shutoff Valve Removal
SUBTASK 27-81-91-020-001
(1) Remove the leading edge standby shutoff valve [13].
(a) Disconnect the electrical connector [1] from the leading edge standby shutoff valve
motor [2].
(b) Examine the electrical connector [1] for corrosion.
NOTE: The inspection of the electrical connector can be done after the removal step or
before the installation step of the electrical connector. This is an operator option.
WARNING
DO THE STEPS BELOW IF THE AIRPLANE OPERATES WHERE
DEICING FLUID THAT CONTAINS POTASSIUM FORMATE OR
POTASSIUM ACETATE IS USED. ALSO, DO THE STEPS FOR ALL
AIRPLANES THAT YOU FOUND CORROSION IN THE ELECTRICAL
CONNECTORS IN THE MAIN WHEEL WELL. THE ELECTRICAL
CONNECTORS ARE IN A SYSTEM THAT IS NECESSARY FOR SAFE
FLIGHT.
(c) If there was corrosion, correct the problem (SWPM 20-60-03).
(d) Remove the lockwire that attaches to the screws [5].
(e) Remove the screws [5] and washers [6] that attach the leading edge standby shutoff
valve [13] to the hydraulic module housing [10].
(f) Put the 5 gallon (19 liter) container, STD-1154, below the leading edge standby shutoff
valve [13] to catch hydraulic fluid that drains from the leading edge standby shutoff
valve [13].
(g) Carefully lift the leading edge standby shutoff valve [13] straight up to remove it from the
standby flight controls hydraulic module.
(h) Remove the packing [9], backup rings [8], packings [11], and backup rings [12] from the
leading edge standby shutoff valve [13].
1) Discard the packing [9] and packings [11].
(i) Put a cover on the hydraulic module housing [10] to keep contamination out of the open
valve hole.

SUBTASK 27-81-91-420-001
(1) Install the new packing [9], backup rings [8], new packings [11], and backup rings [12] on the
leading edge standby shutoff valve [13].
(a) Apply hydraulic fluid, D00153, or MCS 352B fluid, D00054, to the packing [9], backup
rings [8], packings [11], and backup rings [12].
(b) Install the packing [9], backup rings [8], packings [11], and backup rings [12] on the
leading edge standby shutoff valve [13].
SUBTASK 27-81-91-420-002
(2) Install the leading edge standby shutoff valve [13].
(a) Remove the cover from the hydraulic module housing [10].
(b) Carefully install the leading edge standby shutoff valve [13] in the hydraulic module
housing [10].
(c) Install the screws [5] and washers [6] that attach the leading edge standby shutoff
valve [13] to the hydraulic module housing [10].
(d) Install the MS20995NC32 lockwire, G01912 on the screws [5] (TASK 20-10-44-400-801).
(e) If you did not examine the electrical connector [1] at the removal step, do these steps:
NOTE: The inspection of the electrical connector can be done after the removal step or
before the installation step of the electrical connector. This is an operator option.
1) Examine the electrical connector [1] for corrosion.
WARNING
DO THE STEPS BELOW IF THE AIRPLANE OPERATES WHERE
DEICING FLUID THAT CONTAINS POTASSIUM FORMATE OR
POTASSIUM ACETATE IS USED. ALSO, DO THE STEPS FOR ALL
AIRPLANES THAT YOU FOUND CORROSION IN THE ELECTRICAL
CONNECTORS IN THE MAIN WHEEL WELL. THE ELECTRICAL
CONNECTORS ARE IN A SYSTEM THAT IS NECESSARY FOR SAFE
FLIGHT.
2) If there was corrosion, correct the problem (SWPM 20-60-03).
(f) Apply D5026NS or ZC-026 compound, G50171, to the connector (SWPM 20-60-03).
(g) Connect the electrical connector [1] to the leading edge standby shutoff valve motor [2].
NOTE: Corrosion inhibiting compound is applied to the exterior of the mated electrical
connectors after the operational test is completed.

(c) Make sure that the flap control lever is in the UP detent.
(d) Set the alternate flaps arm switch, on the P5 flight controls panel, to the ARM position.
1) Make sure that the STANDBY HYD LOW PRESSURE light comes on.
2) Make sure that the standby hydraulic pump starts.
3) Make sure that the STANDBY HYD LOW PRESSURE light is off.
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE
LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS. THE LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND
SLATS CAN MOVE QUICKLY. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS
AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(e) Set the alternate flaps control switch, on the P5 flight controls panel, to the DOWN
position.
1) Make sure that the manual override lever [4] is in position 2.
2) Make sure that the leading edge flaps and slats fully extend.
(f) Set the alternate flaps control switch to the OFF position.
1) Make sure that the leading edge flaps and slats do not move.
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE
LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS. THE LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND
SLATS CAN MOVE QUICKLY. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS
AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(g) Set the alternate flaps arm switch to the OFF position.
1) Make sure that the manual override lever [4] moves to position 1.
2) Make sure that the leading edge flaps and slats fully retract.
NOTE: The leading edge flaps and slats retract because of the pressurization of
hydraulic system B.
SUBTASK 27-81-91-210-001
(2) Make sure that there is no hydraulic fluid leakage from the valve hydraulic fittings.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-81-91-860-011
(3) Remove power from hydraulic system B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power
Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805.
SUBTASK 27-81-91-212-001
(4) Apply Ardrox AV25 compound, G50170, to the mated electrical connector assembly
completely, until the compound drips from the connector.
NOTE: It is not necessary to remove the excess of corrosion inhibiting compound.

NOTE: You can use Method 1 or Method 2 to measure the AOA sensor angle.
NOTE: For the duration of this test, airspeed must not be simulated.
(a) Method 1 to measure the AOA sensor angle:
1) Install the angle of attack probe test fixture, SPL-1917, on the AOA sensor.
NOTE: The test fixture allows for accurate measurement of the AOA sensor angle.
(b) Method 2 to measure the AOA sensor angle:
1) Do these steps on each Stall Management Yaw Damper (SMYD) to determine when
the AOA sensor angles show 30 degrees airplane nose up:
a) Push the ON/OFF switch on the SMYD.
b) Push the down arrow switch on the SMYD until the display shows GROUND
TESTS?.
c) Push the YES switch.
d) Push the down arrow switch on the SMYD until the display shows ANALOG
INPUTS?.
e) Push the YES switch.
<1> Make sure that the display shows AOA SENSOR.
f) Push the YES switch.
g) The display will show AOA and the angle of the AOA sensor.

H. Autoslat Control Valve Installation
SUBTASK 27-83-21-420-001
(1) Install the autoslat control valve [1]:
(a) Make sure the mating surface of the autoslat control valve [1] and mounting bracket are
clean.
(b) Apply sealant, A00247, on the bolts [2] threads.
(c) Put the autoslat control valve [1] in its position on the bracket.
(d) Install the bolts [2] and washers [3] that attach the autoslat control valve [1].
(e) With the intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550, make sure the bonding
resistance between the autoslat control valve [1] and the structure is less than 0.0025
ohms.
(f) Remove the caps from the hydraulic line [4], hydraulic line [5], hydraulic line [8], hydraulic
line [9], hydraulic line [10], hydraulic line [11] and the plugs from the ports on the autoslat
control valve [1].
SUBTASK 27-83-21-420-002
(2) Connect hydraulic line [4], hydraulic line [5], hydraulic line [8], hydraulic line [9], hydraulic
line [10] and hydraulic line [11] to the autoslat control valve [1].
(a) Tighten the B-nuts on hydraulic line [4], hydraulic line [8], hydraulic line [9], and hydraulic
line [11] to a value of 500 ±25 in-lb (56 ±3 N·m).
(b) Tighten the B-nut on hydraulic line [5] and hydraulic line [10] to a value of 170 ±9 in-lb
(19 ±1 N·m).
SUBTASK 27-83-21-210-002
(3) If you did not examine the electrical connector(s) at the removal step, do these steps:
NOTE: The inspection of the electrical connector(s) can be done after the removal step or
before the installation step of the electrical connector(s). This is an operator option.
(a) Before you connect the electrical connector(s), examine the connector(s) for corrosion.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

CONNECTORS IN THE MAIN WHEEL WELL. THE ELECTRICAL
CONNECTORS ARE IN A SYSTEM THAT IS NECESSARY FOR SAFE
FLIGHT.
(b) If there was corrosion, refer to (SWPM 20-60-03) to correct the problem.
SUBTASK 27-83-21-800-001

SUBTASK 27-83-21-420-003

(Figure 201)
A. General
WARNING
MAKE SURE ALL PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT
CONTROLS SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING
GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY
HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE INBOARD FAN COWL PANEL AND THE INBOARD
AND OUTBOARD THRUST REVERSERS ARE CLOSED AND IN THE
STOWED POSITION OR REMOVED BEFORE YOU EXTEND THE LEADING
EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS. THERE IS NOT SUFFICIENT CLEARANCE FOR
THE FLAPS AND SLATS TO EXTEND IF THE INBOARD FAN COWL PANEL
AND THE INBOARD AND OUTBOARD THRUST REVERSERS ARE IN THE
OPEN POSITION. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(1) Use this task to deactivate the leading edge flaps and slats.

G. Leading Edge Flaps and Slats - Tryout
NOTE: This tryout is to make sure that the leading edge flaps and slats are in a zero energy state.
SUBTASK 27-88-00-710-010
(1) Do these steps to check the spoiler control system (Figure 201):
(a) Move the flap control lever one detent position.
(b) Make sure that there is no movement from the leading edge flaps or slats.
(c) Move the flap control lever back to the initial position.
(d) Move the ALTERNATE FLAPS CONTROL switch to the UP position for one second and
then to the DOWN position for one second.
(e) Turn the Captain's control wheel a minimum of 4 units.
(f) Make sure that there is no movement from the spoiler and wheel forces are higher than
usual.
(g) Move the Captain's control wheel back to the neutral position.
(h) Install a DO NOT OPERATE tag, STD-858, on the Captain's and the First Officer's control
wheel.

E. Leading Edge Flap and Slat Position Indicating System - Operational Test
SUBTASK 27-88-00-710-001
(1) Move the flap control lever to the FLAP UP position.
(a) Make sure each flap and slat is in the retract position and align with the wing structure.
(b) Make sure all the leading edge flap lights on the center instrument panel, P2, and the aft
overhead panel, P5, are off.
(c) Set the master dim and test lights switch, on the P1 panel, to the DIM position.
(d) Push the test switch below the leading edge devices annunciator on the aft overhead
panel, P5.
(e) Make sure all the lights are on.
(f) Release the test switch.
(g) Make sure all the lights go off.
SUBTASK 27-88-00-710-002
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE INBOARD FAN COWL PANEL AND THE INBOARD
AND OUTBOARD THRUST REVERSERS ARE CLOSED AND IN THE
STOWED POSITION OR REMOVED BEFORE YOU EXTEND THE LEADING
EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS. THERE IS NOT SUFFICIENT CLEARANCE FOR
THE FLAPS AND SLATS TO EXTEND IF THE INBOARD FAN COWL PANEL
AND THE INBOARD AND OUTBOARD THRUST REVERSERS ARE IN THE
OPEN POSITION. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(2) Move the flap control lever to the 1-unit detent position.
(a) While the trailing edge flaps start to extend, make sure the amber LE FLAPS TRANSIT
light on the center instrument panel, P2, comes on.
(b) When each flap and slat starts to extend, make sure the TRANSIT amber lights on the aft
overhead panel, P5, come on.
(c) Do these checks when the leading edge flaps are in the full extend position;
1) Make sure the annunciator TRANSIT lights go off.
2) Make sure the FULL EXT green lights come on.
(d) Do these checks when the leading edge slats are at the extend position;
1) Make sure the annunciator TRANSIT lights go off.
2) Make sure the EXT green lights come on.

(1) Do these steps to remove the inboard (stainless steel) proximity sensor [4] of the slat (with the
slats 1 through 8 in the extended position and/or with the slats 1 and 8 in the retracted
position) Figure 401, View B:
NOTE: The stainless steel sensor installed with the applicable hardware and consumables is
interchangeable with the titanium sensor installed with the applicable hardware and
consumables.
NOTE: The inboard proximity sensor [4] of the slats are installed on slats 1 thru 8.
NOTE: The shims and spacers are bonded to their mounting surfaces and should be removed
only if necessary.
(a) Disconnect the wires at the splice.
(b) For the slats 1 and 8 (in the extended position), remove the nuts [8], washers [7],
spacer [1], shim [3], and screws [5].
(c) For the slats 2, 3, 6 and 7 (in the extended position), remove the nuts [8], washers [7],
spacer [2], shim [3] and screws [5].
(d) For slat No. 4 or 5 (in the extended position), remove the nuts [8], washers [7], shim [3],
and screws [15].
(e) For the slats 1 and 8 (in the retracted position),
1) Remove the screws [5], shim [3], and spacer [1] from the inboard sensors of the
slats.
2) Remove the nuts [12], washers [11], bolts [10] and shim [13] from the target [14], at
the inboard sensors of the slats, if necessary.
(f) Measure the thickness of the shims [3], shims [13] and the thickness of the spacer [1],
and keep record of it for easier completion of the sensor-target clearance required during
the installation task of the (stainless steel) proximity sensor [4].
(g) Remove the inboard (stainless steel) proximity sensor [4].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
 ALL; AIRPLANES WITH TITANIUM SENSORS
SUBTASK 27-88-11-020-007

1 through 8 in the extended position and/or with the slats 1 and 8 in the retracted position)
Figure 401, View B:
NOTE: The titanium sensor installed with the applicable hardware and consumables is
interchangeable with the stainless steel sensor installed with the applicable hardware
and consumables.
NOTE: The inboard proximity sensor [4] of the slats are installed on slats 1 thru 8.

(c) For the slats 2, 3, 6 and 7 (in the extended position), remove the two screws [32] that
attach the titanium proximity sensor [26] to the rib and remove the shims [27],
spacer [34], washer [30] that is installed under the nut [31], and nut [31].

(b) For slat No. 1 or 8 (with the slats in the extended position), install the proximity sensor [4]
with screws [5], washers [7], shim [3], spacer [1], and nuts [8] (Upper View B,
Figure 401).
1) Use the thickness dimensions of the aluminum shim [3] and phenolic spacer [1] that
you recorded during the removal procedure to determine the closest amount of
shims [3] you need to install.
a) Use shim [3], as required, to meet the clearance requirement.
<1> Adjust the sensor to target clearance by adding or removing shim
laminations as required.
NOTE: The clearance dimension applies to both the forward and aft
targets.
<2> Apply primer, C00259, to both sides of shim [3] (edges optional) and
allow to dry.
b) Bond the shim [3] and phenolic spacer [1] to the support bracket as follows:
<1> Lightly sand to remove the gloss from the mating surfaces.
<2> Clean the mating surfaces with alcohol, B00065, or alcohol, B50073.
<3> Wipe clean with a cotton wiper, G00034, wiper, G50262, or equivalent.
<4> Mix the adhesive, A00165, fully before you use it.
NOTE: The adhesive must not be used if it is too thick.
<5> Apply two thin, continuous layers of the adhesive, A00165, to each
mating surface.
NOTE: The first layer of the adhesive must dry fully before you apply
the second layer. The second layer of the adhesive must dry
only until it is tacky.
<6> Join the mating surfaces while the adhesive, A00165, is tacky.
<7> Apply sufficient pressure to make good contact.
2) Find the same color wires and make a splice.
3) Attach the wires together to make a bundle.
4) If the wires between the proximity sensor [4] and last clamp are loosened during
adjustment (rigging), do the steps that follow:

last clamping location.
b) Redistribute the slack back to main bundle.
<1> Adjust the clamp size to accommodate the sheep shank area.
<2> Stitch-tie to prevent riding condition.
c) If it necessary, reclamp.

27-88-11-760-801Leading Edge Flap and Slat Proximity Sensor Test Using a LCR MeterPDF p. 4200
3. Leading Edge Flap and Slat Proximity Sensor Test Using a LCR Meter
(Figure 502)
A. General
(1) This test will measure the resistance and inductance of the 3-wire proximity sensor and wire
bundle. And compare the values to a known range. This test also examines the target to
sensor condition.
(2) Obey all applicable warnings, cautions, and maintenance practice instructions when necessary
to measure the Proximity Sensor in the test.
(3) Use an LCR meter (Inductance, Capacitance, Resistance), COM-1741 that has a Universal
Serial Bus (USB) port to record the data with a PC automatically. For example 878B or 879B
have a Flap/Slat Electronics Unit (FSEU) port. Use the specified instructions included with the
LCR meter (Inductance, Capacitance, Resistance), COM-1741.
(4) The Sensor Test Gauge Kit (proximity sensor test set, SPL-1690) consists of six go-gauges,
sensor de-actuator tool and an instruction booklet. Use the go-gauges in place of a sensor, if
you suspect the sensor is faulty. Refer to 27-88 FIM if necessary.

SUBTASK 27-88-11-860-031
WARNING
MAKE SURE PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE LEADING
EDGE AND TRAILING EDGE CONTROL SURFACES. THE LEADING EDGE
AND TRAILING EDGE CONTROL SURFACES CAN EXTEND AND RETRACT
QUICKLY. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU CLOSE OR REMOVE THE INBOARD FAN COWL
AND THRUST REVERSERS BEFORE YOU RETRACT THE LEADING EDGE
FLAPS. THE CLEARANCE IS NOT SUFFICIENT FOR THE FLAPS TO
RETRACT WITH THE INBOARD FAN DUCT COWL AND THE THRUST
REVERSERS IN THE OPEN POSITION. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(1) Make sure that the flaps and slats are in the retracted position.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) If the flaps and slats are not retracted, do this task: Leading Edge Flaps and Slats
Retraction, TASK 27-81-00-860-804.
SUBTASK 27-88-11-010-008
(2) Do this task: FSEU Display and Existing Faults Test, TASK 27-51-00-740-801.
SUBTASK 27-88-11-860-055
WARNING
KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL
SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE
COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC
POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(3) Do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
SUBTASK 27-88-11-700-001
WARNING
MAKE SURE PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE LEADING
EDGE SLATS DURING THIS PROCEDURE. THE SLATS CAN MOVE
AUTOMATICALLY (UNLESS OTHERWISE INHIBITED) WHEN THE
HYDRAULIC SYSTEM IS PRESSURIZED, THE TRAILING EDGE FLAPS ARE
EXTENDED AND THE AIR TO GROUND RELAYS SENSE AN AIRBORNE
CONDITION. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THE INBOARD FAN DUCT COWL AND THE INBOARD AND
OUTBOARD THRUST REVERSERS ARE CLOSED OR REMOVED BEFORE
YOU EXTEND THE LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS IN THIS TEST.
THERE IS NOT SUFFICIENT CLEARANCE FOR THE FLAPS AND SLATS TO
EXTEND IF THE INBOARD FAN DUCT COWL AND THE THRUST
REVERSERS ARE IN THE OPEN POSITION. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.

G. Measure the Proximity Sensor and Wiring Installation Resistance with the Flaps and Slats in
the Retracted Position
SUBTASK 27-88-11-760-001
(1) Refer to the applicable WDM (WDM 27-81-11, WDM 27-81-12, WDM 27-81-21, or WDM
27-81-22) for the three-wire sensor to FSEU ARINC connector pin callout.
SUBTASK 27-88-11-760-010
(2) Connect the LCR meter (Inductance, Capacitance, Resistance), COM-1741 (a digital
voltmeter, STD-6481, or a digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793 may be used to measure the
resistance).
(a) First do the Red to Yellow measurement.
(b) Then the Blue to Yellow measurement.
(c) Alternate connections as needed.
SUBTASK 27-88-11-760-011
(3) Supply power to the LCR meter (Inductance, Capacitance, Resistance), COM-1741.
SUBTASK 27-88-11-760-012
(4) Set the LCR meter (Inductance, Capacitance, Resistance), COM-1741, to measure series
resistance (Rs) at 120 Hz.
SUBTASK 27-88-11-700-002
(5) Measure the resistance at the ARINC connector pins on the E1-1 rack for each sensor under
test and record in the log sheet (Figure 502).
(a) The “DATA HOLD” button is used to "capture" your current measured result.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) To make a new measurement, the "DATA HOLD" must be released, by pressing the
button once, then the new measurement can be made.
(c) Record the resistance of sensors in the appropriate space on log sheet.
NOTE: Values to be recorded in hundredths (two numbers right of the decimal point), for
example XX.XX or XXX.XX.
SUBTASK 27-88-11-760-013
(6) Compare the measured resistance values to Table 504.
Table 504/27-88-11-993-818 SENSOR'S NOMINAL VALUES
VALUE SENSOR CONDITION
Three-wire Sensors
Less than 40 mH Target FAR
40 - 50 mH Correctly rigged NEAR sensor
Greater than 50 mH Target may be rigged too near to the sensor
Resistance on aircraft (Red-Yellow resistance plus Blue-Yellow resistance): ≤ 390 Ω
NOTE: Sensor inductance values will vary between sensor positions because of differences in
operation and design requirements. In some condition, the inductance value cannot be
achieved. Inductance values outside of the nominal range are permitted if the
minimum value of 38.00 mH (Target NEAR) is obtained and no system anomaly is
observed.
SUBTASK 27-88-11-760-014
(7) If the measured resistance value is less than 5.00 ohms, this indicates a short circuit condition.
(a) If there is a short circuit, inspect the associated wiring and connectors for contamination
or damage.
SUBTASK 27-88-11-760-015
(8) If the resistance value as measured between the Red and Yellow leads is greater than 100.00
ohms, this indicates a loose contact or wire damage or a defective sensor.
(a) If there is loose contact or wire damage, inspect the associated wiring and connectors for
contamination or damage.
SUBTASK 27-88-11-760-016
(9) If the resistance value as measured between the Blue and Yellow leads is greater than 351.5
ohms, this indicates a loose contact or wire damage or a defective sensor.
(a) If there is loose contact or wire damage, inspect the associated wiring and connectors for
contamination or damage.
H. Measure the Inductance at the ARINC Connector Pins on the E1-1 Rack for each Sensor
Under Test with the Flaps and Slats in the Retracted Position
SUBTASK 27-88-11-760-002
(1) Refer to the applicable WDM (WDM 27-81-11, WDM 27-81-12, WDM 27-81-21, or WDM
27-81-22) for the three-wire sensor to FSEU ARINC connector pin callout.
SUBTASK 27-88-11-760-017
(2) Connect the LCR meter (Inductance, Capacitance, Resistance), COM-1741, for Red to Blue
measurement.
SUBTASK 27-88-11-700-003
(3) Supply power to the LCR meter (Inductance, Capacitance, Resistance), COM-1741.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-88-11-760-018
(4) Set the LCR meter (Inductance, Capacitance, Resistance), COM-1741, to read series
inductance (Ls) at 1 kHz.
SUBTASK 27-88-11-760-019
(5) Measure the inductance for the targets with the flaps and slats in the retracted position and
record in the log sheet for each sensor (Figure 502).
(a) The “DATA HOLD” button is used to "capture" your current measured result.
(b) To make a new measurement, the "DATA HOLD" must be released, by pressing the
button once, then the new measurement can be made.
(c) Record the inductance of sensors in the appropriate space on log sheet.
NOTE: Values to be recorded in hundredths (two numbers right of the decimal point), for
example XX.XX or XXX.XX.
(d) If you suspect a faulty sensor, use the applicable proximity sensor test set, SPL-1690,
8-758-01, Proximity Sensor Test Kit – Go-Gauge to simulate a configuration change of
the sensors current position to a target FAR or a target NEAR position.
(e) Compare the measured inductance values to Table 504 only if using GO-GAUGES.
SUBTASK 27-88-11-760-020
(6) Make sure that the inductance value for the sensor under test is within the range of Table 504.

27-88-11-720-801Leading Edge Flap and Slat Proximity Sensor Test Using Breakout Box and LCR MeterPDF p. 4211
4. Leading Edge Flap and Slat Proximity Sensor Test Using Breakout Box and LCR Meter
(Figure 503, Figure 504)
A. General
CAUTION
THE PROXIMITY SENSOR BREAKOUT BOX IS USED ONLY TO EXAMINE
BASIC SENSOR HEALTH AND INSTALLATION. DO NOT USE AS A RIGGING
TOOL. RIGGING OF SENSORS AND OTHER MAINTENANCE ACTIONS
SHOULD BE DONE ONLY IN ACCORDANCE WITH AIRLINE OPERATING AND
MAINTENANCE PROCEDURES, APPROVED MAINTENANCE MANUALS, OR
DIRECTIVES OF THE APPROPRIATE CERTIFICATION AGENCY.
(1) The test will measure the inductance and resistance of the 3-wire sensors, sensor wires, and
connectors. And compare the values to a known range. This test also examines the target to
sensor conditions.
(2) This test uses the Crane Sensor Test System made up of the following parts:
(a) Proximity Sensor Breakout Box (BOB) and a LCR Meter.
(b) Sensors Test Gauge Set.
1) The controls on the face of the proximity sensor BOB are used to select the desired
sensor for testing.
a) The proximity sensor BOB does not test two-wire sensors. Two-wire sensors,
do not need to be tested.
2) The Sensor Test Gauge Kit (proximity sensor test set, SPL-1690) consists of six
go-gauges, sensor de-actuator tool and an instruction booklet. Use the go-gauges
in place of a sensor, if you suspect the sensor is faulty. Refer to FIM 27-88 if
necessary.
(3) Obey all applicable warnings, cautions, and maintenance practice instructions when necessary
to measure the Proximity Sensor in the test.
(4) Use an LCR meter that has a USB port to record the data with a PC automatically. For
example 878B or 879B have a USB port. Use the specified instructions included with the LCR
meter. Full instructions are included in the BOB's Sensor Test System.

F. Prepare for the Test
SUBTASK 27-88-11-860-038
WARNING
MAKE SURE PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE LEADING
EDGE AND TRAILING EDGE CONTROL SURFACES. THE LEADING EDGE
AND TRAILING EDGE CONTROL SURFACES CAN EXTEND AND RETRACT
QUICKLY. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU CLOSE OR REMOVE THE INBOARD FAN COWL
AND THRUST REVERSERS BEFORE YOU RETRACT THE LEADING EDGE
FLAPS. THE CLEARANCE IS NOT SUFFICIENT FOR THE FLAPS TO
RETRACT WITH THE INBOARD FAN DUCT COWL AND THE THRUST
REVERSERS IN THE OPEN POSITION. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(1) Make sure that the flaps and slats are in the retracted position.
(a) If the flaps and slats are not retracted, do this task: Leading Edge Flaps and Slats
Retraction, TASK 27-81-00-860-804.
SUBTASK 27-88-11-860-058
(2) Do this task: FSEU Display and Existing Faults Test, TASK 27-51-00-740-801.
SUBTASK 27-88-11-860-056
WARNING
KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL
SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE
COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC
POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(3) Do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
SUBTASK 27-88-11-740-002
WARNING
MAKE SURE PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE LEADING
EDGE AND TRAILING EDGE CONTROL SURFACES. THE LEADING EDGE
AND TRAILING EDGE CONTROL SURFACES CAN EXTEND AND RETRACT
QUICKLY. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THE INBOARD FAN DUCT COWL AND THE INBOARD AND
OUTBOARD THRUST REVERSERS ARE CLOSED OR REMOVED BEFORE
YOU EXTEND THE LEADING EDGE FLAPS AND SLATS IN THIS TEST.
THERE IS NOT SUFFICIENT CLEARANCE FOR THE FLAPS AND SLATS TO
EXTEND IF THE INBOARD FAN DUCT COWL AND THE THRUST
REVERSERS ARE IN THE OPEN POSITION. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(4) Do a test of the leading edge flap and slat proximity sensor.
(a) Push the ON/OFF button on the front panel of the FSEU to turn on the display.
NOTE: The display will show EXISTING FAULTS?.
(b) Push the down arrow until OTHER FUNCTNS? shows on the display.
(c) Push the YES button to select OTHER FUNCTNS? on the FSEU.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(d) Push the down arrow until I/O MONITOR? shows on the display.
(e) Push the YES button to select I/O MONITOR? from the menu.
(f) Push the YES button to select PROX SENSORS? from the I/O MONITOR? menu.
(g) Push the down arrow to step through the proximity sensor states at the LE flaps and slats
UP position.
(h) Make sure that these displays and the proximity sensor states show on the FSEU
(Table 501).

G. Measure the Proximity Sensor and Wiring Installation Resistance with the Flaps and Slats in
the Retracted Position
SUBTASK 27-88-11-480-006
(1) Connect the LCR meter (Inductance, Capacitance, Resistance), COM-1741, leads to the RED
and YELLOW jacks on the front of the proximity sensor breakout box, SPL-14585.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) A digital voltmeter, STD-6481, or a digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793, may be used to
measure the resistance.
SUBTASK 27-88-11-860-040
(2) Set the LCR meter (Inductance, Capacitance, Resistance), COM-1741, to measure series
resistance (Rs) at 120 Hz.
SUBTASK 27-88-11-860-041
(3) Push the L/C/R button to change to the resistance mode.
SUBTASK 27-88-11-860-042
(4) Push and hold the LCR meter (Inductance, Capacitance, Resistance), COM-1741, button for
more than one second to change to series mode.
(a) SER is shown in the middle-right side of the LCR meter (Inductance, Capacitance,
Resistance), COM-1741, display.
SUBTASK 27-88-11-760-007
(5) Measure the resistance for the targets with the flaps and slats in the retracted position (RED to
YELLOW) and record in the log sheet for each sensor (Figure 504).
(a) The “DATA HOLD” button is used to "capture" your current measured result.
(b) To make a new measurement, the "DATA HOLD" must be released, by pressing the
button once, then the new measurement can be made.
(c) Record the resistance of sensors in the appropriate space on log sheet.
NOTE: Values to be recorded in hundredths (two numbers right of the decimal point), for
example XX.XX or XXX.XX.
SUBTASK 27-88-11-200-003
(6) Compare the measured resistance values to Table 506.
SUBTASK 27-88-11-860-043
(7) Use the proximity sensor breakout box, SPL-14585, controls to set the next sensor.
(a) Measure the resistance (RED to YELLOW) and record for each of the remaining sensors.
SUBTASK 27-88-11-480-007
(8) Connect the LCR meter (Inductance, Capacitance, Resistance), COM-1741, leads to the
BLUE and YELLOW jacks on the front of the proximity sensor breakout box, SPL-14585.
(a) A digital voltmeter, STD-6481, or a digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793, may be used to
measure the resistance.
SUBTASK 27-88-11-760-008
(9) Measure the resistance for the targets with the flaps and slats in the retracted position (BLUE
to YELLOW) and record in the log sheet for each sensor (Figure 504) .
(a) The “DATA HOLD” button is used to "capture" your current measured result.
(b) To make a new measurement, the "DATA HOLD" must be released, by pressing the
button once, then the new measurement can be made.
(c) Record the resistance of sensors in the appropriate space on log sheet.
NOTE: Values to be recorded in hundredths (two numbers right of the decimal point), for
example XX.XX or XXX.XX.
SUBTASK 27-88-11-210-003
(10) Compare the measured resistance values to Table 506.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 27-88-11-860-044
(11) Use the proximity sensor breakout box, SPL-14585, controls to set the next sensor.
(a) Measure the resistance (BLUE to YELLOW) and record for each of the remaining

VALUE SENSOR CONDITION
Three-wire Sensor

*[1] There is no range (tolerance) for Target FAR. The nominal 35 mH value for Target FAR is left without tolerance

to BLUE) and record in the log sheet for each sensor (Figure 504).
(a) The “DATA HOLD” button is used to "capture" your current measured result.
(b) To make a new measurement, the "DATA HOLD" must be released, by pressing the
button once, then the new measurement can be made.
(c) Record the inductance of sensors in the appropriate space on log sheet.
NOTE: Values to be recorded in hundredths (two numbers right of the decimal point), for
example XX.XX or XXX.XX.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(d) If you suspect a faulty sensor, use the applicable proximity sensor test set, SPL-1690,
8-758-01, Proximity Sensor Test Kit – Go-Gauge to simulate a configuration change of
the sensors current position to a target FAR or a target NEAR position.
(14) Compare the measured inductance value to Table 506 only if using the GO-GAUGE.
SUBTASK 27-88-11-760-035
(15) Make sure that the inductance value for the sensor under test is within the range of Table 506.
SUBTASK 27-88-11-760-036
(16) Use the proximity sensor breakout box, SPL-14585, controls to set the next sensor.
(a) Measure the inductance (RED to BLUE) and record for each of the remaining sensors.

E. P5-12 Annunciator Panel Removal
SUBTASK 27-88-21-020-001
(1) Do these steps to remove the P5-12 annunciator panel:
(a) Release the fasteners on the front of the P5-12 annunciator panel.
CAUTION
DO NOT APPLY TOO MUCH FORCE. TOO MUCH FORCE WILL CAUSE
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(b) Carefully lower the P5-12 annunciator panel until you can get to the electrical connector.
(c) Disconnect the electrical connector from the rear of the panel.
